॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 20 — "ayaṃ devāya janmane" ("The Twentieth Sūkta"; to the Ṛbhus)

(Printed pp. 1–42. The heading page, p. 1, carries the invocation, the verses of homage, the title of the volume, "Bhāga 3 — Prathamāṣṭake dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ" — the Second Adhyāya of the First Aṣṭaka — and the opening of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya. The verses at the top of p. 1 are given below.)

॥ Invocation and homage verses (p. 1) ॥

॥ श्री महागणाधिपतये नमः ॥

|| śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ ||

वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननम् ॥ यस्य निःश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वन्दे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरम् ॥ वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥

vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānām upakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛta-kṛtyāḥ syus taṃ namāmi gajānanam || yasya niḥśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tam ahaṃ vande vidyā-tīrtha-maheśvaram || vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmāt sarva-prayatnena vedam eva sadā japet ||

Translation:The translation is editorial; the verses are the standard homage verses of this series. "I bow to the elephant-faced one, bowing to whom the good-minded — Vāgīśa [Brahmā] and the rest — become successful at the start of all undertakings. I praise Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara, whose breath the Vedas are, and who made the whole world from the Vedas. The Veda is Śiva, Śiva is the Veda; one who studies the Veda is Sadāśiva; therefore, with every effort, one should always recite the Veda alone." The English is an editorial rendering; the Sanskrit is as printed, read from the Kannada script, with a few letters uncertain.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed pp. 1–2) अथमष्टावार्भवमिति is as printed (also in the Kannada rendering); the Āśvalāyana number is printed ८-९.

अत्र प्रथमाष्टके द्वितीयोऽध्याय आरभ्यते । तत्रायं देवायेत्यष्टर्चं सूक्तम् । तस्य ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । ऋभुदेवताकत्वमनुक्रम्यते । अथमष्टावार्भवमिति ॥ विनियोगस्तु सूक्तस्य लैङ्गिकः स्मार्तो वा द्रष्टव्यः ॥ व्यूढस्य प्रथमे छन्दोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रेऽयं देवाय जन्मन इत्यार्भवस्तृचः । अथ छन्दोमा इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । अभि त्वा देव सवितः प्रेतां यज्ञस्य शंभुवायं देवाय जन्मन इति तृचः ॥ आ. ८-९ । इति ॥

atra prathamāṣṭake dvitīyo 'dhyāya ārabhyate | tatrāyaṃ devāyetyaṣṭarcaṃ sūktam | tasya ṛṣicchandasī pūrvavat | ṛbhudevatākatvamanukramyate | athamaṣṭāvārbhavamiti || viniyogastu sūktasya laiṅgikaḥ smārto vā draṣṭavyaḥ || vyūḍhasya prathame chandome vaiśvadevaśastre 'yaṃ devāya janmana ityārbhavastṛcaḥ | atha chandomā iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | abhi tvā deva savitaḥ pretāṃ yajñasya śaṃbhuvāyaṃ devāya janmana iti tṛcaḥ || ā. 8-9 | iti ||

Translation: "Here, in the First Aṣṭaka, the Second Adhyāya begins. In it the sūkta beginning ayaṃ devāya has eight ṛks. Its ṛṣi and metre are as before. That its deity is the Ṛbhus is stated in the Anukramaṇī: 'athamaṣṭāv ārbhavam' [as printed]. The application of the sūkta is to be known as laiṅgika or smārta. In the first chandoma day of the vyūḍha rite, at the vaiśvadeva-śastra, the tṛca to the Ṛbhus ayaṃ devāya janmane is used. So it is laid down in the section atha chandomāḥ: 'abhi tvā deva savitaḥ, pretāṃ yajñasya śambhuvā, ayaṃ devāya janmane: tṛcas' (Āśv. 8-9)."

Page 2 — Sūkta 20: introduction (end), heading, Rik 1 Saṃhitā

Anuvāda (Kannada rendering): In the first sūkta of the second adhyāya of the first aṣṭaka there are eight ṛks. The ṛṣi and metres of this sūkta are as in the previous sūkta. The Anukramaṇikā says, athamaṣṭāvārbhavam iti, that the Ṛbhus are the deities of this sūkta. The application is both śrauta and smārta. In the rite called vyūḍha, at the time of reciting the mantras called prathama-chandoma, for reciting the vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras, the tṛca connected with the Ṛbhus, ayaṃ devāya janmane, is recited. This matter is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra (Ā. 8-9), in the section atha chandomāḥ: that the tṛca (three ṛks) to Savitṛ beginning abhi tvā deva savitaḥ (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-24-3), the tṛca to Heaven and Earth beginning pretāṃ yajñasya śambhuvā (Ṛ. saṃ. 2-41-19) and the tṛca to the Ṛbhus beginning ayaṃ devāya janmane (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-20-1) are to be recited as the chandoma mantras.

॥ Sūkta — 20 ॥ ॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 5 ॥ Sūkta — 20 ॥ ॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 2 ॥ Varga — 1, 2 ॥ ॥ Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 8 ॥ ॥ Ṛṣiḥ — Medhātithiḥ Kāṇvaḥ ॥ ॥ Devatā — Ṛbhavaḥ ॥ ॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥

Sūkta 20, Rik 1

Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒यं दे॒वाय॒ जन्म॑ने॒ स्तोमो॒ विप्रे॑भिरास॒या । अका॑रि रत्न॒धात॑मः ॥१॥

ayáṃ devā́ya jánmane stómo víprebhir āsayā́ | ákāri ratnadhā́tamaḥ ||1||

Page 3 — Rik 1: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अयम् । देवाय । जन्मने । स्तोमः । विप्रेभिः । आसया ॥ अकारि । रत्नऽधातमः ॥१॥

ayam | devāya | janmane | stomaḥ | viprebhiḥ | āsayā || akāri | ratna 'dhātamaḥ ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

ऋभवो हि मनुष्याः सन्तस्तपसा देवत्वं प्राप्ताः । ते चात्र सूक्ते देवताः । तत्संघो जायमानवाचिना जन्मशब्देनैकवचनान्तेनात्र निर्दिश्यते । जन्मने जायमानाय ऋभुसंघरूपाय देवाय तत्प्रीत्यर्थमयं स्तोमः स्तोत्रविशेषो विप्रेभिर्मेधाविभिर्ऋत्विग्भिरासया स्वकीयेनास्येनाकारि । निष्पादितः । कीदृशः स्तोमः । रत्नधातमोऽतिशयेन रमणीयमणियुक्तादिधनप्रदः । स्तोत्रेण तुष्टा ऋभवो धनं प्रयच्छन्तीत्यर्थः ॥ आसया । आस्यशब्दात्तृतीयैकवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना याजादेशः । व्यत्ययेन प्रकृतियकारस्य लोपः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तः । रत्नधातमः । रत्नानि दधातीति रत्नधाः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

ṛbhavo hi manuṣyāḥ santastapasā devatvaṃ prāptāḥ | te cātra sūkte devatāḥ | tatsaṃgho jāyamānavācinā janmaśabdenaikavacanāntenātra nirdiśyate | janmane jāyamānāya ṛbhusaṃgharūpāya devāya tatprītyarthamayaṃ stomaḥ stotraviśeṣo viprebhirmedhāvibhirṛtvigbhirāsayā svakīyenāsyenākāri | niṣpāditaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ stomaḥ | ratnadhātamo 'tiśayena ramaṇīyamaṇiyuktādidhanapradaḥ | stotreṇa tuṣṭā ṛbhavo dhanaṃ prayacchantītyarthaḥ || āsayā | āsyaśabdāttṛtīyaikavacanasya supāṃ sulugityādinā yājādeśaḥ | vyatyayena prakṛtiyakārasya lopaḥ | cita ityantodāttaḥ | ratnadhātamaḥ | ratnāni dadhātīti ratnadhāḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "The Ṛbhus, being men, attained divinity by austerity; and they are the deities in this sūkta. Their company is denoted here by the word janman, meaning 'one being born', in the singular. For the deva, the god in the form of the company of the Ṛbhus, janmane, being born, for his pleasure, this stoma, a particular hymn, akāri, was made, by the vipras, the wise priests, āsayā, with their own mouth. Of what kind is the hymn? Ratnadhātama, giving in the highest degree wealth such as lovely gems. The sense is: pleased by the hymn, the Ṛbhus give wealth." (Grammatical tail: āsayā, from āsya, yāc for the instrumental singular by supāṃ suluk…, the y of the base dropped by exchange, final udātta by citaḥ; ratnadhātamaḥ, "he holds gems", ratnadhāḥ, the accent of the kṛt final member.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

जन्मने (janmane) — to those who have taken birth as the deities called Ṛbhus | देवाय (devāya) — for the deities (for the company of deities) | रत्नधातमः (ratnadhātamaḥ) — giving wealth such as lovely gems | अयं स्तोमः (ayaṃ stomaḥ) — this particular hymn | विप्रेभिः (viprebhiḥ) — by the wise, that is, by people such as the learned priests | आसया (āsayā) — with (their) mouth | अकारि (akāri) — has been made.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The deities called Ṛbhus were men before and attained divinity. Addressing the company of deities who attained such a divine birth, the learned priests and other people have made this hymn with their own mouth. This excellent hymn, by the grace of the Ṛbhu deities, gives gems and other goods to those who praise.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

This hymn, the bestower of riches has been addressed by the sages with their own mouths to the race (of Ribhus) having divine birth.

Page 4 — Rik 1: Special Topics and grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

That those called Ṛbhus were men formerly and attained divinity by their excellent conduct and the performance of good works is said in many places in the Ṛgveda. Formerly the ṛṣi Aṅgiras had a son named Nītimañjari [as printed]. In his line the ṛṣi named Sudhanvan had three sons, Ṛbhu, Vibhu and Vāja. It is believed that by good works such as the performance of good rites and helping the deities they obtained the birth of gods, or became gods. There is the custom of calling all three sons of Sudhanvan, Ṛbhu and the rest, Ṛbhus; all three sons are called by the name of the eldest. Since they are pupils of Tvaṣṭṛ, they are also called the craftsmen of the gods. It is said here and there that they made the implements needed by deities such as Indra, that is, Indra's chariot and Agni's camasa vessel. In this sūkta there is an account of some of the works they did. Descriptions are found here and there that they have wonderful power and are able to do any work. Since they have the very powers and capacities of the deities, the ṛṣis, regarding them as belonging to the group of the deities, have described them and their works in various ways. It is believed that they dwell in the sun's orb and do their works through the sun's rays. More details about them will be given later.

Āsayā: a word in the instrumental singular. Āsya is a variant form of the word mukha, mouth: the sense is that they recite with the mouth, with the lips.

Ratnadhātamaḥ: this word occurs in the very first ṛk of the Ṛgveda, agnim īḷe. Ratnāni dadhāti (dadāti) iti ratnadhāḥ atiśayena dhanapradaḥ: the sense is one who gives wealth such as gems in a high degree.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 4–5, noted briefly

आसया (āsayā): after the word āsya the instrumental singular suffix ṭā. For it, by the sūtra "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39), the substitute yāc. The y of the base āsya drops by "vyatyayo bahulam" (Pā. sū. 3-1-85): āsayā. Yāc has c as it; so by "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. "1-1-63" [as printed, for 6-1-163]) the final udātta accent comes.

Page 5 (upper) — Rik 1: grammar (end)

रत्नधातमः (ratnadhātamaḥ): the word ratna is always neuter; so by "nabviṣayasyānisantasya" (Phi. sū. 26) it is initial udātta. The analysis is ratnāni dadhāti. After the root, with the word ratna as upapada, kvip or the suffix vic; all the letters of the suffix drop; by the root accent dhā is final udātta; after compounding, by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139) the final member, a kṛdanta, keeps its own accent. The other letters are unaccented by the accent of the remaining unaccented. In ratnadhā final udātta may also be stated by "samāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-223). The suffix tamap is pit; so by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4) it is unaccented; the svarita and pracaya are to be inferred.

॥१॥

Page 5 (lower) — Sūkta 20, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

य इन्द्रा॑य वचो॒युजा॑ ततक्षु॒र्मन॑सा॒ हरी॑ । शमी॑भिर्य॒ज्ञमा॑शत ॥२॥

ya índrāya vacoyújā tatakṣur mánasā hárī | śámībhir yajñám āśata ||2||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ये । इन्द्राय । वचःऽयुजा । ततक्षुः । मनसा । हरी इति ॥ शमीभिः । यज्ञम् । आशत ॥२॥

ye | indrāya | vacaḥ 'yujā | tatakṣuḥ | manasā | harī iti || śamībhiḥ | yajñam | āśata ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

ये ऋभव इन्द्रायेन्द्रप्रीत्यर्थं वचोयुजा ताडनादिकं विना वाङ्मात्रेण रथे युज्यमानौ सुशिक्षितौ हरी एतन्नामकावश्वौ मनसा ततक्षुः संपादितवन्तः । ऋभूणां सत्यसंकल्पत्वात्तत्संकल्पमात्रेणेन्द्रस्याश्वौ संपन्नावित्यर्थः । ते ऋभवः शमीभिर्ग्रहचमसादिनिष्पादनरूपैः कर्मभिर्यज्ञमस्मदीयमाशत । व्याप्तवन्तः । अपोऽप्न इत्यादिषु षड्विंशतिसंख्याकेषु कर्मनामसु शमी शिमीति पठितम् ॥ वचोयुजा । वचसा युञ्जाते । सत्सूद्विषेत्यादिना क्विप् । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेराकारः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । ततक्षुः । तक्षू त्वक्षू तनूकरणे । लिटि झेरुसादेशः । पादादित्वादनिघातः । शमीभिः । शमयन्ति पापानीति शम्यः कर्माणि । औणादिक इन् । कृदिकारादक्तिनः । पा. ४-१-४५ । इति ङीष् । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । आशत । अशू व्याप्तौ । लङि झस्यादादेशः । स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः । तस्य बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । आडागमः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥

ye ṛbhava indrāyendraprītyarthaṃ vacoyujā tāḍanādikaṃ vinā vāṅmātreṇa rathe yujyamānau suśikṣitau harī etannāmakāvaśvau manasā tatakṣuḥ saṃpāditavantaḥ | ṛbhūṇāṃ satyasaṃkalpatvāttatsaṃkalpamātreṇendrasyāśvau saṃpannāvityarthaḥ | te ṛbhavaḥ śamībhirgrahacamasādiniṣpādanarūpaiḥ karmabhiryajñamasmadīyamāśata | vyāptavantaḥ | apo 'pna ityādiṣu ṣaḍviṃśatisaṃkhyākeṣu karmanāmasu śamī śimīti paṭhitam || vacoyujā | vacasā yuñjāte | satsūdviṣetyādinā kvip | supāṃ sulugityādinā vibhakterākāraḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaraḥ | tatakṣuḥ | takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe | liṭi jherusādeśaḥ | pādāditvādanighātaḥ | śamībhiḥ | śamayanti pāpānīti śamyaḥ karmāṇi | auṇādika in | kṛdikārādaktinaḥ | pā. 4-1-45 | iti ṅīṣ | vṛṣāditvādādyudāttaḥ | āśata | aśū vyāptau | laṅi jhasyādādeśaḥ | svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ | tasya bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | āḍāgamaḥ | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "The Ṛbhus who, for Indra, for Indra's pleasure, manasā tatakṣuḥ, produced by the mind, the harī, the two horses of that name, well trained, vacoyujā, yoking themselves to the chariot at a word alone, without beating and the like. Since the Ṛbhus are of true resolve, the two horses of Indra came about by their mere resolve. Those Ṛbhus, śamībhiḥ, by acts in the form of making the graha cups, the camasa vessels and the like, āśata, reached, our sacrifice. Śamī and śimī are read among the twenty-six names for action beginning apaḥ, apnaḥ." (Grammatical tail: vacoyujā, "they yoke at a word", kvip by satsūdviṣa…, ā for the ending by supāṃ suluk…, the accent of the kṛt final member; tatakṣuḥ, takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe, us for jhi in the liṭ, not lowered at the start of the pāda; śamībhiḥ, "they calm sins": śamyaḥ, acts, the Uṇādi in, ṅīṣ by kṛdikārād aktinaḥ (Pā. 4-1-45), initial udātta as one of the vṛṣa-ādi; āśata, aśū vyāptau, at for jha in the laṅ, śnu by svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ, its luk by bahulaṃ chandasi, the augment āṭ, wholly unaccented by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.)

Page 6 — Rik 2: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ये (ye) (ऋभवः (ṛbhavaḥ)) — which Ṛbhu deities | इन्द्राय (indrāya) — for Indra's pleasure | वचोयुजा (vacoyujā) — who can be yoked (to the chariot) by a word of the mouth alone | हरी (harī) — the two horses called Harī | मनसा (manasā) — by mental resolve alone | ततक्षुः (tatakṣuḥ) — produced and gave | (ते ऋभवः (te ṛbhavaḥ)) — such Ṛbhus) | शमीभिः (śamībhiḥ) — by acts (that provide the means of sacrifice such as the graha and camasa) | यज्ञम् (yajñam) — our sacrifice | आशत (āśata) — pervaded.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

These Ṛbhus produced for Indra's pleasure, by mental resolve alone, the two well-trained horses called Harī of Indra's chariot. May such Ṛbhus provide for our sacrifice too the means of sacrifice such as the graha and camasa.

॥ English Translation ॥

The Ribhus who created mentally for Indra his pair of tawny horses that yoke themselves at his command attained the sacrifice by their acts of skill.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Vacoyujā:

ताडनादिकं विना वाङ्मात्रेण रथे युज्यमानौ ॥

tāḍanādikaṃ vinā vāṅmātreṇa rathe yujyamānau ||

("Yoked to the chariot by speech alone, without beating and the like.") The sense is: they yoke themselves to the chariot merely at what Indra says with his mouth, without training such as beating; that is, Indra's command is enough; without any kind of urging by a charioteer they yoke themselves to the chariot: "Harnessing themselves at Indra's word (command)" [as printed] is the intent.

Tatakṣuḥ manasā:

संपादितवन्तः, कृतवन्तः ॥

saṃpāditavantaḥ, kṛtavantaḥ ||

("They produced, they made.") "created" [as printed]. Since the Ṛbhus are expert in the craft-śāstra and of true resolve, they are able, by their power of mind, to create the

Page 7 — Rik 2: Special Topics (end) and grammar

implements of sacrifice, chariots and other things that are means of sacrifice. These Ṛbhu deities need not use tools and materials to make things like modern craftsmen. The word manasā indicates the intent that they have the power and capacity to make anything they want by mere mental resolve.

Harī:

हरतः वहत इति हरी ।

harataḥ vahata iti harī |

("They carry, they convey: harī.") Because they draw the chariot, Indra's horses are named harī. This word, ending in the dual, is generally used in the Ṛgveda to denote Indra's two horses.

Śamībhiḥ:

शमयन्ति पापानीति शम्यः कर्माणि ।

śamayanti pāpānīti śamyaḥ karmāṇi |

("They calm sins: śamyaḥ, acts.") Since the word śamī or śimī is read among the twenty-six names for action beginning apaḥ, apnaḥ (Ni. 3-1), śamībhiḥ means by acts such as sacrifice. The sentence śamībhir yajñam āśata used in this ṛk has several senses. The Ṛbhu deities pervade the sacrifice by their acts, that is, by their works of craft, or by acts that give the sacrificer his wishes; that is, they come to the place of sacrifice. Or, being pleased by the acts such as the giving of oblations that the sacrificer makes to the Ṛbhu deities in the sacrifice, they accept the oblation: the sense can be given in various ways. The chief intent is that these Ṛbhus, by their skill in craft, not only make the means and materials needed for the sacrifice so that the sacrifice is completed with all its parts, but, pleased by the giving of oblations the sacrificer makes in the sacrifice, give the fruit of the sacrifice, and so on.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 7–8, noted briefly

वचोयुजा (vacoyujā): the analysis is vacasā yuñjāte. After the root yujir yoge, with the instrumental-singular word vacas as upapada, by the sūtra "satsūdviṣa…" (Pā. sū. 3-2-61) the suffix kvip; after it the accusative dual suffix au; for it, by "supāṃ suluk" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39), the substitute ā. This is unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4). The u of yuj is udātta by "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-162). After compounding too, by "gatikārako…" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139), the accent of the kṛt final member comes, so that accent stays. By "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-66) the case-ending substitute becomes svarita.

ततक्षुः (tatakṣuḥ): the root takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe. After it liṭ, the 3rd plural substitute jhi; for it, by "parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus…" (Pā. sū. 3-4-82), the substitute us;

Page 8 — Rik 2: grammar (end)

doubling and the other operations: tatakṣuḥ. It stands at the start of the second pāda. Since the bar "apādādau" (Pā. sū. 8-1-18) comes, it is not wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28).

शमीभिः (śamībhiḥ): śamayanti pāpāni iti śamyaḥ, karmāṇi: acts that remove sins are denoted by the word śamī. The root śamu upaśame. By "sarvadhātubhya in" (Uṇ. sū. "4-5-57", zoom-checked: the last glyph has the open top and flat foot of the 7) the suffix in. If the feminine is meant, by "kṛdikārād aktinaḥ" (Pā. sū. 4-1-45 ga.), when the feminine is meant, ṅīṣ comes after a stem ending in an i belonging to a kṛt suffix; but after a stem ending in ktin ṅīṣ does not come: this is the sense of the gaṇa-sūtra. Here the Uṇādi suffix in is a kṛt; since the word śami ends in the i belonging to the suffix in, ṅīṣ comes after it. By "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148) the i belonging to the kṛt drops. Though final udātta would come by the suffix accent, since it is in the vṛṣa-ādi, by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-203) it is initial udātta.

आशत (āśata): the root aśū vyāptau. After it laṅ, the ātmanepada 3rd plural substitute jha. This is a root of the sv-ādi group; so by "svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-73) the vikaraṇa śnu comes: aś + nu + jha; for the vikaraṇa, by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-73), luk. By "āḍ ajādīnām" (Pā. sū. 6-4-72) the augment āṭ; by "āṭaś ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-90) vṛddhi. By "ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-5) the substitute at for the jh: āśata. By "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28) it is wholly unaccented.

॥२॥

Page 8 (lower) — Sūkta 20, Rik 3

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तक्ष॒न्नास॑त्याभ्यां॒ परि॑ज्मानं सु॒खं रथ॑म् । तक्ष॑न्धे॒नुं स॑ब॒र्दुघा॑म् ॥३॥

takṣan nā́satyābhyāṃ párijmānaṃ sukháṃ rátham | tákṣan dhenúṃ sabardúghām ||3||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तक्षन् । नासत्याभ्याम् । परिऽज्मानम् । सुऽखम् । रथम् ॥ तक्षन् । धेनुम् । सबःऽदुघाम् ॥३॥

takṣan | nāsatyābhyām | pari 'jmānam | su 'kham | ratham || takṣan | dhenum | sabaḥ 'dughām ||3||

Page 9 — Rik 3: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

नासत्याभ्यामश्विदेवप्रीत्यर्थं रथं तक्षन् । ऋभवो देवाः कंचिद्रथमतक्षन् । तक्षणेन संपादितवन्तः । कीदृशम् । परिज्मानं परितो गन्तारं सुखं उपर्युपवेशने सुखकरम् । किं च धेनुं कांचिद्गां तक्षन् । धातूनामनेकार्थत्वात्तक्षतिरत्र संपादनवाची । कीदृशीं धेनुम् । सबर्दुघां सबरः क्षीरस्य दोग्ध्रीम् ॥ तक्षन् । बहुलं छन्दसीत्यडभावः । नासत्याभ्याम् । न विद्यते सत्यं ययोस्तावसत्यौ । न असत्यौ नासत्यौ । नभ्राण्नपादित्यादिना नलोपाभावः । परिज्मानम् । अजेः परिपूर्वस्य श्वन्नुक्षन्नित्यादिना । उ. १-१५८ । मन्प्रत्ययेऽकारलोपे आद्युदात्तत्वं च निपातनात् । सबर्दुघाम् । सबः पयो दोग्धीति सबर्दुघा । दुहः कब्घश्च । पा. ३-२-७० । इति कप् । सबरिति रेफान्तं प्रातिपदिकं क्षीरवाचीति संप्रदायविदः । कपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

nāsatyābhyāmaśvidevaprītyarthaṃ rathaṃ takṣan | ṛbhavo devāḥ kaṃcidrathamatakṣan | takṣaṇena saṃpāditavantaḥ | kīdṛśam | parijmānaṃ parito gantāraṃ sukhaṃ uparyupaveśane sukhakaram | kiṃ ca dhenuṃ kāṃcidgāṃ takṣan | dhātūnāmanekārthatvāttakṣatiratra saṃpādanavācī | kīdṛśīṃ dhenum | sabardughāṃ sabaraḥ kṣīrasya dogdhrīm || takṣan | bahulaṃ chandasītyaḍabhāvaḥ | nāsatyābhyām | na vidyate satyaṃ yayostāvasatyau | na asatyau nāsatyau | nabhrāṇnapādityādinā nalopābhāvaḥ | parijmānam | ajeḥ paripūrvasya śvannukṣannityādinā | u. 1-158 | manpratyaye 'kāralope ādyudāttatvaṃ ca nipātanāt | sabardughām | sabaḥ payo dogdhīti sabardughā | duhaḥ kabghaśca | pā. 3-2-70 | iti kap | sabariti rephāntaṃ prātipadikaṃ kṣīravācīti saṃpradāyavidaḥ | kapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | dhātusvara eva śiṣyate | samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaraḥ ||

Translation: "For the Nāsatyas, for the pleasure of the Aśvin gods, takṣan, they fashioned, a chariot: the Ṛbhu gods fashioned a certain chariot, produced it by carving. Of what kind? Parijman, going around, sukha, pleasant for those who sit on it. And they fashioned a dhenu, a certain cow: since roots have many senses, takṣ here means producing. Of what kind is the cow? Sabardughā, the milker of sabar, milk." (Grammatical tail: takṣan, no augment aṭ by bahulaṃ chandasi; nāsatyābhyām, "they in whom there is no truth are asatyau; not asatya, nāsatyau", no loss of n by nabhrāṇnapāt…; parijmānam, after aj with pari by śvann ukṣan… (Uṇ. 1-158), with the suffix man the loss of a and initial udātta are given ready-made; sabardughām, "she milks sabar, milk", kap by duhaḥ kab ghaś ca (Pā. 3-2-70); those who know the tradition say sabar is an r-final stem meaning milk; kap unaccented as pit, the root accent alone stays, and in the compound the accent of the kṛt final member.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

नासत्याभ्याम् (nāsatyābhyām) — for the Aśvin deities | परिज्मानम् (parijmānam) — going everywhere (able to move in all directions) | सुखम् (sukham) — pleasant (to sit in) | रथम् (ratham) — a chariot (these Ṛbhus) | तक्षन् (takṣan) — made at once and gave | (and) सबर्दुघाम् (sabardughām) — giving milk | धेनुम् (dhenum) — a cow too | तक्षन् (takṣan) — produced and gave.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

These Ṛbhu deities by their power produced and gave to the Aśvin deities a pleasant chariot able to move everywhere, and a cow that gives good milk.

॥ English Translation ॥

They constructed for the Nasatyas, an easy-moving chariot which is capable of moving everywhere, and a cow that gives milk.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

As said in the previous ṛk, in this ṛk too and in the following ṛks the extraordinary works of craft done by the Ṛbhu deities are described.

Takṣan: atakṣan. To suit the metre the a of the verb atakṣan is dropped and only takṣan is used. Atakṣan means "they produced, they made"; "built,

Page 10 — Rik 3: Special Topics (end) and grammar

made, chipped, fabricated, fashioned, constructed, carved" [as printed] and other senses may be given. The intent is that, unlike in the previous ṛk where they made the chariot by mental resolve, here they carved and built the chariot with tools, according to the craft-śāstra.

Nāsatyābhyām: na asatyau nāsatyau (nāsatyā): because they are not speakers of untrue words, the Aśvin deities are named nāsatyau or nāsatyā. These Aśvin deities are two; though there is a usage calling one Nāsatya and the other Dasra, there is a usage of using the word nāsatyā for both. So here nāsatyābhyām means aśvinoḥ, for the Aśvin deities. Though nāsatyābhyām is used here in the ablative, it may be taken in the sense of the ablative or of the genitive.

Parijmānam:

परितो गन्तारम्

parito gantāram

("Going around.") Able to move anywhere, that is, able to go in regions such as earth, sky and ocean. This word qualifies the word ratham.

Sukham: pleasant, "easy-moving" [as printed]: the intent is that it can move without tiring or jolting those sitting in the chariot, or that it is made ready with soft seats and the like.

Dhenum: gām, a cow. Generally in the Ṛgveda the word dhenu is used in the sense of a cow that gives milk.

Takṣan: here too the intent is atakṣan. Here a doubt arises: since takṣan means "made, built", is it not impossible to build a cow with tools? So it is fitting that the commentator gave here the sense saṃpāditavantaḥ, "they procured", for the word takṣan.

Sabardughām:

सबरः क्षीरस्य दोग्ध्रीम् । अमृतस्य दोग्ध्रीम् ।

sabaraḥ kṣīrasya dogdhrīm | amṛtasya dogdhrīm |

("The milker of sabar, milk; the milker of nectar.") The intent is: a cow that gives or yields milk, which is called nectar, "the cow that yields milk or ambrosia" [as printed].

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 10–13, noted briefly

तक्षन् (takṣan): the root takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe. Since roots have many senses, here the sense "producing" is meant for takṣ. After it laṅ, the 3rd plural substitute jhi. If the sense tanūkaraṇa were meant, by "tanūkaraṇe takṣaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-76), before a sārvadhātuka in the agent sense, the vikaraṇa śnu would come after takṣ in the sense of paring,

Page 11 — Rik 3: grammar

so the vikaraṇa śnu would be due. But since here the sense "producing" is meant, the vikaraṇa śap comes after this root of the bhv-ādi group: takṣ + a + jhi. By "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-3) ant for the jh; by "itaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-100) the i drops; by "saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-23) the t at the end of the conjunct nt drops; by "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. sū. 8-2-1) the loss of the conjunct final is asiddha when the loss of n is to be made; so the loss of n by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Sā. sū. "4-2-7" [as printed, for Pā. 8-2-7]) does not come. The a of the vikaraṇa and the a of the suffix take the pararūpa. Though the augment aṭ is due by "luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-71), by "bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi" (Pā. sū. 6-4-75), in the Veda, with or without māṅ, the augments aṭ and āṭ come variously. The sense of bahula was explained before. So here the augment aṭ does not come: takṣan.

नासत्याभ्याम् (nāsatyābhyām): na vidyate satyaṃ yayoḥ tau asatyau: those two in whom there is no truth are called asatyau. Na asatyau: different from those who have no truth: that is the sense. In this compound, though the loss of n is due by "nalopo nañaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-3-73), since by "nabhrāṇnapānnavedānāsatyā…" (Pā. sū. 6-3-75) the nañ of the words named in this sūtra keeps its form, the n does not drop. Lengthening of like vowels: nāsatyā.

परिज्मानम् (parijmānam): the root aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ. After this root preceded by the preverb pari, by

श्वन्नुक्षन्पूषन्प्लीहन्क्लेदन्स्नेहन्मूर्धन्मज्जन्नर्यमन्विश्वप्सन्परिज्मन्मातरिश्वन्मघवन्निति (उ. सू. १-१५७)

śvannukṣanpūṣanplīhankledansnehanmūrdhanmajjannaryamanviśvapsanparijmanmātariśvanmaghavanniti (u. sū. 1-157)

(the sūtra number "1-157" as printed here; the bhāṣya gives 1-158) these thirteen words are given ready-made as ending in the suffix kani. Śvan: after the root ṭuo śvi gativṛddhyoḥ the suffix kani comes, and since this sūtra gives the loss of i ready-made, with the loss of i it is established. Ukṣan: the suffix kani after the root ukṣa secane. Pūṣan: after the root pūṣa vṛddhau, kani. Plīhan: the root pliha gatau, after it kani; since this sūtra gives it ready-made, the i in the penultimate is lengthened. Kledan: the root klidū ārdrībhāve, the suffix kani; by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-86) guṇa e for the penultimate i. Sneha: the root ṣṇiha prītau, kani, then the laghūpadha-guṇa. Mūrdhan: the root muha vaicittye; after it kani, the penultimate u lengthened,

Page 12 — Rik 3: grammar

dh for h, and the augment r (ram) after the ū: these come by the ready-made form. The analysis here is muhyanti asmin āhate. Majjan: the root ṭumasjo śuddhau; after it kani: masj + an. For the s, by "stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-40), ś; for that, by "jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi" (Pā. sū. 8-4-53), j: since by "icuyaśānāṃ tālu" ś too is palatal, in its place comes the palatal j that is part of the pratyāhāra jaś: majjan. This is n-final; following the two-form lexicon

ऊष्मया सार्धमूष्मापि मज्जोक्तो मज्जया सह

ūṣmayā sārdhamūṣmāpi majjokto majjayā saha

("Ūṣman together with ūṣmā; majjan is said together with majjā"), they also accept the word majjā as ending in ṭāp. Aryaman: after the root māṅ māne preceded by the word arya, kani; aryamā + an; by "āto lopa iṭi ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-64) the loss of ā: aryaman. When the nominative singular su is added after it, though the penultimate lengthening that would come by "sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-8) is withdrawn by "inhanpūṣāryamṇāṃ śau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-12), by "sau ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-13), when the suffix su follows, the penultimate of a stem ending in in, of han, pūṣan and aryaman is lengthened; so the penultimate is lengthened; by "halṅyābbhyaḥ…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-68) the loss of su; by "nalopaḥ prā…" (Pā. sū. 8-2-7) the loss of n: aryamā. Viśvapsan: the root psā bhakṣaṇe; viśvaṃ psāti iti viśvapsā, meaning Agni. After the root psā, with the word viśva as upapada, kani; by "āto lopa iṭi ca" the loss of ā. Parijman: pari jāyate iti parijmā. The senses moon and Agni are conveyed by this word. After the root janī prādurbhāve preceded by pari, kani; here by the ready-made form the loss of the a of the root jan and the substitute m for the n come: parij + m + an: so the grammarians explain. In the manner of the Vedabhāṣya the derivation is made here in another way. After the root aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ preceded by the preverb pari, by the sūtra "śvannukṣan…" the suffix man: pari + aj + man; by the ready-made form the a of the root drops: parijman. The suffix man is not nit, so there is no scope for initial udātta by "ñnityādir nityam"; final udātta by the suffix accent would be due. But in this very sūtra initial udātta too is given ready-made. So parijman, though ending in the suffix man, is initial udātta. At "ataḥ parijmann ā gahi" (Ṛ. saṃ. sū. 6, ṛ. 9) the Vedabhāṣyakāra, by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate" (Pā. sū. 3-2-75), describes the suffix manin after the root aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ preceded by pari, with the loss of a as a Vedic form, giving parijman, and says this is initial udātta by the nit accent (page "75", zoom-checked: flat-footed 7, lobed 5). Ujjvaladatta, reading parijvan in the sūtra, after the sautra root ju preceded by pari, kani: pariju +

Page 13 — Rik 3: grammar (end)

an, the substitute yaṇ: parijvan, meaning the moon, he explains. But since such usage is not found, this derivation is not fitting. After parijman the accusative singular am: when it comes, the penultimate is lengthened by "sarvanāmasthāne…" (Pā. sū. 6-4-8): parijmānam. Mātariśvan: mātari, in the sky, śvayati, it goes: the analysis gives mātariśvā. With the locative-final mātari as upapada, after the root ṭuo śvi gativṛddhyoḥ, kani; by the ready-made form the i of the root drops; by the ready-made form too the luk due by "supo dhātu…" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71) does not come for the locative in mātari: mātariśvan. In the sūtra "śvayuvamaghonām ataddhite" (Pā. sū. 6-4-133) the word śva takes in śvan meaning dog, and words ending in śvan meaning dog; in mātariśvan the śvan does not mean dog, so when vowel-initial endings such as śas are added, there is no saṃprasāraṇa in mātariśvan: only forms such as mātariśvanaḥ, mātariśvanā result. Maghavan: the root maha pūjāyām; here the suffix kani, gh for the h, and the augment avuk for the root are given ready-made: maghavan. In the sūtra the word iti means "and so on". So, according to usage, the suffix kani may come after other roots too. In the daśapādī this word iti is not read.

सबर्दुघाम् (sabardughām): sabaḥ, milk; dogdhi, milks: such is the analysis; sabardughā results. Those who know the tradition hold that sabar is an r-final stem conveying the sense milk. By "duhaḥ kab ghaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-70), with a subanta as upapada, after the root duha prapūraṇe the suffix kap and gh for the h come; so after the root duh with the subanta sabaḥ as upapada, with the suffix kap and gh for h, sabardugha results. The suffix kap is pit; so by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4) it is unaccented; by "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-162) the u is udātta; after compounding with the subanta sabaḥ by "upapadam atiṅ" (Pā. sū. 2-2-19), by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139) the accent of the kṛt final member comes, and the root's udātta stays. If the feminine is meant, by "ajādyataṣ ṭāp" (Pā. sū. 4-1-4) ṭāp; lengthening of like vowels with ṭāp; this ā is unaccented by "sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-50); it becomes svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-66); the letter before the udātta u of the root is anudātta by "udāttasvaritaparasya sannataraḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-2-40).

॥३॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

युवा॑ना पि॒तरा॒ पुनः॑ स॒त्यम॑न्त्रा ऋजू॒यवः॑ । ऋ॒भवो॑ वि॒ष्ट्य॑क्रत ॥४॥

yúvānā pitárā púnaḥ satyámantrā ṛjūyávaḥ | ṛbhávo viṣṭyakrata ||4||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

युवाना । पितरा । पुनरिति । सत्यऽमन्त्राः । ऋजुऽयवः ॥ ऋभवः । विष्टी । अक्रत ॥४॥

yuvānā | pitarā | punariti | satya 'mantrāḥ | ṛju 'yavaḥ || ṛbhavaḥ | viṣṭī | akrata ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ वर्तेन is as printed twice in the Nirukta quotation; the Special Topics, p. 16, print ऋतेन. The Nirukta number is printed ११-१५.

द्वितीये छन्दोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे युवाना पितरा पुनरित्यार्भवस्तृचः । द्वितीयस्याग्निं वो देवमिति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नो युवाना पितरा पुनरिति तृचौ ॥ आ. ८-१० । इति ॥

dvitīye chandome vaiśvadevaśastre yuvānā pitarā punarityārbhavastṛcaḥ | dvitīyasyāgniṃ vo devamiti khaṇḍe sūtritam | mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca no yuvānā pitarā punariti tṛcau || ā. 8-10 | iti ||

ऋभव एतन्नामका देवाः पितरौ स्वकीयौ मातापितरौ पूर्वं वृद्धावपि पुनर्युवाना तरुणावक्रत । कृतवन्तः । कीदृशाः । सत्यमन्त्रा अवितथमन्त्रसामर्थ्योपेताः । पुरश्चरणाद्यनुष्ठानेन सिद्धमन्त्रत्वाद्यद्यत्फलमुद्दिश्य मन्त्राः प्रयुज्यन्ते तत्तत्फलं तथैव संपद्यते । तस्माज्जीर्णयोः पित्रोर्युवत्वं संपादयितुं समर्था इत्यर्थः । ऋजूयव ऋजुतामात्मन इच्छन्तः । छलरहिता इत्यर्थः । अत एवैतेषामनुष्ठिता मन्त्राः सिध्यन्ति । विष्टी विष्टयो व्याप्तियुक्ताः । सर्वेषु कार्येष्वेतदीयस्य मन्त्रसामर्थ्यस्याप्रतिघातोऽत्र व्याप्तिरुच्यते । ऋभुशब्दं यास्क एवं निर्वक्ति । ऋभव उरु भान्तीति वर्तेन भान्तीति वर्तेन भवन्तीति वा । नि. ११-१५ । इति ॥ युवाना । युवन्शब्दो यौतेः कनिनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेराकारः । पितरा । पूर्ववदाकारः । सत्यमन्त्राः बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । ऋजुशब्दो भावपरः । ऋजुत्वमात्मन इच्छन्ति । क्यच् । अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोर्दीर्घः । पा. ७-४-२५ । इति दीर्घः । क्याच्छन्दसीत्युप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । विष्टी । विष्लृ व्याप्तौ ।

ṛbhava etannāmakā devāḥ pitarau svakīyau mātāpitarau pūrvaṃ vṛddhāvapi punaryuvānā taruṇāvakrata | kṛtavantaḥ | kīdṛśāḥ | satyamantrā avitathamantrasāmarthyopetāḥ | puraścaraṇādyanuṣṭhānena siddhamantratvādyadyatphalamuddiśya mantrāḥ prayujyante tattatphalaṃ tathaiva saṃpadyate | tasmājjīrṇayoḥ pitroryuvatvaṃ saṃpādayituṃ samarthā ityarthaḥ | ṛjūyava ṛjutāmātmana icchantaḥ | chalarahitā ityarthaḥ | ata evaiteṣāmanuṣṭhitā mantrāḥ sidhyanti | viṣṭī viṣṭayo vyāptiyuktāḥ | sarveṣu kāryeṣvetadīyasya mantrasāmarthyasyāpratighāto 'tra vyāptirucyate | ṛbhuśabdaṃ yāska evaṃ nirvakti | ṛbhava uru bhāntīti vartena bhāntīti vartena bhavantīti vā | ni. 11-15 | iti || yuvānā | yuvanśabdo yauteḥ kaninanto nittvādādyudāttaḥ | supāṃ sulugityādinā vibhakterākāraḥ | pitarā | pūrvavadākāraḥ | satyamantrāḥ bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaraḥ | ṛjuśabdo bhāvaparaḥ | ṛjutvamātmana icchanti | kyac | akṛtsārvadhātukayordīrghaḥ | pā. 7-4-25 | iti dīrghaḥ | kyācchandasītyupratyayaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | viṣṭī | viṣlṛ vyāptau |

क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायामिति क्तिच् । तितुत्रेत्यादिनेट्प्रतिबन्धः । तस्माज्जस इयाडियाजीकाराणामुपसंख्यानम् । पा. ७-१-३९-१ । इति तस्येकारादेशः । स चालोऽन्त्यस्य । पा. १-१-५२ । इति सकारस्य भवति । तत्र आद्गुण इति गुणे कृते प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः । पा. ६-१-१०२ । इति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः । तं बाधित्वा परत्वाज्जसि च । पा. ७-३-१०९ । इति ह्रस्वस्य गुणेन भवितव्यमिति चेन्न । संज्ञापूर्वकस्य विधेरनित्यत्वात् । अक्रत । कृञो लुङ् । आत्मनेपदम् । झस्यादादेशः । मन्त्रे घसेत्यादिना । पा. २-४-८० । च्लेर्लुक् । यणादेशः । अडागमः । निघातः ॥

kticktau ca saṃjñāyāmiti ktic | titutretyādineṭpratibandhaḥ | tasmājjasa iyāḍiyājīkārāṇāmupasaṃkhyānam | pā. 7-1-39-1 | iti tasyekārādeśaḥ | sa cālo 'ntyasya | pā. 1-1-52 | iti sakārasya bhavati | tatra ādguṇa iti guṇe kṛte prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ | pā. 6-1-102 | iti pūrvasavarṇadīrghaḥ | taṃ bādhitvā paratvājjasi ca | pā. 7-3-109 | iti hrasvasya guṇena bhavitavyamiti cenna | saṃjñāpūrvakasya vidheranityatvāt | akrata | kṛño luṅ | ātmanepadam | jhasyādādeśaḥ | mantre ghasetyādinā | pā. 2-4-80 | clerluk | yaṇādeśaḥ | aḍāgamaḥ | nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "In the second chandoma, at the vaiśvadeva-śastra, the tṛca to the Ṛbhus is yuvānā pitarā punaḥ. So it is laid down in the section of the second agniṃ vo devam: 'mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ and yuvānā pitarā punaḥ: two tṛcas' (Āśv. 8-10). The Ṛbhus, gods of that name, akrata, made, their pitarau, their own mother and father, who were old before, yuvānā, young punaḥ, again. Of what kind? Satyamantrāḥ, endowed with the power of mantras that never fail: because their mantras are perfected by performing puraścaraṇa and the like, whatever fruit the mantras are used for, that very fruit comes about; so they are able to make their aged parents young again. Ṛjūyavaḥ, desiring straightness for themselves: free of deceit; that is why the mantras they perform succeed. Viṣṭī, possessed of pervasion: here pervasion means that the power of their mantras meets with no obstacle in any undertaking. Yāska derives the word ṛbhu thus: 'the Ṛbhus shine widely, or shine varta, or are varta' (Ni. 11-15)." (Grammatical tail: yuvānā, yuvan from yu with kanin, initial udātta as nit, ā for the ending by supāṃ suluk…; pitarā, ā as before; satyamantrāḥ, a bahuvrīhi, the first member's accent; ṛju here denotes the quality: "they want straightness for themselves", kyac, lengthening by akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ (Pā. 7-4-25), the suffix u by kyāc chandasi, the suffix accent; viṣṭī, viṣḷ vyāptau, ktic by kticktau ca saṃjñāyām, no iṭ by titutra…; for its jas the ī by the statement iyāḍiyājīkārāṇām upasaṃkhyānam (Pā. 7-1-39-1), coming for the s by alo 'ntyasya (Pā. 1-1-52); when guṇa is made by ād guṇaḥ, the lengthening by prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ (Pā. 6-1-102); if it is said that, overriding it, the short vowel should take guṇa by jasi ca (Pā. 7-3-109) as later, no, since a rule stated with a technical name is not nitya; akrata, luṅ of kṛñ, ātmanepada, at for jha, luk of cli by mantre ghasa… (Pā. 2-4-80), yaṇ, the augment aṭ, wholly unaccented.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सत्यमन्त्राः (satyamantrāḥ) — possessed of true mantras | ऋजूयवः (ṛjūyavaḥ) — wishing to stay on the straight path | विष्टी (viṣṭī) — possessed of pervasion (by the power of mantras) | ऋभवः (ṛbhavaḥ) — the deities named Ṛbhus | पितरा (pitarā) — (their aged) parents | पुनः (punaḥ) — again | युवाना (yuvānā) — young | अक्रत (akrata) — made.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The Ṛbhus walk only in the good path. So their mantras never go in vain; they always bear fruit. By such power of their mantras they made their aged parents youthful (young).

॥ English Translation ॥

The honest Ribhus repeating true prayers made (their) parents young again by their skilful acts encountering no opposition through their infallible mantras.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

At the time of reciting the vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras, when the mantras to the Ṛbhu deities are recited, this mantra is recited as the second chandoma mantra. This is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, in the section dvitīyasyāgniṃ vo devam, in the sūtra mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca no yuvānā pitarā punar iti tṛcau (Ā. 8-10).

Yuvānā: yuvānau: youthful, in the age of youth, not in old age.

Page 16 — Rik 4: Special Topics

Pitarā:

स्वकीयौ मातापितरौ

svakīyau mātāpitarau

("Their own mother and father.") Their aged parents.

Punaḥ: again, as they were before in the age of youth.

Satyamantrāḥ:

अवितथमन्त्रसामर्थ्योपेताः । पुरश्चरणाद्यनुष्ठानेन सिद्धमन्त्रत्वाद्यद्यत्फलमुद्दिश्य मन्त्राः प्रयुज्यन्ते तत्तत्फलं तथैव संपद्यते ॥

avitathamantrasāmarthyopetāḥ | puraścaraṇādyanuṣṭhānena siddhamantratvādyadyatphalamuddiśya mantrāḥ prayujyante tattatphalaṃ tathaiva saṃpadyate ||

("Endowed with the power of mantras that never fail; because their mantras are perfected by performing puraścaraṇa and the like, whatever fruit the mantras are used for, that very fruit comes about.") They have gained mastery of the mantras by reciting them with rites such as puraścaraṇa. The intent is that if such men recite a mantra for any intended fruit, that fruit is surely obtained.

Ṛjūyavaḥ:

ऋजुकामाः । ऋजुतामात्मन इच्छन्तः

ṛjukāmāḥ | ṛjutāmātmana icchantaḥ

("Desiring straightness; wishing straightness for themselves.") Those who follow justice or the true path, or who wish to become promoters of the true path.

Ṛbhavaḥ: for the word ṛbhu Yāska gives three kinds of derivation:

ऋभव उरु भान्तीति वा ।

ṛbhava uru bhāntīti vā |

("The Ṛbhus shine widely.") Uru, much; bhānti, they shine: so they are named Ṛbhus. Some think the word rubhu or ṛbhu is formed by joining the last letter ru of uru with the first letter of bhānti, as in ahaḥ + rātriḥ = horā.

ऋतेन भान्तीति वा ।

ṛtena bhāntīti vā |

("They shine by ṛta.") Because they shine by ṛta, that is, by truth or by sacrifice, they are named Ṛbhus.

ऋतेन भवन्तीति वा ।

ṛtena bhavantīti vā |

("They are by ṛta.") Because they exist by ṛta, that is, by truth (by power), that is, they are possessed of power, they are named Ṛbhus. Some say that the first letter ṛ of ṛtena and the first letter bh of bhavanti join to give ṛbhu.

Viṣṭī: viṣṭvī. Since the word viṣṭvī is read among the twenty-six names for action beginning apaḥ, apnaḥ (Ni. 3-1), it means action. To suit the metre the v of viṣṭvī is dropped and it is written viṣṭī. For this word the commentator gives the sense vyāptiyuktāḥ, possessed of pervasion. Pervasion means

सर्वेषु कार्येष्वेतदीयस्य मन्त्रसामर्थ्यस्याप्रतिघातोऽत्र व्याप्तिरुच्यते

sarveṣu kāryeṣvetadīyasya mantrasāmarthyasyāpratighāto 'tra vyāptirucyate

("Here pervasion means that the power of their mantras meets with no obstacle in any undertaking.") The sense is: in all undertakings they are unobstructed by the power of their mantras.

This ṛk makes clear the matter that these Ṛbhus were men formerly and later attained divinity:

Page 17 — Rik 4: Special Topics

विष्ट्वी शमी तरणित्वेन वाघतो मर्तासः सन्तो अमृतत्वमानशुः । सौधन्वना ऋभवः सूरचक्षसः संवत्सरे समपृच्यन्त धीतिभिः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११०-४)

viṣṭvī śamī taraṇitvena vāghato martāsaḥ santo amṛtatvamānaśuḥ | saudhanvanā ṛbhavaḥ sūracakṣasaḥ saṃvatsare samapṛcyanta dhītibhiḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-110-4)

("Having done the acts, the bearers, though mortals, by swiftness attained immortality; the sons of Sudhanvan, the Ṛbhus, sun-eyed, were joined in a year with the rites": editorial and tentative.) Yāska's Nirukta on it:

कृत्वा कर्माणि क्षिप्रत्वेन वोढारो मेधाविनो वा मर्तासः सन्तोऽमृतत्वमानशिरे ऋभवः सूरख्याना वा सूरप्रज्ञा वा संवत्सरे समपृच्यन्त धीतिभिः कर्मभिः ॥

kṛtvā karmāṇi kṣipratvena voḍhāro medhāvino vā martāsaḥ santo 'mṛtatvamānaśire ṛbhavaḥ sūrakhyānā vā sūraprajñā vā saṃvatsare samapṛcyanta dhītibhiḥ karmabhiḥ ||

("Having done the acts quickly, the bearers or the wise, though mortals, attained immortality, the Ṛbhus, sun-famed or sun-wise; in a year they were joined with the dhītis, the acts": editorial and tentative.) The chief intent is: these Ṛbhus, the sons of Sudhanvan, were men formerly. By their wisdom or intelligence, equal to the sun's, they performed all the sacrifices quickly, that is, in a single year, and attained amṛtatvam, divinity (freedom from death).

Yāska gives another sense too for the word ṛbhu:

Ādityaraśmayo 'py ṛbhava ucyante: the sun's rays too are called ṛbhavaḥ. For example:

उद्वत्स्वस्मा अकृणोतना तृणं निवत्स्वपः स्वपस्यया नरः । अगोह्यस्य यदसस्तना गृहे तदद्येदमृभवो नानु गच्छथ ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१६१-११)

udvatsvasmā akṛṇotanā tṛṇaṃ nivatsvapaḥ svapasyayā naraḥ | agohyasya yadasastanā gṛhe tadadyedamṛbhavo nānu gacchatha || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-161-11)

("For him on the heights you made grass, on the depths waters, by your good work, O men; when you slept in the house of the one not to be hidden, today you do not go after this, O Ṛbhus": editorial and tentative.) For this ṛk Yāska gives the Nirukta

अगोह्य आदित्योऽगूहनीयस्तस्य यदस्वपथ गृहे यावत्तत्र भवथ न तावदिह भवथेति ॥

agohya ādityo 'gūhanīyastasya yadasvapatha gṛhe yāvattatra bhavatha na tāvadiha bhavatheti ||

("The one not to be hidden is the sun, who is not to be concealed; as long as you sleep in his house, so long you are not here": editorial and tentative.) The commentator too, explaining the sense of this ṛk, gave for the word ṛbhavaḥ

ऋभवः उरु प्रभूतं भासमानाः ऋतेनादित्येन भासमाना वा ऋतेनोदकेनोदकार्थमुत्पन्ना वा

ṛbhavaḥ uru prabhūtaṃ bhāsamānāḥ ṛtenādityena bhāsamānā vā ṛtenodakenodakārthamutpannā vā

("The Ṛbhus: shining abundantly, or shining by ṛta, the sun, or born by ṛta, water, for the sake of water.")

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 17–19, noted briefly

युवाना (yuvānā): the root yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ. By "kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "1-154" [?]), after the roots yu miśraṇe, vṛṣu secane, takṣū tanūkaraṇe, rājṛ dīptau, dhanvi gatau, dyu abhigamane and divu krīḍādau, the suffix kanin comes; so after the root yu the suffix kanin. Yu + an: by "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-77) the substitute uvaṅ: yuvan. After it, for the accusative dual suffix auṭ, by the sūtra "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39) the substitute ā: yuvānā. By the nit accent the word yuvan is initial udātta.

Page 18 — Rik 4: grammar

पितरा (pitarā): as before, here too the substitute ā for the ending.

सत्यमन्त्राः (satyamantrāḥ): the word satya is final udātta. Satyāḥ, not in vain; mantrāḥ, powers of mantra; yeṣāṃ te, those who have them are satyamantrāḥ: a bahuvrīhi; by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1) the accent of the first member comes.

ऋजूयवः (ṛjūyavaḥ): in ṛju a statement with the quality as chief is intended; the sense is ṛjutva, straightness. When ṛjutvam ātmanaḥ icchanti is meant, by "supa ātmanaḥ kyac" (Pā. sū. 3-1-8) (after a subanta denoting the object, the thing that the one who wishes wishes for his own benefit, the suffix kyac comes optionally in the sense of wishing: such is the sense of the sūtra), kyac comes after the subanta ṛju denoting the object; for the suffix am, by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71), luk: ṛjuya. Now by "akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-25), when a y-initial suffix other than a kṛt or sārvadhātuka follows, a vowel-final aṅga is lengthened. Now by "kyāc chandasi" (Pā. sū. 3-2-170) (kya is a general taking of the three suffixes kyac, kyaṣ, kyaṅ; after a root ending in the suffix kya, in the Veda, in senses such as tācchīlya, the suffix u comes: such is the sense of the sūtra), so when the suffix u comes, ṛjūya + u; by "ato lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-48) the loss of a: ṛjūyu. The suffix accent comes; in the nominative plural, ṛjūyavaḥ.

विष्टी (viṣṭī): viṣḷ vyāptau. By "kticktau ca saṃjñāyām" (Pā. sū. 3-3-174), when a blessing is meant and a name is to be expressed, the suffixes ktic and kta come after the root: so the suffix ktic. Viṣ + ti: here the augment iṭ would be due for ti by "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-35); but since by "titutratathasisusarakaseṣu ca" (Pā. sū. 7-2-9) these ten kṛt suffixes do not take the augment iṭ, the bar comes, so iṭ does not come. By "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-41) ṭ for the t. After the word viṣṭi the ending jas is added. For it, by "iyāḍiyājīkārāṇām upasaṃkhyānam" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39 vā. 1), the three substitutes iyā, ḍiyāc and ī come for a sup; so here the substitute ī. By "alo 'ntyasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-52), what is enjoined naming a word in the sixth case comes to the last letter of the word denoted by the sixth: so it comes for the s, the last letter of jas. Viṣṭi + a + ī. By "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-87) guṇa: viṣṭi + e. By "prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-102), when the vowel of a nominative or accusative ending follows after a, i, u, ṛ, ḷ,

Page 19 — Rik 4: grammar (end)

in place of the former and latter the lengthening of the former like vowel comes as a single substitute: so for i + e the former-like lengthening gives viṣṭī. But when jas follows, besides the lengthening, guṇa is also due by "jasi ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-109), guṇa coming after an aṅga ending in a short ik before jas. By rule, by "vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam" (Pā. sū. 1-4-2), guṇa alone should come; yet by "saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ" (paribhāṣā "95", zoom-checked: the 9-glyph then the lobed 5) the guṇa rule, stated with the technical names short and guṇa, is not nitya, so it does not come. Here, even without justifying the application of the guṇas ī substitute and ād guṇaḥ, in the way stated before, since the guṇa-enjoining jasi ca is not nitya, it does not apply. If it is said that the former-like lengthening comes, the visarga would have to be heard: viṣṭīḥ.

अक्रत (akrata): the root ḍukṛñ karaṇe. Luṅ: kṛ + luṅ; by "cli luṅi" (Pā. sū. 3-1-43) cli comes. The c is called it and dropped; li remains. For it, by "mantre ghasahvaraṇaśavṛdahādvṛckṛgamijanibhyo leḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-80): ghasḷ substituted for the root ad, and hvṛ kauṭilye, with guṇa and the a for pronunciation, as hvara, are mentioned; ṇaśa adarśane; vṛ, by its mention without indicatory letters, takes both vṛñ varaṇe and vṛṅ saṃbhaktau; daha bhasmīkaraṇe; by āt, the ā-final roots such as prā pūraṇe are mentioned; vṛjī varjane, ḍukṛñ karaṇe, gamḷ gatau, janī prādurbhāve: after these, for the li, in the mantra, luk comes; so luk comes. Kṛ + luṅ: for the luṅ, the ātmanepada 3rd plural jha. Kṛ + jha: by "ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-5) at for the jh. Kṛ + ata: by "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-77) the substitute yaṇ; by "luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-71) the augment aṭ: akrata. By "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28) wholly unaccented.

॥४॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सं वो॒ मदा॑सो अग्म॒तेन्द्रे॑ण च म॒रुत्व॑ता । आ॒दि॒त्येभि॑श्च॒ राज॑भिः ॥५॥

saṃ vo mádāso agmaténdreṇa ca marútvatā | ādityébhiś ca rā́jabhiḥ ||5||

Page 20 — Rik 5: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सम् । वः । मदासः । अग्मत । इन्द्रेण । च । मरुत्वता ॥ आदित्येभिः । च । राजऽभिः ॥५॥

sam | vaḥ | madāsaḥ | agmata | indreṇa | ca | marutvatā || ādityebhiḥ | ca | rāja 'bhiḥ ||5||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ ॥१॥ closes Varga 1. The Āśvalāyana number is printed ५-३.

हे ऋभवो वो युष्माकं संबन्धिनो मदासो मदहेतवः सोमा इन्द्रेण चादित्येभिरादित्यैश्च समग्मत । संगताः । ऋभूणामिन्द्रादित्यैः सह सोमपानं तृतीयसवनेऽस्ति । अत एवावाहननिगद आश्वलायनेनैवं पठितः । इन्द्रमादित्यवन्तमृभुमन्तं विभुमन्तं वाजवन्तं बृहस्पतिमन्तं विश्वदेव्यावन्तमावहेति ॥ आ. ५-३ । कीदृशेनेन्द्रेण । मरुत्वता मरुद्भिर्युक्तेन । अत एव मन्त्रान्तरमेवमाम्नायते । मरुद्भिरिन्द्र सख्यं ते अस्तु । ऋग्वे. ८-९६-७ । इति । कीदृशैरादित्येभिः । राजभिर्दीप्यमानैः ॥ मदासः । माद्यन्त्येभिरिति मदाः सोमाः । मदोऽनुपसर्गे । पा. ३-३-६७ । इत्यप् । तस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । आज्जसेरसुगिति जसोऽसुगागमः । अग्मत । गमेः संपूर्वाल्लुङ् । समो गम्यृच्छीत्यादिना । पा. १-३-२९ । आत्मनेपदम् । झस्यादादेशः । मन्त्रे घसेत्यादिना च्लेर्लुक् । गमहनेत्यादिना । पा. ६-४-९८ । उपधालोपः । व्यवहिताश्चेति समो व्यवहितप्रयोगः । निघातः । मरुत्वता । मरुतोऽस्य सन्तीति मरुत्वान् । तसौ मत्वर्थ इति भसंज्ञया पदसंज्ञाया बाधितत्वाज्जश्त्वाभावः । झयः । पा. ८-२-१० । इति मतुपो वत्वम् । आदित्येभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसादेशाभावे बहुवचने झल्येदित्येत्वम् । राजभिः । राजन्शब्दस्य कनिनन्तत्वेन नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥१॥

he ṛbhavo vo yuṣmākaṃ saṃbandhino madāso madahetavaḥ somā indreṇa cādityebhirādityaiśca samagmata | saṃgatāḥ | ṛbhūṇāmindrādityaiḥ saha somapānaṃ tṛtīyasavane 'sti | ata evāvāhananigada āśvalāyanenaivaṃ paṭhitaḥ | indramādityavantamṛbhumantaṃ vibhumantaṃ vājavantaṃ bṛhaspatimantaṃ viśvadevyāvantamāvaheti || ā. 5-3 | kīdṛśenendreṇa | marutvatā marudbhiryuktena | ata eva mantrāntaramevamāmnāyate | marudbhirindra sakhyaṃ te astu | ṛgve. 8-96-7 | iti | kīdṛśairādityebhiḥ | rājabhirdīpyamānaiḥ || madāsaḥ | mādyantyebhiriti madāḥ somāḥ | mado 'nupasarge | pā. 3-3-67 | ityap | tasya pittvādanudāttatvam | dhātusvara eva śiṣyate | ājjaserasugiti jaso 'sugāgamaḥ | agmata | gameḥ saṃpūrvālluṅ | samo gamyṛcchītyādinā | pā. 1-3-29 | ātmanepadam | jhasyādādeśaḥ | mantre ghasetyādinā clerluk | gamahanetyādinā | pā. 6-4-98 | upadhālopaḥ | vyavahitāśceti samo vyavahitaprayogaḥ | nighātaḥ | marutvatā | maruto 'sya santīti marutvān | tasau matvartha iti bhasaṃjñayā padasaṃjñāyā bādhitatvājjaśtvābhāvaḥ | jhayaḥ | pā. 8-2-10 | iti matupo vatvam | ādityebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisādeśābhāve bahuvacane jhalyedityetvam | rājabhiḥ | rājanśabdasya kaninantatvena nittvādādyudāttatvam ||1||

Translation: "O Ṛbhus, vaḥ, your, madāsaḥ, the soma juices that cause exhilaration, sam agmata, have come together with Indra and the Ādityas. In the third pressing the Ṛbhus drink soma together with Indra and the Ādityas. Hence the invitation formula (āvāhana-nigada) is read thus by Āśvalāyana: 'Bring Indra with the Ādityas, with the Ṛbhus, with Vibhu, with Vāja, with Bṛhaspati, with the Viśvadevas' (Āśv. 5-3). With what kind of Indra? Marutvatā, joined with the Maruts. Hence another mantra declares: 'With the Maruts, Indra, let there be friendship for you' (Ṛgveda 8-96-7). With what kind of Ādityas? Rājabhiḥ, shining." (Grammatical tail: madāsaḥ, "by them they are exhilarated": madāḥ, the soma juices; ap by mado 'nupasarge (Pā. 3-3-67), unaccented as pit, the root accent alone stays; the augment asuk for jas by āj jaser asuk; agmata, luṅ after gam with sam, ātmanepada by samo gamyṛcchi… (Pā. 1-3-29), at for jha, luk of cli by mantre ghasa…, the loss of the penultimate by gamahana… (Pā. 6-4-98), sam used separated by vyavahitāś ca, wholly unaccented; marutvatā, "he has Maruts", marutvān; since the bha name of tasau matvarthe overrides the pada name, no jaś; v for the m of matup by jhayaḥ (Pā. 8-2-10); ādityebhiḥ, without ais for bhis by bahulaṃ chandasi, e by bahuvacane jhaly et; rājabhiḥ, rājan, ending in kanin, initial udātta as nit.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे ऋभवः (he ṛbhavaḥ)) — O Ṛbhus | मरुत्वता (marutvatā) — joined with the deities called Maruts | इन्द्रेण च (indreṇa ca) — and with Indra | राजभिः (rājabhiḥ) — shining | आदित्येभिः च (ādityebhiḥ ca) — and (joined) with the Ādityas | वः (vaḥ) — your | मदासः (madāsaḥ) — causing exhilaration (the soma juices) | सं अग्मत (saṃ agmata) — have been brought together.

Page 21 — Rik 5: overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Ṛbhu deities, for you, joined with the Maruts, Indra and the shining Ādityas, the exhilarating soma juice has been made ready.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Ribhus, the exhilerating [sic] Soma juices are ready to be offered to you along with Indra accompanied by the Maruths [sic] and along with the brilliant Adityas.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

At the evening rite called the third pressing, when the soma juice is pressed and offered to the Ṛbhus, it is offered addressing Indra accompanied by the Ādityas, the Ṛbhus, Ṛbhu, Vibhu and Vāja, Bṛhaspati and the Viśvadevas. This is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra:

इन्द्रमादित्यवन्तमृभुमन्तं विभुमन्तं वाजवन्तं बृहस्पतिमन्तं विश्वदेव्यावन्तमावह (आ. ५-३)

indramādityavantamṛbhumantaṃ vibhumantaṃ vājavantaṃ bṛhaspatimantaṃ viśvadevyāvantamāvaha (ā. 5-3)

Saṃ agmata: Skandasvāmin explains these words as saṃgacchadhvam, that is, "come for the drinking of soma".

Madāsaḥ:

माद्यन्त्येभिरिति मदाः मदहेतवः सोमाः ।

mādyantyebhiriti madāḥ madahetavaḥ somāḥ |

("They are exhilarated by them: madāḥ, the soma juices, causes of exhilaration.") Because the drinking of soma produces exhilaration, the soma juice is called madāsaḥ.

Marutvatā:

मरुतोऽस्य सन्तीति मरुत्वान् । मरुद्भिर्युक्तेन ।

maruto 'sya santīti marutvān | marudbhiryuktena |

("He has Maruts: marutvān; joined with the Maruts.") Accompanied by the Marut deities (together with Indra).

Ādityebhiḥ: for the word āditya Yāska gives this derivation too (Ni. 2-13):

आदित्यः कस्मादादत्ते रसानादत्ते भासं ज्योतिषामादीप्तो भासेति वादितेः पुत्र इति वा ॥

ādityaḥ kasmādādatte rasānādatte bhāsaṃ jyotiṣāmādīpto bhāseti vāditeḥ putra iti vā ||

  1. Ādityaḥ kasmād ādatte rasān: ādatta iti ādityaḥ: one who takes, who receives, or who draws: this is the sense of the word āditya. Takes what? Rasān, that is, he draws the water through his rays. The water drawn in this way produces rain in the form of clouds. So, because he draws water through his rays from water-bodies such as the ocean, he is named Āditya.

Page 22 — Rik 5: Special Topics (end) and grammar

  1. Athavā ādatte bhāsaṃ jyotiṣām: because, when the sun rises, the sun's light lowers the light of all other things (such as the moon) and draws that light, he is named Āditya.

  2. Athavā ādīpto bhāseti vā: because he shines in all places, or covering all around, he is named Āditya.

  3. Athavā aditeḥ putra iti vā: because he is the son of the goddess Aditi, mother of the gods, he is named Āditya.

Rājabhiḥ:

दीप्यमानैः ।

dīpyamānaiḥ |

("Shining.") Shining, "brilliant, shining &c." [as printed].

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 22–23, noted briefly

मदासः (madāsaḥ): mādyati ebhir iti madāḥ somāḥ: by these soma juices one obtains joy; so madāḥ is a name of soma. The root madī harṣe. By "mado 'nupasarge" (Pā. sū. 3-3-67), when a subanta other than a preverb is the upapada, the suffix ap comes after the root mad; when ap comes, mad + a. The suffix has p as it, so it is unaccented; the root accent alone remains. After the word mada, when the nominative plural jas is added, mada + jas: by "āj jaser asuk" (Pā. sū. 7-1-50) the augment asuk for the jas after an aṅga ending in short a. Being kit, by the paribhāṣā "ādyantau ṭakitau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-46) it comes as an end-part with jas (as printed: ಅಂತಾವಯವಾಗಿ). Mada + asas: lengthening of the former like vowel; ru and visarga: madāsaḥ.

अग्मत (agmata): after the root gamḷ gatau preceded by the preverb sam, luṅ. Gam + luṅ: in "samo gamyṛcchibhyām" (Pā. sū. 1-3-29) "akarmakāc ca" (Pā. sū. 1-3-26) and, by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam" (Pā. sū. 1-3-12), ātmanepadam are carried on. After the roots gam and ṛ, preceded by the preverb sam and intransitive, in place of the l comes the ātmanepada; so in place of luṅ, when the 3rd plural is meant, the substitute jha named ātmanepada comes. Gam + cli + jha: by "ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-5) at for the jh; by "mantre ghasahvaraṇa…" (Pā. sū. 2-4-80) luk for cli. Gam + ata: now by "gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi" (Pā. sū. 6-4-98), when a vowel-initial suffix that is kit or ṅit follows, the penultimate letter of the roots gam and the rest drops; but when aṅ follows,

Page 23 (upper) — Rik 5: grammar (end)

this loss does not come; so the a of the root gam drops; the augment aṭ: agmata. By "te prāg dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-4-80) the gatis and preverbs must be used immediately before the root; so sam should be used directly. Yet by "chandasi pare 'pi" (Pā. sū. 1-4-81) and "vyavahitāś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-4-82), in the Veda the gatis and preverbs also come after the root and separated from it; so here sam is used separated. By "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" it is wholly unaccented.

मरुत्वता (marutvatā): marutaḥ asya santi iti marutvān: by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. sū. 5-2-94) the suffix matup after marut. The jas that is part of the stem takes luk. With the dropped suffix as condition the pada name would apply; so jaś would be due by "jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte" (Pā. sū. 8-2-39). But by "tasau matvarthe" (Pā. sū. 1-4-19), when a suffix in the sense of matup follows, words ending in t and s get the name bha. Since the bha name comes, the pada name is overridden by it. So marut is not a pada; for that reason jaś does not come. By "jhayaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-10), for the m of a matup after a word ending in a letter of the pratyāhāra jhay, v; the instrumental singular suffix ṭā: marutvatā.

आदित्येभिः (ādityebhiḥ): by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 7-1-10) the substitute ais for bhis does not come. By "bahuvacane jhaly et" (Pā. sū. 7-3-103) e comes.

राजभिः (rājabhiḥ): the root rājṛ dīptau. By "kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "1-154" [?]) the suffix kanin is nit; so by the nit accent rājan is initial udātta. After it the instrumental plural bhis; by "svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne" (Pā. sū. 1-4-17) the pada name; by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" the n drops; ru and visarga: rājabhiḥ.

॥५॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उ॒त त्यं च॑म॒सं न॒वं त्वष्टु॑र्दे॒वस्य॒ निष्कृ॑तम् । अक॑र्त च॒तुरः॒ पुनः॑ ॥६॥

utá tyáṃ camasáṃ naváṃ tváṣṭur devásya níṣkṛtam | ákarta catúraḥ púnaḥ ||6||
