॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उत । त्यम् । चमसम् । नवम् । त्वष्टुः । देवस्य । निःऽकृतम् ॥ अकर्त । चतुरः । पुनरिति ॥६॥

uta | tyam | camasam | navam | tvaṣṭuḥ | devasya | niḥ 'kṛtam || akarta | caturaḥ | punariti ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

उतापि च त्वष्टुरेतन्नामकस्य देवस्य संबन्धी तक्षणव्यापारः । नवं नूतनं त्यं चमसं तं सोमधारणक्षमं काष्ठपात्रविशेषं निष्कृतं निःशेषेण संपादितमकरोदिति शेषः । तक्षणव्यापारकुशलस्य त्वष्टुः शिष्या ऋभवस्तेन निर्मितं तमेकं चमसं पुनरपि चतुरोऽकर्त । चतुर्धा विभक्तांश्चमसान्कृतवन्तः । एकस्य चतुर्विधत्वकरणरूपोऽयमर्थो मन्त्रान्तरेऽपि विस्पष्टः । एकं चमसं चतुरः कृणोतन । ऋग्वे. १-१६१-२ । इति ॥ नवम् । णु स्तुतौ । नूयत इति नवम् । कर्मणि अप्प्रत्ययः । स हि घञोऽपवादत्वाद्घञर्थे सर्वत्र भवति । घञ्प्रत्ययश्चाकर्तरि च कारके संज्ञायाम् । पा. ३-३-१९ । इति कर्तृव्यतिरिक्ते सर्वत्र कारके भवति । यद्यपि तत्र संज्ञायामित्युक्तं तथापि चकारस्य संज्ञाव्यभिचारार्थत्वादसंज्ञायामपि भवत्येव । संबध्यत इति संबन्धः । कर्मणि घञित्युक्तम् । त्वष्टुः । तक्षू त्वक्षू तनूकरणे । औणादिकस्तृन् । ऊदित्त्वात्पक्ष इडभावः । पा. ७-२-४४ । स्कोः संयोगाद्योरन्ते च । पा. ८-२-२९ । इति ककारलोपः । निष्कृतम् । कृञो निरुपसृष्टात्कर्मणि क्तः । प्रादिसमासे नित्यं समासेऽनुत्तरपदस्थस्य । पा. ८-३-४५ । इति षत्वम् । अत्र कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति । पा. २-३-६५ । इति प्राप्ता षष्ठी यद्यपि न लोकाव्ययेति निषिद्धा । पा. २-३-६९ । तथापि कर्तुः शेषत्वेन विवक्षितत्वात्कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया । पा. २-३-१८ । इत्येतस्याः प्राप्तेः शैषिकी षष्ठी । यथा कर्मणि शेषत्वेन विवक्षिते । पा. २-३-५० । माषाणामश्नीयादिति । गतिरनन्तर इति निस उदात्तत्वम् । अकर्त । अकृषत । कृञो लुङि झस्य व्यत्ययेन तादेशः । मन्त्रे घसेत्यादिना च्लेर्लुक् । छन्दस्युभयथेति तिङ आर्धधातुकत्वाद्ङित्त्वाभावेन गुणः । चतुरः । चतुरः शसि । पा. ६-१-१६७ । इत्युकार उदात्तः । पुनः । स्वरादिष्वाद्युदात्तः पठितः ॥

utāpi ca tvaṣṭuretannāmakasya devasya saṃbandhī takṣaṇavyāpāraḥ | navaṃ nūtanaṃ tyaṃ camasaṃ taṃ somadhāraṇakṣamaṃ kāṣṭhapātraviśeṣaṃ niṣkṛtaṃ niḥśeṣeṇa saṃpāditamakaroditi śeṣaḥ | takṣaṇavyāpārakuśalasya tvaṣṭuḥ śiṣyā ṛbhavastena nirmitaṃ tamekaṃ camasaṃ punarapi caturo 'karta | caturdhā vibhaktāṃścamasānkṛtavantaḥ | ekasya caturvidhatvakaraṇarūpo 'yamartho mantrāntare 'pi vispaṣṭaḥ | ekaṃ camasaṃ caturaḥ kṛṇotana | ṛgve. 1-161-2 | iti || navam | ṇu stutau | nūyata iti navam | karmaṇi appratyayaḥ | sa hi ghaño 'pavādatvādghañarthe sarvatra bhavati | ghañpratyayaścākartari ca kārake saṃjñāyām | pā. 3-3-19 | iti kartṛvyatirikte sarvatra kārake bhavati | yadyapi tatra saṃjñāyāmityuktaṃ tathāpi cakārasya saṃjñāvyabhicārārthatvādasaṃjñāyāmapi bhavatyeva | saṃbadhyata iti saṃbandhaḥ | karmaṇi ghañityuktam | tvaṣṭuḥ | takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe | auṇādikastṛn | ūdittvātpakṣa iḍabhāvaḥ | pā. 7-2-44 | skoḥ saṃyogādyorante ca | pā. 8-2-29 | iti kakāralopaḥ | niṣkṛtam | kṛño nirupasṛṣṭātkarmaṇi ktaḥ | prādisamāse nityaṃ samāse 'nuttarapadasthasya | pā. 8-3-45 | iti ṣatvam | atra kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti | pā. 2-3-65 | iti prāptā ṣaṣṭhī yadyapi na lokāvyayeti niṣiddhā | pā. 2-3-69 | tathāpi kartuḥ śeṣatvena vivakṣitatvātkartṛkaraṇayostṛtīyā | pā. 2-3-18 | ityetasyāḥ prāpteḥ śaiṣikī ṣaṣṭhī | yathā karmaṇi śeṣatvena vivakṣite | pā. 2-3-50 | māṣāṇāmaśnīyāditi | gatiranantara iti nisa udāttatvam | akarta | akṛṣata | kṛño luṅi jhasya vyatyayena tādeśaḥ | mantre ghasetyādinā clerluk | chandasyubhayatheti tiṅa ārdhadhātukatvādṅittvābhāvena guṇaḥ | caturaḥ | caturaḥ śasi | pā. 6-1-167 | ityukāra udāttaḥ | punaḥ | svarādiṣvādyudāttaḥ paṭhitaḥ ||

Translation: "Uta, and also: the carving work belonged to the god named Tvaṣṭṛ. He made (is to be supplied) tyam, that, navam, new, camasa, a particular wooden vessel able to hold soma, niṣkṛtam, produced completely. The Ṛbhus, the pupils of Tvaṣṭṛ, who was skilled in carving, akarta, made that one camasa made by him catur, four, punaḥ, again: they made camasas divided four ways. This sense of making one into four is plain in another mantra too: 'Make the one camasa four' (Ṛgveda 1-161-2)." (Grammatical tail: navam, ṇu stutau, "it is praised": navam, the suffix ap in the object sense; being the exception to ghañ, it comes wherever ghañ would; and ghañ comes by akartari ca kārake saṃjñāyām (Pā. 3-3-19) in every kāraka other than the agent; though a name is mentioned there, since ca serves to allow departure from the name, it comes even without a name, as in saṃbandhaḥ, "it is bound", ghañ in the object sense; tvaṣṭuḥ, takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe, the Uṇādi tṛn, no iṭ in one alternative as the root is ūdit (Pā. 7-2-44), the k dropped by skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca (Pā. 8-2-29); niṣkṛtam, kta in the object sense after kṛñ with nis, in the prādi compound ṣ by nityaṃ samāse 'nuttarapadasthasya (Pā. 8-3-45); here the genitive due by kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti (Pā. 2-3-65) is barred by na lokāvyaya… (Pā. 2-3-69), and the instrumental would be due by kartṛkaraṇayos tṛtīyā (Pā. 2-3-18); yet since the agent is meant as a residue, the genitive of residue comes, as when the object is meant as a residue (Pā. 2-3-50), māṣāṇām aśnīyāt; nis udātta by gatir anantaraḥ; akarta, = akṛṣata, luṅ of kṛñ, ta for jha by exchange, luk of cli by mantre ghasa…; by chandasy ubhayathā the tiṅ is ārdhadhātuka, so not ṅit, and guṇa comes; caturaḥ, the u udātta by catur aḥ śasi (Pā. 6-1-167); punaḥ, read as initial udātta in the svar-ādi.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

उत (uta) — and | त्वष्टुः (tvaṣṭuḥ) — called Tvaṣṭṛ | देवस्य (devasya) — made by the craftsman of the gods | नवम् (navam) — new | त्यम् (tyam) — that (fit to be filled with soma juice) | चमसम् (camasam) — the wooden

Page 25 — Rik 6: word-meanings (end), overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

vessel called camasa | निष्कृतम् (niṣkṛtam) — was well made (that, the Ṛbhus) | पुनः (punaḥ) — again | चतुरः (caturaḥ) — into four camasas | अकर्त (akarta) — made.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The deity Tvaṣṭṛ made only one wooden vessel called camasa. The Ṛbhus by their power made it into four and made it convenient.

॥ English Translation ॥

Besides, the Ribhus again made into four that new ladle, the work of the divine Twastri.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Tvaṣṭṛ is famed as the carpenter of the gods ("Twashtri is the carpenter or artisan of the gods" [as printed]). Since the implements of sacrifice, the means used in rites such as sacrifice, are most necessary, Tvaṣṭṛ, who makes them, has an excellent place among the gods. The Ṛbhus are pupils of this Tvaṣṭṛ, the craftsman of the gods. This ṛk praises the power of these Ṛbhus, saying that they made into four the one sacrificial vessel called camasa that their teacher had made.

Uta: and, besides; that is, apart from what was said before, another matter is this.

Tyam: tam, that.

Camasam: a wooden vessel shaped like a ladle, used in the sacrifice for drinking soma.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 25–30, noted briefly

नवम् (navam): the root ṇu stutau. By "ṇo naḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-65) n for the ṇ at the start of the root. In "ṛdor ap" (Pā. sū. 3-3-57), ṝ ca u ca anayoḥ samāhāraḥ ṝduḥ: if the samāhāra-dvandva compound is made, since the collection is one, the singular alone comes. But by "sa napuṃsakam" (Pā. sū. 2-4-17), in a samāhāra compound both the dvigu and the dvandva take the neuter; so here the neuter should properly come. Yet since it is a sūtra, the masculine has come, passing over this rule. In the genitive singular it becomes ṛdoḥ. Here the genitive has come in the sense of the ablative; or this is ablative-final. So the sense of the sūtra is that after roots ending in ṝ and in u

Page 26 — Rik 6: grammar

the suffix ap comes, both in the sense of the action and in the senses of the kārakas other than the agent. So, since the root nu ends in u, the suffix ap comes after it in the kāraka sense of the object. Ṛdor ap is the exception to the sūtra enjoining ghañ, "puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥ prāyeṇa" (Pā. sū. "3-3-19" [as printed, for 3-3-118]). So, since the suffix ap comes in whatever senses the suffix ghañ comes, its application in the senses of the action and of the kārakas other than the agent is established. In the same way, since the sūtra enjoining ghañ says saṃjñāyām, since ghañ comes only when a name is to be expressed, it is natural that the exception ap too should come only when there is a name. But in the ghañ rule the ca in akartari ca is construed with saṃjñāyāṃ ca; thus it is established that ghañ comes both when a name is to be expressed and, by the ca, when it is not. So there is no obstacle to the exception ap coming whether a name is expressed or not. This point is set out in the Vedabhāṣya as "cakārasya saṃjñāvyabhicārārthatvād asaṃjñāyām api bhavaty eva". For this very reason authorities describe the suffix ghañ in the object sense after the root bandh preceded by sam in saṃbadhyate iti saṃbandhaḥ. With nu + a, by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84) guṇa: o; the substitute av; when the accusative singular am is added, by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-107) the pūrvarūpa comes: navam.

त्वष्टुः (tvaṣṭuḥ): the root takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe. After it, by "tṛn tṛcau śaṃsikṣadādibhyaḥ saṃjñāyāṃ cāniṭau" (Uṇ. sū. "2-251", zoom-checked: the printed number is 2-251, not 2-51), the Uṇādi suffix tṛn comes: tvakṣ + tṛ; or by "bahulam anyatrāpi" (Uṇ. sū. "2-252", zoom-checked; the last digit smudged) tṛn. In this alternative, since the root is ūdit, for the ārdhadhātuka after it, by "svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūdito vā" (Pā. sū. 7-2-44) the augment iṭ is optional; so in the alternative the augment iṭ does not come here. By "skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca" (Pā. sū. 8-2-29), at the end of a pada and before a conjunct, the s and k-class letters at the start of a conjunct drop; so the k drops: tvaṣ + tṛ; by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-41) ṭutva: tvaṣṭṛ. When the genitive singular suffix ṅas [as printed: "jas"] is added, tvaṣṭṛ + as: by "ṛta ut" (Pā. sū. 6-1-111), when ṅasi or ṅas follow a ṛ-final word, in place of former and latter, as a single substitute, ut, that is, a short u, comes; so the substitute u; by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-51) it comes followed by r; by "rāt sasya" (Pā. sū. 8-2-24) only the s at the end of a conjunct after r drops: so the s drops: tvaṣṭur, visarga: tvaṣṭuḥ.

Page 27 — Rik 6: grammar

निष्कृतम् (niṣkṛtam): after the root ḍukṛñ karaṇe preceded by the preverb nis, the suffix kta in the object sense. By "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-2-18) the prādi compound of the two, nis + kṛtam. For the s, by "sasajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-66), ru. By "kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-15), when khar follows, visarga for the r: niḥkṛtam. Now by "nityaṃ samāse 'nuttarapadasthasya" (Pā. sū. 8-3-45), when the k-class or p-class follows, ṣ comes for a visarga belonging to is or us not in the final member: so ṣ: niṣkṛtam. The starting of the sūtra nityaṃ samāse, according to the Bhāṣya verse-vārttika "pratiṣedhārthas tu yatno 'yam" (Pā. sū. 8-3-45, śloka-vā. 4), is established to have come in order to bar the ṣ for the visarga of is and us standing in the final member in a compound.

प्रतिषेधार्थस्तु यत्नोऽयम्

pratiṣedhārthastu yatno 'yam

("This effort is for the purpose of barring.") Likewise in the sūtra "isusoḥ sāmarthye" (Pā. sū. 8-3-44), from

नानापदार्थयोर्वर्तमानयोः ख्यायते यदा योगः तस्मिन्षत्वं कार्यं तद्युक्तं तच्चमे नेह

nānāpadārthayorvartamānayoḥ khyāyate yadā yogaḥ tasminṣatvaṃ kāryaṃ tadyuktaṃ taccame neha

(Pā. sū. 8-3-44, vā. 1) it is learnt that the capacity in the form of mutual expectancy of words conveying various things is to be included here. In accordance with this definition, in the compound paramasarpiṣkuṇḍikā, because such capacity of expectancy is lacking, the optional ṣ by the sūtra "isusoḥ" does not come: that is the sense of the vārttika. So the capacity of expectancy alone is meant; therefore in the compound niṣkṛtam, since that capacity is lacking, the optional ṣ by "isusoḥ" cannot come. By "idudupadhasya cāpratyayasya" (Pā. sū. 8-3-41), when the k-class or p-class follows, ṣ comes for a visarga that has i or u as penultimate and does not belong to a suffix; by this alone the ṣ comes. That is why in places such as niṣpratyūham the ṣ is justified by idudupadhasya itself. Some divide the sūtra nityaṃ samāse into two, nityaṃ samāse as one sūtra and anuttarapadasthasya as a second. In the divided second sūtra the word samāse is to be construed. So, explaining that in a compound the visarga in the final member does not take ṣ, all ṣ due to the visarga in a final member is barred; so they explain that, though in isusoḥ sāmarthye both capacities, single meaning and expectancy, are meant, in paramasarpiṣkuṇḍikā the bar anuttarapadasthasya comes, so the optional ṣ does not come, and there is no fault. On their view, in niṣkṛtam, overriding idudupadhasya, if the optional ṣ by isusoḥ is due, the ṣ here must be justified by nityaṃ samāse to prevent it. But this is not accepted by the Mahābhāṣya. So here

Page 28 — Rik 6: grammar

the description of the ṣ by idudupadhasya is right. In devasya niṣkṛtam, by "kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti" (Pā. sū. 2-3-65), when there is connection with a kṛdanta word, the genitive comes after a stem denoting the agent or object defined by the action denoted by the kṛt-final; since deva denotes the agent defined by the root kṛ, the base of the suffix kta in the object sense, the genitive would be due after it. But for this, by "na lokāvyayaniṣṭhākhalartha-tṛnām" (Pā. sū. 2-3-69), la is a general taking of all the la-forms laṭ and the rest; since laṭ and the rest are not used directly, la takes the substitutes of la. The substitutes of la, the u-final kṛt suffixes: since u qualifies kṛtaḥ, by "yena vidhis tadantasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-72) the tadanta is obtained; if it is explained as taking only the suffix u, in places such as hariṃ alaṃkariṣṇuḥ the suffix iṣṇuc and the like would not be taken; where only the suffix u has come, it becomes a kṛdanta by vyapadeśivadbhāva. U, uka, indeclinables, the niṣṭhā in the form of the suffixes kta and ktavatu, the khal-sense suffixes, and tṛn: in "laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau…" (Pā. sū. 3-2-124) the pratyāhāra beginning with the tṛ there and ending with the n in tṛn: when there is use with these, there is the bar that the genitive does not come; so here the genitive is not due. Yet here we intend the agent as a residue. Śeṣa means uktād anyaḥ śeṣaḥ: the relations such as owner-and-owned other than the kārakas and the sense of the stem. The kārakas such as agent and the sense of the stem were stated before the beginning of the sūtra "ṣaṣṭhī śeṣe" (Pā. sū. 2-3-50). The relations such as owner-and-owned have not been stated; so they are other than what was stated. The sense of the sūtra ṣaṣṭhī śeṣe is that the genitive comes in such a sense, the residue. In the present case, if intended as agent, since the bar na loka… comes, the genitive of the agent does not come by kartṛkarmaṇoḥ; then, by "kartṛkaraṇayos tṛtīyā" (Pā. sū. 2-3-18), the instrumental comes after a stem denoting the agent or instrument not expressed by tiṅ, kṛt, taddhita or compound; so the instrumental would have to come; if, not meaning it as agent, it is meant as residue, since there is no intent of denoting the agent, the instrumental of the agent does not come; since there is the intent of residue, the genitive alone comes by ṣaṣṭhī śeṣe. On this point we give a traditional example: māṣāṇām aśnīyāt, one should eat beans. Here, for māṣa, by "kartur īpsitatamaṃ karma" (Pā. sū. 1-4-49),

प्रकृतधातूपस्थाप्यप्रधानीभूतव्यापारप्रयोज्यव्यापारव्यधिकरणफलसंबन्धित्वप्रकारकातिशयेच्छानिरूपितविशेष्यताश्रयः कर्मसंज्ञको भवति

prakṛtadhātūpasthāpyapradhānībhūtavyāpāraprayojyavyāpāravyadhikaraṇaphalasaṃbandhitvaprakārakātiśayecchānirūpitaviśeṣyatāśrayaḥ karmasaṃjñako bhavati

(as printed), the name object applies. For example, the root in question is the root aś; its sense is the activity conducive to contact below the throat.

Page 29 — Rik 6: grammar

By this activity the fruit in the form of contact below the throat arises for the beans. Since in the beans there is no activity conducive to contact, the fruit in the form of contact residing in them is in a locus other than the activity. Thus, the root in question, the root aś; the activity presented by it as principal, the activity conducive to contact below the throat; the fruit impelled by that activity and residing in a locus other than the activity, the fruit in the form of contact below the throat; the wish for excess whose mode is relation to that, the wish of the form

माषाः मद्गळबिलाधस्संयुक्ता भवन्तु

māṣāḥ madgaḷabilādhassaṃyuktā bhavantu

("May the beans be joined below the throat"): since the beans have the substrate of qualificand-hood defined by such a wish, they get the name object. So by "karmaṇi dvitīyā" (Pā. sū. 2-3-2), the accusative comes after a stem denoting the object not expressed by tiṅ and the rest; so the accusative comes: māṣān aśnīyāt. If the object is meant as residue, the genitive comes by ṣaṣṭhī śeṣe: māṣāṇām aśnīyāt. In the same way here too, if the agent is meant as residue, there is no obstacle to the genitive coming in the way said before. By "vivakṣātaḥ kārakāṇi bhavanti" the kārakas come according to intention; so one may intend according to the usage to be explained. Here, if agency is intended, the instrumental would have to come; so we intend the agent as residue. Thus the genitive is justified. By "gatir anantaraḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-2-49), when a kta-final in the object sense follows, a word called gati standing immediately before keeps its own accent; so the own accent of nis, udātta, remains after compounding too. By "upasargāś cābhivarjam" (Phi. sū. 81) nis is initial udātta.

अकर्त (akarta): the sense is akṛṣata. The root ḍukṛñ karaṇe; after it, luṅ, the ātmanepada 3rd plural substitute jha. For the jh, though the substitute at is due by "ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-5), here by "vyatyayo bahulam" (Pā. sū. 3-1-85) the substitute t comes; for the cli come by "cli luṅi" (Pā. sū. 3-1-43), by "mantre ghasahvaraṇaśavṛdahādvṛckṛgamijanibhyo leḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-80), luk; the augment aṭ: akṛ + ta. By "tiṅ śit sārvadhātukam" (Pā. sū. 3-4-113), the eighteen suffixes tip, tas and the rest stated in the section on roots, and the suffixes with ś as it, are called sārvadhātuka; so ta has the name sārvadhātuka, and it is not pit. So by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) it becomes ṅit. Thus, since by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5) the bar to the ik-guṇa comes, the question how guṇa comes here cannot fail to arise. Yet by "chandasy ubhayathā" (Pā. sū. 3-4-117) the suffixes enjoined in the section on roots get in the Veda both names, sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka,

Page 30 (upper) — Rik 6: grammar (end)

so here ta gets the name ārdhadhātuka, not the name sārvadhātuka. So it does not become ṅit by sārvadhātukam apit; therefore the bar to guṇa does not come. Thus guṇa comes by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84). Since it comes in place of ṛ, it comes followed by r: akarta.

चतुरः (caturaḥ): by "cater uran" (Uṇ. sū. "5-236", zoom-checked: 5, then 2, 3, hooked 6) the suffix uran comes after catī yācane; so after the root cat the suffix uran; in the suffix the a is for pronunciation: catur. This is initial udātta by the nit accent. When after it the accusative plural suffix śas is added, by "catur aḥ śasi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-167), when the śas ending follows, the end of the word catur is udātta: so the u is udātta.

पुनः (punaḥ): in the svar-ādi group it is read as initial udātta.

Translation: "In the third chandoma, at the vaiśvadeva-śastra, the two ṛks te no ratnāni dhattana are to the Ṛbhus. So it is laid down in the section of the third, aganma maha: 'indra iṣe dadātu naḥ, and te no ratnāni dhattana: one and two' (Āśv. 8-11). The Ṛbhus set forth in the previous ṛks: you, being joined with suśasti, our fine praises, dhattana, give, to the sunvat, the sacrificer who presses soma, who belongs to us, ratnāni, lovely riches such as gold, gems and pearls, ekam ekam, each in order: 'one by one' is said meaning as much of each of gold and the rest as is wanted. Of what kind are the riches? Trir ā, repeated three times: the threefold repetition of the riches is the best, the middling and the lowest. And also make, dhattana, the sāpta, the rites in the form of groups made up of seven. Of what kind are the sāpta? Trir ā, repeated three times: the seven haviryajñas, agnyādheya, darśapūrṇamāsa and the rest, are one group; the seven pākayajñas, aupāsana-homa, vaiśvadeva and the rest, are the second; the seven somasaṃsthās, agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma and the rest, are the third." (Grammatical tail: ratnāni, ramu krīḍāyām, the suffix na by rameś ta ca (Uṇ. 3-14, zoom-checked) with nit carried on, t for m with it, initial udātta as nit; dhattana, = dhatta, tana for ta by taptanaptanathanāś ca; sāptam, "a group of seven", the suffix añ in the sense of group by saptano 'ñ chandasi (Pā. 5-1-61), the loss of the ṭi by nas taddhite (Pā. 6-4-144), initial vṛddhi and initial udātta as ñit; here by the word for group the members of the group are meant, hence the plural; otherwise, one group repeated three times, it would be singular; sunvate, the ending udātta by śatur anumaḥ; ekam ekam, doubled for repetition by nityavīpsayoḥ, eka with kan after iṇ, initial udātta as nit, the second eka called āmreḍita by tasya param āmreḍitam and unaccented by anudāttaṃ ca; suśastibhiḥ, "by them one praises": śastayaḥ, the ṛks, śaṃsu stutau, ktin in the sense of instrument, the n dropped as it is kit; in the prādi compound "good praises", though by the initial udātta of ktin as nit and the accent of the kṛt final member that would be due, it is overridden by the later final udātta of the final member by man-ktin-vyākhyāna… (Pā. 6-2-151).)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ते (te) — you, set forth before (the Ṛbhus) | सुशस्तिभिः (suśastibhiḥ) — by (our) auspicious praises | नः (naḥ) — our | सुन्वते (sunvate) — (to the sacrificer) who prepares soma | त्रिरा (trirā) — of three kinds (best, middling and lowest) | रत्नानि (ratnāni) — priceless gems and the rest | त्रिरा (trirā) — in the form of three groups | साप्तानि (sāptāni) — the rites called the seven soma-saṃsthās | धत्तन (dhattana) — favour (us with).

Page 32 — Rik 7: overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

May the Ṛbhus, satisfied by our hymns, grant one by one to the sacrificer who prepares and gives the soma juice gems of three kinds, best, middling and lowest, and the three groups, each with seven rites.

॥ English Translation ॥

Confer, therefore, Ribhus, moved by our praises, the three-fold riches upon our sacrificer, one by one ; accomplish the thrice seven-fold works (Sacrifices).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

At the time of reciting the vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras, this ṛk and the next are recited as the third chandoma mantras. This is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, in the section tṛtīyasyāganma maha, in the sūtra indra iṣe dadātu naḥ (Ṛ. saṃ. 8-93-34) te no ratnāni dhattanety ekā dve ca (Ā. 8-11).

In this ṛk the power and abilities of the Ṛbhu deities are not described; it is a prayer that they grant to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice wealth such as gems and the fruits of rites such as sacrifices.

Trirā sāptāni: three sevens, that is, seven repeated three times, or twenty-one. In the order of sacrifices there are chiefly twenty-one kinds of sacrifice. They are divided in three ways.

अग्न्याधेयदर्शपूर्णमासादीनां सप्तानां हविर्यज्ञानामेको वर्गः ॥

agnyādheyadarśapūrṇamāsādīnāṃ saptānāṃ haviryajñānāmeko vargaḥ ||

("The seven haviryajñas, agnyādheya, darśapūrṇamāsa and the rest, are one group.") Agnyādheya, darśapūrṇamāsa and the rest, seven rites, form one group called haviryajña. Since in these rites what is chiefly offered to the gods is havis, they are called haviryajñas. The seven rites agnyādheya, agnihotra, darśapūrṇamāsa, āgrayaṇa, cāturmāsya, dākṣāyaṇa-yajña and sautrāmaṇī belong to this group (Ai. Brā. Bhā. "5-7", zoom-checked: the second number is the flat-footed 7, not the curled 2).

औपासनहोमो वैश्वदेवमित्यादीनां सप्तानां पाकयज्ञानां वर्गो द्वितीयः ॥

aupāsanahomo vaiśvadevamityādīnāṃ saptānāṃ pākayajñānāṃ vargo dvitīyaḥ ||

("The seven pākayajñas, aupāsana-homa, vaiśvadeva and the rest, are the second group.") The group of seven rites, aupāsana, vaiśvadeva and the rest, is named pākayajña. They are also called gṛhya rites. In them what is chiefly offered to the gods is grain. The seven, aupāsana, vaiśvadeva, pārvaṇa, aṣṭakā, māsiśrāddha, sarpabali and īśānabali, belong to this group (according to Dhūrtasvāmin's commentary on the Āpastamba Paribhāṣāsūtra).

Page 33 — Rik 7: Special Topics (end) and grammar

अग्निष्टोमोऽत्यग्निष्टोम इत्यादीनां सप्तानां सोमसंस्थानां वर्गस्तृतीयः ॥

agniṣṭomo 'tyagniṣṭoma ityādīnāṃ saptānāṃ somasaṃsthānāṃ vargastṛtīyaḥ ||

("The seven somasaṃsthās, agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma and the rest, are the third group.") The seven soma rites including the soma-saṃsthās agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma and the rest are the third group. They are called soma rites; in them what is offered to the gods is soma juice. The seven soma rites or soma-saṃsthās are agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma, ukthya, ṣoḍaśin, vājapeya, atirātra and aptoryāma.

These three kinds of groups we have described in Ṛgveda-saṃhitā Part 1, pages "416–417" (zoom-checked; the last digit is the flat-footed 7) and "432–433" [?] (the second group is smudged in the scan).

Ekam ekam:

क्रमेण प्रत्येकम् ॥

krameṇa pratyekam ||

("In order, each one.") The intent is that of the things we like, such as wealth, grain and cattle, one should be given, or all should be given one by one.

Suśastibhiḥ:

शस्यते आभिरिति शस्तयः ऋचः ॥

śasyate ābhiriti śastayaḥ ṛcaḥ ||

("By them one praises: śastayaḥ, the ṛks.") Since the gods are praised with ṛks, they are named śastayaḥ. Suśastayaḥ means excellent ṛks or hymns.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 33–37, noted briefly

रत्नानि (ratnāni): the root ramu krīḍāyām. By the sūtra "rameś ta ca" (Uṇ. sū. "3-294", zoom-checked; the bhāṣya on p. 31 prints this sūtra as 3-14), from "kṛvṛjasidrupanyanisvapibhyo nit" (Uṇ. sū. "3-290", zoom-checked) the word nit is carried on. Rameḥ is a statement of the ṇyanta. The sense of the sūtra is that after the root ram ending in ṇic the suffix na comes; it is nit, and t comes as the final substitute for the root ram. Here, from "dhāpṛvasyajyatibhyo naḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "3-286", zoom-checked), naḥ is carried on. By this sūtra, when the suffix na comes after the ṇyanta root ram, t for the m: rat + i + na. With ṇic made after the root ram, ram + i: by "ata upadhāyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-116) the penultimate vṛddhi: rām + i + na; by "janījṝṣknasurañjo 'mantāś ca" (Dhā. ga. 2 [as read]), janī prādurbhāve, jṝṣ vayohānau, knasu hvaraṇadīptyoḥ, rañja rāge, both the div-ādi and bhv-ādi ones being taken; those ending in am are mit, so it is mit. By "mitāṃ hrasvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-92), when ṇi follows, the penultimate of what is called mit is shortened: shortened. Now with the suffix na and the substitute t, rat + i + na; by "ṇer aniṭi" (Pā. sū. 6-4-51), when an ārdhadhātuka without iṭ

Page 34 — Rik 7: grammar

follows, ṇi drops: so ṇi drops: ratna. The suffix being nit, by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197) it is initial udātta. The word ratna, in the accusative plural, becomes ratnāni.

धत्तन (dhattana): the sense is dhatta. The root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ. After it the loṭ 2nd plural suffix tha: dhā + tha. By "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68) the vikaraṇa śap. For it, by "juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-75), ślu (loss); by "ślau" (Pā. sū. 6-1-10), in places where loss has come naming ślu, the root is doubled: doubling: dhādhā + tha; by "hrasvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-59) the abhyāsa is shortened; by "abhyāse carca" (Pā. sū. 8-4-54) jaś d for the dh: dadhā + tha. By "ī haly aghoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-113), when a consonant-initial sārvadhātuka suffix that is kit or ṅit follows, ī is substituted for the ā of śnā and of abhyasta stems not called ghu; but here the ī substitute does not come. For by "dādhā ghv adāp" (Pā. sū. 1-1-20), roots of the forms dā and dhā, except daip and dāp, are called ghu; so the root dhā is called ghu, and in ī haly aghoḥ there is the bar aghoḥ. So the ī does not come. By "śnābhyastayor ātaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-112), when a kit or ṅit sārvadhātuka suffix follows, the ā of śnā and of an abhyasta drops: the loss: dadh + tha. By "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85) the loṭ is treated as laṅ. By "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-101), in place of tas, thas, tha, mip that came in place of a ṅit l, tām, tam, ta, am come respectively: so ta for tha: dadh + ta. By "dadhas tathoś ca" (Pā. sū. 8-2-38), when t, th, s, dhv follow, the ba-class letters of the root dhāñ, doubled and ending in jhaṣ, take bhaṣ: so dh for the first d: dhadh + ta. Here a doubt arises: when bhaṣ is made, the loss is sthānivat by "acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-57), so the root is thought of as ā-final, and there is no doubled dhā ending in jhaṣ; how does bhaṣ come? Here Vāmana and Mādhavācārya say that by force of the enjoining of bhaṣ, the sthānivadbhāva does not come. Others again say that in "pūrvatrāsiddhīye na sthānivat" there is the bar to sthānivadbhāva when the rules of the section pūrvatrāsiddham (Pā. sū. 8-2-1) are made; since the bhaṣ rule is of the tripādī, when it is made the sthānivadbhāva is barred; so the sthānivadbhāva does not come. Thus, since the doubled jhaṣ-final root dhā is found, there is no obstacle to bhaṣ by dadhas tathoś ca. Dhadh + ta: by

Page 35 — Rik 7: grammar

"khari ca" (Pā. sū. 8-4-55), when a khar letter follows, car letters for the jhal letters: car: dhatta. Now by "taptanaptanathanāś ca" (Pā. sū. 7-1-45), for the t that came as the substitute for the loṭ 2nd plural, the substitutes tap, tanap, tana, thana come; so the substitute tana for ta: dhattana. By "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28) it is wholly unaccented.

साप्तानि (sāptāni): by "saptano 'ñ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 5-1-61), after a first-case fit word whose base is the stem saptan, the suffix añ comes in the sense "tatparimāṇam asya vargasya"; so when saptaparimāṇam asya vargasya is meant, the suffix añ comes after saptan + su. Being taddhita-final, it gets the name prātipadika, and the sup that is part of the stem takes luk by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71): saptan + a. Now by "nas taddhite" (Pā. sū. 6-4-144), when a taddhita suffix follows, the ṭi that is part of an n-final aṅga called bha drops; so an drops: sapt + a. In vowel-final words the last vowel, and in consonant-final words the penultimate vowel together with the final consonant, are called ṭi: this sense is stated by "aco 'ntyādi ṭi" (Pā. sū. 1-1-64). By "yaci bham" (Pā. sū. 1-4-18) what stands immediately before the svādi suffixes with the initials y or a vowel, not in the section kap and not sarvanāmasthāna, is called bha. By "yasmāt pratyayavidhis tadādi pratyaye 'ṅgam", after whatever base a suffix is enjoined, the word beginning with that base is called aṅga when that suffix follows: the name aṅga is enjoined. The suffix has ñ as it. So the initial vṛddhi and the initial udātta accent both come. The initial vṛddhi by "taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-117): when a taddhita suffix that has ñ or ṇ as it follows, vṛddhi comes to the first vowel among the vowels of that word: so it is enjoined. Here the a after the s takes the vṛddhi ā: sāp + a = sāpta. By "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197) initial udātta is enjoined; the natural sense of sāpta is a group limited to the number seven. But here, by figurative indication, the sense "belonging to groups limited to seven" is intended. So the plural is justified. Otherwise, one group repeated three times, so, the group being one, the singular would have to come. After sāpta, the accusative plural śas: sāpta + śas; by "jaśśasoḥ śiḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-20) śi for śas; by "śi sarvanāmasthānam" (Pā. sū. 1-1-42) śi gets the name sarvanāmasthāna.

Page 36 — Rik 7: grammar

So śi has the name sarvanāmasthāna. Therefore by "napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-72), when a sarvanāmasthāna follows, a neuter word ending in jhal or a vowel takes the augment num: the augment num. Sāpta + n + i: by "sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-8) lengthening: sāptāni.

सुन्वते (sunvate): the root ṣuñ abhiṣave; by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-64) s for ṣ; laṭ; by "laṭaḥ śatṛ…" (Pā. sū. 3-2-124) the suffix śatṛ; by "svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-73) the vikaraṇa śnu: su + nu + at. By "huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke" the substitute yaṇ: sunvat. After it the dative singular ṅe: sunvat + e. Here, though the suffix śatṛ stands after the suffix śnu, which is ṅit by the extension "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4), so that one might say śatṛ should be unaccented by "tāsyanudātteṅid…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-186), in the sūtra tāsyanudāttet the ṅit meant is one by original statement; śnu is not ṅit by original statement. So śatṛ is not unaccented; by the suffix accent it is initial udātta. Thus by "śatur anumo nadyajādī" (Pā. sū. 6-1-173), after a word ending in a śatṛ suffix that has no augment num and is final udātta, the letters called nadī and the vowel-initial endings from śas on are udātta; so the suffix ṅe gets the udātta accent.

एकमेकम् (ekam ekam): "nityavīpsayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-4): from the Mahābhāṣya on this sūtra ("tiṅavyayeṣu tasyedaṃ grahaṇam" [as read]) the sense of the word nitya is ābhīkṣṇya, that is, repetition; vīpsā means the wish to pervade. This is a word with both derivation and convention. When the speaker, not having the mutual connection, that is, togetherness, uses a sentence that conveys at once the pervasion of things having separate number, by an action or by a quality, then the particular wish residing in that speaker is indicated by the doubling: this point is clear in Kaiyaṭa, explaining the Bhāṣya

वीप्स्यं कर्ता भवति

vīpsyaṃ kartā bhavati

("The thing to be pervaded is the agent"):

अत्र प्रयोक्ता कर्ता विवक्षितः यदा पृथक्संख्यायुक्तानितरेतरयोगमप्राप्तान्सर्वानर्थान् क्रियया गुणेन वा युगपद्व्याप्नुवन्वाक्यं वक्ति तदा स वक्तृस्थ इच्छाविशेषो द्विर्वचनेन द्योत्यः

atra prayoktā kartā vivakṣitaḥ yadā pṛthaksaṃkhyāyuktānitaretarayogamaprāptānsarvānarthān kriyayā guṇena vā yugapadvyāpnuvanvākyaṃ vakti tadā sa vaktṛstha icchāviśeṣo dvirvacanena dyotyaḥ

("Here the user is meant as agent: when he speaks a sentence pervading at once, by an action or a quality, all things having separate number and not reaching mutual connection, then that particular wish residing in the speaker is to be indicated by doubling.") If the sense in the form of the wish to pervade is meant, in places such as cikīrṣati the wish to pervade jars and the like by actions such as karoti is what cikīrṣati conveys; so there is no room for the doubt that it too should be doubled. For here, though cikīrṣati conveys a wish to pervade, this wish is not the particular wish residing in the user stated before.

Page 37 — Rik 7: grammar (end)

So in places such as cikīrṣati there is no room for doubling. "Sarvasya dve" (Pā. sū. 8-1-1) is the heading here; "padasya" (Pā. sū. 8-1-16) is drawn in here. Thus for the sūtra the sense is: when repetition or the wish to pervade is indicated, in place of the whole word doubling comes. In ekam ekam, by the sūtra just stated, doubling comes when pervasion is indicated. By this, the action in the form of giving presented by the word dhattana in question is construed with each individual. After the root iṇ gatau, by "iṇbhīkāpāśalyatimarcibhyaḥ kan" (Uṇ. sū. "3-323", zoom-checked; printed with a gap in place of the hyphen), after iṇ gatau, ñibhī bhaye, kai śabde, pā pāne, śala gatau, ata sātatyagamane, marca śabde the suffix kan comes; so kan. I + ka, guṇa: eka; the suffix being nit, eka is initial udātta by the nit accent ñnityādir nityam. The second word eka has the name āmreḍita by "tasya param āmreḍitam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-2), the second of a doubled word. So by "anudāttaṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-3), the āmreḍita takes the unaccented tone: wholly unaccented.

सुशस्तिभिः (suśastibhiḥ): 'śasyate ābhir iti śastayaḥ ṛcaḥ': the ṛks that are the instrument of praise are denoted by śastayaḥ. The root śaṃsu stutau. After it, by "striyāṃ ktin" (Pā. sū. 3-3-94), in the feminine, in the sense of the action and in the kāraka senses other than the agent, the suffix ktin comes after the root: kṛ [as printed] śaṃs + ktin. K and n are called it and dropped: śaṃs + ti. By "anidhitāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti" (Pā. sū. 6-4-24), when a suffix with k or ṅ as it follows, the penultimate n of a consonant-final aṅga not having short i as it drops; since a kit suffix follows, the penultimate n drops. Though the penultimate appears to be anusvāra, not n, yet when this loss of n is made the anusvāra is asiddha, so there is an n in the penultimate; therefore it drops: śasti. Śobhanāḥ śastayaḥ suśastayaḥ: by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-2-18) the prādi compound. Śasti is initial udātta by the nit accent; after compounding, if the own accent of the final member came by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139), that initial accent should stay; thus su unaccented, śa udātta, sti svarita, the pracaya: suśastayaḥ should result; but that kṛt final-member accent of gatikāraka… is overridden by the later final accent of the final member enjoined by "man-ktin-vyākhyāna-śayana-āsana-sthāna-yājaka-ādi-krītāḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-2-151); so in śasti the sti is udātta. After it the instrumental plural bhis: suśasti + bhis; bhis, being a sup, is unaccented; by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" it becomes svarita; ru and visarga for the s: suśastibhiḥ.

॥७॥

Rik 8 (last ṛk of the sūkta) pp. 38

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अधा॑रयन्त॒ वह्न॒योऽभ॑जन्त सुकृ॒त्यया॑ । भा॒गं दे॒वेषु॑ य॒ज्ञिय॑म् ॥८॥

ádhārayanta váhnayó 'bhajanta sukṛtyáyā | bhāgáṃ devéṣu yajñíyam ||8||

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अधारयन्त । वह्नयः । अभजन्त । सुऽकृत्यया ॥ भागम् । देवेषु । यज्ञियम् ॥८॥

adhārayanta | vahnayaḥ | abhajanta | su 'kṛtyayā || bhāgam | deveṣu | yajñiyam ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The varga number is not printed after this bhāṣya; the page headers from p. 43 read Varga 3.

वह्नयश्चमसादिसाधननिष्पादनेन यज्ञस्य वोढार ऋभवोऽधारयन्त । पूर्वं मनुष्यत्वेन मरणयोग्या अप्यमृतत्वलाभेन प्राणान्धारितवन्तः । तथा च मन्त्रान्तरमाम्नायते । मर्तासः सन्तो अमृतत्वमानशुः । ऋग्वे. १-११०-४ । इति । किंचैते सुकृत्यया यज्ञसाधनद्रव्यसंपादनरूपेण शोभनव्यापारेण देवेषु मध्ये स्थिता यज्ञियं यज्ञार्हं भागं हविर्लक्षणमभजन्त । सेवितवन्तः । अयमर्थः सौधन्वना यज्ञियं भागमानश । ऋग्वे. ३-६०-१ । इत्यादिमन्त्रान्तरे विस्पष्टः । ब्राह्मणेऽप्यृभवो वै देवेषु तपसा सोमपीथमभ्यजयन् । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३० । इत्याद्युपाख्यानं विस्पष्टम् ॥ वह्नयः । निदित्यनुवृत्तौ वहिश्रीत्यादिना निप्रत्ययः । अभजन्त । पादादित्वादनिघातः । सुकृत्यया । विभाषा कृवृषोः । पा. ३-१-१२० । इति कृञः कर्मणि क्यप् । शोभनं कृत्यं यस्या भजनक्रियायाः सा सुकृत्या । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं बाधित्वा नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । ननु कृत्यशब्दे क्यपः पित्त्वेनानुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वरेणादिरुदात्तः । ततश्चाद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसीत्यनेनाद्युदात्तत्वेन भवितव्यम् । तेन हि पुरस्तादपवादेन परमपि नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं बाध्यत इत्युक्तम् । एवं तर्हि कृञः श च । पा. ३-३-१०० । इति स्त्रियां भावे क्यप्प्रत्ययान्तः कृत्याशब्दः । क्यपः पित्त्वेऽपि व्यत्ययेनोदात्तत्वम् । प्रादिसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन तदेव शिष्यते । भागम् । कर्षात्वतः । पा. ६-१-१५९ । इत्यन्तोदात्तः । यज्ञियम् । यज्ञमर्हतीत्यर्थे यज्ञर्त्विग्भ्यां घखञौ । पा. ५-१-७१ । इति घः । तस्य इयादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

vahnayaścamasādisādhananiṣpādanena yajñasya voḍhāra ṛbhavo 'dhārayanta | pūrvaṃ manuṣyatvena maraṇayogyā apyamṛtatvalābhena prāṇāndhāritavantaḥ | tathā ca mantrāntaramāmnāyate | martāsaḥ santo amṛtatvamānaśuḥ | ṛgve. 1-110-4 | iti | kiṃcaite sukṛtyayā yajñasādhanadravyasaṃpādanarūpeṇa śobhanavyāpāreṇa deveṣu madhye sthitā yajñiyaṃ yajñārhaṃ bhāgaṃ havirlakṣaṇamabhajanta | sevitavantaḥ | ayamarthaḥ saudhanvanā yajñiyaṃ bhāgamānaśa | ṛgve. 3-60-1 | ityādimantrāntare vispaṣṭaḥ | brāhmaṇe 'pyṛbhavo vai deveṣu tapasā somapīthamabhyajayan | ai. brā. 3-30 | ityādyupākhyānaṃ vispaṣṭam || vahnayaḥ | nidityanuvṛttau vahiśrītyādinā nipratyayaḥ | abhajanta | pādāditvādanighātaḥ | sukṛtyayā | vibhāṣā kṛvṛṣoḥ | pā. 3-1-120 | iti kṛñaḥ karmaṇi kyap | śobhanaṃ kṛtyaṃ yasyā bhajanakriyāyāḥ sā sukṛtyā | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ bādhitvā nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvam | nanu kṛtyaśabde kyapaḥ pittvenānudāttatvāddhātusvareṇādirudāttaḥ | tataścādyudāttaṃ dvyacchandasītyanenādyudāttatvena bhavitavyam | tena hi purastādapavādena paramapi nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ bādhyata ityuktam | evaṃ tarhi kṛñaḥ śa ca | pā. 3-3-100 | iti striyāṃ bhāve kyappratyayāntaḥ kṛtyāśabdaḥ | kyapaḥ pittve 'pi vyatyayenodāttatvam | prādisamāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvena tadeva śiṣyate | bhāgam | karṣātvataḥ | pā. 6-1-159 | ityantodāttaḥ | yajñiyam | yajñamarhatītyarthe yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau | pā. 5-1-71 | iti ghaḥ | tasya iyādeśaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ ||

Translation: "The vahnis, the Ṛbhus, bearers of the sacrifice by producing its means such as the camasa, adhārayanta, held: though formerly, as men, subject to death, by gaining immortality they held their life-breaths. So another mantra declares: 'Being mortals, they reached immortality' (Ṛgveda 1-110-4). And these, sukṛtyayā, by the fine activity in the form of producing the materials that are the means of sacrifice, standing among the gods, abhajanta, enjoyed the yajñiya, sacrifice-worthy, bhāga, share in the form of oblation. This sense is plain in other mantras such as 'Sons of Sudhanvan, you reached the sacrificial share' (Ṛgveda 3-60-1). In the Brāhmaṇa too the story is plain: 'The Ṛbhus by austerity won the soma-drinking among the gods' (Ai. Brā. 3-30)." (Grammatical tail: vahnayaḥ, the suffix ni by vahiśri…, with nit carried on; abhajanta, not lowered at the start of the pāda; sukṛtyayā, kyap in the object sense after kṛñ by vibhāṣā kṛvṛṣoḥ (Pā. 3-1-120); "the act of enjoying whose deed is fine" is sukṛtyā; in the bahuvrīhi, overriding the first member's accent, final udātta of the final member by nañsubhyām. An objection: in kṛtya, kyap being unaccented as pit, the first is udātta by the root accent; then by ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi initial udātta should come, for it was said that an exception placed before overrides the later nañsubhyām. Then let kṛtyā be a kyap-final in the feminine in the sense of the action by kṛñaḥ śa ca (Pā. 3-3-100), the kyap udātta by exchange though pit; in the prādi compound that alone stays by the accent of the kṛt final member; bhāgam, final udātta by karṣātvataḥ (Pā. 6-1-159); yajñiyam, gha in the sense "worthy of sacrifice" by yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau (Pā. 5-1-71), iy for it, the suffix accent.)

Page 39 — Rik 8: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

वह्नयः (vahnayaḥ) — these Ṛbhus, who carry out the sacrifice by making its means such as the camasa | अधारयन्त (adhārayanta) — (attained immortality) | सुकृत्यया (sukṛtyayā) — by good work | देवेषु (deveṣu) — among the gods | यज्ञियम् (yajñiyam) — connected with the sacrifice | भागम् (bhāgam) — the share of the oblation too | अभजन्त (abhajanta) — obtained.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

These Ṛbhus made the means of sacrifice and through that became helpers in the performance of sacrifice, and attained immortality. By doing good works connected with the sacrifice they obtained a share of the oblation together with the gods.

॥ English Translation ॥

Ribhus by their skill in fashioning sacrificial utensils and their pious acts lived for ever or became immortal ; they even obtained a share of the sacrifice along with the Gods.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

These Ṛbhus, by their skill in craft, made the means such as the camasa necessarily needed for sacrifice. In a single year they performed all the sacrifices and became worthy of the grace of the gods. By such good works these Ṛbhus became able to hold their life-breaths for ever. Like the gods, they attained immortality (freedom from death). And like the gods they too obtained the fitness to receive the share of the sacrifice, that is, the oblation offered to the gods in the sacrifice.

Adhārayanta: the sense of this word is "they held". Held what? They held their life-breaths. Or the commentator explains the sense as "they attained immortality". Though in this ṛk there are no words expressing the sense "they attained immortality", since it is said in many ṛks that these Ṛbhus, being men, attained divinity by their good works, it seems right that the commentator, taking that very intent here, has explained the word adhārayanta as said above. On this matter the ṛk

विष्ट्वी शमी तरणित्वेन वाघतो मर्तासः सन्तो अमृतत्वमानशुः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११०-४)

viṣṭvī śamī taraṇitvena vāghato martāsaḥ santo amṛtatvamānaśuḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-110-4)

("Having done the acts, the bearers, though mortals, by swiftness attained immortality": editorial and tentative.) states this intent clearly.

Page 40 — Rik 8: Special Topics (end) and grammar

Vahnayaḥ:

चमसादिसाधननिष्पादनेन यज्ञस्य वोढार ऋभवः ॥

camasādisādhananiṣpādanena yajñasya voḍhāra ṛbhavaḥ ||

("The Ṛbhus, bearers of the sacrifice by producing its means such as the camasa.") Because they make the means of sacrifice such as the camasa and so become helpers of the sacrifice, these Ṛbhus are called vahnayaḥ or voḍhāraḥ, that is, those who carry out the rite of sacrifice.

Yajñiyam:

यज्ञार्हं भागम् ॥

yajñārhaṃ bhāgam ||

("The share worthy of the sacrifice.") The share of oblation offered to the gods in the sacrifice. To obtain a share worthy of the sacrifice one must have the standing the gods have. The intent is that the Ṛbhus obtained such honour. This matter is supported in the ṛk

इहेह वो मनसा बन्धुता नर उशिजो जग्मुरभि तानि वेदसा । याभिर्मायाभिः प्रतिजूतिवर्पसः सौधन्वना यज्ञियं भागमानश ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-६०-१)

iheha vo manasā bandhutā nara uśijo jagmurabhi tāni vedasā | yābhirmāyābhiḥ pratijūtivarpasaḥ saudhanvanā yajñiyaṃ bhāgamānaśa || (ṛ. saṃ. 3-60-1)

("Here, here, O men, with your mind and kinship, the eager ones went to those things with knowledge; by the wonders with which, swift of form, sons of Sudhanvan, you reached the sacrificial share": editorial and tentative.) and in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa statement

ब्राह्मणेऽप्यृभवो वै देवेषु तपसा सोमपीथमभ्यजयन् (ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३०)

brāhmaṇe 'pyṛbhavo vai deveṣu tapasā somapīthamabhyajayan (ai. brā. 3-30)

("The Ṛbhus by austerity won the soma-drinking among the gods.")

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 40–43, noted briefly

वह्नयः (vahnayaḥ): "vahiśriśruyudruglāhātvaribhyo nit" (Uṇ. sū. "4-491", zoom-checked); here niḥ is carried on from "vījyājvaribhyo niḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "4-488", zoom-checked). So the sense of the sūtra is that after the roots vaha prāpaṇe and the rest the suffix ni comes, and it is nit; the same explanation is in the Bhāṣya at (Ṛ. saṃ. 3, ṛ. 9). The word nit is not seen in the preceding Uṇādi sūtras. So "nid ity anuvṛttau" here has come through an oversight of the correctors. When the suffix ni comes after the root vah, vahni results. The suffix being nit, the nit accent gives initial udātta.

अभजन्त (abhajanta): this stands at the start of a pāda; so by "anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau" the bar comes. Therefore it is not wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ".

सुकृत्यया (sukṛtyayā): by "vibhāṣā kṛvṛṣoḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-120) the suffix kyap comes after the roots kṛ and vṛṣ; so the suffix kyap [as printed: "tyap"] in the object sense comes after the root kṛ: kṛ + ya. By "hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk" (Pā. sū. 6-1-71), when a kṛt suffix with p as it follows, a short-final aṅga takes the augment tuk; so the augment tuk; the suffix being kit, guṇa is barred: kṛtya. Śobhanaṃ, good, kṛtyam, the work; yasyāḥ, the act of enjoying that has it is called sukṛtyā. So this is a bahuvrīhi compound.

Page 41 — Rik 8: grammar

So by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1), in a bahuvrīhi compound the first member keeps its own accent: the first-member accent is due. The first member su is udātta by "upasargāś cābhivarjam" (Phi. sū. 81); so, if the first-member accent came, su would be initial udātta and the rest would have to be unaccented by the lowering of the remainder. But "nañsubhyām" (Pā. sū. 6-2-172), the final udātta of the final member enjoined after nañ and su in a bahuvrīhi, overrides the first-member accent enjoined by bahuvrīhau. So in sukṛtya the last letter is udātta and the rest take the lowering of the remainder. But here there is a question. The suffix kyap is pit; so by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4) it is unaccented. And in kṛtya, by the initial-udātta accent of "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-162), kṛ is udātta; thus kṛtya is initial udātta; then by "ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi" (Pā. sū. 6-2-119), in a bahuvrīhi compound a two-vowel word after su that is initial udātta keeps the initial udātta in the Veda; since that is enjoined, by this sūtra the final member kṛtya would have to be initial udātta. Though the rule nañsubhyām is read later in the Aṣṭādhyāyī than the rule ādyudāttaṃ dvyac, nañsubhyām does not apply by vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam (Pā. sū. 1-4-2). For ādyudāttaṃ dvyac, though read earlier, is the exception to nañsubhyām. That is, in an instance where nañsubhyām does not apply, ādyudāttaṃ dvyac does not apply either; so, since the definition of conflict,

अन्यत्र चरितार्थयोः शास्त्रयोरेकत्र युगपत्समावेशो विप्रतिषेधः

anyatra caritārthayoḥ śāstrayorekatra yugapatsamāveśo vipratiṣedhaḥ

("Conflict is the meeting at once, in one place, of two rules each with its own scope elsewhere"), is absent, vipratiṣedhe param does not apply. By

येन नाप्राप्ते यो विधिरारभ्यते स तस्य बाधको भवति

yena nāprāpte yo vidhirārabhyate sa tasya bādhako bhavati

("A rule begun where another would necessarily apply overrides it", paribhāṣā "58" (zoom-checked)), it seems natural that ādyudāttaṃ dvyac alone should apply. On that view, in "kṛñaḥ śa ca" (Pā. sū. 3-3-100), śa is a word ending in the first case with the ending dropped; the sense of the sūtra comes out that after the root kṛñ, in the sense of the action and so on, the suffix śa comes, and by the ca the suffix kyap. On this view the two forms kṛtyā and kriyā are established, but kṛtiḥ is not. For "striyāṃ ktin" (Pā. sū. 3-3-94), which enjoins the suffix ktin, is in the feminine section. So, since there is the bar astriyām, it does not come here that by "vāsarūpo 'striyām" (Pā. sū. 3-1-94) in the section "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-91), an exception suffix of different form, enjoined other than in the feminine section, optionally overrides the general rule; for here both the general rule "striyāṃ ktin" (Pā. sū. 3-3-94) and the exception "kṛñaḥ śa ca" are

Page 42 — Rik 8: grammar

in the feminine section; so, since the bar astriyām comes, the exception does not override optionally; then the very form kṛtiḥ would be lacking. So the rule "kṛñaḥ śa ca" is divided into two, "kṛñaḥ" and "śa ca": the sense of the first is that in the feminine the suffix kyap comes after the root kṛñ in the sense of the action and so on. By this kṛtyā is established. For "śa ca" the sense is that in the feminine, after the root kṛñ, in the sense of the action and so on, the suffix śa, and by the ca the suffix ktin, come; since kyap is established from the previous part, the ca does not add kyap but adds ktin; thus the forms kriyā and kṛtiḥ are established. In the present case, by the divided first sūtra "kṛñaḥ", kyap comes in the sense of the action; thus kṛtyā is final udātta; śobhanā ca sā kṛtyā ca: if the prādi compound is made by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-2-18), the accent of the kṛt final member comes by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt"; so in sukṛtya this same accent stays. Since the feminine is shown, by "ajādyataṣ ṭāp" (Pā. sū. 4-1-4) ṭāp: sukṛtya + ā; ṭāp, being pit, is unaccented; with the preceding a the lengthening of like vowels; by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" the single substitute is udātta. For the instrumental singular ṭā that follows, by "anudāttau suppitau" it is unaccented. With sukṛtya + ā, by "āṅi cāpaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-105), before āṅ (the instrumental singular) and os, an aṅga ending in āp takes the substitute e; so in sukṛtya the a takes e, then ay; by "udāttād anudāttasya" the ending becomes svarita: sukṛtyayā.

भागम् (bhāgam): the root bhaja sevāyām. By "halaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-3-121), after a consonant-final root the suffix ghañ comes: ghañ. By "cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-52), when a suffix with gh as it or the suffix ṇyat follows, c and j take the guttural: so g for the j; by "ata upadhāyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-116) the penultimate vṛddhi: bhāga. Now initial udātta would be due by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); its exception, "karṣātvato ghaño 'nta udāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-159): after the root karṣ and roots having ā, the end of the word ending in the ghañ suffix is udātta; so bhāga is final udātta.

यज्ञियम् (yajñiyam): the analysis is yajñam arhati. By "yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau" (Pā. sū. 5-1-71), after the accusative-final words yajña and ṛtvij, in the sense "arhati", the suffixes

Page 43 (upper) — Rik 8: grammar (end)

gha and khañ come respectively; so the suffix gha after yajñam; the sup that is part of the stem takes luk. By "āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām" (Pā. sū. 7-1-2) iy for gh; by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148) the a before the suffix drops: yajñiya. The suffix accent comes; yajñiyam ends in the accusative singular.

इहेन्द्राग्नी इत्यादिकं षडृचं चतुर्थं सूक्तम् । तस्य ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । देवता त्वनुक्रम्यते । इह षळैन्द्राग्नमिति ॥ विनियोगस्तु । अग्निष्टोमेऽच्छावाकशस्त्र इहेन्द्राग्नी उप ह्वय इति सूक्तम् । स्तोत्रमग्ने शस्त्रादिति खण्ड इहेन्द्राग्नी उपेयं वामस्य मन्मन इति नव ॥ आ. ५-१० । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥ तथाभिप्लवषडहे प्रातःसवनेऽच्छावाकशस्त्रे स्तोमातिशंसनार्थमेतदेव सूक्तम् । तथा च सूत्रितम् । अभिप्लवपृष्ठ्याहानीत्युपक्रम्येहेन्द्राग्नी इन्द्राग्नी आ गतम् ॥ आ. ७-५ । इति ॥

ihendrāgnī ityādikaṃ ṣaḍṛcaṃ caturthaṃ sūktam | tasya ṛṣicchandasī pūrvavat | devatā tvanukramyate | iha ṣaḷaindrāgnamiti || viniyogastu | agniṣṭome 'cchāvākaśastra ihendrāgnī upa hvaya iti sūktam | stotramagne śastrāditi khaṇḍa ihendrāgnī upeyaṃ vāmasya manmana iti nava || ā. 5-10 | iti sūtritatvāt || tathābhiplavaṣaḍahe prātaḥsavane 'cchāvākaśastre stomātiśaṃsanārthametadeva sūktam | tathā ca sūtritam | abhiplavapṛṣṭhyāhānītyupakramyehendrāgnī indrāgnī ā gatam || ā. 7-5 | iti ||

Translation: "The sūkta beginning ihendrāgnī, of six ṛks, is the fourth. Its ṛṣi and metre are as before. The deity is stated in the Anukramaṇī: 'iha: six, to Indra and Agni.' The application: in the agniṣṭoma, at the acchāvāka-śastra, the sūkta ihendrāgnī upa hvaye, because it is laid down in the section stotram agne śastrāt: 'ihendrāgnī and upeyaṃ vām asya manmanaḥ: nine' (Āśv. 5-10). Likewise in the abhiplava ṣaḍaha, at the morning pressing, at the acchāvāka-śastra, for the stomātiśaṃsana, this same sūkta: so it is laid down: beginning 'abhiplava and pṛṣṭhya days', 'ihendrāgnī, indrāgnī ā gatam' (Āśv. 7-5)."

Anuvāda (Kannada rendering): The sūkta ihendrāgnī is the fourth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has six ṛks. The ṛṣi and metres of this sūkta are as in the previous sūkta. In the Anukramaṇikā, iha ṣaḷ aindrāgnam iti, it is said that the sūkta of six ṛks ihendrāgnī has Indra and Agni as deities. The application: in the agniṣṭoma rite, when the priest called acchāvāka recites the śastra mantras, the sūkta ihendrāgnī upa hvaye is to be recited. This is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, in the section stotram agne śastrāt, by the sūtra ihendrāgnī upeyaṃ vām asya manmana iti nava (Ā. 5-10). And in the rite called abhiplava ṣaḍaha, at the time of the morning pressing, the acchāvāka priest recites this sūkta for the stomātiśaṃsana. On this the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra says abhiplavapṛṣṭhyāhānīty upakramyehendrāgnī indrāgnī ā gatam (Ā. 7-5).

इ॒हेन्द्रा॒ग्नी उप॑ ह्वये॒ त॒योरित्स्तोम॑मुश्मसि । [accent ?] ता सोमं॑ सोम॒पात॑मा ॥१॥

ihéndrāgnī́ úpa hvaye tayór it stómam uśmasi | [accent ?] tā sómaṃ somapā́tamā ||1|| Bars under इ, द्रा, ये (ह्वये) and, as read, यो (तयोः); strokes over प, म (स्तोमम्), मं and त (पातमा). The bar in तयोः stands between त and यो [accent ?].

iha | indrāgnī iti | upa | hvaye | tayoḥ | it | stomam | uśmasi || tā | somam | soma 'pātamā ||1||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इहास्मिन्कर्मणीन्द्राग्नी देवावुप ह्वये । आह्वयामि । तयोरिन्द्राग्न्योरेव स्तोमं स्तोत्रमुश्मसि । कामयामहे । सोमपातमातिशयेन सोमं पातुं क्षमौ ता तौ देवौ सोमं पिबतामिति शेषः ॥ इन्द्राग्नी । अत्र देवताद्वन्द्वेऽपि पूर्वपदस्यानङ् न भवति । तत्र हि द्वन्द्व इत्यनुवृत्तौ पुनर्द्वन्द्वग्रहणाल्लोकप्रसिद्धसाहचर्याणामेव द्वन्द्व आनङित्युक्तम् । का. ६-३-२६ । तस्मादत्रावग्रहे ह्रस्व इन्द्रशब्दः । समासस्येत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं तु न भवति । अग्निशब्दस्यानुदात्तादित्वेन नोत्तरपदेऽनुदात्तादौ । पा. ६-२-१४२ । इति प्रतिषेधात् । उश्मसि । वश कान्तौ । लटो मस् । इदन्तो मसि । पा. ७-१-४६ । इतीकारोपजनः । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । मसेर्ङित्त्वाद्ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना संप्रसारणम् । ता सोमपातमा । उभयत्र सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः ॥

ihāsminkarmaṇīndrāgnī devāvupa hvaye | āhvayāmi | tayorindrāgnyoreva stomaṃ stotramuśmasi | kāmayāmahe | somapātamātiśayena somaṃ pātuṃ kṣamau tā tau devau somaṃ pibatāmiti śeṣaḥ || indrāgnī | atra devatādvandve 'pi pūrvapadasyānaṅ na bhavati | tatra hi dvandva ityanuvṛttau punardvandvagrahaṇāllokaprasiddhasāhacaryāṇāmeva dvandva ānaṅityuktam | kā. 6-3-26 | tasmādatrāvagrahe hrasva indraśabdaḥ | samāsasyetyantodāttatvam | devatādvandve cetyubhayapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ tu na bhavati | agniśabdasyānudāttāditvena nottarapade 'nudāttādau | pā. 6-2-142 | iti pratiṣedhāt | uśmasi | vaśa kāntau | laṭo mas | idanto masi | pā. 7-1-46 | itīkāropajanaḥ | adāditvācchapo luk | maserṅittvādgrahijyetyādinā saṃprasāraṇam | tā somapātamā | ubhayatra supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ ||

Page 45 — Rik 1: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

Translation: "Iha, in this rite, I upa hvaye, call, the two gods Indra and Agni. Tayoḥ it, of just those two, Indra and Agni, we uśmasi, desire the stoma, hymn. May those two gods, somapātamā, most able to drink soma, drink the soma: that is to be supplied." (Grammatical tail: indrāgnī, here, though a dvandva of deities, the first member does not take ānaṅ; for there, with dvandve carried on, by mentioning dvandva again it is said that ānaṅ is for a dvandva of those whose association is well known in the world (Kā. 6-3-26); so in the avagraha the word indra is short; final udātta by samāsasya; both members do not keep their accent by devatādvandve ca, since agni begins with an unaccented syllable and there is the bar notarapade 'nudāttādau (Pā. 6-2-142); uśmasi, vaśa kāntau, mas of laṭ, the i added by idanto masi (Pā. 7-1-46), śap dropped as an ad-ādi, saṃprasāraṇa by grahijyā… as masi is ṅit; tā, somapātamā, in both the ā by supāṃ suluk….)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इह (iha) — in this rite | इन्द्राग्नी (indrāgnī) — Indra and Agni | उप ह्वये (upa hvaye) — I call | तयोः इत् (tayoḥ it) — of those two alone | स्तोमम् (stomam) — (to make) praise | उश्मसि (uśmasi) — we desire | सोमपातमा (somapātamā) — able to drink soma | ता (tā) — those two | सोमम् (somam) — the soma juice (we have made ready) (may they drink).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Here (for this rite) we call the deities Indra and Agni and make praise. Both of them are especially fit to drink soma: may they drink the soma juice that we have made ready.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

I invoke hither, Indra and Agni ; we desire to present our praise to them; let them who are both greatest drinkers of Soma juice, drink our Soma.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

Uśmasi: vaśa kāntau; kāmayāmahe: we desire.

Somapātamā: somasya atiśayena pātārau: those who drink soma very much.

In this sūkta the deities Indra and Agni are praised together. Praising two deities joined together in this way is special to the Ṛgveda. Mantras that set forth a pair of deities are named saṃstavika mantras (Ni. "7-8", zoom-checked). We have written on this matter before (Ṛgveda-saṃhitā Part 2, pages 710–712).

Page 46 — Rik 1: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar pages 46–48, noted briefly

इन्द्राग्नी (indrāgnī): indraś ca agniś ca indrāgnī: a dvandva compound. By the sūtra "devatādvandve ca" (Pā. sū. 6-3-26), whereby the member before the final member of a dvandva compound naming deities takes the substitute ānaṅ, indrāgnī, though a dvandva naming deities, does not take ānaṅ. For with dvandve carried on from the previous sūtra "ānaṅ ṛto dvandve" (Pā. sū. 6-3-25), when the sense of the sentence is formed, Pāṇini placed the word dvandve again in devatādvandve ca; his intent is that if, carrying on the word of the previous sūtra, this word were not added here, then, since before the word dvandva takes all dvandvas, well known or not, here too all dvandvas would be taken. So ānaṅ would have to come in brahmaprajāpatī too. By the force of using the word dvandva again, it is established that in devatādvandve ca only dvandvas expressing well-known association are taken. Brahmaprajāpatī is not a dvandva expressing well-known association. So there ānaṅ does not come. In the Mahābhāṣya, at the time of rejecting the vārttika "brahmaprajāpatyādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 6-3-26-2), begun to bar the substitute ānaṅ in brahmaprajāpatī, it is described as

स तर्हि वक्तव्यः । न वक्तव्यः । द्वन्द्व इति वर्तमाने पुनर्द्वन्द्वग्रहणस्यैतत्प्रयोजनं लोकवेदयोर्यो द्वन्द्वस्तत्र यथा स्यात् । कश्च लोकवेदयोर्द्वन्द्वः । वेदे ये सहनिर्वापनिर्दिष्टाः । न चैते वेदे सहनिर्वापनिर्दिष्टाः ॥

sa tarhi vaktavyaḥ | na vaktavyaḥ | dvandva iti vartamāne punardvandvagrahaṇasyaitatprayojanaṃ lokavedayoryo dvandvastatra yathā syāt | kaśca lokavedayordvandvaḥ | vede ye sahanirvāpanirdiṣṭāḥ | na caite vede sahanirvāpanirdiṣṭāḥ ||

("Should it then be stated? It need not be stated. While dvandve is current, the purpose of mentioning dvandva again is this: that it should apply to a dvandva of the world and of the Veda. And what is a dvandva of the world and of the Veda? Those named in the Veda as offered together. And these are not named in the Veda as offered together": editorial and tentative.) Sahanirvāpa means "giving together". Here first the mental resolve of giving the oblation, as in indrāvaruṇābhyāṃ juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi, and then, by uttering words such as svāhā, throwing the oblation into the fire: the giving up to the end of one's ownership is meant by nirvāpa; by the word loka the Kalpasūtras are meant; the association of the words in indrāgnī is not well known in this way in the world and the Veda. So here the substitute ānaṅ does not come. In the Kāśikā too it is said: "dvandva ity anuvṛttau punar dvandvagrahaṇāt lokaprasiddhasāhacaryāṇām eva dvandve ānaṅ" (Kā. "3-6-26" [as printed, for 6-3-26]). Though whether ānaṅ comes or not the form is indrāgnī alone, what then is the result of barring ānaṅ here? If ānaṅ came, in the veṣṭana (the avagraha) one would have to say indrāgnī itīndrā agnī. If ānaṅ does not come, it becomes indrāgnī itīndra agnī; for this distinction ānaṅ must not be accepted here. But since uttarapade is a locative statement, by "tasminn iti nirdiṣṭe pūrvasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-66) the sense "of what immediately precedes" is established; thus the sense of the sūtra is "devatāvācakadvandvaghaṭakottarapadāvyavahitapūrvasya ānaṅ bhavati"; in the veṣṭana, in indrāgnī itīndrā-agnī, though there is no separation made by a letter,

Page 47 — Rik 1: grammar

there is a separation made by time. So how does ānaṅ come in the veṣṭana? Tasminn iti nirdiṣṭe pūrvasya bars only separation made by a letter; it does not bar separation made by time. So the starting of the heading-sūtra "saṃhitāyām" is made purposeful. Otherwise, in sūtras such as "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-77), since the specified is taken in tasminn iti, yaṇ and the rest would not come when there is a separation made by time or by a letter; then the heading saṃhitā would be useless. So by the indication of the starting of the saṃhitā heading, the paribhāṣā tasminn iti does not bar separation made by time. In this avagraha, since there is no separation made by a letter, ānaṅ would have to come. So it must become "indrāgnī itīndrā agnī"; the short word indra is right in the avagraha. So here the substitute ānaṅ must not be made. Indrāgnī is final udātta by "samāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-223); the word agni ends in the suffix ni; it is final udātta by the suffix accent, and the a takes anudātta by the lowering of the remainder: this is set out at agnim īḷe. So the word agni is established as beginning with an unaccented syllable; therefore, since by "notarapade 'nudāttādāv apṛthivīrudrapūṣamanthiṣu" (Pā. sū. 6-2-142) there is the bar that, when a final member beginning with an unaccented syllable other than pṛthivī and the rest follows, the accent of both members stated before does not come, the accent of both members enjoined by "devatādvandve ca" (Pā. sū. 6-2-141), that in a dvandva of deities the former and latter members keep their own accent at once, does not come.

उश्मसि (uśmasi): the root vaśa kāntau; laṭ, 1st plural mas: vaś + mas. "Idanto masi" (Pā. sū. 7-1-46): masi is a statement without a case-ending; the i is for pronunciation. In idantaḥ the word anta means "part": it, the i, antaḥ, a part, yasya saḥ: such is the analysis; in it, if the t were not there, yaṇ would come and it would have to be yantaḥ, and the doubt would arise whether the sūtra specifies i or y. To prevent this doubt the t is added in it. So the sense of the sūtra is that the s-final word mas has i as its final part. If i were meant as a substitute, for brevity the sūtra should have been arranged as mas it; so, even without the marks of augments such as ṭ-ness or k-ness, i is an augment. And if the sūtra were made masa ik, whatever sense there is, that same sense results; then why not arrange it so? Because, if arranged so, the doubt would arise that ik is a pratyāhāra. To remove this doubt it is not arranged so. In the present case, in mas, by "idanto masi" the augment i comes: vaś + masi; the root vaś is of the ad-ādi. So for the vikaraṇa that would follow,

Page 48 (upper) — Rik 1: grammar (end)

for the vikaraṇa śap, by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72), luk; by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) masi is ṅit. So by "grahijyāvayivyadhivaṣṭivicativṛścatipṛcchatibhṛjjatīnāṃ ṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-16), when a kit or ṅit suffix follows, the roots grah and the rest take saṃprasāraṇa: saṃprasāraṇa, u for v; pūrvarūpa: uśmasi.

ता (tā): the sense is tau.

सोमपातमा (somapātamā): somaṃ pibati iti somapau; atiśayena somapau, somapātamau, tā; in both places, somapātamā, for the nominative dual suffix au, by the sūtra "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39), the substitute ā comes.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता य॒ज्ञेषु॒ प्र शं॑सतेन्द्रा॒ग्नी शु॑म्भता नरः । ता गा॑य॒त्रेषु॑ गायत ॥२॥

tā yajñéṣu prá śaṃsatendrāgnī́ śumbhatā naraḥ | tā́ gāyatréṣu gāyata ||2|| Bars under य (यज्ञेषु), षु and द्रा; strokes over शं and शु. Line 2: stroke over गा, bar under य, stroke over षु. The Saṃhitā has the lengthened śumbhatā, the Pada the short śumbhata.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता । यज्ञेषु । प्र । शंसत । इन्द्राग्नी इति । शुम्भत । नरः ॥ ता । गायत्रेषु । गायत ॥२॥

tā | yajñeṣu | pra | śaṃsata | indrāgnī iti | śumbhata | naraḥ || tā | gāyatreṣu | gāyata ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे नरो मनुष्या ऋत्विजः ता पूर्वोक्तौ ताविन्द्राग्नी यज्ञेष्वनुष्ठीयमानकर्मसु प्र शंसत शस्त्रैः । तथा शुम्भत । नानाविधैरलंकारैः शोभितौ कुरुत । तथा ता पूर्वोक्तौ ताविन्द्राग्नी गायत्रेषु गायत्रीच्छन्दस्केषु मन्त्रेषु सामरूपेण गायत ॥ ता । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । शुम्भत । अस्य संहितायामन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घः ॥

he naro manuṣyā ṛtvijaḥ tā pūrvoktau tāvindrāgnī yajñeṣvanuṣṭhīyamānakarmasu pra śaṃsata śastraiḥ | tathā śumbhata | nānāvidhairalaṃkāraiḥ śobhitau kuruta | tathā tā pūrvoktau tāvindrāgnī gāyatreṣu gāyatrīcchandaskeṣu mantreṣu sāmarūpeṇa gāyata || tā | supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | śumbhata | asya saṃhitāyāmanyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti dīrghaḥ ||

Translation: "O naraḥ, men — priests! Tā, those two, Indra and Agni, spoken of before, pra śaṃsata, praise, yajñeṣu, in the rites being performed, with śastras. Likewise śumbhata: make them beautiful with ornaments of many kinds. Likewise tā, those same two, Indra and Agni, gāyata, sing, gāyatreṣu, in mantras of the Gāyatrī metre, in the form of sāman." (Grammatical tail: tā, the ā by supāṃ suluk…; śumbhata, its lengthening in the Saṃhitā by anyeṣām api dṛśyate.)

Page 49 — Rik 2: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हे नरः (he naraḥ) — O men (priests) | ता (tā) — the Indra and Agni spoken of before | यज्ञेषु (yajñeṣu) — in the sacrifices | प्र शंसत (pra śaṃsata) — praise well | शुम्भत (śumbhata) — adorn (with ornaments of many kinds) | ता (tā) — both of them | गायत्रेषु (gāyatreṣu) — with ṛks of the Gāyatrī metre | गायत (gāyata) — sing (praise).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O priests, praise well Indra and Agni, set forth before, adorn them with ornaments, and sing them in the manner of sāman singing with ṛks of the Gāyatrī metre.

॥ English Translation ॥

O men, praise Indra and Agni in Sacrifices, decorate them with ornaments and sing them with hymns of Gayatri metres.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In this ṛk the ṛṣi addresses the people, that is, the priests engaged in performing the sacrifice.

शुम्भत (śumbhata) — "adorn", decorate. What is meant here by adorning the deities? How can they, who are not visible, be adorned? This point is not clear.

गायत्रेषु (gāyatreṣu) — with ṛks of the Gāyatrī metre, or with the sāman mantra called gāyatra in the Sāmaveda. Because there is a rule that in all three pressings, the morning pressing and the rest, many ṛks of the seven kinds of metre beginning with Gāyatrī are to be recited, and because the praise is made first with the Gāyatrī metre itself, the ṛṣi, in saying gāyatreṣu here, has addressed the priests and told them: praise with ṛks of the Gāyatrī metre.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

ता (tā) — here too the ā in place of the case-ending by the sūtra supāṃ suluk etc.

शुम्भत (śumbhata) — for this, in the Saṃhitā, lengthening by anyeṣām api dṛśyate (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137), which says that in the Saṃhitā lengthening comes also to words other than those named in the lengthening rules. ॥2॥

Rik 3 pp. 50

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता मि॒त्रस्य॒ प्रश॑स्तय इन्द्रा॒ग्नी ता ह॑वामहे । सो॒म॒पा सोम॑पीतये ॥३॥

tā mitrásya práśastaya indrāgnī́ tā́ havāmahe | somapā́ sómapītaye ||3|| Bars under मि and स्य (मित्रस्य) and द्रा; strokes over श (प्रशस्तय) and ह (हवामहे). Line 2: bars under सो and म (सोमपा), stroke over म (सोमपीतये).

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता । मित्रस्य । प्रऽशस्तये । इन्द्राग्नी इति । ता । हवामहे ॥ सोमऽपा । सोमऽपीतये ॥३॥

tā | mitrasya | pra 'śastaye | indrāgnī iti | tā | havāmahe || soma 'pā | soma 'pītaye ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

मित्रस्य स्नेहविषयस्य ममानुष्ठातुः प्रशस्तये ता पूर्वोक्तौ देवौ संपद्येतामिति शेषः । यद्वा । मित्रस्य मम संबन्धिनौ ताविन्द्राग्नी प्रशस्तये प्रशंसितुमिच्छाम इति शेषः । सोमपा सोमपानक्षमौ ता पूर्वोक्ताविन्द्राग्नी सोमपीतये सोमपानार्थं हवामहे । आह्वयामः ॥ प्रशस्तये । तुमर्थाच्च भाववचनात् । पा० २-३-१५ । इति चतुर्थी । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं बाधित्वा तादौ च निति कृत्यतौ । पा० ६-२-५० । इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सोमपीतये । सोमस्य पीतिर्यस्मिन्कर्मणि तस्मै । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सोमस्य पीतिरिति तत्पुरुषे वा दासीभारादित्वात्पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

mitrasya snehaviṣayasya mamānuṣṭhātuḥ praśastaye tā pūrvoktau devau saṃpadyetāmiti śeṣaḥ | yadvā | mitrasya mama saṃbandhinau tāvindrāgnī praśastaye praśaṃsitumicchāma iti śeṣaḥ | somapā somapānakṣamau tā pūrvoktāvindrāgnī somapītaye somapānārthaṃ havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ || praśastaye | tumarthācca bhāvavacanāt | pā0 2-3-15 | iti caturthī | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ bādhitvā tādau ca niti kṛtyatau | pā0 6-2-50 | iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | somapītaye | somasya pītiryasminkarmaṇi tasmai | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | somasya pītiriti tatpuruṣe vā dāsībhārāditvātpūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "Mitrasya, of the friend — of me, the performer, the object of affection — praśastaye, for the praise, may tā, those two gods spoken of before, come to be [ours]: sampadyetām is to be supplied. Or: those two, Indra and Agni, connected with me, the mitra, we wish to praise (praśastaye): 'we wish' is to be supplied. Somapā, able to drink soma, tā, those two, Indra and Agni, spoken of before, we havāmahe, call, somapītaye, for the drinking of soma." (Grammatical tail: praśastaye, the fourth case by tumarthāc ca bhāvavacanāt (Pā. 2-3-15); overriding the accent of a kṛt final member, the prefix keeps its own accent by tādau ca niti kṛty atau (Pā. 6-2-50); somapītaye, 'for the rite in which there is a drinking of soma', a bahuvrīhi with the first member's accent; or, as the tatpuruṣa 'drinking of soma', the first member's accent because it belongs to the dāsībhāra class.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ता (tā) — those Indra and Agni | मित्रस्य (mitrasya) — of the one who is dear (the sacrificer) | प्रशस्तये (praśastaye) — for (the purpose of) praise; we make the hymn | सोमपा (somapā) — who drink soma | ता इन्द्राग्नी (tā indrāgnī) — those Indra and the other | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — for drinking soma | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we call.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

We call Indra and Agni, who drink soma, to drink soma. Having drunk the soma and being satisfied, may they become the cause of praise for the sacrificer, our friend.

Page 51 — Rik 3: English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

For the benefit of our friend (worshipper) we invoke Indra and Agni, drinkers of Soma juice, to drink the Soma libation.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

ता मित्रस्य प्रशस्तये (tā mitrasya praśastaye) — since there is no verb in this sentence, the commentator says that the verb gāyata of the previous ṛk must be supplied (adhyāhāra). Accordingly the sentence means: praise, that is, make a hymn to, those Indra and Agni for the prosperity (for the sake) of the sacrificer, our (your) friend.

In this ṛk the word tā occurs twice. And in somapā somapītaye too the matter of soma-drinking comes with repetition. Such usages are seen here and there in the Ṛgveda, especially. Such repeated usages may have been current either for the sake of the metre or following the usage of the language of that time. The Kannada note says the bhāṣya supplies gāyata; the bhāṣya as printed on p. 50 supplies sampadyetām or "we wish". Both as printed.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

प्रशस्तये (praśastaye) — the root śaṃsu stutau of the first class, with the prefix pra. After it, ktin having been laid down by striyāṃ ktin (Pā. Sū. 3-3-94) under the heading bhāve (Pā. Sū. 3-3-18), when an action for the sake of another action is the upapada, the suffix ktin comes by the sūtra bhāvavacanāś ca (Pā. Sū. 3-3-11). Since there is a prohibition in titutratathasisusarakaseṣu ca (Pā. Sū. 7-2-9), the augment iṭ does not come. By aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti (Pā. Sū. 6-4-24) the penultimate n is dropped. [On the objection:] by the saying nakārajāv anusvārapañcamau jhali dhātuṣu, in place of n the anusvāra comes by naś cāpadāntasya jhali (Pā. Sū. 8-3-24), the form being śaṃs; this anusvāra is asiddha by pūrvatrāsiddham (Pā. Sū. 8-2-1) when the penultimate n is dropped, so the n is present, and its dropping comes in the manner stated before. By kugatiprādayaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-2-18) the compound with pra gives praśasti. After this the fourth case comes by tumarthāc ca bhāvavacanāt (Pā. Sū. 2-3-15). By tumunṇvulau kriyāyāṃ kriyārthāyām (Pā. Sū. 3-3-10), when an action meant for another action is the upapada, the suffixes tumun and ṇvul come after the root in the future sense; examples: bhoktuṃ vrajati, bhojako vrajati; in both examples, the future action of eating being the purpose, vrajati —

Page 52 — Rik 3: grammar (continued)

— the action is the upapada; so tumun and ṇvul have come after the root bhuj as alternatives. In tumarthāt the analysis is tumaḥ artha iva artho yasya saḥ: 'that which conveys the sense the suffix tumun has' is the word-meaning; and with bhāvaḥ kriyā, ucyate 'nena iti vacanaḥ, bhāvasya vacanaḥ, tasmāt, it means 'expressing an action' (kriyāvācinaḥ). The word pratyayāt must be supplied (adhyāhāra: vivakṣitavākyārthapūrakapadānusandhānam adhyāhāraḥ). Here, since by the rule avyayakṛto bhāve the suffix tumun is laid down only in the sense of the action itself, the action-sense is established by tumarthāt alone; so the further mention of the word bhāvavacana is for taking a particular sūtra; that is, bhāvavacanāt is meant to say 'laid down by the sūtra bhāvavacanāś ca (Pā. Sū. 3-3-11)'; bhāvavacanāś ca means that the suffixes ghañ and the rest, laid down under the heading bhāve (Pā. Sū. 3-3-18), come in the future sense also when an action meant for another action is the upapada; example yāgāya yāti. In pratyayāt, by the pratyayagrahaṇa-paribhāṣā, what ends in it is obtained. So the sense of the sūtra: after nominal stems ending in those suffixes which have the same sense as the suffix tumun and are laid down by the sūtra bhāvavacanāś ca, the fourth case comes. If the word tumarthāt were not there, bhāvavacanāt would mean 'after one with the action-sense'; then in places like pākaḥ, tyāgaḥ, where ghañ has come by bhāve and there is the action-sense, the fourth case would have to come here too; tumarthāt establishes 'when an action meant for another action is the upapada'; here, there being no other action meant for it, the fourth case does not come. If bhāvavacanāś ca were not there, in pācako vrajati the word ending in the suffix ṇvul has a suffix with the same sense as tumun, so the fourth case would have to come; so bhāvavacanāt is needed. With it, since ṇvul is not laid down under the heading bhāve, pāka [as printed; for pācaka] does not have as its last part a suffix laid down by the sūtra bhāvavacanāś ca, so the fourth case does not come. So both tumarthāt and bhāvavacanāt serve to obtain the meaning stated. In the present case, in the explanation tau mitrasya praśastaye sampadyetām, sampadyetām is the action that is the purpose; that is, the praśasti arises for the performer only after the deities Indra and Agni spoken of before have come; so the sampatti serves the action of praising; therefore, the action of sampatti meant for the praising-action being the upapada, ktin comes by bhāvavacanāś ca. In the second explanation, the action of wishing being the upapada, —

Page 53 (upper) — Rik 3: grammar (end)

— after praśaṃs, ktin; so praśasti, ending in the suffix ktin, having the same sense as the suffix tumun and laid down by the sūtra bhāvavacanāś ca, takes the fourth case after it by the sūtra tumarthāt etc. By gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the accent of the kṛt final member would be obtained; overriding it, by tādau ca niti kṛty atau (Pā. Sū. 6-2-50) — when a kṛt suffix other than tu, beginning with t and without the marker n, follows, the gati immediately before keeps its own accent — the first member keeps its own accent; by upasargāś cābhivarjam, pra is accented on its first syllable.

सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — somasya pītir yasmin karmaṇi tasmai: a bahuvrīhi; by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam the first member keeps its own accent. Even if the tatpuruṣa somasya pītiḥ is made, by kuru gārhapata riktagurvasūtajaratyaślīla dṛḍharūpā pārevaḍavā taitilakadrūḥ paṇyakambalo dāsībhārāṇāṃ ca (Pā. Sū. 6-2-42) — the first members of these seven compounds and of the words in the dāsībhārādi class keep their own accent — the first member keeps its own accent. ॥3॥
