॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उ॒ग्रा सन्ता॑ हवाम॒ह उ॒पे॑दं सव॑नं सु॒तं । इ॒न्द्रा॒ग्नी एह ग॑च्छताम् ॥४॥

ugrā́ sántā havāmahá upedaṃ sávanaṃ sutáṃ | indrāgnī́ ehá gacchatām ||4|| Bars under उ (उग्रा), ह (हवामह), उ (उपेदं) and सु; strokes over ता (सन्ता), पे and व (सवनं). Line 2: bars under इ and द्रा, stroke over ग. The print ends the half-verse with sutaṃ.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

उग्रा । सन्ता । हवामहे । उप । इदं । सवनं । सुतं ॥ इन्द्राग्नी इति । आ । इह । गच्छताम् ॥४॥

ugrā | santā | havāmahe | upa | idaṃ | savanaṃ | sutaṃ || indrāgnī iti | ā | iha | gacchatām ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The citation is printed ऋग्वे० १-१६-५, as printed.

सुतमभिषवोपेतमिदमनुष्ठीयमानं सवनं प्रातःसवनादिरूपं कर्मोपसामीप्येन प्राप्तुमुग्रा सन्ता वैरिवधादिषु क्रूरौ सन्तौ देवौ हवामहे । आह्वयामः । इन्द्राग्नी देवाविह कर्मण्या गच्छतां ॥ सन्ता । अस्तेः शतरि श्नसोरल्लोपः । सवनं सुतमिति द्वयं सेमं नः स्तोममा गहि । ऋग्वे० १-१६-५ । इत्यत्रोक्तम् ॥

sutamabhiṣavopetamidamanuṣṭhīyamānaṃ savanaṃ prātaḥsavanādirūpaṃ karmopasāmīpyena prāptumugrā santā vairivadhādiṣu krūrau santau devau havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ | indrāgnī devāviha karmaṇyā gacchatāṃ || santā | asteḥ śatari śnasorallopaḥ | savanaṃ sutamiti dvayaṃ semaṃ naḥ stomamā gahi | ṛgve0 1-16-5 | ityatroktam ||

Page 54 — Rik 4: bhāṣya rendering, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

Translation: "To come near to (upa) idaṃ savanaṃ sutam, this rite now being performed, the pressing in the form of the morning pressing and the rest, furnished with the pressing of soma, we havāmahe, call, the two gods who are ugrā santā, being fierce in slaying enemies and the like. May the two gods Indra and Agni ā gacchatām, come, iha, here to the rite." (Grammatical tail: santā, from as with śatṛ, the a dropped by śnasor allopaḥ; the pair savanaṃ sutam has been explained at semaṃ naḥ stomam ā gahi (Ṛgve. 1-16-5).)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सुतं (sutaṃ) — having the soma juice made ready | इदं सवनं (idaṃ savanaṃ) — the rites now being performed, the morning pressing and the rest | उप (upa) — to come near | उग्रा सन्ता (ugrā santā) — the deities who are fierce (to enemies) | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we call | इन्द्राग्नी (indrāgnī) — O Indra and Agni | इह (iha) — to this place | आ गच्छत (ā gacchata) — come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

To the place where the rites of the morning pressing and the rest, which make the soma juice ready, are going on, we call Indra and Agni, who are terrible to enemies. O Indra and Agni, come here.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke the two (Gods) who are fierce (to their enemies) to come to this Sacrifice where the Soma is prepared; Indra and Agni, come hither.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

उग्रा (ugrā) — vairivadhādiṣu krūrau. The intention is: although Indra and Agni behave generously toward those who praise them, they are fierce toward enemies.

उपेदं सवनं सुतं (upedaṃ savanaṃ sutaṃ) — come near, to drink the soma made ready in the sacrifice we are now performing.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

सन्ता (santā) — the root asa bhuvi; laṭ; by laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau (Pā. Sū. 3-2-124) the substitute śatṛ. By adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ the vikaraṇa śap is dropped (luk). By sārvadhātukam apit (Pā. Sū. 1-2-4) the suffix śatṛ is ṅit. By śnasor allopaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-4-111) — when a sārvadhātuka suffix that is kit or ṅit follows, the a of the suffix śna and of the root as is dropped — the root's a is dropped: s + at = sat. After this, [?] (a short word, unclear), śatṛ is ugit; so by ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-70) — uk it yeṣāṃ te ugitaḥ; adhātoḥ qualifies ugitaḥ; in ac, because it is not possible,

Page 55 (upper) — Rik 4: grammar (end)

there being no qualifier, the root añcu (gatipūjanayoḥ), whose n has been dropped, is taken by ac; ugitaś ca ac ca ugidacaḥ, teṣām ugidacām is the analysis — num is carried on from idito num dhātoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58). So, when a sarvanāmasthāna suffix follows, words that are not roots and are ugit, and the root añc with its n dropped, take the augment num: so the augment num. For the case-ending, by supāṃ suluk the substitute ā; anusvāra and parasavarṇa: it becomes santā.

सवनं, सुतं (savanaṃ, sutaṃ) — for both words the derivation has been set out at semaṃ naḥ stomam ā gahy upedaṃ savanaṃ sutam (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-16-5). ॥4॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता म॒हान्ता॒ स॒दस्प॒ती इ॑न्द्राग्नी॒ र॑क्ष उब्जतं । [accent ?] अप्र॑जाः सन्त्व॒त्रि॑णः ॥५॥ [accent ?]

tā mahā́ntā sadáspatī́ indrāgnī rakṣa ubjataṃ | [accent ?] áprajāḥ santvatriṇaḥ ||5|| [accent ?] Bars under म and ता (महान्ता), द (सदस्) and ती; a stroke over इन् of इन्द्रा; a bar under ग्नी; a stroke over र (or the start of क्ष) of रक्ष. Line 2: stroke over प्र, a bar under the conjunct न्त्व (read as under त्व), stroke over त्रि. The exact syllables of the stroke in रक्ष and the bar in सन्त्व are not certain [accent ?]. The Saṃhitā prints महांता, the Pada महान्ता.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

ता । महान्ता । सदस्पती इति । इन्द्राग्नी इति । रक्षः । उब्जतं ॥ अप्रजाः । सन्तु । अत्रिणः ॥५॥

tā | mahāntā | sadaspatī iti | indrāgnī iti | rakṣaḥ | ubjataṃ || aprajāḥ | santu | atriṇaḥ ||5||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

(Printed अप्रजा आनुत्पन्नाः, read as अप्रजा अनुत्पन्नाः [?].)

तौ पूर्वोक्ताविन्द्राग्नी रक्षो राक्षसजातिमुब्जतं । ऋजुकुरुतं । क्रौर्यं परित्याजयतमित्यर्थः । कीदृशौ । महान्ता महान्तौ गुणैरधिकौ सदस्पती सभापालकौ । तयोः प्रसादादत्रिणो भक्षका राक्षसा अप्रजा अनुत्पन्नाः सन्तु ॥ महान्ता । सान्तमहतः संयोगस्य । पा० ६-४-१० । इति दीर्घः । सदस्पती । सदसस्पती इति समासे षष्ठ्या लुकि प्रातिपदिकसकारस्य रुत्वाभावश्छान्दसः । उभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपदित्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । इन्द्राग्नी । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । अप्रजाः । प्रजायन्त इति प्रजाः । अन्येष्वपि दृश्यते । पा० ३-२-१०१ । इति जनेर्डप्रत्ययः । न प्रजाः अप्रजाः । प्रजाशब्दस्य बहुव्रीहौ हि नित्यमसिच् प्रजामेधयोः । पा० ५-४-१२२ । इत्यसिजादेशः स्यात् । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । अत्रिणः । तृजन्तस्यात्तृशब्दस्य जसश्छान्दस इनुडागमः । चित इति ऋकार उदात्तः । तस्य यणादेश उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादितीकार उदात्तः ॥

tau pūrvoktāvindrāgnī rakṣo rākṣasajātimubjataṃ | ṛjukurutaṃ | krauryaṃ parityājayatamityarthaḥ | kīdṛśau | mahāntā mahāntau guṇairadhikau sadaspatī sabhāpālakau | tayoḥ prasādādatriṇo bhakṣakā rākṣasā aprajā anutpannāḥ santu || mahāntā | sāntamahataḥ saṃyogasya | pā0 6-4-10 | iti dīrghaḥ | sadaspatī | sadasaspatī iti samāse ṣaṣṭhyā luki prātipadikasakārasya rutvābhāvaśchāndasaḥ | ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapadityubhayapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | indrāgnī | āmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | aprajāḥ | prajāyanta iti prajāḥ | anyeṣvapi dṛśyate | pā0 3-2-101 | iti janerḍapratyayaḥ | na prajāḥ aprajāḥ | prajāśabdasya bahuvrīhau hi nityamasic prajāmedhayoḥ | pā0 5-4-122 | ityasijādeśaḥ syāt | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaraḥ | atriṇaḥ | tṛjantasyāttṛśabdasya jasaśchāndasa inuḍāgamaḥ | cita iti ṛkāra udāttaḥ | tasya yaṇādeśa udāttayaṇo halpūrvāditīkāra udāttaḥ ||

Translation: "Tā, those two, Indra and Agni, spoken of before, ubjatam, make straight, rakṣaḥ, the race of rākṣasas: that is, make them give up their cruelty. Of what kind are they? Mahāntā, great, superior in qualities; sadaspatī, guardians of the assembly. By their favour may the atriṇaḥ, the devouring rākṣasas, santu, be aprajāḥ, unborn (without offspring)." (Grammatical tail: mahāntā, the lengthening by sāntamahataḥ saṃyogasya (Pā. 6-4-10); sadaspatī, in the compound sadasaspatī, the genitive having been dropped, the absence of ru for the stem's s is Vedic; both members keep their accent by ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat; indrāgnī, the vocative initial udātta; aprajāḥ, prajāyanta iti prajāḥ, the suffix ḍa after jan by anyeṣv api dṛśyate (Pā. 3-2-101); na prajāḥ aprajāḥ: for prajā in a bahuvrīhi the substitute asic would come by nityam asic prajāmedhayoḥ (Pā. 5-4-122); the accent of the indeclinable first member; atriṇaḥ, the Vedic augment inuṭ to the jas of attṛ ending in tṛc; the ṛ udātta by citaḥ; with yaṇ substituted for it, the ī is udātta by udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt.)

Page 56 — Rik 5: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ता (tā) — spoken of before | महान्ता (mahāntā) — great-souled | सदस्पती (sadaspatī) — protecting the assembly | इन्द्राग्नी (indrāgnī) — Indra and Agni | रक्षः (rakṣaḥ) — the race of rākṣasas | उब्जतं (ubjataṃ) — may they make them give up their cruelty | अत्रिणः (atriṇaḥ) — those rākṣasas who devour (men) | अप्रजाः (aprajāḥ) — without offspring (without descendants) | सन्तु (santu) — may they become.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

May Indra and Agni, great-souled and protectors of the assembly, make the rākṣasas give up their cruelty and walk in the good path. And by the favour of Indra and Agni may the man-eating rākṣasas be left without descendants.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra and Agni, great protectors of Sacrificial house, supress [sic] the Rakshas (demons). and may the devourers of men (demons) be destitute of progeny.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

महान्ता (mahāntā) — of great greatness, great; "great, mighty &c."

सदस्पती (sadaspatī) — "sadas is the well-known sacrificial house; its two lords are Indra and Agni; or, the two guardians of the assembly" (the heading, as printed):

सदः प्रसिद्धं यज्ञगृहं तस्य स्वामिनौ इन्द्राग्नी । सभापालकौ वा ॥

sadaḥ prasiddhaṃ yajñagṛhaṃ tasya svāminau indrāgnī | sabhāpālakau vā ||

When the commentator explains this word, he explains sada as sadas, the assembly, and says sadaspatī means sabhāpālakau, those who protect the assembly. Skandasvāmin says sadaḥ is the sacrificial house, and gives the sense that sadaspatī means: protect from the rākṣasas and others the sacrificial house which we are now [using]. Skandasvāmin's explanation is the better one.

रक्षः (rakṣaḥ) — the rākṣasas, those of cruel nature, "evil spirits" etc. Yāska explains rakṣāṃsi as krūrakarmiṇaḥ, those of cruel deeds (Ni. 10-12).

उब्जतं (ubjataṃ) — krauryaṃ parityājayatam: make them give up their cruel nature. Skandasvāmin, for this word, has explained it so that the intention is: by your power destroy the rākṣasas, or put them down, that is, make them run away:

(Printed वदार्थः, as printed [sic]; read वधार्थः.)

उब्जतिरत्र सामर्थ्यात् वदार्थः न्यग्भावार्थो वा रक्षांसि हतं, न्यग्भूतानि वास्माकं कुरुतं ।

ubjatiratra sāmarthyāt vadārthaḥ nyagbhāvārtho vā rakṣāṃsi hataṃ, nyagbhūtāni vāsmākaṃ kurutaṃ |

अप्रजाः (aprajāḥ) — prajāyanta iti prajāḥ, na prajāḥ aprajāḥ: without offspring, that is, without descendants such as sons and grandsons.

Page 57 — Rik 5: Special Topics (end), grammar

अत्रिणः (atriṇaḥ) — ada bhakṣaṇe | bhakṣayitāraḥ hiṃsitāro 'smākam | devourers, that is, those who harm us.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

महान्ता (mahāntā) — after the word mahat, the suffix au; because by vartamāne pṛṣadbṛhanmahajjagacchatṛvac ca (U. Sū. 2-2-42 as printed, zoom-checked: two dashes, so three groups) it is treated as if ending in śatṛ, the augment num by ugidacām (Pā. Sū. 7-1-70): mahan + t + au; for au the substitute ā by supāṃ suluk; by sāntamahataḥ saṃyogasya (Pā. Sū. 6-4-10) — when a sarvanāmasthāna suffix other than the vocative follows, the vowel penultimate to the n belonging to a conjunct ending in s or to the word mahat is lengthened — the lengthening comes: it becomes mahāntā.

सदस्पती (sadaspatī) — sadasaḥ patī, a genitive tatpuruṣa compound; by kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca (Pā. Sū. 1-2-46) it is a prātipadika. The genitive and au endings, as parts of a prātipadika, are dropped (luk) by supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-71); with the dropped suffix as cause, sadas is a pada by suptiṅantaṃ padam (Pā. Sū. 1-4-14) — words ending in sup and tiṅ are called pada. So by sasajuṣo ruḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-66) the substitute ru for s would be obtained; yet, as a Vedic matter, it does not come here. Sadaḥ is initially udātta by its inherent accent; the word pati ends in the suffix ḍati laid down by pāter ḍatiḥ (U. Sū. 4-4-97, zoom-checked: the last glyph has the flat foot of the 7), and is initially udātta by the suffix accent. For these two, after compounding, by ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat (Pā. Sū. 6-2-140) — in the words listed in the vanaspatyādi class both first and last member keep their own accent at once — both members keep their accent. In the vanaspatyādi class only ten words are listed: 1 vanaspatiḥ, 2 bṛhaspatiḥ, 3 śacīpatiḥ, 4 tanūnapāt, 5 narāśaṃsaḥ, 6 śunaḥśepaḥ, 7 śaṇḍāmarkau, 8 tṛṣṇāvarūthī, 9 lambāviśvavayasau, 10 marmṛtyuḥ. Nor is it an ākṛtigaṇa; so one must consider how the accent of both members comes here through being of the vanaspatyādi class.

इन्द्राग्नी (indrāgnī) — initial udātta by the sūtra of the sixth adhyāya āmantritasya ca (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198). Tau = pūrvoktau; the construction is: he indrāgnī yuvāṃ rakṣaḥ ubjatam.

अप्रजाः (aprajāḥ) — prajāyante iti prajāḥ; by the sūtras anyeṣv api dṛśyate (Pā. Sū. 3-2-101), saptamyāṃ janer ḍaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-2-97) and the rest, when words ending in the seventh case, the fifth case, a prefix,

Page 58 — Rik 5: grammar (end)

or the second case are upapada, the suffix ḍa is laid down after the root jan. By this sūtra [anyeṣv api dṛśyate] it is taught that the suffix ḍa comes after jan even with an upapada other than those mentioned above; by this the suffix ḍa comes here. Although here the suffix ḍa could be derived from upasarge ca saṃjñāyām (Pā. Sū. 3-2-99) — when a name is meant by the whole, with a prefix as upapada, ḍa comes after jan — yet, since aprajāḥ is explained here as anutpannāḥ, a name is not intended. So the suffix ḍa is derived by anyeṣv api dṛśyate. Na prajāḥ aprajāḥ: a nañ-tatpuruṣa; the n of nañ dropped by nalopo nañaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-3-73). If the bahuvrīhi avidyamānāḥ prajāḥ yeṣāṃ te were made, then in nityam asic prajāmedhayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 5-4-122), nañduḥsubhyaḥ is carried on from nañduḥsubhyo halisakthyor anyatarasyām (Pā. Sū. 5-4-121), and from bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac (Pā. Sū. 5-4-113) bahuvrīhau is carried on and changed to the fifth case. So the sense of the sūtra is: after a bahuvrīhi compound ending in the words prajā or medhā following nañ, duḥ or su, the suffix asic comes, and it is a compound-final. By this the suffix asic would have to come; if it came it would be aprajās; after this, when the nominative plural jas came, by yasyeti ca (Pā. Sū. 6-4-148) the a would be dropped and it would have to be aprajasaḥ. Since here aprajāḥ is a plural form and in a bahuvrīhi the nominative plural would not be obtained, the tatpuruṣa compound alone must be accepted here. By tatpuruṣe tulyārtha- (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) the indeclinable first member keeps its accent.

अत्रिणः (atriṇaḥ) — the root ada bhakṣaṇe; by ṇvultṛcau tṛc: attṛ; after it jas; to this, as a Vedic matter, the augment inuṭ: attṛ + inas; the ṛ belonging to the suffix tṛc is udātta by citaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163); in place of this ṛ, by iko yaṇ aci, the r comes by yaṇ substitution; now by udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt (Pā. Sū. 6-1-174) — after a yaṇ preceded by a consonant and standing in place of an udātta, a nadī and the vowel-initial case-endings śas etc. are also udātta — the i becomes udātta. So for this very reason, here by the general rule udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4) the svarita does not come; by the exception udāttayaṇaḥ the udātta alone comes. ॥5॥

Rik 6 (last ṛk of the sūkta) pp. 59

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तेन॑ स॒त्येन॑ जागृ॒तमधि॑ प्रचे॒तुने॑ प॒दे । इ॑न्द्राग्नी॒ शर्म॑ यच्छतम् ॥६॥

téna satyéna jāgṛtám ádhi pracetúne padé | indrāgnī śárma yacchatam ||6|| Strokes over न (तेन), न (सत्येन), धि and ने (प्रचेतुने); bars under स (सत्येन), त (जागृतम्), चे and प (पदे). Line 2: stroke over इन् of इन्द्रा, bar under ग्नी, stroke over र्म.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

तेन । सत्येन । जागृतं । अधि । प्रऽचेतुने । पदे ॥ इन्द्राग्नी इति । शर्म । यच्छतम् ॥६॥

tena | satyena | jāgṛtaṃ | adhi | pra 'cetune | pade || indrāgnī iti | śarma | yacchatam ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The bhāṣya ends with ॥३॥, the close of the third varga.

हे इन्द्राग्नी सत्येनावश्यफलप्रदानादवितथेन तेनास्माभिरनुष्ठितेन कर्मणा प्रचेतुने प्रकर्षेण फलभोगज्ञापके पदे स्वर्गलोकादिस्थानेऽधि जागृतं । आधिक्येन सावधानौ भवतं । ततोऽस्मभ्यं शर्म यच्छतं । सुखं गृहं वा । दत्तं । गयः कृदर इत्यादिषु द्वाविंशतिसंख्याकेषु गृहनामसु शर्म वर्मेत्युक्तम् ॥ जागृतं । जागृ निद्राक्षये । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । प्रचेतुने । चिती संज्ञाने इत्यस्माण्ण्यन्ताद्बाहुलकादौणादिक उनप्रत्ययः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । इन्द्राग्नी । इहेन्द्राग्नी इत्यत्रोक्तं । आमन्त्रितत्वादाद्युदात्तत्वमत्र विशेषः । शृणाति हिनस्ति दुःखमिति शर्म । शॄ हिंसायाम् । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति मनिन् । यच्छतं । इषुगमियमां छ इति छः ॥३॥

he indrāgnī satyenāvaśyaphalapradānādavitathena tenāsmābhiranuṣṭhitena karmaṇā pracetune prakarṣeṇa phalabhogajñāpake pade svargalokādisthāne 'dhi jāgṛtaṃ | ādhikyena sāvadhānau bhavataṃ | tato 'smabhyaṃ śarma yacchataṃ | sukhaṃ gṛhaṃ vā | dattaṃ | gayaḥ kṛdara ityādiṣu dvāviṃśatisaṃkhyākeṣu gṛhanāmasu śarma varmetyuktam || jāgṛtaṃ | jāgṛ nidrākṣaye | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | pracetune | citī saṃjñāne ityasmāṇṇyantādbāhulakādauṇādika unapratyayaḥ | samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | indrāgnī | ihendrāgnī ityatroktaṃ | āmantritatvādādyudāttatvamatra viśeṣaḥ | śṛṇāti hinasti duḥkhamiti śarma | śṝ hiṃsāyām | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti manin | yacchataṃ | iṣugamiyamāṃ cha iti chaḥ ||3||

Translation: "O Indra and Agni! Tena satyena, by that rite performed by us, true — not false, because it surely grants its fruit — adhi jāgṛtam, be watchful in a high degree, be attentive, pracetune pade, in the place that makes known in an eminent way the enjoyment of the fruit, the place such as the world of heaven. Then yacchatam, give, us śarma, happiness, or a house: among the twenty-two names for 'house', gayaḥ, kṛdaram and the rest, śarma and varma are mentioned." (Grammatical tail: jāgṛtam, jāgṛ nidrākṣaye, śap dropped by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ, the loss of accent by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ; pracetune, from citī saṃjñāne in the causative, the Uṇādi suffix una by bāhulaka; in the compound the accent of the kṛt final member; indrāgnī, as stated at ihendrāgnī, the special point here the vocative initial udātta; śṛṇāti hinasti duḥkham iti śarma, śṝ hiṃsāyām, manin by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; yacchatam, cha by iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हे इन्द्राग्नी (he indrāgnī) — O Indra and Agni | सत्येन (satyena) — not fruitless | तेन (tena) — by the rite we perform | प्रचेतुने (pracetune) — making known (the enjoyment that is the fruit of the sacrifice) | पदे (pade) — in the place such as heaven | अधि जागृतं (adhi jāgṛtaṃ) — be especially watchful | शर्म (śarma) — happiness, or a place that gives happiness | यच्छतं (yacchataṃ) — give (to us).

Page 60 — Rik 6: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Indra and Agni, there is no doubt that the rites we perform give their fruit. Heaven and the rest, your dwelling places, make this known. Being watchful on our behalf in those places, bring about happiness for us.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra and Agni, by this unfailing Sacrifice be vigilant in the place which affords knowledge and bestow upon us happiness.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The meaning of this ṛk is somewhat tangled. The meaning of the words tena satyena jāgṛte [as printed] and pracetune pade is not clear. Although the commentator has explained them so that a certain sense comes out, what the ṛṣi intends is not clear. The main intention may be: being satisfied by the hymns we make and by the performance of the sacrifice and the like, be watchful on our behalf and bring about happiness for us.

प्रचेतुने पदे (pracetune pade) — prajñāpake sthale | phalabhogajñāpake pade | the place that makes known.

शर्म (śarma) — sukhaṃ gṛhaṃ vā | happiness, or a house. Since the word śarma is read among the twenty-two names for 'house', gaya, kṛdara and the rest, the word śarma also means a house, a dwelling (Ni. 3-13).

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

जागृतं (jāgṛtaṃ) — jāgṛ nidrākṣaye; loṭ, middle person dual thas; by loṭo laṅvat (Pā. Sū. 3-4-85) it is treated like laṅ; by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101) the substitute tam; by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72) the vikaraṇa śap is dropped (luk); tam is ṅit by sārvadhātukam apit (Pā. Sū. 1-2-4), so by kṅiti ca (Pā. Sū. 1-1-5) guṇa is barred; by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) — a finite verb after a word that is not a finite verb is unaccented — it is wholly unaccented.

Page 61 — Rik 6: grammar (continued)

प्रचेतुने (pracetune) — the root citī saṃjñāne. After it ṇic; by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86) guṇa of the light penultimate: ceti. After this, by the word bahula in uṇādayo bahulam (Pā. Sū. 3-3-1), the Uṇādi suffix una; by ṇer aniṭi (Pā. Sū. 6-4-51) ṇi is dropped; in the locative singular cetune; after compounding with the word pra, by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the accent of the kṛt final member comes; the final member cetuna is accented on its middle syllable by the suffix accent.

इन्द्राग्नी (indrāgnī) — its derivation has been set out at the first mantra of this sūkta, ihendrāgnī. Here indrāgnī is āmantrita, since it is a vocative nominative. So, by āmantritasya ca (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19, as printed), the initial udātta: only this is the special point here compared with before.

शर्म (śarma) — śṛṇāti hinasti duḥkham iti śarma; the root śṝ hiṃsāyām. After it, by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. Sū. 3-2-75) — the suffixes manin, kvanip, vanip and vic come after roots — the suffix manin. Śṝ + man; by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) guṇa, followed by r: it becomes śarma.

यच्छतम् (yacchatam) — yamu uparame, in the bhvādi class. After it loṭ, middle person dual thas, for which the substitute tam. By kartari śap (Pā. Sū. 3-1-68) the vikaraṇa śap: yam + a + tam. Now by iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-77) — after the roots iṣu icchāyām, gaḷḷa gatau [as printed] and yamu uparame, when a suffix with the marker ś follows, the substitute cha comes — cha for the m; by che ca (Pā. Sū. 6-1-73) — before cha, a short vowel takes the augment tuk — tuk; by stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-4-40) c for the t: it becomes yacchatam. There is iṣa gatau in the divādi class, giving iṣyati. Iṣa icchāyām, tudādi, icchati; iṣa ābhīkṣṇye, kryādi, iṣṇāti: so there are three roots iṣ. Here, so that cha comes only for the tudādi root, some read iṣu in the tudādi class and also read iṣu in the sūtra prescribing cha; others say that by maṇḍūkapluti, aci is carried on from aci ra ṛtaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-2-100) and qualifies śiti; so the sense obtained is: when a vowel-initial suffix with the marker ś follows, cha is substituted for iṣ and the rest. Since śyan comes in the divādi class and the vikaraṇa śnā in the kryādi class, although they have the marker ś they are not vowel-initial suffixes with the marker ś, so cha does not come for them. So in the tudādi class and in the sūtra iṣugami,

Page 62 (upper) — Rik 6: grammar (end)

they hold that to read iṣu with the marker u is not from the ṛṣi [anārṣa]. In this way, although the form yacchatam is obtained from the root yamu uparame, it does not fit the meaning yacchatam = dattam explained in the bhāṣya. For the root dāṇ dāne, loṭ, middle person dual thas, the substitute tam comes: dāṇ + a + taṃ. Now by pā ghrā dhmā sthā mnā dāṇ dṛśy arti sarti śada sadāṃ piba jighra dhama tiṣṭha mana yaccha paśya ṛccha dhau śīya sīdāḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78) — when a suffix beginning with ś and having the marker ś follows, the roots pā and the rest take the substitutes piba and the rest — the sixth root dāṇ takes the sixth substitute yaccha: it becomes yacchatam. If the form is taken from this root dāṇ, it fits the meaning explained in the bhāṣya. ॥6॥ An ornament follows: the close of Sūkta 21.

(Printed p. 62, lower part: an invocation ॥ श्रीः ॥, the title ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೆರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ("The Twenty-second Sūkta") and a rule.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note) The bhāṣya runs on to p. 63, whose header reads Varga 4. It prints kṛtsna-devatyā (not kṛṣṇa), and the numbers अनु० १२-४, आ० ४-१५ and आ० ५-५.

प्रातर्युजेत्यादिकमेकविंशत्यृचं पञ्चमं सूक्तम् । तस्य ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । देवताविशेषस्त्वनुक्रम्यते । प्रातर्युजा सैका चतस्र आश्विन्यस्तथा सावित्र्य आग्नेय्यौ द्वे देवीनामेकैकेन्द्राणीवरुणान्यग्नायीनां द्यावापृथिव्यौ पार्थिवी षड्वैष्णव्योऽतो देवा दैवी वेति । सूक्तसंख्यानुवर्तत इत्यस्मिन्खण्डेऽनिरुक्ता संख्या विंशतिः । अनु० १२-४ । इति परिभाषितत्वात्प्रातर्युजेति सूक्ते संख्याविशेषस्यानिरुक्ता संख्या विंशतिसंख्या द्रष्टव्या । सा च विंशतिरेकयाधिकया सह वर्तत इति सैका । तत्रादौ चतस्र ऋचोऽश्विदेवताकाः । पञ्चमीमारभ्याष्टम्यन्ताश्चतस्रः सवितृदेवताकाः । नवमी दशमी चोभे अग्निदेवताके । एकादश्या ऋचो देवसंबन्धिन्यो देव्यो देवताः । द्वादश्या इन्द्रवरुणाग्निपत्न्य इन्द्राणीवरुणान्यग्नाय्यो देवताः । त्रयोदशीचतुर्दश्यौ द्यावापृथिवीदेवताके । पञ्चदशी पार्थिवी । षोडश्याद्याः षड्विष्णुदेवत्याः । षोडशी कृत्स्नदेवत्या वा ॥ अत्र सूक्तविनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥ प्रातरनुवाक आश्विने क्रतौ प्रातर्युजा विबोधयेति चतस्र ऋचः । सूत्रितं च । अथाश्विन एषो उषाः प्रातर्युजेति चतस्रः । आ० ४-१५ । इति ॥ आश्विनग्रहस्य प्रातर्युजेत्येका पुरोनुवाक्या द्विदेवत्यैश्चरन्तीति खण्डे सूत्रितं । आश्विनस्य प्रातर्युजा वि बोधय । आ० ५-५ । इति ॥

prātaryujetyādikamekaviṃśatyṛcaṃ pañcamaṃ sūktam | tasya ṛṣicchandasī pūrvavat | devatāviśeṣastvanukramyate | prātaryujā saikā catasra āśvinyastathā sāvitrya āgneyyau dve devīnāmekaikendrāṇīvaruṇānyagnāyīnāṃ dyāvāpṛthivyau pārthivī ṣaḍvaiṣṇavyo 'to devā daivī veti | sūktasaṃkhyānuvartata ityasminkhaṇḍe 'niruktā saṃkhyā viṃśatiḥ | anu0 12-4 | iti paribhāṣitatvātprātaryujeti sūkte saṃkhyāviśeṣasyāniruktā saṃkhyā viṃśatisaṃkhyā draṣṭavyā | sā ca viṃśatirekayādhikayā saha vartata iti saikā | tatrādau catasra ṛco 'śvidevatākāḥ | pañcamīmārabhyāṣṭamyantāścatasraḥ savitṛdevatākāḥ | navamī daśamī cobhe agnidevatāke | ekādaśyā ṛco devasaṃbandhinyo devyo devatāḥ | dvādaśyā indravaruṇāgnipatnya indrāṇīvaruṇānyagnāyyo devatāḥ | trayodaśīcaturdaśyau dyāvāpṛthivīdevatāke | pañcadaśī pārthivī | ṣoḍaśyādyāḥ ṣaḍviṣṇudevatyāḥ | ṣoḍaśī kṛtsnadevatyā vā || atra sūktaviniyogo laiṅgikaḥ || prātaranuvāka āśvine kratau prātaryujā vibodhayeti catasra ṛcaḥ | sūtritaṃ ca | athāśvina eṣo uṣāḥ prātaryujeti catasraḥ | ā0 4-15 | iti || āśvinagrahasya prātaryujetyekā puronuvākyā dvidevatyaiścarantīti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | āśvinasya prātaryujā vi bodhaya | ā0 5-5 | iti ||

Translation: "The sūkta beginning prātaryujā, of twenty-one ṛks, is the fifth. Its ṛṣi and metre are as before. The particular deities are stated in the Anukramaṇī: 'prātaryujā, with one more [than twenty]: four to the Aśvins, likewise [four] to Savitṛ, two to Agni, one each to the goddesses, to Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī and Agnāyī, to Heaven-and-Earth, to Earth, six to Viṣṇu; from there, the gods, or the divine one.' Because it is laid down in the section sūktasaṃkhyānuvartate that 'the number not stated is twenty' (Anu. 12-4), in the sūkta prātaryujā, where no particular number is stated, the number twenty is to be understood; and that twenty goes together with one more: hence saikā. Of these, the first four ṛks have the Aśvins as deity; the four from the fifth to the eighth, Savitṛ; the ninth and tenth both, Agni; for the eleventh ṛk the deities are the goddesses connected with the gods; for the twelfth, the wives of Indra, Varuṇa and Agni — Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī and Agnāyī; the thirteenth and fourteenth, Heaven-and-Earth; the fifteenth is to Earth; the six from the sixteenth have Viṣṇu as deity; or the sixteenth has all [the gods] (kṛtsna) as deity. Here the application of the sūkta is laiṅgika (by its marks). In the prātaranuvāka, at the Aśvina rite, the four ṛks prātaryujā vibodhaya; and it is laid down: 'Now at the Aśvina, eṣo uṣāḥ, prātaryujā: four' (Āśv. 4-15). For the Āśvina cup, the one ṛk prātaryujā is the puronuvākyā: it is laid down in the section dvidevatyaiś caranti: 'of the Āśvina, prātaryujā vi bodhaya' (Āśv. 5-5)."

Page 63 — Sūkta 22: introduction (end)

Anuvāda (Kannada rendering): The sūkta beginning prātaryujā is the fifth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka; it has twenty-one ṛks. The ṛṣi and metres of this sūkta are as in the previous sūkta. On the deities, it is said in the section sūtrasaṃkhyānuvartate [as printed] of the Anukramaṇī: prātaryujā saikā catasra āśvinyas tathā sāvitrya āgneyyau dve devīnām ekaikendrāṇīvaruṇānyagnāyīnāṃ dyāvāpṛthivye pārthivī ṣaḍvaiṣṇavyo 'to devā daivī veti (Anu. 12-4). As stated in this Anukramaṇī the number of mantras is twenty; but in another place the number of mantras of this sūkta is said to be twenty-one. The first four ṛks of this sūkta have the Aśvins as deity; the ṛks from the fifth to the eighth have Savitṛ as deity; the ninth and tenth ṛks have Agni as deity; for the eleventh ṛk the deities are the goddesses connected with the gods, that is, the wives of the gods; for the twelfth ṛk the deities are Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī and Agnāyī, the wives of the deities Indra, Varuṇa and Agni; the thirteenth and fourteenth ṛks have Heaven-and-Earth as deity; the fifteenth, Earth; the six ṛks from the sixteenth onward have Viṣṇu as deity; or the sixteenth ṛk has kṛtsna, that is, all the gods, as deity. In all, the application of the sūkta is laiṅgika. At the time of reciting the prātaranuvāka mantras, the four ṛks prātaryujā vi bodhaya are to be recited as mantras of the Aśvina rite. This is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra in the sūtra athāśvina eṣo uṣāḥ prātaryujeti catasraḥ (Ā. 4-15). And in the particular homa called the Āśvina cup, the one ṛk prātaryujā is to be recited as the puronuvākyā mantra: this is stated in the section dvidevatyaiś caranti, in the sūtra āśvinasya prātaryujā vi bodhaya (Ā. 5-5). An ornament follows.

Sūkta 22, Rik 1

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

प्रा॒त॒र्युजा॒ वि बो॑धया॒श्विना॒वेह ग॑च्छताम् । अ॒स्य सोम॑स्य पी॒त॑ये ॥१॥

prātaryújā ví bodhayāśvínāv éhá gacchatām | asyá sómasya pītaye ||1|| Bars under प्रा, त (प्रातर्), जा, या (बोधयाश्) and ना (अश्विना); strokes over बो and ग. Line 2: bars under अ and पी, strokes over म (सोमस्य) and त (पीतये).

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

प्रातःऽयुजा । वि । बोधय । अश्विनौ । आ । इह । गच्छताम् ॥ अस्य । सोमस्य । पीतये ॥१॥

prātaḥ 'yujā | vi | bodhaya | aśvinau | ā | iha | gacchatām || asya | somasya | pītaye ||1|| The Pada prints अश्विनौ.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अत्र होताध्वर्युमुद्दिश्य ब्रूते । हे अध्वर्यो प्रातर्युजा प्रातःसवनग्रहेण संयुक्तावश्विनौ देवौ वि बोधय । विशेषेण प्रबुद्धौ कुरु । अश्विनौ प्रबुद्धौ चाश्विनौ देवावस्याभिषवसंस्कारयुक्तस्य सोमस्य पीतये पानायेह कर्मण्या गच्छतां ॥ प्रातर्युञ्जाते गृह्यमाणेन ग्रहेण सहेति प्रातर्युजा । सत्सूद्विषेत्यादिना क्विप् । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अस्य । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । पीतये । व्यत्ययेन क्तिन उदात्तत्वं ॥

atra hotādhvaryumuddiśya brūte | he adhvaryo prātaryujā prātaḥsavanagraheṇa saṃyuktāvaśvinau devau vi bodhaya | viśeṣeṇa prabuddhau kuru | aśvinau prabuddhau cāśvinau devāvasyābhiṣavasaṃskārayuktasya somasya pītaye pānāyeha karmaṇyā gacchatāṃ || prātaryuñjāte gṛhyamāṇena graheṇa saheti prātaryujā | satsūdviṣetyādinā kvip | supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | asya | ūḍidamityādinā vibhakterudāttatvaṃ | pītaye | vyatyayena ktina udāttatvaṃ ||

Translation: "Here the hotṛ speaks addressing the adhvaryu. O adhvaryu! Vi bodhaya, awaken — make fully awake — the two gods, the Aśvins, prātaryujā, joined with the cup of the morning pressing. And may the Aśvins, awakened, ā gacchatām, come, iha, here to the rite, asya somasya pītaye, to drink this soma furnished with the pressing and preparation." (Grammatical tail: prātaryujā, 'they are joined at morning with the cup being taken', kvip by satsūdviṣa…, the ā by supāṃ suluk…, the accent of the kṛt final member; asya, the case-ending udātta by ūḍidam…; pītaye, the udātta of ktin by vyatyaya.)

Page 65 — Rik 1: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे अध्वर्यो) ((he adhvaryo)) — (O adhvaryu) | प्रातर्युजा (prātaryujā) — joined with the cup of the morning pressing | अश्विनौ (aśvinau) — the Aśvin deities | वि बोधय (vi bodhaya) — make them awake (rouse them) | (अश्विनौ) ((aśvinau)) — (O Aśvin deities, awakened) | अस्य (asya) — this (prepared) | सोमस्य (somasya) — of the soma juice | पीतये (pītaye) — for drinking | इह (iha) — to this place | आ गच्छतां (ā gacchatāṃ) — come.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O adhvaryu, awaken the Aśvin deities, needed for the morning pressing. (Rouse them.) Awakened, may they come here and drink the soma juice that has been prepared.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

Awaken the Aswins for the morning Sacrifice; let them both come hither to drink of this Soma-juice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The first half of this ṛk is spoken addressing the priest called adhvaryu.

प्रातर्युजा (prātaryujā) — prātaḥsavanagraheṇa saṃyuktau || The commentator gives the sense: so that they become ready at the time of the morning pressing for taking the cup of soma-drinking connected with the Aśvina rite. Skandasvāmin's intention too is the same. But the author of the Vedārthayatna gives the sense prātaryujā — prātaḥkāle aśvau rathe yojayantau: harnessing their horses to the chariot at morning, getting ready to come to the sacrificial altar. Since there is neither the word 'chariot' nor the word 'horse' here, and since there is the word vibodhaya, 'rouse', and it is improbable that those who have risen from their beds and are harnessing horses to the chariot are to be roused again, this sense is not acceptable. The sense of Sāyaṇa and of Skandasvāmin is the fitting one.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

प्रातर्युजा (prātaryujā) — the analysis is prātaḥ yuñjāte iti prātaryujā: prātaḥ = at the morning pressing; yuñjāte = they join with the cup being taken: this is the sense of the parts. By satsūdviṣadruhaduhayujavidabhidacchidajinīrājām upasarge 'pi kvip (Pā. Sū. 3-2-61) the suffix kvip; by supāṃ suluk the substitute ā for the suffix auṭ; yuj, being a root with u, by the root

Page 66 (upper) — Rik 1: grammar (end)

accent is udātta; an upapada compound; by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt the accent of the kṛt final member.

अस्य (asya) — after the word idam, the genitive singular jas [as printed; for ṅas]; by tyadādīnām aḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-2-102) a for the m; by ato guṇe (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) the following form; by ṭāṅasiṅasām inātsyāḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-12) the substitute sya; by hali lopaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-2-113) id is dropped; since it is not a case of anvādeśa, the unaccented substitute aś by idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudāttas tṛtīyādau (Pā. Sū. 8-3-41, as printed) does not come. The a is udātta by the stem accent; by anudāttau suppitau (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4) the case-ending would be unaccented; but since it comes after the word idam, by ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the case-ending takes the udātta.

पीतये (pītaye) — since the suffix ktin has the marker n, by the nit accent the word pīti would properly be initially udātta; that is, by śeṣanighāta ktin would have to be unaccented; yet here by vyatyaya the suffix ktin is udātta. ॥1॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

या सु॒रथा॑ र॒थीत॑मो॒भा दे॒वा दि॑वि॒स्पृशा॑ । अ॒श्विना॒ ता ह॑वामहे ॥२॥

yā suráthā rathī́tamobhā́ devā́ divispṛ́śā | aśvínā tā́ havāmahe ||2|| Bars under सु, र (रथी), मो, दे and वि (दिवि); strokes over था (सुरथा), त (रथीतमो), दि and शा. Line 2: bars under अ and ना, stroke over ह.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

या । सुऽरथा । रथिऽतमा । उभा । देवा । दिविऽस्पृशा ॥ अश्विना । ता । हवामहे ॥२॥

yā | su 'rathā | rathi 'tamā | ubhā | devā | divi 'spṛśā || aśvinā | tā | havāmahe ||2||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ It opens योभाश्विना देवा, as printed, quoting the ṛk.

योभाश्विना देवा यावुभावश्विनौ देवौ सुरथा शोभनरथयुक्तौ रथीतमा रथिनां मध्येऽतिशयेन रथिनौ दिविस्पृशा द्युलोकनिवासिनौ ता तादृशावश्विनावाह्वयामहे ॥ येत्यादिष्वष्टसु पदेषु सुपां सुलुगिति द्विवचनस्याकारः । सुरथा । शोभनो रथो ययोस्तौ सुरथौ । समासान्तोदात्तत्वापवादं बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरं बाधित्वा नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्त आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । रथीतमा । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति संहितायामिकारस्य दीर्घत्वं । दिविस्पृशा । दिवि स्पृशत इति दिविस्पृशौ । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलमित्यलुक् । गतिकारकोपपदात्कृदिति कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

yobhāśvinā devā yāvubhāvaśvinau devau surathā śobhanarathayuktau rathītamā rathināṃ madhye 'tiśayena rathinau divispṛśā dyulokanivāsinau tā tādṛśāvaśvināvāhvayāmahe || yetyādiṣvaṣṭasu padeṣu supāṃ sulugiti dvivacanasyākāraḥ | surathā | śobhano ratho yayostau surathau | samāsāntodāttatvāpavādaṃ bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaraṃ bādhitvā nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatve prāpta ādyudāttaṃ dvyacchandasītyuttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | rathītamā | anyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti saṃhitāyāmikārasya dīrghatvaṃ | divispṛśā | divi spṛśata iti divispṛśau | kvipceti kvip | tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulamityaluk | gatikārakopapadātkṛditi kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||

Translation: "Yā ubhā aśvinā devā: the two gods, both Aśvins, who are surathā, possessed of a fine chariot, rathītamā, among charioteers eminently charioteers, divispṛśā, dwelling in the world of heaven — tā, those two such Aśvins we havāmahe, call." (Grammatical tail: in the eight words yā etc., the ā for the dual by supāṃ suluk; surathā, 'whose chariot is fine': overriding the first-member accent of a bahuvrīhi, itself an exception to the compound-final udātta, the final udātta of the last member by nañsubhyām would come; then the initial udātta of the last member by ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi; rathītamā, the lengthening of the i in the Saṃhitā by anyeṣām api dṛśyate; divispṛśā, 'they touch heaven', kvip by kvip ca, the non-dropping (aluk) by tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam, the accent of the kṛt final member by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

या उभा अश्विना देवा (yā ubhā aśvinā devā) — both the Aśvin deities who | सुरथा (surathā) — who have a fine chariot | रथीतमा (rathītamā) — who are best among charioteers | दिविस्पृशा (divispṛśā) — who dwell in the world of the gods | ता (tā) — both of them (such) | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we call.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The Aśvin deities have a fine chariot, are most able in driving the chariot, and dwell in the world of the gods. We call both such ones to the sacrifice.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke the two Aswins who are both divine, the best of charioteers, dwellers in heaven, riding in an excellant [sic] car.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

सुरथा (surathā) — śobhanarathayuktau | having a fine chariot.

रथीतमा (rathītamā) — the best among rathikas; rathikas are those who fight seated in a chariot. Skandasvāmin explains: rathītamā — sārathir atra rathy ucyate | atiśayena sārathī — that is, here rathī means charioteer; rathītamā, best among charioteers, or skilled in driving the chariot.

सारथिरत्र रथ्युच्यते । अतिशयेन सारथी ।

sārathiratra rathyucyate | atiśayena sārathī |

दिविस्पृशा (divispṛśā) — divi spṛśata iti divispṛśau | divi spraṣṭārau gantārāv ity arthaḥ || Those who touch, or reach, heaven, that is, those who go to the world of heaven, dwellers in heaven.

दिवि स्पृशत इति दिविस्पृशौ । दिवि स्प्रष्टारौ गन्तारावित्यर्थः ॥

divi spṛśata iti divispṛśau | divi spraṣṭārau gantārāvityarthaḥ ||

Page 68 — Rik 2: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

या (yā) — and in all eight words beginning with it, for the accusative dual suffix auṭ, the substitute ā by supāṃ suluk (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39). Śobhanau rathau yayos tau surathau [as printed]: here by samāsasya (Pā. Sū. 6-1-223) the final udātta would be obtained; overriding it, since this is a bahuvrīhi, the first member's own accent would be obtained by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1). Overriding this too, since the last member follows the word su, the final udātta of the last member would be obtained by nañsubhyām (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172). Since the word ratha is initially udātta, by ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi (Pā. Sū. 6-2-119), the exception to nañsubhyām — in a bahuvrīhi, after the word su, a last member of two syllables that is initially udātta stays initially udātta — the last member keeps its initial udātta. After the root ramu krīḍāyām, the suffix kthan by hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ kthan (U. Sū. 2-159, zoom-checked: the first glyph is the curled 2, the same as in the Pā. 6-2-1 on the same page); the m is dropped by anudāttopadeśa… (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37): it becomes ratha, initially udātta by the nit accent ñnity ādir nityam.

रथीतमौ (rathītamau) — rathaḥ anayor astīti rathinau: by ata iniṭhanau (Pā. Sū. 5-2-115) the suffix ini. With the analysis atiśayena rathinau, by atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau (Pā. Sū. 5-3-55) tamap in the sense of excess; with the internal case-ending as cause rathin is a pada, and the n is dropped by nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya (Pā. Sū. 8-2-7). In the Saṃhitā, by anyeṣām api dṛśyate (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137), the i of the first member is lengthened.

दिविस्पृशा (divispṛśā) — divi spṛśata iti divispṛśau. By kvip ca (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76) — with or without an upapada, after all roots, both in the world and in the Veda, the suffix kvip is seen — the suffix kvip; satsūdviṣa… is an elaboration of this. In divispṛś a tatpuruṣa compound by upapadam atiṅ (Pā. Sū. 2-2-19). By tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam (Pā. Sū. 6-3-14) — in a tatpuruṣa, when a last member ending in a kṛt follows, the locative ending variously is not dropped when a name is meant — the locative in divi is not dropped; the intention is that by the word bahula the aluk comes here even though no name is meant. By gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) — in a tatpuruṣa, a word ending in a kṛt after a gati, a kāraka or an upapada keeps its own accent — the accent of the kṛt final member comes. Spṛś is final udātta by the root accent; spṛśa saṃsparśane is the root. ॥2॥

या वां॒ कशा॒ मधु॑म॒त्यश्वि॑ना सू॒नृता॑वती । त॑या य॒ज्ञं मि॑मिक्षतं ॥३॥

yā vāṃ káśā mádhumaty áśvinā sūnṛ́tāvatī | tayā yajñáṃ mimikṣataṃ ||3|| Bars under वां, शा, म (मत्य) and सू; strokes over धु, श्वि and ता (सूनृता). Line 2: strokes over त (तया) and the first मि, bar under य (यज्ञं).

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

या । वां । कशा । मधुऽमती । अश्विना । सूनृताऽवती ॥ तया । यज्ञं । मिमिक्षतं ॥३॥

yā | vāṃ | kaśā | madhu 'matī | aśvinā | sūnṛtā 'vatī || tayā | yajñaṃ | mimikṣataṃ ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अश्विना हे अश्विनौ देवौ वां युवयोः संबन्धिनी या कशाश्वताडिनी विद्यते तया सहागत्य यज्ञमस्मदीयं मिमिक्षतं । सोमरसेन सेक्तुमिच्छतं । कशयाश्वान्दृढं ताडयित्वा सहसा समागत्य भवद्विषयां सोमरसाहुतिं निष्पादयितुमुद्युक्तौ भवतमित्यर्थः । कीदृशी कशा । मधुमती । अर्णः क्षोद इत्यादिष्वेकशतसंख्याकेषूदकनामसु मधु पुरीषमिति पठितं । तस्मादुदकवतीत्युक्तं भवति । अश्वस्य शीघ्रगत्या यत्स्वेदोदकं स्रवति तेनेयं कशाक्लिन्नेत्यर्थः । सूनृतावती प्रियसत्यवाग्युक्ता । तीव्रेण कशाताडनेन यो ध्वनिर्निष्पद्यते ताडनवेलायामश्वारूढेन च य आक्रोशः क्रियते तदुभयं शीघ्रगमनहेतुत्वेन यजमानस्य प्रियं । यद्वा । श्लोको धारेत्यादिषु सप्तपञ्चाशद्वाङ्नामसु कशा धिषणेति पठितं । अश्विनोर्या वाक् मधुमती माधुर्योपेता पारुष्यरहिता सूनृतावती प्रियत्वसत्यत्वोपेता । फलप्रदानविषयेत्यर्थः । तया वाचा युक्तौ यज्ञं मिमिक्षतमिति योजनीयं ॥ कशा । कश गतिशातनयोः । पचाद्यच् । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । सूनृतावती । ऊन परिहाणे । सुष्ठूनयत्यप्रियमिति सून् । तथाविधमृतं सत्यं यस्यां वाचि सा सूनृता । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं बाधित्वा परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति ऋकार उदात्तः । सा यस्या अस्ति सा कशा सूनृतावतीति कशायाः संज्ञा । एवंनामा या कशेत्यर्थः । संज्ञायां । पा० ८-२-११ । इति मतुपो वत्वं । मिमिक्षतं । मिहेः सन् । हलन्ताच्च । पा० १-२-१० । इति कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः ॥ ढत्वकत्वषत्वानि ॥

aśvinā he aśvinau devau vāṃ yuvayoḥ saṃbandhinī yā kaśāśvatāḍinī vidyate tayā sahāgatya yajñamasmadīyaṃ mimikṣataṃ | somarasena sektumicchataṃ | kaśayāśvāndṛḍhaṃ tāḍayitvā sahasā samāgatya bhavadviṣayāṃ somarasāhutiṃ niṣpādayitumudyuktau bhavatamityarthaḥ | kīdṛśī kaśā | madhumatī | arṇaḥ kṣoda ityādiṣvekaśatasaṃkhyākeṣūdakanāmasu madhu purīṣamiti paṭhitaṃ | tasmādudakavatītyuktaṃ bhavati | aśvasya śīghragatyā yatsvedodakaṃ sravati teneyaṃ kaśāklinnetyarthaḥ | sūnṛtāvatī priyasatyavāgyuktā | tīvreṇa kaśātāḍanena yo dhvanirniṣpadyate tāḍanavelāyāmaśvārūḍhena ca ya ākrośaḥ kriyate tadubhayaṃ śīghragamanahetutvena yajamānasya priyaṃ | yadvā | śloko dhāretyādiṣu saptapañcāśadvāṅnāmasu kaśā dhiṣaṇeti paṭhitaṃ | aśvinoryā vāk madhumatī mādhuryopetā pāruṣyarahitā sūnṛtāvatī priyatvasatyatvopetā | phalapradānaviṣayetyarthaḥ | tayā vācā yuktau yajñaṃ mimikṣatamiti yojanīyaṃ || kaśā | kaśa gatiśātanayoḥ | pacādyac | vṛṣāditvādādyudāttaḥ | sūnṛtāvatī | ūna parihāṇe | suṣṭhūnayatyapriyamiti sūn | tathāvidhamṛtaṃ satyaṃ yasyāṃ vāci sā sūnṛtā | nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ bādhitvā parādiśchandasi bahulamiti ṛkāra udāttaḥ | sā yasyā asti sā kaśā sūnṛtāvatīti kaśāyāḥ saṃjñā | evaṃnāmā yā kaśetyarthaḥ | saṃjñāyāṃ | pā0 8-2-11 | iti matupo vatvaṃ | mimikṣataṃ | miheḥ san | halantācca | pā0 1-2-10 | iti kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ || ḍhatvakatvaṣatvāni ||

Translation: "Aśvinā, O Aśvin gods! Yā kaśā, the whip, the striker of horses, that belongs to vām, you two — come with it and mimikṣatam, wish to sprinkle, our sacrifice with soma juice: that is, having struck the horses hard with the whip and come at once, be ready to bring about the offering of soma juice meant for you. Of what kind is the whip? Madhumatī: among the hundred and one names of water, arṇaḥ, kṣodaḥ and the rest, madhu and purīṣam are read; so 'having water' is what is said: the whip is wet with the sweat that flows from the horse by its swift going. Sūnṛtāvatī, furnished with pleasing and true speech: the sound produced by the sharp stroke of the whip and the shout raised by the rider at the time of striking — both are pleasing to the sacrificer, as causes of swift going. Or: among the fifty-seven names of speech, ślokaḥ, dhārā and the rest, kaśā and dhiṣaṇā are read; the speech of the Aśvins that is madhumatī, sweet, free from harshness, sūnṛtāvatī, pleasing and true — that is, about the granting of fruit; joined with that speech, mimikṣatam the sacrifice: so it is to be construed." (Grammatical tail: kaśā, kaśa gatiśātanayoḥ, ac of the pacādi class, initial udātta as of the vṛṣādi class; sūnṛtāvatī, ūna parihāṇe, suṣṭhu ūnayaty apriyam iti sūn, the speech in which there is such ṛta, truth, is sūnṛtā; overriding the last-member final udātta by nañsubhyām, the ṛ is udātta by parādiś chandasi bahulam; the whip that has it is sūnṛtāvatī, a name of the whip; the v for the m of matup by saṃjñāyām (Pā. 8-2-11); mimikṣatam, san after mih, no guṇa because it is kit by halantāc ca (Pā. 1-2-10); ḍh, k and ṣ.)

Page 70 — Rik 3: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अश्विना (aśvinā) — O Aśvin deities | वां (vāṃ) — your | मधुमती (madhumatī) — soaked with the sweat of the horses | सूनृतावती (sūnṛtāvatī) — furnished with a sound pleasing and true (to the sacrificer who uses the whip) | या कशा (yā kaśā) — the whip that there is | तया (tayā) — with it (that is, using it on the horses and coming swiftly) | यज्ञं (yajñaṃ) — our sacrifice | मिमिक्षतं (mimikṣataṃ) — wish to make it furnished with soma juice (drink the soma). Or: अश्विना (aśvinā) — O Aśvin deities | वां (vāṃ) — your | मधुमती (madhumatī) — sweet, or gentle | सूनृतावती (sūnṛtāvatī) — pleasing and true | या कशा (yā kaśā) — the speech that there is | तया (tayā) — with it (furnished, that is, speaking good words) | यज्ञं (yajñaṃ) — (our) sacrifice | मिमिक्षतं (mimikṣataṃ) — make it furnished with the offering of soma juice.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Aśvin deities, driving your horses with the use of the whip so that they are soaked with sweat, and driving the horses by using the sounds that urge them on swiftly, come quickly (or, with your gentle speech, pleasing and true about the granting of boons), come to our sacrifice and be ready for the offering of soma juice (drink the soma).

॥ English Translation ॥

Aswanis [sic] sprinkle the sacrifice with your whip which is full of sweet juice (honey); lash (your horses) loudly.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The meaning of this ṛk is somewhat tangled. The main intention is: O Aśvin deities, striking the horses of your chariot well with your whip and urging them on with sounds uttered sharply so that the horses move fast, come quickly to this our sacrificial ground, and, made glad by drinking the sweet soma juice, give gladness to us too by your pleasing words.

कशा (kaśā) — pratodaḥ | the whip that urges the horse to move fast; "whip or horsewhip".

मधुमती (madhumatī) — sweet, pleasant to hear (a sound).

Page 71 — Rik 3: Special Topics (end), grammar

सूनृतावती (sūnṛtāvatī) — pleasing, true. In this ṛk, though the words madhumatī and sūnṛtāvatī are qualifiers of the word kaśā, it is more fitting to give each of them a separate definite meaning.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

कशा (kaśā) — the root kaśa gatiśātanayoḥ. After it, by nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134), the suffix ac of the pacādi type. By vṛṣādīnāṃ ca (Pā. Sū. 6-1-203) initial udātta.

सूनृतावती (sūnṛtāvatī) — the root ūna parihāṇe, of the tenth class. With the analysis apriyaṃ suṣṭhu ūnayati, 'that which removes the unpleasant well', it becomes sūn. Sūn-ṛtaṃ = satyaṃ yasyāṃ vāci sā sūnṛtā: a bahuvrīhi. The speech in which there is truth that removes the unpleasant well is understood by the word sūnṛtā. Sūnṛtā asyā astīti sūnṛtāvatī, the whip: by tad asyāsty asminn iti matup (Pā. Sū. 5-2-94) the suffix matup; with sūnṛtā + mat, by saṃjñāyām (Pā. Sū. 8-2-11) — when a name is meant, v for the m of matup — v for the m; by ugitaś ca (Pā. Sū. 6-3-45, as printed) ṅīp: sūnṛtāvatī. The sense: the whip having this name, that is, the speech.

मिमिक्षतम् (mimikṣatam) — the root miha secane. After it, by dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ… (Pā. Sū. 3-1-7), san; by sanyaṅoḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-9) reduplication; by halādiḥ śeṣaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-4-60) the h is removed: mi mih + sa. By halantāc ca (Pā. Sū. 1-2-10) — a san beginning with a jhal after a consonant near i, u, ṛ is kit — sa is kit. Since vasatir dahadihaduho nah mih ruh lih vahis tathā (Pā. Sū. 7-2-10 [?], Kā. 6) is read in the aniṭ-kārikā, the augment iṭ does not come to san; so sa begins with a jhal. Since the suffix sa is thus kit, guṇa is barred by kṅiti ca, so guṇa of the light penultimate by pugantalaghūpadhasya ca (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86) does not come. Mi mih + sa: now by ho ḍhaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-31) — at the end of a pada and before a jhal, ḍh for h — ḍh for the h; by ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si (Pā. Sū. 8-2-41) — before s, k for ṣ and ḍh — k for the ḍh: mi mik + sa; by ādeśapratyayayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-3-59) ṣ for the s: mi mikṣa; this is a root by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-32). Loṭ, in the middle person dual, when tam comes for thas, it becomes mimikṣatam. ॥3॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

न॒हि वा॒मस्ति॑ दूर॒के यत्रा॒ रथे॑न॒ गच्छ॑थः । अ॑श्विना सो॒मिनो॑ गृ॒हम् ॥४॥ [accent ?]

nahí vām ásti dūraké yatrā ráthena gácchathaḥ | aśvinā somíno gṛhám ||4|| [accent ?] Bars under न (नहि), वा, र (दूरके), त्रा and न (रथेन); strokes over स्ति, थे and च्छ. Line 2: a stroke over अ of अश्विना, a bar under सो, a stroke between मि and नो (read as over नो [accent ?]), a bar under गृ. The Pada prints यत्र.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

नहि । वाम् । अस्ति । दूरके । यत्र । रथेन । गच्छथः ॥ अश्विना । सोमिनः । गृहम् ॥४॥

nahi | vām | asti | dūrake | yatra | rathena | gacchathaḥ || aśvinā | sominaḥ | gṛham ||4||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अश्विना हे अश्विनौ देवौ युवां सोमिनः सोमवतो यजमानस्य गृहं प्रति रथेन गच्छथः । स मार्गो वां युवयोर्दूरके दूरदेशे नह्यस्ति । न वर्तते खलु । यद्वा । यत्र गृहे गच्छथस्तच्च गृहं दूरे न भवति ॥ नहि । एवमादीनामन्त इत्यन्तोदात्तः । अस्ति । चादिलोपे विभाषेति निघाताभावः । अत्र हि गृहं दूरे च नास्ति युवां च रथेन गच्छथ इति समुच्चयश्चार्थो गम्यते । चशब्दो न प्रयुज्यत इति चलोपे प्रथमा तिङ्विभक्तिरस्तीति । यत्र । निपातस्य चेति संहितायां दीर्घत्वं । गच्छथः । इयं यद्यपि न प्रथमा तथापि यत्रेति यद्वृत्तयोगान्न निघातः ॥

aśvinā he aśvinau devau yuvāṃ sominaḥ somavato yajamānasya gṛhaṃ prati rathena gacchathaḥ | sa mārgo vāṃ yuvayordūrake dūradeśe nahyasti | na vartate khalu | yadvā | yatra gṛhe gacchathastacca gṛhaṃ dūre na bhavati || nahi | evamādīnāmanta ityantodāttaḥ | asti | cādilope vibhāṣeti nighātābhāvaḥ | atra hi gṛhaṃ dūre ca nāsti yuvāṃ ca rathena gacchatha iti samuccayaścārtho gamyate | caśabdo na prayujyata iti calope prathamā tiṅvibhaktirastīti | yatra | nipātasya ceti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvaṃ | gacchathaḥ | iyaṃ yadyapi na prathamā tathāpi yatreti yadvṛttayogānna nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "Aśvinā, O Aśvin gods! You two gacchathaḥ, go, rathena, by chariot, to the gṛham, house, of the sominaḥ, the sacrificer who has soma. That way is nahi … asti, surely not, vām, for you two, dūrake, in a far place: it is not, indeed. Or: the house to which you go is not far." (Grammatical tail: nahi, final udātta by evamādīnām antaḥ; asti, no loss of accent by cādilope vibhāṣā: for here the conjunctive sense 'the house is not far and you go by chariot' is understood; the word ca is not used, so, ca being dropped, asti is the first finite verb; yatra, lengthening in the Saṃhitā by nipātasya ca; gacchathaḥ, although this is not the first, there is no loss of accent because of its connection with the yad-word yatra.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अश्विना (aśvinā) — O Aśvin deities, (you) | सोमिनः (sominaḥ) — of the sacrificer who prepares the soma juice | गृहं (gṛhaṃ) — to the house | रथेन (rathena) — on the chariot | गच्छथः (gacchathaḥ) — you go | सः (saḥ) — that path | वां (vāṃ) — for you | दूरके (dūrake) — far | नहि अस्ति (nahi asti) — is not, indeed.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Aśvin deities, the house of the sacrificer who prepares the soma juice, to which you have to go on the chariot, is not far. (So you should come quickly.)

Page 73 — Rik 4: English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

For to you, Aswins, the house of the Soma-sacrificer whither you go in your chariot is not far off.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

As said in the previous ṛk, your chariot can move fast. The whip with its sweet sound makes the horses move fast. So for you, who travel by chariot, the house of the performer of the soma sacrifice does not seem far. Seated in the fast-moving chariot you can come quickly to the sacrificer's house. The main intention is: that house is not far.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

नहि (nahi) — final udātta by evādīnām antaḥ (Phi. Sū. 8-2), by which the end of the words read in the evādi class is udātta. Although nahi is not in the evādi class, the intention is that, since it is an ākṛtigaṇa, it must be included there.

अस्ति (asti) — here the intended sense is: gṛhaṃ dūre ca nāsti, yuvāṃ ca rathena gacchathaḥ, the house is not far, and you travel by chariot. So the use of ca is needed; yet here that ca is not used; so by cādilope vibhāṣā (Pā. Sū. 8-1-63) — if ca, vā, ha, aha, eva are dropped, the first finite verb is not made unaccented — the first finite verb asti is not unaccented.

यत्र (yatra) — by nipātasya ca (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136) lengthening comes in the Saṃhitā to a particle in a mantra. Yatra is read in the cādi class; so by cādayo 'sattve (Pā. Sū. 1-4-57) — the words of the cādi class not expressing gender, number, case or a substance are called nipāta — it is a nipāta. Gacchathaḥ: though the dropping of ca is there, since this is not the first finite verb, the prohibition of total lack of accent by cādilope vibhāṣā does not come. Yet since there is connection with a word containing yad, namely yatra, by yadvṛttān nityam (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66) — a finite verb after a word containing yad is not unaccented — the prohibition comes, so total lack of accent does not come. In pūjanāt pūjitam anudāttam (Pā. Sū. 8-1-67), by the further mention of pūjita, it is made known that atra prakaraṇe pañcamīnirdeśe 'pi nānantaryam iṣyate; so even though gacchathaḥ is not immediately after the word yatra, there is no hindrance to the prohibition of lack of accent. ॥4॥ The maxim quoted, as printed: "in this section, even with a fifth-case statement, immediate sequence is not required".

अत्र प्रकरणे पञ्चमीनिर्देशेऽपि नानन्तर्यमिष्यते ।

atra prakaraṇe pañcamīnirdeśe 'pi nānantaryamiṣyate |

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ It opens with the application of ṛks 5–8.

व्यूढस्य द्वितीये छन्दोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे हिरण्यपाणिमूतय इति सावित्र्यश्चतस्रः । द्वितीयस्येति खण्डे सूत्रितं । हिरण्यपाणिमूतय इति चतस्रो मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नः । आ० ८-१० । इति ॥

vyūḍhasya dvitīye chandome vaiśvadevaśastre hiraṇyapāṇimūtaya iti sāvitryaścatasraḥ | dvitīyasyeti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | hiraṇyapāṇimūtaya iti catasro mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ | ā0 8-10 | iti ||

Translation (application): "In the second chandoma day of the vyūḍha [dvādaśāha], at the vaiśvadeva-śastra, the four ṛks to Savitṛ beginning hiraṇyapāṇim ūtaye; it is laid down in the section dvitīyasya: 'hiraṇyapāṇim ūtaye: four; mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ' (Āśv. 8-10)."

ऊतयेऽस्मद्रक्षणार्थं सवितारं देवमुप ह्वये । आह्वयामि । स च सविता देव एतन्मन्त्रप्रतिपाद्यदेवता भूत्वा पदं यजमानेन प्राप्यं स्थानं चेत्ता । ज्ञापयिता भवति । कीदृशं सवितारं । हिरण्यपाणिं यजमानाय दातुं हस्ते सुवर्णधारिणं । यद्वा । देवकर्तृके यागे सविता स्वयमृत्विग्भूत्वा ब्रह्मत्वेनावस्थितः । तदानीं कस्यांचिदिष्टावध्वर्यवस्तस्मै सवित्रे ब्रह्मणे प्राशित्रनामकं पुरोडाशभागं दत्तवन्तः । तच्च प्राशित्रं हस्ते सवित्रा गृहीतं सत्तदीयपाणिं चिच्छेद । ततः प्राशित्रस्य दातारोऽध्वर्यवः सुवर्णमयं पाणिं निर्माय प्रक्षिप्तवन्तः । सोऽयमर्थः कौषीतकिब्राह्मणे समाम्नातः । सवित्रे प्राशित्रं प्रतिजह्रुस्तत्तस्य पाणी प्रचिच्छेद तस्मै हिरण्मयौ प्रतिदधुस्तस्माद्धिरण्यपाणिरिति स्तुत इति । हिरण्यशब्दं पाणिशब्दं च यास्क एवं निर्वक्ति । हिरण्यं कस्माद्ध्रियत आयम्यमानमिति वा ह्रियते जनाज्जनमिति वा हितरमणं भवतीति वा हर्यतेर्वा स्यात्प्रेप्साकर्मणः । नि० २-१० । इति । तथा पाणिः । पणायतेः पूजाकर्मणः । नि० २-२६ । इति ॥ हिरण्यशब्दो नब्विषयत्वादाद्युदात्तः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । ऊतये । उदात्त इत्यनुवृत्तावूतियूतिजूतिसातीत्यादिना क्तिन्नन्तोऽन्तोदात्तो निपातितः । सवितारं । तृचश्चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वं । चेत्ता । चिती संज्ञाने । अस्मादन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात्ताच्छील्ये तृन् । अनित्यमागमशासनमितीडभावः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । देवता । देवात्तल् । पा० ५-४-२७ । इति स्वार्थे तल् । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वमुदात्तत्वं । पदशब्दः पचाद्यजन्तः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तः ॥४॥

ūtaye 'smadrakṣaṇārthaṃ savitāraṃ devamupa hvaye | āhvayāmi | sa ca savitā deva etanmantrapratipādyadevatā bhūtvā padaṃ yajamānena prāpyaṃ sthānaṃ cettā | jñāpayitā bhavati | kīdṛśaṃ savitāraṃ | hiraṇyapāṇiṃ yajamānāya dātuṃ haste suvarṇadhāriṇaṃ | yadvā | devakartṛke yāge savitā svayamṛtvigbhūtvā brahmatvenāvasthitaḥ | tadānīṃ kasyāṃcidiṣṭāvadhvaryavastasmai savitre brahmaṇe prāśitranāmakaṃ puroḍāśabhāgaṃ dattavantaḥ | tacca prāśitraṃ haste savitrā gṛhītaṃ sattadīyapāṇiṃ ciccheda | tataḥ prāśitrasya dātāro 'dhvaryavaḥ suvarṇamayaṃ pāṇiṃ nirmāya prakṣiptavantaḥ | so 'yamarthaḥ kauṣītakibrāhmaṇe samāmnātaḥ | savitre prāśitraṃ pratijahrustattasya pāṇī praciccheda tasmai hiraṇmayau pratidadhustasmāddhiraṇyapāṇiriti stuta iti | hiraṇyaśabdaṃ pāṇiśabdaṃ ca yāska evaṃ nirvakti | hiraṇyaṃ kasmāddhriyata āyamyamānamiti vā hriyate janājjanamiti vā hitaramaṇaṃ bhavatīti vā haryatervā syātprepsākarmaṇaḥ | ni0 2-10 | iti | tathā pāṇiḥ | paṇāyateḥ pūjākarmaṇaḥ | ni0 2-26 | iti || hiraṇyaśabdo nabviṣayatvādādyudāttaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaraḥ | ūtaye | udātta ityanuvṛttāvūtiyūtijūtisātītyādinā ktinnanto 'ntodātto nipātitaḥ | savitāraṃ | tṛcaścittvādantodāttatvaṃ | cettā | citī saṃjñāne | asmādantarbhāvitaṇyarthāttācchīlye tṛn | anityamāgamaśāsanamitīḍabhāvaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | devatā | devāttal | pā0 5-4-27 | iti svārthe tal | litīti pratyayātpūrvamudāttatvaṃ | padaśabdaḥ pacādyajantaḥ | cita ityantodāttaḥ ||4||

Translation: "Ūtaye, for our protection, I upa hvaye, call, the god Savitṛ. And that god Savitṛ, being the deity set forth by this mantra, is the cettā, the one who makes known, the padam, the place to be reached by the sacrificer. What kind of Savitṛ? Hiraṇyapāṇim, holding gold in his hand to give to the sacrificer. Or: in a sacrifice performed by the gods, Savitṛ himself, becoming a priest, was placed as the brahman. Then at a certain iṣṭi the adhvaryus gave to that Savitṛ, the brahman, the portion of the puroḍāśa called prāśitra; and that prāśitra, taken by Savitṛ in his hand, cut off his hand. Then the adhvaryus, the givers of the prāśitra, made a hand of gold and put it on. This matter is recorded in the Kauṣītaki-brāhmaṇa: 'They presented the prāśitra to Savitṛ; it cut off his hands; they put on him hands of gold; therefore he is praised as hiraṇyapāṇi.' Yāska explains the words hiraṇya and pāṇi thus: 'Hiraṇya — why? It is carried (hriyate) when stretched out; or it is carried from man to man; or it is a pleasing good (hita-ramaṇa); or it may be from hary, in the sense of wishing to obtain' (Ni. 2-10); likewise 'pāṇi, from paṇāy, in the sense of honouring' (Ni. 2-26)." (Grammatical tail: hiraṇya, initially udātta because it falls under nab; in the bahuvrīhi the first member's accent; ūtaye, with udāttaḥ carried on, the ktin-form with final udātta is given as a set form by ūtiyūtijūtisāti…; savitāram, final udātta because tṛc is cit; cettā, citī saṃjñāne, with the causative sense included, tṛn in the sense of habit, no iṭ by anityam āgamaśāsanam, initial udātta because it is nit; devatā, tal in its own sense by devāt tal (Pā. 5-4-27), the udātta before the suffix by liti; pada, ending in ac of the pacādi class, final udātta by citaḥ. The bhāṣya ends with ॥४॥, the close of the fourth varga.)

Page 75 — Rik 5: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

ऊतये (ūtaye) — for (our) protection | हिरण्यपाणिं (hiraṇyapāṇiṃ) — holding gold in the hand (for the sacrificer), or having a hand made of gold | सवितारं (savitāraṃ) — the deity named Savitṛ (the sun) | उप ह्वये (upa hvaye) — I call | सः (saḥ) — that Savitṛ | देवता (devatā) — as the deity (set forth by the mantra) | पदं (padaṃ) — the place (to be reached by the sacrificer) | चेत्ता (cettā) — makes known (tells).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

May the deity Savitṛ, who holds in his hand gold to give to the sacrificer, protect us. Called by us, may he come and make known the place to be reached by the sacrificer.

॥ English Translation ॥

I invoke Savitri, the golden-handed (or with gold in his hand) to protect me; among gods he is the one who appoints the place of the worshipper.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

हिरण्यपाणिं (hiraṇyapāṇiṃ) — yajamānāya dātuṃ haste suvarṇadhāriṇam | Because he holds gold in his hand to give to the sacrificer, he is named hiraṇyapāṇi. Or hiraṇmayau pāṇī yasya saḥ: because he has hands made of gold, he is named hiraṇyapāṇi. The commentator says there is a story about this in the Kauṣītaki-brāhmaṇa:

देवकर्तृके यागे सविता स्वयमृत्विग्भूत्वा ब्रह्मत्वेनावस्थितः । तदानीं कस्यांचिदिष्टावध्वर्यवस्तस्मै सवित्रे ब्रह्मणे प्राशित्रनामकं पुरोडाशभागं दत्तवन्तः । तच्च प्राशित्रं हस्ते सवित्रा गृहीतं सत्तदीयपाणिं चिच्छेद । ततः प्राशित्रस्य दातारोऽध्वर्यवः सुवर्णमयं पाणिं निर्माय प्रक्षिप्तवन्तः ॥ सवित्रे प्राशित्रं प्रतिजह्रुस्तत्तस्य पाणी प्रचिच्छेद तस्मै हिरण्मयौ प्रतिदधुस्तस्माद्धिरण्यपाणिरिति स्तुत इति ॥

devakartṛke yāge savitā svayamṛtvigbhūtvā brahmatvenāvasthitaḥ | tadānīṃ kasyāṃcidiṣṭāvadhvaryavastasmai savitre brahmaṇe prāśitranāmakaṃ puroḍāśabhāgaṃ dattavantaḥ | tacca prāśitraṃ haste savitrā gṛhītaṃ sattadīyapāṇiṃ ciccheda | tataḥ prāśitrasya dātāro 'dhvaryavaḥ suvarṇamayaṃ pāṇiṃ nirmāya prakṣiptavantaḥ || savitre prāśitraṃ pratijahrustattasya pāṇī praciccheda tasmai hiraṇmayau pratidadhustasmāddhiraṇyapāṇiriti stuta iti || The passage repeats the bhāṣya; rendered above.

Page 76 — Rik 5: Special Topics (continued)

When the gods were performing a sacrifice, Savitṛ too was one of the priests. But instead of carrying out a priest's duty he was seated in the place of the brahman. Then the priests called adhvaryus in that sacrifice, thinking that this Savitṛ seated in the brahman's place was the brahman, unknowingly gave him the portion of the puroḍāśa called prāśitra, which is to be given to the brahman. But as soon as the mistake became known, before Savitṛ could eat the puroḍāśa, they cut off his hands, which were holding it. So that Savitṛ should not go without hands, the adhvaryus made hands of gold and joined them to Savitṛ. The main intention of this story is that, since Savitṛ's hands were thus made of gold, Savitṛ is praised as hiraṇyapāṇi.

Yāska has explained the derivation of the word hiraṇya and of the word pāṇi thus:

हिरण्यं कस्माद्ध्रियत आयम्यमानमिति वा । ह्रियते जनाज्जनमिति वा । हितरमणं भवतीति वा । हर्यतेर्वा स्यात्प्रेप्साकर्मणः ॥ (नि० २-१०)

hiraṇyaṃ kasmāddhriyata āyamyamānamiti vā | hriyate janājjanamiti vā | hitaramaṇaṃ bhavatīti vā | haryatervā syātprepsākarmaṇaḥ || (ni0 2-10)

There are many reasons why gold gets the name hiraṇya. Since craftsmen and others make ornaments such as bracelets and spread its excellence, it is named hiraṇya; since people use it in dealings such as trade, it is named hiraṇya; since it stands by as a help in times of trouble to those who have it and does them good, it is named hiraṇya; since it gives joy to the mind, it is named hiraṇya; and since all desire it and it is an impeller (in the form of wealth) for all undertakings, it is named hiraṇya.

The derivation of the word pāṇi:

पाणिः पणायतेः पूजाकर्मणः प्रगृह्य पाणी देवान्पूजयन्ति ॥ (नि० २-२६)

pāṇiḥ paṇāyateḥ pūjākarmaṇaḥ pragṛhya pāṇī devānpūjayanti || (ni0 2-26)

Since one joins them and spreads them wide to worship the gods, they are called pāṇi. Hiraṇyapāṇi means one who has gold in the hand, or one who has hands made of gold (made from gold).

सवितारं (savitāraṃ) — Savitṛ. For the word savitṛ Yāska —

Page 77 — Rik 5: Special Topics (end), grammar

सविता सर्वस्य प्रसविता ॥ (नि० १०-३१) आदित्योऽपि सवितोच्यते ॥ (नि० १०-३२)

savitā sarvasya prasavitā || (ni0 10-31) ādityo 'pi savitocyate || (ni0 10-32)

— has given the derivation: "Savitṛ, the impeller (prasavitṛ) of all"; "the sun too is called Savitṛ". That is, because he brings about, that is gives, all the desired things people need, this deity is named Savitṛ; and the sun too is named Savitṛ (sūrya).

स चेत्ता देवता पदं (sa cettā devatā padaṃ) — sa ca savitā yajamānena prāpyasthānaṃ jñāpayitā bhavati: the commentator has explained this sentence as "this Savitṛ makes known the place the sacrificer is fit to reach". Yet the sense does not fit well. What the ṛṣi intends is not clear.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

हिरण्यपाणिं (hiraṇyapāṇiṃ) — the word hiraṇya is always neuter; by nabviṣayasyānisantasya (Phi. Sū. 26) initially udātta; or, as set out at indro vajrī hiraṇyayaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-2), it ends in the suffix kanyan by haryateḥ kanyan hir ca (U. Sū. 5-[?]), so it is initially udātta by the nit accent. Hiraṇyaṃ pāṇau yasya saḥ: a bahuvrīhi. By bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-7 [?], as read) the first member keeps its own accent.

ऊतये (ūtaye) — with the word udāttaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-3-96) carried on, by ūtiyūtijūtisātihetikīrtayaś ca (Pā. Sū. 3-3-97) it is given as a set form ending in ktin and with final udātta.

सवितारम् (savitāram) — the root ṣū preraṇe. By dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) s for the ṣ; by ṇvultṛcau (Pā. Sū. 3-1-133) tṛc: sū + tṛ, the augment iṭ, guṇa, the substitute av: savitṛ. In the accusative singular it becomes savitāram. The suffix tṛc has the marker c; so by citaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the final udātta comes.

चेत्ता (cettā) — the root citī saṃjñāne; after it, by tṛn (Pā. Sū. 3-2-135) — when the agents are of that habit, that nature, or doers of it well, the suffix tṛn comes after the root — the suffix tṛn. By anityam āgamaśāsanam (Paribhā. 66) the rule prescribing the augment iṭ is not binding, so iṭ does not come here. By pugantalaghūpadhasya ca (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86) guṇa of the light penultimate. Nominative singular suffix su: cettṛ + su; by ṛduśanaspurudaṃso 'nehasāṃ ca (Pā. Sū. 7-1-94) — when a su other than the vocative follows, to words ending in ṛ,

Page 78 (upper) — Rik 5: grammar (end)

and to the words uśanas and the rest, the substitute anaṅ comes — the substitute anaṅ: cettan + s. By aptṛntṛcsvasṛnaptṛneṣṭṛtvaṣṭṛkṣattṛhotṛpotṛpraśāstṝṇām (Pā. Sū. 6-4-11) — when a sarvanāmasthāna other than the vocative follows, the vowel penultimate in ap and the rest is lengthened — lengthening; by halṅyābbhyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-68) su is dropped; by nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya (Pā. Sū. 8-2-7) the n is dropped: it becomes cettā. The suffix is nit; by ñnity ādir nityam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) initial udātta.

देवता (devatā) — by devāt tal (Pā. Sū. 5-4-27 [?]) — after the word deva, the suffix tal in its own sense — the suffix tal; by liti (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the v (va) before the suffix is udātta.

पदं (padaṃ) — the root pada gatau. By nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134) the suffix ac; by citaḥ final udātta. ॥5॥

Page 78 (lower) — Sūkta 22, Rik 6

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒पां नपा॑त॒मव॑से सवि॒तार॒मुप॑ स्तु॒हि । तस्य॑ व्र॒तान्यु॑श्मसि ॥६॥ [accent ?]

apā́ṃ nápātam ávase savitā́ram úpa stuhí | tásya vratā́ny uśmasi ||6|| [accent ?] Bars under अ (अपां), त (नपातम्), वि (सवि), र (तारम्) and स्तु; strokes over पा (नपात), व (अवसे) and प (उप). Line 2: a stroke over स्य, a bar under व्र, a stroke just after ता, read as over न्यु [accent ?]. The Pada line 1 ends with a single daṇḍa.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अपां । नपातं । अवसे । सवितारं । उप । स्तुहि । तस्य । व्रतानि । उश्मसि ॥६॥

apāṃ | napātaṃ | avase | savitāraṃ | upa | stuhi | tasya | vratāni | uśmasi ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The bhāṣya runs on to p. 79, whose header reads Varga 5. The Pāṇini number is read २-३-६९ and the Manu number ३-७६.

अत्र होता सामगमृत्विजमन्यं वा शस्त्रिणं ब्रूते । अवसेऽस्मान्रक्षितुं सवितारमुप स्तुहि । तस्य सवितुः संबन्धीनि व्रतानि कर्माणि सोमयागादिरूपाण्युश्मसि । कामयामहे । कीदृशं सवितारं । अपां नपातं जलस्य न पालकं । संतापेन शोषकमित्यर्थः ॥ अपां । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । नपातं । पा रक्षणे । अस्य शत्रन्तः पाच्छब्दः । तस्य नञा समासे नभ्राण्नपादित्यादिना नलोपप्रतिषेध इति वृत्तिकारः । अग्निर्ह्यपो न पाति तच्छोषकत्वात् । तर्हि कथमपामिति षष्ठी । न लोकाव्ययनिष्ठाखलर्थेति । पा० २-३-६९ । कर्मणि षष्ठ्याः प्रतिषेधादिति चेत् । तर्ह्येषा शेषलक्षणास्तु । अग्न्यादित्यावपां कारणतया संबन्धिनावग्नेरापः इति श्रुतेः । आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिः । मनु० ३-७६ । इति स्मृतेश्च । अस्मिन्पक्ष उगिदचामिति नुमभावोऽपि निपातनादेवेति मन्तव्यं । पातेः क्विबन्तस्य तुगभावो निपातनाद्द्रष्टव्यः । अथवा न पातयतीति नपात् । पत्लृ गताविति धातोर्ण्यन्तात्क्विप् । अग्न्यादित्यौ ह्यपां न प्रापकौ प्रत्युत तच्छोषकौ । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अवसे । तुमर्थे सेसेनित्यादिना असेन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । उश्मसि । वश कान्तौ । अदिप्रभृतिभ्य इति शपो लुक् । इदन्तो मसिरितीकारोपजनः ॥

atra hotā sāmagamṛtvijamanyaṃ vā śastriṇaṃ brūte | avase 'smānrakṣituṃ savitāramupa stuhi | tasya savituḥ saṃbandhīni vratāni karmāṇi somayāgādirūpāṇyuśmasi | kāmayāmahe | kīdṛśaṃ savitāraṃ | apāṃ napātaṃ jalasya na pālakaṃ | saṃtāpena śoṣakamityarthaḥ || apāṃ | ūḍidamityādinā vibhakterudāttatvaṃ | napātaṃ | pā rakṣaṇe | asya śatrantaḥ pācchabdaḥ | tasya nañā samāse nabhrāṇnapādityādinā nalopapratiṣedha iti vṛttikāraḥ | agnirhyapo na pāti tacchoṣakatvāt | tarhi kathamapāmiti ṣaṣṭhī | na lokāvyayaniṣṭhākhalartheti | pā0 2-3-69 | karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhyāḥ pratiṣedhāditi cet | tarhyeṣā śeṣalakṣaṇāstu | agnyādityāvapāṃ kāraṇatayā saṃbandhināvagnerāpaḥ iti śruteḥ | ādityājjāyate vṛṣṭiḥ | manu0 3-76 | iti smṛteśca | asminpakṣa ugidacāmiti numabhāvo 'pi nipātanādeveti mantavyaṃ | pāteḥ kvibantasya tugabhāvo nipātanāddraṣṭavyaḥ | athavā na pātayatīti napāt | patlṛ gatāviti dhātorṇyantātkvip | agnyādityau hyapāṃ na prāpakau pratyuta tacchoṣakau | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | avase | tumarthe sesenityādinā asen | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | uśmasi | vaśa kāntau | adiprabhṛtibhya iti śapo luk | idanto masiritīkāropajanaḥ ||

Translation: "Here the hotṛ speaks to the sāman-singing priest, or to another priest who recites the śastra. Upa stuhi, praise, Savitṛ, avase, to protect us. Tasya, of that Savitṛ, the vratāni, rites, in the form of the soma sacrifice and the like, we uśmasi, desire. What kind of Savitṛ? Apāṃ napātam, not the protector of water: that is, its drier by his heat." (Grammatical tail: apām, the case-ending udātta by ūḍidam…; napātam, pā rakṣaṇe, pāt ending in śatṛ; in its compound with nañ the dropping of n is barred by nabhrāṇ napāt…, says the author of the vṛtti; for Agni does not protect the waters, being their drier. Then how the genitive apām? If it is said that the genitive of the object is barred by na lokāvyayaniṣṭhākhalartha… (Pā. 2-3-69), then let this be the genitive of relation (śeṣa): Agni and Āditya are related to the waters as their cause, by the śruti agner āpaḥ and the smṛti ādityāj jāyate vṛṣṭiḥ (Manu 3-76). On this view the absence of num by ugidacām is also to be held as from the set form, and the absence of tuk in pā ending in kvip likewise. Or: na pātayatīti napāt, kvip after the causative of patḷ gatau: Agni and Āditya do not lead the waters to [men], but rather dry them up; the accent of the indeclinable first member; avase, asen in the sense of the infinitive by tumarthe sesen…, initial udātta as nit; uśmasi, vaśa kāntau, śap dropped by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ, the i added by idanto masi.)

Page 79 — Rik 6: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अपां (apāṃ) — of water | नपातं (napātaṃ) — not the protector (the one who dries it) | सवितारं (savitāraṃ) — Savitṛ | अवसे (avase) — for our protection | उप स्तुहि (upa stuhi) — praise | तस्य (tasya) — connected with him | व्रतानि (vratāni) — the rites, the soma sacrifice and the rest | उश्मसि (uśmasi) — we wish (to perform).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

We wish to perform the rites, the soma sacrifice and the rest, connected with Savitṛ. Therefore praise Savitṛ, who dries the water with his heat.

॥ English Translation ॥

Praise Savitri, who is no friend of water for our protection; we desire to perform his worship.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The commentator explains that the hotṛ speaks this ṛk addressing either the udgātṛ, who sings the sāman, or another priest who recites the śastra mantras.

अपां नपातं (apāṃ napātaṃ) — jalasya na pālakam | jalasya śoṣakam: the commentator here says the sense is that the sun is named apāṃ napāt because he is opposed to water, the one who dries up water.

Page 80 — Rik 6: Special Topics (end), grammar

But Yāska says that the word apāṃ napāt and the word tanūnapāt are words of the same meaning, and gives two meanings for the word tanūnapāt: ājya (melted ghee) and Agni (Ni. 10-18 and 8-5). But the meaning given here by the commentator is the fitting one.

व्रतानि (vratāni) — somayāgādirūpāṇi karmāṇi | A vrata is a rite performed by rule; here it means rites such as the soma sacrifice.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

उश्मसि (uśmasi) — kāmayāmahe | we wish. The intention is: we wish to perform the soma sacrifices and the rest addressed to Savitṛ.

अपां (apāṃ) — by ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the ending ām after the word ap is udātta.

नपातम् (napātam) — the root pā rakṣaṇe, laṭ; by laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau the substitute śatṛ for laṭ: pā + at, the vikaraṇa śap, the following form, lengthening of like vowels: pāt; na + pāt = napāt. By nañ (Pā. Sū. 2-2-6) — nañ compounds with a related word ending in sup, and it is a tatpuruṣa — the nañ-tatpuruṣa compound. By nalopo nañaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-3-73), when a last member follows, the n of nañ would be dropped. But by nabhrāṇnapānnavedānāsatyānamucinakulanakhanapuṃsakanakṣatranākeṣu prakṛtyā (Pā. Sū. 6-3-75) the n of the nañ-compounds in this sūtra stays as it is, that is, is not dropped; so the n is not dropped. The author of the vṛtti has said this point, and it is right. Apāṃ napāt means Agni. Apāṃ = of water; napāt = not the one who protects: so the analysis. Agni does not protect water; he only dries it. So it is fitting that apāṃ napāt denotes Agni. But in apāṃ napāt, by kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti (Pā. Sū. 2-3-65), the genitive of the object would have to be stated. For that, since the suffix śatṛ, a substitute for la, is used, there is the prohibition of the genitive by na lokāvyayaniṣṭhākhalarthatṛnām (Pā. Sū. 2-6-69 [?], as read). So, if it is asked how the genitive of the object is obtained in apāṃ napāt: then we do not accept the genitive of the object here at all. By ṣaṣṭhī śeṣe (Pā. Sū. 2-3-50) we accept the genitive of relation, and we take the water, which is the object, as intended in the sense of relation. Since Agni and Āditya are both causes of water, they are related to ap:

Page 81 — Rik 6: grammar (continued)

the śruti अग्नेरापः (agner āpaḥ) (Tai. Ā. 8-2), "water came from Agni", teaches that Agni is the cause of water; and the Manusmṛti आदित्याज्जायते वृष्टिः (ādityāj jāyate vṛṣṭiḥ) (Manu 3-76), "rain arises from the sun", teaches that the sun is the cause of water. So the genitive comes here in the relation of produced and producer, and there is no difficulty about the genitive. Here another doubt arises: in places like napāt, napātam, when a sarvanāmasthāna suffix follows, since śatṛ is ugit, by ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-70) — when a sarvanāmasthāna suffix follows, the augment num comes to an ugit not belonging to a root and to the root añc with its n dropped — the augment num might be said to come. On this view one must say that the augment num does not come because the absence of num is laid down as a set form (nipātana) by giving napāt in the sūtra nabhrāṇnapāt. Or: after the root pā, the suffix kvip by kvip ca (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76); in kvip all its letters are dropped; by nipātana the augment tuk for pā: pāt. On this view there is no use of a substitute for la and the like, so the prohibition na lokāvyaya… does not come; so the genitive of the object can come by kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti, and there is no trouble of resorting to the genitive of relation. At ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat (Pā. Sū. 6-2-140) the author of the vṛtti has stated this view: pāteḥ kvipi nipātanāt tuk. Or: na pātayati, na prāpayatīti napāt: after the root patḷ gatau, ṇic; by ata upadhāyāḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116) vṛddhi of the penultimate: pāt + i; after these the suffix kvip; by ṇer aniṭi (Pā. Sū. 6-4-51) — when an ārdhadhātuka not beginning with iṭ follows, ṇi is dropped — ṇic is dropped. It is well known that Agni and Āditya are both driers of water (those who make it dry); so they are not those who lead water [to men] but rather driers. On this view there is no need to resort to a set form; the genitive of the object too is obtained. On the first view, pā is udātta by the root accent; śap being pit, and śatṛ, standing in place of la, being a sārvadhātuka with the accent of the original teaching, are both unaccented; by ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ the ā in pā is udātta. On the last two views only the root accent comes in pā. After compounding, by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the accent of the kṛt final member comes and that accent stays.

अवसे (avase) — the root ava rakṣaṇe. By tumarthe sesenasaasen… (Pā. Sū. 3-4-9), in the sense of the suffix tumun, that is, in the action sense by the rule avyayakṛto bhāve, the suffix asen comes. The suffix is nit; so by the nit accent initial udātta.

Page 82 (upper) — Rik 6: grammar (end)

उश्मसि (uśmasi) — the root vaśa kāntau; laṭ, first person plural mas; by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72) śap is dropped (luk); by idanto masi (Pā. Sū. 7-1-46) the augment i as the final part; by sārvadhātukam apit (Pā. Sū. 1-2-4) mas is ṅit; by grahijyāvayivyadhivaṣṭi… (Pā. Sū. 6-1-16) saṃprasāraṇa of the v: u, and the preceding form. ॥6॥
