॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

वि॒भ॒क्तारं॑ हवाम॒हे वसो॑श्चि॒त्रस्य॒ राध॑सः । स॒वि॒तारं॑ नृ॒चक्ष॑सं ॥७॥

vibhaktā́raṃ havāmahé vásoś citrásya rā́dhasaḥ | savitā́raṃ nṛcákṣasaṃ ||7|| Bars under वि, भ, हे, श्चि and स्य; strokes over रं (विभक्तारं), सो and ध. Line 2: bars under स, वि and नृ; strokes over ता and क्ष.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

विऽभक्तारं । हवामहे । वसोः । चित्रस्य । राधसः ॥ सवितारं । नृऽचक्षसं ॥७॥

vi 'bhaktāraṃ | havāmahe | vasoḥ | citrasya | rādhasaḥ || savitāraṃ | nṛ 'cakṣasaṃ ||7||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

(Printed हूयतेः and विभक्ताभ्यः, as printed.)

वसोर्निवासहेतोश्चित्रस्य सुवर्णरजतादिरूपेण बहुविधस्य राधसो धनस्य विभक्तारं अस्य यजमानस्यैतावद्धनदानमुचितमिति विभागकारिणं नृचक्षसं मनुष्याणां प्रकाशकारिणं सवितारं हवामहे । कौषीतकिन एतस्या ऋचो व्याख्यानरूपे ब्राह्मणे सवितुर्विभागहेतुत्वमेव समामनन्ति । यदेतद्वसोश्चित्रं राधस्तदेष सविता विभक्ताभ्यः प्रजाभ्यो विभजतीति ॥ विभक्तारं । तृचश्चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वं । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन तदेव शिष्यते । हवामहे । हूयतेर्बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणं । वसोः । वस निवासे । शॄस्वृस्निहीत्यादिना उः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेर्नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । राधसः । असुनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । नृचक्षसं । नॄंश्चष्ट इति नृचक्षाः । तं नृचक्षसं । चक्षेर्बहुलं शिच्च । उ० ४-२३२ । इत्यसुन् । शित्त्वादनार्धधातुकत्वेन ख्याञादेशाभावः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

vasornivāsahetościtrasya suvarṇarajatādirūpeṇa bahuvidhasya rādhaso dhanasya vibhaktāraṃ asya yajamānasyaitāvaddhanadānamucitamiti vibhāgakāriṇaṃ nṛcakṣasaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ prakāśakāriṇaṃ savitāraṃ havāmahe | kauṣītakina etasyā ṛco vyākhyānarūpe brāhmaṇe saviturvibhāgahetutvameva samāmananti | yadetadvasościtraṃ rādhastadeṣa savitā vibhaktābhyaḥ prajābhyo vibhajatīti || vibhaktāraṃ | tṛcaścittvādantodāttatvaṃ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvena tadeva śiṣyate | havāmahe | hūyaterbahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇaṃ | vasoḥ | vasa nivāse | śṝsvṛsnihītyādinā uḥ | nidityanuvṛtternittvādādyudāttaḥ | rādhasaḥ | asunanto nittvādādyudāttaḥ | nṛcakṣasaṃ | nṝṃścaṣṭa iti nṛcakṣāḥ | taṃ nṛcakṣasaṃ | cakṣerbahulaṃ śicca | u0 4-232 | ityasun | śittvādanārdhadhātukatvena khyāñādeśābhāvaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||

Translation: "We havāmahe, call, Savitṛ, the vibhaktāram, the distributor — the one who makes the division 'this much gift of wealth is fit for this sacrificer' — of the rādhas, wealth, citra, of many kinds in the form of gold, silver and the like, of the vasu, the cause of dwelling; nṛcakṣasam, the illuminer of men. The Kauṣītakins, in the brāhmaṇa that explains this ṛk, record only Savitṛ's being the cause of division: 'This bright wealth of vasu, this Savitṛ distributes to the creatures that are divided.'" (Grammatical tail: vibhaktāram, final udātta because tṛc is cit, which alone remains by the accent of the kṛt final member; havāmahe, saṃprasāraṇa by bahulaṃ chandasi; vasoḥ, vasa nivāse, u by śṝsvṛsnihi…, initially udātta as nit, nit being carried on; rādhasaḥ, ending in asun, initially udātta as nit; nṛcakṣasam, 'he sees men', asun by cakṣer bahulaṃ śic ca (U. 4-232), and, being śit, not ārdhadhātuka, so no substitute khyāñ; the accent of the kṛt final member.)

Page 83 — Rik 7: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

वसोः (vasoḥ) — connected with the house | चित्रस्य (citrasya) — of many kinds | राधसः (rādhasaḥ) — of wealth | विभक्तारं (vibhaktāraṃ) — the one who divides | नृचक्षसं (nṛcakṣasaṃ) — who gives light (gives knowledge) to men | सवितारं (savitāraṃ) — Savitṛ | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we call.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

We call Savitṛ, who distributes, according to each one's fitness, wealth such as gold and silver connected with houses and the like (together with houses and the like), and who gives light.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke Savitri, the distributor of various kinds of wealth including the house and the enlighter [sic] of men.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The main intention of this ṛk: the deity Savitṛ gives wealth and the like of many kinds, gives houses and the like as dwelling places, and gives knowledge to people according to each one's fitness. We call such a Savitṛ.

विभक्तारं (vibhaktāraṃ) — vibhāgakāriṇam | the one who distributes according to each one's fitness, or who gives wealth and the like according to each one's rites, such as the performance of sacrifice.

वसोश्चित्रस्य राधसः (vasoś citrasya rādhasaḥ) — wealth of many kinds and riches, together with houses and the like as dwelling places.

नृचक्षसं (nṛcakṣasaṃ) — nṝṃś caṣṭa iti nṛcakṣāḥ | taṃ nṛcakṣasam | manuṣyāṇāṃ prakāśakāriṇam || The meaning is: he who gives knowledge to men, who impels the intellect. On this the well-known Gāyatrī mantra, धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् (dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt), clearly makes known that Savitṛ impels our intellect.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

विभक्तारम् (vibhaktāram) — after the root bhaja with the prefix vi, the suffix tṛc. The suffix is cit, so the cit accent comes. After the compound with the word vi, the accent of the kṛt final member comes and that accent stays.

हवामहे (havāmahe) — the root hveñ saṃprasāraṇe [as printed]. With hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam carried on, by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. Sū. 6-1-34) saṃprasāraṇa: u for the v;

Page 84 (upper) — Rik 7: grammar (end)

by saṃprasāraṇāc ca (Pā. Sū. 6-1-108) the preceding form; laṭ, mahiṅ; by ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e (Pā. Sū. 3-4-79) e for the ṭi; śap, guṇa, the substitute av; by ato dīrgho yañi (Pā. Sū. 7-3-101) the stem ending in a is lengthened.

वसोः (vasoḥ) — the root vasa nivāse. By śṝsvṛsnihitrapyasivasihanikliśibandhimanibhyaś ca (U. Sū. 1-10) the suffix u; the word nit from the preceding sūtra dhānye nit is carried on into this sūtra; so, the suffix being nit, the nit accent comes.

राधसः (rādhasaḥ) — rādha sādha saṃsiddhau; by sarvadhātubhyo 'sun (U. Sū. 4-6-28 [?]) the suffix asun. The suffix being nit, rādhasaḥ is initially udātta.

नृचक्षसं (nṛcakṣasaṃ) — nṝn caṣṭe iti (one who gives light to men): so the analysis; it becomes nṛcakṣāḥ; in the accusative singular it becomes nṛcakṣasam. By cakṣer bahulaṃ śic ca (U. Sū. 4-6-27 [?]) the suffix asun comes after the root cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci, and it is variously śit: so the suffix asun. The suffix being śit, by tiṅśit sārvadhātukam it is called sārvadhātuka; so the substitute khyāñ for the root cakṣiṅ by cakṣiṅaḥ khyāñ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-54), which applies when an ārdhadhātuka suffix follows, does not come. By the nit accent cakṣas is initially udātta. After compounding, the accent of the kṛt final member comes. Here asiḥ is carried on from mithune 'siḥ pūrvavac ca sarvam (U. Sū. 4-6-[?]). Jñānendrasarasvatī and others have explained it this way; yet the Veda commentator, to suit the accent, has carried on asun here by maṇḍūkānuvṛtti. ॥7॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सखा॑य॒ आ नि षी॑दत सवि॒ता स्तोम्यो॒ नु नः॑ । दाता॒ राधां॑सि शुंभति ॥८॥

sákhāya ā́ ní ṣīdata savitā́ stomyo nú naḥ | dātā rā́dhāṃsi śuṃbhati ||8|| Strokes over खा, षी and नः; bars under य (सखाय), वि (सवि) and म्यो. Line 2: a bar under ता (दाता), a stroke over धां. The Saṃhitā prints शुंभति, the Pada शुम्भति.

सखायः । आ । नि । सीदत । सविता । स्तोम्यः । नु । नः ॥ दाता । राधांसि । शुम्भति ॥८॥

sakhāyaḥ | ā | ni | sīdata | savitā | stomyaḥ | nu | naḥ || dātā | rādhāṃsi | śumbhati ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

(Printed सर्वत्रोपविशत, as printed.)

सखिभूता हे ऋत्विज आ नि षीदत । सर्वत्रोपविशत । नोऽस्माकमयं सविता नु क्षिप्रं स्तोम्यः स्तुतियोग्यो राधांसि धनानि दाता प्रदातुमुद्युक्तः । एष सविता शुम्भति । शोभते ॥ समानाः सन्तः ख्यान्ति प्रकाशन्त इति सखायः । ख्या प्रकथने । समाने ख्यः स चोदात्तः । उ० ४-१३६ । इतीण्प्रत्ययः । तत्संनियोगेन डित्त्वं यलोपश्च । डित्त्वादाकारलोपः । समानस्य छन्दसीत्यादिना । पा० ६-३-८४ । समानशब्दस्य सादेशः । इण्संनियोगेनोदात्तत्वं । जसि सख्युरसंबुद्धौ । पा० ७-१-९२ । इति णित्त्वाद्वृद्धिरायादेशश्च । नि षीदत । सदेरप्रतेः । पा० ८-३-६६ । इति षत्वं । स्तोमेषु प्रतिपाद्यत्वेन भवः स्तोम्यः । भवे छन्दसीति यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । दाता दानशीलः । ताच्छील्ये तृन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । राधांसि । गतं । कर्तृकर्मणोः कृतीति प्राप्तायाः षष्ठ्या न लोकाव्ययेति प्रतिषेधः ॥

sakhibhūtā he ṛtvija ā ni ṣīdata | sarvatropaviśata | no 'smākamayaṃ savitā nu kṣipraṃ stomyaḥ stutiyogyo rādhāṃsi dhanāni dātā pradātumudyuktaḥ | eṣa savitā śumbhati | śobhate || samānāḥ santaḥ khyānti prakāśanta iti sakhāyaḥ | khyā prakathane | samāne khyaḥ sa codāttaḥ | u0 4-136 | itīṇpratyayaḥ | tatsaṃniyogena ḍittvaṃ yalopaśca | ḍittvādākāralopaḥ | samānasya chandasītyādinā | pā0 6-3-84 | samānaśabdasya sādeśaḥ | iṇsaṃniyogenodāttatvaṃ | jasi sakhyurasaṃbuddhau | pā0 7-1-92 | iti ṇittvādvṛddhirāyādeśaśca | ni ṣīdata | saderaprateḥ | pā0 8-3-66 | iti ṣatvaṃ | stomeṣu pratipādyatvena bhavaḥ stomyaḥ | bhave chandasīti yat | yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvaṃ | dātā dānaśīlaḥ | tācchīlye tṛn | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | rādhāṃsi | gataṃ | kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛtīti prāptāyāḥ ṣaṣṭhyā na lokāvyayeti pratiṣedhaḥ ||

Translation: "O priests, sakhāyaḥ, become friends, ā ni ṣīdata, sit down all round. Naḥ, our, Savitṛ here is nu, quickly, stomyaḥ, worthy of praise; he is the dātā, ready to give, rādhāṃsi, riches. This Savitṛ śumbhati, shines." (Grammatical tail: sakhāyaḥ, 'being equal (samāna), they shine (khyānti)'; khyā prakathane, the suffix iṇ by samāne khyaḥ sa codāttaḥ (U. 4-136), along with it the ḍit nature and dropping of y; the ā dropped because it is ḍit; sa for samāna by samānasya chandasi… (Pā. 6-3-84); the udātta along with iṇ; vṛddhi and the substitute āy because by jasi sakhyur asaṃbuddhau (Pā. 7-1-92) [the ending is] ṇit; ni ṣīdata, ṣ by sader aprateḥ (Pā. 8-3-66); stomyaḥ, 'existing in the stomas as the one set forth', yat by bhave chandasi, initial udātta by yato 'nāvaḥ; dātā, 'given to giving', tṛn in the sense of habit, initial udātta as nit; rādhāṃsi has been explained; the genitive that would come by kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti is barred by na lokāvyaya….)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सखायः (sakhāyaḥ) — O friends (O priests who are friends) | आ नि षीदत (ā ni ṣīdata) — sit down all round | सविता (savitā) — (this) Savitṛ | नः (naḥ) — by us | नु (nu) — at once | स्तोम्यः (stomyaḥ) — fit for praise | राधांसि (rādhāṃsi) — riches | दाता (dātā) — as the giver | शुम्भति (śumbhati) — shines.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O priests, this Savitṛ shines, ready to give wealth and the like to all of us. We must praise him at once. So, friends, all of you sit down all round.

॥ English Translation ॥

Friends, come and sit down; Savitri is now to be praised by us, for he is the bestower of riches and shining brightly.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

सखायः (sakhāyaḥ) — sakhibhūtā ṛtvijaḥ | Here the sacrificer has addressed the priests as his friends. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1) it is said that the priests are the sacrificer's friends:

ऋत्विजो वा अस्य सखायः ।

ṛtvijo vā asya sakhāyaḥ |

Page 86 — Rik 8: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

सखायः (sakhāyaḥ) — samānāḥ santaḥ khyānti prakāśante iti sakhāyaḥ: that is, those who shine as being of equal rank. The root khyā prakathane. By samāne khyaḥ sa codāttaḥ (U. Sū. 4-[?]) — after the root khyā with the word samāna as upapada, the suffix iṇ comes; it is ḍit; the y is dropped; the upapada is udātta — this is the sense of the sūtra following the Veda commentary. When the suffix iṇ comes here by this sūtra: khyā + i; since the suffix is ḍit, the ā, the ṭi, is dropped, and the y is dropped. By samānasya chandasy amūrdhaprabhṛtyudarkeṣu (Pā. Sū. 6-3-84) — when a last member follows other than the words mūrdhan, prabhṛti, udarka, sa is substituted for the word samāna — the substitute sa for samāna: it becomes sakhi. The author of the Svaramañjarī and others have explained it the same way. If explained so, the word sakhi would be lost to use in the world [outside the compound]. So it is proper to take the reading found now in the Uṇādi, samāne khyaḥ sa codāttaḥ, and explain that the substitute sa comes by this very sūtra. See the explanation of this at (Ṛ. Sū. 1-4-4, as printed). After the word sakhi, jas; by sakhyur asaṃbuddhau (Pā. Sū. 7-1-92) — a sarvanāmasthāna other than the vocative after a stem in the form of the word sakhi is treated as ṇit — jas is like ṇit; so by aco 'ñṇiti (Pā. Sū. 7-2-115) vṛddhi; by eco 'yavāyāvaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-78) the substitute āy; s, ru and visarga: it becomes sakhāyaḥ.

निषीदत (niṣīdata) — the root ṣadḷ viśaraṇādau; by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) s for the ṣ; loṭ, middle person tha; by loṭo laṅvat (Pā. Sū. 3-4-85) treated like laṅ; by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101) the substitute ta; śap; by pāghrādhmā… (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78) the substitute sīda: it became sīdata. When it follows the prefix ni, by sader aprateḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-3-66) — after the iṇ that is the final of a prefix other than prati, ṣ comes for the s of the root sad — ṣ: it becomes niṣīdata.

स्तोम्यः (stomyaḥ) — stomeṣu pratipādyatvena bhavaḥ: when the sense 'existing in' is intended, by bhave chandasi (Pā. Sū. 4-4-110) — after a related word ending in the seventh case, the suffix yat in the sense 'existing in' — the suffix yat; by yato 'nāvaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-213) — a word ending in a yat laid down after a word other than nau, if it has two vowels, is udātta at the beginning — initial udātta comes.

Page 87 (upper) — Rik 8: grammar (end)

दाता (dātā) — the meaning is 'given to giving'. By tṛn (Pā. Sū. 3-2-135), in the sense of habit, the suffix tṛn comes after the root dhāñ [as printed]; by the nit accent initial udātta.

राधांसि (rādhāṃsi) — explained in the seventh mantra. Rādhas is the word denoting the object in the action of the root dā, which is the base of the kṛt suffix tṛn. So by kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti (Pā. Sū. 2-3-65) — after a word denoting either agent or object of the action that is the base of a kṛt suffix, the genitive comes — the genitive of the object would be obtained. But since tṛn is used, the prohibition by na lokāvyayaniṣṭhākhalarthatṛnām (Pā. Sū. 2-3-69) comes, so the genitive of the object does not come. By karmaṇi dvitīyā (Pā. Sū. 2-3-2) — after a nominal stem denoting an object not expressed by the tiṅ and the like, the second case comes — the second case comes. ॥8॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अग्ने पत्नी॑रि॒हा व॑ह दे॒वाना॑मुश॒तीरुप॑ । त्वष्टा॑रं॒ सोम॑पीतये ॥९॥

agne pátnīr ihā́ vaha devā́nām uśatī́r úpa | tváṣṭāraṃ sómapītaye ||9|| Strokes over त्नी, व (वह), वा (देवानाम्) and प (उप); bars under रि, दे and श. Line 2: a stroke over ष्टा, a bar under रं, a stroke over म (सोम).

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अग्ने । पत्नीः । इह । आ । वह । देवानां । उशतीः । उप ॥ त्वष्टारं । सोमऽपीतये ॥९॥

agne | patnīḥ | iha | ā | vaha | devānāṃ | uśatīḥ | upa || tvaṣṭāraṃ | soma 'pītaye ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ It opens with the application; the Āśvalāyana number is printed ५-५.

अग्निष्टोमे प्रातःसवनेऽग्ने पत्नीरिहा वहेति नेष्टुः प्रस्थितयाज्या । प्रशास्ता ब्राह्मणाच्छंसीति खण्डे सूत्रितं । अग्ने पत्नीरिहा वहोक्षान्नाय वशान्नाय । आ० ५-५ । इति ॥

agniṣṭome prātaḥsavane 'gne patnīrihā vaheti neṣṭuḥ prasthitayājyā | praśāstā brāhmaṇācchaṃsīti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | agne patnīrihā vahokṣānnāya vaśānnāya | ā0 5-5 | iti ||

Translation (application): "In the agniṣṭoma, at the morning pressing, agne patnīr ihā vaha is the prasthita-yājyā of the neṣṭṛ; it is laid down in the section praśāstā brāhmaṇācchaṃsī: 'agne patnīr ihā vaha, ukṣānnāya vaśānnāya' (Āśv. 5-5)."

हे अग्ने उशतीः कामयमाना देवानां पत्नीरिन्द्राण्याद्या इह देवयजनदेश आ वह । तथा त्वष्टारं देवं सोमपीतये सोमपानार्थमुप समीप आ वह ॥ पत्नीः । डत्यन्तः पतिशब्द आद्युदात्तः । पत्युर्नो यज्ञसंयोगे । पा० ४-१-३३ । इति ङीप् । तत्संनियोगेन नकारश्च । ङीपः पित्त्वाड्डतिस्वर एव । उशतीः । वश कान्तौ । लटः शतृ । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । शतुर्ङित्त्वाद्ग्रहिज्यादिना संप्रसारणं । उगितश्चेति ङीप् । शतुरनुम इति ङीबुदात्तः ॥

he agne uśatīḥ kāmayamānā devānāṃ patnīrindrāṇyādyā iha devayajanadeśa ā vaha | tathā tvaṣṭāraṃ devaṃ somapītaye somapānārthamupa samīpa ā vaha || patnīḥ | ḍatyantaḥ patiśabda ādyudāttaḥ | patyurno yajñasaṃyoge | pā0 4-1-33 | iti ṅīp | tatsaṃniyogena nakāraśca | ṅīpaḥ pittvāḍḍatisvara eva | uśatīḥ | vaśa kāntau | laṭaḥ śatṛ | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | śaturṅittvādgrahijyādinā saṃprasāraṇaṃ | ugitaśceti ṅīp | śaturanuma iti ṅībudāttaḥ ||

Translation: "O Agni! Bring (ā vaha) iha, here to the place of the sacrifice, the uśatīḥ, desiring, patnīḥ, wives, devānām, of the gods — Indrāṇī and the rest. Likewise bring near (upa) the god Tvaṣṭṛ somapītaye, to drink soma." (Grammatical tail: patnīḥ, the word pati, ending in ḍati, is initially udātta; ṅīp by patyur no yajñasaṃyoge (Pā. 4-1-33), and with it the n; since ṅīp is pit, the accent of ḍati alone; uśatīḥ, vaśa kāntau, śatṛ for laṭ, śap dropped by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ, saṃprasāraṇa by grahijyā… since śatṛ is ṅit, ṅīp by ugitaś ca, the ṅīp udātta by śatur anumaḥ….)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | उशतीः (uśatīḥ) — full of love | देवानां (devānāṃ) — of the gods | पत्नीः (patnīḥ) — the women (wives) | इह (iha) — to this place | आ वह (ā vaha) — bring | त्वष्टारं (tvaṣṭāraṃ) — Tvaṣṭṛ too | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — to drink soma | उप (upa) — near (bring).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, bring here, to drink soma, the wives who are dear to the gods, and Tvaṣṭṛ.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, bring hither, the anxious wives of the gods and the god Twashtri to drink our Soma

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In the agniṣṭoma sacrifice, in the morning rite of pressing soma called the morning pressing, the priest called neṣṭṛ uses the ṛk agne patnīḥ as the yājyā mantra. On this the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra (Ā. 5-5), in the section praśāstā brāhmaṇācchaṃsī, has the sūtra agne patnīr ihā vaha (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-9) ukṣānnāya vaśānnāya (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-43-11).

In this ṛk and in the next three ṛks the wives of the gods are set forth. In this ṛk the name of no particular god's wife is indicated; it only speaks of the wives of the gods in general.

उशतीः (uśatīḥ) — vaśa kāntau | kāmayamānāḥ || dear to the gods, radiant; "loving, anxious &c."

त्वष्टारं (tvaṣṭāraṃ) — Tvaṣṭṛ. Why the ṛṣi has called Tvaṣṭṛ along with the wives of the gods is not clear.

Page 89 (upper) — Rik 9: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

पत्नीः (patnīḥ) — the root pā rakṣaṇe. By pāter ḍatiḥ (U. Sū., number not clear [?]) the suffix ḍati comes after the root pā rakṣaṇe; by the force of its being made ḍit, even without the name bha, the ṭi is dropped by ṭeḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-4-143). The word pati is initially udātta by the suffix accent. By pratyur no yajñasaṃyoge [as printed, for patyur] (Pā. Sū. 4-1-33) — when connection with the sacrifice, in the form of enjoying its fruit, is meant, ṅīp comes after the word pati in the feminine, and n is substituted for the t[i] of pati — with ṅīp and the n it becomes patnī. If the sūtra is explained as laying down only the substitute n, then ṅīp comes by ṛnnebhyo ṅīp (Pā. Sū. 4-1-5), as for stems ending in n. Ṅīp is pit; so by anudāttau suppitau (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4) it is unaccented, and thus the accent of the suffix ḍati alone stays.

उशतीः (uśatīḥ) — the root vaśa kāntau, laṭ; by laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe (Pā. Sū. 3-2-124) the substitute śatṛ, the vikaraṇa śap; by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72) it is dropped (luk); by sārvadhātukam apit, śatṛ is ṅit; so by grahijyāvayivyadhivaṣṭi… (Pā. Sū. 6-1-16) saṃprasāraṇa, u for the v, the preceding form: uśat. By ugitaś ca (Pā. Sū. 4-1-6) — after a nominal stem ending in an ugit, in the feminine, ṅīp — ṅīp. By śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173) — after a word that ends in a śatṛ without the augment num and is final-udātta, the nadī and the vowel-initial endings śas and the rest are also udātta — ṅīp is udātta. ॥9॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ ग्ना अ॑ग्न इ॒हाव॑से॒ होत्रां॑ यवि॒ष्ठ भार॑तीं । वरू॑त्रीं धि॒षणां॑ वह ॥१०॥

ā gnā́ agna ihā́vase hótrāṃ yaviṣṭhá bhā́ratīṃ | várūtrīṃ dhiṣáṇāṃ vaha ||10|| Strokes over अ (अग्न), व (अवसे), त्रां and र (भारतीं); bars under इ, से and ष्ठ. Line 2: a stroke over रू, a bar under धि, a stroke over णां.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ । ग्नाः । अग्ने । इह । अवसे । होत्रां । यविष्ठ । भारतीं ॥ वरूत्रीं । धिषणां । वह ॥१०॥

ā | gnāḥ | agne | iha | avase | hotrāṃ | yaviṣṭha | bhāratīṃ || varūtrīṃ | dhiṣaṇāṃ | vaha ||10||

Page 90 — Rik 10: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The Uṇādi number of होत्रां is read ४-१६७ [?]; the others are printed नि० ८-१३, पा० ६-४-१५६, पा० ७-२-३४, उ० २-८२. The bhāṣya ends with ॥५॥, the close of the fifth varga.

हे अग्ने अवसेऽस्मानवितुं ग्ना देवपत्नीरिहा वह । तथा हे यविष्ठ युवतमाग्ने होत्रां होमनिष्पादकाग्निपत्नीं भारतीं भरतनामकस्यादित्यस्य पत्नीं वरूत्रीं वरणीयां धिषणां वाग्देवीं चा वह । वाग्वै धिषणेति वाजसनेयकं । भरत आदित्यः । नि० ८-१३ । इति यास्केनोक्तत्वात्तस्य पत्नी भारतीत्युच्यते ॥ गम्यन्त इति ग्नाः । गम्लृ सृप्लृ गतौ । औणादिको ड्नप्रत्ययः । डित्त्वाट्टिलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । होत्रां । हुयामाश्रुभसिभ्यस्त्रन् । उ० ४-१६७ । इति त्रन्नन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अतिशयेन युवा यविष्ठः । अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ । स्थूलदूरेत्यादिना । पा० ६-४-१५६ । यणादिपरस्य लोपः पूर्वस्य च गुणः । भारतीं । शार्ङ्गरवादेरवृत्कृतत्वात् ङीनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । वरूत्रीं । ग्रसितस्कभितेत्यादौ । पा० ७-२-३४ । यद्यपि वरूतृशब्दस्तृजन्त इत्युक्तं तथाप्यन्त इतिकरणस्य प्रदर्शनार्थत्वाद्वरूतृशब्दस्तृन्नन्तोऽपि द्रष्टव्यः । तेन नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । शेषनिघातेन ऋकारस्यानुदात्तत्वादुदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादित्यपि न ङीप उदात्तत्वं । धिषणां । क्युप्रत्ययानुवृत्तौ धृषेर्धिष च संज्ञायां । उ० २-८२ । इति क्युः ॥५॥

he agne avase 'smānavituṃ gnā devapatnīrihā vaha | tathā he yaviṣṭha yuvatamāgne hotrāṃ homaniṣpādakāgnipatnīṃ bhāratīṃ bharatanāmakasyādityasya patnīṃ varūtrīṃ varaṇīyāṃ dhiṣaṇāṃ vāgdevīṃ cā vaha | vāgvai dhiṣaṇeti vājasaneyakaṃ | bharata ādityaḥ | ni0 8-13 | iti yāskenoktatvāttasya patnī bhāratītyucyate || gamyanta iti gnāḥ | gamlṛ sṛplṛ gatau | auṇādiko ḍnapratyayaḥ | ḍittvāṭṭilopaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | hotrāṃ | huyāmāśrubhasibhyastran | u0 4-167 | iti trannanto nittvādādyudāttaḥ | atiśayena yuvā yaviṣṭhaḥ | atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau | sthūladūretyādinā | pā0 6-4-156 | yaṇādiparasya lopaḥ pūrvasya ca guṇaḥ | bhāratīṃ | śārṅgaravāderavṛtkṛtatvāt ṅīnanto nittvādādyudāttaḥ | varūtrīṃ | grasitaskabhitetyādau | pā0 7-2-34 | yadyapi varūtṛśabdastṛjanta ityuktaṃ tathāpyanta itikaraṇasya pradarśanārthatvādvarūtṛśabdastṛnnanto 'pi draṣṭavyaḥ | tena nittvādādyudāttatvaṃ | śeṣanighātena ṛkārasyānudāttatvādudāttayaṇo halpūrvādityapi na ṅīpa udāttatvaṃ | dhiṣaṇāṃ | kyupratyayānuvṛttau dhṛṣerdhiṣa ca saṃjñāyāṃ | u0 2-82 | iti kyuḥ ||5||

Translation: "O Agni! Avase, to protect us, bring (ā vaha) iha, here, the gnāḥ, the wives of the gods. Likewise, O yaviṣṭha, youngest Agni, bring hotrām, the wife of Agni who brings about the offering; bhāratīm, the wife of the sun named Bharata; varūtrīm, the choice-worthy; and dhiṣaṇām, the goddess of speech — 'dhiṣaṇā is speech', says the Vājasaneyaka. Because Yāska says 'Bharata is the sun' (Ni. 8-13), his wife is called Bhāratī." (Grammatical tail: gnāḥ, 'they are gone to', gamḷ sṛpḷ gatau, the Uṇādi suffix ḍna, the ṭi dropped as it is ḍit, the suffix accent; hotrām, ending in tran by huyāmāśrubhasibhyas tran (U. 4-167 [?]), initial udātta as nit; yaviṣṭha, 'most young', iṣṭhan by atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau; by sthūladūra… (Pā. 6-4-156) the part from the yaṇ on is dropped and the preceding vowel takes guṇa; bhāratīm, because the śārṅgaravādi list is not closed with vṛt, it ends in ṅīn and is initially udātta as nit; varūtrīm, at grasitaskabhita… (Pā. 7-2-34): although varūtṛ is said to end in tṛc, the iti at the end serves to show examples, so varūtṛ is also to be taken as ending in tṛn; hence initial udātta as nit; with the ṛ unaccented by śeṣanighāta, the ṅīp is not udātta even by udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt; dhiṣaṇām, with kyu carried on, kyu by dhṛṣer dhiṣa ca saṃjñāyām (U. 2-82).)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | अवसे (avase) — to protect us | ग्नाः (gnāḥ) — the wives of the gods | इह (iha) — to this place | आ वह (ā vaha) — bring | यविष्ठ (yaviṣṭha) — O Agni, best among the young | होत्रां (hotrāṃ) — the wife of Agni, who carries the oblations to the gods | भारतीं (bhāratīṃ) — Bhāratī (the wife of the sun named Bharata) | वरूत्रीं (varūtrīṃ) — worthy of honour, or to be desired | धिषणां (dhiṣaṇāṃ) — the goddess of speech too | आ वह (ā vaha) — bring.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O young Agni, bring for our protection the wives of the gods — Hotrā, Bhāratī, and the goddess of speech, worthy of honour and to be desired, and the others.

॥ English Translation ॥

O youthful Agni, bring hither for our protection the goddesses, Hotra, Bharathi, Varutri, and Dhishana.

Page 91 — Rik 10: Special Topics, grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In this ṛk the women Hotrā, Bhāratī, Varūtrī and Dhiṣaṇā, wives of the gods, are invoked. Though they are all different deities, since the words Hotrā (Ni. 2-23 [?]), Bhāratī (Ni. 2-23 [?]) and Dhiṣaṇā (2-23 [?]) are all read among the names of speech, and since the word varūtrī, in the sense 'choice-worthy', is also a qualifier of the word dhiṣaṇā, there is room for doubt whether they are all different deities or different names of the goddess of speech. Following the commentator's explanation, Hotrā should be taken as the wife of Agni who brings about the offering (since the word hotrā is read among the names of sacrifice in Ni. 3-19 [?], she can be called the wife of Agni, lord of the sacrifice); Bhāratī as the wife of the sun named Bharata (Ni. 8-13); and Dhiṣaṇā as the goddess of speech.

ग्नाः (gnāḥ) — gnā iti strīnāma | devapatnyaḥ | The word gnāḥ is read among the names of speech too (Ni. 2-23 [?]). But there is also the Nirukta statement menā gnā iti strīṇām (Ni. 3-21): "menāḥ, gnāḥ — these are names of women". The commentator on the Nirukta has said that women are called gnāḥ because men go near women for intercourse: gnāḥ — gacchanti hy enāḥ maithunena dharmeṇa. In this ṛk gnāḥ, women, means, as said in the previous ṛk, the wives of the gods. The word gnāḥ is read in the Ṛgveda in the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-10; 1-61-8; 4-9-4; 5-43-13; 5-46-2; 5-46-8; 6-50-15; 6-68-4; 10-95-[?].

मेना ग्ना इति स्त्रीणाम् । ग्नाः गच्छन्ति ह्येनाः मैथुनेन धर्मेण ।

menā gnā iti strīṇām | gnāḥ gacchanti hyenāḥ maithunena dharmeṇa |

यविष्ठ (yaviṣṭha) — atiśayena yuvā yaviṣṭhaḥ | young, youthful, a man in his prime.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

ग्नाः (gnāḥ) — gamyante iti gnāḥ. The root gamḷ sṛpḷ gatau; after it the Uṇādi suffix ḍna; by the force of its being made ḍit, even without the name bha, by ṭeḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-4-143) the am, the ṭi of the root, is dropped: g + na = gna. In the accusative plural it becomes gnāḥ. Gna is final udātta by the suffix accent.

होत्रां (hotrāṃ) — by huyāmāśrubhasibhyas tran (U. Sū. 4-607 [?], as read) — after the roots hu dānādanayoḥ, yā prāpaṇe, mā māne, śru śravaṇe, bhasa bhartsanadīptyoḥ, the suffix tran —

Page 92 — Rik 10: grammar (continued)

— the suffix tran; the suffix being nit, initial udātta comes. Hu + tra: by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) guṇa: hotra; in the feminine it becomes hotrā, ending in the accusative singular.

यविष्ठ (yaviṣṭha) — the analysis is atiśayena yuvā. By atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau (Pā. Sū. 5-3-55): when the kṛt suffix lyuṭ comes in the agent sense after the root śīṅ svapne preceded by ati, it becomes atiśayana. Atiśayanam eva atiśāyanam: since it is given as a set form in the sūtra atiśāyane, the ś syllable is lengthened and it becomes atiśāyane. So in common usage too the form atiśāyana is correct. By abādhakāny api nipātanāni bhavanti, atiśayana with a short śa is also correct. Though the root śīṅ alone means sleeping, the root śīṅ with the prefix ati expresses, by the force of the prefix, the sense of excellence; excellence does not mean 'more': it means overpowering in the form of making less. The sense of the sūtra: after a stem expressing a meaning marked by such excellence, the suffixes tamap and iṣṭhan come in their own sense. If the sūtra is explained, taking atiśāyana as ending in lyuṭ in the action sense, as atiśāyane 'rthe tamabiṣṭhanau bhavataḥ, then the meaning of the suffix would become primary, and laghor atiśayanam, laghutamam alone would have to result; the masculine and feminine forms laghutamaḥ, laghutamā and the rest would not be obtained. If the sense is given as atiśāyane vartamānāt prātipadikāt svārthe tamabiṣṭhanau bhavataḥ, the suffixes tamap and iṣṭhan would come only after words like atiśaya, prakarṣa; after words like āḍhya, which do not mean excess, these suffixes could not come. So atiśāyane must be taken as a qualifier of the meaning of the stem; then, since the sense stated before results, no fault arises. Here, when iṣṭhan comes after the word yuvan: yuvan + iṣṭhan. In sthūladūrayuvahrasvakṣiprakṣudrāṇāṃ yaṇādiparaṃ pūrvasya ca guṇaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-4-156), iṣṭhemeyassu is carried on from turiṣṭhemeyassu (Pā. Sū. 6-4-154), meaning 'when iṣṭhan, imanic, īyasun follow'; lopaḥ is carried on from allopo 'naḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-4-134). Lupyate iti lopaḥ: the word lopa ending in ghañ in the action sense; yaṇ ādir yasya tat yaṇādi ends in a dropped genitive; param, the first case in the sense of the sixth; by iko guṇavṛddhī (Pā. Sū. 1-1-3) — wherever guṇa and vṛddhi are laid down by naming them, the word ikaḥ in the sixth case is supplied — ikaḥ is obtained. Pūrvasya: 'preceding' than what? Since yaṇādi param comes before it, 'preceding' with respect to the following yaṇādi is intended. On the view that the word yuvan is not a quality-word, by the rule ajādī guṇavacanād eva

Page 93 — Rik 10: grammar (continued)

iṣṭhan and īyasun could not come; yet, by the indication given in this very sūtra, which lays down dropping and guṇa before iṣṭhan and the rest, iṣṭhan and īyasun do come after the word yuvan. In fact, on looking at the Mahābhāṣya on the sūtras ākaḍārād ekā saṃjñā (Pā. Sū. 1-4-1) and jāter astrīviṣayād ayopadhāt (Pā. Sū. 4-1-63), it appears that the word yuvan is also a quality-word. Thus the sense of the sūtra is: the yaṇādi following the six words sthūla, dūra, yuvan, hrasva, kṣipra, kṣudra is dropped and the preceding ik takes guṇa. Taking lopa as ending in ghañ in the object sense, one need not explain yaṇādi as ending in a dropped genitive: it is in the first case itself. On this view the sense is: the yaṇādi following these six words is dropped, and the preceding ik takes guṇa. In the words yuvan and hrasva, the letters y and v in the first and r and v in the second both belong to the pratyāhāra yaṇ; if the word param were not in the sūtra, the first yaṇ in these two words would also have to be dropped. In yuvan + iṣṭhan, by this sūtra the van is dropped, and with guṇa of the u: yo + iṣṭha, the substitute av: it becomes yaviṣṭha. By āmantritasya ca (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) it is wholly unaccented.

भारतीम् (bhāratīm) — by bhṛmṛdṛśiyajiparvipacyamitaminamiharyibhyo 'tac (U. Sū. 3-110 [?]) — after these ten roots, bhṛñ bharaṇe, mṛṅ prāṇatyāge, dṛśir prekṣaṇe, yaja devapūjādau, parva pūraṇe, ḍupacaṣ pāke, ama gatau, tamu kāṅkṣāyām, ṇama prahvatve śabde ca, harya gatikāntyoḥ, the suffix atac comes — when the suffix atac comes after the root bhṛ, with guṇa it becomes bharata. By prajñādibhyaś ca (Pā. Sū. 5-4-38) — after the words read in the prajñādi class, the suffix aṇ in their own sense — the suffix aṇ; by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-2-117) the initial vṛddhi: it became bhārata; this is a name of the sun (Āditya). When bhāratasya strī is intended, since this ends in the suffix aṇ, ṅīp would be obtained by ṭiḍḍhāṇañ… (Pā. Sū. 4-1-15); yet, since in the śārṅgaravādi class there is no vṛt to show the end of the list, the śārṅgaravādi class is established as an ākṛtigaṇa; so by śārṅgaravādyaño ṅīn (Pā. Sū. 4-1-73) — śārṅgaravādi is a word ending in a dropped fifth case; ataḥ from ajādyataḥ (Pā. Sū. 4-1-4) and jāteḥ from jāter astrīviṣayāt (Pā. Sū. 4-1-63) are carried on; since ataḥ qualifies jāteḥ, by yena vidhis tadantasya (Pā. Sū. 1-1-72) 'ending in it' is obtained. So, in the feminine, after the words read in the śārṅgaravādi class and after a genus-word ending in the a of the suffix añ, ṅīn comes — the suffix ṅīn

Page 94 — Rik 10: grammar (continued)

comes; by yasyeti ca (Pā. Sū. 6-4-148) the a before the suffix is dropped; ṅīn is nit, so by ñnity ādir nityam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) initial udātta comes. If this word were not included in the śārṅgaravādi class, ṅīp, marked by ending in aṇ, would come by ṭiḍḍhāṇañ…; and since that is pit, by the accent of an unaccented suffix the a of aṇ would be udātta and bhāratī would have to be accented in the middle.

वरूत्रीम् (varūtrīm) — by grasita-skabhita-stabhita-uttabhita-catta-vikasta-viśasta-śaṃstṛ-śāstṛ-tarutṛ-tarūtṛ-varutṛ-varūtṛ-varūtrī-ujjvaliti-kṣariti-kṣamiti-vamity-amitīti ca (Pā. Sū. 7-2-34) these eighteen words are given as set forms. The sense: here grasu adane; skambhu, stambhu — these two are sautra roots meaning 'to obstruct'; when the suffix kta comes after them, since these roots have the marker u, there is the option of iṭ by udito vā (Pā. Sū. 7-2-56), so the prohibition of iṭ would be obtained by yasya vibhāṣā; yet the augment iṭ is given as a set form. By the mention of stabhita alone the form in uttabhita would also be obtained; still, since uttabhita is mentioned again, it is established that the augment iṭ is not given as a set form for the kta after stambh when it follows a prefix other than ut. In ut + stabhita, by udaḥ sthāstambhoḥ pūrvasya (Pā. Sū. 8-4-61) the preceding homorganic. For the kta after cate yācane and kasa gatau, the absence of iṭ is given as a set form; for the tṛc after śasu hiṃsāyām, śaṃsu stutau, śāsu anuśiṣṭau, the absence of iṭ is given as a set form. For the tṛc after tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, vṛṅ sambhaktau, vṛñ varaṇe, the augments uṭ and ūṭ are given as set forms. Since by the set form varūtṛ alone varūtrī would be obtained in the feminine with ṅīp marked by ending in ṛ by ṛnnebhyo ṅīp (Pā. Sū. 4-1-5), the further mention of varūtrī is for elaboration (explanation). For the śap after the four roots jvala dīptau, kṣara saṃcalane, ṭuvamu udgiraṇe, ama gatyādiṣu, the substitute i is given as a set form. In the sūtra, after kṣariti, some read kṣamiti; on this view it is to be known that the substitute i for the śap after the root kṣamūṣ sahane is a set form. As said before, by this sūtra varūtrī results when tṛc comes after the root vṛñ, with the augment ūṭ, guṇa, ṅīp and the yaṇ substitute. If this word varūtṛ is taken, the ṛ of tṛc would have to be udātta by the cit accent. It must be said that here there is no set form for one ending in tṛn. Yet, since there is the word iti at the end of this sūtra, and since it is used with the aim of showing the kinds of examples in the Veda, the word varūtṛ ending in tṛn also is

Page 95 (upper) — Rik 10: grammar (end)

to be taken as given as a set form by this sūtra. Thus by the nit accent varūtṛ is initially udātta; by anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-158) it follows that the ū and the ṛ are unaccented. Though, with the ī of ṅīp as cause, r comes in place of this ṛ by the yaṇ substitute, it is not a yaṇ standing in place of an udātta but one standing in place of an unaccented vowel. So even by udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt (Pā. Sū. 6-1-174) the udātta accent does not come to ṅīp.

धिषणाम् (dhiṣaṇām) — by dhṛṣer dhiṣa ca saṃjñāyām (U. Sū. 2-2-81 [?], as read), kyuḥ being carried on from kṛpṛvṛjimandinidhāñaḥ kyuḥ (U. Sū. 2-240 [?], as read): when a name is meant, the suffix kyu comes after the root and the substitute dhiṣ for the root; so with the suffix kyu after the root dhṛṣ and the substitute dhiṣ: dhiṣ + yu; since the suffix is kit, guṇa of the light penultimate does not come. By yuvor anākau (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1) the substitute ana for yu; in the feminine, ṭāp, ṇ for the n: it becomes dhiṣaṇā. ॥10॥

On this page the print has the labels exchanged: the Saṃhitā stands under the heading ॥ पदपाठः ॥ and the Pada under ॥ संहितापाठः ॥, as printed.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒भि नो॑ दे॒वीरव॑सा म॒हः शर्म॑णा नृ॒पत्नीः॑ । अच्छि॑न्नपत्राः सचन्तां ॥११॥

abhí no devī́r ávasā maháḥ śármaṇā nṛpátnīḥ | ácchinnapatrāḥ sacantāṃ ||11|| Strokes over नो, व (अवसा), र्म and त्नीः; bars under अ, दे, म (महः) and नृ. Line 2: a stroke over च्छि. The print has सचंतां.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अभि । नः । देवीः । अवसा । महः । शर्मणा । नृऽपत्नीः ॥ अच्छिन्नऽपत्राः । सचन्तां ॥११॥

abhi | naḥ | devīḥ | avasā | mahaḥ | śarmaṇā | nṛ 'patnīḥ || acchinna 'patrāḥ | sacantāṃ ||11||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The bhāṣya runs on to p. 96 (header Varga 6). The reference for supāṃ supo bhavanti is printed म० ७-१-३९, as printed.

देवीर्देव्यो देवपत्न्योऽवसा रक्षणेन महो महता शर्मणा च सुखेन च सह नोऽस्मानभि सचन्तां । आभिमुख्येन सेवन्तां । कीदृश्यो देव्यः । नृपत्नीर्मनुष्याणां पालयित्र्यः अच्छिन्नपत्रा अच्छिन्नपक्षाः । न हि पक्षिरूपाणां देवपत्नीनां पक्षाः केनचिच्छिद्यन्ते ॥ देवीः । पुंयोगादाख्यायां । पा० ४-१-४८ । इति ङीषन्तः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । दीर्घाज्जसि चेति प्रतिषेधस्य वा छन्दसीति पाक्षिकस्योक्तेः पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वं । अवसा । अव रक्षणे । असुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । महः । मह पूजायां । क्विप् । सुपां सुपो भवन्ति । म० ७-१-३९ । इति तृतीयैकवचनस्य ङसादेशः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । नृपत्नीः । समासान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । अच्छिन्नपत्राः । न छिन्नान्यच्छिन्नानि । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अच्छिन्नानि पत्राणि यासां ताः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

devīrdevyo devapatnyo 'vasā rakṣaṇena maho mahatā śarmaṇā ca sukhena ca saha no 'smānabhi sacantāṃ | ābhimukhyena sevantāṃ | kīdṛśyo devyaḥ | nṛpatnīrmanuṣyāṇāṃ pālayitryaḥ acchinnapatrā acchinnapakṣāḥ | na hi pakṣirūpāṇāṃ devapatnīnāṃ pakṣāḥ kenacicchidyante || devīḥ | puṃyogādākhyāyāṃ | pā0 4-1-48 | iti ṅīṣantaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | dīrghājjasi ceti pratiṣedhasya vā chandasīti pākṣikasyokteḥ pūrvasavarṇadīrghatvaṃ | avasā | ava rakṣaṇe | asun | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | mahaḥ | maha pūjāyāṃ | kvip | supāṃ supo bhavanti | ma0 7-1-39 | iti tṛtīyaikavacanasya ṅasādeśaḥ | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvaṃ | nṛpatnīḥ | samāsāntodāttatve prāpte parādiśchandasi bahulamityuttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | acchinnapatrāḥ | na chinnānyacchinnāni | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | acchinnāni patrāṇi yāsāṃ tāḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||

Translation: "May the devīḥ, goddesses, the wives of the gods, abhi sacantām, attend, face to face, naḥ, us, avasā, with protection, and with mahaḥ, great, śarmaṇā, happiness. Of what kind are the goddesses? Nṛpatnīḥ, protectors of men; acchinnapatrāḥ, of uncut wings: for the wings of the wives of the gods, who have the form of birds, are not cut by anyone." (Grammatical tail: devīḥ, ending in ṅīṣ by puṃyogād ākhyāyām (Pā. 4-1-48), final udātta by the suffix accent; the lengthening of the like preceding vowel, since the bar dīrghāj jasi ca is said to be optional by vā chandasi; avasā, ava rakṣaṇe, asun, initial udātta as nit; mahaḥ, maha pūjāyām, kvip, the substitute ṅas for the instrumental singular by supāṃ supo bhavanti (as printed, Ma. 7-1-39), the case-ending udātta by sāv ekācaḥ…; nṛpatnīḥ, the compound-final udātta being due, the last member's initial udātta by parādiś chandasi bahulam; acchinnapatrāḥ, na chinnāny acchinnāni, the indeclinable first member's accent; 'whose wings are uncut', in the bahuvrīhi the first member's accent.)

Page 96 — Rik 11: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

नृपत्नीः (nṛpatnīḥ) — who protect men | अच्छिन्नपत्राः (acchinnapatrāḥ) — having wings (pinions) not cut off | देवीः (devīḥ) — the wives of the gods | अवसा (avasā) — with protection | महः (mahaḥ) — abundant | शर्मणा (śarmaṇā) — and with happiness | नः (naḥ) — us | अभि सचन्तां (abhi sacantāṃ) — attend especially (favour).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The goddesses are able to protect men; they have uncut wings. May such ones protect us and favour us by giving abundant happiness.

॥ English Translation ॥

May the goddesses, the protectresses of men whose wrings [sic] are uncut come hither with their protection and support.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

अभि (abhi) — ābhimukhyena | especially, chiefly, without fail and so on.

महः (mahaḥ) — mahatā | tṛtīyārthe ṣaṣṭhī || Though this word qualifies the instrumental śarmaṇā, the genitive case is used here. It means abundant, much.

नृपत्नीः (nṛpatnīḥ) — manuṣyāṇāṃ pālayitryaḥ | those able to protect men (the wives of the gods): the intention is the goddesses spoken of in the previous ṛk — Hotrā, wife of Agni; Bhāratī, wife of Bharata (the sun); and Dhiṣaṇā, the goddess of speech — that is, the wives of the gods.

Page 97 — Rik 11: Special Topics (end), grammar

अच्छिन्नपत्राः (acchinnapatrāḥ) — na hi pakṣirūpāṇāṃ devapatnīnāṃ pakṣāḥ kenacic chidyante | Since no one cuts the wings of the wives of the gods who bear the form of birds, the commentator has explained this word as their being named acchinnapatrāḥ. This word is used nowhere else in the Ṛgveda except in this ṛk. What the ṛṣi intends in using this word is not clearly known.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

देवीः (devīḥ) — after the root divu krīḍādau, by nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134), the suffix ac of the pacādi type; with guṇa of the light penultimate it became deva. Now the analysis is devasya striyaḥ devyaḥ. Puṃyogād ākhyāyām (Pā. Sū. 4-1-48): the word division is puṃyogāt, ākhyāyām. From ajādyataṣ ṭāp (Pā. Sū. 4-1-4) ataḥ is carried on. Puṃsā yogaḥ puṃyogaḥ, tasmāt: puṃyogāt, a fifth case of cause. The heading striyām (Pā. Sū. 4-1-3) comes in; puṃyogāt is construed with striyām. So the sense is puṃyogād dhetoḥ striyāṃ vartamānāt. In ākhyāyām, by supāṃ supo bhavanti (Pā. Ma. 7-1-39) the seventh case substitutes for the fifth. The word ākhyā means 'expressing'. 'Expressing what?' — since puṃyogāt is present, it comes to mean puṃso vācakāt. The three words puṃs, yogāt, striyām are present. Puṃsā is present, though subordinate, as a qualifier of the last member yoga, a part of the compound. If it is asked why it should not mean 'expressing what? — expressing the connection with a man', or striyām ākhyāyām, 'expressing the woman': on the first view, words like gaṇaka, though in the feminine through connection with a man, do not express the connection with a man; so ṅīṣ would fail to come there. On the second view, if the sense is 'first expressing the woman rather than the connection with a man', then, since expressing a woman is not possible without connection with a man, it would be impossible. If the sense is 'expressing the woman after the connection with a man', words in the feminine through connection with a man would by rule express women; so there would be no exclusion of others. Thus, by the rule saṃbhavavyabhicārābhyāṃ syād viśeṣaṇam arthavat — saṃbhava, fitness; vyabhicāra, exclusion of others — since in the first view it is not possible and in the second view there is no exclusion of others, striyām ākhyāyām cannot be said. So puṃsā, though subordinate, is construed with ākhyāyām: puṃsaḥ ākhyāyām, giving the sense 'expressing a man'. By this qualifier ṅīṣ does not come in words like prasūtā, prajātā. Words like prasūtā, caused by connection with a man, have as their ground of use a state after conception —

संभवव्यभिचाराभ्यां स्याद्विशेषणमर्थवत् ।

saṃbhavavyabhicārābhyāṃ syādviśeṣaṇamarthavat |

Page 98 — Rik 11: grammar (continued)

— and so, though in the feminine through connection with a man, they do not express the meaning 'man'. So the qualifier puṃs has a purpose in this sūtra: to prevent ṅīṣ. From anyato ṅīṣ (Pā. Sū. 4-1-40) ṅīṣ is carried on. Prātipadikāt is the heading; ataḥ qualifies prātipadikāt, so 'ending in it' is obtained. So the sense of the sūtra: after a nominal stem ending in short a, which, by reason of (as a mark of) connection with a man, expresses a woman and is well known as expressing a man, ṅīṣ comes. Here puṃyoga means connection with a man. Since there is no authority to take a particular one, some hold that both the connection with a man in the form of producer and produced, and the connection in the form of marriage, are intended. On their view, when kekayasya duhitā is meant, ṅīṣ comes and kekayī results. Others, from a study of the Bhāṣya passage (Vyā. Ma. Bhāṣya 4-1-48) —

यथैव ह्यसावकुर्वती किंचित्पापं भर्तृकृतान्बन्धनादिक्लेशाँल्लभत एवं प्रेष्यशब्दमपि लभते ।

yathaiva hyasāvakurvatī kiṃcitpāpaṃ bhartṛkṛtānbandhanādikleśām̐llabhata evaṃ preṣyaśabdamapi labhate |

"just as she, doing no wrong at all, receives the troubles of binding and the like caused by the husband, so she receives the word 'servant' too" — hold that this sūtra applies only to the connection with a man in the form of marriage, not to the connection in the form of producer and produced; in places like kekayī they hold that ṅīṣ, marked as of the gaurādi class, comes by ṣidgaurādibhyaś ca (Pā. Sū. 4-1-41). Some divide the word puṃyogāt into three words, pum, yogāt, ākhyāyām: pum ends in a dropped genitive; it is repeated and construed with both yogāt and ākhyāyām: puṃso yogāt, puṃsa ākhyāyām; the other points are as before. Even so, following the view of the author of the Kaiyaṭa [as printed], the two-word division has been shown. When ṅīṣ comes by this sūtra: deva + ī; by yasyeti ca (Pā. Sū. 6-4-148) the a is dropped; by the suffix accent this is final udātta. After the word devī, jas: devī + as; here by prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-102) — when the vowel of the first- or second-case endings follows a vowel of the ak group, the lengthening of the like preceding vowel comes as a single substitute for both — the lengthening would come, though the prohibition by dīrghāj jasi ca (Pā. Sū. 6-1-105) — after a long vowel, before jas or an ic-vowel, the lengthening of the like preceding vowel does not come — would apply. Yet by vā chandasi (Pā. Sū. 6-1-106) — in the Veda, the lengthening of the like preceding vowel comes optionally even after a long vowel before jas and ic — being laid down optionally, the lengthening comes in one alternative: it becomes devīs; ru and visarga.

अवसा (avasā) — the root ava rakṣaṇe. By sarvadhātubhyo 'sun (U. Sū. 4-6-28 [?], as read) the suffix asun. The suffix is nit, so the initial udātta accent comes.

महः (mahaḥ) — the root maha pūjāyām; by kvip ca the suffix kvip; by supāṃ supo bhavanti (Pā. Ma. 7-1-39) the instrumental singular coming after the word mah,

Page 99 (upper) — Rik 11: grammar (end)

— ṭā — takes the substitute ṅas. By sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168) — when the locative plural su follows, after a word that has one vowel, the case-endings from the third on are udātta — the case-ending is udātta.

नृपत्नीः (nṛpatnīḥ) — nṝṇāṃ patnyaḥ nṛpatnīḥ, ending in the nominative plural. Here too, by vā chandasi, the optional lengthening of the like preceding vowel comes. By patyur no yajñasaṃyoge, n is substituted for the i of the word pati; by ṛnnebhyo ṅīp (Pā. Sū. 4-1-5), ṅīp marked by ending in n; ṅīp, being pit, is unaccented. By the Uṇādi sūtra pāter ḍatiḥ, after the root pā, the suffix ḍati and the dropping of the ṭi give pati. By the suffix accent it is initially udātta, and this alone remains. So the word patnī is initially udātta; after the genitive tatpuruṣa with the word nṛ, the final udātta would be obtained by samāsasya (Pā. Sū. 6-1-223); though by parādiś chandasi bahulam (Pā. Sū. 6-2-199) the sense of this sūtra is that in the Veda the beginning of the following word is optionally udātta, here the author of the vārttika has collected the meaning of the word bahula:

परादिश्च परान्तश्च पूर्वान्तश्चापि दृश्यते । पूर्वादयश्च दृश्यन्ते व्यत्ययो बहुलं यतः ॥

parādiśca parāntaśca pūrvāntaścāpi dṛśyate | pūrvādayaśca dṛśyante vyatyayo bahulaṃ yataḥ ||

— "the beginning of the following, the end of the following, and the end of the preceding are also seen; and the beginnings of the preceding are seen: for the interchange is manifold." Examples: for the beginning of the following, tu vijātā urukṣayā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-9); for the end of the following, ni yena muṣṭihatyayā, yas tricakraḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-8-2); for the end of the preceding, viśvāyur dhehi. By this vārttika, as in urukṣayā, here too the beginning of the last member becomes udātta.

अच्छिन्नपत्राः (acchinnapatrāḥ) — na chinnāni: by nañ (Pā. Sū. 2-2-6) the nañ compound; by nalopo nañaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-3-73) the n is dropped: it becomes acchinnāni. Acchinna is a tatpuruṣa with an indeclinable first member; so, overriding the final udātta by samāsasya, by tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) the indeclinable first member keeps its own accent. Acchinnāni patrāṇi yāsāṃ tāḥ acchinnapatrāḥ: a bahuvrīhi compound. Here by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. Sū. 3-2-1, as printed) the first member's own accent comes. ॥11॥

Page 99 (lower) — Sūkta 22, Rik 12

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इ॒हेन्द्रा॒णीमुप॑ ह्वये वरुणा॒नीं स्व॒स्तये॑ । अ॒ग्नायीं॒ सोम॑पीतये ॥१२॥

ihéndrāṇī́m úpa hvaye varuṇānī́ṃ svastáye | agnā́yīṃ sómapītaye ||12|| Bars under इ, द्रा, णा and स्व; strokes over प (उप) and, at the end, ये (स्तये). Line 2: bars under अ and यीं; a stroke over म.

Page 100 — Rik 12: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इह । इन्द्राणीं । उप । ह्वये । वरुणानीं । स्वस्तये ॥ अग्नायीं । सोमऽपीतये ॥१२॥

iha | indrāṇīṃ | upa | hvaye | varuṇānīṃ | svastaye || agnāyīṃ | soma 'pītaye ||12||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इहास्मिन्कर्मणि स्वस्तयेऽस्माकमविनाशाय सोमपीतये सोमपानाय चेन्द्रवरुणाग्नीनां पत्नीराह्वयामि ॥ इन्द्राणीं । वरुणानीं । इन्द्रवरुणेत्यादिना । पा० ४-१-४९ । पुंयोगे ङीष्प्रत्यय आनुगागमश्च । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अग्नायीं । वृषाकप्यग्निकुसितकुसिदानामुदात्तः । पा० ४-१-३७ । इति ङीप् । तत्संनियोगेनेकारस्यैकार उदात्तः । सोमपीतये । असकृत्पूर्वोक्तं ॥

ihāsminkarmaṇi svastaye 'smākamavināśāya somapītaye somapānāya cendravaruṇāgnīnāṃ patnīrāhvayāmi || indrāṇīṃ | varuṇānīṃ | indravaruṇetyādinā | pā0 4-1-49 | puṃyoge ṅīṣpratyaya ānugāgamaśca | pratyayasvaraḥ | agnāyīṃ | vṛṣākapyagnikusitakusidānāmudāttaḥ | pā0 4-1-37 | iti ṅīp | tatsaṃniyogenekārasyaikāra udāttaḥ | somapītaye | asakṛtpūrvoktaṃ ||

Translation: "Iha, in this rite, svastaye, for our not perishing, and somapītaye, for drinking soma, I call the wives of Indra, Varuṇa and Agni." (Grammatical tail: indrāṇīm, varuṇānīm, by indravaruṇa… (Pā. 4-1-49), in the sense of connection with a man, the suffix ṅīṣ and the augment ānuk; the suffix accent; agnāyīm, ṅīp by vṛṣākapyagnikusitakusidānām udāttaḥ (Pā. 4-1-37), and along with it the udātta ai for the i; somapītaye, stated before more than once.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इह (iha) — to this place | इन्द्राणीं (indrāṇīṃ) — Indra's wife | वरुणानीं (varuṇānīṃ) — Varuṇa's wife | अग्नायीं (agnāyīṃ) — and Agni's wife | स्वस्तये (svastaye) — for (our) welfare (and) | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — and for drinking soma | उप ह्वये (upa hvaye) — I call.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

For bringing about good for us and for drinking soma, I call Indrāṇī, the wife of Indra, Varuṇānī, the wife of Varuṇa, and the goddess Agnāyī, the wife of Agni, to come here.

॥ English Translation ॥

I invoke here Indrani, Varunani, and Agnayi, for our welfare and to drink the Soma-juice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

इन्द्राणी, वरुणानी, अग्नायी (indrāṇī, varuṇānī, agnāyī) — Indra's wife is called Indrāṇī, Varuṇa's wife Varuṇānī, and Agni's wife Agnāyī. On this Yāska —

Page 101 — Rik 12: Special Topics (end), grammar

इन्द्राणीन्द्रस्य पत्न्यग्नाय्यग्नेः पत्न्यश्विन्यश्विनोः पत्नी राट् राजते । रोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नी । वरुणानी च वरुणस्य पत्नी । (नि० १२-४६)

indrāṇīndrasya patnyagnāyyagneḥ patnyaśvinyaśvinoḥ patnī rāṭ rājate | rodasī rudrasya patnī | varuṇānī ca varuṇasya patnī | (ni0 12-46)

— has said so: "Indrāṇī is the wife of Indra; Agnāyī, of Agni; Aśvinī, of the Aśvins; Rāṭ, she shines; Rodasī is the wife of Rudra; and Varuṇānī the wife of Varuṇa" (Ni. 12-46). They are named the wives of the gods. In some ṛks, without naming them separately, they are spoken of together as 'the wives of the gods'. As examples we have given some ṛks here:

इन्द्राणीमासु नारिषु सुभगामहमश्रवं । नह्यस्या अपरं चन जरसा मरते पतिर्विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-८६-११) नाहमिन्द्राणि रारण सख्युर्वृषाकपेरृते (ऋ० सं० १०-८६-१२) उताहमस्मि वीरिणीन्द्रपत्नी मरुत्सखा विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-८६-९) इन्द्राणीमह्व ऊतये वरुणानीं स्वस्तये (ऋ० सं० २-३२-८) उत ग्ना व्यन्तु देवपत्नीरिन्द्राण्यग्नाय्यश्विनी राट् । आ रोदसी वरुणानी शृणोतु व्यन्तु देवीर्य ऋतुर्जनीनाम् ॥ (ऋ० सं० ५-४६-८) देवानां पत्नीरुशतीरवन्तु नः प्रावन्तु नस्तुजये वाजसातये । याः पार्थिवासो या अपामपि व्रते ता नो देवीः सुहवाः शर्म यच्छत ॥ (ऋ० सं० ५-४६-७)

indrāṇīmāsu nāriṣu subhagāmahamaśravaṃ | nahyasyā aparaṃ cana jarasā marate patirviśvasmādindra uttaraḥ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-86-11) nāhamindrāṇi rāraṇa sakhyurvṛṣākaperṛte (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-86-12) utāhamasmi vīriṇīndrapatnī marutsakhā viśvasmādindra uttaraḥ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-86-9) indrāṇīmahva ūtaye varuṇānīṃ svastaye (ṛ0 saṃ0 2-32-8) uta gnā vyantu devapatnīrindrāṇyagnāyyaśvinī rāṭ | ā rodasī varuṇānī śṛṇotu vyantu devīrya ṛturjanīnām || (ṛ0 saṃ0 5-46-8) devānāṃ patnīruśatīravantu naḥ prāvantu nastujaye vājasātaye | yāḥ pārthivāso yā apāmapi vrate tā no devīḥ suhavāḥ śarma yacchata || (ṛ0 saṃ0 5-46-7) The last number is read ५-४६-७.) The names of the wives of the gods are read in many such ṛks. (Glosses of these quotations are not given in the source.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

इन्द्राणीं, वरुणानीं (indrāṇīṃ, varuṇānīṃ) — by indravaruṇabhavaśarvarudramṛḍahimāraṇyayavayavanamātulācāryāṇām ānuk (Pā. Sū. 4-1-49), the sense of the sūtra is that the augment ānuk and the suffix ṅīṣ come in the feminine after the twelve words indra and the rest. Here for the four words hima, araṇya, yava, yavana both the augment ānuk and the suffix ṅīṣ are laid down; for the other eight words, since ṅīṣ is established by puṃyogād ākhyāyām (Pā. Sū. 4-1-48), only the augment ānuk is laid down here. When, after the present words indra, varuṇa, ṅīṣ comes by puṃyogād ākhyāyām: indra + ī, varuṇa + ī; by the present sūtra indravaruṇa… the augment ānuk. Ānuk is kit; so by ādyantau ṭakitau (Pā. Sū. 1-1-46) — an augment marked ṭ comes as the first part, one marked k —

Page 102 — Rik 12: grammar (end)

— as the final part, of that for which it is laid down — it comes as the final part: indra + ān + ī, varuṇa + ān + ī; lengthening of like vowels; in the first, by aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi (Pā. Sū. 8-4-2), ṇ for the n: it becomes indrāṇī, varuṇānī. Ṅīṣ is udātta by the suffix accent ādyudāttaś ca (Pā. Sū. 3-1-3); thus both these words are final udātta.

अग्नायीं (agnāyīṃ) — the analysis is agneḥ strī. In vṛṣākapyagnikusitakusidānām udāttaḥ (Pā. Sū. 4-1-37), ai ca is carried on from the preceding sūtra pūtakratorai ca; from saṃkhyāvyayāder ṅīp (Pā. Sū. 4-1-26) ṅīp is carried on. So the sense of the sūtra results: after the four words vṛṣākapi, agni, kusita, kusida, in the feminine, the suffix ṅīp comes, and the substitute ai for the final letter of these four words; this ai is also udātta. By this sūtra, after the present word agni, the suffix ṅīp and the udātta substitute ai for the i come. Agnai + ī: by eco 'yavāyāvaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-78) the substitute āy for ai: it becomes agnāyī. Although the word agni, formed with the suffix ni by aṅger nalopaś ca (U. Sū. 4-50), is final udātta by the suffix accent, and the substitute ai coming in its place would be udātta anyway by sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ (Pā. Sū. 1-1-50), yet the word vṛṣākapi, by laghāvante dvayoś ca bahvaṣo guruḥ — in a word of many vowels ending in one or two light vowels, the heavy vowel before the light one is udātta — has ṣā udātta and the rest unaccented by śeṣanighāta; so it is final-unaccented, and the substitute ai in its place would by sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ have to be unaccented. Therefore the udātta is laid down in the present sūtra. For the three words other than vṛṣākapi, though no udātta is laid down, the udātta is established by likeness of place.

सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — its derivation has been set out many times before. ॥12॥

Page 102 (lower) — Sūkta 22, Rik 13

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

म॒ही द्यौः पृ॑थि॒वी च॑ न इ॒मं य॒ज्ञं मि॑मिक्षतां । पि॒पृ॒तां नो॒ भरी॑मभिः ॥१३॥

mahī́ dyáuḥ pṛthivī́ ca na imáṃ yajñáṃ mimikṣatāṃ | pipṛtā́ṃ no bhárīmabhiḥ ||13|| Bars under म (मही), थि, इ (इमं) and य (यज्ञं); strokes over पृ, च and the first मि. Line 2: bars under पि, पृ and नो; a stroke over री.

Page 103 — Rik 13: Pada, bhāṣya

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

मही । द्यौः । पृथिवी । च । नः । इमं । यज्ञं । मिमिक्षतां ॥ पिपृतां । नः । भरीमऽभिः ॥१३॥

mahī | dyauḥ | pṛthivī | ca | naḥ | imaṃ | yajñaṃ | mimikṣatāṃ || pipṛtāṃ | naḥ | bharīma 'bhiḥ ||13||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The Āśvalāyana numbers are printed ८-१०, २-९, २-१६, ३-१०, ६-५. The bhāṣya prints the root of pipṛtām as पॄ with hrasva iti eke, and the sūtra number पा० ७-४-७७.

द्वितीये छन्दोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इति द्यावापृथिव्यनिविद्धानीयस्तृचः । द्वितीयस्याग्निं व इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नो युवाना पितरा पुनः । आ० ८-१० । इति ॥ आग्रयणेष्टौ मही द्यौरित्येषा द्यावापृथिव्यैककपालस्यानुवाक्या । आग्रयणं व्रीहिश्यामाकेति खण्डे सूत्रितं । ये के च ज्मा महिनो अहिमाया मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नः । आ० २-९ । इति ॥ अग्निमन्थनेऽप्येषा विनियुक्ता । प्रातर्वैश्वदेव्यामिति खण्डे सूत्रितं । अभि त्वा देव सवितर्मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नः । आ० २-१६ । इति ॥ विष्यन्दमानं सांनाय्यमनयैवाहवनीयदेशे निनयेत् । विध्यपराध इति खण्डे तथैव सूत्रितं । विष्यन्दमानं मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इत्यन्तःपरिधिदेशे निनयेयुः । आ० ३-१० । इति ॥ आश्विनशस्त्रेऽप्येषा । संस्थिते ष्वाश्विनायेति खण्डे सूत्रितं । मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नस्ते हि द्यावापृथिवी विश्वशंभुवा । आ० ६-५ । इति ॥

dvitīye chandome vaiśvadevaśastre mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti dyāvāpṛthivyanividdhānīyastṛcaḥ | dvitīyasyāgniṃ va iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca no yuvānā pitarā punaḥ | ā0 8-10 | iti || āgrayaṇeṣṭau mahī dyaurityeṣā dyāvāpṛthivyaikakapālasyānuvākyā | āgrayaṇaṃ vrīhiśyāmāketi khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyā mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ | ā0 2-9 | iti || agnimanthane 'pyeṣā viniyuktā | prātarvaiśvadevyāmiti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | abhi tvā deva savitarmahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ | ā0 2-16 | iti || viṣyandamānaṃ sāṃnāyyamanayaivāhavanīyadeśe ninayet | vidhyaparādha iti khaṇḍe tathaiva sūtritaṃ | viṣyandamānaṃ mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na ityantaḥparidhideśe ninayeyuḥ | ā0 3-10 | iti || āśvinaśastre 'pyeṣā | saṃsthite ṣvāśvināyeti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naste hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśaṃbhuvā | ā0 6-5 | iti ||

Translation (application): "In the second chandoma day, at the vaiśvadeva-śastra, the tṛca to Heaven-and-Earth, mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ, the one to be put in the place of the nivid; it is laid down in the section dvitīyasyāgniṃ vaḥ: 'mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ, yuvānā pitarā punaḥ' (Āśv. 8-10). In the āgrayaṇa-iṣṭi, mahī dyauḥ is the anuvākyā of the one-potsherd cake to Heaven-and-Earth; it is laid down in the section āgrayaṇaṃ vrīhiśyāmāka: 'ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyāḥ, mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ' (Āśv. 2-9). It is used also at the churning of fire; it is laid down in the section prātarvaiśvadevyām: 'abhi tvā deva savitaḥ, mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ' (Āśv. 2-16). With this same ṛk one should pour the sāṃnāyya that is trickling away on to the place of the āhavanīya: so it is laid down in the section vidhyaparādha: 'the trickling one, with mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ, they should pour within the enclosing sticks' (Āśv. 3-10). It is used also at the āśvina-śastra; it is laid down in the section saṃsthite ṣv āśvināya: 'mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ, te hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśambhuvā' (Āśv. 6-5)."

मही महती द्यौर्द्युलोकदेवता पृथिवी भूमिदेवता च नोऽस्मदीयमिमं यज्ञं मिमिक्षतां । स्वकीयसारभूतेन रसेन मिमिक्षतां । सेक्तुमिच्छतां । तथा भरीमभिर्भरणैः पोषणैर्नोऽस्मान्पिपृतां । उभे देव्यौ पूरयतां ॥ मही । महच्छब्दादुगितश्चेति ङीप् । अच्छब्दलोपश्छान्दसः । बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानमिति ङीप उदात्तत्वं । द्यौः । दिव्शब्दः प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । गोतो णित् । पा० ७-१-९० । इति ततः परस्य सोर्णिद्वद्भावाद्वृद्धिरपि स्थानिवद्भावेनोदात्ता । पृथिवी । प्रथ प्रख्याने । प्रथेः षिवन्संप्रसारणं च । उ० १-१५० । इति षिवन्प्रत्ययः । षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च । पा० ४-१-४१ । इति ङीष् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । मिमिक्षतां । मिह सेचने । सनि द्विर्भावहलादिशेषौ । ढत्वकत्वषत्वानि । पिपृतां । पॄ पालनपूरणयोः । ह्रस्व इत्येके । शपः श्लुः । अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च । पा० ७-४-७७ । इत्यभ्यासस्याकारस्येकारः । तिङः प्रत्ययस्वरः । भरीमभिः । डुभृञ् धारणपोषणयोः । हुसृधृक्षिभृभ्य ईमनिनिति ईमन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

mahī mahatī dyaurdyulokadevatā pṛthivī bhūmidevatā ca no 'smadīyamimaṃ yajñaṃ mimikṣatāṃ | svakīyasārabhūtena rasena mimikṣatāṃ | sektumicchatāṃ | tathā bharīmabhirbharaṇaiḥ poṣaṇairno 'smānpipṛtāṃ | ubhe devyau pūrayatāṃ || mahī | mahacchabdādugitaśceti ṅīp | acchabdalopaśchāndasaḥ | bṛhanmahatorupasaṃkhyānamiti ṅīpa udāttatvaṃ | dyauḥ | divśabdaḥ prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | goto ṇit | pā0 7-1-90 | iti tataḥ parasya sorṇidvadbhāvādvṛddhirapi sthānivadbhāvenodāttā | pṛthivī | pratha prakhyāne | pratheḥ ṣivansaṃprasāraṇaṃ ca | u0 1-150 | iti ṣivanpratyayaḥ | ṣidgaurādibhyaśca | pā0 4-1-41 | iti ṅīṣ | pratyayasvaraḥ | mimikṣatāṃ | miha secane | sani dvirbhāvahalādiśeṣau | ḍhatvakatvaṣatvāni | pipṛtāṃ | pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ | hrasva ityeke | śapaḥ śluḥ | artipipartyośca | pā0 7-4-77 | ityabhyāsasyākārasyekāraḥ | tiṅaḥ pratyayasvaraḥ | bharīmabhiḥ | ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ | husṛdhṛkṣibhṛbhya īmaniniti īman | nittvādādyudāttaḥ ||

Translation: "May mahī, great, dyauḥ, the deity of the heavenly world, and pṛthivī, the deity of the earth, mimikṣatām, wish to sprinkle, imaṃ yajñam, this our sacrifice, with their own essential juice. Likewise may they pipṛtām, fill, naḥ, us, bharīmabhiḥ, with supports, nourishments: may both goddesses fill us." (Grammatical tail: mahī, ṅīp after mahat by ugitaś ca, the dropping of at Vedic, the ṅīp udātta by bṛhanmahator upasaṃkhyānam; dyauḥ, div final udātta by the stem accent; by goto ṇit (Pā. 7-1-90) the su after it is like ṇit, and the vṛddhi too is udātta by sthānivadbhāva; pṛthivī, pratha prakhyāne, the suffix ṣivan by pratheḥ ṣivan saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca (U. 1-150), ṅīṣ by ṣidgaurādibhyaś ca (Pā. 4-1-41), the suffix accent; mimikṣatām, miha secane, with san reduplication and halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, then ḍh, k and ṣ; pipṛtām, pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ (some say short), ślu for śap, i for the a of the reduplication by artipipartyoś ca (Pā. 7-4-77), the accent of the tiṅ suffix; bharīmabhiḥ, ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, īman by husṛdhṛkṣibhṛbhya īman, initial udātta as nit.)

Page 104 — Rik 13: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

मही (mahī) — great | द्यौः (dyauḥ) — the deity of the heavenly world | पृथिवी च (pṛthivī ca) — together with the deity of the earth | नः (naḥ) — our | इमं यज्ञं (imaṃ yajñaṃ) — this sacrifice | मिमिक्षतां (mimikṣatāṃ) — may they be ready to make it full of juice | भरीमभिः (bharīmabhiḥ) — with nourishing works | नः (naḥ) — us | पिपृतां (pipṛtāṃ) — may they make full.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

May the deities of the world of the gods and of the earth make our sacrifice full of juice, and nourish us with nourishing things.

॥ English Translation ॥

May the great Heaven and Earth sprinkle (with sweetness) this our Sacrifice ; may they fill us with nourishments.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

This ṛk has many applications. At the time of reciting the vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras, on the second chandoma, this ṛk mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ is used as the mantra for the recitation of a mantra with Heaven-and-Earth as deity. In the section dvitīyasyāgniṃ vaḥ of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra there is the sūtra mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) yuvānā pitarā punaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-20-4) (Ā. 8-10).

In the āgrayaṇa-iṣṭi, this ṛk mahī dyauḥ is used as the puronuvākyā ṛk for the offering of the one-potsherd cake with Heaven-and-Earth as deity. In the section āgrayaṇaṃ vrīhiśyāmāka of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra this matter is explained in the sūtra ye ke ca jmā mahino ahimāyāḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-52-14 [?]) mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) (Ā. 2-9).

At the time of churning the fire too this ṛk is applied. In the section prātarvaiśvadevyām of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra there is the sūtra abhi tvā deva savitaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3) mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) (Ā. 2-16).

When pouring the puroḍāśa called sāṃnāyya to the place of the āhavanīya, this mantra is recited. In the section vidhyaparādha of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra there is the sūtra viṣyandamānaṃ mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) ity antaḥparidhideśe ninayeyuḥ (Ā. 3-10).

Page 105 — Rik 13: Special Topics (continued)

In the recitation of the āśvina-śastra mantras too, its application is explained in the section saṃsthite ṣv āśvināya of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra by the sūtra mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) te hi dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśambhuvā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-160-1) (Ā. 6-5).

Apart from such śrauta rites, this mantra is used also in domestic rites and on occasions of prayer to the earth.

द्यौः, पृथिवी (dyauḥ, pṛthivī) — heaven and earth. Though there are many mantras that praise together (as a pair, saṃstavika) the two deities Heaven-and-Earth who preside over heaven and earth, there are also some mantras that praise them using the separate words dyauḥ and pṛthivī:

उप श्वासय पृथिवीमुत द्यां पुरुत्रा ते मनुतां विष्ठितं जगत् ॥ (ऋ० सं० ६-४७-२९) मित्रो जनान्यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्यां । (ऋ० सं० ३-५९-१) विश्वकर्मन्हविषा वावृधानः स्वयं यजस्व पृथिवीमुत द्यां ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-८१-६)

upa śvāsaya pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ purutrā te manutāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ jagat || (ṛ0 saṃ0 6-47-29) mitro janānyātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ | (ṛ0 saṃ0 3-59-1) viśvakarmanhaviṣā vāvṛdhānaḥ svayaṃ yajasva pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-81-6)

Glosses of these quotations are not given in the source. There are twenty-four words, rodasī, purandhrī [as printed: svadhe purandhī] and the rest, that indicate the meaning of the word dyāvāpṛthivī (Ni. 3-30 [?], as read). In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, with dyauḥ pitaḥ pṛthivi mātaḥ, heaven is addressed as father and the earth as mother. In the Ṛgveda the world (the universe) is generally counted in three main divisions (worlds): heaven, mid-air and earth. Heaven too has three divisions: nāka (the highest, best place in heaven), viṣṭap (the middle region) and pṛṣṭha (the lower part). Though there are no particular divisions in the mid-air, words like vyoman, rocana (the shining region) and antarikṣa indicate a difference in meaning. The word pṛthivī too is called by names such as pṛthivī (the wide region), mahī (the great region), iḷā (this world), vasumatī (rich in wealth). In the Ṛgveda the word dyāvāpṛthivī is generally used thinking of the presiding deities of heaven and earth.

द्यौः पितः पृथिवि मातः ।

dyauḥ pitaḥ pṛthivi mātaḥ |

यज्ञं मिमिक्षतां (yajñaṃ mimikṣatāṃ) — svakīyasārabhūtena rasena sektum icchatām | The intention is: may the deities Heaven-and-Earth, who preside over heaven and earth, favour this sacrifice so that it is well accomplished with the best things in heaven and on earth.

Page 106 — Rik 13: Special Topics (end), grammar

पिपृतां नो भरीमभिः (pipṛtāṃ no bharīmabhiḥ) — bharaṇasamarthair annai rasaiś ca || May they make our sacrifice complete with nourishing articles of food and with drinks such as soma juice.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

मही (mahī) — the word mahat, being treated like one ending in śatṛ by vartamāne pṛṣadbṛhanmahajjagacchatṛvac ca (U. Sū. 2-[?]), is ugit. By ugitaś ca (Pā. Sū. 4-1-6), ṅyāpprātipadikāt (Pā. Sū. 4-1-12 [?], as read), the word prātipadikāt is the heading. Ugitaḥ qualifies prātipadikāt; so by yena vidhis tadantasya (Pā. Sū. 1-1-72) a qualifier denotes what ends in it, and 'ending in it' is obtained. Though, this being a rule of suffixes, by samāsapratyayavidhau pratiṣedhaḥ (Pā. Sū. 1-1-72 Vā. 4444 [?]) — in rules of compounds and of suffixes, the obtaining of 'ending in it' is to be prohibited — the prohibition would apply, yet by ugidvarṇagrahaṇavarjam (Pā. Sū. 1-1-72 Vā. 4445 [?]) — except where an ugit or a letter is mentioned, the prohibition of 'ending in it' is to be stated in rules of compounds and suffixes — since here there is the mention of an ugit, ugitaḥ, the prohibition does not come. Or: the heading anupasarjanāt (Pā. Sū. 4-1-14) makes known that in the section on feminine suffixes there is the rule of 'ending in it'; so 'ending in it' is obtained. Striyām (Pā. Sū. 4-1-3) is the heading. From ṛnnebhyo ṅīp (Pā. Sū. 4-1-5) ṅīp is carried on. So the sense of the sūtra: after a nominal stem ending in an ugit, ṅīp comes in the feminine. Ugit is of two kinds: 1. a nominal stem; 2. a suffix. By the qualification of residing only in a nominal stem, wherever a nominal stem is mentioned, there is the prohibition vyapadeśivadbhāvo 'prātipadikena (Paribhā. 33); so vyapadeśivadbhāva cannot come there. Here, since the u-marked suffix is in both the stem and the suffix, vyapadeśivadbhāva comes here. So mahat is a stem ending in an ugit. When ṅīp follows it: mahat + ī; as a Vedic matter the word at is dropped. Viśiṣṭa apadeśaḥ, vyapadeśaḥ means the main usage. Vyapadeśinā tulyam, vyapadeśivat: for something unaccompanied, the usage 'ending in it' does not come in the main sense; yet, in the way an operation comes where there is the main usage, in the same way the operation comes: this is the meaning of vyapadeśivadbhāva. Here mahat is ugit by extension; yet, since it is not at the end of another, the main usage 'ending in an ugit' cannot come. In atimahat there is the main usage 'ending in an ugit'. Here, as the operation comes where there is the main usage, so here the operation comes: this results from vyapadeśivadbhāva. So

Page 107 — Rik 13: grammar (continued)

there is no hindrance here to ṅīp coming. Ṅīp is pit; so by anudāttau suppitau it would be unaccented. Yet by bṛhanmahator upasaṃkhyānam, read at śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173) — the nadī-named suffix and the vowel-initial case-endings śas and the rest after the words bṛhat and mahat are also udātta — it is udātta. By yū stryākhyau nadī (Pā. Sū. 1-4-3): on the view that it names letters, the sense of the sūtra is that the letters ī and ū that convey the specific sense of being always feminine get the name nadī; on the view that it names what ends in them, words ending in ī and ū that convey the specific sense of being always feminine get the name nadī. Here, on the view that it names letters, ṅīp has the name nadī. Though the udātta would be established by the extension of being treated like śatṛ, we have explained before that the vārttika was begun to obtain the restriction that the udātta is excluded for a suffix after words other than bṛhat and mahat.

द्यौः (dyauḥ) — this word can be derived in two ways. 1. The root dyuta dīptau; after it, by the word bahula in uṇādayo bahulam (Pā. Sū. 3-3-1), the Uṇādi suffix ḍo comes. By the force of the suffix being made ḍit, even without the name bha, the ṭi of the root, ut, is dropped: it became dyo. After this, the nominative singular suffix su. Goto ṇit (Pā. Sū. 7-1-90) means that the suffixes named sarvanāmasthāna after the word go — that is, the five suffixes su, au, jas, am, auṭ — are like ṇit. Here the author of the vārttika, in otaḥ ṇid iti vācyam (Pā. Sū. Vā. 7-1-90-1), says the sūtra goto ṇit should be made oto ṇit; that is, the word gotaḥ should be taken away and the word otaḥ put in its place. Accordingly it results that the sarvanāmasthāna suffixes after a word ending in o are like ṇit, that is, like those marked ṇ. So the su after the word dyo ending in o becomes like ṇit; by aco 'ñṇiti (Pā. Sū. 7-2-115) — when suffixes marked ñ or ṇ follow, a stem ending in a vowel takes vṛddhi — vṛddhi, au for o, and with ru and visarga for su it becomes dyauḥ. On this view the o is udātta by the suffix accent; the au coming in its place is also udātta by likeness of place. 2. Div is a nominal stem ending in v; it is udātta by phiṣo 'nta udāttaḥ. After it the suffix su; by diva aut (Pā. Sū. 7-1-84) — when the suffix su follows, the substitute au for the final letter of the nominal stem div — the substitute au for the v of div: di + au + s; by iko yaṇ aci (Pā. Sū. 6-1-77) y for the i: dyau s, the au having come in place of v. By sthānivad ādeśaḥ (Pā. Sū. 1-1-56), with sthānivadbhāva, it is as if v were there. So one may doubt that by halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt (Pā. Sū. 6-1-68) the su should be dropped;

Page 108 — Rik 13: grammar (continued)

but in sthānivad ādeśo 'nalvidhau (Pā. Sū. 1-1-56), analvidhau means that sthānivadbhāva does not come in a rule about letters; so when making the rule about letters halṅyābbhyaḥ, sthānivadbhāva does not come. So the su is not dropped. With ru and visarga it becomes dyauḥ. On this view the i in div is udātta; the au coming in place of the v, by asvarakāṇām asvarakā ādeśāḥ, is unaccented; by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4) — an unaccented vowel after a yaṇ standing in place of an udātta or svarita becomes svarita — the au after the y standing in place of the udātta i becomes svarita: this is the situation. In the present Veda commentary, where it says div śabdaḥ prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttaḥ, it would be right to read dyo śabdaḥ bāhulakāt auṇādikaḍopratyayāntaḥ, pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ. It is not unknown to scholars that the present reading has arisen through the carelessness of scribes and proof-readers.

दिव्शब्दः प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । द्योशब्दः बाहुलकात् औणादिकडोप्रत्ययान्तः प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः ।

divśabdaḥ prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | dyośabdaḥ bāhulakāt auṇādikaḍopratyayāntaḥ pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ |

पृथिवी (pṛthivī) — the root pratha prakhyāne; by pratheḥ ṣivan saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca (U. Sū. 1-144 [?], as read), the suffix ṣivan comes after the root prath, and the root takes saṃprasāraṇa: so when the suffix ṣivan comes, saṃprasāraṇa and ṛ for the r: pṛth + iv = pṛthiv; the suffix is ṣit. By ṣidgaurādibhyaś ca (Pā. Sū. 4-1-41) — after words marked ṣ and words read in the gaurādi class, ṅīṣ in the feminine — ṅīṣ comes. Though here the suffix is ṣit, and the word pṛthiv is not ṣit, yet by the maxim avayave 'caritārthaṃ liṅgaṃ samudāyopakārakaṃ bhavati, since the ṣ-marking in the suffix has no other purpose, that ṣ-marking qualifies the whole; pṛthivī is final udātta by the suffix accent.

अवयवेऽचरितार्थं लिङ्गं समुदायोपकारकं भवति ।

avayave 'caritārthaṃ liṅgaṃ samudāyopakārakaṃ bhavati |

मिमिक्षताम् (mimikṣatām) — the root miha secane. By dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā (Pā. Sū. 3-1-7) the suffix san; by sanyaṅoḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-9) reduplication: mih mih + sa; by halādiḥ śeṣaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-4-60) the h of the first mih is dropped. Loṭ, third person tas; by loṭo laṅvat (Pā. Sū. 3-4-85) treated like laṅ; by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101) the substitute tām. Since the root mih is in the aniṭ-kārikā, vasatir dahadihaduho nah mih ruh lih vahis tathā (Pā. Sū. Pā. Mā. 7-2-10-6 [?], as read), the augment iṭ is barred by ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt (Pā. Sū. 7-2-10). Mimih + sa + tām: now by ho ḍhaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-31) ḍh for h; for this ḍh, by ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si (Pā. Sū. 8-8-41 [?], as read) the substitute t [sic; for k]; for the s after it, by ādeśapratyayayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-3-59)

Page 109 — Rik 13: grammar (end)

ṣ: it becomes mimikṣatām. By tiṅṅatiṅaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) it is wholly unaccented.

पिपृताम् (pipṛtām) — the root pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ; some hold that pṛ ends in a short vowel. Loṭ, third person tas, the substitute tām as before, śap; by juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-75) ślu (dropping); by ślau (Pā. Sū. 6-1-10) reduplication; on the view that ślu has come, by artipipartyoś ca (Pā. Sū. 7-4-77) — ṛ gatau, pṝ, pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ — i comes as the final substitute for their reduplication: so for the ṛ of the first pṛ, i; by uraṇ raparaḥ it comes followed by r. By halādiḥ śeṣaḥ the r is removed: it becomes pipṛtām. In the Bhāṣya it is described as: first, by ur at (Pā. Sū. 7-4-66), when a suffix follows, a comes for the ṛ of the reduplication; then i for the a by artipipartyoś ca. In fact, since the rule laying down i is an exception to ur at, it is right to say that i comes first. Here, since the root pṛ ending in a short vowel is taken, the u for the ṛ of the second pṛ by udoṣṭhyapūrvasya (Pā. Sū. 7-1-102) does not come. Since there is the prohibition kṅiti ca (Pā. Sū. 1-1-5), guṇa does not come. Since this is at the beginning of the pāda, by the prohibition apādādau, the total lack of accent by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ does not come. So by the suffix accent tām is udātta.

भरीमभिः (bharīmabhiḥ) — the root ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ. By husṛdhṛkṣibhṛbhya īman (Daśa. Pā. 6 [as printed]) — after the roots hu dānādanayoḥ, styai[ñ] ācchādane [as printed], ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, dhṛñ avasthāne, svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ, sṛ gatau, the suffix īman comes — when īman comes: bhṛ + īman, guṇa; the suffix is nit, so by the nit accent bharīmabhiḥ is initially udātta. ॥13॥
