॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

वरु॑णः प्रावि॒ता भु॑वन्मि॒त्रो विश्वा॑भिरू॒तिभिः॑ । क॑रतां नः सु॒राध॑सः ॥६॥ [accent ?]

váruṇaḥ prāvitā́ bhuvan mitró víśvābhir ūtíbhiḥ | karatāṃ naḥ surā́dhasaḥ ||6|| [accent ?] Strokes over रु, भु, श्वा and भिः; bars under वि (प्राविता), मि and रू. Line 2: a stroke over क (read as printed), a bar under सु, a stroke over ध [accent ?]. The Pada heading on this page is printed ॥ प्रतिपदार्थ ॥, as printed.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

वरुणः । प्रऽअविता । भुवत् । मित्रः । विश्वाभिः । ऊतिऽभिः ॥ करतां । नः । सुऽराधसः ॥६॥

varuṇaḥ | pra 'avitā | bhuvat | mitraḥ | viśvābhiḥ | ūti 'bhiḥ || karatāṃ | naḥ | su 'rādhasaḥ ||6||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The numbers are printed पा० ७-३-८८ and ६-२-११७.

अयं वरुणोऽस्माकं प्राविता भुवत् । प्रकर्षेण रक्षको भवतु । मित्रश्च विश्वाभिरूतिभिः सर्वाभी रक्षाभिः प्राविता भुवत् । तावुभावपि नोऽस्मान्सुराधसः प्रभूतधनयुक्तान्करतां । कुरुतां ॥ अविता । तृचश्चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वं । प्रादिसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन तदेव शिष्यते । भुवत् । भू सत्तायां । लेटस्तिप् । लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः । इतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । गुणे प्राप्ते भूसुवोस्तिङि । पा० ७-३-८८ । इति प्रतिषेधः । उवङादेशः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । विश्वाभिः । अशिप्रुषीत्यादिना क्वन्नन्तो विश्वशब्द आद्युदात्तः । टाप्सुपोरनुदात्तत्वात्तदेव शिष्यते । ऊतिभिः । ऊतियूतीत्यादिना क्तिन्नुदात्तः । करतां । कृञ् करणे । भौवादिकः । लोटस्तस् । तसस्तां । कर्तरि शप् । गुणो रपरत्वं । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । सुराधसः । राध साध संसिद्धौ । राध्नोत्यनेनेति राधो धनं । शोभनं राधो येषां ते । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं प्राप्तं सोर्मनसी अलोमोषसी । पा० ६-२-११७ । इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वेन बाध्यते ॥

ayaṃ varuṇo 'smākaṃ prāvitā bhuvat | prakarṣeṇa rakṣako bhavatu | mitraśca viśvābhirūtibhiḥ sarvābhī rakṣābhiḥ prāvitā bhuvat | tāvubhāvapi no 'smānsurādhasaḥ prabhūtadhanayuktānkaratāṃ | kurutāṃ || avitā | tṛcaścittvādantodāttatvaṃ | prādisamāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvena tadeva śiṣyate | bhuvat | bhū sattāyāṃ | leṭastip | leṭo 'ḍāṭāvityaḍāgamaḥ | itaśca lopa itīkāralopaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | guṇe prāpte bhūsuvostiṅi | pā0 7-3-88 | iti pratiṣedhaḥ | uvaṅādeśaḥ | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | viśvābhiḥ | aśipruṣītyādinā kvannanto viśvaśabda ādyudāttaḥ | ṭāpsuporanudāttatvāttadeva śiṣyate | ūtibhiḥ | ūtiyūtītyādinā ktinnudāttaḥ | karatāṃ | kṛñ karaṇe | bhauvādikaḥ | loṭastas | tasastāṃ | kartari śap | guṇo raparatvaṃ | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | tiṅaśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvaraḥ śiṣyate | surādhasaḥ | rādha sādha saṃsiddhau | rādhnotyaneneti rādho dhanaṃ | śobhanaṃ rādho yeṣāṃ te | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ prāptaṃ sormanasī alomoṣasī | pā0 6-2-117 | ityuttarapadādyudāttatvena bādhyate ||

Translation: "May this Varuṇa bhuvat, be, prāvitā, our protector in an eminent way. And may Mitra bhuvat, be, the protector viśvābhir ūtibhiḥ, with all protections. May both of them karatām, make, naḥ, us, surādhasaḥ, possessed of abundant wealth." (Grammatical tail: avitā, final udātta as tṛc is cit, which alone remains in the prādi compound by the kṛt final member's accent; bhuvat, bhū sattāyām, tip for leṭ, the augment aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau, i dropped by itaś ca lopaḥ…, śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; the guṇa due is barred by bhūsuvos tiṅi (Pā. 7-3-88); the substitute uvaṅ; loss of accent by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ; viśvābhiḥ, viśva, ending in kvan by aśipruṣi…, initially udātta, which alone remains as ṭāp and the sup are unaccented; ūtibhiḥ, the ktin udātta by ūtiyūti…; karatām, kṛñ karaṇe of the bhvādi class, tas for loṭ, tām for tas, śap by kartari śap, guṇa followed by r; śap unaccented as pit, and the tiṅ too by the lasārvadhātuka accent, so the root accent remains; surādhasaḥ, rādha sādha saṃsiddhau, 'by it one accomplishes': rādhaḥ, wealth; 'whose wealth is fine'; the bahuvrīhi first-member accent being due, the final udātta of the last member by nañsubhyām is due, and that is overridden by the last member's initial udātta by sor manasī alomoṣasī (Pā. 6-2-117).)

Page 163 — Rik 6: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

वरुणः (varuṇaḥ) — Varuṇa (our) | प्राविता (prāvitā) — as chief protector | भुवत् (bhuvat) — may he be | मित्रः (mitraḥ) — Mitra | विश्वाभिः (viśvābhiḥ) — with all | ऊतिभिः (ūtibhiḥ) — protections (may he be our protector) | (these Mitra and Varuṇa) नः (naḥ) — us | सुराधसः (surādhasaḥ) — especially possessed of wealth | करतां (karatāṃ) — may they make.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

May Varuṇa be our chief protector; may Mitra too protect us, giving all his protections. And may both these, Mitra and Varuṇa, make us possessed of wealth, that is, give us much wealth.

॥ English Translation ॥

May Varuna be our special protector; may Mitra protect us with all kinds of protections; may they make us possessors of great riches.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

विश्वाभिः ऊतिभिः (viśvābhiḥ ūtibhiḥ) — with protections of many kinds. Here 'of many kinds' means protections such as food and the like, a place to live, and warding off the fear that comes from enemies: this is the intention.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

प्राविता (prāvitā) — the root ava rakṣaṇe; by ṇvultṛcau (Pā. Sū. 3-1-133) tṛc; by ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-2-35) the augment iṭ: avitṛ. By kugatiprādayaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-2-18) the prādi compound with the word pra. Tṛc is cit, so by citaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) avitṛ is final udātta; after compounding too, by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the same accent stays. After prāvitṛ,

Page 164 — Rik 6: grammar (continued)

the suffix su; by ṛduśanaspurudaṃso 'nehasāṃ ca (Pā. Sū. 7-1-94) the substitute anaṅ; by aptṛntṛc… (Pā. Sū. 6-4-11) lengthening; by halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt… (Pā. Sū. 6-1-68) su is dropped; by nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya (Pā. Sū. 8-2-7) the n [printed "the s"] is dropped.

भुवत् (bhuvat) — the root bhū sattāyām; after it, by liṅarthe leṭ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-7), leṭ; for it the substitute tip: bhū + ti. By leṭo 'ḍāṭau (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94) — leṭ takes the augments aṭ, āṭ — the augment aṭ: bhū + a + ti. By itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97) — the i of a suffix in the parasmaipada is dropped — the i is dropped: bhū + at; for the vikaraṇa śap, by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. Sū. 2-4-73), luk. By sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) — when a sārvadhātuka suffix (that is, a tiṅ suffix and a suffix marked ś) or an ārdhadhātuka (the name of the suffixes laid down under the root heading other than these) follows, a word ending in i, u, ṛ, ḷ takes guṇa — the guṇa o for the ū in bhū would be due; but by bhūsuvos tiṅi (Pā. Sū. 7-3-88) — when a tiṅ suffix named sārvadhātuka follows, bhū and sū do not take guṇa — the prohibition comes, so guṇa does not come. Aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau (Pā. Sū. 6-4-77): the word division is aci, śnudhātubhruvām, yvoḥ, iyaṅuvaṅau; iś ca uś ca = yū, tayoḥ yvoḥ: 'of i and u'. Yvoḥ is a qualifier of dhātoḥ; by yena vidhis tadantasya (Pā. Sū. 1-1-72) 'ending in it' is obtained: roots ending in i and u. Śnu and bhrū both always end in u, never in i; so, there being no possibility and no exclusion (no fitness for excluding others), yvoḥ is not a qualifier of śnu, bhrū. The maxim saṃbhavavyabhicārābhyāṃ syād viśeṣaṇam arthavat must be stated here. The fourth pāda of the sixth adhyāya and the four pādas of the seventh adhyāya, these five pādas of the Aṣṭādhyāyī, are under the aṅga heading; this too being under the aṅga heading, aṅgasya (Pā. Sū. 6-4-1) is the heading. By the maxim yaṃ vinā…, pratyaye is implied; it is changed to the seventh case; aci, being its qualifier, gives the 'beginning with it'; śnudhātubhruvām being a qualifier of aṅgasya, by yena vidhis tadantasya (Pā. Sū. 1-1-72) 'ending in it' is obtained. So the sense of the sūtra: a stem ending in the suffix śnu, a stem ending in roots ending in i, u, and a stem ending in the word bhrū take the substitutes iyaṅ, uvaṅ when a vowel-initial suffix follows. So for i, iyaṅ,

Page 165 — Rik 6: grammar (continued)

and for u, uvaṅ. Short and long i, u are both taken. In bhū + at, when uvaṅ comes for the ū: bhuv + at = bhuvat. By tiṅṅatiṅaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) it is wholly unaccented.

विश्वाभिः (viśvābhiḥ) — the root viśa praveśane; by aśūpruṣilaṭikaṇikhaṭiviśibhyaḥ kvan (U. Sū. 1-149) the suffix kvan; viśva is initially udātta by the nit accent. After it, when the feminine is intended, by ajādyataṣ ṭāp (Pā. Sū. 4-1-4) ṭāp; the instrumental plural bhis; ṭāp and bhis are both unaccented by anudāttau suppitau (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4); so in viśvābhiḥ the initial udātta alone stays.

ऊतिभिः (ūtibhiḥ) — by ūtiyūtijūtisātihetibhyaś ca [as printed] (Pā. Sū. 3-3-97) the udātta ktin comes.

करताम् (karatām) — the root ḍukṛñ karaṇe, here in the bhvādi (first) class; loṭ. For it by tiptasjhi… (Pā. Sū. 3-4-78) tas: kṛ + tas; by kartari śap (Pā. Sū. 3-1-68) the vikaraṇa śap; by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) guṇa for the ṛ; it comes followed by r by uraṇ raparaḥ (Pā. Sū. 1-1-51), that is ar: kar + a + tas; by loṭo laṅvat (Pā. Sū. 3-4-85) treated like laṅ; by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101) the substitute tām. Śap being pit, it is unaccented; the following tiṅ tām, by tāsy anudāttenṅid adupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam ahnviṅoḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186), is unaccented. The root accent alone remains.

सुराधसः (surādhasaḥ) — the root rādha sādha saṃsiddhau. Rādhnoti anena: 'by this one attains accomplishment': rādhaḥ, meaning wealth. Śobhanaṃ rādhaḥ yeṣāṃ te, 'those who have fine wealth': by anekam anyapadārthe (Pā. Sū. 2-2-24) the bahuvrīhi compound. By sarvadhātubhyo 'sun (U. Sū. 4-628 [?], as read) the word rādhas, ending in the suffix asun, is initially udātta by the nit accent. After the bahuvrīhi compound, by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the first member's own accent would be due; overriding it, by nañsubhyām (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) — in a bahuvrīhi compound the last member after nañ and su is final udātta — the final udātta would be due. Overriding this too, by sor manasī alomoṣasī (Pā. Sū. 6-2-117) — words ending in man and words ending in as, other than the two words loman and uṣas, after the word su,

Page 166 (upper) — Rik 6: grammar (end)

are initially udātta (man: what ends in it is mannanta; as: what ends in it is asanta) — so the last member has the initial udātta accent. ॥6॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

म॒रुत्व॑न्तं हवामह॒ इन्द्र॒मा सोम॑पीतये । स॒जूर्ग॒णेन॑ तृम्पतु ॥७॥

marútvantaṃ havāmaha índram ā́ sómapītaye | sajū́r gaṇéna tṛmpatu ||7|| Bars under म (मरुत्), ह (हवामह) and द्र; strokes over त्व and म (सोम). Line 2: bars under स and ग, a stroke over न (गणेन). The print has तृंपतु.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

मरुत्वन्तं । हवामहे । इन्द्रं । आ । सोमऽपीतये ॥ सऽजूः । गणेन । तृम्पतु ॥७॥

marutvantaṃ | havāmahe | indraṃ | ā | soma 'pītaye || sa 'jūḥ | gaṇena | tṛmpatu ||7||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Numbers as printed: पा० ८-२-१०, १-४-१९, ६-१-१७६, का० ६-१-१७६, पा० ८-२-६६, ८-२-७६, ६-२-१९९-१, ७-१-५९. The paribhāṣā number (small, split across the line end) reads 7 followed by a glyph that is 6 or 9.

मरुत्वन्तं मरुद्भिर्युक्तमिन्द्रं सोमपीतये सोमपानायाऽऽ हवामहे । आह्वयामः । स चेन्द्रो गणेन मरुत्समूहेन सजूः सह तृम्पतु । तृप्तो भवतु ॥ मरुत्वन्तं । मरुतोऽस्य सन्तीति मरुत्वान् । झयः । पा० ८-२-१० । इति मतुपो वत्वं । तसौ मत्वर्थे । पा० १-४-१९ । इति भसंज्ञायां पदसंज्ञाया बाधितत्वाज्जश्त्वाभावः । मतुप्सुपौ पित्त्वादनुदात्तौ । ननु ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् । पा० ६-१-१७६ । इति मतुप उदात्तत्वेन भवितव्यं स्वरविधौ व्यञ्जनमविद्यमानवत् । परि० ७[६/९?] । इति तकारस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वेन ह्रस्वात्परत्वात् । न । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यामित्यत्र नुड्ग्रहणसामर्थ्यादविद्यमानवत्परिभाषा नाश्रीयत इति वृत्तावुक्तं । का० ६-१-१७६ । अतो मरुच्छब्दस्य स्वर एव शिष्यते । सजूः । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । संपदादिलक्षणः क्विप् । समाना प्रीतिर्यस्येति बहुव्रीहिः । समानस्य छन्दसीति सभावः । ससजुषो रुः । पा० ८-२-६६ । इति रुत्वं । र्वोरुपधायाः । पा० ८-२-७६ । इत्युपधादीर्घः । बहुव्रीहिस्वरे प्राप्ते त्रिचक्रादीनां छन्दसि । पा० ६-२-१९९-१ । इत्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । तृम्पतु । तृप तृम्प तृप्तौ । तुदादिभ्यः शः । शे मुचादीनां । पा० ७-१-५९ । इति नुमागमः ॥

marutvantaṃ marudbhiryuktamindraṃ somapītaye somapānāyā ' ' havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ | sa cendro gaṇena marutsamūhena sajūḥ saha tṛmpatu | tṛpto bhavatu || marutvantaṃ | maruto 'sya santīti marutvān | jhayaḥ | pā0 8-2-10 | iti matupo vatvaṃ | tasau matvarthe | pā0 1-4-19 | iti bhasaṃjñāyāṃ padasaṃjñāyā bādhitatvājjaśtvābhāvaḥ | matupsupau pittvādanudāttau | nanu hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup | pā0 6-1-176 | iti matupa udāttatvena bhavitavyaṃ svaravidhau vyañjanamavidyamānavat | pari0 7[6/9?] | iti takārasyāvidyamānavattvena hrasvātparatvāt | na | hrasvanuḍbhyāmityatra nuḍgrahaṇasāmarthyādavidyamānavatparibhāṣā nāśrīyata iti vṛttāvuktaṃ | kā0 6-1-176 | ato marucchabdasya svara eva śiṣyate | sajūḥ | juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | saṃpadādilakṣaṇaḥ kvip | samānā prītiryasyeti bahuvrīhiḥ | samānasya chandasīti sabhāvaḥ | sasajuṣo ruḥ | pā0 8-2-66 | iti rutvaṃ | rvorupadhāyāḥ | pā0 8-2-76 | ityupadhādīrghaḥ | bahuvrīhisvare prāpte tricakrādīnāṃ chandasi | pā0 6-2-199-1 | ityuttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | tṛmpatu | tṛpa tṛmpa tṛptau | tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ | śe mucādīnāṃ | pā0 7-1-59 | iti numāgamaḥ ||

Translation: "We ā havāmahe, call, marutvantam, accompanied by the Maruts, Indra, somapītaye, to drink soma. And may that Indra tṛmpatu, be satisfied, sajūḥ, together, gaṇena, with the host of Maruts." (Grammatical tail: marutvantam, 'he has Maruts': marutvān; the v for the m of matup by jhayaḥ (Pā. 8-2-10); with the name bha by tasau matvarthe (Pā. 1-4-19) the name pada is overridden, so no jaśtva; matup and sup unaccented as pit. But should matup not be udātta by hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup (Pā. 6-1-176), since by svaravidhau vyañjanam avidyamānavat (Paribhāṣā 7[6 or 9], the number runs over the line end; the first glyph is the flat-footed 7, the second a hooked glyph not settled between 6 and 9) the t, treated as not there, makes it follow a short vowel? No: the vṛtti says (Kā. 6-1-176) that in hrasvanuḍbhyām, by the force of the mention of nuṭ, the paribhāṣā on what is not there is not resorted to; so only the accent of marut remains; sajūḥ, juṣī prītisevanayoḥ, kvip of the sampadādi type; 'whose love is the same', a bahuvrīhi; sa by samānasya chandasi…; ru by sasajuṣo ruḥ (Pā. 8-2-66); the penultimate lengthened by rvor upadhāyāḥ… (Pā. 8-2-76); the bahuvrīhi accent being due, the last member's final udātta by tricakrādīnāṃ chandasi (Pā. 6-2-199-1); tṛmpatu, tṛpa tṛmpa tṛptau, śa by tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ, the augment num by śe mucādīnām (Pā. 7-1-59).)

ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यामित्यत्र नुड्ग्रहणसामर्थ्यादविद्यमानवत्परिभाषा नाश्रीयते ।

hrasvanuḍbhyāmityatra nuḍgrahaṇasāmarthyādavidyamānavatparibhāṣā nāśrīyate |

Page 167 — Rik 7: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

मरुत्वन्तं (marutvantaṃ) — accompanied by the Marut deities | इन्द्रं (indraṃ) — Indra | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — for drinking soma | आ हवामहे (ā havāmahe) — we call | (that Indra) गणेन (gaṇena) — with the hosts of Maruts | सजूः (sajūḥ) — together | तृम्पतु (tṛmpatu) — may he be satisfied.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

We call Indra, accompanied by the Marut deities, to drink soma. May that Indra (come here, drink the soma and) be satisfied together with the Maruts.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke Indra with his Maruts to drink the Soma-juice; may he be satisfied with his host (of Maruts).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

सजूः तृम्पतु (sajūḥ tṛmpatu) — juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | samānā prītir yasya sajūḥ | The intention is: may Indra and the Marut deities be satisfied alike, that is, may both be satisfied. Since here sajūḥ means 'having the same satisfaction' and tṛmpatu means 'may he be satisfied', one may doubt that there is the fault of repetition; the answer can be given that, since many such usages are in currency, they are not much worth noting.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

मरुत्वन्तम् (marutvantam) — the analysis is marutaḥ asya santi, 'he has the Maruts'. By tad asyāsty asminn iti matup (Pā. Sū. 5-2-94) the suffix matup after the word marut: marut + mat. By jhayaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-10) — the m of matup after a word ending in a jhay letter takes v — the v: marut + vat. Marut is a word ending in t; so by tasau matvarthe (Pā. Sū. 1-4-19) — when a suffix in the sense of matup follows, words ending in t and s get the name bha — the name bha comes. By this name bha, the name pada that would come by suptiṅantaṃ padam, taking the internal case-ending as cause, is overridden. Since thus marut has no name pada, by jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte (Pā. Sū. 8-4-[blank in the print]) — the jhal letters at the end of a pada take j, b, g, ḍ, d — the d does not come for the t. After marutvat,

Page 168 — Rik 7: grammar (continued)

the accusative singular suffix am; by ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-70) the augment num: marutvan + t + am; anusvāra and parasavarṇa: marutvantam. Matup because it is pit, and am because it is a sup, are both unaccented by anudāttau suppitau (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4); but am, though a sup, is not pit. So the line of the Veda commentary matupsupau pittvād anudāttau (matup and sup both unaccented because pit) is a slip. By the paribhāṣā svaravidhau vyañjanam avidyamānavat (Paribhā. 7[6 or 9], see p. 166) — in making an accent rule a consonant is as if not there — the t of marut is as if not there. So the suffix matup, vat, is as if following ru, a short vowel. Then by hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup (Pā. Sū. 6-1-176) — a matup immediately after a final-udātta word ending in a short vowel, or immediately after the augment nuṭ, is udātta — the question arises that the matup after maru should be udātta. To this the author of the Kāśikā-vṛtti (Kā. 6-1-176) has given the answer at the present sūtra. In the sūtra hrasvanuḍbhyām, the example for nuṭ is akṣaṇvantaḥ. After the word akṣi, matup; with asthidadhisakthyakṣṇām anaṅ udāttaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-75) carried on, by chandasy api dṛśyate — in the Veda the substitute anaṅ is seen for the words asthi and the rest, and it is udātta. Since here api dṛśyate is said, there is the exclusion of all restricting conditions. The previous sūtra laid down the substitute anaṅ when a vowel-initial case-ending of the third onward follows. This substitute anaṅ comes both in places like asthabhiḥ, where a consonant-initial case-ending follows, and in places like asthanvantaṃ yad anasthā bibharti, where no case-ending follows. In asthanvantam, matup after the word asthi, the substitute anaṅ; by anor nuṭ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-16) nuṭ for the matup, and the dropping of the a of an; thus when the substitute anaṅ comes by this sūtra: akṣan + mat; by pūrvatrāsiddham (Pā. Sū. 8-2-1), since anor nuṭ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-16) is asiddha, first by nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya (Pā. Sū. 8-2-7) the n is dropped; now, since by its former state it ended in an, by anor nuṭ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-16) — the matup after a word ending in an takes the augment nuṭ — the augment nuṭ: akṣa + n + mat; since nuṭ is asiddha (Pā. Sū. 8-2-1), by mād upadhāyāś ca mator vo 'yavādibhyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-70 [?], as read) v for the m, and by aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi (Pā. Sū. 8-4-2) ṇ for the n: it becomes akṣaṇvat; the a of kṣa is udātta. Thus akṣa is final udātta and ends in a short vowel. But after it there is the augment nuṭ, n. So, there being an intervention, the matup is not after a short vowel. For that reason the mention of nuṭ is made in the sūtra hrasvanuḍbhyām.

Page 169 — Rik 7: grammar (continued)

Here, on the view that the paribhāṣā svaravidhau vyañjanam avidyamānavat applies, since the n is treated as not there, it is as if absent; then the mat is as if immediately after akṣa, which ends in a short vowel. So the udātta of matup could be established anyway. If so, the mention of nuṭ again would have to be useless. Pāṇini does not use useless words; so, by the force of the mention of nuṭ, we accept that in the matter of the sūtra hrasvanuḍbhyām the paribhāṣā svaravidhau vyañjanam avidyamānavat does not apply: so they say. The Kāśikā statement giving this meaning: hrasvanuḍbhyām ity atra nuḍgrahaṇasāmarthyād avidyamānavatparibhāṣā nāśrīyate (Kā. 6-1-176). If the paribhāṣā on what is not there does not come here, the n is not made non-existent, so the matup is not immediately after the short-vowel-final, final-udātta akṣa; so the mention of nuṭ has its purpose. Therefore in the present case, if svaravidhau is not applied when making hrasvanuḍbhyām, since there is the intervention of t, the matup is not immediately after maru, which ends in a short vowel and is final udātta. So the matup is not udātta. Marut ends in the suffix uti by mṛgror utiḥ (U. Sa. 1-94), so it is final udātta by the suffix accent, and this stays. Here some others exclude the udātta of matup in another way too. Namely, the paribhāṣā svaravidhau is made known by the exclusion of pṛthivī and the rest in nottarapade 'nudāttādāv apṛthivīrudrapūṣamanthiṣu (Pā. Sū. 6-2-142). In places like dyāvāpṛthivī, since pṛthivī does not begin with an unaccented vowel, nottarapade anudāttādau, which gives the meaning anudāttādau uttarapade paratah ubhayapadaprakṛtisvaraḥ na bhavati, does not apply at all. If so, the exclusion of pṛthivī and the rest, being useless, by the maxim vyarthaṃ sat kiṃcid arthaṃ jñāpayati, makes known svaravidhau. Once it is made known, since in making the accent the consonants beginning with p are as if not there, pṛthivī begins with an unaccented vowel. So the exclusion apṛthivī… is purposeful, to remove the prohibition nottarapade 'nudāttādau that would come in dyāvāpṛthivī. By the force of this indication, this paribhāṣā applies only in rules aimed at accent; that is, to a consonant contrary to the usage of being the first part of an unaccented vowel included in the range of the object of the rule, and to a consonant contrary to the usage of being the last part of an udātta included in that range — to these two the paribhāṣā svaravidhau applies in making the accent. Uddeśyakoṭipraviṣṭodāttādisaṃbandhi caramāvayavatvādivyavahāravirodhi vyañjanaṃ svaravidhau avidyamānavat bhavati: this is the meaning drawn out from the paribhāṣā. The t of the present marut is not such. For marut is contrary both to the usage 'ending in a short vowel' and to the usage 'final udātta';

Page 170 — Rik 7: grammar (continued)

the t: in the udātta rule, the matup immediately after a final-udātta word ending in a short vowel is the object; for the t, contrary to the usage of being the final part of an udātta included in this range of the object, the treatment as not there comes, and marut is final udātta; but for the t, contrary to the usage 'ending in a short vowel', the treatment as not there does not come, so marut does not become short-vowel-final. Therefore by hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup the udātta does not come to matup in marutvantam. In akṣaṇvantam the n is the first part of the matup, so it is no obstacle to whatever usage of being a final part connected with the udātta included in the range of the object of hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup, which has the form 'a matup following immediately after a final-udātta short-vowel-final word'. So svaravidhau does not apply. Therefore the mention of nuṭ is purposeful; on this view there is no burden of having to imagine the non-application of the paribhāṣā svaravidhau in the matter of the sūtra hrasvanuḍbhyām by the force of the mention of nuṭ. For that very reason in the Paribhāṣenduśekhara (because it applies in rules aimed at accent) it is said: udaśvitvān ity atra hrasvanuḍbhyām iti matubudāttatvaṃ ca nety ākaraḥ (Pari. Śe. [?]).

उदश्वित्वानित्यत्र ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यामिति मतुबुदात्तत्वं च नेत्याकरः ।

udaśvitvānityatra hrasvanuḍbhyāmiti matubudāttatvaṃ ca netyākaraḥ |

सजूः (sajūḥ) — samānaḥ juṣ (samānā prītiḥ): those who have one and the same kind of love. The root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; after it, by sampadādibhyaḥ kvip (Pā. Sū. 3-3-108 vārttika), kvip comes in the action sense. By samānasya chandasy amūrdhaprabhṛtyudarkeṣu (Pā. Sū. 6-3-84) — the substitute sa comes in the Veda for the word samāna before a last member other than the three words mūrdhan, prabhṛti, udarka — the substitute sa for samāna: it becomes sajuṣ. Sasajuṣo ruḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-66): the ru substitute comes for the final s of a pada and for the word sajuṣ at the end of a pada; or, the meaning is that the ru substitute comes for the final letter of a pada ending in the word sajuṣ. Here after the word sajuṣ the first-case suffix su; for it, by halṅyābbhyaḥ, the dropping. Now sajuṣ is a pada by suptiṅantaṃ padam (Pā. Sū. 1-4-14); by vyapadeśivadbhāva it is also a pada ending in the word sajuṣ. The substitute ru for its final ṣ: it became sajur. By rvor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-76) — at the end of a pada, the penultimate letter of a root ending in r or v is lengthened — the u is lengthened: sajūr. By kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-3-15) the visarga for the r: it becomes sajūḥ. Gaṇena sajūḥ: having the same love with the host, is the meaning. Sajūḥ is a bahuvrīhi, so by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the first member's own accent would be due. But overriding it, by antodāttaprakaraṇe tricakrā-

Page 171 (upper) — Rik 7: grammar (end)

dīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam (Pā. Sū. 6-2-199-1) the last member gets the final udātta accent.

तृम्पतु (tṛmpatu) — the root tṛpa tṛmpha tṛptau; loṭ, tip; by eruḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-86) tu for ti: tṛp + tu; by tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-77) the vikaraṇa śa: tṛp + a + tu; by śe tṛmphādīnām (Pā. Sū. 7-1-59-1) — when the suffix śa follows, tṛmph and the rest take the augment num — the augment num. If the augment num were given by reading tṛmpha as such in the list of roots, the n would have to be dropped by aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti (Pā. Sū. 6-4-24). So the vārttika would not be needed if these roots were read in the mucādi class. Tṛnp + atu: by naś cāpadāntasya jhali (Pā. Sū. 8-3-24) anusvāra for the n; by anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-4-58) the homorganic m: it becomes tṛmpatu. In the Veda commentary it is tṛpa tṛmpa tṛptau; since such a reading is not found in the list of roots, tṛpa tṛmpha is taken. ॥7॥

índrajyeṣṭhā marudgaṇā dévāsaḥ pū́ṣarātayaḥ | viśve máma śrutā hávaṃ ||8|| [accent ?] Strokes over द्र, म (मरु), वा and ष (पूष); bars under ष्ठा, णा and सः. Line 2: a bar under श्वे, strokes over the second म (मम) and over वं, a bar under ता; the positions in line 2 are not certain [accent ?].

indra 'jyeṣṭhāḥ | marut 'gaṇāḥ | devāsaḥ | pūṣa 'rātayaḥ || viśve | mama | śruta | havaṃ ||8||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Numbers as printed: पा० ८-१-७४, ३-४-१०१, ३-३-७५.

हे देवास इन्द्रमरुद्रूपा विश्वे सर्वे यूयं मम हवमाह्वानं श्रुत । शृणुत । कीदृशाः । इन्द्रज्येष्ठाः । इन्द्रो ज्येष्ठो मुख्यो येषु ते । तथाविधा मरुद्गणाः मरुत्समूहरूपाः । पूषरातयः । पूषाख्यो देवो रातिर्दाता येषामिन्द्रमरुतां ते पूषरातयः ॥ इन्द्रज्येष्ठाः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । पादादित्वादनिघातः । मरुद्गणाः । विभाषितं विशेषवचने बहुवचनं । पा० ८-१-७४ । इति पूर्वस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वादनिघातः । देवासः पूषरातयः । पूर्ववत् । श्रुत । श्रु श्रवणे । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनं थ । तस्थस्थमिपां । पा० ३-४-१०१ । इति तादेशः । व्यत्ययेन शप् । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोरिति गुणे प्राप्ते क्ङिति चेति प्रतिषेधः । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति दीर्घः । हवं । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । भावेऽनुपसर्गस्य । पा० ३-३-७५ । इत्यप् । संप्रसारणं परपूर्वत्वं गुणावादेशौ । पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । धातुस्वरः शिष्यते ॥

he devāsa indramarudrūpā viśve sarve yūyaṃ mama havamāhvānaṃ śruta | śṛṇuta | kīdṛśāḥ | indrajyeṣṭhāḥ | indro jyeṣṭho mukhyo yeṣu te | tathāvidhā marudgaṇāḥ marutsamūharūpāḥ | pūṣarātayaḥ | pūṣākhyo devo rātirdātā yeṣāmindramarutāṃ te pūṣarātayaḥ || indrajyeṣṭhāḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | pādāditvādanighātaḥ | marudgaṇāḥ | vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣavacane bahuvacanaṃ | pā0 8-1-74 | iti pūrvasyāvidyamānavattvādanighātaḥ | devāsaḥ pūṣarātayaḥ | pūrvavat | śruta | śru śravaṇe | loṇmadhyamabahuvacanaṃ tha | tasthasthamipāṃ | pā0 3-4-101 | iti tādeśaḥ | vyatyayena śap | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoriti guṇe prāpte kṅiti ceti pratiṣedhaḥ | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti dīrghaḥ | havaṃ | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | bhāve 'nupasargasya | pā0 3-3-75 | ityap | saṃprasāraṇaṃ parapūrvatvaṃ guṇāvādeśau | pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | dhātusvaraḥ śiṣyate ||

Page 172 — Rik 8: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

Translation: "O devāsaḥ, gods, in the form of Indra and the Maruts, viśve, all of you, śruta, hear, mama havam, my call. Of what kind are you? Indrajyeṣṭhāḥ: those among whom Indra is the eldest, the chief; such ones, marudgaṇāḥ, in the form of the host of Maruts; pūṣarātayaḥ: Indra and the Maruts, whose rāti, giver, is the god called Pūṣan." (Grammatical tail: indrajyeṣṭhāḥ, the vocative initial udātta; not unaccented as it begins the pāda; marudgaṇāḥ, not unaccented because the preceding is treated as not there by vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣavacane bahuvacanam (Pā. 8-1-74); devāsaḥ, pūṣarātayaḥ, as before; śruta, śru śravaṇe, tha of loṭ second person plural, the substitute ta by tasthasthamipām… (Pā. 3-4-101); śap by vyatyaya, dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; the guṇa due by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ is barred by kṅiti ca; lengthening by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ; havam, hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca, ap by bhāve 'nupasargasya (Pā. 3-3-75); saṃprasāraṇa, the preceding form, guṇa and av; unaccented as pit; the root accent remains.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

इन्द्रज्येष्ठाः (indrajyeṣṭhāḥ) — having Indra as chief | मरुद्गणाः (marudgaṇāḥ) — joined with the host of Marut deities | पूषरातयः (pūṣarātayaḥ) — accompanied by the deity Pūṣan, the giver of wealth | विश्वे देवासः (viśve devāsaḥ) — O all deities (you) | मम (mama) — my | हवं (havaṃ) — call | श्रुत (śruta) — hear.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O all deities, you are accompanied by Indra, the chief among the deities, and by the Marut deities, and by the deity called Pūṣan who gives wealth. Such as you are, hear the call that I make.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Gods with the divine hosts of Maruts with Indra at your head among whom Pusha is most liberal, hear all of you this my call.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

इन्द्रज्येष्ठाः (indrajyeṣṭhāḥ) — jyeṣṭhaśabdaḥ pradhānavacanaḥ | indraḥ pradhānabhūto yeṣāṃ te indrajyeṣṭhāḥ || Jyeṣṭha means chief, principal. So indrajyeṣṭhāḥ means those who have Indra as chief, as principal: "Indra at their heads". That is, Indra is the leader of the gods ("leader"): it means the gods who set out with him in front.

Page 173 — Rik 8: Special Topics (end), grammar

पूषरातयः (pūṣarātayaḥ) — pūṣākhyo devo rātir dātā yeṣāṃ te pūṣarātayaḥ || Rāti means giver, giver of wealth: the intention is, accompanied by such a deity called Pūṣan.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

इन्द्रज्येष्ठाः (indrajyeṣṭhāḥ) — this is āmantrita; but since it is at the beginning of the pāda, there is the prohibition anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau (Pā. Sū. 8-1-18), so the total lack of accent by the eighth-book āmantritasya ca (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) does not come. By the sixth-book āmantritasya ca (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198) the initial udātta alone comes.

मरुद्गणाः (marudgaṇāḥ) — this is an āmantrita ending in the plural. Here by vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣavacane (Pā. Sū. 8-1-74) — when an āmantrita ending in the plural that is a qualifier follows, the preceding āmantrita ending in the plural that denotes the thing qualified is optionally treated as not there. (Here the word bahuvacana is not in the sūtra; but since the author of the Mahābhāṣya has supplied it, the stated meaning is to be known as right.) By this sūtra, since the preceding word indrajyeṣṭhāḥ, before the āmantrita marudgaṇāḥ, is treated as not there, marudgaṇāḥ does not become one following a pada. So the total lack of accent of the eighth book does not come.

देवासः, पूषरातयः (devāsaḥ, pūṣarātayaḥ) — both are āmantritas ending in the plural. Here, since devāḥ is at the beginning of the second pāda, the prohibition anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau (Pā. Sū. 8-1-18) comes, and since the preceding words before pūṣarātayaḥ are treated as not there as said before, the total lack of accent of the eighth book does not come. By the sixth-book āmantritasya ca the initial udātta alone comes.

श्रुत (śruta) — the root śru śravaṇe. Loṭ, second person plural, the suffix tha: śru + tha. By loṭo laṅvat (Pā. Sū. 3-4-85) the extension of being like laṅ. By tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101) — in place of a la marked ṅ, tām, tam, ta, am come in order for the four suffixes tas, thas, tha, mip — the substitute ta for tha: śru + ta. By śruvaḥ śṛ ca (Pā. Sū. 3-1-74) — instead of the vikaraṇa śap, the vikaraṇa śnu after the root śru, and the substitute śṛ for the root — the vikaraṇa śnu would be due; but overriding it, śap comes by interchange; for it, by bahulaṃ chandasi, luk. By sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) — when a sārvadhātuka or ārdhadhātuka suffix follows, a stem ending in ik takes guṇa — guṇa would be due for the u of śru;

Page 174 — Rik 8: grammar (end)

but by kṅiti ca (Pā. Sū. 1-1-5) — taking suffixes marked g, k, ṅ as cause, guṇa and vṛddhi do not come — the prohibition comes. Here ta is not by nature git, kit or ṅit. But by sārvadhātukam apit (Pā. Sū. 1-2-4) a sārvadhātuka suffix that is not pit is like ṅit; so the treatment as ṅit comes and it is ṅit. Śruta: now, at the time of the Saṃhitā, by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-3-135) — a two-vowelled word ending in tiṅ and in short a, in a mantra, is lengthened at the time of the Saṃhitā — lengthening.

हवम् (havam) — the root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca. In bhāve 'nupasargasya (Pā. Sū. 3-3-75), from ṛdor ap (Pā. Sū. 3-3-57) ap is carried on, and from hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca… (Pā. Sū. 3-3-72) hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam is carried on. So after the root hveñ without a prefix, in the action sense, the suffix ap and saṃprasāraṇa for hveñ both come: when ap and saṃprasāraṇa come, by saṃprasāraṇāc ca (Pā. Sū. 6-1-108) the preceding form comes, giving hu + a; now by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ, guṇa: ho + a; by eco 'yavāyāvaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-78) the substitute av: it became hava. The suffix ap is pit; so by anudāttau suppitau (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4) — a sup and a pit are both unaccented — after the unaccented, the root accent alone remains. So the a of ha is udātta; when the accusative singular suffix am is attached, by ami pūrvaḥ the preceding form comes and it becomes havam. ॥8॥

hatá vṛtráṃ sudānava índreṇa sáhasā yujā́ | mā́ no duḥśaṃsa īśata ||9|| Bars under ह (हत), वृ, व (दानव), ण and यु; strokes over सु, द्रे and ह (सहसा). Line 2: a stroke over नो, a bar under दुः, a stroke over शं.

हत । वृत्रं । सुऽदानवः । इन्द्रेण । सहसा । युजा ॥ मा । नः । दुःऽशंसः । ईशत ॥९॥

hata | vṛtraṃ | su 'dānavaḥ | indreṇa | sahasā | yujā || mā | naḥ | duḥ 'śaṃsaḥ | īśata ||9||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The Uṇādi number is printed उ० ३-३२. Printed नोऽस्मान्प्रति मेशत, as printed.

हे सुदानवः शोभनदानयुक्ता मरुद्गणाः सहसा बलवता युजा योग्येनेन्द्रेण सह वृत्रं शत्रुं हत । नाशयत । दुःशंसो दुष्टेन शंसनेन कीर्तनेन युक्तो वृत्रो नोऽस्मान्प्रति मेशत । समर्थो मा भूत् ॥ हत । हन हिंसागत्योः । लोटस्थ । तस्य त । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । सुदानवः । डुदाञ् दाने । दाभाभ्यां नुः । उ० ३-३२ । इत्यौणादिको नुप्रत्ययः । प्रादिसमास आमन्त्रितनिघातः । युजा । युजिर् योगे । ऋत्विगित्यादिना क्विन् । सावेकाच इति तृतीयैकवचनस्योदात्तत्वं । दुःशंसः । ईषद्दुःसुष्विति खल् । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं । ईशत । ईश ऐश्वर्ये । माङि लुङि प्राप्ते छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति व्यत्ययेन लङ् । तस्य बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुगभावः । न माङ्योग इत्याडागमाभावः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥

he sudānavaḥ śobhanadānayuktā marudgaṇāḥ sahasā balavatā yujā yogyenendreṇa saha vṛtraṃ śatruṃ hata | nāśayata | duḥśaṃso duṣṭena śaṃsanena kīrtanena yukto vṛtro no 'smānprati meśata | samartho mā bhūt || hata | hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ | loṭastha | tasya ta | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | anudāttopadeśetyādinānunāsikalopaḥ | sudānavaḥ | ḍudāñ dāne | dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ | u0 3-32 | ityauṇādiko nupratyayaḥ | prādisamāsa āmantritanighātaḥ | yujā | yujir yoge | ṛtvigityādinā kvin | sāvekāca iti tṛtīyaikavacanasyodāttatvaṃ | duḥśaṃsaḥ | īṣadduḥsuṣviti khal | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvaṃ | īśata | īśa aiśvarye | māṅi luṅi prāpte chandasi luṅlaṅliṭa iti vyatyayena laṅ | tasya bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo lugabhāvaḥ | na māṅyoga ityāḍāgamābhāvaḥ | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "O sudānavaḥ, hosts of Maruts furnished with fine gifts! Hata, destroy, vṛtram, the enemy, together with Indra, sahasā, mighty, yujā, fit [as an ally]. May the duḥśaṃsaḥ, Vṛtra, furnished with evil fame, mā īśata, not have power, naḥ, over us: may he not be able." (Grammatical tail: hata, hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ, tha of loṭ, ta for it, śap dropped by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ, the nasal dropped by anudāttopadeśa…; sudānavaḥ, ḍudāñ dāne, the Uṇādi suffix nu by dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ (U. 3-32); a prādi compound; the vocative loss of accent; yujā, yujir yoge, kvin by ṛtvig…, the instrumental singular udātta by sāv ekācaḥ; duḥśaṃsaḥ, khal by īṣadduḥsuṣu…, the syllable before the suffix udātta by liti; īśata, īśa aiśvarye: with māṅ, luṅ being due, laṅ by vyatyaya under chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ; for it no dropping of śap by bahulaṃ chandasi; no augment aṭ by na māṅyoge; loss of accent by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) सुदानवः ((he) sudānavaḥ) — O Marut deities who give excellent wealth and the like (you) | सहसा (sahasā) — strong | युजा (yujā) — fit (that is, your companion) | इन्द्रेण (indreṇa) — together with Indra | वृत्रं (vṛtraṃ) — the demon Vṛtra (or the enemy) | हत (hata) — destroy | दुःशंसः (duḥśaṃsaḥ) — that Vṛtra, known as wicked | नः (naḥ) — us | मा ईशत (mā īśata) — may he not trouble.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O all you hosts of Maruts who give wealth and the like, together with Indra, who is strong and your companion, slay the demon Vṛtra. May that Vṛtra, known as wicked, not cause us trouble.

॥ English Translation ॥

O liberal gods, aided by your powerful friend, Indra, destroy Vritra, let not the wicked one prevail against us.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

सुदानवः (sudānavaḥ) — ḍudāñ dāne | śobhanadānayuktāḥ || that is, the deities who give excellent things: "liberal doners" [sic].

सहसा (sahasā) — sahaḥ means strength, power. This word is in the instrumental singular.

Page 176 — Rik 9: Special Topics (end), grammar

युजा (yujā) — yujir yoge | being together, fit.

दुःशंसः (duḥśaṃsaḥ) — duṣṭena śaṃsanena yuktaḥ | one blamed with evil words, one known as wicked, one of wicked nature.

ईशत (īśata) — īśa aiśvarye | mā īśata means: may he not hold power over us, may he not trouble us: this is the intention.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

हत (hata) — the root hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ. Loṭ, second person plural, the suffix tha: han + tha; by loṭo laṅvat (Pā. Sū. 3-4-85) treated like laṅ; by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101) the substitute ta: han + ta; by kartari śap (Pā. Sū. 3-1-68) the vikaraṇa śap; for it, by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72), luk. Now by anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37) — when a jhal-initial suffix that is kit or ṅit follows, the final nasal of roots taught unaccented and ending in a nasal, of the tanoty-ādi roots ending in a nasal, and of the root van is dropped — the n is dropped. Han is included in the kārikā that counts the roots taught unaccented, manyahannāpkṣipchupitaptipastipyatidṛpyatī; so it is taught unaccented.

मन्यहन्नाप्क्षिप्छुपितप्तिपस्तिप्यतिदृप्यती ।

manyahannāpkṣipchupitaptipastipyatidṛpyatī |

सुदानवः (sudānavaḥ) — the root ḍudāñ dāne. By dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ (U. Sū. 3-312, read at zoom: the last glyph is the round-headed 2) — after the roots ḍudāñ dāne and bhā dīptau, the suffix nu — when the suffix nu comes after the root dā, it becomes dānu. With the word su, by kugatiprādayaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-2-18), the prādi compound; since it follows a pada, and since it is not at the beginning of a pāda, by the eighth-book sūtra āmantritasya ca (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) it is wholly unaccented.

युजा (yujā) — the root yujir yoge. By ṛtvigdadhṛksragdiguṣṇigañcuyujikruñcāṃ ca (3-2-59) — when ṛtu is upapada, after the root yaj, and after dhṛṣ, sṛj, diś, ut-prefixed snih, añc, yuj, kruñc, the suffix kvin comes; some special operations too are given as set forms. When kvin comes after the root dhṛṣ, reduplication and final udātta are given as set forms: it becomes dadhṛk. When kvin in the object sense comes after sṛj, the augment am is given as a set form: it becomes srak. After snih with ut, the dropping of the final letter of the prefix and ṣ for s are given as set forms. After the root yuj —

Page 177 — Rik 9: grammar (end)

— kvin comes by the sūtra stated before. All the letters of kvin are dropped in turn. After it the instrumental singular suffix ṭā: yuj + ā. By sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168) — when the locative plural su follows, after a word that has a single vowel, the case-ending of the third onward is udātta — that case-ending is udātta.

दुःशंसः (duḥśaṃsaḥ) — by īṣadduḥsuṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal (Pā. Sū. 3-3-126) — when dus in the sense of difficulty, or īṣat, su in the sense of ease, are upapada, the suffix khal comes after roots in the action and object senses — khal comes after the root śaṃsu stutau with the prefix dus: dus + śaṃs + a: it becomes duśśaṃsa. By liti (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the vowel before the suffix is udātta.

ईशत (īśata) — īśa aiśvarye. Since there is connection with māṅ, as in mā no duḥśaṃsa īśata, by māṅi luṅ (Pā. Sū. 3-3-175) — when māṅ is used, luṅ comes after the root — luṅ would be due. But by chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-6) — when a connection of the meanings of two roots is shown, luṅ, laṅ, liṭ come at all times — by interchange laṅ comes. Middle voice, third person singular: īś + ta, śap; though luk would be due by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72), by bahulaṃ chandasi the śap is not dropped. When the augment aṭ would be due by luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-4-71), by na māṅyoge (Pā. Sū. 6-4-74) — with māṅ, the augments aṭ, āṭ do not come — the prohibition comes: it becomes īśata. By tiṅṅatiṅaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) — a word ending in tiṅ after a word not ending in tiṅ is unaccented — it becomes wholly unaccented. ॥9॥ An ornament follows.

Page 177 (lower) — Sūkta 23, Rik 10

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वा॑न्दे॒वान्ह॑वामहे म॒रुतः॒ सोम॑पीतये । [accent ?] उ॒ग्रा हि पृश्नि॑मातरः ॥१०॥

víśvān devā́n havāmahe marútaḥ sómapītaye | [accent ?] ugrā́ hi pṛ́śnimātaraḥ ||10|| Strokes over श्वा, over the syllable with ह after देवान् (read as over ह [accent ?]) and over म (सोम); bars under दे, म (मरुतः) and तः. Line 2: a bar under उ, a stroke over श्नि.

Page 178 — Rik 10: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वान् । देवान् । हवामहे । मरुतः । सोमऽपीतये ॥ उग्राः । हि । पृश्निऽमातरः ॥१०॥

viśvān | devān | havāmahe | marutaḥ | soma 'pītaye || ugrāḥ | hi | pṛśni 'mātaraḥ ||10||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Numbers as printed: ऋग्वे० ५-५८-५, उ० ४-५२. The bhāṣya ends with ॥९॥, the close of the ninth varga.

मरुतो मरुत्संज्ञकान्विश्वान्सर्वान्देवान्सोमपीतये हवामहे । सोमपानार्थमाह्वयामः । ते च मरुत उग्राः शत्रुभिरसह्यबलाः पृश्निमातरः पृश्नेर्नानावर्णयुक्ताया भूमेः पुत्राः । हिशब्दः प्रसिद्ध्यर्थः । सा च प्रसिद्धिः पृश्नेः पुत्राः । ऋग्वे० ५-५८-५ । इति मन्त्रान्तरादवगन्तव्या ॥ पृश्निमातरः । पृश्निर्माता येषां ते । पृश्निशब्दो घृणिः पृश्निरित्यणादावाद्युदात्तो निपातितः । उ० ४-५२ । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥९॥

maruto marutsaṃjñakānviśvānsarvāndevānsomapītaye havāmahe | somapānārthamāhvayāmaḥ | te ca maruta ugrāḥ śatrubhirasahyabalāḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ pṛśnernānāvarṇayuktāyā bhūmeḥ putrāḥ | hiśabdaḥ prasiddhyarthaḥ | sā ca prasiddhiḥ pṛśneḥ putrāḥ | ṛgve0 5-58-5 | iti mantrāntarādavagantavyā || pṛśnimātaraḥ | pṛśnirmātā yeṣāṃ te | pṛśniśabdo ghṛṇiḥ pṛśnirityaṇādāvādyudātto nipātitaḥ | u0 4-52 | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||9||

Translation: "We havāmahe, call, somapītaye, to drink soma — call for drinking soma — viśvān devān, all the gods named marutaḥ, Maruts. And those Maruts are ugrāḥ, of strength not to be borne by enemies, pṛśnimātaraḥ, sons of pṛśni, the earth furnished with many colours. The word hi is for what is well known; and that renown — 'sons of Pṛśni' (Ṛgve. 5-58-5) — is to be learnt from another mantra." (Grammatical tail: pṛśnimātaraḥ, 'whose mother is Pṛśni'; the word pṛśni is given as a set form with initial udātta in the Uṇādi list beginning ghṛṇiḥ pṛśniḥ (U. 4-52); in the bahuvrīhi the first member's own accent.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

मरुतः (marutaḥ) — the Marut deities (and) | विश्वान् देवान् (viśvān devān) — all the deities | सोमपीतये (somapītaye) — for drinking soma | हवामहे (havāmahe) — we call | (those Marut deities) उग्राः (ugrāḥ) — who cannot be subdued by enemies | पृश्निमातरः (pṛśnimātaraḥ) — sons of the earth furnished with many colours | हि (hi) — well known.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

We call the Marut deities and all other deities to drink soma. Those Marut deities, being of great valour, cannot be defeated by enemies. They are sons of the earth furnished with many colours. This matter is well known.

॥ English Translation ॥

We invoke all the divine gods and the Maruts who are mighty and are the Sons of many coloured earth, to drink the Soma juice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

उग्राः (ugrāḥ) — cruel, "fierce": that is, of great valour when fighting with enemies; therefore unconquerable by enemies.

Page 179 — Rik 10: Special Topics (continued)

पृश्निमातरः (pṛśnimātaraḥ) — the commentator has given this word the meaning "sons of the earth furnished with many colours". And, as an example, giving the ṛk —

पृश्नेः पुत्रा उपमासो रभिष्ठाः स्वया मत्या मरुतः सं मिमिक्षुः ॥ (ऋ० सं० ५-५८-५)

pṛśneḥ putrā upamāso rabhiṣṭhāḥ svayā matyā marutaḥ saṃ mimikṣuḥ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 5-58-5)

— when explaining that ṛk he has explained the words pṛśneḥ putrāḥ as gorūpāyā antarikṣasya vā putrasthānīyāḥ, that is, sons of the earth in the form of a cow, or of the mid-air. Skandasvāmin says —

पृश्निरिति द्युनाम । द्यौर्माता येषां मरुतां ते पृश्निमातरः । दिवः पुत्रा इत्यर्थः ॥

pṛśniriti dyunāma | dyaurmātā yeṣāṃ marutāṃ te pṛśnimātaraḥ | divaḥ putrā ityarthaḥ ||

— that pṛśni is heaven, and they are sons of the mid-air. Since the movement of the Maruts is in the mid-air itself, it is fitting to say they are born from it. Yāska has explained this word thus —

स्वः । पृश्निः । नाकः । गौः । विष्टप् । नभ इति षट् साधारणानि ॥ साधारणान्युत्तराणि दिवश्चादित्यस्य ॥ (नि० २-१३)

svaḥ | pṛśniḥ | nākaḥ | gauḥ | viṣṭap | nabha iti ṣaṭ sādhāraṇāni || sādhāraṇānyuttarāṇi divaścādityasya || (ni0 2-13)

— that is, the six words svaḥ, pṛśniḥ, nākaḥ, gauḥ, viṣṭap, nabhaḥ are common words denoting both heaven (divaḥ) and the sun. And —

पृश्निरादित्यो भवति । प्राश्नुत एनं वर्ण इति नैरुक्ताः संस्प्रष्टा रसान् । संस्प्रष्टा भासं ज्योतिषां ॥ संस्पृष्टो भासेति वा ॥ अथ द्यौः संस्पृष्टा ज्योतिर्भिः पुण्यकृद्भिश्च ॥ (नि० २-१४)

pṛśnirādityo bhavati | prāśnuta enaṃ varṇa iti nairuktāḥ saṃspraṣṭā rasān | saṃspraṣṭā bhāsaṃ jyotiṣāṃ || saṃspṛṣṭo bhāseti vā || atha dyauḥ saṃspṛṣṭā jyotirbhiḥ puṇyakṛdbhiśca || (ni0 2-14)

Pṛśni means the sun. Because excellent radiance pervades him all round, the etymologists (the authors of the Nirukta) say that pṛśni means the sun. Saṃspraṣṭā rasān means: sa hi nityakālam eva rasānāṃ saṃspraṣṭā bhavati | athāsya karma rasādānam | — because he is the cause of giving water, the essence, in the form of rain, the sun is named pṛśni. Or saṃspraṣṭā bhāsaṃ jyotiṣām — the light of the planets, stars, moon and the rest becomes dim through the surpassing light of the sun. Or saṃspṛṣṭo bhāseti vā — because he pervades everywhere with his radiance, pṛśni means the sun.

स हि नित्यकालमेव रसानां संस्प्रष्टा भवति । अथास्य कर्म रसादानम् ।

sa hi nityakālameva rasānāṃ saṃspraṣṭā bhavati | athāsya karma rasādānam |

Further, pṛśni means dyauḥ. For saṃspṛṣṭā jyotirbhiḥ puṇyakṛdbhiś ca — because it is joined with light and with the doers of merit, pṛśni means dyauḥ (heaven).

Page 180 — Rik 10: Special Topics (end)

This is Yāska's explanation; so it is fitting to accept the meaning that pṛśni is dyauḥ, heaven, the mid-air, and to say of the word pṛśnimātaraḥ that it means divas putrāḥ, those born in the mid-air.

यद्यूयं पृश्निमातरो मर्तासः स्यातन ॥ (ऋ० सं० १-३८-४)

yadyūyaṃ pṛśnimātaro martāsaḥ syātana || (ṛ0 saṃ0 1-38-4)

When explaining the meaning of this ṛk, he has explained the word pṛśnimātaraḥ as pṛśnināmakadhenuputrā marutaḥ (the Maruts, sons of the cow named Pṛśni). On many occasions of praising the Marut deities the use of the word pṛśnimātaraḥ is seen in particular. So it can be freely said that a definite meaning of this word was current. We have given below the ṛks of the Ṛgveda in which this word is used —

पृश्निनामकधेनुपुत्रा मरुतः ।

pṛśnināmakadhenuputrā marutaḥ |

यद्यूयं पृश्निमातरो मर्तासः स्यातन ॥ (ऋ० सं० १-३८-४) अर्चन्तो अर्कं जनयन्त इन्द्रियमधि श्रियो दधिरे पृश्निमातरः ॥ (ऋ० सं० १-८५-२) पृषदश्वा मरुतः पृश्निमातरः शुभंयावानो विदथेषु जग्मयः ॥ (ऋ० सं० १-८९-७) सुजातासो जनुषा पृश्निमातरो दिवो मर्या आ नो अच्छा जिगातन ॥ (ऋ० सं० ५-५९-६) उदीरयन्त वायुभिर्वाश्रासः पृश्निमातरः ॥ (ऋ० सं० ८-७-३) उदु स्वानेभिरीरत उद्रथैरुदु वायुभिः । उत्स्तोमैः पृश्निमातरः ॥ (ऋ० सं० ८-७-१७) अभीमृतस्य विष्टपं दुहते पृश्निमातरः ॥ (ऋ० सं० ९-३४-५) स्वश्वाः स्थ सुरथाः पृश्निमातरः स्वायुधा मरुतो याथना शुभं ॥ (ऋ० सं० ५-५७-२) कोपयथ पृथिवीं पृश्निमातरः शुभे यदुग्राः पृषतीरयुग्ध्वं ॥ (ऋ० सं० ५-५७-३)

yadyūyaṃ pṛśnimātaro martāsaḥ syātana || (ṛ0 saṃ0 1-38-4) arcanto arkaṃ janayanta indriyamadhi śriyo dadhire pṛśnimātaraḥ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 1-85-2) pṛṣadaśvā marutaḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ śubhaṃyāvāno vidatheṣu jagmayaḥ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 1-89-7) sujātāso januṣā pṛśnimātaro divo maryā ā no acchā jigātana || (ṛ0 saṃ0 5-59-6) udīrayanta vāyubhirvāśrāsaḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 8-7-3) udu svānebhirīrata udrathairudu vāyubhiḥ | utstomaiḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 8-7-17) abhīmṛtasya viṣṭapaṃ duhate pṛśnimātaraḥ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 9-34-5) svaśvāḥ stha surathāḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ svāyudhā maruto yāthanā śubhaṃ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 5-57-2) kopayatha pṛthivīṃ pṛśnimātaraḥ śubhe yadugrāḥ pṛṣatīrayugdhvaṃ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 5-57-3)

Glosses of these quotations are not given in the source. We have given above all the ṛks in which the word pṛśnimātaraḥ is used. Since in these ṛks the word pṛśnimātaraḥ is explained as meaning the Maruts alone, it can freely be said that this word is used in a definite sense only with regard to these deities.

Page 181 (upper) — Rik 10: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

पृश्निमातरः (pṛśnimātaraḥ) — pṛśniḥ mātā yeṣāṃ te: the meaning of the analysis is those whose mother is the earth of many colours. The grammarians give the word pṛśni the meaning 'one of small body'; so by pṛśnir alpatanau (Amarakośa) this is how it results. But the Veda commentator has described the meaning here as the earth with many colours. This form is established from the root spṛśa saṃsparśane. By ghṛṇipṛśnipārṣṇicūrṇibhūrṇi (U. Sū. 4-52) — after ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ, spṛśa saṃsparśane, pṛṣu secane, cara gatau, ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, the suffix ni comes, and some operations and the initial udātta are also given as set forms: this is the sense of the sūtra. In ghṛṇi, when the suffix ni comes after the root ghṛ, the absence of the guṇa that would be due by sārvadhātuka… is given as a set form, and by ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam, ṇ comes for the n: it becomes ghṛṇi. When the suffix ni comes after the root spṛś, the dropping of the s belonging to the root and the absence of guṇa are given as set forms in this sūtra: so it becomes pṛśni. Likewise in pārṣṇi vṛddhi, in cūrṇi the substitute ū for the penultimate of the root, and in bhūrṇi u for the ṛ of the root are given as set forms, and those forms are established: so it is to be known. When the bahuvrīhi compound comes, by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the first member's own accent comes, and pṛśni stays initially udātta. ॥10॥ An ornament follows. The header of p. 181 reads Varga 10.

मरुतां देवानां तन्यतुः शब्दो धृष्णुया धार्ष्ट्ययुक्तः सन्नेति । गच्छति । केषामिव । जयतां विजययुक्तानां शूराणां भटानामिव । हे नरो नेतारो मरुतो यूयं यद्यदा शुभं शोभनं देवयजनं याथन प्राप्नुथ । तदा त्वदीयः शब्दो गच्छतीति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ तन्यतुः । तनु विस्तारे । ऋतन्यञ्जीत्यादिना । उ० ४-२ । यतुच्प्रत्ययः । धृष्णुया । ञिधृषा प्रागल्भ्ये । त्रसिगृधिधृषिक्षिपेः क्नुः । पा० ३-२-१४० । सुपां सुलुगिति सोर्याजादेशः । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । याथन । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति थनादेशः । यच्छब्दयोगान्निघाताभावः ॥

marutāṃ devānāṃ tanyatuḥ śabdo dhṛṣṇuyā dhārṣṭyayuktaḥ sanneti | gacchati | keṣāmiva | jayatāṃ vijayayuktānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ bhaṭānāmiva | he naro netāro maruto yūyaṃ yadyadā śubhaṃ śobhanaṃ devayajanaṃ yāthana prāpnutha | tadā tvadīyaḥ śabdo gacchatīti pūrvatrānvayaḥ || tanyatuḥ | tanu vistāre | ṛtanyañjītyādinā | u0 4-2 | yatucpratyayaḥ | dhṛṣṇuyā | ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye | trasigṛdhidhṛṣikṣipeḥ knuḥ | pā0 3-2-140 | supāṃ sulugiti soryājādeśaḥ | cittvādantodāttaḥ | yāthana | taptanaptanathanāśceti thanādeśaḥ | yacchabdayogānnighātābhāvaḥ ||

Translation: "The tanyatuḥ, sound, of the Maruts, the gods, eti, goes forth, being dhṛṣṇuyā, bold. Like whose? Jayatām iva, like that of victorious heroes, warriors. O naraḥ, leaders, Maruts! Yat, when, you yāthana, reach, śubham, the fine place of worship of the gods, then your sound goes: the construction is with the preceding." (Grammatical tail: tanyatuḥ, tanu vistāre, the suffix yatuc by ṛtanyañji… (U. 4-2); dhṛṣṇuyā, ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye, knu by trasigṛdhidhṛṣikṣipeḥ knuḥ (Pā. 3-2-140), the substitute yāc for su by supāṃ suluk, final udātta as cit; yāthana, the substitute thana by taptanaptanathanāś ca; no loss of accent because of the connection with yad.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे) नरः ((he) naraḥ) — O Marut deities, leaders of men (you) | यत् (yat) — when | शुभं (śubhaṃ) — to the places of good rites such as sacrifice | याथन (yāthana) — you go (then) | मरुतां (marutāṃ) — of the Marut deities | तन्यतुः (tanyatuḥ) — the sound (full of joy) | जयतामिव (jayatām iva) — like the shout of victory of victorious warriors | धृष्णुया (dhṛṣṇuyā) — full of boldness | एति (eti) — comes forth.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Marut deities, leaders, when you go to the sacrifices and other good rites, the shout of joy you make is very deep, like the shout of joy of victorious warriors.

॥ English Translation ॥

Brave Maruts, when you go to the Sacrifice, the shouts of Maruts spreads [sic] with exultation like that of conquerors.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

जयतामिव (jayatām iva) — as warriors who have come back victorious over enemies in battle make a shout of joy marking victory.

तन्यतुः (tanyatuḥ) — for this Yāska has explained tanyatus tanitrī vāco 'nyasyāḥ: making a sound, the speech of another deity. The word tanyatuḥ is also read in the Ṛgveda in the ṛks 1-32-13; 1-116-12 (zoom-checked); 5-25-8; 6-6-2; 7-3-6; 9-100-3; 10-65-13 (numbers in small type, as read).

तन्यतुस्तनित्री वाचोऽन्यस्याः ।

tanyatustanitrī vāco 'nyasyāḥ |

धृष्णुया (dhṛṣṇuyā) — full of boldness, deep, very loud.

यत् (yat) — yadā | when.

Page 183 — Rik 11: Special Topics (end), grammar

शुभं (śubhaṃ) — to the good rite, that is, the performance of sacrifice, worship of the gods and the like. Skandasvāmin has given this word the meaning 'the water in the clouds'. Accordingly the intention is that the Marut deities, with roarings such as lightning and thunder, go near the clouds and make rain fall.

याथन (yāthana) — for the sake of the metre the final syllable is long in the Saṃhitā.

नरः (naraḥ) — vocative, first case plural. Netāraḥ: leaders, chiefs.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

तन्यतुः (tanyatuḥ) — the root tanu vistāre. By ṛtanyañjivanyañjyarpimadyatyaṅgikuyukṛśibhyaḥ katnijyatujalijiṣṭujiṣṭhajisansyanithinulyasāsānukaḥ (U. Sū. 4-442, read at zoom; the last glyph is the curled 2) — after these twelve roots, ṛ gatau, tanu vistāre, añjū vyaktyādau, vanu yācane, añjū vyaktyādau, ṛ gatau ending in ṇic, madī harṣe, ata sātatyagamane, agi gatau, ku śabde, yu miśraṇe, kṛśa tanūkaraṇe, the twelve suffixes katnic, yatuc, alic, iṣṭuc, iṣṭhac, isan, syan, ithin, uli, asa, āsa, ānuk come in order — the suffix yatuc comes after the root tan.

धृष्णुया (dhṛṣṇuyā) — the root ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye. After it, by trasigṛdhidhṛṣikṣipeḥ knuḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-2-140) — after trasī udvege, gṛdhu abhikāṅkṣāyām, ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye, kṣipa preraṇe, when the agents are of that habit, that nature, or doers of it well, the suffix knu comes — the suffix knu. In the suffix nu remains. Dhṛṣ + nu; by raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade (Pā. Sū. 8-4-1) ṇ for the n; after dhṛṣṇu the first-case singular suffix su. For it, by supāṃ suluk pūrvasavarṇācchheyāḍāḍyāyājālaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) — in the Veda, in place of the sup endings, suluk, pūrvasavarṇa, ā, āt, śe, yā, ḍā, ḍyā, yāc, āl come according to usage — the substitute yāc comes here; it is cit, so by citaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the final udātta accent comes.

याथन (yāthana) — the root yā prāpaṇe; loṭ, second person plural, the suffix tha. By loṭo laṅvat (Pā. Sū. 3-4-85) treated like laṅ; by tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101) the substitute ta for tha; the vikaraṇa śap; for it, by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72), luk: yā + ta. Now by taptanaptanathanāś ca

Page 184 (upper) — Rik 11: grammar (end)

(Pā. Sū. 7-1-45) — for the ta coming in place of loṭ, one of the substitutes tap, tanap, tana, thana comes according to usage — the substitute thana: it becomes yāthana. Here, though total lack of accent would be due by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28), by yadvṛttān nityam (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66) — a word ending in tiṅ after a word containing yad is not unaccented — the prohibition comes. So total lack of accent does not come. In the Saṃhitā, by anyeṣām api dṛśyate (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137), it becomes yāthanā. ॥11॥

haskārāt | vi 'dyutaḥ | pari | ataḥ | jātāḥ | avantu | naḥ || marutaḥ | mṛḷayantu | naḥ ||12||

हस्काराद्दीप्तिकराद्विद्युतो विशेषेण दीप्यमानादतोऽन्तरिक्षात्परि जाताः सर्वत उत्पन्ना मरुतो नोऽस्मानवन्तु । रक्षन्तु । तथाविधा मरुतो नोऽस्मान्मृळयन्तु । सुखयन्तु ॥ हस्कारात् । हसे हसने । अत्र तु प्रकाशमात्रे वर्तते । अस्मात्संपदादिलक्षणः क्विप् । अस्मिन्नुपपदे डुकृञ् करण इत्यस्मात्कर्मण्यण् । पा० ३-२-१ । इत्यण्प्रत्ययः । तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थेत्यादिना पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते गतिकारकेत्यादिना कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अतः । कृकमीत्यादिना । पा० ८-३-४६ । विसर्जनीयस्य सत्वं ॥

haskārāddīptikarādvidyuto viśeṣeṇa dīpyamānādato 'ntarikṣātpari jātāḥ sarvata utpannā maruto no 'smānavantu | rakṣantu | tathāvidhā maruto no 'smānmṛḷayantu | sukhayantu || haskārāt | hase hasane | atra tu prakāśamātre vartate | asmātsaṃpadādilakṣaṇaḥ kvip | asminnupapade ḍukṛñ karaṇa ityasmātkarmaṇyaṇ | pā0 3-2-1 | ityaṇpratyayaḥ | tatpuruṣe tulyārthetyādinā pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte gatikāraketyādinā kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | ataḥ | kṛkamītyādinā | pā0 8-3-46 | visarjanīyasya satvaṃ ||

Translation: "May the Maruts, pari jātāḥ, born on all sides, ataḥ, from this mid-air, vidyutaḥ, from the lightning shining in a special way, haskārāt, which makes brightness, avantu, protect, naḥ, us. May such Maruts mṛḷayantu, make us happy." (Grammatical tail: haskārāt, hase hasane, here meaning only 'light'; kvip of the sampadādi type after it; with this as upapada, after ḍukṛñ karaṇe, aṇ by karmaṇy aṇ (Pā. 3-2-1); the first-member accent being due by tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…, the kṛt final member's accent by gatikāraka…; ataḥ, s for the visarga by kṛkami… (Pā. 8-3-46).)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हस्कारात् (haskārāt) — making light | विद्युतः (vidyutaḥ) — shining especially | अतः (ataḥ) — from it, that is, from the mid-air | परि (pari) — in the upper part | जाताः (jātāḥ) — born | मरुतः (marutaḥ) — the Marut deities | नः (naḥ) — us | अवन्तु (avantu) — may they protect | (and) नः (naḥ) — for us | मृळयन्तु (mṛḷayantu) — may they make happiness.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

May the Marut deities, born in the upper part of the lightning, which is very bright so as to dazzle in the mid-air, protect us and make happiness for us.

॥ English Translation ॥

May the Maruts born from the lightning in the resplendent region protect us and make us happy.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

हस्कारात् (haskārāt) — hase hasane atra tu prakāśamātre vartate || Though the root has means laughing, the commentator says it is used here in the sense of light. Haḥ + kārāt means: making light. Skandasvāmin explains the word haḥ as a sound marking the cry of distress people use when in trouble, and gives this ṛk the sense: removing the cry of distress of the people, may the cloud make rain fall, protect us and make happiness.

विद्युतः (vidyutaḥ) — viśeṣeṇa dīpyamānāt | shining especially. The meaning 'from the lightning' can also be given to this word.

परि अतः जाताः (pari ataḥ jātāḥ) — the Marut deities born in the upper part of the mid-air, covered by light and lightning, that is, in the mid-air above the earth. Since the movement of the Marut deities is always in the mid-air itself, there may be a custom of saying that the Maruts are born in the mid-air.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

हस्कारात् (haskārāt) — has, light; karoti, makes: so the analysis. The root hase hasane; here the root is in the sense of light, because roots have many meanings. By sampadādibhyaḥ

Page 186 — Rik 12: grammar (end)

kvip (Pā. Sū. 3-3-108, Vā. 9) — after the roots read in the sampadādi class, kvip comes in the action sense — when kvip comes after the root has and all its letters are dropped, only has remains. When the object-word has in the accusative singular is upapada, by karmaṇy aṇ (Pā. Sū. 3-2-1) — when an object-word is upapada, aṇ comes after the root — the suffix aṇ comes after the root kṛ, ḍukṛñ karaṇe: has + kṛ + a. By aco 'ñṇiti (Pā. Sū. 7-11, as printed) vṛddhi ār for the ṛ: it becomes haskāra. This is a tatpuruṣa compound. So by tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) — in a tatpuruṣa compound the seven first members beginning with tulyārthaka (words meaning 'equal') keep their own accent — the own accent of has, ending in the second case, that is, by dhātoḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-162), its being udātta, would be due; overriding it, by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) — in a tatpuruṣa compound, a kṛt-final word after a gati, a kāraka or an upapada keeps its own accent — the last member keeps its own accent; the last member kāra is final udātta by the suffix accent. So after compounding too that own accent stays. By tatropapadaṃ saptamīstham (Pā. Sū. 3-1-92) — in the sūtras under the heading dhātoḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-91), words such as has that express the meaning conveyed by words in the seventh case such as karmaṇi get the name upapada — has has the name upapada. For the s in has + kāra, by sasajuṣo ruḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-66) — the final s of a pada and the word sajuṣ take the substitute ru — the substitute ru; by kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-3-15) — at the end of a pada, visarga comes for an r before a khar letter and for an r at a pause — visarga. Haḥ + kāra: by ataḥ kṛkamikaṃsakumbhapātrakuśākarṇīṣv anavyayasya (Pā. Sū. 8-3-46) — when the seven words kṛ and the rest follow, for a visarga after a that does not belong to an indeclinable, s comes always in a compound; but a visarga in a last member does not get the s — so s for the visarga: haskāra is established. ॥12॥ An ornament follows.

ā́ pūṣañ citrábarhiṣam ā́ghṛṇe dharúṇaṃ diváḥ | ājā naṣṭáṃ yáthā paśúṃ ||13|| [accent ?] Strokes over पू, ब, घृ and णं; bars under चि, ष (बर्हिष), ध and दि. Line 2: strokes over आ (आजा) and था; bars under न and प [accent ?].

ā | pūṣan | citra 'barhiṣaṃ | āghṛṇe | dharuṇaṃ | divaḥ || ā | aja | naṣṭaṃ | yathā | paśuṃ ||13||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The Uṇādi number is printed उ० ३-५८; the sūtra quoted with it is printed अर्जेर्णिलुक्च.

हे पूषन् चित्रबर्हिषं विचित्रैर्दर्भैर्युक्तं धरुणं यागस्य धारकं सोमं दिव आ द्युलोकादाहरेति शेषः । पूषा विशेष्यते । आघृणे आगतदीप्तियुक्त । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । हे अज गमनशील यथा लोके नष्टं पशुं महारण्यादावन्विष्य कश्चिदाहरति तद्वत् ॥ आघृणे । घृ क्षरणदीप्त्योरित्यस्माद्घृणिः पृश्निरिति निप्रत्ययो निपातितः । ऋवर्णाच्चेति वक्तव्यमिति णत्वं । प्रादिसमासः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । धरुणं । धृञ् धारणे । अस्माण्ण्यन्ताद्धातोरर्जेर्णिलुक्च । उ० ३-५८ । इत्युनन्प्रत्ययः । व्यत्ययेन नित्स्वराभावे प्रत्ययस्वरः । दिवः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना षष्ठ्या उदात्तत्वं । अज । अज गतिक्षेपणयोः ॥

he pūṣan citrabarhiṣaṃ vicitrairdarbhairyuktaṃ dharuṇaṃ yāgasya dhārakaṃ somaṃ diva ā dyulokādāhareti śeṣaḥ | pūṣā viśeṣyate | āghṛṇe āgatadīptiyukta | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | he aja gamanaśīla yathā loke naṣṭaṃ paśuṃ mahāraṇyādāvanviṣya kaścidāharati tadvat || āghṛṇe | ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyorityasmādghṛṇiḥ pṛśniriti nipratyayo nipātitaḥ | ṛvarṇācceti vaktavyamiti ṇatvaṃ | prādisamāsaḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | dharuṇaṃ | dhṛñ dhāraṇe | asmāṇṇyantāddhātorarjerṇilukca | u0 3-58 | ityunanpratyayaḥ | vyatyayena nitsvarābhāve pratyayasvaraḥ | divaḥ | ūḍidamityādinā ṣaṣṭhyā udāttatvaṃ | aja | aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ ||

Translation: "O Pūṣan! Bring (ā) from the world of heaven (divaḥ) the soma, citrabarhiṣam, joined with many-coloured darbha grass, dharuṇam, the upholder of the sacrifice: 'bring' is to be supplied. Pūṣan is qualified: āghṛṇe, furnished with brightness that has come. The illustration for it: O aja, moving one! Yathā, as in the world someone, searching in a great forest and the like, brings back naṣṭaṃ paśum, a lost animal — so." (Grammatical tail: āghṛṇe, from ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ, the suffix ni given as a set form in ghṛṇiḥ pṛśniḥ…; ṇ by ṛvarṇāc ceti vaktavyam; a prādi compound; the vocative initial udātta; dharuṇam, dhṛñ dhāraṇe, the suffix unan after it in the causative by the sūtra as printed (U. 3-58); with the nit accent not applying by vyatyaya, the suffix accent; divaḥ, the genitive udātta by ūḍidam…; aja, aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

आघृणे (āghṛṇe) — furnished with light | अज (aja) — of moving nature | पूषन् (pūṣan) — O Pūṣan | चित्रबर्हिषं (citrabarhiṣaṃ) — together with variegated darbha grass | धरुणं (dharuṇaṃ) — the soma, the support of the sacrifice | (as a man) नष्टं (naṣṭaṃ) — lost | पशुं (paśuṃ) — an animal | यथा (yathā) — in the manner in which | आ (harati) — searches and brings (so) | दिवः (divaḥ) — from the world of heaven | आ (hara) — bring and give.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Pūṣan, furnished with light, since you are of moving nature, bring us from the world of heaven the soma, which is joined with variegated darbha grass and is the support of the sacrifice, just as one searches out and brings back an animal lost in the world.

Page 188 — Rik 13: English, Special Topics

॥ English Translation ॥

Resplendent and swift-moving Pushan, bring from heaven the Soma juice with the variegated sacred grass as a man brings back a stray animal.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The meaning of this ṛk is somewhat tangled. The main intention is: O Pūṣan, you are of great brightness and can move fast; so, as one searches out and brings back an animal (a cow, a goat and the like) lost in the world, bring and give us from heaven the soma, joined with variegated darbha grass and the support of the sacrifice.

पूषन् (pūṣan) — since the word pūṣa is read among the twenty-one words denoting the earth, gauḥ, gmā, jmā and the rest, pūṣa also means the earth. Here the word pūṣan is the deity named Pūṣan. Since this deity is well known as one who searches out and brings back lost things, there is such a description in many ṛks. Yāska's explanation of this word —

पूषा । अथ यद्रश्मिपोषं पुष्यति तत्पूषा भवति ॥ (नि० १२-१६)

pūṣā | atha yadraśmipoṣaṃ puṣyati tatpūṣā bhavati || (ni0 12-16)

— is this: because he is full of rays or beams, this deity is named Pūṣā. Since Pūṣā is one of the twelve Ādityas, they say that Pūṣan is a particular form of the sun. For that reason, when describing this deity, they use qualifying words such as furnished with brightness, shining, furnished with light. And Yāska has put ajāḥ pūṣṇaḥ (Ni. 2-2[6 or 9], zoom: second group ends in a hooked glyph) among the ādiṣṭopayojana words. Ādiṣṭopayojana means a qualifying word that sets out a meaning suited to be construed with that particular deity, as is well known in usage. For example harī indrasya, rāsabhāv aśvinoḥ, niyuto vāyoḥ and so on: that is, the word harī (Indra's horses) is used in the Veda only to indicate Indra's horses. Likewise the word rāsabhā is used in the praise of the Aśvin deities and the word niyutaḥ when praising Vāyu. So it is to be known that the word aja is used when praising the deity Pūṣan. In this ṛk too there is the use of the word aja. The commentator has explained it as 'of moving nature'. Since the sun (Pūṣā) moves through the three worlds and sees everything, it is natural to call him 'of moving nature'. To support the meaning of the word pūṣā —

Page 189 — Rik 13: Special Topics (end)

— Yāska has given two ṛks as examples, śukraṃ te anyad yajataṃ te (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-58-1) and pathas-pathaḥ paripatiṃ vacasyā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-49-8).

चित्रबर्हिषं (citrabarhiṣaṃ) — vicitradarbhair yuktam | The commentator says: joined with variegated darbha grass. How the soma is joined with darbha grass is not clear. It may be said so because the soma vessel is usually placed on darbha grass. Skandasvāmin has also given citram the meaning 'worthy of worship'. The author of the Vedārthayatna has given the word citrabarhiṣam the meaning 'joined with variegated feathers' ("feathers"). That soma has feathers seems strange; that meaning is not quite fitting.

आघृणे (āghṛṇe) — since the word ghṛṇaḥ is read among the twelve names of day, vastoḥ, dyauḥ and the rest, ghṛṇaḥ is a name of the day (Ni. 2-21, zoom-checked); because he makes the day, the sun (Pūṣā) is named ghṛṇi. There is the śruti statement ghṛṇiḥ sūrya ādityaḥ (Tai. U.). And since the word ghṛṇiḥ is read among the eleven words jamat and the rest conveying the meaning jvalataḥ (Ni. 2-28, zoom-checked), the word ghṛṇi means 'shining'. This is the meaning the commentator gives here. Since there is the prefix ā with this word, ā samantāt dīptiyuktaḥ: having brightness spreading or scattered all round is the meaning.

घृणिः सूर्य आदित्यः ।

ghṛṇiḥ sūrya ādityaḥ |

धरुणं (dharuṇaṃ) — yāgasya dhārakam | the chief thing that supports the sacrifice, that is, the soma juice: this is the intention.

दिवः (divaḥ) — from the world of heaven. Skandasvāmin has joined the word dharuṇam with the word divaḥ — divaḥ dharuṇam = divaḥ dhartāram — and given the meaning: upholding heaven, nourishing heaven. Since soma juice is well known to be in heaven, the meaning the commentator gives, 'bring and give the soma juice from heaven', is the fitting one. The śruti statement tṛtīyasyām ito divi soma āsīt (Tai. Brā. 3-2-1) supports the point that soma was in heaven.

तृतीयस्यामितो दिवि सोम आसीत् ।

tṛtīyasyāmito divi soma āsīt |

अज (aja) — aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ | since the root aj has the meaning of going, the meaning 'of moving nature' fits here.

नष्टं यथा पशुं (naṣṭaṃ yathā paśuṃ) — as one is glad when a lost animal is found, so we would be glad if the soma in heaven were brought and given to us: to suggest this, the comparison may have been used. The small Nirukta numbers on these pages were zoom-read on Oct 28: 2-2[6/9], 2-21, 2-28.

Page 190 (upper) — Rik 13: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

आघृणे (āghṛṇe) — the root ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ. Ghṛṇipṛśni… (U. Sū. 4-52): its meaning has been set out at ugrā hi pṛśnimātaraḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-10). By this, the suffix ni: ghṛ + ni; by ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam, ṇ for the n; with the prefix ā, by kugatiprādayaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-2-18), the compound; since it is at the beginning of the pāda, the total lack of accent by the eighth-book āmantritasya ca does not come. By the sixth-book āmantritasya ca the initial udātta comes.

धरुणम् (dharuṇam) — the root dhṛñ dhāraṇe. After it the suffix ṇic: dhṛ + i; now by dhārer ṇiluk ca [as printed] (Daśapā. 4) — after the root dhṛñ ending in the suffix ṇic, the suffix unan comes, and the ṇic is dropped (luk) — when the suffix unan and the dropping of ṇi come: dhṛ + una; by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) guṇa ar for the ṛ: dharuna; now by aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi (Pā. Sū. 8-4-2) ṇ for the n: it becomes dharuṇa. Overriding the initial udātta of the suffix laid down by ādyudāttaś ca (Pā. Sū. 3-1-3), since the suffix is nit the initial udātta would be due by ñnity ādir nityam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197); but here, according to the sūtra vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85), the initial udātta of the suffix alone comes and the u becomes udātta.

दिवः (divaḥ) — ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171): here ekācaḥ and antodāttāt are carried on. Ekācaḥ, having nothing to exclude, is not a qualifier of ūṭh; even if it qualifies the whole joined with ūṭh there is no hindrance; in places like praṣṭhauh the ūh formed with ūṭh is meaningful and is obtained. So the case-endings other than sarvanāmasthāna after ūṭh and the rest, which are final udātta and monosyllabic, are udātta; so the genitive ending is udātta. Therefore by anudāttau suppitau the case-ending does not become unaccented.

अज (aja) — formed from the root aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ. ॥13॥ An ornament follows.

Page 190 (lower) — Sūkta 23, Rik 14

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

पू॒षा राजा॑न॒माघृ॑णि॒रप॑गूळ्हं॒ गुहा॑ हि॒तं । अवि॑न्दच्चि॒त्र॑बर्हिषं ॥१४॥ [accent ?]

pūṣā́ rā́jānam ā́ghṛṇir ápagūḷhaṃ gúhā hitáṃ | ávindac citrabarhiṣaṃ ||14|| [accent ?] Bars under पू, न (राजान), णि, ळ्हं and हि; strokes over जा, घृ, प (अप) and हा. Line 2 (p. 191): strokes over वि and त्र (as in the Pada) [accent ?], a bar under च्चि.

Page 191 — Rik 14: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

पूषा । राजानं । आघृणिः । अपऽगूळ्हं । गुहा । हितं ॥ अविन्दत् । चित्रऽबर्हिषं ॥१४॥

pūṣā | rājānaṃ | āghṛṇiḥ | apa 'gūḷhaṃ | guhā | hitaṃ || avindat | citra 'barhiṣaṃ ||14||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Numbers as printed: पा० ८-२-३१, ८-२-४०.

आघृणिः पूषा राजानं सोममविन्दत् । अलभत । कीदृशं । अपगूळ्हमत्यन्तगूढं । तत्र हेतुः । गुहा हितं गुहासदृशे दुर्गमे द्युलोके स्थितं । तथा चित्रबर्हिषं ॥ अपगूळ्हं । गुहू संवरणे । निष्ठेति कर्मणि क्तः । हो ढः । पा० ८-२-३१ । इति ढत्वं । झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः । पा० ८-२-४० । इति धकारः । ष्टुत्वढलोपदीर्घाः । समासे गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । गुहा । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या लुक् । हितं । निष्ठायां दधातेर्हिः ॥

āghṛṇiḥ pūṣā rājānaṃ somamavindat | alabhata | kīdṛśaṃ | apagūḷhamatyantagūḍhaṃ | tatra hetuḥ | guhā hitaṃ guhāsadṛśe durgame dyuloke sthitaṃ | tathā citrabarhiṣaṃ || apagūḷhaṃ | guhū saṃvaraṇe | niṣṭheti karmaṇi ktaḥ | ho ḍhaḥ | pā0 8-2-31 | iti ḍhatvaṃ | jhaṣastathordho 'dhaḥ | pā0 8-2-40 | iti dhakāraḥ | ṣṭutvaḍhalopadīrghāḥ | samāse gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvaṃ | guhā | supāṃ sulugiti saptamyā luk | hitaṃ | niṣṭhāyāṃ dadhāterhiḥ ||

Translation: "Āghṛṇiḥ, the bright Pūṣan, avindat, found, obtained, rājānam, King Soma. Of what kind? Apagūḷham, utterly hidden. The reason for that: guhā hitam, placed in the world of heaven, hard to reach like a cave. And citrabarhiṣam." (Grammatical tail: apagūḷham, guhū saṃvaraṇe, kta in the object sense by niṣṭhā, ḍh by ho ḍhaḥ (Pā. 8-2-31), dh by jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ (Pā. 8-2-40), ṣṭutva, dropping of ḍh and lengthening; in the compound the prefix keeps its own accent by gatir anantaraḥ; guhā, the locative dropped by supāṃ suluk; hitam, hi for dhā by niṣṭhāyāṃ dadhāter hiḥ.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

आघृणिः (āghṛṇiḥ) — furnished with brightness | पूषा (pūṣā) — Pūṣan | अपगूळ्हं (apagūḷhaṃ) — utterly hidden | गुहा (guhā) — in a place hard to reach, like a cave | हितं (hitaṃ) — kept | चित्रबर्हिषं (citrabarhiṣaṃ) — joined with variegated darbha grass | राजानं (rājānaṃ) — the soma juice | अविन्दत् (avindat) — obtained.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The shining Pūṣan brought (for us) the soma juice, joined with variegated darbha grass, which was in a most secret place.

॥ English Translation ॥

The resplendent Pushan found out the Soma (king) although concealed in a secret cave placed upon the sacred grass.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

राजानं (rājānaṃ) — there is a custom of calling soma 'king'. Such usage is seen more in the Yajurveda than in the Ṛgveda.

Page 192 — Rik 14: Special Topics (continued)

सोमं राजानमवसेऽग्निं गीर्भिर्हवामहे ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-१४१-३) सोमस्य राज्ञो वरुणस्य धर्मणि बृहस्पतेरनुमत्या उ शर्मणि ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-१६७-३)

somaṃ rājānamavase 'gniṃ gīrbhirhavāmahe || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-141-3) somasya rājño varuṇasya dharmaṇi bṛhaspateranumatyā u śarmaṇi || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-167-3)

— and there are many such examples. In the first anuvāka of the second chapter of the sixth book of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda (Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-1) there is the explanation that soma is the king and the metres Gāyatrī and the rest are his servants.

अपगूळ्हं (apagūḷhaṃ) — atyantagūḍham | nigūḷham ācchāditam | the meaning is: kept in a most secret place. On this matter Skandasvāmin has told an old legend —

अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । असुराः सोमं राजानं दीयमानमग्नेर्हस्तादपहृत्य गुहायां न्यदधुः । तं पर्येषमाणा अन्ये देवा नाविन्दन् । पूषा त्वविन्दत् ।

atretihāsamācakṣate | asurāḥ somaṃ rājānaṃ dīyamānamagnerhastādapahṛtya guhāyāṃ nyadadhuḥ | taṃ paryeṣamāṇā anye devā nāvindan | pūṣā tvavindat |

— that is: the demons stole the soma from the hand of Agni and kept it in a most secret place, a cave. However much the gods searched for it, they did not find it. Pūṣan alone searched it out and brought it.

गुहा हितं (guhā hitaṃ) — that is, hidden in a hard-to-reach secret place like a cave. Here guhā can be taken to mean a cave or a secret place. In the Ṛgveda and the Upaniṣads too it is customary to indicate a thing kept in a secret place known to no one by the words guhā hitam —

गुहा त्रीणि निहिता नेङ्गयन्ति तुरीयं वाचो मनुष्या वदन्ति ॥ (ऋ० सं० १-१६४-४५) अविन्दद्दिवो निहितं गुहा निधिं वेर्न गर्भं परिवीतमश्मन्यनन्ते अन्तरश्मनि ॥ (ऋ० सं० १-१३०-३) गुहा हितं गुह्यं गूळ्हमप्स्वपीवृतं मायिनं क्षियन्तं ॥ (ऋ० सं० २-११-५) अभिनक्षन्तो अभि ये तमानशुर्निधिं पणीनां परमं गुहा हितं ॥ (ऋ० सं० २-२४-६) तिस्रो महीरुपरास्तस्थुरत्या गुहा द्वे निहिते दर्श्येका ॥ (ऋ० सं० ३-५६-२)

guhā trīṇi nihitā neṅgayanti turīyaṃ vāco manuṣyā vadanti || (ṛ0 saṃ0 1-164-45) avindaddivo nihitaṃ guhā nidhiṃ verna garbhaṃ parivītamaśmanyanante antaraśmani || (ṛ0 saṃ0 1-130-3) guhā hitaṃ guhyaṃ gūḷhamapsvapīvṛtaṃ māyinaṃ kṣiyantaṃ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 2-11-5) abhinakṣanto abhi ye tamānaśurnidhiṃ paṇīnāṃ paramaṃ guhā hitaṃ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 2-24-6) tisro mahīruparāstasthuratyā guhā dve nihite darśyekā || (ṛ0 saṃ0 3-56-2)

प्रवाच्यं वचसः किं मे अस्य गुहा हितमुप निणिग्वदन्ति ॥ (ऋ० सं० ४-५-८) चित्रं सन्तं गुहा हितं सुवेदं कूचिदर्थिनं ॥ (ऋ० सं० ४-७-६) त्वामग्ने अङ्गिरसो गुहा हितमन्वविन्दञ्छिश्रियाणं वनेवने ॥ (ऋ० सं० ५-११-६)
