चित्रबर्हिषं (citrabarhiṣaṃ) — this word is in the previous ṛk too. What the right meaning of this word is is not clear.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

अपगूळ्हम् (apagūḷham) — the prefix apa, the root guhū saṃvaraṇe. After it, by niṣṭhā (Pā. Sū. 3-2-102) — after a root in the past sense, the suffixes kta, ktavatu come — the suffix kta in the object sense: ap + guh + ta. Now by ho ḍhaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-31) — when a jhal letter follows, and at the end of a pada, ḍh is substituted for h — for the h before the jhal letter t, the substitute ḍh: guḍh + ta. By jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-40) — the t and th after a letter in the pratyāhāra jhaṣ not belonging to the root dhā take dh — dh for the t: guḍh + dha; by ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-4-41), by ṣṭutva, ḍh for the dh: guḍh + ḍha. By ḍho ḍhe lopaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-3-13) — a ḍh before a ḍh is dropped — the ḍh is dropped: gu + ḍha. By ḍhralope pūrvasya dīrgho 'ṇaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-3-111) — an aṇ before the ḍh and r that cause the dropping of ḍh and r is lengthened — the u is lengthened: gū + ḍha: it became apagūḍha. Now, according to the tradition of the Bahvṛcas, ajmadhyasthaḍakārasya ḷakāraṃ bahvṛcā jaguḥ | ajmadhyasthaḍhakārasya ḷhakāraṃ vai yathākramam ||, the ḍh between vowels becomes ḷh: it becomes apagūḷham. Apa and gūḷham both form a prādi compound. By gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) — when a word ending in the suffix kta in the object sense follows, the immediately preceding gati keeps its own accent — the accent of apa alone stays. Apa is initially udātta by upasargāś cābhivarjam (Phi. Sū. 82).

अज्मध्यस्थडकारस्य ळकारं बह्वृचा जगुः । अज्मध्यस्थढकारस्य ळ्हकारं वै यथाक्रमम् ॥

ajmadhyasthaḍakārasya ḷakāraṃ bahvṛcā jaguḥ | ajmadhyasthaḍhakārasya ḷhakāraṃ vai yathākramam ||

गुहा (guhā) — for the locative singular suffix after this word, by supāṃ suluk (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) — for the meaning of the sūtra see the eleventh mantra — luk; instead of guhāyām it stays as guhā.

हितं (hitaṃ) — after the root ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, the suffix kta: dhā + ta. By dadhāter hiḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-4-42) — when a t-initial kit suffix follows, the root dhā takes the substitute hi — when hi comes for dhā: hi + ta; the accusative singular suffix am: it becomes hitam. ॥14॥

उतो अपि च स पूषा मह्यं यजमानायेन्दुभिर्यागहेतुभिः सोमैर्युक्तान्षड्वसंतादीनृतूननुसेषिधत् । अनुक्रमेण पुनःपुनर्वर्तयन्वर्तत इति शेषः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । गोभिर्बलीवर्दैर्यवं न चर्कृषत् । नशब्द उपमार्थः । यथा यवमुद्दिश्य भूमिं प्रतिसंवत्सरं पुनःपुनः कृषति तद्वत् ॥ मह्यं । ङयि च । पा० ६-१-२१२ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । इन्दुभिः । उन्दी क्लेदने । उन्देरिच्चादेः । उ० १-१३ । इत्युप्रत्यय उकारस्येकारादेशश्च । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तत्वं । युक्तान् । दीर्घादटि समानपाद इति संहितायां नकारस्य रुत्वं । आतोऽटि नित्यमिति सानुनासिक आकारः । अनुसेषिधत् । षिधु गत्यां । धातोरेकाचः । पा० ३-१-२२ । इति यङ् । यङोऽचि च । पा० २-४-७४ । इति तस्य लुक् । प्रत्ययलक्षणेन सन्यङोः । पा० ६-१-९ । इति द्विर्भावः । हलादिशेषः । गुणो यङ्लुकोः । पा० ७-४-८२ । इत्यभ्यासस्य गुणः । इण्कोः । पा० ८-३-५७ । इति षत्वं । सनादित्वाद्धातुसंज्ञायां लटः शतृ । कर्तरि शप् । अदादिवच्चेति वचनात्तस्य लुक् । नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुः । पा० ७-१-७८ । इति नुम्प्रतिषेधः । प्रत्ययस्वरे प्राप्तेऽभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वं । गोभिः । सावेकाच इति भिस उदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते न गोश्वन्निति प्रतिषेधः । चर्कृषत् । कृष विलेखने । यङ्लुकि द्विर्भावहलादिशेषचर्त्वानि । रुग्रिकौ च लुकि । पा० ७-४-९१ । इत्यभ्यासस्य रुगागमः । अस्माद्यङ्लुगन्ताल्लेटस्तिप् । इतश्च लोपः । लेटोऽडाटावित्यडागमः । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । लघूपधगुणे प्राप्ते नाभ्यस्तस्याचि पिति । पा० ७-३-८७ । इति निषेधः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥१०॥

Page 195 — Rik 15: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

Translation: "Uto, and also, saḥ, that Pūṣan, mahyam, for me, the sacrificer, anuseṣidhat, keeps turning in order again and again — 'keeps turning' is to be supplied — the six seasons, spring and the rest, yuktān, joined indubhiḥ, with somas, the means of the sacrifice. The illustration for it: gobhir yavaṃ na carkṛṣat: the word na is in the sense of comparison: as one, aiming at barley, ploughs the ground again and again every year with bullocks — so." (Grammatical tail: mahyam, initial udātta by ṅayi ca (Pā. 6-1-212); indubhiḥ, undī kledane, the suffix u and i for the initial u by underic cādeḥ (U. 1-13), initial udātta as nit is carried on; yuktān, in the Saṃhitā ru for the n by dīrghād aṭi samānapāde, the nasalised ā by āto 'ṭi nityam; anuseṣidhat, ṣidhu gatyām, yaṅ by dhātor ekācaḥ… (Pā. 3-1-22), dropped by yaṅo 'ci ca (Pā. 2-4-74); by the mark of the suffix, reduplication by sanyaṅoḥ (Pā. 6-1-9), halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, guṇa of the reduplicate by guṇo yaṅlukoḥ (Pā. 7-4-82), ṣ by iṇkoḥ (Pā. 8-3-57); being a root as of the sanādi class, śatṛ for laṭ, śap, dropped by the statement adādivac ca; num barred by nābhyastāc chatuḥ (Pā. 7-1-78); the suffix accent being due, initial udātta by abhyastānām ādiḥ; gobhiḥ, the udātta of bhis due by sāv ekācaḥ is barred by na gośvan…; carkṛṣat, kṛṣa vilekhane, in yaṅluk reduplication, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ and cartva; the augment ruk for the reduplicate by rugrikau ca luki (Pā. 7-4-91); after this yaṅluk stem, tip for leṭ, i dropped by itaś ca lopaḥ, the augment aṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau, śap dropped by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ; the guṇa of the light penultimate is barred by nābhyastasyāci piti (Pā. 7-3-87); loss of accent by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

उतो (uto) — and | सः (saḥ) — that Pūṣan | मह्यं (mahyaṃ) — for me who am performing the sacrifice | इन्दुभिः (indubhiḥ) — with the soma juices, the chief things in the sacrifice | युक्तान् (yuktān) — joined | षट् (ṣaṭ) — the six seasons, spring and the rest | (as a farmer) गोभिः (gobhiḥ) — with bullocks | यवं (yavaṃ) — to obtain the grain called yava (wheat [as printed], barley) | न चर्कृषत् (na carkṛṣat) — as he ploughs the ground again and again | अनुसेषिधत् (anuseṣidhat) — may he carry them on in an order of turning, one after the other.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

As the farmer ploughs the ground again and again, that is, many times, with bullocks to grow the grain called yava, so may that Pūṣan make the six seasons, joined with the soma juices that accomplish the sacrifice, go on in an order of turning, one after the other.

॥ English Translation ॥

And he has brought to me successively the six (seasons) connected with the drops of the Soma juice as a man repeatedly ploughs a field with bullocks for the sake of barley.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The meaning of this ṛk does not fit very well. The comparison too is not good. The intention of this ṛk may be: as the farmer ploughs the ground again and again to grow the grain yava, so may he make the seasons, spring and the rest, and the soma sacrifices we perform in those seasons, come again and again. Since the seasons, spring and the rest, come every year, it came about many times. To grow grain the ground must be ploughed many times. So, to suggest the meaning 'many times', —

Page 196 — Rik 15: Special Topics (end), grammar

— this comparison may have been given. In this ṛk there is only the word ṣaṭ. The commentator has explained ṣaṭ as the six seasons.

इन्दुभिः (indubhiḥ) — with drops of soma juice: since, when soma juice is pressed with a creeper, it falls drop by drop, it is customary to speak of soma juice by words for drops (indavaḥ, indubhiḥ and the like).

गोभिः (gobhiḥ) — though gobhiḥ means 'with cows', the commentator and Skandasvāmin both hold that here gobhiḥ must be given the meaning 'with bullocks', the means for the work of farming.

न (na) — this word is used here in the sense of comparison.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

मह्यं (mahyaṃ) — after the word asmad, the dative singular suffix ṅe: asmad + ṅe. Now by tubhyamahyau ṅayi (Pā. Sū. 7-2-95) — when the suffix ṅe follows, the part up to m of the words yuṣmad, asmad, that is yuṣm, asm, take the substitutes tubhya, mahya in order — the substitute mahya for asm: mahya + ad + ṅe; by ato guṇe (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) the following form: mahyad + ṅe; by ṅe prathamayor am (Pā. Sū. 7-1-28) the substitute am for ṅe: mahyad + am; by śeṣe lopaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-2-90) the ad is dropped. On the view that śeṣe lopaḥ applies to the final letter, when the d is dropped, by ami pūrvaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-107) the preceding form: it becomes mahyam. On the view of dropping the final, the single substitute arising by the preceding form would have to be udātta by ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-5): that is, in mahyam the final a would turn out udātta. On the view of dropping the ṭi, by the accent of the loss of the udātta, anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-161), the case-ending would have to be udātta. If so, by ṅayi ca (Pā. Sū. 6-1-212) — when the suffix ṅe follows, the beginning of the words yuṣmad, asmad is udātta — the initial udātta accent comes.

इन्दुभिः (indubhiḥ) — the root undī kledane. By underic cādeḥ (U. Sū. 1-13), after the root und, the suffix u and the substitute i for the first u: so the suffix u. With i for the u it becomes indu. By dhānye nit (U. Sū. 1-9), nit is carried on into this sūtra. So since the suffix is nit, and by ñnity ādir nityam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197), this is initially udātta.

युक्तान् (yuktān) — yuktān, ending in the accusative plural, + anu: for these, at the time of the Saṃhitā, by dīrghād aṭi samānapāde (Pā. Sū. 8-3-9) — if the n and a letter of the pratyāhāra aṭ are in one and the same pāda,

Page 197 — Rik 15: grammar (continued)

— the n before the aṭ letter, when it follows a long vowel, takes the substitute ru — so the substitute ru for the n: yuktār + anu. Now by āto 'ṭi nityam (Pā. Sū. 8-3-3) — the long ā before the ru that is before an aṭ letter always becomes nasal — the ā becomes nasal: yuktā̃r + anu; by bhobhagoaghoapūrvasya yo 'śi (Pā. Sū. 8-3-17) y for the r; by lopaḥ śākalyasya (Pā. Sū. 8-3-19) the y is dropped; by pūrvatrāsiddham (Pā. Sū. 8-2-1), when making the lengthening of like vowels, the dropping of y is asiddha. So the lengthening of like vowels does not come.

अनुसेषिधत् (anuseṣidhat) — the root ṣidhu gatyām. By dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-22) — when repetition or intensity is shown, yaṅ comes after a root that is monosyllabic and begins with a consonant — yaṅ: ṣidh + ya; by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) s for ṣ: sidh + ya. By yaṅo 'ci ca (Pā. Sū. 2-4-74) — yaṅ is dropped (luk) when a vowel-initial suffix follows, and even when none follows — yaṅ is dropped (luk): it stays as sidh. Though yaṅ is thus dropped, by pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam (Pā. Sū. 1-1-62) — though a suffix is dropped, an operation caused by the suffix comes — whatever operation would come if yaṅ were there comes now too. But here the dropping has come by pronouncing the word luk. So it may be said that by na lumatāṅgasya (Pā. Sū. 1-1-63) the mark of the suffix should be barred. The sense of the sūtra na lumatāṅgasya: in places where the dropping has come by pronouncing luk, ślu, lup, words containing lu, an operation aimed at the stem caused by the dropped suffix does not come, whether laid down under the aṅga heading or not. The present reduplication comes to what ends in yaṅ; so it is not an operation aimed at the stem. Therefore this prohibition does not come here. By sanyaṅoḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-9) — the first monosyllabic part of a root ending in san or yaṅ is reduplicated, and if the root begins with a vowel, the second monosyllabic part — with the reduplication: sidh + sidh. By halādiḥ śeṣaḥ (7-4-60) — the first consonant of the reduplicate remains, the other consonants of the reduplicate are dropped — the dh is dropped: si + sidh. By guṇo yaṅlukoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-4-82) — in yaṅ and in yaṅluk the reduplicate takes guṇa — guṇa for si, e for the i: sesidh. By iṇkoḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-3-57) the cerebral substitute (ṣatva) for an s after the letters of the pratyāhāra iṇ: so the s after se becomes ṣ: seṣidh.

सन्क्यच्काम्यच्क्यष्क्यङोऽथाचारक्विब्णिज्यङौ तथा । यगाय ईयङ् णिङ् चेति द्वादशामी सनादयः ॥

sankyackāmyackyaṣkyaṅo 'thācārakvibṇijyaṅau tathā | yagāya īyaṅ ṇiṅ ceti dvādaśāmī sanādayaḥ ||

— so they count the sanādi suffixes. Thus what ends in yaṅ ends in a sanādi suffix. And so by sanā-

Page 198 — Rik 15: grammar (continued)

dyantā dhātavaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-32) — what ends in the sanādi suffixes gets the name dhātu — seṣidh gets the name dhātu. Thus when śatṛ comes for the suffix laṭ by laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe (Pā. Sū. 3-2-124): seṣidh + at. By kartari śap (Pā. Sū. 3-1-68) the vikaraṇa śap. Carkarītaṃ parasmaipadam adādivac ca draṣṭavyam (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-8-4 [as printed]): carkarīta is the name for what ends in yaṅluk; it is only parasmaipada; it is also as if in the adādi class; so what ends in yaṅluk is as if in the adādi class. Therefore by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72) śap is dropped (luk). This very meaning results from the gaṇasūtra carkarītaṃ ca read in the adādi class. Since, having declared atha trayaḥ parasmaipadinaḥ and read the roots ṣasa, ṣasti svapne, vaśa kāntau, this gaṇasūtra comes after them, it results that what ends in yaṅluk is parasmaipada. Since it is read in the adādi class, it is adādi too. So it also results that, after a root of whatever vikaraṇa, if yaṅ is dropped (luk), the vikaraṇa śap alone comes there and it is dropped. When the suffix su is put after seṣidhat, by ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-70) num would be due; for it, by nābhyastāc chatuḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-78) — a śatṛ suffix after a reduplicated stem does not take num — the prohibition comes. By the sixth-book sūtra ubhe abhyastam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-5) — the whole of a word with reduplication gets the name abhyasta — seṣidh has the name abhyasta; when the accent of the śatṛ suffix should remain, by abhyastānām ādiḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189) — when a vowel-initial sārvadhātuka in place of la, without the augment iṭ, follows, the beginning of the abhyasta is udātta — se becomes udātta.

गोभिः (gobhiḥ) — by sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168): su means the locative plural; when the locative plural suffix follows, the case-ending of the third onward after whatever word has a single vowel is udātta; so the udātta accent would be due for the case-ending; but by the sūtra stated next the prohibition comes. Na gośvansāvavarṇarāḍaṅkruṅkṛdbhyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-182): the sense of the sūtra is that the case-ending and the matup after the words go, śvan, words ending in a/ā in the nominative singular, the word rāṭ ending in kvip, the word aṅ formed with kvin after the root añcu, the word kruñ formed with kvin after kruñca gatikauṭilyālpībhāvayoḥ, and the word kṛt formed with kvip after the root kṛñ, do not take the udātta laid down by the sūtras of the sixth book. At cau (Pā. Sū. 6-1-222), introducing the sūtra na gośvan, kasya tarhi? yo 'nena kenacil lakṣaṇena

prāptasya vibhaktisvarasya pratiṣedham | yadi vibhaktisvarasya pratiṣedhaḥ, vṛkṣavān, plakṣavān, atra na prāpnoti | matubgrahaṇam api prakṛtam anuvartate kva prakṛtam? hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup iti — in the Mahābhāṣya it is made clear that this is a prohibition of the accent of matup and of the case-ending, and that it is a prohibition of the general accents of the sixth book. These points are also established by the Kaiyaṭa on this Bhāṣya.

कस्य तर्हि । योऽनेन केनचिल्लक्षणेन प्राप्तस्य विभक्तिस्वरस्य प्रतिषेधम् । यदि विभक्तिस्वरस्य प्रतिषेधः वृक्षवान् प्लक्षवान् अत्र न प्राप्नोति । मतुब्ग्रहणमपि प्रकृतमनुवर्तते क्व प्रकृतम् । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् इति ।

kasya tarhi | yo 'nena kenacillakṣaṇena prāptasya vibhaktisvarasya pratiṣedham | yadi vibhaktisvarasya pratiṣedhaḥ vṛkṣavān plakṣavān atra na prāpnoti | matubgrahaṇamapi prakṛtamanuvartate kva prakṛtam | hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup iti |

चर्कृषत् (carkṛṣat) — the root kṛṣa vilekhane. By dhātor ekācaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-22) yaṅ; for it, by yaṅo 'ci ca (Pā. Sū. 2-4-74), luk; by the mark of the suffix it ends in yaṅ. By sanyaṅoḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-9) reduplication: kṛṣ + kṛṣ. By ur at (Pā. Sū. 7-4-66) — when a suffix follows, the ṛ of the reduplicate takes a — ar for the ṛ; by the mark of the suffix the suffix is to be taken as following. Though yaṅ is dropped (luk), the author of the Śekhara has made clear at the sūtra na lumatāṅgasya that ur at still comes by the mark of the suffix: kar + kṛṣ; by halādiḥ śeṣaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-4-60) the r is removed. By abhyāse carc ca (Pā. Sū. 8-4-54) — the jhal letters of the reduplicate take car and jaś letters — the first k becomes c: cakṛṣ. By rugrikau ca luki (Pā. Sū. 7-4-91) — in yaṅluk, the reduplicate of a root with ṛ as penultimate takes the augments ruk, rik, rīk — the words ṛdupadhasya and rīk from rīg ṛdupadhasya ca (Pā. Sū. 7-4-90) are carried on into the previous sūtra. After carkṛṣ, leṭ by liṅarthe leṭ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-7); for it tip; by itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97) — in the parasmaipada, the i of the tip coming in place of leṭ is dropped — the i is dropped. By leṭo 'ḍāṭau (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94) the augment aṭ: carkṛṣ + at; the vikaraṇa śap; by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72) luk. By pugantalaghūpadhasya ca (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86) — when a sārvadhātuka or ārdhadhātuka suffix follows, the ik vowel of a stem ending in puk or with a light penultimate takes guṇa — guṇa would be due. But by nābhyastasyāci piti sārvadhātuke (Pā. Sū. 7-3-87) — when a vowel-initial sārvadhātuka suffix marked p follows, the guṇa of the light penultimate does not come — the prohibition comes. So guṇa does not come. By tiṅṅatiṅaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) — a word ending in tiṅ after a word not ending in tiṅ is unaccented — the tiṅ-final carkṛṣat, after na, a word not ending in tiṅ, is wholly unaccented. ॥15॥ An ornament follows.

ambáyo yanty ádhvabhir jāmáyo adhvarīyatā́ṃ | pṛñcatī́r mádhunā páyaḥ ||16|| Strokes over यो (अम्बयो), ध्व and यो (जामयो); bars under अ, य (यन्ति), जा and य (अध्वरीयताम्). Line 2: bars under पृ and च, strokes over धु and यः, a bar under ना.

अम्बयः । यन्ति । अध्वऽभिः । जामयः । अध्वरिऽयतां ॥ पृञ्चतीः । मधुना । पयः ॥१६॥

ambayaḥ | yanti | adhva 'bhiḥ | jāmayaḥ | adhvari 'yatāṃ || pṛñcatīḥ | madhunā | payaḥ ||16||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Numbers as printed: आ० ५-१, उ० ४-१३८, उ० ४-११४, म० ७-४-३५, पा० ७-४-३९.

अपोनप्त्रीये एकधनासूपानीतासु स्वयमनुगच्छन्नम्बय इति द्वे अनुब्रूयात् । तृतीययापो देवीरित्यनयैकधनासु हविर्धानं प्रविष्टासु स्वयमनुप्रविशेत् । तथैव सूत्रितं । अम्बयो यन्त्यध्वभिरिति तिस्र उत्तमयानुप्रपद्येत । आ० ५-१ । इति ॥

aponaptrīye ekadhanāsūpānītāsu svayamanugacchannambaya iti dve anubrūyāt | tṛtīyayāpo devīrityanayaikadhanāsu havirdhānaṃ praviṣṭāsu svayamanupraviśet | tathaiva sūtritaṃ | ambayo yantyadhvabhiriti tisra uttamayānuprapadyeta | ā0 5-1 | iti ||

Translation (application): "At the aponaptrīya, when the ekadhanā waters have been brought, going along himself, he should recite the two ṛks ambayaḥ; with the third, āpo devīḥ, when the ekadhanā waters have entered the havirdhāna, he should himself enter after them. So it is laid down: 'ambayo yanty adhvabhiḥ: three; with the last he should go in after' (Āśv. 5-1)."

अध्वरीयतामध्वरमात्मन इच्छतामस्माकमम्बयो मातृस्थानीया आपः । तथा च कौषीतकिब्राह्मणे समाम्नायते । अम्बयो यन्त्यध्वभिरित्यापो वा अम्बय इति । ता आपोऽध्वभिर्देवयजनमार्गैर्यन्ति । गच्छन्ति । कीदृश्य आपः । जामयो हितकारिण्यो बन्धवः । तथा मधुना माधुर्यरसेन युक्तं पयः पृञ्चतीर्गवादिषु योजयन्त्यः ॥ अम्बयः । रबि लबि अबि शब्दे । एतस्मादच इः । उ० ४-१३८ । इति प्रकरणे बाहुलकादिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अध्वभिः । अदेर्ध च । उ० ४-११४ । इति क्वनिप् । पित्त्वात्प्रत्ययस्यानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । जामयः । जमु अदने । बाहुलकादिः । अध्वरीयतां । अध्वरशब्दात्सुप आत्मनः क्यजिति क्यच् । क्यचि चेतीत्वं । अपुत्रादीनामिति वक्तव्यं । म० ७-४-३५ । इति वचनान्न छन्दस्यपुत्रस्येतीत्वनिषेधाभावः । सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति कव्यध्वरपृतनस्य । पा० ७-४-३९ । इत्यकारलोपोऽपि न भवति । क्यच्प्रत्ययान्तधातोर्लटः शतृ । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण तयोः क्यचा सहैकादेशः । एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वे सति शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इति षष्ठ्या उदात्तत्वं । पृञ्चतीः । पृची संपर्के । लटः शतृ । रुधादिभ्यः श्नम् । श्नसोरल्लोपः । अनुस्वारपरसवर्णौ । उगितश्चेति ङीप् । वा छन्दसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वं । शतुरनुम इति ङीप उदात्तत्वं ॥

adhvarīyatāmadhvaramātmana icchatāmasmākamambayo mātṛsthānīyā āpaḥ | tathā ca kauṣītakibrāhmaṇe samāmnāyate | ambayo yantyadhvabhirityāpo vā ambaya iti | tā āpo 'dhvabhirdevayajanamārgairyanti | gacchanti | kīdṛśya āpaḥ | jāmayo hitakāriṇyo bandhavaḥ | tathā madhunā mādhuryarasena yuktaṃ payaḥ pṛñcatīrgavādiṣu yojayantyaḥ || ambayaḥ | rabi labi abi śabde | etasmādaca iḥ | u0 4-138 | iti prakaraṇe bāhulakādiḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | adhvabhiḥ | aderdha ca | u0 4-114 | iti kvanip | pittvātpratyayasyānudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ | jāmayaḥ | jamu adane | bāhulakādiḥ | adhvarīyatāṃ | adhvaraśabdātsupa ātmanaḥ kyajiti kyac | kyaci cetītvaṃ | aputrādīnāmiti vaktavyaṃ | ma0 7-4-35 | iti vacanānna chandasyaputrasyetītvaniṣedhābhāvaḥ | sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyanta iti kavyadhvarapṛtanasya | pā0 7-4-39 | ityakāralopo 'pi na bhavati | kyacpratyayāntadhātorlaṭaḥ śatṛ | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | śatuśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa tayoḥ kyacā sahaikādeśaḥ | ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityantodāttatve sati śaturanumo nadyajādī iti ṣaṣṭhyā udāttatvaṃ | pṛñcatīḥ | pṛcī saṃparke | laṭaḥ śatṛ | rudhādibhyaḥ śnam | śnasorallopaḥ | anusvāraparasavarṇau | ugitaśceti ṅīp | vā chandasīti pūrvasavarṇadīrghatvaṃ | śaturanuma iti ṅīpa udāttatvaṃ ||

Translation: "Of us, adhvarīyatām, who wish the sacrifice for ourselves, the ambayaḥ, mother-like waters — so it is recorded in the Kauṣītaki-brāhmaṇa: 'ambayo yanty adhvabhiḥ: the waters indeed are the ambayaḥ' — those waters yanti, go, adhvabhiḥ, by the paths to the place of worship of the gods. Of what kind are the waters? Jāmayaḥ, kinsfolk who do good; and pṛñcatīḥ, mixing, in cows and the like, the payaḥ, milk, joined madhunā, with sweet juice." (Grammatical tail: ambayaḥ, rabi labi abi śabde, i after it by ac iḥ (U. 4-138) in the section, by bāhulaka; the suffix accent; adhvabhiḥ, kvanip by ader dha ca (U. 4-114), with the suffix unaccented as pit, the root accent; jāmayaḥ, jamu adane, i by bāhulaka; adhvarīyatām, kyac after adhvara by supa ātmanaḥ kyac, the ī by kyaci ca; by the statement aputrādīnām iti vaktavyam (Ma. 7-4-35) the bar na chandasy aputrasya does not apply; by sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante the dropping of a by kavyadhvarapṛtanasya (Pā. 7-4-39) also does not come; śatṛ for laṭ after the root ending in kyac; śap unaccented as pit, and śatṛ too by the lasārvadhātuka accent; their single substitute with kyac being final udātta by ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ, the genitive is udātta by śatur anumo nadyajādī; pṛñcatīḥ, pṛcī saṃparke, śatṛ for laṭ, śnam by rudhādibhyaḥ śnam, a dropped by śnasor allopaḥ, anusvāra and parasavarṇa, ṅīp by ugitaś ca, the long like vowel by vā chandasi, the ṅīp udātta by śatur anumaḥ….)

Page 201 — Rik 16: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अध्वरीयतां (adhvarīyatāṃ) — for us who desire the performance of sacrifice | जामयः (jāmayaḥ) — who do good like kinsfolk | अम्बयः (ambayaḥ) — the waters in the form of mothers (the deities presiding over the waters) | पयः (payaḥ) — the milk of cows | मधुना (madhunā) — with sweet juice | पृञ्चतीः (pṛñcatīḥ) — making it mixed | अध्वभिः (adhvabhiḥ) — by the way of the worship of the gods | यन्ति (yanti) — flow.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

The waters, for us who desire the performance of sacrifice, are in the form of mothers, that is, worthy of honour like a mother. They do good like kinsfolk. They make the milk of cows sweet. Such water is flowing in our path.

॥ English Translation ॥

The Sacred waters (dear mothers) of the Sacrificers are flowing by the way mixing the milk (of cows) with sweetness.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

अम्बयः (ambayaḥ) — in the Kauṣītaki-brāhmaṇa there is the explanation, ambayo yanty adhvabhir ity āpo vā ambayaḥ, that the word ambaya means the waters. Since it is customary to call a mother amba, it is to be known that the water here is addressed by a word expressing affection. In the Ṛgveda it is customary to call the deities presiding over the waters (or the waters) āpo devīḥ, with the feeling of honour, like honoured women. Besides, it is customary always to address these deities presiding over the waters in the feminine plural. The sūktas with the Waters as deity are very deep, full of meaning, joined with devotion, and very beautiful.

अम्बयो यन्त्यध्वभिरित्यापो वा अम्बयः ।

ambayo yantyadhvabhirityāpo vā ambayaḥ |

जामयः (jāmayaḥ) — hitakāriṇyo bandhavaḥ | kinsfolk who are well-wishers. The use of this word is in the Ṛgveda in the ṛks 1-31-10; 3-52-3 (zoom: the second group's digits are the lobed 5 and a curled 2, not the 4-glyph); 4-25-3; 8-102-13; 9-26-5; 9-65-1; 9-66-8; 9-89-4; 10-10-10 (small type, as read).

Page 202 — Rik 16: Special Topics (end), grammar

अध्वरीयतां (adhvarīyatāṃ) — adhvareṇa (by sacrifice) devayajanaṃ kartum icchatām || who desire to perform the sacrifice.

पृञ्चतीः (pṛñcatīḥ) — miśrayantyaḥ: mixing.

मधुना पयः (madhunā payaḥ) — the ṛṣi may have used this expression because water is most needed to support life, because flowing water in rivers and the like is sweet, unlike sea water, and because cows, by drinking such water, give tasty milk.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

अम्बयः (ambayaḥ) — the root rabi labi abi śabde; for the i of the root abi the it-name and dropping have come. So this is idit, that is, having i as it; so by idito num dhātoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58) — after the last vowel of a root marked i comes the augment num (n) — the augment num. By ac iḥ (U. Sū. 4-528 read at zoom in the small type: the 5-glyph, curled 2, 8-glyph; the bhāṣya prints उ० ४-१३८, so the two differ as printed) — after a root ending in a vowel comes the suffix i — this is its meaning. Though the root amb does not end in a vowel, since bahulam is said in this section, the suffix i comes here. By the suffix accent the i is udātta.

अध्वभिः (adhvabhiḥ) — by ader dha ca (U. Sū. 4-[?] in the small type, four lobed glyphs that I cannot separate at zoom; the bhāṣya prints उ० ४-११४) — after the root ada bhakṣaṇe the suffix kvanip comes, and dh for the d of the root — when the suffix kvanip comes and dh for the d, it becomes adhvan. The suffix kvanip is pit; so by anudāttau suppitau (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4) it is unaccented, and the root accent alone stays.

जामयः (jāmayaḥ) — the root jamu adane; after it, by the mention of bahula, the suffix i.

अध्वरीयतां (adhvarīyatāṃ) — na vidyate dhvaraḥ (hiṃsā) yasmin saḥ adhvaraḥ; by nañsubhyām (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172) final udātta. The analysis is adhvaram ātmanaḥ icchanti iti adhvarīyantaḥ, teṣām adhvarīyatām. By supa ātmanaḥ kyac (Pā. Sū. 3-1-8) and the paribhāṣā pratyayagrahaṇe yasmāt sa vihitas tadādes tadantasya grahaṇam (Paribhā. 24), in supaḥ 'ending in it' is obtained. It became subantāt. From dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā (Pā. Sū. 3-1-7) the three words karmaṇaḥ, icchāyām, vā are carried on. Karmaṇaḥ is a word in the fifth case, so 'from what expresses the object' results. 'The object with regard to what?' — when this expectation arises, icchāyām is present, so it results: 'being the object with regard to the root iṣ'. The word ātman conveys the meaning sva, 'oneself'. When purpose is intended, the fourth case ātmane would be fitting here; yet intending the purpose as a relation, by ṣaṣṭhī

Page 203 — Rik 16: grammar (continued)

śeṣe (Pā. Sū. 2-3-50) the genitive has come. Thus ātmanaḥ means 'for one's own purpose'. Sva intends the one who wishes. And so the sense of the sūtra: in the sense 'wishes', kyac comes after a sup-ending word expressing the object that is for the purpose of the one who wishes. This mantra is one with the Waters as deity. Those who praise the Water deity wish the sacrifice for their own purpose: this is the situation. Then adhvaram is a sup-ending word that is the object with regard to the root iṣ in icchati. This object is for the purpose of those who wish. Therefore after the word adhvaram the suffix kyac comes: adhvara + am + kyac. Kyac is included among the twelve sanādi suffixes counted as sankyackāmyac…; so by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-32) — what ends in san and the rest gets the name dhātu — adhvarīya gets the name dhātu. By supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-71) — a sup that is part of a root or a nominal stem is dropped (luk) — the am is dropped (luk): adhvara + ya. By kyaci ca (Pā. Sū. 7-4-33) — when the suffix kyac follows, ī is substituted for that a — the substitute ī for the a before ya: it became adhvarī + ya. But here by na chandasy aputrasya (Pā. Sū. 7-4-35) — when kyac follows, for words ending in a other than the word putra, the substitute ī and lengthening do not come — the question arises that the prohibition of ītva should come for the word adhvara (not being putra). To this the author of the vārttika has said by the vārttika aputrādīnām iti vaktavyam (Pā. Sū. 7-4-35 Vā.) that instead of aputrasya one should read aputrādīnām in the sūtra. Now it means that, leaving aside the words putra and the rest, for a word ending in a, when kyac follows, ītva does not come. The answer is that since the word adhvara is included among the putrādi, the prohibition of ītva does not come for it. By kavyadhvarapṛtanasyarci lopaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-4-39) — in the matter of the ṛk, when the suffix kyac follows, the final letter of the words kavi, adhvara, pṛtanā is dropped — the dropping of the a of the word adhvara would be due. But by sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante (Paribhā. 36 as read; the 3 is the ಇ-glyph, the 6 the hooked glyph) — in the Veda all operations come optionally — the a is not dropped. By vartamāne laṭ (Pā. Sū. 3-2-123) laṭ comes after the root adhvarīya ending in the suffix kyac; for it by laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe (Pā. Sū. 3-2-124) the substitute śatṛ; by kartari śap (Pā. Sū. 3-1-68) the vikaraṇa śap (a): it became adhvarīya + a + at. By citaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the a of kyac, being cit, is udātta. By anudāttau suppitau (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4) śap is unaccented. Śatṛ is a sārvadhātuka in place of la; it follows the a-final original teaching śap. So by tāsy anu-

Page 204 — Rik 16: grammar (continued)

dāttenṅid adupadeśāt… (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) śatṛ is unaccented; for these two unaccented a's, by ato guṇe (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97), the following form comes. By sthānivadbhāva it is unaccented. For this a and the a of kyac, again by the following form, a short a comes. Since it comes in place of both udātta and unaccented, by ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-5) it becomes udātta. Thus adhvarīyat is final udātta. After it the genitive plural ām: adhvarīyat + ām. Here by śatur anumo nadyajādī (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173) — if a word ending in the suffix śatṛ without the augment num is final udātta, the nadī-named suffix and the vowel-initial case-endings śas and the rest after it are also udātta — the ām is udātta.

पृञ्चतीः (pṛñcatīḥ) — the root pṛcī saṃparke. After it laṭ; for it śatṛ: pṛc + at. By rudhādibhyaḥ śnam (Pā. Sū. 3-1-78) the vikaraṇa śna; by the force of being mit, it comes after the ṛ of pṛ: pṛ + na + c + at. By śnasor allopaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-4-111) — when a sārvadhātuka suffix that is kit or ṅit follows, the a of the suffix śna and of the root as is dropped — the a of the suffix śna is dropped: pṛ + n + c + at. By stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-4-40) the palatalisation of the n, the ñ, is asiddha when making the anusvāra; so by naś cāpadāntasya jhali (Pā. Sū. 8-3-24) — when a jhal letter follows, the n and m not at the end of a pada take anusvāra — anusvāra; for it by anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-4-58) — before a yay letter, the anusvāra takes the homorganic of the following — before the c comes, by place, the homorganic nasal ñ. Pṛñc + at: when making anusvāra and parasavarṇa, since there is the prohibition na padānta… svarasavarṇānusvāra… (Pā. Sū. 1-1-58), the sthānivadbhāva for the dropping of a by acaḥ parasmin (Pā. Sū. 1-1-57) does not come. The ṛ of śatṛ has the it-name; the ṛ is in the pratyāhāra uk; so śatṛ is ugit. By ugitaś ca (Pā. Sū. 4-1-6) — when the feminine is intended after a nominal stem ending in an ugit, ṅīp comes — ṅīp comes: pṛñcat + ī. On the view that it names letters, by yū stryākhyau nadī (Pā. Sū. 1-4-3) the ī has the name nadī; so by śatur anumo nadyajādī the ī is udātta. After pṛñcatī, jas; by vā chandasi (Pā. Sū. 6-1-106) — in the Veda, after a long vowel, if jas or an ic follows, the long like vowel comes optionally — the long like vowel comes. ॥16॥ An ornament follows.

Rik 17 pp. 205

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒मूर्या उप॒ सूर्ये॒ याभि॑र्वा॒ सूर्यः॑ स॒ह । ता नो॑ हिन्वन्त्व॒ध्वरं॑ ॥१७॥

amū́r yā́ upa sū́rye yā́bhir vā sū́ryaḥ sahá | tā́ no hinvantv adhváraṃ ||17|| Bars under अ, प (उप), र्ये, वा and स (सह); strokes over भि and र्यः. Line 2: a stroke over नो, a bar under ध्व; the stroke over रं, shown in the Pada, is read in the Saṃhitā too.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अमूः । याः । उप । सूर्ये । याभिः । वा । सूर्यः । सह ॥ ताः । नः । हिन्वन्तु । अध्वरं ॥१७॥

amūḥ | yāḥ | upa | sūrye | yābhiḥ | vā | sūryaḥ | saha || tāḥ | naḥ | hinvantu | adhvaraṃ ||17||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

या अमूरापः सूर्ये उप समीपेनावस्थिताः । आपः सूर्ये समाहिता इति श्रुत्यन्तरात् । वाथवा सूर्यो याभिरद्भिः सह वर्तते । पूर्वत्रापां प्राधान्यमुत्तरत्र सूर्यस्येति विशेषः । तास्तादृश्य आपो नोऽस्मदीयमध्वरं यागं हिन्वन्तु । प्रीणयन्तु ॥ याभिः । सावेकाच इति विभक्त्युदात्तत्वस्य न गोश्वन्साववर्णेति प्रतिषेधः । शेषा तु प्रक्रिया स्पष्टा ॥

yā amūrāpaḥ sūrye upa samīpenāvasthitāḥ | āpaḥ sūrye samāhitā iti śrutyantarāt | vāthavā sūryo yābhiradbhiḥ saha vartate | pūrvatrāpāṃ prādhānyamuttaratra sūryasyeti viśeṣaḥ | tāstādṛśya āpo no 'smadīyamadhvaraṃ yāgaṃ hinvantu | prīṇayantu || yābhiḥ | sāvekāca iti vibhaktyudāttatvasya na gośvansāvavarṇeti pratiṣedhaḥ | śeṣā tu prakriyā spaṣṭā ||

Translation: "Those waters, yāḥ amūḥ, which are set upa, near, sūrye, the sun — from another śruti, 'the waters are placed in the sun' — vā, or, yābhiḥ, the waters with which the sun is saha, together; in the first [half] the waters are the chief, in the second the sun: that is the difference. May such waters hinvantu, gladden, naḥ adhvaram, our sacrifice." (Grammatical tail: yābhiḥ, the case-ending udātta by sāv ekācaḥ is barred by na gośvansāvavarṇa…; the rest of the derivation is clear.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

याः अमूः (yāḥ amūḥ) — which these waters | सूर्ये उप (sūrye upa) — are near the sun | वा (vā) — or | सूर्यः (sūryaḥ) — the sun | याभिः (yābhiḥ) — with which waters | सह (saha) — is together | ताः (tāḥ) — those waters | नः (naḥ) — our | अध्वरं (adhvaraṃ) — sacrifice | हिन्वन्तु (hinvantu) — may they carry out gladly.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

May those waters which are near the sun, or near which waters the sun is, make our sacrifice come to pass gladly.

॥ English Translation ॥

Those sacred waters who are near the sun or to whom the sun is near, may they promote our sacrifice.

Page 206 — Rik 17: Special Topics, grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

या उप सूर्ये (yā upa sūrye) — the waters near the sun, that is, the water (sea water) drawn up by the sun's rays and in the mid-air in the form of clouds. In the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka too there is the śruti statement āpaḥ sūrye samāhitāḥ. Yābhir vā sūryaḥ saha — this sentence too has the same meaning; it is said in another way, by changing the case and number. Or, since the sun's rays fall on bodies of water such as rivers, it may be said that the sun is near the water. In sum this mantra suggests that there is a close connection between water and the sun.

आपः सूर्ये समाहिताः ।

āpaḥ sūrye samāhitāḥ |

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

याभिः (yābhiḥ) — after the word yad, bhis; by tyadādīnām aḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-2-102) — when a case-ending follows, the final letter of the words read in the tyadādi class takes a — the a for the d, the following form, ṭāp when the feminine is shown, the lengthening of like vowels; yā + bhis, ru and visarga for the s: it becomes yābhiḥ. Sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168): the meaning of the sūtra is that when the locative plural suffix su follows, the case-ending after a monosyllabic form that conveys the same meaning as the monosyllabic form found before su is udātta. In the Mahābhāṣya on this sūtra:

सावितिकिमिदं प्रथमैकवचनस्य ग्रहणमाहोस्वित्सप्तमीबहुवचनस्य ।

sāvitikimidaṃ prathamaikavacanasya grahaṇamāhosvitsaptamībahuvacanasya |

"What is sau — is it the taking of the nominative singular or of the locative plural?" — that is, does the word sau take the first-case singular suffix su, or the locative plural sup? The Bhāṣya: kutaḥ saṃdehaḥ? — what is the reason for doubt? Samāno nirdeśaḥ: even if the locative ṅi is put after the nominative singular su, it becomes sau; when the p of the locative plural sup is removed by the it-name, it stands as su, and even if the locative singular ṅi is put after it, it becomes sau. Since in both the first and the seventh case the form sau is the same, doubt arises. Here the author of the Kaiyaṭa has described the intention thus:

यदि शास्त्रीयं सुरूपं गृह्यते तदा प्राथम्यात्प्रथमैकवचनस्य ग्रहणेन भाव्यम् । अथ प्रायोगिकं ततः सप्तमीबहुवचनस्य । तद्धि प्रयोगे सुरूपं श्रूयते । प्रथमैकवचने तु विकृतरूपप्रयोगे न सुरूपमिति संशयानः पृच्छति सावितिकिमिति ।

yadi śāstrīyaṃ surūpaṃ gṛhyate tadā prāthamyātprathamaikavacanasya grahaṇena bhāvyam | atha prāyogikaṃ tataḥ saptamībahuvacanasya | taddhi prayoge surūpaṃ śrūyate | prathamaikavacane tu vikṛtarūpaprayoge na surūpamiti saṃśayānaḥ pṛcchati sāvitikimiti |

That is: on the view of taking the form su established in the technical usage of the science, by the maxim prathamopasthite parityāge kāraṇābhāvaḥ, among the twenty-one suffixes su and the rest the first, the nominative singular su, is taken; if it is intended to take the su heard in usage, the locative plural is taken. For in the nominative singular the order su —

प्रथमोपस्थिते परित्यागे कारणाभावः ।

prathamopasthite parityāge kāraṇābhāvaḥ |

Page 207 — Rik 17: grammar (continued)

— is not heard as the form su, because it is changed: for example rāmaḥ and the like, where the su has become visarga. In places like rāmāsu the order su is heard in the locative plural. So on the view of taking the usage, the seventh would have to be taken. Since there is such doubt, in the Bhāṣya the question has been considered whether the nominative singular or the locative plural is taken. The answer:

सप्तमीबहुवचनस्य ग्रहणम् । कथं ज्ञायते । यदयं नगोश्वन्साववर्णेति प्रतिषेधं शास्ति । कथं कृत्वा ज्ञापकम् । यदि प्रथमैकवचनस्य ग्रहणं स्याद्गोशुनोः प्रतिषेधवचनमनर्थकं स्यात् ।

saptamībahuvacanasya grahaṇam | kathaṃ jñāyate | yadayaṃ nagośvansāvavarṇeti pratiṣedhaṃ śāsti | kathaṃ kṛtvā jñāpakam | yadi prathamaikavacanasya grahaṇaṃ syādgośunoḥ pratiṣedhavacanamanarthakaṃ syāt |

"The locative plural is taken. How is it known? Because he teaches the prohibition nagośvansāvavarṇa… (Pā. Sū. 6-1-182). How does that make it known? If the nominative singular were taken, the statement of prohibition for go and śvan would be pointless." That is: in the nominative singular the forms are gauḥ and śvā; in the word go, gauḥ is a monosyllabic form ending in au; in the word śvan, śvā is a monosyllabic form ending in ā. In gobhyām, śvabhyām, the case-ending is after the o-final monosyllable go and after the short-vowel-final monosyllable śva. So in the nominative singular, after whatever monosyllabic form there is, there is no such case-ending after that monosyllable; so sāv ekācaḥ would not apply at all, and the statement of prohibition would be useless. If the locative plural is taken, in the locative plural goṣu, śvasu, the monosyllabic forms go and śva are found when the locative plural su follows. So after the monosyllables go, śva, the bhyām in gobhyām, śvabhyām would get the udātta by sāv ekācaḥ. To prevent it, the prohibition of the udātta for the case-ending after go, śvan in the sūtra nagośvan is purposeful. So the author of the Bhāṣya has established that the locative plural alone is taken. From the Bhāṣya that states the indication itself it results that in sāv ekācaḥ the taking of the form is intended. Otherwise, sau ya ekāc —

Page 208 — Rik 17: grammar (continued)

— since in the nominative singular there are the monosyllables gauḥ, śvā, if the accent were due, the prohibition would be purposeful and could not indicate the stated meaning; if the taking of the form is intended, sau yadrūpaviśiṣṭaḥ ekāc: when the nominative singular su follows, whatever monosyllabic form there is, gauḥ, śvā, after it in gobhyaḥ, śvabhyaḥ there is no case-ending, so the prohibition is incongruous and indicates the stated meaning.

If the nominative singular is taken, a fault comes in yātā, where laṭ comes after the root yā, śatṛ for it, luk for śap, and the instrumental singular ṭā: for in the nominative singular, since the dropping of the conjunct-final is asiddha, whether as yān or as yānt, there is a monosyllabic form. After it there is no case-ending of the third onward, but after yāt there is the third case-ending. So in the nominative singular, yadarthaviśiṣṭam ekājrūpam, since there is no case-ending of the third onward after the monosyllable qualified by that meaning, sāv ekācaḥ would not come here. By taking the changed form yānt in the nominative singular, the original form yāt cannot be taken; and the maxim —

यदागमास्तद्गुणीभूतास्तद्ग्रहणेन गृह्यन्ते ।

yadāgamāstadguṇībhūtāstadgrahaṇena gṛhyante |

— 'augments, being subordinate to it, are taken by its mention' — says that where the mention is of what lacks the augment, what has the augment is also taken; so by the mention of yāns, which has the augment, yāt, which lacks it, cannot be taken. And tanmadhyapatitas tadgrahaṇena gṛhyate (Paribhā. 90 as printed, zoom-checked on p. 208: the 9-glyph and the ring) makes known only that by the mention of the bare thing the qualified one is taken; by the qualified yānt the bare yāt cannot be taken.

तन्मध्यपतितस्तद्ग्रहणेन गृह्यते ।

tanmadhyapatitastadgrahaṇena gṛhyate |

In sāv ekācaḥ one does not describe the meaning by intending the taking of the form, 'whatever monosyllabic form expressing a meaning there is before su'. Rather the meaning of the sūtra sāv ekācaḥ is: when su follows, whatever word is monosyllabic, the case-ending of the third onward after that word is udātta. Thus, since the word yāt is monosyllabic in the nominative singular, the case-ending after it may get the udātta. But though in yātā there is no fault, a fault comes in doṣabhyām. In the nominative singular doḥ the word doṣ is monosyllabic. When bhyām comes after it, after the substitute doṣan by paddannomāshṛnniśasanyūṣandoṣan… (Pā. Sū. 6-1-63), in doṣan + bhyām too the bhyām would have to be udātta. The mid-udātta accent doṣabhyām is what is desired here. So the taking of the form must be intended. Now the monosyllabic form before su is doḥ. After it there is no bhyām. So by sāv ekācaḥ the case-ending does not get the udātta; but by anudāttau suppitau it is unaccented. The word doṣ —

Page 209 — Rik 17: grammar (continued)

— ends in the suffix ḍosi by damer ḍosiḥ (U. Sū. 3-28 at zoom: the first digit is a heavy-headed glyph that looks like a 3 with a dot above, then 2 and 8 [lobed]; Vol 3 elsewhere reads this as 2-28), and is final udātta by the suffix accent. When the substitute doṣan coming in its place is also final udātta, the mid-udātta doṣabhyām is established. Even if sau is intended as the locative plural, if one does not intend the taking of the form in sāv ekācaḥ as said before, the fault comes in doṣabhyām. Thus, since the intention to take the form in sāv ekācaḥ is needed to prevent the udātta of the case-ending in doṣabhyām, once that is established, if the nominative singular is taken, the udātta cannot come in yātā. For that it must be held that the locative plural alone is taken. Now since in the locative yātsu is the form, sau yad ekājrūpaṃ yāt, and the case-ending after it exists, the udātta accent is established in places like yātā, yādbhyām. Even if sāv ekācaḥ is held to be the locative and the taking of the form is intended, the fault comes in doṣabhyām. In doḥṣu, when su follows, there is the form doḥ. This is not heard in doṣabhyām. Yet since in place of doṣ the substitute doṣan has come, by the sthānivadbhāva of sthānivad ādeśaḥ (Pā. Sū. 1-1-56) the form doṣan becomes like the form doḥ. So in the locative plural, since there is a case-ending of the third onward after whatever form there is, the bhyām would have to be udātta. In the Taittirīya, doṣabhyāṃ svāhā is mid-udātta, so it cannot be said that the udātta of the case-ending is desired. Only where the form found when the locative plural follows is actually heard does sāv ekācaḥ come. Where it is not directly heard, we say that, imagining by sthānivadbhāva and the like that the same form is there, the present sūtra does not enter. Thus in doṣabhyām, since doḥ is not heard, sāv ekācaḥ does not come here. Then on this view the examples śunaḥ, śunā given by the author of the Bhāṣya at the sūtra nagośvan would have to be incongruous. In the locative plural form śvasu, the form śva is heard here; since the dropping of n is an accent rule, even though by nalopaḥ supsvara… (Pā. Sū. 8-2-2) it is asiddha, it becomes as if śvan were there. In śunaḥ, śunā the form śvan, heard in the Veda, is not heard as either śva or śvan; so here sāv ekācaḥ does not apply at all. Then why should the prohibition come here? So it is to be held that there is no strict requirement that the form be directly heard. Now, though by saṃprasāraṇa u has come for the v, a part of śvan, and a change has come to the part, by ekadeśavikṛtam ananyavat, imagining that śvan itself is there, sāv ekācaḥ would be due; to avoid it, the example śunaḥ, śunā of the prohibition becomes congruous. Likewise in doṣabhyām, by sthānivadbhāva the form doḥ —

एकदेशविकृतमनन्यवत् ।

ekadeśavikṛtamananyavat |

Page 210 — Rik 17: grammar (continued)

— being there, one may object that the case-ending should be udātta. The answer: according to usage we repeat ekācaḥ. So the meaning drawn out of the sūtra is: when the su suffix follows, whatever monosyllabic word expressing a meaning is heard, on the view that the case-ending after such a form is after that very monosyllable, it gets the udātta. Doṣabhyām follows the polysyllable doṣa, so the udātta accent does not come here. If the word sau were not there, it would mean ekācaḥ paraṃ tṛtīyādir vibhaktir udāttā syāt. In rājñā the ṭā is after the monosyllable rājñ, so it would have to be udātta. If ekācaḥ were not there, the meaning of the sūtra sāv ekācaḥ would be sau vartamānāt śabdāt parā tṛtīyādir vibhaktir udāttā syāt. Then too in rājñā, since the ṭā is after the word found in sau, it would have to be udātta. On this view of sau, a word like dvābhyām, for which being followed by su is not possible, would have to be excluded. So here both sau and ekācaḥ must be there. The conclusion has been reached that by sau the locative plural alone is to be taken and that the taking of the form is also intended.

Even so, in the feminine, in words like ābhyām and in forms like ebhiḥ, eṣām, the case-ending would have to be udātta by sāv ekācaḥ. So the total lack of accent cannot be obtained. In the feminine the locative form is āsu; so when su follows, the monosyllabic form ā is heard; in ābhyām the bhyām after such an ā would have to get the udātta by sāv ekācaḥ. In the masculine and neuter the locative form is eṣu. So, though when su follows e is monosyllabic, in ebhiḥ, eṣām the bhis and ām after such an e would have to get the udātta by sāv ekācaḥ.

When the case-ending thus gets the udātta, by the śeṣānudātta accent anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-158) the stem's being unaccented is established anyway. That being so, in the sūtra idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudāttas tṛtīyādau (Pā. Sū. 2-4-32) the rule laying down the unaccented for aś becomes useless. Being useless, it makes known that when aś has come in anvādeśa, the case-ending there does not get the udātta. So it cannot be said that in places like ebhiḥ the case-ending cannot be udātta. For if the rule of the unaccented for aś were wholly useless, by the maxim —

व्यर्थं सत् किंचिदर्थं ज्ञापयति ।

vyarthaṃ sat kiṃcidarthaṃ jñāpayati |

— it could be said to make known the stated meaning. But it is not wholly useless. Where by sāv ekācaḥ the case-ending must not get the udātta, there, by śeṣanighāta, the stem cannot be unaccented; there the rule of the unaccented is purposeful. For example, the masculine —

Page 211 (upper) — Rik 17: grammar (end)

— and neuter ābhyām and the like: in the masculine and neuter, when su follows, the monosyllabic form is e, not ā; so in the locative plural there is no such monosyllabic form. In the feminine āsu, when the locative plural follows, the form ā does exist; but the meaning is different: it is a monosyllabic form expressing the feminine, while the ā of the masculine and neuter ābhyām is a monosyllabic form expressing masculine and neuter. So, since what follows sau yadarthaviśiṣṭam ekājrūpam is not there, the udātta is not established for the masculine-neuter ābhyām; so the stem does not become unaccented by śeṣanighāta. Here, to obtain the unaccented, the rule of the unaccented is purposeful. Therefore the rule of the unaccented cannot make known that in the matter of anvādeśa the case-ending accent does not come. Since in the nominative singular it does not end in a/ā, it cannot be said that in ebhiḥ and the like the udātta is barred by nagośvan. In ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) antodāttāt is carried on. In ābhyām the stem is unaccented. So since there is no case-ending after a final udātta, the udātta of the case-ending cannot be established by ūḍidam. So it cannot be said that the udātta accent of the case-ending is what is desired. In Vedic usages like ebhir agne piba [as printed] and ebhir agne duvo giraḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14-1) total lack of accent alone is heard. Here, even taking the refined meaning of sāv ekācaḥ, the case-ending would have to be udātta. So in places like ebhiḥ the total lack of accent must be held to be Vedic. The author of the Uddyota, when describing the Pradīpa's intention, says, ebhir agne ityādau sarvānudāttapadaśravaṇaṃ tu chāndasam iti tadbhāvaḥ (Uddyota 6-1-168) and so on. It seems that the work that resolved this, which the Candrakalā saw in the Śekhara of the present sūtra, is lost. It now results that, even taking the refined meaning of sāv ekācaḥ in the manner of the available Śekhara, its application in ebhiḥ cannot be stopped. Considering the present case: in yābhiḥ the udātta of the case-ending would be due by sāv ekācaḥ. For that, by nagośvansāvavarṇarāḍaṅkruṅkṛdbhyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-182) — after the word go, the word śvan, words ending in a/ā in the nominative singular, the word rāṭ ending in kvip, the word aṅ formed with kvip after the root añc, the word kruñ formed with kvin after the root kruñc, and the word kṛt formed with kvip after the root kṛ, the case-ending and the matup do not get the udātta — since in the nominative singular yā ends in a/ā, the bhis after yā does not get the udātta. The rest of the derivation is clear. ॥17॥

एभिरग्ने इत्यादौ सर्वानुदात्तपदश्रवणं तु छान्दसमिति तद्भावः ।

ebhiragne ityādau sarvānudāttapadaśravaṇaṃ tu chāndasamiti tadbhāvaḥ |

एभिरग्ने पिब सोमं । एभिरग्ने दुवो गिरः ॥ (ऋ० सं० १-१४-१)

ebhiragne piba somaṃ | ebhiragne duvo giraḥ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 1-14-1) An ornament follows.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒पो दे॒वीरुप॑ ह्वये॒ यत्र॒ गावः॒ पिब॑न्ति नः । सि॒न्धुभ्यः॒ कर्त्वं॑ ह॒विः ॥१८॥

apó devī́r úpa hvaye yátra gā́vaḥ píbanti naḥ | sindhúbhyaḥ kártvaṃ havíḥ ||18|| Bars under अ, दे, ये (ह्वये), त्र (यत्र) and वः; strokes over प (उप) and ब (पिबन्ति). Line 2: bars under सि, भ्यः and ह; a stroke over र्त्वं.

अपः । देवीः । उप । ह्वये । यत्र । गावः । पिबन्ति । नः ॥ सिन्धुऽभ्यः । कर्त्वं । हविः ॥१८॥

apaḥ | devīḥ | upa | hvaye | yatra | gāvaḥ | pibanti | naḥ || sindhu 'bhyaḥ | kartvaṃ | haviḥ ||18||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ The number is printed पा० ३-४-१४.

नोऽस्मदीया गावो यत्र यास्वप्सु पिबन्ति पानं कुर्वन्ति ता आपो देवीरुप ह्वये । आह्वयामि । सिन्धुभ्यः स्यन्दनशीलाभ्योऽद्भ्यो देवताभ्यो हविः कर्त्वं । अस्माभिः कर्तव्यं ॥ अपः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना शस उदात्तत्वं । पिबन्ति । पाघ्रेत्यादिना पिबादेशः । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ निपातैर्यद्यदीत्यादिना निघाताभावः । कर्त्वं । डुकृञ् करणे । कृत्यार्थे तवैकेन्केन्यत्वनः । पा० ३-४-१४ । इति कर्मणि त्वन्प्रत्ययः । गुणः । नित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

no 'smadīyā gāvo yatra yāsvapsu pibanti pānaṃ kurvanti tā āpo devīrupa hvaye | āhvayāmi | sindhubhyaḥ syandanaśīlābhyo 'dbhyo devatābhyo haviḥ kartvaṃ | asmābhiḥ kartavyaṃ || apaḥ | ūḍidamityādinā śasa udāttatvaṃ | pibanti | pāghretyādinā pibādeśaḥ | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | tiṅaśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvareṇādyudāttatvaṃ || nipātairyadyadītyādinā nighātābhāvaḥ | kartvaṃ | ḍukṛñ karaṇe | kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ | pā0 3-4-14 | iti karmaṇi tvanpratyayaḥ | guṇaḥ | nitsvareṇādyudāttatvaṃ ||

Translation: "I upa hvaye, call, the āpaḥ devīḥ, divine waters, yatra, in which waters naḥ gāvaḥ, our cows, pibanti, drink. Havis is kartvam, to be made by us, sindhubhyaḥ, for the deities, the waters that are of flowing nature." (Grammatical tail: apaḥ, the śas udātta by ūḍidam…; pibanti, the substitute piba by pāghrā…, śap unaccented as pit, and the tiṅ by the lasārvadhātuka accent, so initial udātta by the root accent; no loss of accent by nipātair yadyadi…; kartvam, ḍukṛñ karaṇe, the suffix tvan in the object sense by kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ (Pā. 3-4-14), guṇa, initial udātta by the nit accent.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

नः (naḥ) — our | गावः (gāvaḥ) — cows | यत्र (yatra) — in which body of water | पिबन्ति (pibanti) — drink water | (ताः) अपः देवीः ((tāḥ) apaḥ devīḥ) — that excellent water | उप ह्वये (upa hvaye) — I call | सिन्धुभ्यः (sindhubhyaḥ) — with regard to those flowing waters | हविः (haviḥ) — the giving of the oblation | कर्त्वं (kartvaṃ) — must be made.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

I call that excellent water, in whatever body of water, a river and the like, our cows drink. With regard to that flowing water we must necessarily make the giving of oblations.

Page 213 — Rik 18: English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

I invoke hither the sacred waters at which our cows drink; our oblations are to be made to those streams.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

सिन्धुभ्यः (sindhubhyaḥ) — syandanaśīlābhyo devatābhyaḥ | In this ṛk and in other ṛks that set forth the deities presiding over the waters, the ṛṣis have made hymns with regard to āpo devīḥ, that is, excellent or honoured flowing water. On some occasions the water of lakes, tanks and the like, which do not flow, is also indicated. So sweet water fit for drinking is especially praised. Sea water is not seen to have so much pre-eminence.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

अपः (apaḥ) — after the word ap, the accusative plural suffix śas; for the ś, by laśakv ataddhite (Pā. Sū. 1-3-8) the it-name comes, and by tasya lopaḥ (Pā. Sū. 1-3-9) it is dropped: ap + as = apas; for the s, by sasajuṣo ruḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-2-66) ru, by kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-3-15) the visarga: it becomes apaḥ. Here in ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171), ekācaḥ from sāv ekācaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-168), antodāttāt from antodāttād uttarapadāt… (Pā. Sū. 6-1-169), and asarvanāmasthānam from añceś chandasy asarvanāmasthānam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-170) are carried on. Ūṭh is not a monosyllabic form. Because it is not monosyllabic, ekācaḥ is not its qualifier, asaṃbhavāt: the maxim is saṃbhavavyabhicārābhyāṃ syād viśeṣaṇam arthavat — saṃbhava, fitness; vyabhicāra, exclusion of others. Now the meaning of the sūtra: the case-ending other than sarvanāmasthāna after ūṭh, which is final udātta and stands penultimate, and after the word idam, the six padādi words, ap, pums, rai, div, which are final udātta and monosyllabic, is udātta. If by ūṭh the whole containing ūṭh is intended, then ekācaḥ is a qualifier for ūṭh too. Then the meaning for the part ūṭh: the case-ending other than sarvanāmasthāna after a monosyllabic word containing ūṭh, final udātta and penultimate, is udātta. Examples praṣṭhauhaḥ, viśvauhaḥ and the like. Since ekācaḥ is mentioned in the sūtra, the qualifier, by śrutānumitayoḥ śrutasaṃbandho balīyān, is not a qualifier of the stem. So, though the stems praṣṭhauh, viśvauh are polysyllabic, since ūh is monosyllabic, the accent applies; likewise in places like brāhmaṇapadā —

संभवव्यभिचाराभ्यां स्याद्विशेषणमर्थवत् । श्रुतानुमितयोः श्रुतसंबन्धो बलीयान् ।

saṃbhavavyabhicārābhyāṃ syādviśeṣaṇamarthavat | śrutānumitayoḥ śrutasaṃbandho balīyān |

Page 214 — Rik 18: grammar (continued)

— the final udātta is established. The present word ap is final udātta and monosyllabic. So the śas, a non-sarvanāmasthāna case-ending after it, is udātta.

पिबन्ति (pibanti) — the root pā pāne; after it laṭ, the third person plural suffix jhi; by jho 'ntaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-1-3) the substitute ant for jh: pā + anti; by kartari śap (Pā. Sū. 3-1-68) the vikaraṇa śap: pā + a + anti. Now by pāghrādhmāsthāmnādāṇdṛśyartisartiśadasadāṃ pibajighradhamatiṣṭhamanayacchapaśyarcchadhauśīyasīdāḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78) — when a suffix beginning with the it-named ś follows, the eleven roots pā and the rest take the eleven substitutes piba and the rest. Whether the substitute is piba ending in a or pib ending in b has been explained at the sūkta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-18-11 [as printed]). When the substitute piba comes: piba + a + anti; twice, by ato guṇe (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) — if the guṇa letters a, e, o follow a short a not at the end of a pada, the following form comes as a single substitute for the places before and after — the following form: it becomes pibanti. On this view, by the vārttika pibādeśo nipātanāt (Pā. Sū. Vā. 6-1-162) read in the sūtra dhātoḥ, the i of pi is udātta, the a of ba unaccented by the śeṣānudātta; the a of the vikaraṇa śap is unaccented by anudāttau suppitau (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4) since it is pit; the a coming by the following form in place of these unaccented a's is unaccented by sthānivadbhāva; by the lasārvadhātuka accent of tāsy anudātten… (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the a of anti is unaccented. Again, the following form is unaccented by sthānivadbhāva. This unaccented follows the udātta i. So by udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-4-66) it is svarita: this is the situation on the view of the a-final substitute. On the view of the consonant-final substitute pib, by dhātoḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-162) the i of pi is udātta, śap unaccented as before, anti likewise, the following form likewise, the svarita likewise. On the first view there is no occasion at all for pugantalaghūpadhasya ca (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86): since piba ends in a, the b is the penultimate; a light vowel is not the penultimate. On the second view, by aṅgavṛtte punarvṛttāv avidhir niṣṭhitasya (Paribhā. 90, zoom-checked on p. 214) — once a stem-section rule has come and a form is completed, another stem-section rule does not come — after the substitute piba has come, guṇa does not come for the penultimate letter; so guṇa is warded off; and it must be known that the sixth adhyāya's fourth pāda and the whole of the seventh adhyāya are the stem section. Nipātair yadyadihantakuvinnec ceccaṇkaccid yatrayuktam (Pā. Sū. 8-1-30): the word yatra in yad and the rest is a single word ending in a dropped third case; here, if a compound with the word yukta is intended, the qualifier nipātaiḥ is unconnected. If a compound is accepted, the word ending in yatra would be a part of the compound. Then by padārthaḥ padārthenānveti na tu tadekadeśena, the meaning of one word —

अङ्गवृत्ते पुनर्वृत्तावविधिर्निष्ठितस्य । पदार्थः पदार्थेनान्वेति न तु तदेकदेशेन ।

aṅgavṛtte punarvṛttāvavidhirniṣṭhitasya | padārthaḥ padārthenānveti na tu tadekadeśena |

Page 215 — Rik 18: grammar (end)

— is construed only with the meaning of the qualified presented by another word; it is not construed with a part; so for nipātaiḥ there is no construction with the word ending in yatra, a part of the compound. If such construction is intended, since there is no connection (sāmarthya), the compound cannot come. That is why all teachers accept that in ṛddhasya rājapuruṣaḥ there is no construction of ṛddhasya with rājñaḥ, a part of the compound. Thus the meaning of the sūtra results: since by this sūtra there is the prohibition that a tiṅ-final word joined with the particles yat, yadi, hanta, kuvit, net, cet, caṇ, kaccit, yatra is not unaccented, the total lack of accent by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) does not come for pibanti.

ऋद्धस्य राजपुरुषः ।

ṛddhasya rājapuruṣaḥ |

कर्त्वम् (kartvam) — the root (ḍu)kṛñ karaṇe. Kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-14): in the sūtra tayor eva kṛtyaktakhalarthāḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-70) it is said that the kṛtya suffixes, the suffix kta and the khalartha suffixes come only in the two senses of action and object. So action and object are both kṛtya senses. The sūtra kṛtyāḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-95) is a heading up to the sūtra ṇvultṛcau (Pā. Sū. 3-1-133). In the science of grammar the suffixes belonging to this heading are called kṛtya suffixes. And so the meaning of the sūtra: in the kṛtya sense, in the form of action and object, the suffixes tavai, ken, kenya, tvan come after a root. By this, when tvan comes in the object sense after the root kṛ: kṛ + tvan; by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) — when sārvadhātuka and ārdhadhātuka suffixes follow, the ik end of a stem takes guṇa — when the ārdhadhātuka tva follows, guṇa for the ṛ; it comes followed by r: kar + tvan; the n has the it-name and is removed: kartva; this is initially udātta by ñnity ādir nityam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197). In the nominative singular it becomes kartvam. ॥18॥

अ॒प्स्व१॒॑न्तर॒मृत॑म॒प्सु भे॑ष॒जम॒पामु॒त प्रश॑स्तये । [accent ?] देवा॒ भव॑त वा॒जिनः॑ ॥१९॥

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अप्ऽसु । अन्तः । अमृतं । अप्ऽसु । भेषजं । अपां । उत । प्रऽशस्तये ॥ देवाः । भवत । वाजिनः ॥१९॥

ap 'su | antaḥ | amṛtaṃ | ap 'su | bheṣajaṃ | apāṃ | uta | pra 'śastaye || devāḥ | bhavata | vājinaḥ ||19||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Numbers as printed: पा० ६-२-११६, ६-२-५०.

अप्सु जलेष्वन्तर्मध्येऽमृतं पीयूषं वर्तते । तस्याब्विकारत्वात् । अमृतं वा आप इति श्रुत्यन्तराच्च । तथैवाप्सु भेषजमौषधं वर्तते । क्षुद्रोगनिवर्तकस्यान्नस्याप्कार्यत्वात् । उतापि च तादृशीनामपां देवतानां प्रशस्तये प्रशंसार्थं हे देवा ऋत्विजादयो ब्राह्मणाः । एते वै देवाः प्रत्यक्षं यद्ब्राह्मणा इति श्रुत्यन्तरात् । वाजिनो वेगवन्तो भवत । शीघ्रं स्तुतिं कुरुतेत्यर्थः ॥ अप्सु । ऊडिदमित्यादिना सप्तम्या उदात्तत्वं । संहितायामुदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरित इति स्वरितत्वं । अमृतं । नञो जरमरमित्रमृताः । पा० ६-२-११६ । इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । प्रशस्तये । तादौ च निति । पा० ६-२-५० । इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । भवत । आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदिति पूर्वस्यामन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वेन पादादित्वान्न निघातः ॥

apsu jaleṣvantarmadhye 'mṛtaṃ pīyūṣaṃ vartate | tasyābvikāratvāt | amṛtaṃ vā āpa iti śrutyantarācca | tathaivāpsu bheṣajamauṣadhaṃ vartate | kṣudroganivartakasyānnasyāpkāryatvāt | utāpi ca tādṛśīnāmapāṃ devatānāṃ praśastaye praśaṃsārthaṃ he devā ṛtvijādayo brāhmaṇāḥ | ete vai devāḥ pratyakṣaṃ yadbrāhmaṇā iti śrutyantarāt | vājino vegavanto bhavata | śīghraṃ stutiṃ kurutetyarthaḥ || apsu | ūḍidamityādinā saptamyā udāttatvaṃ | saṃhitāyāmudāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ svarita iti svaritatvaṃ | amṛtaṃ | naño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ | pā0 6-2-116 | ityuttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | praśastaye | tādau ca niti | pā0 6-2-50 | iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvaṃ | bhavata | āmantritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavaditi pūrvasyāmantritasyāvidyamānavattvena pādāditvānna nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "Apsu antaḥ, within the waters, is amṛtam, nectar, because it is a product of water, and from the other śruti 'the waters indeed are nectar'. Likewise apsu, in the waters, is bheṣajam, medicine, since food, which removes the disease of hunger, is a product of water. Uta, and, praśastaye, for the praise of such waters, the deities, O devāḥ, priests and the rest, the brāhmaṇas — from the other śruti 'these indeed are the visible gods, the brāhmaṇas' — bhavata, be, vājinaḥ, swift: that is, make the praise quickly." (Grammatical tail: apsu, the locative udātta by ūḍidam…; in the Saṃhitā svarita by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ; amṛtam, the last member's initial udātta by nañño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ (Pā. 6-2-116); praśastaye, the prefix keeps its own accent by tādau ca niti… (Pā. 6-2-50); bhavata, since the preceding vocative is treated as not there by āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat, it is at the beginning of the pāda, so no loss of accent.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अप्सु अन्तः (apsu antaḥ) — in the midst of the waters (in water) | अमृतं (amṛtaṃ) — there is nectar | अप्सु (apsu) — in water | भेषजं (bheṣajaṃ) — there is medicine that destroys disease | उत (uta) — and | (हे) देवाः ((he) devāḥ) — O deities (and people, priests, sacrificers and the rest) | अपां (apāṃ) — of the waters | प्रशस्तये (praśastaye) — for praise, or to make hymns | वाजिनः (vājinaḥ) — swift (ready quickly) | भवत (bhavata) — be.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

There is nectar in water; in water there is the power that cures disease, that is, of medicine. Therefore, O deities and people, priests, sacrificers and the rest, be ready quickly to praise those waters.

Page 217 — Rik 19: English, Special Topics

॥ English Translation ॥

(There is) ambrosia in the waters, (there is) medicine in the waters; therefore divine priests, be prompt in their praise.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The śruti statement of the Taittirīya Upaniṣad describes very well the qualities and pre-eminence of water —

आपो वा इदꣳ सर्वं विश्वा भूतान्यापः प्राणा वा आपः पशव आपोऽन्नमापोऽमृतमापः सम्राडापो विराडापः स्वराडापश्छन्दाꣳस्यापो ज्योतीꣳष्यापो यजूꣳष्यापः सत्यमापः सर्वा देवता आपो भूर्भुवः सुवराप ओं ॥

āpo vā idam̐ sarvaṃ viśvā bhūtānyāpaḥ prāṇā vā āpaḥ paśava āpo 'nnamāpo 'mṛtamāpaḥ samrāḍāpo virāḍāpaḥ svarāḍāpaśchandām̐syāpo jyotīm̐ṣyāpo yajūm̐ṣyāpaḥ satyamāpaḥ sarvā devatā āpo bhūrbhuvaḥ suvarāpa oṃ ||

— that is, everything has arisen from water. All living beings and animals live by water; that is, water itself is the support of all living creatures and plants. Without water no living being can live. So water itself is said to be life. Since plants, trees and the vegetable kingdom grow by water, water is directly and indirectly food for living beings. Without food one can live some days; without water it is impossible to live. In our body most is water; since blood and the rest are in liquid form, water is most necessary for living. So it is no exaggeration to call water nectar. Since water is one of the five elements, since there is the śruti statement āpo vā idam agre salilam āsīt, and since the śruti says that other things were created from water, it is fitting to say that everything is the very form of water, or that water is the root of all things. So the śruti proclaims that water is the form of all the deities.

आपो वा इदमग्रे सलिलमासीत् ।

āpo vā idamagre salilamāsīt |

अमृतं भेषजं (amṛtaṃ bheṣajaṃ) — since water is most necessary for living beings and is the support of life, it is called nectar. Since nectar is in liquid form, and since all liquid things are indicated by the word āpaḥ, 'water', it is right to call water nectar. Many diseases can be cured by water; and since medicines are generally in liquid form mixed with water, it is also fitting to say that medicines are in water. How great the pre-eminence of water is in the matter of curing disease is described specially in medical works such as the Āyurveda.

देवाः (devāḥ) — though the deities are addressed here as devāḥ, it may be said to mean either people such as priests and sacrificers, or the deities. Or since śruti statements such as —

Page 218 — Rik 19: Special Topics (end), grammar

एते वै देवाः प्रत्यक्षं यद्ब्राह्मणाः ।

ete vai devāḥ pratyakṣaṃ yadbrāhmaṇāḥ |

— say that brāhmaṇa priests are visible deities, the brāhmaṇas have been addressed by the word deva.

वाजिनः (vājinaḥ) — vegavantaḥ, śīghragāminaḥ: quickly, promptly, without delay, and so on. Or, since there is the śruti statement annaṃ vai vājaḥ, that vāja means food, it may be explained as: furnished with food or oblation, that is, praise with offerings of oblation and the like.

अन्नं वै वाजः ।

annaṃ vai vājaḥ |

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

अप्सु (apsu) — after the word ap, the locative plural suffix su; for the meaning of ūḍidampadādyapumraidyubhyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) see the previous mantra. By this the case-ending su is udātta. In place of this udātta u, at the time of the Saṃhitā, when the vowel of the word antaḥ follows, by iko yaṇ aci (Pā. Sū. 6-1-77) the yaṇ v comes. And so this v is a yaṇ that has come in place of an udātta; by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4) — an unaccented after a yaṇ that has come in place of an udātta or svarita becomes svarita — the unaccented a of the word antaḥ becomes svarita.

अमृतं (amṛtaṃ) — when a bahuvrīhi compound of nañ with the word mṛta comes, the n is dropped and only a remains. By bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the own accent would be due; overriding it, by nañño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-2-116) — in a bahuvrīhi compound, the four words jara, mara, mitra, mṛta after nañ take the initial udātta — the last member mṛta gets the initial udātta accent.

प्रशस्तये (praśastaye) — the prefix pra, the root śaṃsu stutau. By striyāṃ ktin (Pā. Sū. 3-3-94) the suffix ktin; the n is dropped by aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti (Pā. Sū. 6-4-24): praśasti; dative singular praśastaye. Here by tādau ca niti kṛty atau (Pā. Sū. 6-2-50) — when a kṛt suffix other than tu, without the marker n and beginning with t, follows, the immediately preceding gati keeps its own accent — the gati pra gets its own accent. This is an exception to the kṛt accent laid down by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139); pra is initially udātta by upasargāś cābhivarjam (Phi. Sū. 81). This same accent stays after compounding, in the manner shown before.

भवत (bhavata) — before it is the āmantrita devāḥ; by āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat (Pā. Sū. 8-1-72) — a preceding word ending in a vocative first case is as if not there — the treatment as not there comes. And so bhavata does not follow a pada. It comes to be at the beginning of the pāda —

Page 219 (upper) — Rik 19: grammar (end)

— too. Since in the rule of the unaccented there is the heading padāt (Pā. Sū. 8-1-17), the unaccented comes only for what follows a pada. Since it is said anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau (Pā. Sū. 8-1-18), the unaccented does not come for what is at the beginning of a pāda. So for the word bhavata the total lack of accent by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) does not come. ॥19॥

Page 219 (lower) — Sūkta 23, Rik 20

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒प्सु मे॒ सोमो॑ अब्रवीद॒न्तर्विश्वा॑नि भेष॒जा । अ॒ग्निं च॑ वि॒श्वशं॑भुव॒माप॑श्च वि॒श्वभे॑षजीः ॥२०॥

apsú me sómo abravīd antár víśvāni bheṣajā́ | agníṃ ca viśváśaṃbhuvam ā́paś ca viśvábheṣajīḥ ||20|| Bars under अ (अप्सु), मे, द (अब्रवीद्) and ष (भेषजा); strokes over मो and श्वा. Line 2: bars under अ, व (विश्व), व (भुवम्) and व (विश्वभे); strokes over च, शं, प (आपश्) and भे.
