अप्ऽसु । मे । सोमः । अब्रवीत् । अन्तः । विश्वानि । भेषजा ॥ अग्निं । च । विश्वऽशंभुवं । आपः । च । विश्वऽभेषजीः ॥२०॥

ap 'su | me | somaḥ | abravīt | antaḥ | viśvāni | bheṣajā || agniṃ | ca | viśva 'śaṃbhuvaṃ | āpaḥ | ca | viśva 'bheṣajīḥ ||20||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Numbers as printed: आ० २-१३, तै० सं० २-६-६-१, पा० ६-२-१०६. The bhāṣya ends with ॥११॥, the close of the eleventh varga.

कारीर्यामुत्तरस्याज्यभागस्याप्सु म इत्येषानुवाक्या । वर्षकामेष्टिरिति खण्डेऽप्स्वग्ने सधिष्टवाप्सु मे सोमो अब्रवीत् । आ० २-१३ । इति सूत्रितं ॥

kārīryāmuttarasyājyabhāgasyāpsu ma ityeṣānuvākyā | varṣakāmeṣṭiriti khaṇḍe 'psvagne sadhiṣṭavāpsu me somo abravīt | ā0 2-13 | iti sūtritaṃ ||

Translation (application): "At the kārīrī [iṣṭi], this ṛk apsu me is the anuvākyā of the second ājyabhāga; it is laid down in the section varṣakāmeṣṭi: 'apsv agne sadhiṣ ṭava, apsu me somo abravīt' (Āśv. 2-13)."

अप्सु जलेष्वन्तर्मध्ये विश्वानि भेषजा सर्वाण्यौषधानि सन्तीति मे मह्यं मन्त्रदर्शिने मुनये सोमो देवोऽब्रवीत् । तथा विश्वशंभुवं सर्वस्य जगतः सुखकरमेतन्नामकं चाग्निं चाप्सु वर्तमानं सोमोऽब्रवीत् । तथा च तैत्तिरीया अग्नेस्त्रयो ज्यायांस इत्यनुवाके सोऽपः प्राविशदित्यग्नेरप्सु प्रवेशमामनन्ति । तै० सं० २-६-६-१ । लतागुल्मवृक्षमूलादीनामौषधानां वृष्टिजन्यत्वेन जलवर्तित्वं प्रसिद्धं । विश्वभेषजीः । विश्वानि भेषजानि यासु तथाविधा अपोऽप्यब्रवीत् ॥ भेषजा । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । विश्वशंभुवं । भवतेरन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात्क्विप् । व्यत्ययेन पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । यद्वा । विश्वे सर्वेऽपि व्यापाराः सुखकरा यस्य । बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायां । पा० ६-२-१०६ । इति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । आपः । कर्मणि शसि प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन जस् । अप्तृन्नित्यादिनोपधादीर्घः । विश्वभेषजीः । विश्वशंभुरितिवत् ॥११॥

apsu jaleṣvantarmadhye viśvāni bheṣajā sarvāṇyauṣadhāni santīti me mahyaṃ mantradarśine munaye somo devo 'bravīt | tathā viśvaśaṃbhuvaṃ sarvasya jagataḥ sukhakarametannāmakaṃ cāgniṃ cāpsu vartamānaṃ somo 'bravīt | tathā ca taittirīyā agnestrayo jyāyāṃsa ityanuvāke so 'paḥ prāviśadityagnerapsu praveśamāmananti | tai0 saṃ0 2-6-6-1 | latāgulmavṛkṣamūlādīnāmauṣadhānāṃ vṛṣṭijanyatvena jalavartitvaṃ prasiddhaṃ | viśvabheṣajīḥ | viśvāni bheṣajāni yāsu tathāvidhā apo 'pyabravīt || bheṣajā | supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | viśvaśaṃbhuvaṃ | bhavaterantarbhāvitaṇyarthātkvip | vyatyayena pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | yadvā | viśve sarve 'pi vyāpārāḥ sukhakarā yasya | bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyāṃ | pā0 6-2-106 | iti pūrvapadāntodāttatvaṃ | āpaḥ | karmaṇi śasi prāpte vyatyayena jas | aptṛnnityādinopadhādīrghaḥ | viśvabheṣajīḥ | viśvaśaṃbhuritivat ||11||

Translation: "Somaḥ, the god Soma, abravīt, told me, me, the seer who saw the mantra, that apsu antaḥ, within the waters, are viśvāni bheṣajā, all medicines. Likewise Soma told of Agni, viśvaśambhuvam, the bringer of happiness to the whole world, so named, who is in the waters. And so the Taittirīyas record in the anuvāka agnes trayo jyāyāṃsaḥ Agni's entry into the waters: 'he entered the waters' (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-6-1). That medicines such as creepers, bushes, the roots of trees and the like are in water, as they are produced by rain, is well known. Viśvabheṣajīḥ: he told also of the waters, such that all medicines are in them." (Grammatical tail: bheṣajā, the ā by supāṃ suluk; viśvaśambhuvam, kvip after bhū with the causative sense included; the first member's own accent by vyatyaya; or: 'whose all activities make happiness': in the bahuvrīhi the first member is final udātta by bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām (Pā. 6-2-106); āpaḥ, śas being due in the object sense, jas by vyatyaya; the lengthening of the penultimate by aptṛn…; viśvabheṣajīḥ, as for viśvaśambhuḥ.)

Page 220 — Rik 20: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अप्सु अन्तः (apsu antaḥ) — in the midst of the waters | विश्वानि (viśvāni) — all | भेषजा (bheṣajā) — medicines that destroy disease, that there are | अग्निं च (agniṃ ca) — Agni | विश्वशंभुवं (viśvaśambhuvaṃ) — as the one who makes happiness for the whole world | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters | विश्वभेषजीः (viśvabheṣajīḥ) — as furnished with all medicines that destroy disease | सोमः (somaḥ) — the deity Soma | मे (me) — to me | अब्रवीत् (abravīt) — told.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

In the midst of the waters are all the medicines that remove diseases. Agni makes happiness for the whole world; the waters are joined with all medicines. So the deity Soma told me.

॥ English Translation ॥

Soma has revealed to me that in the waters are all medicaments; that Agni is the benefactor of the Universe, the waters contain all the healing medicines.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In the kārīrī sacrifice this ṛk apsu me is recited as the puronuvākyā mantra when making the ājyabhāga offering. On this matter, in the section varṣakāmeṣṭi of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, it is said that the ṛks apsv agne sadhiṣ ṭava (8-43-9) and apsu me somo abravīt (1-23-20) are to be used as the yājyā and puronuvākyā mantras (Ā. 2-13). The main intention of this ṛk: Soma himself told me that Agni, who makes happiness for the whole world, is in the waters in the form of lightning, and that all the herbs that cure the diseases of living beings are in the waters themselves. On the point that Agni is in the waters, the commentator has cited the sentence so 'paḥ prāviśat taṃ devatāḥ praiṣam aicchan from the anuvāka agnes trayo jyāyāṃso bhrātara āsan in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 2-6-6-1). We have explained before ( [blank in the print] ) its explanation and the explanation on this subject in the Ṛgveda.

सोऽपः प्राविशत्तं देवताः प्रैषमैच्छन् ।

so 'paḥ prāviśattaṃ devatāḥ praiṣamaicchan |

अग्निं च विश्वशंभुवं (agniṃ ca viśvaśambhuvaṃ) — there is no need to explain at length the benefit that comes to the whole world from Agni. Besides giving us warmth when it is cold, we use Agni for cooking food and in many other useful or most necessary works.

Page 221 — Rik 20: Special Topics (end), grammar

Since this matter is known by everyone's experience, there is no need to say more.

आपश्च विश्वभेषजीः (āpaś ca viśvabheṣajīḥ) — we have explained in the previous ṛk itself what the part of water is in curing diseases.

सोमः (somaḥ) — for the word soma the commentator has said somadevaḥ, the deity Soma. Soma here is to be known as the Moon, the presiding deity of plants and trees.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

भेषजा (bheṣajā) — by supāṃ suluk (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the substitute ā for the nominative plural jas.

विश्वशंभुवम् (viśvaśambhuvam) — viśvasya śaṃ bhavatīti (bhāvayatīti) viśvaśambhūḥ, tam: so the analysis. Here after the root bhū with the causative sense included, by kvip ca (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76) kvip; the sup, a part of a nominal stem, is dropped (luk): viśvaśambhū; after it the accusative singular am; by na bhūsudhiyoḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-4-85) the yaṇ is barred; by aci śnudhātu… (Pā. Sū. 6-4-77) the substitute uvaṅ: it becomes viśvaśambhuvam. Here, though by samāsasya (Pā. Sū. 6-1-223) the final udātta (which is satiśiṣṭa) would be right, by vyatyaya [it is said that] the first member viśva gets the final udātta. By śeṣanighāta the other letters are unaccented. Among them the unaccented ś syllable becomes svarita by udāttād anudāttasya… (Pā. Sū. 8-4-66). The other two letters, by svaritāt saṃhitāyām anudāttānām (Pā. Sū. 1-2-39), are in the monotone (pracaya): this is the situation. Here the word viśva is formed by the suffix kvan by aśūpruṣilaṭi… (U. Sū. 1-149). So at (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-9-1) it has been described as initially udātta by ñnity ādir nityam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197). So if the first member's own accent is said here by vyatyaya, the initial udātta would have to come; then the form viśvaśambhuvam [with that accent] would not result: it must be viśvaśambhuvam [with final udātta on viśva]. So in the Veda commentary vyatyayena pūrvapadāntodāttatvam is the right reading. Yet through the carelessness of the proof-readers and others it may have dropped to vyatyayena pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam. However this may be, in describing the meaning there is no description by the commentator of a meaning that fits this derivation. So it is clear that the commentator was not pleased with this derivation. That is why he begins with yadvā and gives another derivation: viśve — all activities; śambhuvaḥ — that make happiness; yasya — whose; saḥ — he is viśvaśambhūḥ, tam: a bahuvrīhi compound. On this view the compound-final udātta —

व्यत्ययेन पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । व्यत्ययेन पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ।

vyatyayena pūrvapadāntodāttatvam | vyatyayena pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam |

Page 222 — Rik 20: grammar (end)

— overriding it, by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the first member's own accent would be due. But in bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām (Pā. Sū. 6-2-106), pūrvapadam from bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) is carried on. It must be changed into the genitive case to suit the meaning of the present sentence; antaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-2-92) is the heading. So it becomes pūrvapadasya antaḥ; by ādir udāttaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-2-64) udāttaḥ is carried on. Saṃjñāyām is a qualifier of the whole; and so, when a name is shown by the whole, the end of the word viśva, the first member of a bahuvrīhi compound, is udātta: so viśva is final udātta. On this view there is no trouble of having to establish the accent by vyatyaya.

आपः (āpaḥ) — this is the object word with regard to the root abravīt. So when the object sense is intended, by the teaching karmaṇi dvitīyā (Pā. Sū. 2-3-2) the second case; and since the word ap always ends in the plural, when the plurality of the object sense is intended, by bahuṣu bahuvacanam (Pā. Sū. 1-4-21) it would be right for the accusative plural śas to come. Yet by vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85), by interchange, the nominative plural case-ending jas has come here: ap + as. Now since the suffix as, named sarvanāmasthāna, follows, by aptṛntṛc… (Pā. Sū. 6-4-11) — when a sarvanāmasthāna other than the vocative follows, the penultimate letter of the word ap and of words ending in the suffixes tṛn and the rest is lengthened — lengthening: āpas; for the s, ru and visarga.

विश्वभेषजीः (viśvabheṣajīḥ) — viśvāni bheṣajāni yāsu tāḥ: so the analysis; here, overriding the first member's own accent caused by the bahuvrīhi, the first member gets the final udātta in the manner stated at viśvaśambhuvam. By bhiyaḥ ṣug ghrasvaś ca (U. Sū. 1-135 as printed at zoom: ∩, ∩, ಇ, lobed 5; the last digit is not clear between 5 and 4) — after the root ñibhī bhaye, the suffix aj and the augment ṣuk for the root — when the suffix aj, shortening of the root and the augment ṣuk come after the root bhī, it becomes bhiṣaj. Bhiṣajaḥ imāḥ: so the analysis. By tasyedam (Pā. Sū. 4-3-120) the suffix aṇ: bhiṣaj + a; now since the suffix is ṇit, by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-2-117) vṛddhi in bhi would give bhai; yet by set form e comes for the ī of bhi. When the feminine is intended, ṅīṣ comes and it becomes bheṣajī. The ī of ṅīṣ is udātta by the suffix accent. An ornament follows.

ā́paḥ pṛṇītá bheṣajáṃ várūthaṃ tanvè máma | [accent ?] jyok ca sū́ryaṃ dṛśé ||21|| Strokes over प (आपः), भे, रू and म (the second of मम); bars under णी, ष (भेषजं) and त (तन्वे); after तन्वे the print has the independent-svarita sign ३ with a stroke above and a bar below, written here ३॒॑. हे आपो मम तन्वे शरीरार्थं वरूथं रोगनिवारकं भेषजमौषधं पृणीत । पूरयत । किंच ज्योक् चिरं सूर्यं दृशे द्रष्टुं नीरोगा वयं शक्नुयामेति शेषः ॥ पृणीत । पॄ पालनपूरणयोः । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनं थ । तस्य तस्थस्थमिपामिति तादेशः । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । प्वादीनां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वः । ई हल्यघोरितीत्वं । ऋवर्णाच्चेति णत्वं । सतिशिष्टस्वरबलीयस्त्वमन्यत्र विकरणेभ्य इति तिङः स्वरः शिष्यते । आप इत्यस्यामन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदित्यविद्यमानवत्त्वे पादादित्वान्निघाताभावः । वरूथं । वृञ् वरणे । जॄवृञ्भ्यामूथन् । उ० २-६ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । तन्वे । ङिति ह्रस्वश्च । पा० १-४-६ । इति नदीसंज्ञा पाक्षिकीत्याडागमाभावः । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्त्युदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेनोदात्तस्वरितयोरिति स्वरितत्वं । दृशे । दृशे विख्ये च । पा० ३-४-११ । इति तुमर्थे निपात्यते ॥

he āpo mama tanve śarīrārthaṃ varūthaṃ roganivārakaṃ bheṣajamauṣadhaṃ pṛṇīta | pūrayata | kiṃca jyok ciraṃ sūryaṃ dṛśe draṣṭuṃ nīrogā vayaṃ śaknuyāmeti śeṣaḥ || pṛṇīta | pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ | loṇmadhyamabahuvacanaṃ tha | tasya tasthasthamipāmiti tādeśaḥ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | pvādīnāṃ hrasva iti hrasvaḥ | ī halyaghoritītvaṃ | ṛvarṇācceti ṇatvaṃ | satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvamanyatra vikaraṇebhya iti tiṅaḥ svaraḥ śiṣyate | āpa ityasyāmantritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavadityavidyamānavattve pādāditvānnighātābhāvaḥ | varūthaṃ | vṛñ varaṇe | jṝvṛñbhyāmūthan | u0 2-6 | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | tanve | ṅiti hrasvaśca | pā0 1-4-6 | iti nadīsaṃjñā pākṣikītyāḍāgamābhāvaḥ | udāttayaṇo halpūrvāditi vibhaktyudāttatve prāpte vyatyayenodāttasvaritayoriti svaritatvaṃ | dṛśe | dṛśe vikhye ca | pā0 3-4-11 | iti tumarthe nipātyate ||

Translation: "O āpaḥ, waters! Pṛṇīta, fill up, bheṣajam, medicine, varūtham, that wards off disease, tanve mama, for my body. And jyok, long, may we, free from disease, be able dṛśe, to see, sūryam, the sun: this is to be supplied." (Grammatical tail: pṛṇīta, pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ, tha of loṭ second person plural, ta for it by tasthasthamipām…, śnā by kryādibhyaḥ śnā, shortening by pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ, ī by ī halyaghoḥ, ṇ by ṛvarṇāc ca; by satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvam anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ the accent of the tiṅ remains; since the vocative āpaḥ is treated as not there by āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat, the word is at the beginning of the pāda, so no loss of accent; varūtham, vṛñ varaṇe, ūthan by jṝvṛñbhyām ūthan (U. 2-6), initial udātta as nit; tanve, the nadī name by ṅiti hrasvaś ca (Pā. 1-4-6) being optional, no augment āṭ; the case-ending udātta being due by udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt, by vyatyaya svarita by udāttasvaritayoḥ…; dṛśe, given as a set form in the infinitive sense by dṛśe vikhye ca (Pā. 3-4-11).)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

आपः (āpaḥ) — O waters, or O deities presiding over the waters | मम (mama) — my | तन्वे (tanve) — for the body | वरूथं (varūthaṃ) — that wards off disease | भेषजं (bheṣajaṃ) — medicine | पृणीत (pṛṇīta) — make full (that is, make the body full, so that it is without disease) | (by doing so I) सूर्यं (sūryaṃ) — the sun | ज्योक् (jyok) — for a long time | दृशे (dṛśe) — will see (will be able to see, that is, will be able to live long).

Page 224 — Rik 21: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O waters (or O deities presiding over the waters), so that my body may be without disease, make the excellent medicine full (make it ready); then, free from disease, may I see the sun for a long time, that is, may I live long.

॥ English Translation ॥

Waters, grant me a medicament that shall be an armour to my body that I may long behold the Sun.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

पृणीत (pṛṇīta) — pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ || make full: the intention is, make the body without diseases and the like, and able to do its work in order.

वरूथं (varūthaṃ) — varaṇīyam, roganivārakam || to be desired, that is, warding off disease.

ज्योक् च सूर्यं दृशे (jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśe) — seeing the sun for a long time, that is, living long. There are some ṛks in the Ṛgveda that suggest this same intention —

तस्मा अग्निर्भारतः शर्म यंसज्ज्योक्पश्यात्सूर्यमुच्चरन्तं । (ऋ० सं० ४-२५-४) तव क्रत्वा तवोतिभिर्ज्योक्पश्येम सूर्यं ॥ (ऋ० सं० ९-४-६) शं नः क्षेत्रमुरु ज्योतींषि सोम ज्योङ्नः सूर्यं दृशये रिरीहि ॥ (ऋ० सं० ९-९१-६) उद्यन्तं त्वा मित्रमहो दिवेदिवे ज्योग्जीवाः प्रति पश्येम सूर्य ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-३७-७) ज्योक्पश्येम सूर्यमुच्चरन्तमनुमते मृळया नः स्वस्ति ॥ (ऋ० सं० १०-५९-६)

tasmā agnirbhārataḥ śarma yaṃsajjyokpaśyātsūryamuccarantaṃ | (ṛ0 saṃ0 4-25-4) tava kratvā tavotibhirjyokpaśyema sūryaṃ || (ṛ0 saṃ0 9-4-6) śaṃ naḥ kṣetramuru jyotīṃṣi soma jyoṅnaḥ sūryaṃ dṛśaye rirīhi || (ṛ0 saṃ0 9-91-6) udyantaṃ tvā mitramaho divedive jyogjīvāḥ prati paśyema sūrya || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-37-7) jyokpaśyema sūryamuccarantamanumate mṛḷayā naḥ svasti || (ṛ0 saṃ0 10-59-6)

Besides these, in the Yajurveda too there are many sentences suggesting this intention, such as —

पश्येम शरदः शतं … ज्योक् च सूर्यं दृशे । ज्योक् च पश्यामि सूर्यं ।

paśyema śaradaḥ śataṃ … jyok ca sūryaṃ dṛśe | jyok ca paśyāmi sūryaṃ |

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

पृणीत (pṛṇīta) — the root pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ. Loṭ, second person plural, the suffix tha: pṝ + tha. By loṭo laṅvat (Pā. Sū. 3-4-85) [the extension] —

Page 225 — Rik 21: grammar (continued)

— the operations of laṅ come to loṭ: so the treatment as laṅ. By tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-101) — for the four suffixes tas, thas, tha, mip the substitutes tām, tam, ta, am come in order — the substitute ta for tha: pṝ + ta. By kryādibhyaḥ śnā (Pā. Sū. 3-1-81) — when a sārvadhātuka suffix in the agent sense follows, the vikaraṇa suffix śnā (nā) comes after a root of the kryādi class — so when śnā comes: pṝ + nā + ta. By pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-80) — the roots read in the list of roots beginning with pūñ pavane are shortened — the ṝ of pṝ is shortened to ṛ: pṛ + nā + ta. By ī halyaghoḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-4-113) — when a consonant-initial sārvadhātuka that is kit or ṅit follows, the ā of the suffix śnā and the ā of a reduplicated stem take the substitute ī — when the substitute ī comes: pṛ + nī + ta. Ṛvarṇāc ceti vaktavyam: this is a paraphrase of the meaning of raṣābhyāṃ ṇatve ṛkāragrahaṇam (Pā. Sū. 8-4-1, vārttika 1). Its meaning is that ṇ is substituted for the n after ṛ. By this the n gets the substitute ṇ, and it becomes pṛṇīta.

आपः (āpaḥ) — this ends in the vocative first case. So by sāmantritam (Pā. Sū. 2-3-48) — what ends in the vocative first case gets the name āmantrita — it has the name āmantrita. So by āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat (Pā. Sū. 8-1-72) — the preceding āmantrita is avidyamānavat, that is, as if not there though it is there — the treatment as not there comes. So pṛṇīta does not follow a pada; it is at the beginning of the pāda. So since there is no word not ending in tiṅ before the word ending in tiṅ, the total lack of accent by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ does not come. Satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvam anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ: in the matter of vikaraṇas, though it is satiśiṣṭa, that is, comes last, that accent is not stronger: so they say with anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ. The ta, the tiṅ suffix, gets the initial udātta by the suffix accent. The others are unaccented by the śeṣānudātta accent.

वरूथम् (varūtham) — the root vṛñ varaṇe. By jṝvṛñbhyām ūthan (U. Sū. 2-163, zoom-checked) — after the roots jṝ vayohānau of the kryādi class, jṝṣ vayohānau of the divādi class, and vṛñ varaṇe, the suffix ūthan comes — when ūthan comes: vṛ + ūtha. The ṛ takes guṇa; it becomes ar: it becomes varūtha. The suffix is nit; so by the nit accent initial udātta comes.

तन्वे (tanve) — the root tanu vistāre. By bhṛmṛśītṛcaritsaritanidhanimimasjibhya uḥ (U. Sū. 1-7, zoom-checked: the flat-footed 7) — after the roots bhṛñ bharaṇe, mṛṅ prāṇatyāge, śīṅ svapne, tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, cara gatibhakṣaṇayoḥ, tsara chadmagatau, tanu vistāre, dhana dhānye, ḍumiñ prakṣepaṇe, ṭumasjo śuddhau, the suffix u comes — so after the root tan the suffix u: tan + u = tanu, final udātta by the suffix accent. After it the dative case-ending ṅe: tanu + e. Ṅiti hrasvaś ca (Pā. Sū. 1-4-6):

Page 226 — Rik 21: grammar (end)

here, since there is the word ca, two sentences result. Yū stryākhyau nadī is carried on: īś ca ūś ca = yū. Since it is a sūtra, though there is an ic vowel after the long vowel, the prohibition of the long like vowel by dīrghāj jasi ca (Pā. Sū. 6-1-105) does not come. Striyam evācakṣāte iti stryākhyau: those that convey only the feminine, that is, always feminine: this is the meaning. Neyaṅuvaṅsthānāv astrī (Pā. Sū. 1-4-4): the whole sūtra except na is carried on: iyaṅuvaṅoḥ sthānaṃ = sthitiḥ yayoḥ tau: the meaning is, fit to get the substitutes iyaṅ, uvaṅ. By vāmi (Pā. Sū. 1-4-5) vā comes; and so when a suffix with the it-name ṅ follows, words ending in ī and ū, always feminine, fit to get the substitutes iyaṅ, uvaṅ, other than the word strī, optionally get the name nadī: this is the meaning of the first sentence ṅiti. Hrasvaś ca is the second sentence. Here the words yū stryākhyau nadī vā ṅiti are carried on. And so, when a suffix with the it-name ṅ follows, words ending in short i or short u optionally get the name nadī: this is its meaning. The meaning of the first sentence does not apply here. Though the meaning of the second sentence applies, since it says 'optionally' there, here the word tanu does not have the name nadī. So by āṇ nadyāḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-112) the augment āṭ does not come; by the yaṇ substitute, when v comes for the u, it becomes tanve. Here, since e is a sup, by anudāttau suppitau the unaccented would be due. Overriding it, by udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt (Pā. Sū. 6-1-174) — y, v, l that have come in place of an udātta letter and are after a consonant: the nadī-named letters and the case-endings śas and the rest coming after such y, v, l are also udātta — the udātta would be due for the e after the v. Yet since it is said vyatyayo bahulam, here, contrary to this, by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4) — the unaccented after a yaṇ that has come in place of an udātta or svarita becomes svarita — the unaccented e becomes svarita. To make this svarita known, the numeral ३ is indicated after it.

दृशे (dṛśe) — the root dṛśir prekṣaṇe. Dṛśe vikhye ca (Pā. Sū. 3-4-11): the meaning is that in the sense of the suffix tumun, that is, in the action sense, the two forms dṛśe and vikhye are given as set forms. Here, after the root dṛś and after the root khyā preceded by the prefix vi, the suffix ke is given as a set form in the sense of the suffix tumun. Dṛś + e: the suffix is kit, so dṛś does not take guṇa of the light penultimate. In vikhyā + e, since the suffix is kit, by āto lopa iṭi ca (Pā. Sū. 6-4-64) the ā is dropped. ॥21॥

Rik 22 pp. 227

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

इ॒दमा॑पः॒ प्र व॑हत॒ यत्किं च॑ दुरि॒तं मयि॑ । यद्वा॒हम॑भिदु॒द्रोह॒ यद्वा॑ शे॒प उ॒तानृ॑तं ॥२२॥

idám āpaḥ prá vahata yát kíṃ ca duritáṃ máyi | yad vāhám abhidudróha yád vā śepá utā́nṛtaṃ ||22|| Bars under इ, पः, त (वहत) and रि; strokes over मा, व (वहत), च and यि. Line 2: bars under द्वा, दु and शे; strokes over म (अहम्), द्वा (the second यद्वा) and नृ; a bar under उ (उत).

इदं । आपः । प्र । वहत । यत् । किं । च । दुःऽइतं । मयि ॥ यत् । वा । अहं । अभिऽदुद्रोह । यत् । वा । शेपे । उत । अनृतं ॥२२॥

idaṃ | āpaḥ | pra | vahata | yat | kiṃ | ca | duḥ 'itaṃ | mayi || yat | vā | ahaṃ | abhi 'dudroha | yat | vā | śepe | uta | anṛtaṃ ||22||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Numbers as printed: आ० ३-५, ६-१३, पा० ६-४-१२०.

पशौ मार्जन इदमापः प्र वहतेत्येषा विनियुक्ता । हुतायां वपायामिति खण्डे सूत्रितं । इदमापः प्रवहत । आ० ३-५ । इति ॥ एषैवावभृथेष्टौ स्नाने विनियुक्ता । पत्नीसंयाजैश्चरित्वेति खण्ड इदमापः प्र वहत सुमित्र्या न आप ओषधयः सन्तु । आ० ६-१३ । इति सूत्रितं ॥

paśau mārjana idamāpaḥ pra vahatetyeṣā viniyuktā | hutāyāṃ vapāyāmiti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | idamāpaḥ pravahata | ā0 3-5 | iti || eṣaivāvabhṛtheṣṭau snāne viniyuktā | patnīsaṃyājaiścaritveti khaṇḍa idamāpaḥ pra vahata sumitryā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu | ā0 6-13 | iti sūtritaṃ ||

Translation (application): "At the animal sacrifice, at the cleansing, this ṛk idam āpaḥ pra vahata is used; it is laid down in the section hutāyāṃ vapāyām: 'idam āpaḥ pra vahata' (Āśv. 3-5). This same ṛk is used at the bath in the avabhṛtha-iṣṭi; it is laid down in the section patnīsaṃyājaiś caritvā: 'idam āpaḥ pra vahata, sumitryā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu' (Āśv. 6-13)."

मयि यजमाने यत्किं च दुरितमज्ञानान्निष्पन्नं । वाथवाहं यजमानोऽभिदुद्रोह सर्वतो बुद्धिपूर्वकं द्रोहं कृतवानस्मि वाथवा शेपे साधुजनं शप्तवानस्मीति यदस्ति । उतापि चानृतमुक्तवानिति यदस्ति । तदिदं सर्वमपराधजातं प्र वहत । मत्तोऽपनीय प्रवाहेणान्यतो नयत ॥ मयि । मपर्यन्तस्य त्वमावेकवचन इति मादेशे कृतेऽतो गुण इति पररूपे च सति योऽचीति दकारस्य यकारादेशः । एकादेशस्वरेण मकारात्परस्याकारस्योदात्तत्वं । दुद्रोह । द्रुह जिघांसायां । णलि गुणे द्विर्वचनह्रस्वहलादिशेषाः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं । यद्वृत्तयोगान्निघाताभावः । शेपे । शप आक्रोशे । लिटि व्यत्ययेन तङ् । उत्तमैकवचनमिट् । टेरेत्वं । अत एकहल्मध्ये । पा० ६-४-१२० । इत्येत्वाभ्यासलोपौ । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वं । पूर्ववन्निघाताभावः ॥

mayi yajamāne yatkiṃ ca duritamajñānānniṣpannaṃ | vāthavāhaṃ yajamāno 'bhidudroha sarvato buddhipūrvakaṃ drohaṃ kṛtavānasmi vāthavā śepe sādhujanaṃ śaptavānasmīti yadasti | utāpi cānṛtamuktavāniti yadasti | tadidaṃ sarvamaparādhajātaṃ pra vahata | matto 'panīya pravāheṇānyato nayata || mayi | maparyantasya tvamāvekavacana iti mādeśe kṛte 'to guṇa iti pararūpe ca sati yo 'cīti dakārasya yakārādeśaḥ | ekādeśasvareṇa makārātparasyākārasyodāttatvaṃ | dudroha | druha jighāṃsāyāṃ | ṇali guṇe dvirvacanahrasvahalādiśeṣāḥ | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvaṃ | yadvṛttayogānnighātābhāvaḥ | śepe | śapa ākrośe | liṭi vyatyayena taṅ | uttamaikavacanamiṭ | ṭeretvaṃ | ata ekahalmadhye | pā0 6-4-120 | ityetvābhyāsalopau | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttatvaṃ | pūrvavannighātābhāvaḥ ||

Translation: "Whatever duritam, sin arising from ignorance, there is mayi, in me, the sacrificer; or, yad vā, what there is of my, the sacrificer's, having abhidudroha, done hurt knowingly on all sides; or of my having śepe, cursed, good people; uta, and also of my having spoken anṛtam, falsehood — idam, all this mass of offences, pra vahata, carry away: taking it from me, lead it elsewhere by your current." (Grammatical tail: mayi, after the substitute ma by tvamāv ekavacane for the part up to m, and the following form by ato guṇe, y for the d by yo 'ci; the a after m udātta by the single-substitute accent; dudroha, druha jighāṃsāyām, with ṇal, guṇa, reduplication, shortening and halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; the syllable before the suffix udātta by liti; no loss of accent because of connection with yad; śepe, śapa ākrośe, in liṭ the middle endings by vyatyaya, first person singular iṭ, e for the ṭi, the e and the dropping of the reduplicate by ata ekahalmadhye… (Pā. 6-4-120); final udātta by the suffix accent; no loss of accent as before.)

Page 228 — Rik 22: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

मयि (mayi) — in me, the sacrificer | यत्किं च (yat kiṃ ca) — whatever | दुरितं (duritaṃ) — sins done through ignorance there are | वा (vā) — or | अहं (ahaṃ) — I | यत् अभिदुद्रोह (yat abhidudroha) — though I have done hurt (to anyone) knowingly | वा (vā) — or | यत् शेपे (yat śepe) — though I have spoken evil words about someone | उत (uta) — and | अनृतं (anṛtaṃ) — though (I have spoken) a lie | इदं (idaṃ) — such sin | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters | प्र वहत (pra vahata) — (separating it from me) may they carry it away in the form of a current.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

May the waters (the flowing water) carry away in their current all such sins: the sins that may be in me, done through ignorance; or if I have done hurt to anyone; or if I have spoken evil words; and if I have told lies.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Waters, whatever sin there is in me, whatever ill-will I may have borne to others, whatever imprecations I may have uttered, and whatever falschood [sic] I may have told, wash it away all from me.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In the animal sacrifice this ṛk idam āpaḥ pra vahata is recited for the cleansing (sprinkling). In the section hutāyāṃ vapāyām of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra it is said that the ṛk idam āpaḥ pra vahata is to be recited as the cleansing mantra (Ā. 3-5). Besides this, in the avabhṛtha-iṣṭi performed at the end of the sacrifice, this mantra is used at the time of bathing. This matter is stated in the section patnīsaṃyājaiś caritvā, that the mantras idam āpaḥ pra vahata and sumitryā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu are to be recited (Ā. 6-13).

दुरितं (duritaṃ) — ajñānān niṣpannaṃ kāyikaṃ pāpam || the sin in the form of acts done through ignorance or knowingly, that is, sins done by the use of force, such as beating someone: this is the meaning.

अभिदुद्रोह (abhidudroha) — thinking evil with the mind is called droha. This is a sin of the mind.

शेपे, अनृतं (śepe, anṛtaṃ) — cursing, telling lies and the like are sins done by speech. These are of speech. The prayer is that the flowing water may carry away these three kinds of sins.

Page 229 (upper) — Rik 22: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

मयि (mayi) — the word yuṣmad [as printed; for asmad], locative singular; for the part up to m, by tvamāv ekavacane (Pā. Sū. 7-2-97) the substitute ma: ma + ad + i; by ato guṇe (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) the following form: mad + i; by yo 'ci (Pā. Sū. 7-2-89) — when a vowel-initial case-ending without a substitute follows, the d of the words yuṣmad, asmad takes y — so when y comes it becomes tvayi [as printed; mayi].

दुद्रोह (dudroha) — the root druha jighāṃsāyām. Liṭ, parasmaipada, third person singular ti; by parasmaipadānāṃ ṇal… (Pā. Sū. 3-4-82) ṇal: druh + a. By liṭi dhātoḥ… (Pā. Sū. 6-1-8) reduplication. By hrasvaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-4-59) shortening: though it is already short here, since it is said parjanyaval lakṣaṇaṃ pravartate (Paribhā. 120), the shortening comes. By halādiḥ śeṣaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-4-60) the r and h of the first druh are dropped: dudruh + a, guṇa of the light penultimate. Yadvṛttān nityam (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66): a word ending in tiṅ after a word in which there is the word yad is not unaccented. Here, by the further mention of pūjita in pūjanāt pūjitam (Pā. Sū. 8-1-67), it is made known that atra prakaraṇe pañcamīnirdeśe 'pi nānantaryam iṣyate. So even though there is an intervention, the prohibition of the unaccented comes by this. In the same way in śepe too the unaccented is barred.

पर्जन्यवल्लक्षणं प्रवर्तते । अत्र प्रकरणे पञ्चमीनिर्देशेऽपि नानन्तर्यमिष्यते ।

parjanyavallakṣaṇaṃ pravartate | atra prakaraṇe pañcamīnirdeśe 'pi nānantaryamiṣyate |

शेपे (śepe) — the root śapa ākrośe; liṭ: though this is a parasmaipada root, the middle-voice suffix comes by vyatyaya. First person singular, iṭ: śap + i. By ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e (Pā. Sū. 3-4-79) e for the i; reduplication; by ata ekahalmadhye 'nādeśāder liṭi (Pā. Sū. 6-4-120) — when a liṭ that is kit follows, a short a standing between single consonants and belonging to a stem whose initial is not a substitute takes e, and the reduplicate is dropped — when the e and the dropping of the reduplicate come, it becomes śepe. ॥22॥ An ornament follows.

āpaḥ | adya | anu | acāriṣaṃ | rasena | saṃ | agasmahi || payasvān | agne | ā | gahi | taṃ | mā | saṃ | sṛja | varcasā ||23||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Numbers as printed: आ० ३-६, पा० ७-२-३५, ७-२-४, ७-२-२, १-३-२९, १-२-१३.

पशावाहवनीयोपस्थान आपो अद्यान्वचारिषमित्येषा । मनोतायै संप्रेषित इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । एत्योपतिष्ठन्त आपो अद्यान्वचारिषं । आ० ३-६ । इति ॥

paśāvāhavanīyopasthāna āpo adyānvacāriṣamityeṣā | manotāyai saṃpreṣita iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | etyopatiṣṭhanta āpo adyānvacāriṣaṃ | ā0 3-6 | iti ||

Translation (application): "At the animal sacrifice, at the attendance on the āhavanīya, this ṛk āpo adyānv acāriṣam; it is laid down in the section manotāyai saṃpreṣite: 'having come, they attend with āpo adyānv acāriṣam' (Āśv. 3-6)."

अद्यास्मिन्दिनेऽवभृथार्थमापोऽन्वचारिषं । जलान्यनुप्रविष्टोऽस्मि । प्रविश्य च रसेन जलसारेण समगस्महि । संगताः स्मः । हे अग्ने पयस्वान् जले वर्तमानत्वेन पयोयुक्तस्त्वमा गहि । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यागच्छ । तं मा तादृशं स्नातं मां वर्चसा तेजसा सं सृज । संयोजय ॥ आपः । कर्मणि शसि प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन जस् । अचारिषं । चर गत्यर्थः । लुङि च्लेः सिच् । आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः । पा० ७-२-३५ । इतीट् । नेटि । पा० ७-२-४ । इति वृद्धिप्रतिषेधेऽप्राप्ते तदपवादतयातो ल्रान्तस्य । पा० ७-२-२ । इत्युपधाया वृद्धिः । अगस्महि । समो गम्यृच्छिभ्यामित्यात्मनेपदं । पा० १-३-२९ । च्लेः सिच् । मन्त्रे घसेत्यादिना च्लेर्लुगभावश्छान्दसः । एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तादितीट्प्रतिषेधः । वा गमः । पा० १-२-१३ । इति सिचः कित्त्वादनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । गहि । लोटि गमेः सिपो हिः । अपित्त्वेन ङित्त्वादनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । अतो हेरिति लुग्न भवति । असिद्धवदत्राभादिति मलोपस्यासिद्धत्वात् ॥

adyāsmindine 'vabhṛthārthamāpo 'nvacāriṣaṃ | jalānyanupraviṣṭo 'smi | praviśya ca rasena jalasāreṇa samagasmahi | saṃgatāḥ smaḥ | he agne payasvān jale vartamānatvena payoyuktastvamā gahi | asminkarmaṇyāgaccha | taṃ mā tādṛśaṃ snātaṃ māṃ varcasā tejasā saṃ sṛja | saṃyojaya || āpaḥ | karmaṇi śasi prāpte vyatyayena jas | acāriṣaṃ | cara gatyarthaḥ | luṅi cleḥ sic | ārdhadhātukasyeḍvalādeḥ | pā0 7-2-35 | itīṭ | neṭi | pā0 7-2-4 | iti vṛddhipratiṣedhe 'prāpte tadapavādatayāto lrāntasya | pā0 7-2-2 | ityupadhāyā vṛddhiḥ | agasmahi | samo gamyṛcchibhyāmityātmanepadaṃ | pā0 1-3-29 | cleḥ sic | mantre ghasetyādinā clerlugabhāvaśchāndasaḥ | ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāditīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | vā gamaḥ | pā0 1-2-13 | iti sicaḥ kittvādanudāttopadeśetyādinānunāsikalopaḥ | gahi | loṭi gameḥ sipo hiḥ | apittvena ṅittvādanudāttopadeśetyādinānunāsikalopaḥ | ato heriti lugna bhavati | asiddhavadatrābhāditi malopasyāsiddhatvāt ||

Translation: "Adya, on this day, for the avabhṛtha, I anv acāriṣam, have entered after, the āpaḥ, waters. And having entered, rasena, with the essence of the waters, we sam agasmahi, have come together. O Agni, payasvān, furnished with water as being in the waters, ā gahi, come, to this rite. Tam mā, me, such a one, bathed, saṃ sṛja, join, varcasā, with splendour." (Grammatical tail: āpaḥ, śas being due in the object sense, jas by vyatyaya; acāriṣam, cara in the sense of going, sic for cli in luṅ, iṭ by ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ (Pā. 7-2-35); since the bar on vṛddhi by neṭi (Pā. 7-2-4) does not apply, as its exception ato lrāntasya (Pā. 7-2-2) gives vṛddhi of the penultimate; agasmahi, middle voice by samo gamyṛcchibhyām (Pā. 1-3-29); sic for cli; the absence of luk of cli by mantre ghasa… is Vedic; iṭ barred by ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt; sic is kit by vā gamaḥ (Pā. 1-2-13), so the nasal is dropped by anudāttopadeśa…; gahi, hi for sip of gam in loṭ; being ṅit as not pit, the nasal dropped by anudāttopadeśa…; hi is not dropped by ato heḥ, since the dropping of m is asiddha by asiddhavad atrābhāt.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

अद्य (adya) — now (on this day) | आपः (āpaḥ) — the water | अन्वचारिषं (anvacāriṣaṃ) — I have entered (for the avabhṛtha bath) | (then) रसेन (rasena) — with the essence of water | समगस्महि (samagasmahi) — we have come together | (हे) अग्ने ((he) agne) — O Agni | पयस्वान् (payasvān) — you, joined with water, that is, being in the water | आ गहि (ā gahi) — come (into this bathing rite) | (and) तं मा (taṃ mā) — me (who have bathed) | वर्चसा (varcasā) — with splendour | संसृज (saṃsṛja) — join.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Now I have entered the water for the (avabhṛtha) bath. May all the essence that is in the water join with us. O Agni, since you are in the water, come to this bathing rite and make me, who have bathed, splendid.

Page 231 — Rik 23: English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

I have this day entered into the waters; we have mingled with their essence; O Agni, existing in the waters, approach and fill me with vigour.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

In the animal sacrifice, at the time of attending on the āhavanīya fire, they recite the ṛk āpo adyānv acāriṣam. This matter is stated in the section manotāyai saṃpreṣite of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra, in the sūtra etyopatiṣṭhanta āpo adyānv acāriṣam (Ā. 3-6).

आपः (āpaḥ) — Skandasvāmin too says dvitīyārthe prathamā: the word āpaḥ, in the first case, is to be given the meaning of the second case.

रसेन (rasena) — jalasāreṇa: with the essence of water, "essence of water". The intention is: may pure water remove the faults (the dirt) inside and outside my body.

पयस्वान् (payasvān) — payasā jalena yuktaḥ, or payasi tiṣṭhatīti payasvān: he who is in the water. In the Yajurveda, sentences such as so 'paḥ prāviśat say that Agni hid himself in the water. So it is said on many occasions that Agni is in the water. The second half of this ṛk has Agni as its deity.

सोऽपः प्राविशत् ।

so 'paḥ prāviśat |

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

आपः (āpaḥ) — in the object sense it would be right for śas to come and form apaḥ. But here by vyatyayo bahulam (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85) the case-ending jas comes instead of śas in the object sense.

अचारिषम् (acāriṣam) — the root cara gatau; by luṅ, cleḥ sic, sic; mip with the substitute am, the augment aṭ: a + car + s + am. By ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-2-35) an ārdhadhātuka beginning with a consonant other than y takes the augment iṭ. When iṭ comes: acar + is + am. Vṛddhi would be due by sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. Sū. 7-2-1); then by neṭi (Pā. Sū. 7-2-4), when a sic beginning with iṭ follows, vṛddhi does not come: so the bar on vṛddhi would be due. But by its exception ato lrāntasya (Pā. Sū. 7-2-2) — when a sic in the parasmaipada follows, the short a of a stem ending in r or l that follows the short a takes vṛddhi — the vṛddhi comes; ṣatva: it becomes acāriṣam.

Page 232 (upper) — Rik 23: grammar (end)

अगस्महि (agasmahi) — by samo gamyṛcchibhyām (Pā. Sū. 1-3-29) — the substitutes of la after the intransitive roots gam and ṛcch following the prefix sam are middle — the middle-voice suffix comes. Luṅ, first person plural mahiṅ; for cli, sic: gam + s + mahi, the augment aṭ. By mantre ghasahvaraṇaśavṛdahādvṛc kṛgamijanibhyo leḥ (Pā. Sū. 2-4-80) the luk of cli would be due; yet since this is Vedic, by sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante the luk of cli does not come. By ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt (Pā. Sū. 7-2-10) — a val-initial ārdhadhātuka after a root that is monosyllabic in its teaching and taught unaccented does not take the augment iṭ — the iṭ is barred. By vā gamaḥ (Pā. Sū. 1-2-13) — the jhal-initial liṅ and sic after the root gam are optionally kit — sic is kit. So by anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37) the nasal m is dropped, the augment aṭ: it becomes agasmahi. ॥23॥ An ornament follows.

Page 232 (lower) — Sūkta 23, Rik 24 (last ṛk of the sūkta)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सं मा॑ग्ने॒ वर्च॑सा सृज॒ सं प्र॒जया॒ समायु॑षा । वि॒द्युर्मे॑ अ॒स्य दे॒वा इन्द्रो॑ वि॒द्यात्स॒ह ऋषि॑भिः ॥२४॥ [accent ?]

sáṃ māgne várcasā sṛja sáṃ prajáyā sám ā́yuṣā | vidyúr me asyá devā́ índro vidyā́t sahá ṛ́ṣibhiḥ ||24|| [accent ?] Strokes over मा, र्च and यु; bars under ग्ने, ज (सृज), प्र and या. Line 2: bars under वि, अ, दे, वि (विद्यात्) and ह (सह); strokes over मे, द्रो and षि; read with the Pada [accent ?].

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सं । मा । अग्ने । वर्चसा । सृज । सं । प्रऽजया । सं । आयुषा ॥ विद्युः । मे । अस्य । देवाः । इन्द्रः । विद्यात् । सह । ऋषिऽभिः ॥२४॥

saṃ | mā | agne | varcasā | sṛja | saṃ | pra 'jayā | saṃ | āyuṣā || vidyuḥ | me | asya | devāḥ | indraḥ | vidyāt | saha | ṛṣi 'bhiḥ ||24||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ Numbers as printed: पा० ३-४-१०८, ७-२-७९, ६-१-९६, ६-१-१२८. The bhāṣya ends with ॥१२॥ (the twelfth varga) and ॥४॥ (the end of the fourth sūkta of the anuvāka [as read]).

हे अग्ने वर्चःप्रजायुर्भिर्मां संयोजय । देवाः सोमपातारोऽस्य मे यजमानस्य विद्युः । अनुष्ठानं जानीयुः । किंच इन्द्रश्च ऋषिगणैः सह ममानुष्ठानं विद्यात् । जानीयात् ॥ विद्युः । विद ज्ञाने । लिङो झेर्जुस् । पा० ३-४-१०८ । यासुट् । लिङः सलोपः । पा० ७-२-७९ । इति सकारलोपः । उस्यपदान्तात् । पा० ६-१-९६ । इति पररूपत्वं । यासुट उदात्तत्वेऽप्येकादेश उकारोऽप्युदात्तः ॥ अस्य । इदमोऽन्वादेश इत्यशनुदात्तः । विभक्तिरपि सुप्त्वेनानुदात्ता । सह ऋषिभिरित्यत्र ऋत्यकः । पा० ६-१-१२८ । इति प्रकृतिभावः ॥१२॥ ॥४॥

he agne varcaḥprajāyurbhirmāṃ saṃyojaya | devāḥ somapātāro 'sya me yajamānasya vidyuḥ | anuṣṭhānaṃ jānīyuḥ | kiṃca indraśca ṛṣigaṇaiḥ saha mamānuṣṭhānaṃ vidyāt | jānīyāt || vidyuḥ | vida jñāne | liṅo jherjus | pā0 3-4-108 | yāsuṭ | liṅaḥ salopaḥ | pā0 7-2-79 | iti sakāralopaḥ | usyapadāntāt | pā0 6-1-96 | iti pararūpatvaṃ | yāsuṭa udāttatve 'pyekādeśa ukāro 'pyudāttaḥ || asya | idamo 'nvādeśa ityaśanudāttaḥ | vibhaktirapi suptvenānudāttā | saha ṛṣibhirityatra ṛtyakaḥ | pā0 6-1-128 | iti prakṛtibhāvaḥ ||12|| ||4||

Page 233 — Rik 24: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

Translation: "O Agni, join me with splendour, offspring and life. May the gods, the soma-drinkers, vidyuḥ, know, the rite asya me, of me, this sacrificer. And may Indra too, saha ṛṣibhiḥ, together with the hosts of ṛṣis, vidyāt, know my rite." (Grammatical tail: vidyuḥ, vida jñāne, jus for jhi of liṅ by liṅo jher jus [as printed; jher jus] (Pā. 3-4-108), yāsuṭ, the s dropped by liṅaḥ salopaḥ… (Pā. 7-2-79), the following form by usy apadāntāt (Pā. 6-1-96); since yāsuṭ is udātta, the single substitute u is also udātta; asya, the unaccented aś by idamo 'nvādeśe…, and the case-ending too unaccented as a sup; in saha ṛṣibhiḥ the original state by ṛty akaḥ (Pā. 6-1-128).)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

हे अग्ने (he agne) — O Agni | मा (mā) — me | वर्चसा (varcasā) — with splendour (with power) | प्रजया (prajayā) — with sons and descendants | आयुषा (āyuṣā) — with life | सं सृज (saṃ sṛja) — join | देवाः (devāḥ) — the gods (who have drunk soma) | अस्य मे (asya me) — my performance of sacrifice (may they know) | इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | ऋषिभिः सह (ṛṣibhiḥ saha) — together with the ṛṣis | विद्यात् (vidyāt) — may he know the sacrifice I have performed.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Agni, grant me splendour, sons and descendants, and long life. May the gods, and Indra together with the ṛṣis, know the sacrifice I have performed.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, confer upon me vigour, progeny and long life; the gods may know of this my sacrifice and Indra, with the Rishis may know it.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The meaning of the first half of this ṛk can be known easily. Agni is prayed to give splendour, sons and descendants, and long life. The meaning of the second half is not so clear; for the words vidyur me asya the commentator has explained the meaning "the performance of sacrifice I do". In the sentence indro vidyāt saha ṛṣibhiḥ, why the word ṛṣibhiḥ is used is also unclear. It seems the ṛṣi's intention is that this sacrifice, or hymn, made with regard to the deities, should be known to Indra, to the deities and to the other ṛṣis.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

विद्युः (vidyuḥ) — vida jñāne; liṅ, third person plural jhi; by jher jus (Pā. Sū. 6-1-96 [as printed; for 3-4-108]) jus comes for the jhi in place of liṅ; jus, the augment yāsuṭ: vid + yās + us; dropping of the s,

Page 234 (upper) — Rik 24: grammar (end)

vidyā + us: by usy apadāntāt (Pā. Sū. 6-1-96) — when us follows an a/ā not at the end of a pada, the following form comes as a single substitute — when the following form comes, vidyus; ru and visarga.

सह ऋषिभिः (saha ṛṣibhiḥ) — by ṛty akaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-128) — when a short ṛ follows, the a, i, u, ṛ at the end of a pada are made short and also keep their original state — shortening and the original state come. So guṇa does not come. ॥24॥ An ornament follows: the close of Sūkta 23. The header of p. 234 reads "Maṃ. 1 A. 6 Sū. 24", the new anuvāka.

॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 24 — "kasya nūnaṃ katamasyāmṛtānām" ("The Twenty-fourth Sūkta"; first sūkta of the Sixth Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 234 lower–294.)

Page 234 (lower) — Sūkta 24: title and introduction

Title: ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ("The Twenty-fourth Sūkta"). The header of this page reads "Maṃ. 1 A. 6 Sū. 24".

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note) Numbers as printed: आ० ९-३ and ऐ० ब्रा० ७-१८; the Aitareya number ७-१८ is settled at zoom (first glyph = flat-footed 7).

प्रथममण्डलस्य षष्ठेऽनुवाके सप्त सूक्तानि । तत्र कस्य नूनमिति पञ्चदशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तं । अजीगर्तपुत्रस्य शुनःशेपस्यार्षं । त्रैष्टुभं । अभि त्वा देवेति तृचो गायत्रः । आद्याया अनिरुक्तत्वात्प्रजापतिर्देवता । अग्नेर्वयमित्यस्याग्निः । अभि त्वा देवेत्यस्य तृचस्य सविता । भगभक्तस्येत्येषा भगदेवताका वा । शेषा वारुण्यः । तथा चानुक्रान्तं । कस्य पञ्चोनाजीगर्तिः शुनःशेपः स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातो वारुणं तु त्रैष्टुभमादौ काय्याग्नेय्यौ सावित्रस्तृचो गायत्रोऽस्यान्त्या भागी वेति ॥ राजसूयेऽभिषेचनीयेऽहनि मरुत्वतीये परिसमाप्ते सत्येतदादिकं सूक्तसप्तकमभिषिक्तस्य पुत्रादिभिः परिवृतस्य राज्ञः पुरस्ताद्धोत्राख्यातव्यं । तथा च सूत्रेऽभिहितं । संस्थिते मरुत्वतीये दक्षिणत आहवनीयस्य हिरण्यकशिपावासीनोऽभिषिक्ताय पुत्रामात्यपरिवृताय राज्ञे शौनःशेपमाचक्षीत । आ० ९-३ । इति । ब्राह्मणं च भवति । तदेतत्परऋक्शतगाथं शौनःशेपमाख्यानं तद्धोता राज्ञेऽभिषिक्तायाचष्टे हिरण्यकशिपावासीन आचष्टे हिरण्यकशिपावासीनः प्रतिगृणाति । ऐ० ब्रा० ७-१८ । इति ॥

prathamamaṇḍalasya ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke sapta sūktāni | tatra kasya nūnamiti pañcadaśarcaṃ prathamaṃ sūktaṃ | ajīgartaputrasya śunaḥśepasyārṣaṃ | traiṣṭubhaṃ | abhi tvā deveti tṛco gāyatraḥ | ādyāyā aniruktatvātprajāpatirdevatā | agnervayamityasyāgniḥ | abhi tvā devetyasya tṛcasya savitā | bhagabhaktasyetyeṣā bhagadevatākā vā | śeṣā vāruṇyaḥ | tathā cānukrāntaṃ | kasya pañconājīgartiḥ śunaḥśepaḥ sa kṛtrimo vaiśvāmitro devarāto vāruṇaṃ tu traiṣṭubhamādau kāyyāgneyyau sāvitrastṛco gāyatro 'syāntyā bhāgī veti || rājasūye 'bhiṣecanīye 'hani marutvatīye parisamāpte satyetadādikaṃ sūktasaptakamabhiṣiktasya putrādibhiḥ parivṛtasya rājñaḥ purastāddhotrākhyātavyaṃ | tathā ca sūtre 'bhihitaṃ | saṃsthite marutvatīye dakṣiṇata āhavanīyasya hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīno 'bhiṣiktāya putrāmātyaparivṛtāya rājñe śaunaḥśepamācakṣīta | ā0 9-3 | iti | brāhmaṇaṃ ca bhavati | tadetatparaṛkśatagāthaṃ śaunaḥśepamākhyānaṃ taddhotā rājñe 'bhiṣiktāyācaṣṭe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīna ācaṣṭe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīnaḥ pratigṛṇāti | ai0 brā0 7-18 | iti ||

Translation: "In the sixth anuvāka of the first maṇḍala there are seven sūktas. Of these the first is the sūkta kasya nūnam, of fifteen ṛks; its ṛṣi is Śunaḥśepa, son of Ajīgarta; it is in triṣṭubh; the tṛca abhi tvā deva is in gāyatrī. Because the first ṛk does not name its deity, Prajāpati is its deity; of agner vayam, Agni; of the tṛca abhi tvā deva, Savitṛ; bhagabhaktasya has Bhaga as deity, optionally; the rest are to Varuṇa. And so the Anukramaṇī: 'kasya, fifteen less five [as printed: pañcona]; Ājīgarti Śunaḥśepa, he, the adopted Vaiśvāmitra Devarāta; to Varuṇa, in triṣṭubh; at the beginning one to Ka and one to Agni; a tṛca to Savitṛ in gāyatrī, of which the last is to Bhaga, optionally.' In the rājasūya, on the day of the consecration, when the marutvatīya is finished, this group of seven sūktas beginning here is to be narrated by the hotṛ before the consecrated king, surrounded by his sons and the rest. And so it is said in the sūtra: 'When the marutvatīya is finished, seated on a golden cushion to the south of the āhavanīya, he should tell the Śaunaḥśepa to the consecrated king, surrounded by his sons and ministers' (Āśv. 9-3). And there is the brāhmaṇa: 'This is the Śaunaḥśepa story, of more than a hundred ṛks and with gāthās; the hotṛ tells it to the consecrated king; seated on a golden cushion he tells it; seated on a golden cushion [the adhvaryu] responds' (Ai. Brā. 7-18 [as read])."

Anuvāda (Kannada rendering): With this sūkta the sixth anuvāka of the first maṇḍala begins. In it there are seven sūktas. In the first sūkta, kasya nūnam, there are fifteen ṛks. For all seven sūktas in this anuvāka the ṛṣi is Śunaḥśepa, son of Ajīgarta. The three ṛks beginning abhi tvā deva savitaḥ are in the Gāyatrī metre. The remaining ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. Since in the first ṛk no deity is set forth by name, —

Page 235 — Sūkta 24: introduction (continued)

— Prajāpati himself is its deity; for the ṛk agner vayam, Agni is the deity; for the three ṛks abhi tvā, Savitṛ is the deity. But among these three ṛks, for the third ṛk, bhagabhaktasya, Savitṛ or Bhaga is the deity; for all the remaining ṛks Varuṇa is the deity. On this matter the Anukramaṇī says thus —

कस्य पञ्चोनाजीगर्तिः शुनःशेपः स कृत्रिमो वैश्वामित्रो देवरातो वारुणं तु त्रैष्टुभमादौ काय्याग्नेय्यौ सावित्रस्तृचो गायत्रोऽस्यान्त्या भागी वेति ॥

kasya pañconājīgartiḥ śunaḥśepaḥ sa kṛtrimo vaiśvāmitro devarāto vāruṇaṃ tu traiṣṭubhamādau kāyyāgneyyau sāvitrastṛco gāyatro 'syāntyā bhāgī veti ||

— that is: for the sūkta kasya nūnam, containing fifteen ṛks, the ṛṣi is Śunaḥśepa, son of Ajīgarta. This Śunaḥśepa is well known by the name Devarāta as the adopted son of the ṛṣi Viśvāmitra. This sūkta has Varuṇa as deity and is made of ṛks in the Triṣṭubh metre. But for the first two ṛks Ka, that is Prajāpati, and Agni are the deities. For the next ṛks, that is 3–5, Savitṛ is the deity; for the fifth ṛk it is said that Savitṛ or Bhaga is the deity. These three ṛks are in the Gāyatrī metre. For all the remaining ṛks Varuṇa is the deity and the metre is Triṣṭubh.

Its application: in the rājasūya sacrifice, on the day of consecration, after the recitation of the marutvatīya-śastra mantras, the hotṛ must recite the seven sūktas beginning kasya nūnam (the seven sūktas of this anuvāka) facing the consecrated king, surrounded by sons and other kinsfolk. On this matter the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra says thus —

संस्थिते मरुत्वतीये दक्षिणत आहवनीयस्य हिरण्यकशिपावासीनोऽभिषिक्ताय पुत्रामात्यपरिवृताय राज्ञे शौनःशेपमाचक्षीत ॥ (आ० ९-३) ब्राह्मणं च भवति — तदेतत्परऋक्शतगाथं शौनःशेपमाख्यानं तद्धोता राज्ञेऽभिषिक्तायाचष्टे हिरण्यकशिपावासीन आचष्टे हिरण्यकशिपावासीनः प्रतिगृणाति ॥ (ऐ० ब्रा० ७-१८)

saṃsthite marutvatīye dakṣiṇata āhavanīyasya hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīno 'bhiṣiktāya putrāmātyaparivṛtāya rājñe śaunaḥśepamācakṣīta || (ā0 9-3) brāhmaṇaṃ ca bhavati — tadetatparaṛkśatagāthaṃ śaunaḥśepamākhyānaṃ taddhotā rājñe 'bhiṣiktāyācaṣṭe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīna ācaṣṭe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīnaḥ pratigṛṇāti || (ai0 brā0 7-18)

— that is: in the rājasūya sacrifice, after the recitation of the marutvatīya-śastra mantras, the consecrated king must sit, together with his sons and ministers, on a golden seat (cushion) to the south of the āhavanīya fire. Then the hotṛ must recite the seven sūktas, connected with Śunaḥśepa, that is, having Śunaḥśepa as ṛṣi, beginning kasya nūnam (Ā. 9-3).

Page 236 (upper) — Sūkta 24: introduction (end), heading block

In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa too it is said on this matter: the hotṛ must recite the hundred ṛks (97 ṛks [as printed]) of the seven sūktas beginning kasya nūnam, which contain the Śunaḥśepa story, while sprinkling the king who has been consecrated and is seated on the golden seat (Ai. Brā. 7-18). An ornament follows.

Translation: "With this ṛk kasya, Śunaḥśepa, bound to the sacrificial post and not knowing where to turn, wonders: 'which god should I run to?' And so it is handed down: 'Come, I shall run to the gods' — he went first of the gods to Prajāpati himself (Ai. Brā. 7-16). We, named Śunaḥśepa, manāmahe, utter, the cāru, fine, nāma, name, of which, katamasya, of what kind, kasya devasya, god, among the amṛtānām, immortal gods? Which god will give me, who am about to die, again mahyai aditaye, to the great earth? By that gift, being immortal, may I dṛśeyam, see, my father and mother. From the śruti 'Ka is indeed the name of Prajāpati', by the common word kasya it is understood that by this ṛk Prajāpati himself was approached." (Grammatical tail: katamasya, ḍatamac in asking about a class among many (Pā. 5-3-93), final udātta by citaḥ; amṛtānām, the last member's final udātta by nañsubhyām being due, the last member's initial udātta by nañño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ; manāmahe, mana jñāne, śap by vyatyaya, not unaccented as it begins the pāda; mahyai, the case-ending udātta by udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt; dāt, the luk of sic by gātisthā… (Pā. 2-4-77), no augment aṭ by bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi; dṛśeyam, dṛśir prekṣaṇe, am for mip in the benedictive liṅ, the suffix ak by dṛśer ag vaktavyaḥ (Ma. 3-1-86-2), an exception to śap; no guṇa of the light penultimate as it is kit; for if aṅ came by liṅy āśiṣy aṅ (Pā. 3-1-86), guṇa would come by ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ (Pā. 7-4-16); yāsuṭ, dropping of s, iy by ato yeyaḥ, guṇa by ād guṇaḥ; the e udātta by the accent of yāsuṭ; in mātaraṃ ca, by the word ca, dṛśeyam is to be supplied again; so with regard to it this tiṅ-ending is the first one, and by cavāyoge prathamā it is not made unaccented.)
