(वयं (vayaṃ) — we, named Śunaḥśepa) अमृतानां (amṛtānāṃ) — among the gods | कतमस्य (katamasya) — belonging to which class | कस्य देवस्य (kasya devasya) — of which god | चारु (cāru) — auspicious | नाम (nāma) — the name | मनामहे (manāmahe) — shall we utter? | कः (kaḥ) — which god | नः (naḥ) — us | मह्यै (mahyai) — great | अदितये (aditaye) — to the earth (so as to be on the earth, that is, so as to live) | दात् (dāt) — will give? (by his so giving, I) | पितरं च (pitaraṃ ca) — (my) father | मातरं च (mātaraṃ ca) — (my) mother | पुनः (punaḥ) — again | दृशेयं (dṛśeyaṃ) — shall I see?

Page 238 — Rik 1: overall sense, explanation, English, Special Topics

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Who among the gods is the best? By remembering (praising) which god will this trouble of mine be removed and release from bondage come, and who will favour me to live on the earth like everyone? When shall I see my father and mother again?

॥ Viśeṣārthaḥ ॥ explanation

In the sacrifice performed by the king named Hariścandra, the ṛṣi named Śunaḥśepa, bound as a victim to the sacrificial post, not knowing where to turn and seeing death before him, speaks thus, with a cry of distress, thinking which god he should take refuge with so as to be released from bondage: the gods are many. Among them who is the best? By uttering whose name, or praising whom, will he free me, who am facing death, from the noose, and protect me so as to live again like the other people on the earth? When shall I, escaped from this trouble, see my father and mother? Lamenting in this way he first remembers Prajāpati. Afterwards, knowing from him that if he remembers Agni he will be released from bondage, he praises Agni in the next ṛk.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

Of many immortal gods whose good name should we contemplate? Who will deliver us back to the vast earth that I may again behold my father and mother?

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

It has been said before that all seven sūktas in this anuvāka are used in the rājasūya sacrifice for sprinkling the consecrated king, the sacrificer. On this matter the legend about Śunaḥśepa is described at length in the Purāṇas and the like, and in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. Since the legend in the Purāṇas and the like differs, and since it is not so fit to be taken as authority, we explain here only the legend in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. This story is described thus in the 33rd adhyāya of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa —

The legend of Śunaḥśepa (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa), as printed. The print gives it as continuous prose, the khaṇḍas closed by ॥१॥, ॥२॥ … ; the line-breaks below follow the sentences.

§ 1 — Hariścandra and Nārada (printed pp. 238 lower–239).

हरिश्चन्द्रो ह वैधस ऐक्ष्वाको राजापुत्र आस । तस्य ह शतं जाया बभूवुस्तासु पुत्रं न लेभे । तस्य ह पर्वतनारदौ गृह ऊषतुः स ह नारदं पप्रच्छ — यं न्विमं पुत्रमिच्छन्ति ये विजानन्ति ये च न । किंस्वित्पुत्रेण विन्दते तन्म आचक्ष्व नारदेति ॥ स एकया पृष्टो दशभिः प्रत्युवाच — ऋणमस्मिन्संनयत्यमृतत्वं च गच्छति । पिता पुत्रस्य जातस्य पश्येच्चेज्जीवतो मुखं ॥ यावन्तः पृथिव्यां भोगा यावन्तो जातवेदसि । यावन्तो अप्सु प्राणिनां भूयान्पुत्रे पितुस्ततः ॥ शश्वत्पुत्रेण पितरोऽत्यायन्बहुलं तमः । आत्मा हि जज्ञ आत्मनः स इरावत्यतितारिणी ॥ किं नु मलं किमजिनं किमु श्मश्रूणि किं तपः । पुत्रं ब्रह्माण इच्छध्वं स वै लोकोऽवदावदः ॥ अन्नं ह प्राणः शरणं ह वासो रूपं हिरण्यं पशवो विवाहाः । सखा ह जाया कृपणं ह दुहिता ज्योतिर्ह पुत्रः परमे व्योमन् ॥ पतिर्जायां प्रविशति गर्भो भूत्वा स मातरं । तस्यां पुनर्नवो भूत्वा दशमे मासि जायते ॥ तज्जाया जाया भवति यदस्यां जायते पुनः । आभूतिरेषा भूतिर्बीजमेतन्निधीयते ॥ देवाश्चैतामृषयश्च तेजः समभरन्महत् । देवा मनुष्यानब्रुवन्नेषा वो जननी पुनः ॥ नापुत्रस्य लोकोऽस्तीति तत्सर्वे पशवो विदुः । तस्मात्तु पुत्रो मातरं स्वसारं चाधिरोहति । एष पन्था उरुगायः सुशेवो यं पुत्रिण आक्रमन्ते विशोकाः । तं पश्यन्ति पशवो वयांसि च तस्मात्ते मात्रापि मिथुनी भवन्ति । इति हास्मा आख्याय ॥१॥

hariścandro ha vaidhasa aikṣvāko rājāputra āsa | tasya ha śataṃ jāyā babhūvustāsu putraṃ na lebhe | tasya ha parvatanāradau gṛha ūṣatuḥ sa ha nāradaṃ papraccha — yaṃ nvimaṃ putramicchanti ye vijānanti ye ca na | kiṃsvitputreṇa vindate tanma ācakṣva nāradeti || sa ekayā pṛṣṭo daśabhiḥ pratyuvāca — ṛṇamasminsaṃnayatyamṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati | pitā putrasya jātasya paśyeccejjīvato mukhaṃ || yāvantaḥ pṛthivyāṃ bhogā yāvanto jātavedasi | yāvanto apsu prāṇināṃ bhūyānputre pitustataḥ || śaśvatputreṇa pitaro 'tyāyanbahulaṃ tamaḥ | ātmā hi jajña ātmanaḥ sa irāvatyatitāriṇī || kiṃ nu malaṃ kimajinaṃ kimu śmaśrūṇi kiṃ tapaḥ | putraṃ brahmāṇa icchadhvaṃ sa vai loko 'vadāvadaḥ || annaṃ ha prāṇaḥ śaraṇaṃ ha vāso rūpaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavo vivāhāḥ | sakhā ha jāyā kṛpaṇaṃ ha duhitā jyotirha putraḥ parame vyoman || patirjāyāṃ praviśati garbho bhūtvā sa mātaraṃ | tasyāṃ punarnavo bhūtvā daśame māsi jāyate || tajjāyā jāyā bhavati yadasyāṃ jāyate punaḥ | ābhūtireṣā bhūtirbījametannidhīyate || devāścaitāmṛṣayaśca tejaḥ samabharanmahat | devā manuṣyānabruvanneṣā vo jananī punaḥ || nāputrasya loko 'stīti tatsarve paśavo viduḥ | tasmāttu putro mātaraṃ svasāraṃ cādhirohati | eṣa panthā urugāyaḥ suśevo yaṃ putriṇa ākramante viśokāḥ | taṃ paśyanti paśavo vayāṃsi ca tasmātte mātrāpi mithunī bhavanti | iti hāsmā ākhyāya ||1||

Translation: "Hariścandra, son of Vedhas, of the line of Ikṣvāku, was a king without a son. He had a hundred wives; among them he obtained no son. Parvata and Nārada lived in his house. He asked Nārada: 'This son whom people desire, those who understand and those who do not — what does one gain by a son? Tell me that, Nārada.' Asked in one verse, he answered in ten: (1) He pays off his debt in him and reaches immortality — the father who sees the face of his son born living. (2) As many enjoyments as there are on earth, as many in fire, as many in the waters for living beings — greater than those is the father's in a son. (3) Always by a son have fathers crossed over the abundant darkness; for the self is born of the self; he is a boat laden with food that carries across. (4) What is the dirt, what the antelope-skin, what the beard, what the austerity? Desire a son, O brahmins; he is the world that is well spoken of. (5) Food is life, clothing is shelter, gold is beauty, cattle are marriages; a wife is a friend, a daughter is a pity; a son is light in the highest heaven. (6) The husband enters the wife; becoming an embryo, he enters the mother; becoming new again in her, he is born in the tenth month. (7) That is the wife's wifehood (jāyā), that he is born (jāyate) in her again; she is the source, the becoming; the seed is placed in her. (8) The gods and the seers brought great splendour to her; the gods said to men: 'She is your mother again.' (9) 'For the sonless there is no world': all animals know this; therefore the son mounts even mother and sister. (10) This is the wide, pleasant path which those with sons tread without sorrow; animals and birds see it; therefore they mate even with the mother. Having told him this, —"

§ 2 — The vow to Varuṇa; Rohita (pp. 239–240).

अथैनमुवाच वरुणं राजानमुपधाव पुत्रो मे जायतां तेन त्वा यजा इति । तथेति स वरुणं राजानमुपससार पुत्रो मे जायतां तेन त्वा यजा इति तथेति तस्य पुत्रो जज्ञे रोहितो नाम । तं होवाचाजनि वै ते पुत्रो यजस्व माऽनेनेति स होवाच यदा वै पशुर्निर्दशो भवत्यथ स मेध्यो भवति निर्दशो न्वस्त्वथ त्वा यजा इति तथेति । स ह निर्दश आस तं होवाच निर्दशो न्वभूद्यजस्व माऽनेनेति स होवाच यदा वै पशोर्दन्ता जायन्तेऽथ मेध्यो भवति दन्ता न्वस्य जायन्तामथ त्वा यजा इति तथेति । तस्य ह दन्ता जज्ञिरे तं होवाचाज्ञत वा अस्य दन्ता यजस्व माऽनेनेति स होवाच यदा वै पशोर्दन्ताः पद्यन्तेऽथ स मेध्यो भवति दन्ता न्वस्य पद्यन्तामथ त्वा यजा इति तथेति । तस्य ह दन्ताः पेदिरे तं होवाचापत्सत वा अस्य दन्ता यजस्व माऽनेनेति स होवाच यदा वै पशोर्दन्ताः पुनर्जायन्तेऽथ स मेध्यो भवति दन्ता न्वस्य पुनर्जायन्तामथ त्वा यजा इति तथेति । तस्य ह दन्ताः पुनर्जज्ञिरे तं होवाचाज्ञत वा अस्य पुनर्दन्ता यजस्व माऽनेनेति स होवाच यदा वै क्षत्रियः सांनाहुको भवत्यथ स मेध्यो भवति संनाहं नु प्राप्नोत्वथ त्वा यजा इति तथेति । स ह संनाहं प्रापत्तं होवाच संनाहं नु प्राप्नोद्यजस्व माऽनेनेति स तथेत्युक्त्वा पुत्रमामन्त्रयामास ततायं वै मह्यं त्वामददाद्धन्त त्वयाहमिमं यजा इति । स ह नेत्युक्त्वा धनुरादायारण्यमुपातस्थौ स संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार ॥२॥

athainamuvāca varuṇaṃ rājānamupadhāva putro me jāyatāṃ tena tvā yajā iti | tatheti sa varuṇaṃ rājānamupasasāra putro me jāyatāṃ tena tvā yajā iti tatheti tasya putro jajñe rohito nāma | taṃ hovācājani vai te putro yajasva mā 'neneti sa hovāca yadā vai paśurnirdaśo bhavatyatha sa medhyo bhavati nirdaśo nvastvatha tvā yajā iti tatheti | sa ha nirdaśa āsa taṃ hovāca nirdaśo nvabhūdyajasva mā 'neneti sa hovāca yadā vai paśordantā jāyante 'tha medhyo bhavati dantā nvasya jāyantāmatha tvā yajā iti tatheti | tasya ha dantā jajñire taṃ hovācājñata vā asya dantā yajasva mā 'neneti sa hovāca yadā vai paśordantāḥ padyante 'tha sa medhyo bhavati dantā nvasya padyantāmatha tvā yajā iti tatheti | tasya ha dantāḥ pedire taṃ hovācāpatsata vā asya dantā yajasva mā 'neneti sa hovāca yadā vai paśordantāḥ punarjāyante 'tha sa medhyo bhavati dantā nvasya punarjāyantāmatha tvā yajā iti tatheti | tasya ha dantāḥ punarjajñire taṃ hovācājñata vā asya punardantā yajasva mā 'neneti sa hovāca yadā vai kṣatriyaḥ sāṃnāhuko bhavatyatha sa medhyo bhavati saṃnāhaṃ nu prāpnotvatha tvā yajā iti tatheti | sa ha saṃnāhaṃ prāpattaṃ hovāca saṃnāhaṃ nu prāpnodyajasva mā 'neneti sa tathetyuktvā putramāmantrayāmāsa tatāyaṃ vai mahyaṃ tvāmadadāddhanta tvayāhamimaṃ yajā iti | sa ha netyuktvā dhanurādāyāraṇyamupātasthau sa saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra ||2||

Translation: "— he said to him: 'Go to king Varuṇa: "Let a son be born to me; with him I shall sacrifice to you."' 'So be it.' He went to king Varuṇa: 'Let a son be born to me; with him I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' A son named Rohita was born to him. [Varuṇa] said to him: 'A son has been born to you; sacrifice to me with him.' He said: 'When an animal is more than ten days old, then it is fit for sacrifice; let him be more than ten days old, then I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' He became more than ten days old. [Varuṇa] said: 'He is more than ten days old; sacrifice to me with him.' He said: 'When an animal's teeth come, then it is fit for sacrifice; let his teeth come, then I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' His teeth came. [Varuṇa] said: 'His teeth have come; sacrifice to me with him.' He said: 'When an animal's teeth fall, then it is fit; let his teeth fall …' His teeth fell. '… When an animal's teeth come again, then it is fit; let his teeth come again …' His teeth came again. [Varuṇa] said: 'His teeth have come again; sacrifice to me with him.' He said: 'When a kṣatriya is armed, then he is fit for sacrifice; let him obtain his armour, then I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it.' He obtained his armour. [Varuṇa] said: 'He has obtained his armour; sacrifice to me with him.' He said 'So be it', and called his son: 'My dear, he gave you to me; come, let me sacrifice to him with you.' He said 'No', took his bow and went off to the forest; he wandered a year in the forest."

§ 3 — Hariścandra afflicted; Indra's counsel caraiva; Śunaḥśepa bought (printed p. 240).

Printed as one paragraph ending ॥३॥; the five verses carry no numbers in the print. As printed: अशनया परीतम् (aśanayā parītam), हतश्चरैवेति (hataś caraiveti), मध्यमे (madhyame).

अथ हैक्ष्वाकं वरुणो जग्राह तस्य होदरं जज्ञे तदु ह रोहितः शुश्राव सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच — नानाश्रान्ताय श्रीरस्तीति रोहित शुश्रुम । पापो नृषद्वरो जन इन्द्र इच्चरतः सखा चरैवेति ॥ चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह द्वितीयं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच — पुष्पिण्यौ चरतो जङ्घे भूष्णुरात्मा फलग्रहिः । शेरेऽस्य सर्वे पाप्मानः श्रमेण प्रपथे हतश्चरैवेति ॥ चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह तृतीयं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच — आस्ते भग आसीनस्योर्ध्वस्तिष्ठति तिष्ठतः । शेते निपद्यमानस्य चराति चरतो भगश्चरैवेति ॥ चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह चतुर्थं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच — कलिः शयानो भवति संजिहानस्तु द्वापरः । उत्तिष्ठंस्त्रेता भवति कृतं संपद्यते चरंश्चरैवेति ॥ चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह पञ्चमं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय तमिन्द्रः पुरुषरूपेण पर्येत्योवाच — चरन्वै मधु विन्दति चरन्स्वादुमुदुम्बरम् । सूर्यस्य पश्य श्रेमाणं यो न तन्द्रयते चरंश्चरैवेति ॥ चरैवेति वै मा ब्राह्मणोऽवोचदिति ह षष्ठं संवत्सरमरण्ये चचार सोऽजीगर्तं सौयवसिमृषिमशनया परीतमरण्य उपेयाय । तस्य ह त्रयः पुत्रा आसुः शुनःपुच्छः शुनःशेपः शुनोलाङ्गूल इति तं होवाच ऋषेऽहं ते शतं ददाम्यहमेषामेकेनाऽऽत्मानं निष्क्रीणा इति स ज्येष्ठं पुत्रं निगृह्णान उवाच नन्विममिति नो एवेममिति कनिष्ठं माता तौ ह मध्यमे संपादयाञ्चक्रतुः शुनःशेपे तस्य ह शतं दत्त्वा स तमादाय सोऽरण्याद्ग्राममेयाय । स पितरमेत्योवाच तत हन्ताहमनेनाऽऽत्मानं निष्क्रीणा इति स वरुणं राजानमुपससारानेन त्वा यजा इति तथेति भूयान्वै ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियादिति वरुण उवाच तस्मा एतं राजसूयं यज्ञक्रतुं प्रोवाच तमेतमभिषेचनीये पुरुषं पशुमालेभे ॥३॥

atha haikṣvākaṃ varuṇo jagrāha tasya hodaraṃ jajñe tadu ha rohitaḥ śuśrāva so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya tamindraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryetyovāca — nānāśrāntāya śrīrastīti rohita śuśruma | pāpo nṛṣadvaro jana indra iccarataḥ sakhā caraiveti || caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocaditi ha dvitīyaṃ saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya tamindraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryetyovāca — puṣpiṇyau carato jaṅghe bhūṣṇurātmā phalagrahiḥ | śere 'sya sarve pāpmānaḥ śrameṇa prapathe hataścaraiveti || caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocaditi ha tṛtīyaṃ saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya tamindraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryetyovāca — āste bhaga āsīnasyordhvastiṣṭhati tiṣṭhataḥ | śete nipadyamānasya carāti carato bhagaścaraiveti || caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocaditi ha caturthaṃ saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya tamindraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryetyovāca — kaliḥ śayāno bhavati saṃjihānastu dvāparaḥ | uttiṣṭhaṃstretā bhavati kṛtaṃ saṃpadyate caraṃścaraiveti || caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocaditi ha pañcamaṃ saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya tamindraḥ puruṣarūpeṇa paryetyovāca — caranvai madhu vindati caransvādumudumbaram | sūryasya paśya śremāṇaṃ yo na tandrayate caraṃścaraiveti || caraiveti vai mā brāhmaṇo 'vocaditi ha ṣaṣṭhaṃ saṃvatsaramaraṇye cacāra so 'jīgartaṃ sauyavasimṛṣimaśanayā parītamaraṇya upeyāya | tasya ha trayaḥ putrā āsuḥ śunaḥpucchaḥ śunaḥśepaḥ śunolāṅgūla iti taṃ hovāca ṛṣe 'haṃ te śataṃ dadāmyahameṣāmekenātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇā iti sa jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ nigṛhṇāna uvāca nanvimamiti no evemamiti kaniṣṭhaṃ mātā tau ha madhyame saṃpādayāñcakratuḥ śunaḥśepe tasya ha śataṃ dattvā sa tamādāya so 'raṇyādgrāmameyāya | sa pitarametyovāca tata hantāhamanenātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇā iti sa varuṇaṃ rājānamupasasārānena tvā yajā iti tatheti bhūyānvai brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyāditi varuṇa uvāca tasmā etaṃ rājasūyaṃ yajñakratuṃ provāca tametamabhiṣecanīye puruṣaṃ paśumālebhe ||3||

Translation: "Then Varuṇa seized the Aikṣvāka [Hariścandra]; his belly swelled [dropsy]. Rohita heard of it. He came from the forest to the village. Indra, in the form of a man, came round to him and said: 'There is no fortune for one who has not toiled, Rohita; so we have heard. The man who sits among men is bad; Indra is the friend of the wanderer. Wander on!' 'A Brahmin has told me to wander' — so he wandered a second year in the forest. He came from the forest to the village; Indra, in the form of a man, came round to him and said: 'The wanderer's legs are flowering; his body grows and gathers fruit; all his sins lie slain by the toil on the road. Wander on!' … a third year …: 'The fortune of one who sits, sits; it stands up for one who stands; it lies down for one who lies; it moves for one who moves. Wander on!' … a fourth year …: 'Kali is the one lying down; Dvāpara the one getting up; Tretā the one standing; Kṛta is attained by the one who moves. Wander on!' … a fifth year …: 'The wanderer finds honey, the wanderer the sweet udumbara fruit. See the splendour of the Sun, who never tires as he moves. Wander on!' 'A Brahmin has told me to wander' — so he wandered a sixth year in the forest. He came in the forest upon the seer Ajīgarta Sauyavasi, overcome by hunger. He had three sons: Śunaḥpuccha, Śunaḥśepa and Śunolāṅgūla. [Rohita] said to him: 'Seer, I give you a hundred [cows]; with one of these I shall ransom myself.' He, holding back the eldest son, said: 'Surely not this one.' 'Nor this one,' said the mother of the youngest. The two of them settled on the middle one, Śunaḥśepa. Having given a hundred for him, [Rohita] took him and came from the forest to the village. He came to his father and said: 'Father, look, I ransom myself with this one.' He went to king Varuṇa: 'With this one I shall sacrifice to you.' 'So be it,' said Varuṇa, 'a Brahmin is worth more than a kṣatriya.' He taught him this sacrificial rite, the Rājasūya; at the Abhiṣecanīya he took him as the human victim."

§ 4 — The priests; Śunaḥśepa's prayers and release (printed pp. 240–241).

Page 241 begins at मानुषमिव. As printed: निःशान (niḥśāna), कनीय (kanīya).

तस्य ह विश्वामित्रो होताऽऽसीज्जमदग्निरध्वर्युर्वसिष्ठो ब्रह्माऽयास्य उद्गाता तस्मा उपाकृताय नियोक्तारं न विविदुः स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिर्मह्यमपरं शतं दत्ताहमेनं नियोक्ष्यामीति तस्मा अपरं शतं ददुस्तं स निनियोज । तस्मा उपाकृताय नियुक्तायाऽऽप्रीताय पर्यग्निकृताय विशसितारं न विविदुः स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिर्मह्यमपरं शतं दत्ताहमेनं विशसिष्यामीति तस्मा अपरं शतं ददुः सोऽसिं निःशान एयाय । अथ ह शुनःशेप ईक्षाञ्चक्रेऽमानुषमिव वै मा विशसिष्यन्ति हन्ताहं देवता उपधावामीति स प्रजापतिमेव प्रथमं देवतानामुपससार — कस्य नूनं कतमस्यामृतानामित्येतयर्चा । तं प्रजापतिरुवाचाग्निर्वै देवानां नेदिष्ठस्तमेवोपधावेति सोऽग्निमुपससाराग्नेर्वयं प्रथमस्यामृतानामित्येतयर्चा । तमग्निरुवाच सविता वै प्रसवानामीशे तमेवोपधावेति स सवितारमुपससाराभि त्वा देव सवितरित्येतेन तृचेन । तं सवितोवाच वरुणाय वै राज्ञे नियुक्तोऽसि तमेवोपधावेति स वरुणं राजानमुपससारात उत्तराभिरेकत्रिंशता । तं वरुण उवाचाग्निर्वै देवानां मुखं सुहृदयतमस्तं नु स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति सोऽग्निं तुष्टावात उत्तराभिर्द्वाविंशत्या । तमग्निरुवाच विश्वान्नु देवान् स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति स विश्वान्देवांस्तुष्टाव — नमो महद्भ्यो नमो अर्भकेभ्य इत्येतयर्चा । तं विश्वे देवा ऊचुरिन्द्रो वै देवानामोजिष्ठो बलिष्ठः सहिष्ठः सत्तमः पारयिष्णुतमस्तं नु स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति स इन्द्रं तुष्टाव यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा इति चैतेन सूक्तेनोत्तरस्य च पञ्चदशभिः । तस्मा इन्द्रः स्तूयमानः प्रीतो मनसा हिरण्यरथं ददौ तमेतया प्रतीयाय शश्वदिन्द्र इति । तमिन्द्र उवाचाश्विनौ नु स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति सोऽश्विनौ तुष्टावात उत्तरेण तृचेन । तमश्विना ऊचतुरुषसं नु स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति स उषसं तुष्टावात उत्तरेण तृचेन । तस्य ह स्मर्च्यृच्युक्तायां विपाशो मुमुचे कनीय ऐक्ष्वाकस्योदरं भवत्युत्तमस्यामेवर्च्युक्तायां विपाशो मुमुचेऽगद ऐक्ष्वाक आस ॥४॥

tasya ha viśvāmitro hotāsījjamadagniradhvaryurvasiṣṭho brahmā 'yāsya udgātā tasmā upākṛtāya niyoktāraṃ na vividuḥ sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasirmahyamaparaṃ śataṃ dattāhamenaṃ niyokṣyāmīti tasmā aparaṃ śataṃ dadustaṃ sa niniyoja | tasmā upākṛtāya niyuktāyāprītāya paryagnikṛtāya viśasitāraṃ na vividuḥ sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasirmahyamaparaṃ śataṃ dattāhamenaṃ viśasiṣyāmīti tasmā aparaṃ śataṃ daduḥ so 'siṃ niḥśāna eyāya | atha ha śunaḥśepa īkṣāñcakre 'mānuṣamiva vai mā viśasiṣyanti hantāhaṃ devatā upadhāvāmīti sa prajāpatimeva prathamaṃ devatānāmupasasāra — kasya nūnaṃ katamasyāmṛtānāmityetayarcā | taṃ prajāpatiruvācāgnirvai devānāṃ nediṣṭhastamevopadhāveti so 'gnimupasasārāgnervayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānāmityetayarcā | tamagniruvāca savitā vai prasavānāmīśe tamevopadhāveti sa savitāramupasasārābhi tvā deva savitarityetena tṛcena | taṃ savitovāca varuṇāya vai rājñe niyukto 'si tamevopadhāveti sa varuṇaṃ rājānamupasasārāta uttarābhirekatriṃśatā | taṃ varuṇa uvācāgnirvai devānāṃ mukhaṃ suhṛdayatamastaṃ nu stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti so 'gniṃ tuṣṭāvāta uttarābhirdvāviṃśatyā | tamagniruvāca viśvānnu devān stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti sa viśvāndevāṃstuṣṭāva — namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhya ityetayarcā | taṃ viśve devā ūcurindro vai devānāmojiṣṭho baliṣṭhaḥ sahiṣṭhaḥ sattamaḥ pārayiṣṇutamastaṃ nu stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti sa indraṃ tuṣṭāva yacciddhi satya somapā iti caitena sūktenottarasya ca pañcadaśabhiḥ | tasmā indraḥ stūyamānaḥ prīto manasā hiraṇyarathaṃ dadau tametayā pratīyāya śaśvadindra iti | tamindra uvācāśvinau nu stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti so 'śvinau tuṣṭāvāta uttareṇa tṛcena | tamaśvinā ūcaturuṣasaṃ nu stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti sa uṣasaṃ tuṣṭāvāta uttareṇa tṛcena | tasya ha smarcyṛcyuktāyāṃ vipāśo mumuce kanīya aikṣvākasyodaraṃ bhavatyuttamasyāmevarcyuktāyāṃ vipāśo mumuce 'gada aikṣvāka āsa ||4||

Translation: "Viśvāmitra was his Hotṛ, Jamadagni the Adhvaryu, Vasiṣṭha the Brahman, Ayāsya the Udgātṛ. When he had been brought forward, they found no one to bind him [to the post]. Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'Give me another hundred and I shall bind him.' They gave him another hundred, and he bound him. When he had been brought forward, bound, propitiated with the Āprī verses and had fire carried round him, they found no one to slaughter him. Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'Give me another hundred and I shall slaughter him.' They gave him another hundred; he came sharpening his knife. Then Śunaḥśepa reflected: 'They will slaughter me as if I were not a man. Look, I shall run to the deities.' He went first of the deities to Prajāpati, with the ṛk kasya nūnaṃ katamasyāmṛtānām. Prajāpati said to him: 'Agni is the nearest of the gods; run to him.' He went to Agni with the ṛk agner vayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānām. Agni said to him: 'Savitṛ rules over the impulses; run to him.' He went to Savitṛ with the triplet abhi tvā deva savitaḥ. Savitṛ said to him: 'You have been bound for king Varuṇa; run to him.' He went to king Varuṇa with the thirty-one [ṛks] that follow. Varuṇa said to him: 'Agni is the mouth of the gods, the most kind-hearted; praise him, and then we shall release you.' He praised Agni with the twenty-two that follow. Agni said to him: 'Praise the All-gods, and then we shall release you.' He praised the All-gods with the ṛk namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhyaḥ. The All-gods said to him: 'Indra is the most vigorous, strongest, most powerful, truest of the gods, the best at bringing across; praise him, and then we shall release you.' He praised Indra with the sūkta yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ and with fifteen [ṛks] of the next. Indra, pleased as he was praised, gave him in his mind a golden chariot; he acknowledged it with the ṛk śaśvad indra. Indra said to him: 'Praise the Aśvins, and then we shall release you.' He praised the Aśvins with the triplet that follows. The Aśvins said to him: 'Praise Uṣas, and then we shall release you.' He praised Uṣas with the triplet that follows. As each ṛk was spoken, the fetter came loose and the Aikṣvāka's belly grew smaller; when the last ṛk was spoken, the fetter came off and the Aikṣvāka was well."

§ 5 — The Añjaḥsava; Devarāta; Ajīgarta's plea; Viśvāmitra adopts Śunaḥśepa (printed pp. 241–242).

As printed: शुनःशेपोऽञ्जस्सवं (śunaḥśepo 'ñjassavaṃ; the conjunct is crowded, so the reading is not certain), शुनश्शेपो (śunaśśepo) once, ज्ञपयोऽऽराजपुत्र (jñapayo 'rājaputra; the print is not clear and the reading is doubtful). Page 242 begins at निह्नुवे.

तमृत्विज ऊचुस्त्वमेव नोऽस्याह्नः संस्थामधिगच्छेत्यथ हैतं शुनःशेपोऽञ्जस्सवं ददर्श तमेताभिश्चतसृभिरभिसुषाव यच्चिद्धि त्वं गृहे गृह इत्यथैनं द्रोणकलशमभ्यवनिनायोच्छिष्टं चम्वोर्भरेत्येतयर्चा । अथ हास्मिन्नन्वारब्धे पूर्वाभिश्चतसृभिः स स्वाहाकाराभिर्जुहवाञ्चकाराथैनमवभृथमभ्यवनिनाय त्वं नो अग्ने वरुणस्य विद्वानित्येताभ्यामथैनमत ऊर्ध्वमग्निमाहवनीयमुपस्थापयाञ्चकार शुनश्चिच्छेपं निदितं सहस्रादिति । अथ ह शुनश्शेपो विश्वामित्रस्याङ्कमाससाद स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिर्ऋषे पुनर्मे पुत्रं देहीति नेति होवाच विश्वामित्रो देवा वा इमं मह्यमरासतेति स ह देवरातो वैश्वामित्र आस तस्यैते कापिलेयबाभ्रवाः । स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिस्त्वं वेहि विह्वयावहा इति स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिराङ्गिरसो जन्मनाऽस्याजीगर्तिः श्रुतः कविः । ऋषे पैतामहात्तन्तोर्माऽपगाः पुनरेहि मामिति स होवाच शुनःशेपोऽदर्शुस्त्वा शासहस्तं न यच्छूद्रेष्वलप्सत । गवां त्रीणि शतानि त्वमवृणीथा मदङ्गिर इति । स होवाचाजीगर्तः सौयवसिस्तद्वै मा तात तपति पापं कर्म मया कृतं । तदहं निह्नुवे तुभ्यं प्रतियन्तु शता गवामिति स होवाच शुनःशेपो यः सकृत्पापकं कुर्यात्कुर्यादेनत्ततोऽपरं । नापागाः शौद्रान्न्यायादसन्धेयं त्वया कृतमिति । असन्धेयमिति ह विश्वामित्र उपससाद स होवाच विश्वामित्रो भीम एव सौयवसिः शासेन विशिशासिषुः । अस्थान्मैतस्य पुत्रो भूर्ममैवोपेहि पुत्रतामिति । स होवाच शुनःशेपः स वै यथा नो ज्ञपयोऽऽराजपुत्र तथा वद । यथैवाऽऽङ्गिरसः सन्नुपेयां तव पुत्रतामिति स होवाच विश्वामित्रो ज्येष्ठो मे त्वं पुत्राणां स्यास्तव श्रेष्ठा प्रजा स्यात् । उपेया दैवं मे दायं तेन वै त्वोपमन्त्रय इति । स होवाच शुनःशेपः संज्ञानानेषु वै ब्रूयात्सौहार्द्याय मे श्रियै । यथाहं भरतऋषभोपेयां तव पुत्रतामित्यथ ह विश्वामित्रः पुत्रानामन्त्रयामास मधुच्छन्दाः शृणोतन ऋषभो रेणुरष्टकः । ये के च भ्रातरः स्थ नास्मै ज्यैष्ठ्याय कल्पध्वमिति ॥५॥

tamṛtvija ūcustvameva no 'syāhnaḥ saṃsthāmadhigacchetyatha haitaṃ śunaḥśepo 'ñjassavaṃ dadarśa tametābhiścatasṛbhirabhisuṣāva yacciddhi tvaṃ gṛhe gṛha ityathainaṃ droṇakalaśamabhyavanināyocchiṣṭaṃ camvorbharetyetayarcā | atha hāsminnanvārabdhe pūrvābhiścatasṛbhiḥ sa svāhākārābhirjuhavāñcakārāthainamavabhṛthamabhyavanināya tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya vidvānityetābhyāmathainamata ūrdhvamagnimāhavanīyamupasthāpayāñcakāra śunaścicchepaṃ niditaṃ sahasrāditi | atha ha śunaśśepo viśvāmitrasyāṅkamāsasāda sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasirṛṣe punarme putraṃ dehīti neti hovāca viśvāmitro devā vā imaṃ mahyamarāsateti sa ha devarāto vaiśvāmitra āsa tasyaite kāpileyabābhravāḥ | sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasistvaṃ vehi vihvayāvahā iti sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasirāṅgiraso janmanā 'syājīgartiḥ śrutaḥ kaviḥ | ṛṣe paitāmahāttantormā 'pagāḥ punarehi māmiti sa hovāca śunaḥśepo 'darśustvā śāsahastaṃ na yacchūdreṣvalapsata | gavāṃ trīṇi śatāni tvamavṛṇīthā madaṅgira iti | sa hovācājīgartaḥ sauyavasistadvai mā tāta tapati pāpaṃ karma mayā kṛtaṃ | tadahaṃ nihnuve tubhyaṃ pratiyantu śatā gavāmiti sa hovāca śunaḥśepo yaḥ sakṛtpāpakaṃ kuryātkuryādenattato 'paraṃ | nāpāgāḥ śaudrānnyāyādasandheyaṃ tvayā kṛtamiti | asandheyamiti ha viśvāmitra upasasāda sa hovāca viśvāmitro bhīma eva sauyavasiḥ śāsena viśiśāsiṣuḥ | asthānmaitasya putro bhūrmamaivopehi putratāmiti | sa hovāca śunaḥśepaḥ sa vai yathā no jñapayo 'rājaputra tathā vada | yathaivāṅgirasaḥ sannupeyāṃ tava putratāmiti sa hovāca viśvāmitro jyeṣṭho me tvaṃ putrāṇāṃ syāstava śreṣṭhā prajā syāt | upeyā daivaṃ me dāyaṃ tena vai tvopamantraya iti | sa hovāca śunaḥśepaḥ saṃjñānāneṣu vai brūyātsauhārdyāya me śriyai | yathāhaṃ bharataṛṣabhopeyāṃ tava putratāmityatha ha viśvāmitraḥ putrānāmantrayāmāsa madhucchandāḥ śṛṇotana ṛṣabho reṇuraṣṭakaḥ | ye ke ca bhrātaraḥ stha nāsmai jyaiṣṭhyāya kalpadhvamiti ||5||

Translation: "The priests said to him: 'You yourself bring the rite of this day to its completion for us.' Then Śunaḥśepa saw the Añjaḥsava [the quick pressing of soma]. He pressed the soma with these four [ṛks], yac cid dhi tvaṃ gṛhe gṛhe. Then he poured it into the droṇa-kalaśa with the ṛk ucchiṣṭaṃ camvor bhara. Then, while [the king] kept hold of him, he made the offerings with the four preceding [ṛks] that end in svāhā. Then he led him to the Avabhṛtha [the final bath] with the two [ṛks] tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya vidvān. After that he had him attend upon the Āhavanīya fire with śunaś cic chepaṃ niditaṃ sahasrāt. Then Śunaḥśepa sat down in Viśvāmitra's lap. Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'Seer, give me back my son.' 'No,' said Viśvāmitra, 'the gods have given him to me.' He became Devarāta Vaiśvāmitra; the Kāpileyas and Bābhravas are his descendants. Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'You come here; let the two of us call to him.' Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'You are an Āṅgirasa by birth, the son of Ajīgarta, a renowned seer. Seer, do not leave the line of your grandfathers; come back to me.' Śunaḥśepa said: 'They saw you with the knife in your hand, a thing not found even among Śūdras. You chose three hundred cows over me, O Aṅgiras.' Ajīgarta Sauyavasi said: 'That evil deed I did torments me, my son. I make amends to you: let the hundreds of cows go back.' Śunaḥśepa said: 'He who does an evil thing once will do the next one too. You have not turned away from the ways of a Śūdra; what you did cannot be mended.' 'Cannot be mended,' Viśvāmitra repeated, and came forward. Viśvāmitra said: 'Terrible was Sauyavasi, wanting to cut you up with the knife. Do not stay his son; come to be my son.' Śunaḥśepa said: 'Tell us, prince, as you make it known, how I, being an Āṅgirasa, may become your son.' Viśvāmitra said: 'You shall be the eldest of my sons, and your offspring the best. You shall receive my divine inheritance; with that I call you.' Śunaḥśepa said: 'If they agree, say it, for my friendship and my fortune, so that I may become your son, bull of the Bharatas.' Then Viśvāmitra called his sons: 'Madhucchandas, hear, and Ṛṣabha, Reṇu and Aṣṭaka, and all you who are brothers: grant him the seniority.'"

§ 6 — Viśvāmitra's sons; the recitation of the legend (printed p. 242).

As printed: पुर एत्रा (pura etrā), देवराताय (devarātāya), परऋक्शतगाथं (paraṛkśatagāthaṃ; zoom of PDF 256, Oct 28: the printed word reads तदेतत्…ऋक्कृतगाथं (-ṛkkṛtagāthaṃ), not -क्शत-; the two letters between तत् and ऋ are a crowded conjunct I cannot settle [?], so the form परऋक्शतगाथं above is superseded). The end of the passage carries no paragraph number.

तस्य ह विश्वामित्रस्यैकशतं पुत्रा आसुः पञ्चाशदेव ज्यायांसो मधुच्छन्दसः पञ्चाशत्कनीयांसः । तद्ये ज्यायांसो न ते कुशलं मेनिरे ताननु व्याजहारान्तान्वः प्रजा भक्षीष्टेति त एतेऽन्ध्राः पुण्ड्राः शबराः पुलिन्दा मूतिबा इत्युदन्त्या बहवो वैश्वामित्रा दस्यूनां भूयिष्ठाः । स होवाच मधुच्छन्दाः पञ्चाशता सार्धं यन्नः पिता संजानीते तस्मिंस्तिष्ठामहे वयं । पुरस्त्वा सर्वे कुर्महे त्वामन्वञ्चो वयं स्मसीति । अथ ह विश्वामित्रः प्रतीतः पुत्रांस्तुष्टाव । ते वै पुत्राः पशुमन्तो वीरवन्तो भविष्यथ । ये मानं मेऽनुगृह्णन्तो वीरवन्तमकर्त मा । पुर एत्रा वीरवन्तो देवरातेन गाथिनाः । सर्वे राध्याः स्थ पुत्रा एष वः सद्विवाचनं । एष वः कुशिका वीरो देवरातस्तमन्वित । युष्मांश्च दायं म उपेता विद्यां यामु च विद्मसि । ते सम्यञ्चो वैश्वामित्राः सर्वे साकं सरातयः । देवराताय तस्थिरे धृत्यै श्रैष्ठ्याय गाथिनाः । अधीयत देवरातो रिक्थयोरुभयोर्ऋषिः । जह्नूनां चाधिपत्ये दैवे वेदे च गाथिनां । तदेतत्परऋक्शतगाथं शौनःशेपमाख्यानं । तद्धोता राज्ञेऽभिषिक्तायाऽऽचष्टे । हिरण्यकशिपावासीन आचष्टे हिरण्यकशिपावासीनः प्रतिगृह्णाति यशो वै हिरण्यं यशसैवैनं तत्समर्धयति । ओमित्यृचः प्रतिगर एवं तथेति गाथाया ओमिति वै दैवं तथेति मानुषं दैवेन चैवैनं तन्मानुषेण च पापादेनसः प्रमुञ्चति । तस्माद्यो राजा विजिती स्यादप्ययजमान आख्यापयेतैवैतच्छौनःशेपमाख्यानं न हास्मिन्नल्पं चनैनः परिशिष्यते । सहस्रमाख्यात्रे दद्याच्छतं प्रतिगरित्र एते चैवाऽऽसने श्वेतश्चाश्वतरीरथो होतुः । पुत्रकामा हाप्याख्यापयेरँल्लभन्ते ह पुत्राँल्लभन्ते ह पुत्रान् ॥

tasya ha viśvāmitrasyaikaśataṃ putrā āsuḥ pañcāśadeva jyāyāṃso madhucchandasaḥ pañcāśatkanīyāṃsaḥ | tadye jyāyāṃso na te kuśalaṃ menire tānanu vyājahārāntānvaḥ prajā bhakṣīṣṭeti ta ete 'ndhrāḥ puṇḍrāḥ śabarāḥ pulindā mūtibā ityudantyā bahavo vaiśvāmitrā dasyūnāṃ bhūyiṣṭhāḥ | sa hovāca madhucchandāḥ pañcāśatā sārdhaṃ yannaḥ pitā saṃjānīte tasmiṃstiṣṭhāmahe vayaṃ | purastvā sarve kurmahe tvāmanvañco vayaṃ smasīti | atha ha viśvāmitraḥ pratītaḥ putrāṃstuṣṭāva | te vai putrāḥ paśumanto vīravanto bhaviṣyatha | ye mānaṃ me 'nugṛhṇanto vīravantamakarta mā | pura etrā vīravanto devarātena gāthināḥ | sarve rādhyāḥ stha putrā eṣa vaḥ sadvivācanaṃ | eṣa vaḥ kuśikā vīro devarātastamanvita | yuṣmāṃśca dāyaṃ ma upetā vidyāṃ yāmu ca vidmasi | te samyañco vaiśvāmitrāḥ sarve sākaṃ sarātayaḥ | devarātāya tasthire dhṛtyai śraiṣṭhyāya gāthināḥ | adhīyata devarāto rikthayorubhayorṛṣiḥ | jahnūnāṃ cādhipatye daive vede ca gāthināṃ | tadetatparaṛkśatagāthaṃ śaunaḥśepamākhyānaṃ | taddhotā rājñe 'bhiṣiktāyācaṣṭe | hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīna ācaṣṭe hiraṇyakaśipāvāsīnaḥ pratigṛhṇāti yaśo vai hiraṇyaṃ yaśasaivainaṃ tatsamardhayati | omityṛcaḥ pratigara evaṃ tatheti gāthāyā omiti vai daivaṃ tatheti mānuṣaṃ daivena caivainaṃ tanmānuṣeṇa ca pāpādenasaḥ pramuñcati | tasmādyo rājā vijitī syādapyayajamāna ākhyāpayetaivaitacchaunaḥśepamākhyānaṃ na hāsminnalpaṃ canainaḥ pariśiṣyate | sahasramākhyātre dadyācchataṃ pratigaritra ete caivāsane śvetaścāśvatarīratho hotuḥ | putrakāmā hāpyākhyāpayeram̐llabhante ha putrām̐llabhante ha putrān ||

Translation: "Viśvāmitra had a hundred and one sons: fifty older than Madhucchandas and fifty younger. The older ones did not think it right. He pronounced on them: 'Your offspring shall inherit the ends [of the land].' These are the Andhras, Puṇḍras, Śabaras, Pulindas and Mūtibas, many dwelling at the borders; the descendants of Viśvāmitra are the most numerous of the Dasyus. Madhucchandas, together with the fifty, said: 'What our father agrees to, by that we stand. We all put you in front; we follow after you.' Then Viśvāmitra, pleased, praised his sons: 'You, my sons, will be rich in cattle and rich in heroes, you who, honouring my wish, have made me rich in heroes. Gāthins, with Devarāta going before, you will be rich in heroes. You are all to prosper, my sons; this is a true word for you. This hero of yours, Kuśikas, is Devarāta; follow him. He will receive you as my inheritance, and the knowledge we know. Those Vaiśvāmitras, the Gāthins, all of one mind, all sharing the gift, stood by Devarāta for his steadiness and his seniority. Devarāta the seer was placed in both inheritances: in the lordship of the Jahnus and in the divine Veda of the Gāthins.' This is the Śaunaḥśepa legend, with more than a hundred ṛks and with gāthās. The Hotṛ tells it to the anointed king. Seated on a golden cushion he tells it; seated on a golden cushion [the Adhvaryu] responds. Gold is glory: with glory he thus makes him prosper. Om is the response to a ṛk, tathā to a gāthā; om is divine, tathā human. With the divine and the human he thus frees him from sin and guilt. Therefore a king who is victorious, even if he is not sacrificing, should have this Śaunaḥśepa legend told; then not the least guilt remains in him. He should give a thousand to the teller and a hundred to the responder, and these two seats; and to the Hotṛ a white chariot drawn by mules. Those who want sons should also have it told; they obtain sons, they obtain sons."

Page 243 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (Śunaḥśepākhyānavu)

Title, as printed: ಶುನಶ್ಶೇಪಾಖ್ಯಾನವು ("The Śunaḥśepa story"). The Kannada retelling runs to p. 249 and is translated here in full, page by page. The bracketed summaries in small type are the source's own.

[Hariścandra's wish for a son is granted. The praise of having sons.]

Hariścandra, son of Vedhas, born in the Ikṣvāku line, had a hundred wives, yet no son was born to him. Once, when the seers Parvata and Nārada came to his house, Hariścandra said to Nārada: "O Nārada, human beings, who have the power of discernment, and also the other creatures, which lack it, long eagerly for offspring. What is gained by the birth of offspring?" So he asked.

To the question Hariścandra asked in one sentence, Nārada gives his answer in ten sentences, as set out below:

  1. The father, together with the joy he feels at seeing the face of the son born to him, also pays off his debt to the ancestors through that son and attains immortality.

  2. A father's joy at gaining a son is greater than the enjoyment to be had from the earth, greater than the help to be had from fire, and beyond the use to be had from water. The enjoyment that comes from gaining a son is far greater than all these enjoyments.

  3. Through his son a father crosses many great dangers. Since the father is himself born again as a son, the son carries the father across the sorrows of this world and the next in the sea of worldly life, just as a boat stocked beforehand with provisions carries a man across a river or a sea.

  4. What is the use of a householder's life without children? Why brahmacarya? Why the vānaprastha stage? Why become a wandering ascetic? What is the use of these? "O best of Brahmins, desire offspring": so the world says of people who give up married life in order to practise the Vedic rites.

  5. Food protects life. Clothes protect from cold. Gold gives the use of ornaments. Marriage and the like bring wealth in the form of cattle. The wife becomes a friend. The daughter becomes an object of affection. But the son alone shines in the highest world of the gods as a lamp that lights up the self.

Page 244 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (continued)

  1. The husband enters the wife in the form of seed. When the seed changes into the form of an embryo, he makes her a mother. Afterwards he is born from her again, in the tenth month.

  2. Only when the husband is born in her womb does the wife truly receive the meaningful name "jāyā". The seed produced in her she raises in the form of a son, makes it shine and makes it beautiful.

  3. The gods and the seers have granted the highest radiance to her who has become a jāyā. Then the gods declared to human beings: "She becomes your mother."

  4. Even animals know that one without offspring has no lasting state; and among them the male young even covers its own mother or sister.

  5. This is the road on which those who have sons walk free of sorrow. Even beasts and birds know it. In these words he praised the having of sons.

[A son is born to Hariścandra. Varuṇa comes again and again and insists that the son be given to him as an offering in sacrifice. But Hariścandra puts forward one reason after another, keeps postponing the sacrifice and slips out of it.]

Then Nārada advised Hariścandra: "Go to Varuṇa and pray to him to grant you a son. And give him your word that, after the son is born, you will offer that very son to him in sacrifice." Hariścandra went to Varuṇa as told and prayed: "Grant me a son. I shall give him to you as an offering." At once a son named Rohita was born. Varuṇa came and said: "A son has been born to you. Give him as an offering." To that Hariścandra said: "Before any creature becomes fit to be an offering, ten days must pass. Let ten days pass for my son too. Then I shall offer him to you." When ten days had passed for Rohita, Varuṇa came and asked for him. Then Hariścandra said: "For any creature to be given as an offering, its teeth must have come. When my son's teeth have come, I shall offer him." After Rohita's teeth had come, Varuṇa came and asked for him. Then Hariścandra said: "No creature should be given as an offering until its teeth have fallen. Let this one's teeth fall too." Varuṇa came again: "Rohita's teeth are falling; give him as an offering." Hariścandra asked for time until his teeth had grown again.

Page 245 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (continued)

Then, when Varuṇa came, he said: "One born in a warrior family is not fit to be an offering until he puts on a warrior's armour. Wait until then." When that time also came and Varuṇa firmly demanded Rohita, Hariścandra called his son and said: "Child, I must now give you as an offering to Varuṇa, who granted you to me." Rohita said: "That shall never be." He took up his bow, fled to escape into a lonely forest, and wandered there for one year.

[Rohita wanders aimlessly in the forest for six years. Then he buys from his parents a Brahmin's son named Śunaḥśepa, to give to Varuṇa as the offering in his place.]

After Rohita had escaped and gone, Varuṇa seized Hariścandra, and Hariścandra was struck with dropsy (mahodara). Rohita heard the news, left the forest and came to a village. Indra came in human form, met him and said: "O Rohita, there is no happiness for one who does not travel. However excellent a man may be, if he grows up among the people of one caste he falls into wrong ways and is ruined. So go about in lonely regions. Indra becomes the friend of the man who travels like this. You too go about." So he advised.

Rohita understood that a Brahmin had advised him to travel, and he wandered in the forest for a second year as well. Then, as he was coming to a village, Indra came again in human form and said: "The feet of a man who travels are like the nectar of flowers. From that flower the self grows and gains the fruit of good health. All his sins are removed by the toil of travelling. So go about."

Following that word, Rohita went about for a third year as well. Just when he was entering the village again, Indra came and said: "The fortune of a man sitting in one place sits in one place like him. If he goes about, it too goes about and grows. So go about."

In the same way a fourth year passed. At the time he again entered the village, Indra came, described the nature of the four yugas, and told Rohita to go about once more. Rohita completed the fifth year in the same way. Just as he was entering the village, Indra came and said: "Honey and the sweet udumbara fruit come to the man who travels. See the radiance of the Sun, who does not tire even with his ceaseless moving. Like him, you too go about."

Page 246 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (continued)

Rohita wandered in the forest for the sixth year as well. Then he met a seer named Ajīgarta, son of one called Suyavas. That Ajīgarta, through poverty, was fasting in the forest without food. He had three children, named Śunaḥpuccha, Śunaḥśepa and Śunolāṅgūla. Rohita went to the seer and said: "O seer, I shall give you a hundred cows. Give me one of your three sons. I shall give him to Varuṇa as the offering in my place and so escape." Ajīgarta agreed to it, but he would not send away his eldest son. His wife would not let go of the youngest. Leaving those two, only the middle one was obtained. As agreed, Rohita gave Ajīgarta the hundred cows, brought Śunaḥśepa to his father and told him of the arrangement he had made. Hariścandra went to Varuṇa and said: "In place of my son I shall give you this one as the offering." Varuṇa agreed that this would do, since a Brahmin is greater than a kṣatriya. Then Varuṇa explained the procedure of the Rājasūya sacrifice to the king and arranged for a human sacrifice, in place of the animal sacrifice, on the day of the rite.

[Four great seers become the priests. The appointed time of the human sacrifice draws near. To escape a terrible death, Śunaḥśepa appeals to the gods. The gods he appealed to and the mantras he uttered.]

For this human sacrifice Viśvāmitra was appointed Hotṛ, Jamadagni Adhvaryu, Vasiṣṭha Brahman and Ayāsya Udgātṛ. After the rites that come before the sacrifice were over, no one would agree to tie Śunaḥśepa to the sacrificial post. "If you give me another hundred cows, I shall tie him," said Ajīgarta, and came forward. They agreed and gave him a hundred cows. Then Ajīgarta tied his son to the post. Next, after the Āprī hymn had been recited and fire carried round him, no one would agree to cut him. "If you give me another hundred cows, I myself will cut him," said Ajīgarta, and came forward for that too. He took the hundred cows in the same way, sharpened his knife and got ready to kill his son. Śunaḥśepa woke to the fact that they would cut him like an animal. He resolved, "I shall take refuge among the gods," and appealed to Prajāpati with the sūkta "kasya nūnaṃ katamasya" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-1). Prajāpati appeared and said: "Agni is the deity nearest to all of you; take refuge in him." Then, when Śunaḥśepa prayed to Agni with the ṛk "agner vayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānām", Agni came and said: "Savitṛ is the lord of all beings; take refuge in him." Then

Page 247 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (continued)

he prayed with the three ṛks beginning with the ṛk "abhi tvā deva savitaḥ". Then Savitṛ came and said: "You have been bound by Varuṇa, who is the lord; take refuge in him." Then, when he prayed to Varuṇa with thirty-one ṛks, Varuṇa came and said: "Agni is, as it were, the mouth of all the gods and is most merciful. If you pray to him now, we shall all release your bond." When he again prayed to Agni with twenty-two ṛks, Agni came and said: "If you pray to the Viśvedevas, you will be released." Then Śunaḥśepa entreated them with "namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhyaḥ" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-27-13). They came and said: "Indra is the most powerful of all, very strong and enduring; among the gods he is the nearest to truth, and he knows the means of bringing every matter to its end. If you pray to him, we shall release you." Then, when Śunaḥśepa prayed with the sūkta "yac cid dhi satya somapā" and with fifteen ṛks of the sūkta after it, Indra came, was pleased with his hymn and granted him a chariot made of gold. Śunaḥśepa accepted it with the words "śaśvad indra". Indra again instructed him: "Pray to the Aśvin deities. Then we shall release you." The Aśvins, being prayed to, came and said: "Pray to the goddess Uṣas. We shall release you." While the prayer to Uṣas went on, as he spoke the three ṛks one by one, the noose of Varuṇa's bond gradually loosened and Hariścandra's dropsy kept getting better. When he uttered the last ṛk, the noose was taken off completely and Hariścandra regained his health as before.

[Śunaḥśepa's release; his way of pressing the soma juice in the form of the Añjaḥsava. Viśvāmitra accepts him as his son.]

Then the priests said to Śunaḥśepa: "Now you too are a priest, like us. Take part with us in this special rite." Then he learnt the procedure of pressing the soma juice, which in the form of the Añjaḥsava is done very quickly. After he had pressed it, he took it and went, reciting the four ṛks "yac cid dhi tvaṃ gṛhe gṛhe". Uttering the ṛk "ucchiṣṭaṃ camvoḥ", he brought it into the droṇa-kalaśa. As soon as Hariścandra touched [him], he uttered the mantra "yatra grāvā" and offered the oblation with the word "svāhā". Then he came with the implements needed for the avabhṛtha, recited the ṛk "tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya" and performed the avabhṛtha. After this he called Hariścandra to the Āhavanīya fire and recited the mantra "śunaś cic chepaṃ niditam".

Page 248 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (continued)

At last Śunaḥśepa went to Viśvāmitra's side. Ajīgarta too came up to him and said: "O seer, give my son back." Viśvāmitra said: "That cannot be. The gods have given him to me as a gift." From then on he became Viśvāmitra's son, named Devarāta ("given by the gods"). (Later the Kāpileyas and the Babhrus were born from him.) Then Ajīgarta called Śunaḥśepa: "You are a seer who belongs to the family of Ajīgarta. So do not forget your line; come back to us." Śunaḥśepa answered his father: "Not even a Caṇḍāla takes a knife in his hand to kill his son. To you the three hundred cows were worth more than I. Out of greed for them you took the knife to cut me, your son." When he mocked him so, Ajīgarta said: "Child, what I did before was wrong. I shall rid myself of this sin. I shall give you a hundred cows too. Come home." In answer Śunaḥśepa said: "You, who once did not shrink from this sinful deed, will not fear to do such deeds again and again. For this deed of yours there is no reconciliation at all." Viśvāmitra too said: "Yes, for this deed there is no expiation at all."

Viśvāmitra said to Śunaḥśepa: "When he held the knife in his hand to kill you, Ajīgarta was terrible to look at. Do not be his son again. Come to my house and be my son." Then Śunaḥśepa voiced his doubt: "How can one born in the line of Aṅgiras become a kinsman of Viśvāmitra?" Viśvāmitra then called all his children and declared: "O Madhucchandas and the rest, from today you have no right of seniority in my property. From today all of it is Śunaḥśepa's. He is the eldest of all."

[Viśvāmitra's descendants. The reward for those who recite the story of Śunaḥśepa.]

The seer Viśvāmitra had a hundred children. Fifty were older than Madhucchandas and the rest were younger. The older fifty did not accept that Śunaḥśepa should be the heir to Viśvāmitra's property. When they opposed it, Viśvāmitra cursed them to have low offspring. As the result of that curse, various low clans were born, such as the Śabaras and the Pulindas. Madhucchandas and the younger fifty bowed to Viśvāmitra's decision and honoured Śunaḥśepa: "O Śunaḥśepa, we shall always be obedient to our father's command, and as he wishes we shall give you the place of first honour." Viśvāmitra was pleased with their obedience and said: "O children, because you agreed to my wish, honoured me and made my fatherhood fruitful, may abundant cows and offspring be your reward. Having taken this Devarāta as your leader,

Page 249 — Rik 1: the Kannada retelling (end); word note

be victorious. This Devarāta has gained the eminence of the Jahnu line and the divine knowledge of the Gāthi line, and is renowned as a seer. May you, who walk under this seer's leadership, and your children gain every prosperity." So he blessed them.

This story of Śunaḥśepa is told in more than a hundred ṛks. After holy water has been sprinkled on the king, the Hotṛ sits on a jewelled blanket adorned with gold thread and recites it. The Adhvaryu, who gives the response "oṃ tathā", sits in the same way and increases the king's glory. With the divine word "oṃ", which belongs to the ṛks (they are apauruṣeya, not of human authorship), and with the human assent "tathā", the Adhvaryu makes the king free of sin. Therefore every king who wishes to be victorious should hear this Śunaḥśepa story, both for his victory and for the cleansing of the sinful acts that come with it. To those who recite this story a thousand cows should be given; and to the Adhvaryu, who encourages the king by giving the needed words of assent, a hundred cows. To the Hotṛ a silver chariot yoked with excellent horses should be given. Those who have no son, whether they recite this tale or hear it, will surely obtain sons.

॥ ಶುನಶ್ಶೇಪಾಖ್ಯಾನವು ಮುಗಿದುದು ॥ (The Śunaḥśepa story ends.)

This story of Śunaḥśepa is told at length in Vālmīki's Rāmāyaṇa. There Śunaḥśepa is said to be the son of a seer named Ṛcīka; and in place of the name of king Hariścandra there is the name of a king Ambarīṣa, lord of Ayodhyā and other lands. The Bhāgavata and Viṣṇu Purāṇas also give an account of this tale. But in the Purāṇas and similar works the tale comes with small differences; in its main points it is like this one.

कस्य देवस्य अथवा कस्य कतमस्य देवस्य (kasya devasya athavā kasya katamasya devasya) — the meaning is "of which god, of what kind of god". Here Śunaḥśepa recites this ṛk while thinking to himself which god he should take refuge in (or praise) to be freed from the sacrificial post to which the sacrificial victim is tied. Although the word kasya has the general sense "which", here the word also means Prajāpati. So the commentator, explaining it, says that Śunaḥśepa first asked Prajāpati for help, and on this point cites the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence:

हन्ताहं देवता उपधावामीति स प्रजापतिमेव प्रथमं देवतानामुपससार ।

hantāhaṃ devatā upadhāvāmīti sa prajāpatimeva prathamaṃ devatānāmupasasāra |

"Look, I shall run to the deities": so saying, he went first of the deities to Prajāpati (Ai. Brā. 7-16).

Page 250 — Rik 1: word notes and grammar

अमृतानां (amṛtānāṃ) — मरणरहितानां देवानां (maraṇarahitānāṃ devānāṃ), "of the gods who are free from death".

मह्यै अदितये (mahyai aditaye) — among the twenty-one names of the earth beginning with gauḥ, gmā, the words mahī and aditiḥ are read (Ni. 1-1), so these words mean pṛthivī, the earth. Since both words here convey the same sense, the word mahī can be given the meaning "broad, great".

पुनर्दात्, पितरं च दृशेयं मातरं च (punar dāt, pitaraṃ ca dṛśeyaṃ mātaraṃ ca) — Śunaḥśepa, tied to the sacrificial post and standing in the victim's place, understood that death was near and was at a loss for fear. He laments: "Shall I again become a creature that belongs to the earth as before? That is, which deity will favour me so that I may live on the earth again? And how shall I be freed from this noose of death and see my father and mother?" In the next ṛk he prays to Agni to be freed from his bond.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

कतमस्य (katamasya) — by the sūtra (Pā. Sū. 5-3-93)

वा बहूनां जातिपरिप्रश्ने डतमच्

vā bahūnāṃ jātiparipraśne ḍatamac

the suffix ḍatamac comes after the words kim, yat and tad when one out of many is singled out and a class is meant, and after the word kim when a question about the class is meant. Kaiyaṭa (kaiyaṭakāraru) says, on the words

किमादीनां द्विबह्वर्थे प्रत्ययविधानादुपाध्यानर्थक्यं पूर्वसूत्रे द्वयोरिति अत्र सूत्रे जातिपरिप्रश्ने इति च न कर्तव्यमिति भावः

kimādīnāṃ dvibahvarthe pratyayavidhānādupādhyānarthakyaṃ pūrvasūtre dvayoriti atra sūtre jātiparipraśne iti ca na kartavyamiti bhāvaḥ

"since the suffix is enjoined for kim and the rest in the sense of two and of many, the limiting conditions (upādhi) are pointless"; and "the sense is that in the earlier sūtra the word dvayoḥ, and in this sūtra the words jātiparipraśne, need not be stated". Therefore the suffix also comes when action, quality or name is meant, as in katama eṣāṃ pācakaḥ ("which of these is the cook?"), śūraḥ, devadattaḥ. kim + atama: loss of the ṭi.

अमृतानां (amṛtānāṃ) — the acute on the last syllable of the second member, due by nañsubhyām (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172), is set aside by nañjo jaramaramitramṛtāḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-2-116): in a bahuvrīhi compound, the first syllable of the second members jara, mara, mitra and mṛta after nañ is acute. So the first syllable of mṛta is acute.

मनामहे (manāmahe) — the root mana jñāne, of the Divādi class. So the vikaraṇa śyan would be expected, but śap comes by the Vedic interchange. laṭ, first person plural, mahiṅ, e-substitution; lengthening by akṛtsārva[dhātukayor dīrghaḥ] (Pā. Sū. 7-4-25).

दात् (dāt) — ḍudāñ dāne; luṅ, third person singular tip, cli; sic in its place: dā + s + ti; loss of i by itaś ca lopaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97); by gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu (Pā. Sū. 2-4-77)

Page 251 (upper) — Rik 1: grammar (end)

the sic after the roots gai, sthā, dā, dhā, pā and bhū is dropped (luk); so sic is dropped. The aṭ augment does not come, because this is Vedic.

दृशेयं (dṛśeyaṃ) — the root dṛśir prekṣaṇe. āśīrliṅ, first person singular mip, substituted by am. By dṛśer agvaktavyaḥ (Pā. Ma. 3-1-87-3 [as printed]), when the benedictive liṅ follows the root dṛś, a comes; so aṅ in place of śap. Since aṅ is kit, the laghūpadha guṇa does not come. By liṅy āśiṣy aṅ (Pā. Sū. 3-1-86), in the Veda aṅ comes after the root when the benedictive liṅ follows. When aṅ comes, guṇa is required by ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-4-16): when aṅ follows, roots ending in ṛ and the root dṛś take guṇa. The yāsuṭ augment: dṛś + yās + am; loss of the s. By ato yeyaḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-2-8 [as printed; for 7-2-80]), iy comes for the yā that is part of a sārvadhātuka after short a: so iy, then guṇa. ॥1॥

Page 251 (lower) — Sūkta 24, Rik 2

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒ग्नेर्व॒यं प्र॑थ॒मस्या॒मृता॑नां॒ मना॑महे॒ चारु॑ दे॒वस्य॒ नाम॑ । स नो॑ म॒ह्या अदि॑तये॒ पुन॑र्दात्पि॒तरं॑ च दृ॒शेयं॑ मा॒तरं॑ च ॥२॥

agnér vayáṃ prathamásyāmṛ́tānāṃ mánāmahe cā́ru devásya nā́ma | sá no mahyā́ áditaye púnar dāt pitáraṃ ca dṛśéyaṃ mātáraṃ ca ||2|| Strokes over प्र, ता (मृता), ना (मना), रु and म (नाम); bars under अ, व (वयं), थ, स्या, नां, हे, दे and स्य. Line 2: strokes over नो, दि, न (पुन), रं (पितरं), यं (दृशेयं) and रं (मातरं); bars under म (मह्या), ये, त्पि, दृ and मा. In Ṛk 1 the stroke in दृशेयं stands over शे; here it stands over यं.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अग्नेः । वयं । प्रथमस्य । अमृतानां । मनामहे । चारु । देवस्य । नाम । सः । नः । मह्यै । अदितये । पुनः । दात् । पितरं । च । दृशेयं । मातरं । च ॥२॥

agneḥ | vayaṃ | prathamasya | amṛtānāṃ | manāmahe | cāru | devasya | nāma | saḥ | naḥ | mahyai | aditaye | punaḥ | dāt | pitaraṃ | ca | dṛśeyaṃ | mātaraṃ | ca ||2||

Page 252 — Rik 2: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

इत्थं प्रथमयर्चा विचिकित्सां कृत्वा प्रजापतेः सकाशात्तं देवमग्निं निश्चित्यानयर्चा तुष्टाव । तथा च श्रूयते । तं प्रजापतिरुवाचाग्निर्वै देवानां नेदिष्ठस्तमेवोपधावेति सोऽग्निमुपससाराग्नेर्वयं प्रथमस्यामृतानामित्येतयर्चा । ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१६ । इति । पूर्ववद्योजना । दाद्ददातु दृशेयं पश्यानीत्येवमाशीःपरत्वेन पदद्वयं योज्यं ॥

itthaṃ prathamayarcā vicikitsāṃ kṛtvā prajāpateḥ sakāśāttaṃ devamagniṃ niścityānayarcā tuṣṭāva | tathā ca śrūyate | taṃ prajāpatiruvācāgnirvai devānāṃ nediṣṭhastamevopadhāveti so 'gnimupasasārāgnervayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānāmityetayarcā | ai. brā. 7-16 | iti | pūrvavadyojanā | dāddadātu dṛśeyaṃ paśyānītyevamāśīḥparatvena padadvayaṃ yojyaṃ ||

Gist: Having voiced his doubt in the first ṛk and learnt from Prajāpati that the god is Agni, he praised Agni with this ṛk. So it is heard: "Prajāpati said to him: 'Agni is the nearest of the gods; run to him.' He went to Agni with this ṛk, agner vayaṃ prathamasyāmṛtānām" (Ai. Brā. 7-16). The construction is as before. The two words are to be construed as a wish: dāt = "may he give", dṛśeyam = "may I see".

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

वयं (vayaṃ) — we (Śunaḥśepa) | अमृतानां (amṛtānāṃ) — (among the gods) who are free from death | प्रथमस्य (prathamasya) — who is the first | देवस्य (devasya) — who is a god | अग्नेः (agneḥ) — of Agni | चारु (cāru) — auspicious | नाम (nāma) — the name | मनामहे (manāmahe) — let us utter | सः (saḥ) — that god Agni | नः (naḥ) — us (who are facing death) | मह्यै (mahyai) — to the great | अदितये (aditaye) — to the earth | पुनः दात् (punaḥ dāt) — may he give again | पितरं मातरं च (pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca) — father and mother | दृशेयं (dṛśeyaṃ) — may I see.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

Having learnt from Prajāpati that Agni is the first among the gods, I (Śunaḥśepa) utter the auspicious name of Agni, the chief of the gods. May Agni (pleased by this) send me (who am facing death) back to the great earth. (Freed from death by Agni's grace,) I shall see my father and mother.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed

Of many immortal gods we shall contemplate the god Agni's name first; he will deliver us back to this vast earth that I may again behold my father and mother.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

As said before, Śunaḥśepa learnt from Prajāpati that Agni is able to protect him. So Śunaḥśepa first prays to Agni, as the best among the gods, to protect him, to let him live on the earth again, and to grant that he see his father and mother again.

The special explanation given under the previous ṛk applies to this ṛk too.

वयं (vayaṃ) — although the plural "we" is used here, it is to be understood as applying to Śunaḥśepa, who is praying to Agni.

Page 253 (upper) — Rik 2: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

मह्यै (mahyai) — meaning mahatyai, "to the great". By vartamāne pṛṣadbṛhanmahajjagacchatṛvac ca (Uṇ. Sū. 2-…; the digits are not clear [?]), these words are formed irregularly (nipātana) as ending in the suffix ati. Because they are treated like words in śatṛ, by ugitaś ca (Pā. Sū. 4-1-6) ṅīp comes; the at is dropped as a Vedic usage. By bṛhanmahator upasaṅkhyānam (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173 vā. 1) the ṅīp is acute. The suffix ṅe follows the word mahī. By āṇ nadyāḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-12 [as printed; for 7-3-112]), āṭ comes before a ṅit case-ending after a stem ending in a nadī; by āṭaś ca (Pā. Sū. 6-1-70 [as printed; for 6-1-90]), vṛddhi. mahī + ai: yaṇ substitution. By udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt (Pā. Sū. 6-1-17 [as printed; for 6-1-174]), after a yaṇ standing in place of an acute vowel and preceded by a consonant, a nadī ending and a case-ending from śas onwards are acute. So the case-ending is acute.

दृशेयं (dṛśeyaṃ) — its derivation is given under the previous mantra. Through the ca in mātaraṃ ca, dṛśeyaṃ is drawn in (anukṛṣṭa). Compared with that, the dṛśeyaṃ that stands in the mantra is the one uttered first. By cavāyoge prathamā (Pā. Sū. 8-1-59), a finite verb uttered first does not become unaccented when there is a connection with ca or vā; so the loss of all accents is blocked. ॥2॥ An ornament follows.

Page 253 (lower) — Sūkta 24, Rik 3

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अ॒भि त्वा॑ देव सवित॒रीशा॑नं॒ वार्या॑णां । सदा॑वन्भा॒गमी॑महे ॥३॥ [accent ?]

abhí tvā deva savitar ī́śānaṃ vā́ryāṇāṃ | sádāvan bhāgám īmahe ||3|| [accent ?] Strokes over त्वा, शा and र्या; bars under अ, त (सवित) and नं. Line 2: strokes over दा and मी; a bar under the conjunct न्भा (read as भा॒; it may stand under व [accent ?]).

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अभि । त्वा । देव । सवितः । ईशानं । वार्याणां । सदा । अवन् । भागं । ईमहे ॥३॥

abhi | tvā | deva | savitaḥ | īśānaṃ | vāryāṇāṃ | sadā | avan | bhāgaṃ | īmahe ||3||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

प्रथमे छन्दोमे वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे अभि त्वा देव सवितरिति सावित्रस्तृचः सूक्तस्थानीयः । अथ छन्दोमा इति खण्डेऽभि त्वा देव सवितः प्रेतां यज्ञस्य शंभुवा ।

prathame chandome vaiśvadevaśastre abhi tvā deva savitariti sāvitrastṛcaḥ sūktasthānīyaḥ | atha chandomā iti khaṇḍe 'bhi tvā deva savitaḥ pretāṃ yajñasya śaṃbhuvā |

Page 254 — Rik 3: bhāṣya (continued), word-meanings, overall sense, English

As printed: "अ. ४-७" (अ. for आ., the Āśvalāyana reference).

आ. ८-९ । इति सूत्रितं ॥ अभित्वेत्येषाग्निमन्थनेऽपि विनियुक्ता । प्रातर्वैश्वदेव्यामिति खण्डेऽभि त्वा देव सवितर्मही द्यौः पृथिवी च नः । आ. २-१६ । इति सूत्रितं । श्रूयते च । अभि त्वा देव सवितरिति सावित्रीमन्वाह । ऐ. ब्रा. १-१६ । इति ॥ तथा प्रवर्ग्येऽप्येषा विनियुक्ता । अथोत्तरमिति खण्डेऽभि त्वा देव सवितः समी वत्सं न मातृभिः । अ. ४-७ । इति सूत्रितं ॥ तथा ग्रावस्तोत्रेऽपि । एतस्मिन्काले ग्रावस्तुदिति खण्डे मध्यमस्वरेणेदं सवनमभि त्वा देव सवितः । आ. ५-१२ । इति सूत्रितं ॥ अथाग्निना प्रेरितः सन्सवितारमभि त्वेत्यनेन तृचेन प्रार्थयते । तथैव श्रूयते । तमग्निरुवाच सविता वै प्रसवानामीशे तमेवोपधावेति स सवितारमुपससाराभि त्वा देव सवितरित्येतेन तृचेन । ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१६ । इति । हे सदावन् सदा सर्वदा रक्षक हे सवितर्देव वार्याणां वरणीयानां धनानामीशानं स्वामिनं त्वां प्रति भागं भजनीयं धनमभि सर्वत ईमहे । याचामहे ॥ ईशानं । ईश ऐश्वर्ये लटः शानच् । तास्यनुदात्तेदिति लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । वार्याणां । वृञ् संभक्तौ । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् । ईडवन्देत्यादिनाद्युदात्तत्वं । अवन् । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । भागं । कर्षात्वत इति घञोऽन्त उदात्तः ॥

ā. 8-9 | iti sūtritaṃ || abhitvetyeṣāgnimanthane 'pi viniyuktā | prātarvaiśvadevyāmiti khaṇḍe 'bhi tvā deva savitarmahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ | ā. 2-16 | iti sūtritaṃ | śrūyate ca | abhi tvā deva savitariti sāvitrīmanvāha | ai. brā. 1-16 | iti || tathā pravargye 'pyeṣā viniyuktā | athottaramiti khaṇḍe 'bhi tvā deva savitaḥ samī vatsaṃ na mātṛbhiḥ | a. 4-7 | iti sūtritaṃ || tathā grāvastotre 'pi | etasminkāle grāvastuditi khaṇḍe madhyamasvareṇedaṃ savanamabhi tvā deva savitaḥ | ā. 5-12 | iti sūtritaṃ || athāgninā preritaḥ sansavitāramabhi tvetyanena tṛcena prārthayate | tathaiva śrūyate | tamagniruvāca savitā vai prasavānāmīśe tamevopadhāveti sa savitāramupasasārābhi tvā deva savitarityetena tṛcena | ai. brā. 7-16 | iti | he sadāvan sadā sarvadā rakṣaka he savitardeva vāryāṇāṃ varaṇīyānāṃ dhanānāmīśānaṃ svāminaṃ tvāṃ prati bhāgaṃ bhajanīyaṃ dhanamabhi sarvata īmahe | yācāmahe || īśānaṃ | īśa aiśvarye laṭaḥ śānac | tāsyanudāttediti lasārvadhātukānudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ | vāryāṇāṃ | vṛñ saṃbhaktau | ṛhalorṇyat | īḍavandetyādinādyudāttatvaṃ | avan | āmantritanighātaḥ | bhāgaṃ | karṣātvata iti ghaño 'nta udāttaḥ ||

Gist: In the first Chandoma, in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra, the Savitṛ triplet abhi tvā deva savitaḥ takes the place of the sūkta (Āś. 8-9). It is also used at the kindling of fire by friction (Āś. 2-16; Ai. Brā. 1-16: "with abhi tvā deva savitaḥ he recites the Sāvitrī"), in the Pravargya (Āś. 4-7) and in the Grāvastotra (Āś. 5-12). Impelled by Agni, Śunaḥśepa prays to Savitṛ with this triplet (Ai. Brā. 7-16). "O ever-protecting divine Savitṛ, we ask you, the lord of the riches to be chosen, for a share of wealth from every side." The grammatical tail notes the accents of īśānam (śānac; root accent by tāsy anudāttet), vāryāṇām (ṇyat; initial acute by īḍavanda…), avan (vocative lowered) and bhāgam (ghañ, final acute by karṣātvataḥ).

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

सदावन् (sadāvan) — O you who always protect | सवितः देव (savitaḥ deva) — O god Savitṛ | वार्याणां (vāryāṇāṃ) — of the riches (things) to be desired | ईशानं (īśānaṃ) — (you) who are the lord | भागं (bhāgaṃ) — the desired wealth | अभि ईमहे (abhi īmahe) — we ask.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O god Savitṛ, who always protect, we ask you, the lord of wealth (lord of wealth or of desired things), for the wealth (we) desire.

॥ English Translation ॥

Divine and ever protecting Savitri, the lord of all that is desirable, we ask for wealth- [sic]

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The uses (viniyoga) of this ṛk are as follows:

When the mantras of the Vaiśvadeva-śastra are recited, the triplet (three ṛks) abhi tvā deva savitaḥ, addressed to Savitṛ, is to be recited as the mantra of the first Chandoma. This is set out in the sūtra abhi tvā deva savitaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3) pretāṃ yajñasya śaṃbhuvā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-41-19) of the section **atha

Page 255 — Rik 3: Special Topics (continued)

chandomāḥ** of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Āś. 8-9).

This ṛk abhi tvā is also to be recited at the start of a sacrifice, when fire is churned from the araṇis. This is set out by the sūtra abhi tvā deva savitaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3) mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca naḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13) in the section prātarvaiśvadevam (Āś. 2-16). On this point there is the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence abhi tvā deva savitar iti sāvitrīm anvāha (Ai. Brā. 1-16).

It is also to be recited in the sacrifice called Pravargya; the sūtra abhi tvā deva savitaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3) samī vatsaṃ na mātṛbhiḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-104-2) in the section athottaram of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra explains this (Āś. 4-7).

It is also to be recited at the Grāvastotra, that is, when the stones used for pressing the soma juice are praised; the sūtra madhyamasvareṇedaṃ savanam abhi tvā deva savitaḥ in the section grāvastut tells this (Āś. 5-12).

Śunaḥśepa, sent on by Prajāpati, approached Agni and praised him; then, urged by Agni to praise Savitṛ, he praises Savitṛ with the three ṛks beginning abhi tvā deva savitaḥ. In this ṛk and in the next, Śunaḥśepa prays to Savitṛ to give him wealth and the like. It seems strange that Śunaḥśepa, tied to the sacrificial post and facing death, leaves off praying for his release and prays that wealth and power be given to him, who is close to death.

ईशानं वार्याणां (īśānaṃ vāryāṇāṃ) — वरणीयानां धनानां स्वामिनं (varaṇīyānāṃ dhanānāṃ svāminaṃ): the lord of the wealth and power that all desire, that is, the one who gives wealth and power.

भागं (bhāgaṃ) — भजनीयं (bhajanīyaṃ): worthy to be worshipped.

The main sense of this ṛk may be this: "O god Savitṛ, you are the lord of the wealth and power that all desire, and you are worthy of worship. I pray to such a one as you." Here Śunaḥśepa prays to Savitṛ, calling him the giver of what is desired and worthy of worship; it does not appear that he has asked to be given wealth. In this ṛk there is no word that indicates wealth. Although the commentator has explained the word vāryāṇāṃ as "riches desired by all", one may freely say that here the thing desired is not wealth but release from death.

Page 256 — Rik 3: grammar

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

वार्याणां (vāryāṇāṃ) — vṛñ saṃbhaktau. By ṛhalor ṇyat (Pā. Sū. 3-1-120 [as printed; for 3-1-124]), ṇyat comes after a root ending in ṛ or in a consonant; so ṇyat after the root vṛ: vṛ + ya. By aco ñṇiti (Pā. Sū. 7-2-115), vṛddhi ār comes for the ṛ: vārya. By īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ (Pā. Sū. 5-1-214 [as printed; for 6-1-214]), the first syllable of the roots īḍ and the rest, when they end in the suffix ṇyat, is acute; so vārya has the initial acute.

भागं (bhāgaṃ) — bhaja sevāyām. By halaś ca (Pā. Sū. 3-3-121), ghañ comes after a root ending in a consonant: bhaj + a. By cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ (Pā. Sū. 7-3-52), kutva (j → g); upadhā-vṛddhi. By karṣātvato ghaño 'nta udāttaḥ (Pā. Sū. 6-1-59 [as printed; for 6-1-159]), the last syllable of the root karṣ of the first class and of a root with ā ending in the suffix ghañ is acute; so the final acute comes. ॥3॥ An ornament follows.

yaḥ | cit | hi | te | itthā | bhagaḥ | śaśamānaḥ | purā | nidaḥ | adveṣaḥ | hastayoḥ | dadhe ||4||

स्वकीये धने वैरिभिरपहृते सति वैरिगृहीतं धनं सर्वो लोको निन्दति द्वेष्टि च । अतो धनस्तुतिर्न नियतेत्याशङ्क्याह । निदः पुरा अद्वेषो निन्दायाः पूर्वं स्वकीयत्वेन व्यवस्थिते सति तदानीं द्वेषरहितः । तस्मात्स्वकीयत्वाभिप्रायेण स्तूयमानत्वमुक्तमित्यर्थः ॥ इत्था । प्रकारवचने इदमुस्थमुः । पा. ५-३-२४ । सुपां सुलुगिति व्यत्ययेन विभक्तेर्डादेशः । टिलोप उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेणाकार उदात्तः । शशमानः । शश प्लुतगतौ । इह तु स्तुत्यर्थः । ताच्छील्यवयोवचनेति । पा. ३-२-१२९ । ताच्छीलिकश्चानश् । कर्तरि शप् । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं । निदः । णिदि कुत्सायां । संपदादिलक्षणः क्विप् । सावेकाच इति पञ्चम्या उदात्तत्वं । अद्वेषः । न विद्यते द्वेषोऽस्येति बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । दधे । कर्मणि लिट् । तस्यार्धधातुकत्वेनाभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तो न भवति । प्रत्ययस्वर एव शिष्यते । यद्वृत्तयोगान्निघाताभावः ॥

svakīye dhane vairibhirapahṛte sati vairigṛhītaṃ dhanaṃ sarvo loko nindati dveṣṭi ca | ato dhanastutirna niyatetyāśaṅkyāha | nidaḥ purā adveṣo nindāyāḥ pūrvaṃ svakīyatvena vyavasthite sati tadānīṃ dveṣarahitaḥ | tasmātsvakīyatvābhiprāyeṇa stūyamānatvamuktamityarthaḥ || itthā | prakāravacane idamusthamuḥ | pā. 5-3-24 | supāṃ sulugiti vyatyayena vibhakterḍādeśaḥ | ṭilopa udāttanivṛttisvareṇākāra udāttaḥ | śaśamānaḥ | śaśa plutagatau | iha tu stutyarthaḥ | tācchīlyavayovacaneti | pā. 3-2-129 | tācchīlikaścānaś | kartari śap | cita ityantodāttatvaṃ | nidaḥ | ṇidi kutsāyāṃ | saṃpadādilakṣaṇaḥ kvip | sāvekāca iti pañcamyā udāttatvaṃ | adveṣaḥ | na vidyate dveṣo 'syeti bahuvrīhau nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | dadhe | karmaṇi liṭ | tasyārdhadhātukatvenābhyastānāmādirityādyudātto na bhavati | pratyayasvara eva śiṣyate | yadvṛttayogānnighātābhāvaḥ ||

Gist: "O Savitṛ, the desirable wealth that has been held in your hands, that wealth we ask for" (construed with the previous ṛk). Cit is for honour, hi for "well known"; that wealth deserves honour is known everywhere. Itthā śaśamānaḥ: praised in this way. To the objection that wealth seized by enemies is blamed and hated by all, he answers nidaḥ purā adveṣaḥ: before such blame, while it is still one's own, it is free from hatred; so it is praised as one's own. The grammatical tail covers itthā (thamu; ḍā for the case-ending), śaśamānaḥ (cānaś; final acute), nidaḥ (kvip; acute ablative), adveṣaḥ (bahuvrīhi; final acute by nañsubhyām) and dadhe (passive liṭ; suffix accent; no lowering because of yat).

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे सवितः (he savitaḥ) — O god Savitṛ) निदः पुरा (nidaḥ purā) — before it is blamed | अद्वेषः (adveṣaḥ) — not deserving hatred | इत्था (itthā) — in this way | शशमानः (śaśamānaḥ) — praised | यः भगः (yaḥ bhagaḥ) — which desirable wealth | ते (te) — your | हस्तयोः (hastayoḥ) — in the hands | दधे (dadhe) — was held (that wealth we ask for) | चित् हि (cit hi) — (that wealth deserves praise) is well known, is it not? sic: the print ends ".?"

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O god Savitṛ, (although wealth that is carried off and lost deserves blame,) before that it does not deserve hatred; (that wealth,) thus praised, which is in your hands (we ask for).

॥ English Translation ॥

(We ask for) that wealth which has been retained in your hand and is so much praised against every envy or reproach

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The meaning of this ṛk is obscure. The intent does not fit properly.

चित् (cit) — the commentator says that this word is used in the sense of honour and that the word hi denotes "well known".

इत्था (itthā) — in this way; that is, everyone praises wealth as an excellent thing. Such भगः (bhagaḥ), that is, भजनीयो धनविशेषः (bhajanīyo dhanaviśeṣaḥ): the particular wealth that one longs for.

Page 258 — Rik 4: Special Topics (continued), grammar

शशमानः (śaśamānaḥ) — शश प्लुतपतौ । शस्यमानः स्तूयमानः (śaśa plutapatau | śasyamānaḥ stūyamānaḥ) [sic: प्लुतपतौ for प्लुतगतौ]: being praised, being extolled.

पुरा निदः (purā nidaḥ) — what use these words have in this ṛk, and what meaning, is not at all clear. निदः (nidaḥ) — ṇidi kutsāyāṃ: being blamed. No one blames wealth; everyone praises it. But when enemies, that is foes, carry it off, people blame it: so the commentator explains. The intent does not fit properly.

भगः — भजनीयः धनविशेषः (bhagaḥ — bhajanīyaḥ dhanaviśeṣaḥ) — although the commentator has said "the particular wealth that is desired", here the thing desired should be understood to be not wealth but life-span, that is, life itself.

अद्वेषः — अविद्यमानो द्वेषो यस्मिन्सोऽद्वेषः । द्वेषवर्जितः (adveṣaḥ — avidyamāno dveṣo yasmin so 'dveṣaḥ | dveṣavarjitaḥ) — free from hatred, needed by all, praised by all, and so on.

In this ṛk Śunaḥśepa may have prayed to Savitṛ to give him the life that all desire.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

इत्था (itthā) — by idamas thamuḥ (Pā. Sū. 5-3-24), the suffix thamu comes after the word idam in the sense of manner: idam + tham. By etetau rathoḥ (Pā. Sū. 5-3-4), when a suffix beginning with r or th follows, idam is replaced by eta and it respectively; so the substitute it: it + tham = ittham. By taddhitaś cāsarvavibhaktiḥ (Pā. Sū. 1-1-38) this is an indeclinable, so the following case-ending would properly be dropped. Yet, by Vedic interchange, through supāṃ suluk (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the instrumental singular ṭā is replaced by ḍā; the ṭi am is dropped, giving itthā.

शशमानः (śaśamānaḥ) — śaśa plutagatau, here in the sense of praise. By tācchīlyavayovacanaśaktiṣu cānaś (Pā. Sū. 3-2-129), cānaś comes for laṭ in the sense of habit; the vikaraṇa śap: śaś + a + āna. By āne muk (Pā. Sū. 7-2-82), the muk augment. By citaḥ, the final acute. ॥4॥ An ornament follows.

भ॑गभक्तस्य ते व॒यमुद॑शेम॒ तवाव॑सा । मू॒र्धानं॑ रा॒य आ॒रभे॑ ॥५॥

bhagabhaktasya te vayám úd aśema távā́vasā | mūrdhā́naṃ rāyá ārábhe ||5|| Strokes over भ (first), द (उद) and व (अव), and in line 2 (p. 259) over नं and भे; bars under व (वयं), म (शेम), मू, रा and आ.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

भगऽभक्तस्य । ते । वयं । उत् । अशेम । तव । अवसा । मूर्धानं । रायः । आऽरभे ॥५॥

bhaga 'bhaktasya | te | vayaṃ | ut | aśema | tava | avasā | mūrdhānaṃ | rāyaḥ | ā 'rabhe ||5||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

As printed: रक्षणेनोदशेम (not -शेमः); the bhāṣya ends with the varga number ॥१३॥ (Varga 13 ends here).

हे सवितः ते त्वदीया वयं शुनःशेपनामानो भगभक्तस्य धनेन संयुक्तस्य तवावसा रक्षणेनोदशेम । उत्कर्षेण व्याप्नुमः । किं कर्तुं । रायो धनस्य मूर्धानमुत्कर्षमारभे । प्रारब्धुं । धनिकत्वप्रसिद्ध्या व्याप्ता भूयास्मेत्यर्थः । भगशब्दो वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अशेम । अशू व्याप्तौ । लिङि व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । शप् । रायः । ऊडिदमिति षष्ठ्या उदात्तत्वं । आरभे । कृत्यार्थे तवैकेनिति तुमर्थे केन्प्रत्ययः । नित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥१३॥

he savitaḥ te tvadīyā vayaṃ śunaḥśepanāmāno bhagabhaktasya dhanena saṃyuktasya tavāvasā rakṣaṇenodaśema | utkarṣeṇa vyāpnumaḥ | kiṃ kartuṃ | rāyo dhanasya mūrdhānamutkarṣamārabhe | prārabdhuṃ | dhanikatvaprasiddhyā vyāptā bhūyāsmetyarthaḥ | bhagaśabdo vṛṣāditvādādyudāttaḥ | tṛtīyā karmaṇīti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | aśema | aśū vyāptau | liṅi vyatyayena parasmaipadaṃ | śap | rāyaḥ | ūḍidamiti ṣaṣṭhyā udāttatvaṃ | ārabhe | kṛtyārthe tavaikeniti tumarthe kenpratyayaḥ | nitsvareṇādyudāttatvaṃ ||13||

Gist: "O Savitṛ, may we, yours, named Śunaḥśepa, through the protection of you who are endowed with wealth, rise to and take hold of the height of wealth": may we be filled with the fame of being rich. The grammatical tail notes the accents of bhaga (vṛṣādi, initial acute) and of the compound (tṛtīyā karmaṇi), aśema (parasmaipada by interchange; śap), rāyaḥ (acute genitive by ūḍidam) and ārabhe (ken in the sense of the infinitive; initial acute).

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥

(हे सवितः (he savitaḥ) — O Savitṛ) | ते (te) — who are yours | वयं (vayaṃ) — we (Śunaḥśepas) | भगभक्तस्य (bhagabhaktasya) — who is endowed with wealth | तव (tava) — your | अवसा (avasā) — by the protection | रायः (rāyaḥ) — of wealth | मूर्धानं (mūrdhānaṃ) — the highest state | आरभे (ārabhe) — to begin (to enjoy) | उदशेम (udaśema) — may we pervade (may we proceed).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥

O Savitṛ, may we who are yours, through the protection of you who are endowed with wealth, begin to enjoy the height of wealth (the fame of being very rich).

॥ English Translation ॥

(O Savitri,) may we under the protection of you who are rich in wealth obtain the best of prosperity that we may enjoy it.

Page 260 — Rik 5: Special Topics, grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

भगभक्तस्य — धनेन संयुक्तस्य (bhagabhaktasya — dhanena saṃyuktasya) — possessed of wealth. Skandasvāmin explains this word as

भगो देवः तेनापि सेवितस्य, भजनीयेन वा हविषा स्तोत्रेण वा सर्वमनुष्यैः सेवितस्य ॥

bhago devaḥ tenāpi sevitasya, bhajanīyena vā haviṣā stotreṇa vā sarvamanuṣyaiḥ sevitasya ||

that is, "served by the deity named Bhaga; or served by all men with objects of worship such as worshipful oblations".

उत् अशेम — उत्कर्षेण व्याप्नुमः (ut aśema — utkarṣeṇa vyāpnumaḥ) — we pervade in a special way, that is, we obtain. तव अवसा (tava avasā) — by your protection we pervade, that is, we obtain your protection; the intent is: we desire your protection.

मूर्धानं रायः (mūrdhānaṃ rāyaḥ) — the excellence of wealth, that is, abundant wealth: "Plenty of riches."

आरभे, आरब्धुं (ārabhe, ārabdhuṃ) — to begin, to enjoy.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

भगभक्तस्य (bhagabhaktasya) — by ghañarthe kavidhānam, the suffix ka comes after the root bhaj, with kutva. Bhagena bhaktaḥ: an instrumental tatpuruṣa. The word bhaga is initial-acute, being in the vṛṣādi group. By śeṣanighāta, the final syllable, which is unaccented, becomes svarita. Even after compounding, by tṛtīyā karmaṇi (Pā. Sū. 6-2-48), when a word ending in kta in the passive sense follows, a word in the instrumental keeps its own accent. So, as an exception to the thāthādi accent, the first member keeps its own accent.

आरभे (ārabhe) — by kṛtyārthe tavaikenkenyatvanaḥ (Pā. Sū. 3-4-14) and tayor eva kṛtyaktakhalarthāḥ, since the kṛtya suffixes are enjoined in the senses of bhāva and karman, bhāva and karman are the kṛtyārthas; in those senses the suffixes tavai, ken, kenya and tvan come. Here the suffix ken comes after the root rabh, preceded by āṅ. Only its e remains: ā + rabh + e = ārabhe. By the nit accent it is initial-acute. ॥5॥

Page 260 (lower) — Sūkta 24, Rik 6 (the Varuṇa riks begin)

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

न॒हि ते॑ क्ष॒त्रं न सहो॒ न म॒न्युं वय॑श्च॒नामी प॒तय॑न्त आ॒पुः । नेमा आपो॑ अनिमि॒षं चर॑न्ती॒र्न ये वात॑स्य प्रमि॒नन्त्यभ्वं॑ ॥६॥
