॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

सदा यविष्ठ सर्वदा युवतम हे अग्ने वरेण्यो वरणीयस्त्वं नोऽस्माकं होता होमनिष्पादको भूत्वा दिवित्मता दीप्तिमता वचसा स्तूयमानः सन् नि षीदेति शेषः । कीदृशस्त्वं । मन्मभिर्ज्ञापकैस्तेजोभिर्युक्त इति शेषः ॥ यविष्ठ । युवशब्दादिष्ठनि स्थूलदूरेत्यादिना । पा ६-४-१५६ । यणादिपरस्य लोपः । पूर्वस्योकारस्य गुणश्च । अवादेशः । आमंत्रितनिघातः । मन्मभिः । मन ज्ञाने । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंत इति मनिन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । दिवित्मता । दिवु क्रीडादौ । इक्श्तिपौ धातुनिर्देशे । पा. ३-३-१०८-२ । इतीक्प्रत्ययः । तेन च धातुवाचिना दिविशब्देन धात्वर्थो दीप्तिर्लक्ष्यते । यद्वा । औणादिको भावे किप्रत्ययः । दिविशब्दान्मतुपि तकारोपजनश्छांदसः । यद्वा । बाहुलकाद्दिवेर्भाव इतक् । मतुपि तसौ मत्वर्थ इति भत्वाज्जश्त्वाभावः । वचः । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयैकवचनस्य लुक् ॥

sadā yaviṣṭha sarvadā yuvatama he agne vareṇyo varaṇīyastvaṃ no 'smākaṃ hotā homaniṣpādako bhūtvā divitmatā dīptimatā vacasā stūyamānaḥ san ni ṣīdeti śeṣaḥ | kīdṛśastvaṃ | manmabhirjñāpakaistejobhiryukta iti śeṣaḥ ‖ yaviṣṭha | yuvaśabdādiṣṭhani sthūladūretyādinā | pā 6-4-156 | yaṇādiparasya lopaḥ | pūrvasyokārasya guṇaśca | avādeśaḥ | āmaṃtritanighātaḥ | manmabhiḥ | mana jñāne | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyaṃta iti maninpratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvaṃ | divitmatā | divu krīḍādau | ikśtipau dhātunirdeśe | pā. 3-3-108-2 | itīkpratyayaḥ | tena ca dhātuvācinā diviśabdena dhātvartho dīptirlakṣyate | yadvā | auṇādiko bhāve kipratyayaḥ | diviśabdānmatupi takāropajanaśchāṃdasaḥ | yadvā | bāhulakāddiverbhāva itak | matupi tasau matvartha iti bhatvājjaśtvābhāvaḥ | vacaḥ | supāṃ sulugiti tṛtīyaikavacanasya luk ‖ Numbers zoom-read at 450 dpi: पा ६-४-१५६ (printed without a point after पा), ३-३-१०८-२.

Gist: O ever-youngest Agni, chosen one, become our hotṛ and sit down, praised with shining words; you are endowed with splendours that make things known.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ सदा (sadā) — always | यविष्ठ (yaviṣṭha) — being exceedingly young | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | वरेण्यः (vareṇyaḥ) — chosen (by us) | मन्मभिः (manmabhiḥ) — with splendours (shining) | दिवित्मता (divitmatā) — splendid | वचः (vacaḥ) — praised with (our) words of praise | नः (naḥ) — for us | होता (hotā) — as the performer of the homa | नि (षीद) (ni (ṣīda)) — sit down.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni, you are ever young. We choose you alone for our sacrificial work. Shining with your splendours, and praised by our splendid words of praise, come here as the one who performs the homa for us, and sit down.

॥ English Translation ॥

O ever youthful Agni, being praised with brilliant hymn, sit down, here, as we have selected you as our Hotri to perform the sacrifice.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

सदा यविष्ठ (sadā yaviṣṭha) — sarvadā yuvatama: one who is always young. However much firewood and the like is put in, Agni keeps blazing strongly; so they call him ever young.

Page 351 — Rik 2: Special Topics (end), grammar

वरेण्यः (vareṇyaḥ) — varaṇīyaḥ: one who has been chosen; they have chosen Agni alone to carry out the sacrifice. Or the sense "best" may also be given.

मन्मभिः (manmabhiḥ) — mana jñāne; jñāpakais tejobhir yuktaḥ: the commentator explains the word as "endowed with splendour that makes known", that is, with natural splendour. The authors of the Vedārthayatna take manmabhiḥ as dhyānaiḥ, "meditations" (so in English in the print), by meditations. This sense too fits here.

दिवित्मता (divitmatā) — dīptimatā: shining. Since the word qualifies vacaḥ, "with shining words" may be explained as excellent, meaningful, mature words and the like.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar, noted briefly; numbers zoom-read at 450 dpi, v3a

यविष्ठ (yaviṣṭha) — atiśayena yuvā yaviṣṭhaḥ. By "अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ" (Pā. Sū. 5-3-55) iṣṭhan after yuvan; by "स्थूलदूरयुवह्रस्व-" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-156) before iṣṭhan the part from the yaṇ onward is dropped; then the preceding u takes guṇa: yo + iṣṭha; by "एचोऽयवायावः" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-78) av for o: yaviṣṭha. In the vocative, the nighāta by "आमन्त्रितस्य च".

मन्मभिः (manmabhiḥ) — mana jñāne, divādi; by "अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-130, as printed: the middle digit is the curled 2; for 3-2-75) the suffix manin: manman, an n-stem. Before the instrumental plural bhis it is called pada, so by "नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य" the n is dropped; since that loss is asiddha, bhis does not become ais; with rutva and visarga, manmabhiḥ. Manin being nit, by "ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम्" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) initially acute.

दिवित्मता (divitmatā) — divu krīḍādau, divādi, read in the ten senses krīḍā, vijigīṣā and so on. By "इक्श्तिपौ धातुनिर्देशे" (Pā. Sū. 3-3-108-2), when a root is named, the suffixes ik and śtip come; here ik: diviḥ. Divi means the root div; but here, by lakṣaṇā, the root's sense, light, is to be taken; then divi means light. Or, in the abstract sense,

Page 352 — Rik 2: grammar (end)

an Uṇādi suffix is to be stated; then divi means light directly. In the sense diviḥ asya asti (that which has light), by "तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप्" (Pā. Sū. 5-2-94) the suffix matup; with divimat, the t augment comes in the middle as a Vedic form; after divitmat, the instrumental singular ṭā gives divitmatā. Or: by bahula, after the root div the suffix itak in the abstract sense; after divit, matup gives divitmat; by "तसौ मत्वर्थे" (Pā. Sū. 1-4-19) a stem in t is called bha before a possessive suffix, so there is no pada name and no jaśtva; in the instrumental singular divitmatā.

वचः (vacaḥ) — vaca paribhāṣaṇe, adādi; by "सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन्" (Uṇ. Sū. 4-6[?]8, as printed: the third glyph is blurred; on p. 290 the same sūtra is printed ४-६-२८) the suffix asun: vacas, an s-stem. When the instrumental singular is meant, by "सुपां सुलुक्" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) it takes luk: vacaḥ. Ending in a nit suffix, it is initially acute. ॥२॥

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ हि ष्मा॑ सू॒नवे॑ पि॒तापिर्यज॑त्या॒पये॑ । सखा॒ सख्ये॒ वरे॑ण्यः ॥३॥ [accent ?]

ā hí ṣmā sūnáve pitā́piryájatyāpáye | sakhā sákhye váreṇyaḥ ||3|| [accent ?] Saṃhitā accents as printed, read on 450-dpi line crops (v3a); Pada unaccented, though the print marks the Pada too. Flagged [accent ?] on line 2: the first bar stands between स and खा of सखा; it is given under खा. The Pada prints आपिः and आपये (with long ā). IAST mechanical from the marks.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

आ । हि । स्म । सूनवे । पिता । आपिः । यजति । आपये । सखा । सख्ये । वरेण्यः ॥३॥

ā | hi | sma | sūnave | pitā | āpiḥ | yajati | āpaye | sakhā | sakhye | vareṇyaḥ ‖3‖

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने वरेण्यो वरणीयः पितापि पितृस्थानीयस्त्वं सूनवे पुत्रस्थानीयाय मह्यमभीष्टं देहीति शेषः । हि स्मेति निपातद्वयं सर्वथेत्यमुमर्थमाचष्टे । अभीष्टदाने दृष्टांतद्वयमुच्यते । यथापिर्बंधुरापये बंधव आ यजति हि स्म । सर्वथा ददातीति शेषः । सखा प्रियः सख्ये प्रियायाभीष्टं सर्वथा ददाति तथा त्वमपि देहि ॥ स्मा सूनवे । निपातस्य चेति दीर्घः । यजतीत्यस्य सखा सख्य इत्यत्राप्यनुषंगात्तदपेक्षयेयं प्रथमेति चादिलोपे विभाषेति न निहन्यते । यद्वा । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । सख्ये । समाने ख्यः स चोदात्त इति सखिशब्द इण्प्रत्ययांत आद्युदात्तः । सुपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे स एव शिष्यते ॥

he agne vareṇyo varaṇīyaḥ pitāpi pitṛsthānīyastvaṃ sūnave putrasthānīyāya mahyamabhīṣṭaṃ dehīti śeṣaḥ | hi smeti nipātadvayaṃ sarvathetyamumarthamācaṣṭe | abhīṣṭadāne dṛṣṭāṃtadvayamucyate | yathāpirbaṃdhurāpaye baṃdhava ā yajati hi sma | sarvathā dadātīti śeṣaḥ | sakhā priyaḥ sakhye priyāyābhīṣṭaṃ sarvathā dadāti tathā tvamapi dehi ‖ smā sūnave | nipātasya ceti dīrghaḥ | yajatītyasya sakhā sakhya ityatrāpyanuṣaṃgāttadapekṣayeyaṃ prathameti cādilope vibhāṣeti na nihanyate | yadvā | hi ceti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | sakhye | samāne khyaḥ sa codātta iti sakhiśabda iṇpratyayāṃta ādyudāttaḥ | supaḥ pittvādanudāttatve sa eva śiṣyate ‖ No numbers in this bhāṣya.

Gist: O Agni, worthy to be chosen, being like a father, give me, who am like a son, what I desire; as a kinsman gives to a kinsman, and a friend to a dear friend, wholly, so do you give.

Page 353 — Rik 3: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ आपिः (āpiḥ) — one who is a kinsman | आपये (āpaye) — to his kinsman (and) | सखा (sakhā) — a (dear) friend | सख्ये (sakhye) — to his friend | आ यजति हि स्म (ā yajati hi sma) — (what is desired) surely gives, does he not (so) | सूनवे (sūnave) — to me, who stand as a son | पिता (pitā) — you, who are as a father (graciously grant my desire).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni, as a kinsman provides for the desire of his own close kinsman, and as one who is a friend for that of his dear friend, so do you, who are like a father, fulfil for me, who am like a son, my desire.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, you are indeed as a loving father to a son, as a kinsman to a kinsman, as a friend to a friend.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

आपिः, आपये (āpiḥ, āpaye) — bandhuḥ bandhave: as a kinsman behaves with goodwill towards his kinsman, so; in this ṛk the ṛṣi points to the great love there is between father and son, between kinsmen, and between friends, and prays that Agni likewise should protect him.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

स्मा सूनवे (smā sūnave) — sma is a particle; so by "निपातस्य च" (6-2-136, as printed, without "Pā. Sū."; the middle digit is the curled 2; for 6-3-136) it is lengthened in the mantra.

यजति (yajati) — yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, bhvādi; laṭ third singular. Following a word that is not a verb, the nighāta would come; but here, since

Page 354 — Rik 3: grammar (end)

the verb is understood also in sakhā sakhye, it is the first one uttered; so by "चादिलोपे विभाषा" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-63), when ca, vā and the like are dropped, the first-uttered tiṅanta is not all-anudātta, and the nighāta does not come. Or: by "हि च" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34) a tiṅanta joined with hi is not anudātta, so the nighāta is naturally barred. Śap and tip being anudātta, by the root's accent yajati is initially acute.

सख्ये (sakhye) — since "शेषो घ्यसखि" excludes it, sakhi is not called ghi; so before the dative singular ṅe the yaṇ substitute comes: sakhye. By "समाने ख्यः स चोदात्तः" (Uṇ. Sū. 4-5[7?]6, as printed: the third glyph is a 2-like shape with a flat foot, read as 7 with doubt), with samāna as upapada, the root khyā prakathane takes the suffix iṇ, which is ḍit; samāna is replaced by sa and is udātta; the loss of y is laid down in the sūtra itself. Because the suffix is ḍit, the ā of khyā, called ṭi, is dropped; the y is dropped by the sūtra itself: sakhi. Since sa is made udātta, sakhi is initially acute. The sup ending is anudātta by "अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-4), so the accent stated before remains as sati-śiṣṭa; sakhye too is initially acute. ॥३॥ A printed ornament follows; Ṛk 4 begins on the same page.

हे अग्ने वरुणादयो देवास्त्वद्बंधवस्त्वया प्रेरिता रिशादसो हिंसकानदंतो नोऽस्मदीयं बर्हिर्यज्ञमासीदंतु । तत्र दृष्टांतः । यथा मनुषः प्रजापतेर्यज्ञमासीदंति । तद्वत् ॥ बर्ही रिशादसः । विसर्जनीयस्य रुत्वे कृते रो रि । पा. ८-३-१४ । इति रेफलोपः । ढ्रलोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घोऽणः । पा. ६-३-१११ । इतीकारस्य दीर्घत्वं । रिशादसः । रिश हिंसायां । रिशंति हिंसंतीति रिशाः शत्रवः । इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः । तानदंतीति रिशादसः । सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । सीदंतु । षद्लृ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु । पाघ्रेत्यादिना सीदादेशः । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । मनुषः । मन ज्ञाने । मन्यते जानातीति मनुः प्रजापतिः । जनेरुसिर्निच्च । उ. २-११६-११८ । इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलमन्यत्रापि । उ. २-१२२ । इत्यौणादिक उसिप्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । यथा । यथेति पादांते । फि. ४. १७ । इति सर्वानुदात्तत्वं ॥

The print has शतुश्च in the note on सीदंतु, as printed.

Gist: O Agni, may Varuṇa and the other gods, your kinsmen, sent by you, devourers of the harmful, sit on our sacrificial grass, as they sit at the sacrifice of Manu Prajāpati.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (अग्ने) ((agne)) — (O Agni) | रिशादसः (riśādasaḥ) — the destroyers of enemies | वरुणः (varuṇaḥ) — Varuṇa | मित्रः (mitraḥ) — Mitra | अर्यमा (aryamā) — together with Aryaman | यथा (yathā) — in the manner in which | मनुषः (manuṣaḥ) — of Manu (they sat on the altar in the place of sacrifice, so) | नः (naḥ) — our | बर्हिः (barhiḥ) — on the seat of the sacrificial ground | आ सीदंतु (ā sīdaṃtu) — may they come and sit.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni, as Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman, the destroyers of enemies, once graciously sat on the seat of Manu's sacrificial ground, so may they now too sit on the seat of our sacrificial ground.

॥ English Translation ॥

Let Varuna, Mitra, Aryama, destroyers of the wicked, sit down upon our sacred grass as they did at the Sacrifice of Manu.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

अर्यमा (aryamā) — one of the twelve Ādityas, a son of Aditi.

Page 356 — Rik 4: Special Topics (end), grammar

बर्हिः (barhiḥ) — the seat of darbha grass, made ready by cutting the tips of the darbha called kuśa and spreading them soft in three layers, so that the gods may come and sit on the sacrificial altar.

रिशादसः (riśādasaḥ) — riśa hiṃsāyām; riśanti hiṃsantīti riśāḥ śatravaḥ; tān adantīti riśādasaḥ: the root riś means to harm; those who harm are called riśāḥ, enemies; since they destroy such enemies, riśādasaḥ means destroyers of enemies.

सीदंतु मनुषो यथा (sīdaṃtu manuṣo yathā) — as the gods came to the sacrificial ground in the sacrifice made by Manu Prajāpati and sat on the darbha seat, so may Mitra, Varuṇa and the others come to this our sacrificial ground and sit: this is the ṛṣi's prayer.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

बर्ही रिशादसः (barhī riśādasaḥ) — with barhis + riśādasaḥ, by "ससजुषो रुः" (Pā. Sū. 8-2-66) the word-final s of barhis becomes ru; by "रो रि" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-14) an r before an r is dropped, so the r of barhir is dropped. With barhi + riśādasaḥ, by "ढ्रलोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घोऽणः" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-111) the preceding aṇ is lengthened when a following letter is the cause of the loss of ḍh or r; so the i is lengthened: barhī riśādasaḥ.

रिशादसः (riśādasaḥ) — riśa hiṃsāyām, tudādi. By "इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-135), since the penultimate is an ik, the suffix ka; being kit, no guṇa of the light penultimate: riśa. Riśān adanti iti riśādasaḥ: those who eat, destroy, enemies. By "सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन्" (Uṇ. Sū. 4-6[?]8, as printed: the third glyph is blurred, as on p. 352) the suffix asun after ad bhakṣaṇe: riśādas, an s-stem; nominative plural riśādasaḥ. By "गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत्" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139), the first member being a kāraka upapada, the kṛt final member keeps its accent; adas, ending in a nit suffix, is initially acute, so in riśādasaḥ the ā after ś is udātta.

सीदंतु (sīdaṃtu) — ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu, bhvādi; in the loṭ third plural anta gives antu; the vikaraṇa śap; before it,

Page 357 — Rik 4: grammar (end)

by "पाघ्राध्मास्था-" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-78) the root takes the substitute sīda; by "अतो गुणे" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) pararūpa: sīdantu. Śap being pit is anudātta; after an adupadeśa, the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta by "तास्यनुदात्तेत्-" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186); then the root's end-acute, coming by "धातोः" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-162), remains as sati-śiṣṭa.

मनुषः (manuṣaḥ) — mana jñāne, divādi. Manyate jānātīti manuḥ prajāpatiḥ: the one who knows all. With "जनेरुसिर्निच्च" continuing, by "बहुलमन्यत्रापि" (Uṇ. Sū. 2-278, as read: the third glyph is the flat-footed 7; the bhāṣya gives उ. २-१२२) the suffix usi after man, and it is nit: manus, an s-stem. In the genitive singular the ending as; since the s follows an iṇ and is part of a suffix, it becomes ṣ: manuṣaḥ. Ending in a nit suffix, by "ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम्" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) it is initially acute.

यथा (yathā) — by "प्रकारवचने थाल्" (Pā. Sū. 5-3-23) thāl after yad in the sense of manner; since it is called vibhakti, by "त्यदादीनामः" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-102) the final becomes a: yathā. By "यथेति पादान्ते" (Phi. Sū. 85), standing at the end of the pāda, yathā is wholly anudātta, so the nighāta accent comes here. ॥४॥ A printed ornament follows; Ṛk 5 begins on the same page.

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे पूर्व्य अस्मदादेः पूर्वमुत्पन्न होतर्होमनिष्पादकाग्ने नोऽस्मदीयस्यास्य प्रवर्तमानस्य यज्ञस्य सख्यस्य चास्मदनुग्रहस्य च सिद्ध्यर्थं मंदस्व । त्वं हृष्टो भव । इमा अस्माभिः प्रयुज्यमाना गिर उ षु स्तुतिरूपा वाचोऽपि श्रुधि शृणु ॥ पूर्व्य । आमंत्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । होतरित्यस्य नामंत्रिते समानाधिकरण इति पूर्वस्य विद्यमानत्वादाष्टमिको निघातः । अस्य । ऊडिदमिति षष्ठ्या उदात्तत्वं । मंदस्व । मदि स्तुतिमोदमदस्वप्नकांतिगतिषु । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वं । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः । अपादादाविति पर्युदासादाष्टमिकनिघाताभावः । सख्यस्य । सख्युः कर्म सख्यं । सख्युर्यः । पा. ५-१-१२६ । इति यप्रत्ययः । यस्येति लोपे प्रत्ययस्वरः । उ षु । सुञः । पा. ८-३-१०७ । इति षत्वं । श्रुधि । श्रु श्रवणे । श्रुशृणुपॄकृवृभ्यश्छंदसीति हेर्धिरादेशः । बहुलं छंदसीति शपो लुक् ॥२०॥

he pūrvya asmadādeḥ pūrvamutpanna hotarhomaniṣpādakāgne no 'smadīyasyāsya pravartamānasya yajñasya sakhyasya cāsmadanugrahasya ca siddhyarthaṃ maṃdasva | tvaṃ hṛṣṭo bhava | imā asmābhiḥ prayujyamānā gira u ṣu stutirūpā vāco 'pi śrudhi śṛṇu ‖ pūrvya | āmaṃtritādyudāttatvaṃ | hotarityasya nāmaṃtrite samānādhikaraṇa iti pūrvasya vidyamānatvādāṣṭamiko nighātaḥ | asya | ūḍidamiti ṣaṣṭhyā udāttatvaṃ | maṃdasva | madi stutimodamadasvapnakāṃtigatiṣu | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvaṃ | tiṅaśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvaraḥ | apādādāviti paryudāsādāṣṭamikanighātābhāvaḥ | sakhyasya | sakhyuḥ karma sakhyaṃ | sakhyuryaḥ | pā. 5-1-126 | iti yapratyayaḥ | yasyeti lope pratyayasvaraḥ | u ṣu | suñaḥ | pā. 8-3-107 | iti ṣatvaṃ | śrudhi | śru śravaṇe | śruśṛṇupṝkṛvṛbhyaśchaṃdasīti herdhirādeśaḥ | bahulaṃ chaṃdasīti śapo luk ‖20‖ Numbers zoom-read at 450 dpi: पा. ५-१-१२६, ८-३-१०७; the closing ॥२०॥ marks the end of Varga 20 (Ṛks 1–5).

Gist: O ancient one, Agni the hotṛ, rejoice for the success of this our sacrifice and of your favour to us, and hear these words of praise we offer.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ पूर्व्य (pūrvya) — ancient (more than all of us) | होतः (hotaḥ) — and performer of the homa, O Agni | नः (naḥ) — our | अस्य (asya) — (now going on) by this sacrifice | च (ca) — and | सख्यस्य (sakhyasya) — by (our) friendship (for their increase) | मंदस्व (maṃdasva) — be pleased | इमाः (imāḥ) — used by us | गिरः उ षु (giraḥ u ṣu) — our words of praise too | श्रुधि (śrudhi) — listen.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni, you are more ancient than all of us and the performer of the homa. Being pleased by the sacrifice we are now performing and by our friendship, make it grow. Listen also to these words of praise of ours that we use.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Ancient Hotri, Agni, be pleased with this our sacrifice and with our friendship and listen to these our prayers.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

पूर्व्य (pūrvya) — asmadādeḥ pūrvam utpanna: born before all of us, ancient.

होतः (hotaḥ) — performer of the homa, the one who brings the gods to the sacrifice.

Page 359 — Rik 5: Special Topics (end), grammar

अस्य (asya) — of this sacrifice; by the sacrifice we are now performing.

सख्यस्य (sakhyasya) — the sense is: so that you, regarding us as friends, may show favour. On the theme of desiring the friendship of the gods: tavedd hi sakhyam astṛtam (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-5); devānāṃ sakhyam upasedimā vayaṃ devā na āyuḥ pra tirantu jīvase (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-2); anu vrātāsas tava sakhyam īyur anu devā mamire vīryaṃ te (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-163-8); yayor asti pra ṇaḥ sakhyaṃ deveṣv adhyāpyam (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-10-3); yad imo sakhyam āvara imasya pāhy andhasaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-13-21); pra so agne tavotibhiḥ suvīrābhis tirate vājabharmabhiḥ | yasya tvaṃ sakhyam āvaraḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-19-30); adabdhasya svadhāvato dūtasya rebhataḥ sadā | agneḥ sakhyaṃ vṛṇīmahe (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-44-20) — many such examples can be given.

तवेद्धि सख्यमस्तृतं ॥ देवानां सख्यमुपसेदिमा वयं देवा न आयुः प्र तिरंतु जीवसे ॥ अनु व्रातासस्तव सख्यमीयुरनु देवा ममिरे वीर्यं ते ॥ ययोरस्ति प्र णः सख्यं देवेष्वध्याप्यं ॥ यदिमो सख्यमावर इमस्य पाह्यंधसः । प्र सो अग्ने तवोतिभिः सुवीराभिस्तिरते वाजभर्मभिः । यस्य त्वं सख्यमावरः ॥ अदब्धस्य स्वधावतो दूतस्य रेभतः सदा ॥ अग्नेः सख्यं वृणीमहे ॥

taveddhi sakhyamastṛtaṃ ‖ devānāṃ sakhyamupasedimā vayaṃ devā na āyuḥ pra tiraṃtu jīvase ‖ anu vrātāsastava sakhyamīyuranu devā mamire vīryaṃ te ‖ yayorasti pra ṇaḥ sakhyaṃ deveṣvadhyāpyaṃ ‖ yadimo sakhyamāvara imasya pāhyaṃdhasaḥ | pra so agne tavotibhiḥ suvīrābhistirate vājabharmabhiḥ | yasya tvaṃ sakhyamāvaraḥ ‖ adabdhasya svadhāvato dūtasya rebhataḥ sadā ‖ agneḥ sakhyaṃ vṛṇīmahe ‖

Glosses, editorial and tentative: "your friendship is unbroken"; "we have come to the friendship of the gods; may the gods prolong our life for living"; "the companies followed your friendship, the gods measured your might"; "whose friendship towards us is to be gained among the gods"; "since you have chosen this friendship, drink of this juice"; "he prospers, O Agni, by your aids rich in heroes and booty, whose friendship you have chosen"; "we choose the friendship of Agni, the unharmed, self-powered messenger, ever resounding".

मंदस्व (maṃdasva) — be pleased, be delighted.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

पूर्व्य (pūrvya) — pūrve bhavaḥ pūrvyaḥ: one born before; yat in the sense of "being there"; in the vocative pūrvya. Standing not after another word, by "आमन्त्रितस्य च" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198) it is initially acute.

होतः (hotaḥ) — hu dānādanayoḥ, juhotyādi; tṛc in the agent sense; vocative hotaḥ. Here both pūrvya and hotaḥ are āmantrita. Then by "आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत्" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-72) the earlier āmantrita would be treated as non-existent; but here

Page 360 — Rik 5: grammar (end)

the two words are in apposition, both meaning the same thing; so by "नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरणे सामान्यवचनम्" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-73) it is not treated as non-existent, that is, it counts as a word standing before; so by "आमन्त्रितस्य च" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19) hotaḥ, an āmantrita after a word, takes the nighāta accent.

अस्य (asya) — after idam, the genitive singular ṅas; by "त्यदादीनामः" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-102) the stem takes a; with idas, after a, by "टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-12) ṅas becomes sya; before a consonant-initial suffix by "हलि लोपः" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-113) the id is dropped: asya. By "ऊडिदम्पदादि-" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the ending is udātta: asya is end-acute.

मंदस्व (maṃdasva) — madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu, bhvādi; loṭ second singular maṃdasva. Being idit, it takes num. Śap is anudātta as pit; the tiṅ after an adupadeśa is anudātta by "तास्यनुदात्तेत्-" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186); the root's end-acute remains; maṃdasva is initially acute. Since "अपादादौ" excludes it, by "तिङ्ङतिङः" (Pā. Sū. 5-1-28, as printed: the first glyph is the same as the 5 of the bhāṣya's ५-१-१२६; for 8-1-28) the nighāta does not come.

सख्यस्य (sakhyasya) — sakhyuḥ karma sakhyam: the work of a friend. By "सख्युर्यः" (Pā. Sū. 5-1-126) the suffix ya in the sense of state or action; before a y-initial suffix the stem is bha: sakhya; genitive singular. By the suffix accent sakhyasya is medially acute.

उ षु (u ṣu) — by "सुञः" (Pā. Sū. 8-3-107), after a conditioning sound (iṇ or a ka-class letter) in the preceding word, the s of the particle suñ becomes ṣ; here, after u, the ṣatva comes.

श्रुधि (śrudhi) — śru śravaṇe, bhvādi; loṭ second singular, hi for si. By "बहुलं छन्दसि" (Pā. Sū. 2-4-73) the vikaraṇa śap takes luk; by "श्रुशृणुपॄकृवृभ्यश्छन्दसि" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-102) dhi for hi: śrudhi. ॥५॥ A printed ornament follows.

यत् । चित् । हि । शश्वता । तना । देवंऽदेवं । यजामहे । त्वे इति । इत् । हूयते । हविः ॥६॥

yat | cit | hi | śaśvatā | tanā | devaṃ-devaṃ | yajāmahe | tve iti | it | hūyate | haviḥ ‖6‖

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने यच्चिद्धि यद्यपि शश्वता शाश्वतेन नित्येन तना विस्तृतेन हविषा देवंदेवमन्यमन्यं वरुणेंद्रादिरूपं नानाविधं देवताविशेषं यजामहे तथापि तद्धविः सर्वं त्वे इत्त्वय्येव हूयते । अतो देवांतरविषयो यागोऽपि त्वदीयैव सेवेत्यर्थः ॥ तना । तनु विस्तारे । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । यद्वा । पचाद्यच् । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयाया आकारः । देवंदेवं । नित्यवीप्सयोरिति द्विर्भावः । तस्य परमाम्रेडितमित्युत्तरस्याम्रेडितसंज्ञायामनुदात्तं चेति सर्वानुदात्तत्वं । यजामहे । निपातैर्यद्यदिहंतेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । त्वे । युष्मच्छब्दात्सप्तम्येकवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगिति शे आदेशः । त्वमावेकवचन इति मपर्यंतस्य त्वादेशः । शेषलोपेऽतो गुण इति पररूपत्वं । शे । पा. १-१-१३ । इति प्रगृह्यसंज्ञायां प्लुतप्रगृह्या अचि । पा. ६-१-१२५ । इति प्रकृतिभावः । हूयते । अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोः । पा. ७-४-२५ । इति दीर्घः ॥

Gist: O Agni, although we worship god after god, Varuṇa, Indra and the rest, with constant and ample oblation, all that oblation is offered in you alone; so even the worship of other gods is service to you.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (अग्ने) ((agne)) — (O Agni) | यच्चिद्धि (yaccid dhi) — whatever | शश्वता (śaśvatā) — constant (without missing a single day) | तना (tanā) — and most abundant, with that oblation | देवंदेवं (devaṃdevaṃ) — all the gods (Varuṇa, Indra and the others) | यजामहे (yajāmahe) — we worship | हविः (haviḥ) — all that oblation | त्वे इत् (tve it) — in you alone | हूयते (hūyate) — is offered.

Page 362 — Rik 6: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni, the oblation, offered without missing a single day, that is, offered every day, and most abundant, which we offer intending it for the gods Varuṇa, Indra and the others — all that oblation we offer first in you, that is, we offer it through you alone.

॥ English Translation ॥

Whatever we offer as plentiful oblations to the different deities every day is assuredly offered to (through) you.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

शश्वता (śaśvatā) — śāśvatena, nityena: which we offer every day.

तना (tanā) — vistṛtena: with ample, abundant oblation.

देवंदेवं (devaṃdevaṃ) — anyam anyaṃ varuṇendrādirūpaṃ nānāvidhaṃ devatāviśeṣam: every deity, that is, intending the various gods Varuṇa, Indra and the others.

त्वे इत् हूयते हविः (tve it hūyate haviḥ) — the oblation we offer intending the other gods we offer in you alone, Agni. Since by the scriptural statement parokṣaṃ vā anye devā ijyante the other gods are not seen by the eye, we offer in Agni alone the oblation that is to be given to them, intending them. The sense is: you, the messenger of the gods, carry the oblation offered in you to them.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥ grammar, noted briefly; numbers read at 450 dpi, v3a

तना (tanā) — tanu vistāre, tanādi; by "क्विप् च" (Pā. Sū. 3-2-76) the suffix kvip, wholly dropped: tan, an n-stem; instrumental singular tanā. Or: by "नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यः-" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134), being in the pacādi list, the suffix ac: tana, an a-stem; for the instrumental singular, by "सुपां सुलुक्" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the substitute ā: tanā.

देवंदेवम् (devaṃdevam) — by "नित्यवीप्सयोः" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-4), when repetition (vīpsā) is meant, the word is doubled; here vīpsā is meant. By "तस्य परमाम्रेडितम्" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-2) the latter form is called āmreḍita;

Page 363 — Rik 6: grammar (end)

by "अनुदात्तं च" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-3) the repeated latter form is all-anudātta; so the latter form takes the nighāta accent.

यजामहे (yajāmahe) — yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu; first plural. Because of its connection with yat in yaccid dhi, by "निपातैर्यद्यदिहन्त-" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-30) the tiṅanta's nighāta does not come.

त्वे (tve) — after yuṣmad, for the locative singular, by "सुपां सुलुक्" the substitute śe; being śit, it replaces the whole. By "त्वमावेकवचने" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-97) tva for the part up to m; with tva + ad + e, by "शेषे लोपः" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-90) the ad after the m-part is dropped; by "अतो गुणे" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-97) pararūpa: tve. By "शे" (Pā. Sū. 1-1-13) śe is called pragṛhya, so tve is pragṛhya; with tve + iti, by "प्लुतप्रगृह्या अचि नित्यम्" (Pā. Sū. 7-4-25, as printed; for 6-1-125; the bhāṣya gives ६-१-१२५) there is no sandhi.

हूयते (hūyate) — hu dānādanayoḥ, juhotyādi; laṭ third singular in the passive; by "टित आत्मनेपदानाम्-" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-79) e; by "सार्वधातुके यक्" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-67) yak; by "अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोर्दीर्घः" (Pā. Sū. 7-4-15, as printed; for 7-4-25; the bhāṣya gives ७-४-२५) the vowel-final stem is lengthened before a y-initial suffix other than a kṛt or sārvadhātuka: hūyate. ॥६॥ A printed rule follows; Ṛk 7 begins on the same page.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

प्रियः । नः । अस्तु । विश्पतिः । होता । मन्द्रः । वरेण्यः । प्रियाः । सुऽअग्नयः । वयं ॥७॥

priyaḥ | naḥ | astu | viśpatiḥ | hotā | mandraḥ | vareṇyaḥ | priyāḥ | su-agnayaḥ | vayaṃ ‖7‖

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

विश्पतिर्विशां प्रजानां पालको होता होमनिष्पादको मंद्रो हृष्टो वरेण्यो वरणीयोऽग्निर्नोऽस्माकं प्रियोऽस्तु । वयमपि स्वग्नयः शोभनाग्नियुक्ताः संतस्तव प्रिया भूयास्मेति शेषः ॥ विश्पतिः ॥ पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते परादिश्छंदसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । वरेण्यः । वृञ एण्यः । उ. ३-९८ । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । स्वग्नयः । बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥

viśpatirviśāṃ prajānāṃ pālako hotā homaniṣpādako maṃdro hṛṣṭo vareṇyo varaṇīyo 'gnirno 'smākaṃ priyo 'stu | vayamapi svagnayaḥ śobhanāgniyuktāḥ saṃtastava priyā bhūyāsmeti śeṣaḥ ‖ viśpatiḥ ‖ patyāvaiśvarya iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvare prāpte parādiśchaṃdasi bahulamityuttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | vareṇyaḥ | vṛña eṇyaḥ | u. 3-98 | vṛṣāditvādādyudāttatvaṃ | svagnayaḥ | bahuvrīhau nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāṃtodāttatvaṃ ‖ Number zoom-read at 450 dpi: उ. ३-९८.

Gist: May Agni, protector of the people, the hotṛ, joyful and worthy to be chosen, be dear to us; and may we, having good fires, be dear to you.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ विश्पतिः (viśpatiḥ) — lord of the people | होता (hotā) — performer of the homa | मन्द्रः (mandraḥ) — content | वरेण्यः (vareṇyaḥ) — best (chosen by us): Agni | नः (naḥ) — to us | प्रियः (priyaḥ) — as one who does favour | अस्तु (astu) — may he be | वयं (vayaṃ) — we too | स्वग्नयः (svagnayaḥ) — endowed with auspicious fires | प्रियाः (priyāḥ) — may we become dear (to Agni).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ May Agni — protector of the people, performer of the homa, content and best — be one who does us favour. May we too, joined with auspicious fires, become dear to Agni.

॥ English Translation ॥

May Agni, the lord of men, the sacrificing priest (Hotri), the gracious, and the great (or the chosen) be kind (dear) to us ; may we, possessed of holy fires, be dear to Agni.

Page 365 — Rik 7: Special Topics, grammar

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

प्रियाः स्वग्नयो वयं (priyāḥ svagnayo vayaṃ) — in this ṛk Agni is praised with several epithets: viśpati, hotā, mandra, vareṇya. So the ṛṣi has referred to Agni, endowed with such qualities, in the plural. Or, since Agni is present in every house as lord of the house, the plural priyāḥ svagnayaḥ may have been used thinking of the fires (in our houses) that bring auspiciousness.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

विश्पतिः (viśpatiḥ) — viśāṃ patiḥ viśpatiḥ: the lord of the people. By "पत्यावैश्वर्ये" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-18), when pati in the sense of lordship is the final member, the first member keeps its accent; this being attained, by "परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलम्" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-199), bahula being mentioned, the final member's initial acute comes here: viśpatiḥ is medially acute.

वरेण्यः (vareṇyaḥ) — by "वृञ एण्यः" (Uṇ. Sū. 3-3[?]8, in the Kannada grammar's series: the middle digit is not settled; the bhāṣya gives उ. ३-९८), after vṛñ varaṇe the suffix eṇya; before it, by "सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-84) guṇa of the root's ṛ; since it replaces ṛ, by "उरण् रपरः" (Pā. Sū. 1-1-51) it is followed by r: vareṇyaḥ. Though the suffix accent would come, by "वृषादीनां च" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-203) it is initially acute; vareṇya is read in the vṛṣādi list.

स्वग्नयः (svagnayaḥ) — śobhanāḥ agnayaḥ yeṣāṃ te svagnayaḥ: those who have holy fires; a bahuvrīhi. By "नञ्सुभ्याम्" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172), in a bahuvrīhi the final member after nañ or su is end-acute; so here agni, after su, is end-acute. Before jas, by "जसि च" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-109) the stem takes guṇa; before the vowel, ay: svagnayaḥ. ॥७॥

Rik 8 pp. 366

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

स्व॒ग्नयो॒ हि वार्यं॑ दे॒वासो॑ दधि॒रे च॑ नः । स्व॒ग्नयो॑ मनामहे ॥८॥

svagnáyo hí vā́ryaṃ devā́so dadhiré ca naḥ | svagnáyo manāmahe ||8|| Saṃhitā accents as printed, read on 450-dpi line crops (v3a); Pada unaccented, though the print marks the Pada too. IAST mechanical from the marks.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

सुऽअग्नयः । हि । वार्यं । देवासः । दधिरे । च । नः । सुऽअग्नयः । मनामहे ॥८॥

su-agnayaḥ | hi | vāryaṃ | devāsaḥ | dadhire | ca | naḥ | su-agnayaḥ | manāmahe ‖8‖

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

स्वग्नयः शोभनाग्नियुक्ता देवासो दीप्यमाना ऋत्विजो नोऽस्मदीयं वार्यं वरणीयं हविर्हि यस्माद्दधिरे धृतवंतः तस्माद्वयं स्वग्नयः शोभनाग्नियुक्ताः संतो मनामहे । त्वां याचामहे ॥ वार्यं । वृञ् वरणे । वृङ् संभक्तौ । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् । ईडवंदेत्यादिनाद्युदात्तत्वं । दधिरे । इरेचश्चित्त्वादंतोदात्तत्वं । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । मनामहे । मन ज्ञाने । व्यत्ययेन शप् ॥

svagnayaḥ śobhanāgniyuktā devāso dīpyamānā ṛtvijo no 'smadīyaṃ vāryaṃ varaṇīyaṃ havirhi yasmāddadhire dhṛtavaṃtaḥ tasmādvayaṃ svagnayaḥ śobhanāgniyuktāḥ saṃto manāmahe | tvāṃ yācāmahe ‖ vāryaṃ | vṛñ varaṇe | vṛṅ saṃbhaktau | ṛhalorṇyat | īḍavaṃdetyādinādyudāttatvaṃ | dadhire | irecaścittvādaṃtodāttatvaṃ | hi ceti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | manāmahe | mana jñāne | vyatyayena śap ‖ No numbers in this bhāṣya.

Gist: Since the shining priests with good fires have taken up our choice oblation, we too, having good fires, entreat you.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ स्वग्नयः (svagnayaḥ) — endowed with excellent fires | देवासः (devāsaḥ) — and shining, the priests | नः (naḥ) — our | वार्यं (vāryaṃ) — excellent oblation | हि (hi) — for which reason | दधिरे (dadhire) — they have taken up (for that reason) | स्वग्नयः (svagnayaḥ) — joined with auspicious fires (we too) | मनामहे (manāmahe) — beseech (you).

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ The shining priests, joined with excellent fires, have taken up our excellent oblation to offer to you for our welfare. Therefore we too, having auspicious fires, pray to you for our welfare.

Page 367 — Rik 8: English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ English Translation ॥

As the brilliant priests possessed of holy fires have taken charge of our oblation, so we with holy fires pray to you.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

वार्यं (vāryaṃ) — varaṇīyaṃ, śreṣṭham: an excellent thing, the oblation.

देवासः (devāsaḥ) — dīpyamānā ṛtvijaḥ: shining priests.

मनामहे (manāmahe) — tvāṃ yācāmahe: we pray.

This ṛk may also be explained differently: svagnayaḥ prasannāgniyuktā devāso devā vāryaṃ varaṇīyaṃ dhanaṃ no 'smabhyaṃ dadhire ca dadati khalu | ataḥ svagnayaḥ prasannāgniyuktā vayaṃ tvāṃ manāmahe stumahe — that is, the gods joined with Agni give us the excellent wealth and the like that we need; therefore we, joined with Agni (worshipping Agni), praise you, Agni.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

वार्यम् (vāryam) — vṛñ varaṇe, svādi. By "ऋहलोर्ण्यत्" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-124), the root ending in ṛ, the suffix ṇyat; being ṇit, by "अचो ञ्णिति" (Pā. Sū. 7-2-115) vṛddhi of the root; followed by r: vārya; accusative singular. By "ईडवन्दवृशंसदुहां ण्यतः" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-214) these roots ending in ṇyat are initially acute; so the suffix accent is set aside and the initial acute comes.

दधिरे (dadhire) — ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, juhotyādi; in the liṭ third plural, by "लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेच्" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-81) irec for jha; doubling conditioned by liṭ; halādiśeṣa, shortening and jaśtva in the reduplicate; with dadhā + ire, the suffix being kit, by "आतो लोप इटि च" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-64) the ā is dropped: dadhire. Irec being cit, by "चितः" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163) the end-acute comes. Since hi precedes, the nighāta does not come.

मनामहे (manāmahe) — mana jñāne, divādi. By "दिवादिभ्यः श्यन्" (Pā. Sū. 3-1-69) śyan would come before the first plural; but by "व्यत्ययो बहुलम्"

Page 368 — Rik 8: grammar (end)

(Pā. Sū. 3-1-85) here the vikaraṇa śap comes. By "अतो दीर्घो यञि" (Pā. Sū. 7-3-101) before mahiṅ the a-final stem is lengthened. By "टित आत्मनेपदानां टेरे" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-79) the suffix takes e: manāmahe. Following a non-verb, by "तिङ्ङतिङः" (Pā. Sū. 8-1-28) the nighāta accent.

देवासः (devāsaḥ) — with deva + jas, by "आज्जसेरसुक्" (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50) the jas after an a-final stem takes the augment asuk: asas; lengthening of the like vowel, rutva and visarga: devāsaḥ. ॥८॥ A printed rule follows; Ṛk 9 begins on the same page.

॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अथा॑ न उ॒भये॑षा॒ममृ॑त॒ मर्त्या॑नां । मि॒थः स॑न्तु॒ प्रश॑स्तयः ॥९॥

áthā na ubháyeṣāmámṛta mártyānāṃ | mitháḥ santu práśastayaḥ ||9|| Saṃhitā accents as printed, read on 450-dpi line crops (v3a); Pada unaccented, though the print marks the Pada too. IAST mechanical from the marks.

॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥

अथ । नः । उभयेषां । अमृत । मर्त्यानां । मिथः । संतु । प्रऽशस्तयः ॥९॥

atha | naḥ | ubhayeṣāṃ | amṛta | martyānāṃ | mithaḥ | saṃtu | pra-śastayaḥ ‖9‖

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने अमृत मरणरहिताग्ने अथ कर्मानुष्ठानानंतरं मर्त्यानां मनुष्याणां नोऽस्माकमस्मत्स्वामिनस्तव चोभयेषां मिथः परस्परं प्रशस्तयः प्रशंसारूपा वाचः संतु । सम्यगनुष्ठितमिति यजमानविषया प्रशंसा । सम्यगनुगृहीतमित्यग्निविषया ॥ अथ । निपातस्य चेति संहितायां दीर्घः । अमृत । अपादादाविति पर्युदासात्षाष्ठिकमाद्युदात्तत्वं । मर्त्यानां । मृङ् प्राणत्यागे । असिहसीत्यादिना तन्प्रत्ययांतो मर्तशब्दः । तस्माद्भवे छंदसि । पा. ४-४-११० । इति यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । संतु । श्नसोरल्लोपः । प्रशस्तयः । तादौ चेति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

he agne amṛta maraṇarahitāgne atha karmānuṣṭhānānaṃtaraṃ martyānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ no 'smākamasmatsvāminastava cobhayeṣāṃ mithaḥ parasparaṃ praśastayaḥ praśaṃsārūpā vācaḥ saṃtu | samyaganuṣṭhitamiti yajamānaviṣayā praśaṃsā | samyaganugṛhītamityagniviṣayā ‖ atha | nipātasya ceti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaḥ | amṛta | apādādāviti paryudāsātṣāṣṭhikamādyudāttatvaṃ | martyānāṃ | mṛṅ prāṇatyāge | asihasītyādinā tanpratyayāṃto martaśabdaḥ | tasmādbhave chaṃdasi | pā. 4-4-110 | iti yat | yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvaṃ | saṃtu | śnasorallopaḥ | praśastayaḥ | tādau ceti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvaṃ ‖ Number read at 450 dpi: पा. ४-४-११०.

Gist: O immortal Agni, after the rite let there be words of praise between both of us, us mortals and you: "well performed" for the sacrificer, "well favoured" for Agni.

Page 369 — Rik 9: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अमृत (amṛta) — O Agni, free from death | अथ (atha) — after the completion of the sacrificial rite | प्रशस्तयः (praśastayaḥ) — (in the matter of the rite, ours and yours) words in the form of praise | मर्त्यानां (martyānāṃ) — being human | नः (naḥ) — to us | उभयेषां (ubhayeṣāṃ) — (we and you) to both sides | मिथः (mithaḥ) — mutually (and for the happiness of both) | संतु (saṃtu) — may they be fulfilled.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni, free from death, after the sacrificial rite, may the words of praise, ours and yours, that ought to pass concerning the rite, praising the fruitfulness of the sacrifice, bring happiness to both sides, to us who are human and to you.

॥ English Translation ॥

And now, Agni, may there be an interchange of praises between you, the immortal, and us the mortals.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

उभयेषां (ubhayeṣāṃ) — to both, to you who are Agni and to us who are men.

अमृत (amṛta) — free from death.

प्रशस्तयः (praśastayaḥ) — praśaṃsārūpā vācaḥ | samyag anuṣṭhitam iti yajamānaviṣayā praśaṃsā | samyag anugṛhītam ity agniviṣayā: conversation in the form of mutual praise; Agni says, "you have carried out the sacrifice well", and the people, the sacrificers, say, "we have been favoured by you": they greet each other in this way.

॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥

अथ (atha) — by "चादयोऽसत्त्वे" (Pā. Sū. 1-4-57) it is called nipāta; by "निपातस्य च" (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136) it is lengthened in the Saṃhitā: athā.

अमृत (amṛta) — mṛṅ prāṇatyāge; kta in the abstract sense; na vidyate mṛtaṃ yasya saḥ amṛtaḥ; in the vocative amṛta. Standing at the beginning of a pāda, the exclusion "अपादादौ" bars the nighāta of the eighth book; by "आमन्त्रितस्य च" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-198) it is initially acute.

Page 370 — Rik 9: grammar (end)

मर्त्यानाम् (martyānām) — mṛṅ prāṇatyāge; by "असिहसिमृग्रि-" (Uṇ. Sū. 3-366, in the Kannada grammar's series) the suffix tan; guṇa of the root before tan, followed by r: marta. Then by "भवे छन्दसि" (Pā. Sū. 4-4-110) yat in the sense of "being there"; before a y by "यस्येति च" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-148) the preceding a is dropped: martya; genitive plural martyānām. By "यतोऽनावः" (Pā. Sū. 6-1-213), as it is not the word nau and ends in yat, it is initially acute.

संतु (saṃtu) — asa bhuvi, adādi; in the loṭ third plural the anta substitute for jha; by "एरुः" (Pā. Sū. 3-4-86) u. With as + antu, by "अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः" (Pā. Sū. 2-4-72) the vikaraṇa takes luk; by "श्नसोरल्लोपः" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-111), before a vowel-initial ṅit suffix, the a of as is dropped: santu.

प्रशस्तयः (praśastayaḥ) — śaṃsu stutau; before ktin, by "अनिदितां हल-" (Pā. Sū. 6-4-24) the penultimate n is dropped: praśasti; nominative plural. By "तादौ च निति कृत्यतौ" (Pā. Sū. 6-2-50), before a t-initial nit kṛt suffix other than tu, the gati keeps its own accent; since ktin follows, the gati's udātta is not set aside: praśastayaḥ is initially acute. ॥९॥ A printed rule follows; Ṛk 10 begins on the same page.

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वे॑भिरग्ने अ॒ग्निभि॑रि॒मं य॒ज्ञमि॒दं वचः॑ । चनो॑ धाः सहसो यहो ॥ १० ॥

víśvebhir agne agníbhir imáṃ yajñám idáṃ vácaḥ | cáno dhāḥ sahaso yaho || 10 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

विश्वेभिः । अग्ने । अग्निऽभिः । इमम् । यज्ञम् । इदम् । वचः ॥ चनः । धाः । सहसः । यहो इति ॥ १० ॥

viśvebhiḥ | agne | agni-bhiḥ | imam | yajñam | idam | vacaḥ || canaḥ | dhāḥ | sahasaḥ | yaho iti || 10 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

सहसो बलस्य यहो पुत्र हे देवतारूपाग्ने विश्वेभिरग्निभिः सर्वैराहवनीयादिभिर्युक्तस्त्वमिममस्मदीयं यज्ञमिदमस्मदीयं वचः स्तोत्रं च सेवमानश्च नोऽन्नं धाः । अस्मभ्यं धेहि ॥ विश्वेभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसादेशाभावः । चनः । चायृ पूजानिशामनयोः । चायेरन्ने ह्रस्वश्च । उ. ४-१९९ । इत्यसुन् । तत्संनियोगेन नुडागमश्च । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । धाः । लुङि गातिस्था० । पा. २-४-७७ । इति सिचो लुक् । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः । सहसो यहो इति सुबामन्त्रित इति पराङ्गवद्भावादामन्त्रितस्य च इति षष्ठ्यामन्त्रितसमुदायो निहन्यते ॥

sahaso balasya yaho putra he devatārūpāgne viśvebhir agnibhiḥ sarvair āhavanīyādibhir yuktas tvam imam asmadīyaṃ yajñam idam asmadīyaṃ vacaḥ stotraṃ ca sevamānaś ca no 'nnaṃ dhāḥ | asmabhyaṃ dhehi || viśvebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisādeśābhāvaḥ | canaḥ | cāyṛ pūjāniśāmanayoḥ | cāyer anne hrasvaś ca | u. 4-199 | ity asun | tatsaṃniyogena nuḍāgamaś ca | nittvād ādyudāttatvam | dhāḥ | luṅi gātisthā… | pā. 2-4-77 | iti sico luk | bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pīty aḍabhāvaḥ | sahaso yaho iti subāmantrita iti parāṅgavadbhāvād āmantritasya ceti ṣaṣṭhyāmantritasamudāyo nihanyate ||

Translation: "O yaho — son — of sahas, of strength, Agni, god! Joined with all (viśvebhiḥ) your fires — the Āhavanīya and the rest — receiving this sacrifice of ours and this our speech, our hymn, give (dhāḥ) us canaḥ — food: give to us. Viśvebhiḥ: ais for bhis does not occur, by bahulaṃ chandasi. Canaḥ: cāyṛ pūjāniśāmanayoḥ; asun by Uṇ. 4-199 with shortening of the vowel in the sense of 'food'; nuṭ inserted; first-syllable acute from nit. Dhāḥ: in the luṅ, loss of sic by P. 2-4-77; aṭ absent. Sahaso yaho: the vocative group is [treated as] one, and is lowered as a whole." Bhāṣya ends ॥ २१ ॥ = Varga 21. Grammar page 373, noted briefly: the words treated are viśvebhiḥ [viśva + bhis: ais would be substituted by P. 7-1-9 ato bhisa ais, but not in the Veda (P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi); e for a by P. 7-3-103 bahuvacane jhaly et; ru-visarga], canaḥ [cāyṛ pūjāniśāmanayoḥ, bhvādi; in the sense of 'food' asun by cāyer anne hrasvaś ca (U. sū. 4-639 as printed, middle digit read as 3; bhāṣya: 4-199); the shortening of cā → ca, the augment nuṭ; cayas… with y lost by P. 6-1-66 lopo vyor vali, hence canas; the accusative singular of the neuter am lost by P. 7-1-23 svamor napuṃsakāt, and ru-visarga; first-syllable acute by nit P. 6-1-197], dhāḥ [ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; the Vedic luṅ in the sense of the imperative by P. 3-4-6; 2nd singular sip → s; cli → sic, which is lost by P. 2-4-77 gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu because dhā has the name ghu; aṭ absent by P. 6-4-75 bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi; the s of sip → ru-visarga; the verb is lowered since it follows a word that is not a finite verb (no sūtra number printed)] and sahaso yaho [sahas 'strength' → sahasaḥ genitive; yaho is a vocative, so it has the name āmantrita; P. 2-1-2 subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare makes the preceding sahasaḥ a part of it; P. 8-1-19 āmantritasya ca lowers the whole group; the group sahaso yaho is wholly anudātta]; numerals checked against the print, w3. The print closes: "The 26th sūkta is ended."

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ सहसः (sahasaḥ) — of strength | यहो (yaho) — O son | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | विश्वेभिः अग्निभिः (viśvebhiḥ agnibhiḥ) — with all your fires, the Āhavanīya and the rest | इमं यज्ञम् (imaṃ yajñam) — this our sacrifice | इदं वचः (idaṃ vacaḥ) — this our hymn | (सेवमानः) ((sevamānaḥ)) — accepting | चनः (canaḥ) — food | धाः (dhāḥ) — give [to us].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni, son of strength! Joined with all your fires — the Āhavanīya and the rest — accept this our sacrifice and this our praise, and give us food, our sustenance.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

Agni, Son of Strength, accept this Sacrifice and this our praise with the three different Sacrificial fires, and grant us abundant food.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ विश्वेभिः अग्निभिः — with many fires: i.e. with those fires established in the sacrifice — the Āhavanīya, Gārhapatya and Dakṣiṇāgni — or with the many fires in the various places or houses. चनः — food; cana is a name for food, according to Yāska (Ni. 6-16). सहसः — of strength: among the twenty-eight names of strength beginning ojaḥ, pājaḥ the word sahas is read, so sahasaḥ means 'of strength' (Ni. 3-9). यहो — son: among the fifteen names for 'offspring', beginning with tukk, tokam, the word yahuḥ is read, so yaho is 'O son' (no reference printed). In the Ṛgveda Agni, and on some occasions Indra too, is called sahasas putra — the son of strength or of power — as is specially seen. Some examples (glosses editorial and tentative):

अग्निं होतारं मन्ये दास्वन्तं वसुं सूनुं सहसो जातवेदसं विप्रं न जातवेदसम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१२७-१) agniṃ hotāraṃ manye dāsvantaṃ vasuṃ sūnuṃ sahaso jātavedasaṃ vipraṃ na jātavedasam || — "I hold Agni as the hotṛ, the giver, the good one, the son of strength, Jātavedas, like a sage."

द्वन्नः सर्पिरासुतिः प्रत्नो होता वरेण्यः । सहसस्पुत्रो अद्भुतः ॥ (ऋ. सं. २-७-६) dvannaḥ sarpir āsutiḥ pratno hotā vareṇyaḥ | sahasas putro adbhutaḥ || — "Wood-eater [?], whose drink is ghee, the ancient hotṛ, the chosen, the wonderful son of strength." (The print has broken type between द्व and न्नः.)

अग्निं सूनुं सनश्रुतं सहसो जातवेदसम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-११-४) agniṃ sūnuṃ sanaśrutaṃ sahaso jātavedasam || — "Agni, the son of strength, famed of old, Jātavedas."

विद्युद्रथः सहसस्पुत्रो अग्निः शोचिष्केशः पृथिव्यां पाजो अश्रेत् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-१४-१) vidyudrathaḥ sahasas putro agniḥ śociṣkeśaḥ pṛthivyāṃ pājo aśret || — "Agni, son of strength, chariot of lightning, flame-haired, has taken his might on the earth."

अग्ने द्युम्नेन जागृवे सहसः सूनवाहुत ॥ (ऋ. सं. ३-२४-३) agne dyumnena jāgṛve sahasaḥ sūnav āhuta || — "O Agni, wakeful with splendour, son of strength, oblation-receiver."

अस्माकमग्ने अध्वरं जुषस्व सहसः सूनो त्रिषधस्थ हव्यम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ५-४-८) asmākam agne adhvaraṃ juṣasva sahasaḥ sūno triṣadhastha havyam || — "O Agni, take our sacrifice, son of strength, seated in the three places, the oblation."

हुवे वः सूनुं सहसो युवानमद्रोघवाचं मतिभिर्यविष्ठम् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ६-५-१) huve vaḥ sūnuṃ sahaso yuvānam adroghavācaṃ matibhir yaviṣṭham || — "I call your son of strength, the young one, of guileless speech, the most youthful, with hymns."

In these and many other riks the words sahasaḥ sūnuḥ and sahasas putraḥ are used of Agni.

॥ Close of Sūkta 26 ॥ p. 373, large print: "The 26th sūkta is ended." An ornament follows. The varga number is not given in the colophon.

॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೇಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 27 — "aśvaṃ na tvā vāravantam" ("The Twenty-seventh Sūkta"; fourth sūkta of the Sixth Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 374–407. The introductory note, Kannada rendering and heading block are on p. 374; Rik 1 begins at the foot of p. 374.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note; printed p. 374) checked against the print, w3

अश्वं न त्वेति त्रयोदशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तम् । पूर्ववदृष्यादयः । त्रयोदश्या नमो महद्भ्य इत्यस्याः त्रिष्टुप् छन्दः । विश्वे देवा देवता । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् — अश्वं सप्तोना गायत्रेऽन्त्या दैवी त्रिष्टुबिति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरुत्तमावर्जितस्य सूक्तस्य विनियोग उक्तः ॥

aśvaṃ na tveti trayodaśarcaṃ caturthaṃ sūktam | pūrvavad ṛṣyādayaḥ | trayodaśyā namo mahadbhya ity asyāḥ triṣṭup chandaḥ | viśve devā devatā | tathā cānukrāntam — aśvaṃ saptonā gāyatre 'ntyā daivī triṣṭubiti || prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayor uttamāvarjitasya sūktasya viniyoga uktaḥ ||

Translation: "The sūkta aśvaṃ na tvā has thirteen riks and is the fourth [of this anuvāka]. The ṛṣi and the rest are as before. The thirteenth rik, namo mahadbhyaḥ, is in Triṣṭubh; its deity is the Viśvedevas. So the Anukramaṇikā says: 'aśvam — seven less [than twenty, i.e. thirteen riks]; Gāyatrī; the last, daivī [of the Viśvedevas], Triṣṭubh' [the bracketed explanation editorial and tentative; the quotation read from the print]. The application of the sūkta [apart from the last rik] has been stated for the Prātaranuvāka and the Aśvina-śastra."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ Aśvaṃ na tvā is the fourth sūkta of the sixth anuvāka and has thirteen riks. The ṛṣi and the rest are as before (Śunaḥśepa; Gāyatrī). The thirteenth rik, namo mahadbhyaḥ, is in the Triṣṭubh metre, and its deity is the Viśvedevas. The Anukramaṇikā says: 'aśvaṃ saptonā gāyatre 'ntyā daivī triṣṭubiti' [as printed]. Of this sūkta, leaving out one rik at the end, the remaining twelve riks are to be used, at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras, as mantras of the Aśvina-śastra.

॥ Heading block of the sūkta (p. 374) ॥

मण्डल १ — अनुवाक ६ — सूक्त २७ । अष्टक १ — अध्याय २ — वर्ग २२, २३, २४ । ऋक्संख्या १३ । ऋषिः — शुनःशेप आजीगर्तिः । देवता — १–१२ अग्निः । १३ विश्वे देवाः । छन्दः — १–१२ गायत्री । १३ त्रिष्टुप् ।

Maṇḍala 1 — Anuvāka 6 — Sūkta 27. Aṣṭaka 1 — Adhyāya 2 — Varga 22, 23, 24. Riks: 13. Ṛṣi: Śunaḥśepa Ājīgarti. Devatā: 1–12 Agni; 13 the Viśvedevas. Metre: 1–12 Gāyatrī; 13 Triṣṭubh. Varga numerals read from the print, w3.

Rik 1 pp. 374–378

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

अश्वं॒ न त्वा॒ वार॑वन्तं व॒न्दध्या॑ अ॒ग्निं नमो॑भिः । स॒म्राज॑न्तमध्व॒राणां॑ ॥ १ ॥

áśvaṃ ná tvā vā́ravantaṃ vandádhyā agníṃ námobhiḥ | samrā́jantam adhvarā́ṇāṃ || 1 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

अश्वम् । न । त्वा । वारऽवन्तम् । वन्दध्यै । अग्निम् । नमःऽभिः ॥ सम्ऽराजन्तम् । अध्वराणाम् ॥ १ ॥

aśvam | na | tvā | vāra-vantam | vandadhyai | agnim | namaḥ-bhiḥ || sam-rājantam | adhvarāṇām || 1 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अध्वराणां यज्ञानां सम्राजन्तं सम्राट्स्वरूपं स्वामिनमग्निं त्वां नमोभिः स्तुतिभिर्वन्दध्यै वन्दितुं प्रवृत्ताः स्म इति शेषः । अत्र दृष्टान्तः । वारवन्तं वालयुक्तमश्वं न अश्वमिव । अश्वो यथा वालैर्बाधकान्मशकमक्षिकादीन्परिहरति तथा त्वमपि ज्वालाभिरस्मद्विरोधिनः परिहरसीत्यर्थः ॥ वारवन्तम् । मतुपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । घञन्तो ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तो वारशब्दः । कर्षात्वत इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं व्यत्ययेन न प्रवर्तते । वन्दध्यै । वदि अभिवादनस्तुत्योः । इदितो नुम् धातोरिति नुम् । तुमर्थे सेसेनित्यध्यैप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । सम्राजन्तम् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेण स एव । अध्वराणाम् । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥

adhvarāṇāṃ yajñānāṃ samrājantaṃ samrāṭsvarūpaṃ svāminam agniṃ tvāṃ namobhiḥ stutibhir vandadhyai vanditum pravṛttāḥ sma iti śeṣaḥ | atra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vāravantaṃ vālayuktam aśvaṃ na aśvam iva | aśvo yathā vālair bādhakān maśakamakṣikādīn pariharati tathā tvam api jvālābhir asmadvirodhinaḥ pariharasīty arthaḥ || vāravantam | matupaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | ghañanto ñittvād ādyudātto vāraśabdaḥ | karṣātvata ity antodāttatvaṃ vyatyayena na pravartate | vandadhyai | vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ | idito num dhātor iti num | tumarthe sesen ity adhyaipratyayaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | samrājantam | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | śatuś ca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvaraḥ śiṣyate | samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvareṇa sa eva | adhvarāṇām | nañsubhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatvam ||

Translation: "We have set out to praise — vandadhyai — with salutations (namobhiḥ), with hymns, you, Agni, samrājantam — shining as an emperor — the lord of the adhvaras, the sacrifices; [as one does] a horse (aśvaṃ na) vāravantam — having a tail (vāla). An illustration: as a horse with its tail drives off the troublesome gnats, flies and the like, so you drive off those hostile to us with your flames. Vāravantam: the accent of matup is lowered since it is pit; the word vāra ending in ghañ, being ñit, has the first syllable acute; the end-acute by P. 6-1-159 [karṣātvato ghañaḥ] does not apply, by vyatyaya. Vandadhyai: vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ; num by P. 7-1-58; the infinitive adhyai by P. 3-4-9; the accent of the suffix. Samrājantam: the accent of śap is lowered, the root's accent remains. Adhvarāṇām: end-acute by P. 6-2-172 [nañsubhyām]." Grammar pages 376–377, noted briefly: the words treated are vāravantam [vārayati daṃśakān — 'what keeps off insects' = a tail; vṛ + ac by P. 3-1-134 nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ, or ghañ, giving vāra — vāla by the ra/la interchange (kapilakādi); vāra + matup by P. 5-2-94; m → v by P. 8-2-9 mādupadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ; accusative singular — the print explains that Śunaḥśepa's word is read as vālavantam in the Kannada gloss], vandadhyai [vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ; idito num dhātoḥ P. 7-1-58; adhyai for the infinitive by P. 3-4-9 tumarthe se-sen-ase-asen-kase-kasen-adhyai-adhyain-kadhyai-kadhyain-śadhyai-śadhyain-tavai-tavenkenkenyatvanaḥ; the suffix's accent: adhyai has the middle acute], samrājantam [sam + rājṛ dīptau, ubhayapadī, bhvādi; śatṛ in the sense of laṭ; śap, and a + a by P. 6-1-97 ato guṇe; num in the accusative singular (no sūtra number printed); the accent: śap is pit so anudātta; śatṛ is lowered by P. 6-1-186; the root's accent remains; the compound with sam as gati keeps the kṛt-accent, P. 6-2-139] and adhvarāṇām [na vidyate dhvaro hiṃsā yasmin so 'dhvaraḥ; nañ-bahuvrīhi; the end-acute by P. 6-2-172; the genitive plural lengthens its vowel; n → ṇ: adhvarāṇām]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अध्वराणाम् (adhvarāṇām) — of the sacrifices | सम्राजन्तम् (samrājantam) — shining as an emperor | अग्निम् (agnim) — to Agni | त्वा (tvā) — to you | नमोभिः (namobhiḥ) — with salutations [of praise] | वन्दध्यै (vandadhyai) — to praise | वारवन्तम् (vāravantam) — with a tail | अश्वम् न (aśvam na) — like a horse [we praise you, who drive away enemies in all directions].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ You are the emperor of all sacrifices. As a horse, with its tail, drives away the gnats and flies in all directions, you drive away enemies in all directions with your flames; such Agni we praise with hymns.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

We have come to worship Agni, the sovereign lord of sacrifices with praises; that Agni who scatters enemies like a horse which brushes off flies with his tail.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ In this rik Agni is described only as a horse with its tail. There is no obvious similarity between a horse with its tail and Agni; so the commentator supplies some words: 'as a horse with its tail drives off gnats and flies without trouble, so Agni drives off enemies.' अश्वं न — like a horse; the particle na here does not give a negation but the sense of comparison, 'as'; this sense of na exists in the Veda only, not in later Sanskrit. वारवन्तम् — in this word r is used in place of l by vyatyaya; so it means vālavantam, 'having a tail'. नमोभिः — with salutations, with praises. सम्राजन्तम् अध्वराणाम् — like an emperor in sacrifices — Agni who shines with great glory, as the verb rāj dīptau implies. There is no sacrifice without Agni; therefore he is chief, the one who shines as lord and emperor.

Rik 2 pp. 377–380

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

स घा॑ नः सू॒नुः शव॑सा पृ॒थुप्र॑गामा सु॒शेवः॑ । मी॒ढ्वाँ अ॒स्माकं॑ बभूयात् ॥ २ ॥

sá ghā naḥ sūnúḥ śávasā pṛthúpragāmā suśévaḥ | mīḍhvā́m̐ asmā́kaṃ babhūyāt || 2 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

सः । घ । नः । सूनुः । शवसा । पृथुऽप्रगामा । सुऽशेवः ॥ मीढ्वान् । अस्माकम् । बभूयात् ॥ २ ॥

saḥ | gha | naḥ | sūnuḥ | śavasā | pṛthu-pragāmā | su-śevaḥ || mīḍhvān | asmākam | babhūyāt || 2 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

स घ स एवाग्निर्नोऽस्माकं सुशेवः सुसुखो भवत्विति शेषः । कीदृशः । शवसा बलस्य सूनुः पुत्रः । पृथुप्रगामा पृथुप्रगमनः । किंचास्माकं मीढ्वान्कामानां वर्षिता बभूयात् । भवतु ॥ घा नः । ऋचि तुनुघमक्षुतङ्कुत्रोरुष्याणाम् । पा. ६-३-१३३ । इति दीर्घः । शवसा । सुपां सुपो भवन्तीति ङसष्टादेशः । पृथुप्रगामा । प्रकर्षेण गमनं प्रगामः । हलश्चेति घञ् । पृथुः प्रगामो यस्यासौ पृथुप्रगामा । सुपां सुलुगिति पूर्वसवर्ण आकारः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सुशेवः । इण्शीभ्यां वन् । उ. १-१५२ । इति शेवशब्दो वन्प्रत्ययान्त आद्युदात्तः । ततो बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । मीढ्वान् । मिह सेचन इत्यस्मात् क्वसुप्रत्ययान्तो दाश्वान् साह्वान् मीढ्वांश्चेति निपातितः । बभूयात् । भवतेश्छान्दसस्य लिटस्तिङां तिङो भवन्ति । म. ७-१-३९ । इति लिङादेशः । यासुट्स्थानिवद्भावादार्धधातुकत्वाच्छबभावः । द्विर्वचने भवतेरः । पा. ७-४-७३ । इत्यत्वम् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥

sa gha sa evāgnir no 'smākaṃ suśevaḥ susukho bhavatv iti śeṣaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ | śavasā balasya sūnuḥ putraḥ | pṛthupragāmā pṛthupragamanaḥ | kiṃcāsmākaṃ mīḍhvān kāmānāṃ varṣitā babhūyāt | bhavatu || ghā naḥ | ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām | pā. 6-3-133 | iti dīrghaḥ | śavasā | supāṃ supo bhavantīti ṅasaṣṭādeśaḥ | pṛthupragāmā | prakarṣeṇa gamanaṃ pragāmaḥ | halaś ceti ghañ | pṛthuḥ pragāmo yasyāsau pṛthupragāmā | supāṃ suluk iti pūrvasavarṇa ākāraḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | suśevaḥ | iṇśībhyāṃ van | u. 1-152 | iti śevaśabdo vanpratyayānta ādyudāttaḥ | tato bahuvrīhau nañsubhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatve prāpte ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasīty uttarapadādyudāttatvam | mīḍhvān | miha secana ity asmāt kvasupratyayānto dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ceti nipātitaḥ | babhūyāt | bhavateś chāndasasya liṭas tiṅāṃ tiṅo bhavanti | ma. 7-1-39 | iti liṅādeśaḥ | yāsuṭsthānivadbhāvād ārdhadhātukatvāc chababhāvaḥ | dvirvacane bhavater aḥ | pā. 7-4-73 | ity atvam | tiṅ atiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "May that very Agni be suśevaḥ — very gracious — to us: this is to be supplied. What kind? Śavasā sūnuḥ — son of strength; pṛthupragāmā — of wide-ranging going. And may he be mīḍhvān — the rainer of desires, the one who showers down wishes — for us (babhūyāt). Ghā naḥ: lengthening by P. 6-3-133 [ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām]. Śavasā: the genitive ṅas replaced by ṭā by supāṃ supo bhavanti. Pṛthupragāmā: 'a going forward is pragāma'; ghañ by P. 3-3-… [halaś ca]; 'he of whom the going is wide'; the ā by the lengthening of the preceding by supāṃ suluk; the first member's accent in the bahuvrīhi. Suśevaḥ: śeva with van (Uṇ. 1-152) has the first syllable acute; then in the bahuvrīhi the second member's initial acute by P. 6-2-119 [ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi], overriding the end-acute of nañsubhyām. Mīḍhvān: from miha secane with kvasu, formed by nipātana [dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca]. Babhūyāt: for the Vedic liṭ of bhū, liṅ is substituted by tiṅāṃ tiṅo bhavanti (M. 7-1-39); since yāsuṭ counts as the original and is ārdhadhātuka, there is no śap; in the reduplication a by P. 7-4-73; lowered by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ." Grammar pages 379–380, noted briefly: the words treated are ghā naḥ [gha is an Upadeśa-particle; its vowel is lengthened in the Saṃhitā in a rik by P. 6-3-133 ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām], śavasā [śavas 'strength', an s-stem; for the genitive singular ending, ṭā by the dictum supāṃ supo bhavanti, established by vyatyayo bahulam P. 3-1-85], pṛthupragāmā [gam + ghañ with pra: halaś ca P. 3-3-121; upadhāvṛddhi P. 7-2-116 ata upadhāyāḥ; pṛthuḥ pragāmo yasya: a bahuvrīhi; nominative singular su → ā by supāṃ suluk; the accent of the first member, P. 6-2-1], suśevaḥ [śīṅ svapne + van by U. sū. 1-150 iṇśībhyāṃ van (bhāṣya: 1-152); guṇa; śeva; the su-compound: nañsubhyām P. 6-2-172 would give the end-acute, but P. 6-2-119 ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi gives the acute to the first syllable of a disyllabic second member, e.g. śeva], mīḍhvān [miha secane; kvasu by nipātana P. 6-1-12 dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca; ha → ḍha by P. 8-2-31; the dhva with ṣṭutva; the nominative singular: num, lengthening, su lost, and t/s lost; in the Saṃhitā mīḍhvām̐ by P. 8-3-1 ato 'ṭi nityam], and babhūyāt [bhū sattāyām,* bhvādi; liṭ in the sense of loṭ by P. 3-4-6 chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ; liṅ substituted for it by tiṅāṃ tiṅo bhavanti (Pā. Ma. 7-1-39); i lost by P. 3-4-100 itaś ca; yāsuṭ by P. 3-4-103; being sthānivat it is ārdhadhātuka, so no śap; doubling; a for the reduplicate by bhavater aḥ P. 7-4-73; jaśtva: babhūyāt; the verb is lowered by P. 8-1-28 tiṅṅatiṅaḥ because it follows asmākam*, a word that is not a finite verb]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ शवसा (śavasā) — of strength | सूनुः (sūnuḥ) — son | पृथुप्रगामा (pṛthupragāmā) — having swift movement | सः घ (saḥ gha) — that very Agni | नः (naḥ) — to us | सुशेवः (suśevaḥ) — gracious [of friendly mind] | अस्माकम् (asmākam) — our | मीढ्वान् (mīḍhvān) — the showerer of desired things | बभूयात् (babhūyāt) — may he be.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ May that Agni, the son of strength, of swift movement, be gracious to us and shower down our wishes.

॥ English Translation ॥

May he (Agni), the son of strength who moves swiftly, give comfort to us and shower down blessings upon us.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ घ — a particle meaning 'indeed'; its vowel is lengthened in the Saṃhitā for the sake of the metre. सूनुः शवसा — son of strength, or of power. We have explained this word before (see p. 372). पृथुप्रगामा — prakarṣeṇa gamanaṃ pragāmaḥ; pṛthuḥ pragāmo yasyāsau: one of great motion; that is, who by his rays pervades all round. सुशेवः — sumukhaḥ: kind; may he be favourable and gracious to us. मीढ्वान् — miha secane; kāmānāṃ varṣayitā: the showerer of desires, i.e. the giver.

Rik 3 pp. 380–383

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

स नो॑ दू॒राच्चा॒साच्च॒ नि मर्त्या॑दघा॒योः । पा॒हि सद॒मिद्वि॒श्वायुः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

sá no dūrā́c cāsā́c ca ní mártyād aghāyóḥ | pāhí sádam íd viśvā́yuḥ || 3 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

सः । नः । दूरात् । च । आसात् । च । नि । मर्त्यात् । अघऽयोः ॥ पाहि । सदम् । इत् । विश्वऽआयुः ॥ ३ ॥

saḥ | naḥ | dūrāt | ca | āsāt | ca | ni | martyāt | agha-yoḥ || pāhi | sadam | it | viśva-āyuḥ || 3 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने विश्वायुर्व्याप्तगमनः स त्वं दूराच्च दूरेऽपि आसाच्चासन्नदेशेऽपि अघायोरघं पापमनिष्टं कर्तुमिच्छतो मर्त्यान्मनुष्याद्वैरिणो नोऽस्मान्सदमित् सर्वदैव नि पाहि । नितरां पालय ॥ अघायोः । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । अश्वाघस्यात् । पा. ७-४-३७ । इत्यात्वम् । पाहि । पादादित्वादनिघातः । विश्वायुः । इण् गतावित्यस्माद्भावे एतेर्णिच्च । उ. २-११९ । इत्युसिः । विश्वमयनं गगनं [as printed] यस्येति बहुव्रीहिः । बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायामिति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥

he agne viśvāyur vyāptagamanaḥ sa tvaṃ dūrāc ca dūre 'pi āsāc cāsannadeśe 'py aghāyor aghaṃ pāpam aniṣṭaṃ kartum icchato martyān manuṣyād vairiṇo no 'smān sadam it sarvadaiva ni pāhi | nitarāṃ pālaya || aghāyoḥ | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | aśvāghasyāt | pā. 7-4-37 | ity ātvam | pāhi | pādāditvād anighātaḥ | viśvāyuḥ | iṇ gatāv ity asmād bhāve eter ṇic ca | u. 2-119 | ity usiḥ | viśvam ayanaṃ gaganaṃ [as printed] yasyeti bahuvrīhiḥ | bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām iti pūrvapadāntodāttatvam ||

Translation: "O Agni, viśvāyuḥ — of all-pervading motion! You, from far (dūrāt) and from near (āsāt), protect (ni pāhi) always (sadam it) naḥ — us — from martyāt — the mortal, the enemy — aghāyoḥ — who wishes to do harm, evil, ill: protect completely. Aghāyoḥ: kyac in the sense 'wishing for oneself'; ā by P. 7-4-37 [aśvāghasyāt]. Pāhi: no lowering as it stands at the beginning of the pāda. Viśvāyuḥ: from iṇ gatau with usi in the sense of the action, by eter ṇic ca (Uṇ. 2-119); 'one whose going (ayana) is everywhere' [the print has gaganam for gamanam here]; a bahuvrīhi; the first member has the end-acute by P. 6-2-106." Grammar pages 381–382, noted briefly: the words treated are aghāyoḥ [agham ātmana icchati — 'wishes evil to oneself' [as printed]; kyac by P. 3-1-8 supa ātmanaḥ kyac; u after kyac in the Veda by P. 3-2-170 kyācchandasi; the a of kyac is lost by P. 6-4-48; aśvāghasyāt P. 7-4-37 makes agha end in ā before kyac in the Veda, so aghāyu; ablative singular aghāyoḥ], pāhi [pā rakṣaṇe, adādi; loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi; hi is not lost since it does not follow a short a; the verb is not lowered since it is at the head of the pāda (the restriction apādādau; no number printed)] and viśvāyuḥ [iṇ gatau, adādi + usi in the sense of the action by U. sū. 2-275 eter ṇic ca (bhāṣya: 2-119); it is ṇit, so vṛddhi of the i by P. 7-2-115 aco ñṇiti; āy by P. 6-1-78 eco 'yavāyāvaḥ: āyus; viśvam āyur (ayanaṃ) gamanaṃ yasya, a bahuvrīhi; the accent of the first member's end by P. 6-2-106 bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām where the name is concerned; 'the acute that would be on the first syllable of the first member is displaced by an end-acute'; viśvāyuḥ has the middle acute]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (अग्ने) ((agne)) — O Agni | विश्वायुः (viśvāyuḥ) — of all-pervading movement | सः (saḥ) — such you | दूरात् च (dūrāt ca) — from afar | आसात् च (āsāt ca) — and from near | अघायोः (aghāyoḥ) — wishing us harm | मर्त्यात् (martyāt) — from the mortal [enemy] | नः (naḥ) — us | सदम् इत् (sadam it) — always | नि पाहि (ni pāhi) — protect well.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni! You pervade all places. Therefore protect us always against enemies who wish us harm, whether they are far away or close at hand.

॥ English Translation ॥

Do you, therefore Agni who is omnipresent, ever protect us from the wicked mortal seeking to do us injury whether near or afar.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ दूरात् च आसात् च — from afar or from near. अघायोः — agha means sin, ill, harm; a man who wishes to do it is aghāyu: from such a man, who wishes us harm, [protect us]. सदम् इत् — sarvadaiva: always. विश्वायुः — viśvam ayanaṃ gamanaṃ yasya: one who has movement or travel in all places; all-pervading.

Rik 4 pp. 382–384

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

इ॒ममू॒ षु त्वम॒स्माकं॑ स॒निं गा॑य॒त्रं नव्यां॑सं । अग्ने॑ दे॒वेषु॒ प्र वो॑चः ॥ ४ ॥

imám ū ṣú tvám asmā́kaṃ saníṃ gāyatráṃ návyāṃsaṃ | ágne devéṣu prá vocaḥ || 4 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); the print has इममू (short a); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

इमम् । ऊं इति । सु । त्वम् । अस्माकम् । सनिम् । गायत्रम् । नव्यांसम् ॥ अग्ने । देवेषु । प्र । वोचः ॥ ४ ॥

imam | ūṃ iti | su | tvam | asmākam | sanim | gāyatram | navyāṃsam || agne | deveṣu | pra | vocaḥ || 4 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने त्वमस्माकमस्मत्संबन्धिनमिममू षु पुरोदेशेऽनुष्ठीयमानमपि सनिं हविर्दानं नव्यांसं नवतरं गायत्रं स्तुतिरूपं वचोऽपि देवेषु देवानामग्रे प्र वोचः । प्रब्रूहि ॥ ऊ षु । निपातस्य चेति संहितायां दीर्घत्वम् । सुञः इति षत्वम् । नव्यांसम् । नवशब्दादीयसुनीकारलोपश्छान्दसः । ईयसुनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । वोचः । छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति लोडर्थे प्रार्थनायां लुङ्यस्यतिवक्तीति च्लेरङादेशः । पा. ३-१-५२ । वच उम् । पा. ७-४-२० ॥

he agne tvam asmākam asmatsaṃbandhinam imam ū ṣu purodeśe 'nuṣṭhīyamānam api saniṃ havirdānaṃ navyāṃsaṃ navataraṃ gāyatraṃ stutirūpaṃ vaco 'pi deveṣu devānām agre pra vocaḥ | prabrūhi || ū ṣu | nipātasya ceti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvam | suñaḥ iti ṣatvam | navyāṃsam | navaśabdād īyasunīkāralopaś chāndasaḥ | īyasuno nittvād ādyudāttatvam | vocaḥ | chandasi luṅlaṅliṭa iti loḍarthe prārthanāyāṃ luṅy asyativaktīti cler aṅādeśaḥ | pā. 3-1-52 | vaca um | pā. 7-4-20 ||

Translation: "O Agni! Declare (pra vocaḥ) in the presence of the gods (deveṣu) this sani — gift of oblation — of ours, being performed here at the front [of the altar], and also this navyāṃsam — newest — gāyatram — hymn in the Gāyatrī metre, in the form of praise. Ū ṣu: lengthening of the particle in the Saṃhitā; ṣa by suñaḥ. Navyāṃsam: from nava with īyasun; the loss of the ī is Vedic; since īyasun is nit, the first syllable is acute. Vocaḥ: the Vedic luṅ in the sense of the imperative (prayer); aṅ for cli by P. 3-1-52 [asyati-vakti-khyātibhyo 'ṅ]; um augment of vac by P. 7-4-20." Grammar pages 383–384, noted briefly: the words treated are ū ṣu [ū with its vowel lengthened by P. 6-3-136 nipātasya ca; su → ṣu by P. 8-3-107 suñaḥ], navyāṃsam [nava + īyasun in the sense of excess (no sūtra number printed); the ī of īyas lost as a Vedic form; the a of nava lost by P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca: navyas; being ugit, num before the accusative singular (a sarvanāmasthāna); lengthening by P. 6-4-14 atvasantasya cādhātoḥ: navyāṃsam; īyasun has n as it, so the first syllable is acute: the a after n] and vocaḥ [vaca paribhāṣaṇe, adādi (or brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci); the Vedic luṅ in the sense of the imperative by P. 3-4-6; sip; the i lost by itaś ca (no number printed); cli by P. 3-1-43 cli luṅi, and aṅ for it by P. 3-1-52 asyativaktikhyātibhyo 'ṅ; vac + a + s with the augment um by P. 7-4-20 vaca um; guṇa of the last vowel since um is mit; ru-visarga: vocaḥ; the aṭ augment is absent by P. 6-4-75 bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi; the verb has the tiṅanta lowering (no number printed)]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (अग्ने) ((agne)) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | अस्माकम् (asmākam) — our [offered] | इमं सनिम् (imaṃ sanim) — this oblation | नव्यांसम् (navyāṃsam) — newest | गायत्रम् (gāyatram) — the hymn | देवेषु (deveṣu) — in front of the gods | प्र वोचः (pra vocaḥ) — proclaim well.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni! Praise well, in the presence of the gods, this oblation that we offer and this our newest hymn.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, announce to the gods this our offering and this our newest hymn (consisting of verses of Gayatri metre).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ इमम् ऊ सु सनिम् — this gift: the oblation that we have now prepared before us for offering to you. गायत्रं नव्यांसम् — a hymn that has been newly composed by us, in the Gāyatrī metre. Or, by gāyatram is meant 'composed so as to be suitable for singing': that sense may also be taken. अग्ने देवेषु प्र वोचः — O Agni, you tell the gods, close to them, the matter of our oblation and the newly composed hymn.

Rik 5 pp. 384–386

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

आ नो॑ भज पर॒मेष्वा वाजे॑षु मध्य॒मेषु॑ । शिक्षा॒ वस्वो॒ अन्त॑मस्य ॥ ५ ॥

ā́ no bhaja paraméṣv ā́ vā́jeṣu madhyaméṣu | śíkṣā vásvo ántamasya || 5 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

आ । नः । भज । परमेषु । आ । वाजेषु । मध्यमेषु ॥ शिक्ष । वस्वः । अन्तमस्य ॥ ५ ॥

ā | naḥ | bhaja | parameṣu | ā | vājeṣu | madhyameṣu || śikṣa | vasvaḥ | antamasya || 5 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने परमेषूत्कृष्टेषु द्युलोकवर्तिषु वाजेष्वन्नेषु नोऽस्मानाभज । सर्वतः प्रापय । मध्यमेष्वन्तरिक्षलोकवर्तिषु वाजेष्वा भज । अन्तमस्यान्तिकतमस्य भूलोकस्य संबन्धिनि वस्वो वसूनि शिक्ष । देहि ॥ शिक्ष । शिक्ष विद्योपादाने । शपः पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरः । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घः । अन्तमस्य । अन्तिकतमस्य तमे तादेश्च । पा. ६-४-१४९-९ । इति तिकशब्दलोपः ॥ २२ ॥

he agne parameṣūtkṛṣṭeṣu dyulokavartiṣu vājeṣv anneṣu no 'smān ābhaja | sarvataḥ prāpaya | madhyameṣv antarikṣalokavartiṣu vājeṣv ā bhaja | antamasyāntikatamasya bhūlokasya saṃbandhini vasvo vasūni śikṣa | dehi || śikṣa | śikṣa vidyopādāne | śapaḥ pittvād dhātusvaraḥ | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaḥ | antamasya | antikatamasya tame tādeś ca | pā. 6-4-149-9 | iti tikaśabdalopaḥ || 22 ||

Translation: "O Agni! Bring us (ā bhaja), from every side, to the parameṣu — the highest — vājeṣu — foods — that are in the world of heaven; bring us also to the middle foods in the antarikṣa. Give (śikṣa) the vasvaḥ — the riches — that pertain to antamasya — the nearest world, the earth. Śikṣa: śikṣa vidyopādāne ['to learn' — here, 'to give']; since śap is pit, the root's accent [stands]; lengthening in the Saṃhitā by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ. Antamasya: antikatamasya; the loss of tika by tame tādeś ca (Pā. 6-4-149-9 [as printed])." Bhāṣya ends ॥ २२ ॥ = Varga 22. Grammar pages 385–386, noted briefly: the words treated are śikṣa [śikṣa vidyopādāne, bhvādi; the root is taken in other senses too, so here 'give'; loṭ 2nd singular sip → hi (no number printed); the hi is lost after a stem ending in a by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ; śap is pit so anudātta by P. 3-1-4 anudāttau suppitau; the root's end-acute stands; the lengthening of the final a in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-135 dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ] and antamasya [antikatamasya — the superlative of antika; the elements from the t of tika are dropped before tamap by tame tādeś ca (Pā. sū. 6-4-149-9 as printed); so antima — and the genitive antimasya; the print also gives the form antamasya]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (हे अग्ने) ((he agne)) — O Agni | परमेषु वाजेषु (parameṣu vājeṣu) — in the foods of the highest, i.e. of heaven | नः (naḥ) — us | आ भज (ā bhaja) — bring [make us obtain] | मध्यमेषु वाजेषु (madhyameṣu vājeṣu) — in the foods of the middle world [the antarikṣa] | आ भज (ā bhaja) — bring | अन्तमस्य (antamasya) — of the nearest, i.e. the earth | वस्वः (vasvaḥ) — riches | शिक्ष (śikṣa) — give.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni! Cause us to obtain the foods of the highest world, heaven, and of the middle world, the antarikṣa; and give us the riches of the nearest world, the earth.

॥ English Translation ॥

Procure for us the food that is in heaven and firmament and grant us the wealth that is on earth.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Only the words parameṣu, madhyameṣu and antamasya occur in this rik; they simply mean 'the highest, the middle, the nearest (place)'. The commentator explains them respectively as the world of heaven, the antarikṣa and the earth. आ भज — prāpaya: cause to get. शिक्ष — though śikṣa in the sense of 'teaching knowledge' is given, here the general sense 'give' is to be taken.

Rik 6 pp. 386–388

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

वि॒भ॒क्तासि॑ चित्रभानो॒ सिन्धो॑रू॒र्मा उ॑पा॒क आ । स॒द्यो दा॒शुषे॑ क्षरसि ॥ ६ ॥

vibhaktā́si citrabhāno síndhor ūrmā́ upāká ā́ | sadyó dāśúṣe kṣarasi || 6 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

विऽभक्ता । असि । चित्रभानो इति चित्रऽभानो । सिन्धोः । ऊर्मौ । उपाके । आ ॥ सद्यः । दाशुषे । क्षरसि ॥ ६ ॥

vi-bhaktā | asi | citrabhāno iti citra-bhāno | sindhoḥ | ūrmau | upāke | ā || sadyaḥ | dāśuṣe | kṣarasi || 6 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे चित्रभानो विचित्ररश्मियुक्ताग्ने विभक्ता विशिष्टस्य धनस्य प्रापयितासि । तत्र दृष्टान्त उच्यते । आकार उपमार्थः । यथा सिन्धोर्नद्या उपाके समीपे ऊर्मौ ऊर्मिं तरङ्गोपलक्षितं कुल्यादिप्रवाहं विभजन्ति तद्वत् । दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय सद्यस्तदानीमेव क्षरसि । कर्मफलभूतां वृष्टिं करोषि ॥ सिन्धोः । स्यन्दू प्रस्रवणे । स्यन्देः संप्रसारणं धश्च । उ. १-१२ । इत्युप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तत्वम् । ऊर्मिः । अर्तेरूच्च । उ. ४-४४ । इति मिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । दाशुषे । धृतव्रताय दाशुषे । ऋग्वे. १-२५-६ । इत्यत्रोक्तम् ॥

he citrabhāno vicitraraśmiyuktāgne vibhaktā viśiṣṭasya dhanasya prāpayitāsi | tatra dṛṣṭānta ucyate | ākāra upamārthaḥ | yathā sindhor nadyā upāke samīpe ūrmau ūrmiṃ taraṅgopalakṣitaṃ kulyādipravāhaṃ vibhajanti tadvat | dāśuṣe havirdattavate yajamānāya sadyas tadānīm eva kṣarasi | karmaphalabhūtāṃ vṛṣṭiṃ karoṣi || sindhoḥ | syandū prasravaṇe | syandeḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ dhaś ca | u. 1-12 | ity upratyayaḥ | nidity anuvṛtter ādyudāttatvam | ūrmiḥ | arter ūc ca | u. 4-44 | iti miḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | dāśuṣe | dhṛtavratāya dāśuṣe | ṛgve. 1-25-6 | ity atroktam ||

Translation: "O citrabhāno — Agni of many-coloured rays! You are vibhaktā — the one who gives a choice portion of wealth. An illustration: the ā [in ūrmā] is in the sense of comparison. As [men], near a river (sindhoḥ), divide up (vi bhajanti) in the ūrmau — in the stream marked by waves — the flow into canals and the like [by islets], so you [divide wealth]. For the dāśuṣe — the sacrificer who has given the oblation — at once (sadyaḥ), then and there, you pour (kṣarasi): you make rain, the fruit of the rite. Sindhoḥ: syandū prasravaṇe; saṃprasāraṇa and dh by Uṇ. 1-12 [syandeḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ dhaś ca]; first-syllable acute by nit. Ūrmiḥ: ū by Uṇ. 4-44 [arter ūc ca]; mi; the accent of the suffix. Dāśuṣe: explained under Ṛ. 1-25-6." Grammar page 388, noted briefly: the words treated are sindhoḥ [syandū prasravaṇe + u by U. sū. 1-11 (bhāṣya: 1-12) syandeḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ dhaś ca; saṃprasāraṇa of the y of the root; dh for the d; the y becomes i, whence sindhu; genitive singular sindhoḥ; the u is nit — hence first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam], ūrmiḥ [ṛ gatau + mi by Uṇ. 4-44 arter ūc ca; the ū is substituted for the ṛ, with ur aṇ raparaḥ (no number printed) giving ūr; the suffix mi has the initial acute by P. 3-1-3 ādyudāttaś ca, so ūrmi is end-acute] and dāśuṣe [dāś dāne; its process has been given in the preceding discussion (Ṛ. 1-25-6); kvasu, saṃprasāraṇa, ṣatva]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ चित्रभानो (citrabhāno) — O Agni of many-coloured rays | त्वम् (tvam) — you | सिन्धोः (sindhoḥ) — of the river | उपाके (upāke) — near [the middle part, where there are islets] | ऊर्मौ (ūrmau) — in the form of waves | [प्रवाहान् विभजन्ति इव] ([pravāhān vibhajanti iva]) — as [the islets] divide the stream all round | विभक्ता असि (vibhaktā asi) — you are the one who shares [wealth in a undivided way] | दाशुषे (dāśuṣe) — to the offerer of oblations | सद्यः (sadyaḥ) — at once | क्षरसि (kṣarasi) — you pour [the rain, the fruit of the rite].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni of manifold radiance! As islets in the midst of a river's flow divide the stream of waves and make it spread all round, so you divide your unbroken wealth among us. And to the sacrificer who offers oblations, you at once give the fruit of his rite.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Chitrabhanu, or Agni with wonderful or various lustre, you are the distributor of riches as the waves of a river are parted by islets (in the middle of the river); you shower rewards upon the giver of oblations.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ विभक्ता — viśiṣṭasya dhanasya prāpayitāsi: you give all the wealth. चित्रभानो — this word is used specially in addressing Agni. Citra — wonderful, or of many kinds; bhānu — rays; hence 'with wonderful or varied lustre'. सिन्धोरूर्मा — 'as the waters of a river are divided': here the ā [of ūrmā] indicates the sense of iva ('like'), as the commentator says. Syandū prasravaṇe — because it flows as a stream, the word sindhu means a river. क्षरसि — vṛṣṭiṃ karoṣi: you cause the rain; the meaning is 'you pour [the desired things] as rain does'.

Rik 7 pp. 388–390

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

यम॑ग्ने पृ॒त्सु मर्त्य॒मवा॒ वाजे॑षु॒ यं जु॒नाः । स यन्ता॒ शश्व॑ती॒रिषः॑ ॥ ७ ॥

yám agne pṛtsú mártyam ávā vā́jeṣu yáṃ junā́ḥ | sá yántā śáśvatīr íṣaḥ || 7 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

यम् । अग्ने । पृत्ऽसु । मर्त्यम् । अवाः । वाजेषु । यम् । जुनाः ॥ सः । यन्ता । शश्वतीः । इषः ॥ ७ ॥

yam | agne | pṛt-su | martyam | avāḥ | vājeṣu | yam | junāḥ || saḥ | yantā | śaśvatīḥ | iṣaḥ || 7 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे अग्ने पृत्सु संग्रामेषु यं मर्त्यं यजमानमवा अवसि रक्षसि । यं पुरुषं वाजेषु संग्रामेषु जुनाः प्रेरयसि । स नरो यजमानः शाश्वतीरिषो नित्यान्यन्नानि यन्ता । नियन्तुं समर्थो भवति ॥ पृत्सु । पदादिषु मांस्पृत्स्नूनामुपसंख्यानम् । पा. ६-१-६३-१ । इति पृतनाशब्दस्य पृदादेशः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अवाः । आवः । अकाराकारयोर्विपर्ययः । यद्वा । लेट्याडागमः । इतश्चेति सिप इकारस्य लोपः । जुनाः । जू इति गत्यर्थः सौत्रो धातुः । लङः सिप् । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडागमाभावः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । यन्ता । तृनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । शश्वतीः । उगितश्चेति ङीप् ॥

he agne pṛtsu saṃgrāmeṣu yaṃ martyaṃ yajamānam avā avasi rakṣasi | yaṃ puruṣaṃ vājeṣu saṃgrāmeṣu junāḥ prerayasi | sa naro yajamānaḥ śāśvatīr iṣo nityāny annāni yantā | niyantuṃ samartho bhavati || pṛtsu | padādiṣu māṃspṛtsnūnām upasaṃkhyānam | pā. 6-1-63-1 | iti pṛtanāśabdasya pṛdādeśaḥ | sāvekāca iti vibhakter udāttatvam | avāḥ | āvaḥ | akārākārayor viparyayaḥ | yadvā | leṭy āḍāgamaḥ | itaś ceti sipa ikārasya lopaḥ | junāḥ | jū iti gatyarthaḥ sautro dhātuḥ | laṅaḥ sip | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pīty aḍāgamābhāvaḥ | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ | yantā | tṛno nittvād ādyudāttatvam | śaśvatīḥ | ugitaś ceti ṅīp ||

Translation: "O Agni!
