The mortal (martyam), the sacrificer, whom (yam) you protect (avāḥ) in the pṛtsu — battles — and whom you impel (junāḥ) in the vājeṣu — contests — that man, the sacrificer, becomes yantā of śaśvatīḥ iṣaḥ — constant, lasting foods: becomes able to control [them]. Pṛtsu: pṛd substituted for pṛtanā by the vārttika under P. 6-1-63; the case-ending's acute by sāvekāca. Avāḥ: [for] āvaḥ, with a and ā transposed; or, in the leṭ, the augment āṭ; loss of the i of sip by P. 3-4-97. Junāḥ: the root jū in the sense of 'going', a sautra root; laṅ, sip; śnā by the kryādi rule; no aṭ by bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi; no lowering because of the yat-connection. Yantā: tṛn, being nit, first-syllable acute. Śaśvatīḥ: ṅīp by P. 4-1-6 [ugitaś ca]." Grammar pages 389–390, noted briefly: the words treated are pṛtsu [pṛtanā + sup: in the locative plural sup, pṛt is substituted by padādiṣu māṃspṛtsnūnām upasaṃkhyānam (Pā. sū. 6-1-63-2 as printed; bhāṣya 6-1-63-1); the case-ending is anudātta, but by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ it takes the acute], avāḥ [ava rakṣaṇe, bhvādi; laṅ 2nd singular sip with śap; with the augment, āvaḥ; in the Veda the a and ā are transposed — or it is taken as a leṭ, with āṭ by P. 3-4-94 leṭo 'ḍāṭau; the i of sip lost by P. 3-4-97 itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu; śap is pit, so anudātta; by the root's accent the first syllable is acute], junāḥ [jū gatau, a sautra root, kryādi; laṅ 2nd singular sip; śnā by P. 3-1-81 kryādibhyaḥ śnā; junās, ru-visarga; no aṭ by P. 6-4-75 bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi; the verb is not lowered since yam is joined to it, P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttān nityam; by the vikaraṇa's accent it is end-acute], yantā [yamu uparame; tṛn in the sense of agent (no number printed); nominative singular yantā; tṛn is nit so first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-197], and śaśvatīḥ [śaśvat + ṅīp by P. 4-1-6 ugitaś ca; the accusative plural śaśvatīḥ]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (अग्ने) ((agne)) — O Agni | पृत्सु (pṛtsu) — in battles | यं मर्त्यम् (yaṃ martyam) — the man whom | अवाः (avāḥ) — you protect | वाजेषु (vājeṣu) — in contests | यम् (yam) — the man whom | जुनाः (junāḥ) — you inspire | सः (saḥ) — that man | शश्वतीः इषः (śaśvatīḥ iṣaḥ) — eternal food | यन्ता (yantā) — becomes master [lord].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni! The sacrificer whom you protect in battles and whom you inspire in contests becomes the lord of eternal food.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, that mortal (man) whom you protect in battles, whom you encourage in all battles will always command food.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ पृत्सु, वाजेषु — among the forty-six words for 'battle', beginning raṇaḥ, vivāk, the words pṛtsu and vāje are read (Ni. 3-9 as printed, the same numeral as for 'strength' on p. 372); so pṛtsu and vājeṣu mean 'in battles'. जुनाः — jū iti gatyarthaḥ sautro dhātuḥ: the root jū has the sense of going; junāḥ means 'you make go [into battle]', you rouse, you incite, you encourage, and the like. यन्ता — yā prāpaṇe [the print's gloss]: one who has [gained]. शश्वतीः इषः — constant food: always-existing food — one who has always a [sure] means of livelihood, who is never in want of food.

Rik 8 pp. 391–392

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

नकि॑रस्य सहन्त्य पर्ये॒ता कय॑स्य चित् । [accent ?] वाजो॑ अस्ति श्र॒वाय्यः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

nákir asya sahantya paryetā́ káyasya cit | vā́jo asti śravā́yyaḥ || 8 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: a dot-like mark above स of सहन्त्य, perhaps a broken svarita stroke, left unmarked; Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

नकिः । अस्य । सहन्त्य । परिऽएता । कयस्य । चित् ॥ वाजः । अस्ति । श्रवाय्यः ॥ ८ ॥

nakiḥ | asya | sahantya | pari-etā | kayasya | cit || vājaḥ | asti | śravāyyaḥ || 8 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे सहन्त्य शत्रूणामभिभवनशीलाग्ने अस्य त्वद्भक्तस्य यजमानस्य कयस्य चित्कस्यापि पर्येता नकिः । आक्रमिता नास्ति । किंचास्य यजमानस्य श्रवाय्यः श्रवणीयो वाजोऽस्ति । बलविशेषोऽस्ति ॥ कयस्य । यकारोपजनश्छान्दसः । श्रवाय्यः । श्रुदक्षिस्पृहिगृहिभ्य आय्यः । उ. ३-९५ । इत्याय्यप्रत्ययः ॥

he sahantya śatrūṇām abhibhavanaśīlāgne asya tvadbhaktasya yajamānasya kayasya cit kasyāpi paryetā nakiḥ | ākramitā nāsti | kiṃcāsya yajamānasya śravāyyaḥ śravaṇīyo vājo 'sti | balaviśeṣo 'sti || kayasya | yakāropajanaś chāndasaḥ | śravāyyaḥ | śrudakṣispṛhigṛhibhya āyyaḥ | u. 3-95 | ity āyyapratyayaḥ ||

Translation: "O sahantya — Agni, who is wont to overcome enemies! Of this sacrificer, your devotee, kayasya cit — of any one whatsoever [kasya cit] — there is no (nakiḥ) paryetā — overcomer, assailant. And for this sacrificer there is vājaḥ — a notable strength — that is śravāyyaḥ — renowned. Kayasya: the insertion of y is Vedic. Śravāyyaḥ: the suffix āyya after śru [etc.] by Uṇ. 3-95." Grammar page 392, noted briefly: the words treated are kayasya [kim + ṅas: ka for kim by P. 7-2-103 kimaḥ kaḥ; sya for ṅas by P. 7-1-12 ṭāṅasiṅasām inātsyāḥ; y inserted in the Veda for the sake of the metre, whence kayasya] and śravāyyaḥ [śru śravaṇe, bhvādi + āyya by U. sū. 3-376 śrudakṣispṛhigṛhibhya āyyaḥ (bhāṣya: 3-95); guṇa of u before the suffix by P. 7-3-84, av (no number printed) — śravāyya; the suffix's accent makes the word middle-acute]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (सहन्त्य) ((sahantya)) — O Agni, destroyer of enemies | अस्य (asya) — of this [sacrificer] | कयस्य चित् (kayasya cit) — of anyone | पर्येता (paryetā) — a conqueror | नकिः (nakiḥ) — not at all | श्रवाय्यः (śravāyyaḥ) — famous | वाजः (vājaḥ) — strength [or food] | अस्ति (asti) — is [there].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni, destroyer of enemies! No enemy whatever can overcome this sacrificer of yours; for this sacrificer there is a well-known strength — [through your grace] — and food.

॥ English Translation ॥

Subduer of enemies, (Agni) no conqueror of your worshipper ever exists; for his might is well-known.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ नकिः — among the nine words beginning hikam, nukam, which state the sarvapadasamāmnāya, the word nakiḥ is read (no reference printed); so nakiḥ may here be given the sense 'there is no' (or any sense that suits the context). सहन्त्य — śatrūṇām abhibhavanaśīla: one with the ability to defeat enemies. पर्येता — pari eteti paryetā ākramitā: the one who attacks, who conquers. कयस्य चित् — kasya cit: the syllable ya is inserted here for the metre. वाजः — strength or food. श्रवाय्यः — śravaṇīyaḥ: renowned.

Rik 9 pp. 392–395

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

स वाजं॑ वि॒श्वच॑र्षणि॒रर्व॑द्भिरस्तु॒ तरु॑ता । विप्रे॑भिरस्तु॒ सनि॑ता ॥ ९ ॥

sá vā́jaṃ viśvácarṣaṇir árvadbhir astu tárutā | víprebhir astu sánitā || 9 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

सः । वाजम् । विश्वऽचर्षणिः । अर्वत्ऽभिः । अस्तु । तरुता ॥ विप्रेभिः । अस्तु । सनिता ॥ ९ ॥

saḥ | vājam | viśva-carṣaṇiḥ | arvat-bhiḥ | astu | tarutā || viprebhiḥ | astu | sanitā || 9 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

विश्वचर्षणिः सर्वैर्मनुष्यैरुपेतः सोऽग्निरर्वद्भिरश्वैर्वाजं संग्रामं तरुता तारयिताऽस्तु । विप्रेभिर्मेधाविभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः सहितस्तुष्टोऽग्निः सनिता फलस्य दाताऽस्तु ॥ विश्वचर्षणिः । विश्वे चर्षणयो यस्य । बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायामिति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । अर्वद्भिः । ऋ गतौ । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति वनिप् । भिस्यर्वणस्त्रसावनञः । पा. ६-४-१२७ । इति नकारस्य तृ इत्ययमादेशः । तरुता । तॄ प्लवनतरणयोः । अस्माद्ग्रसितस्कभितेत्यादौ । पा. ७-२-३४ । तृन्नन्तो निपातितः । निपातनादेवेकारस्योत्वम् ॥

viśvacarṣaṇiḥ sarvair manuṣyair upetaḥ so 'gnir arvadbhir aśvair vājaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ tarutā tārayitā 'stu | viprebhir medhāvibhir ṛtvigbhiḥ sahitas tuṣṭo 'gniḥ sanitā phalasya dātā 'stu || viśvacarṣaṇiḥ | viśve carṣaṇayo yasya | bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām iti pūrvapadāntodāttatvam | arvadbhiḥ | ṛ gatau | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti vanip | bhisy arvaṇas trasāvanañaḥ | pā. 6-4-127 | iti nakārasya tṛ ity ayam ādeśaḥ | tarutā | tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ | asmād grasitaskabhitety ādau | pā. 7-2-34 | tṛnnanto nipātitaḥ | nipātanād evekārasyotvam ||

Translation: "May that Agni — viśvacarṣaṇiḥ, who is accompanied by all men — be tarutā — the one who carries across — the vāja — the battle — with arvadbhiḥ — horses. And, pleased, being accompanied by the viprebhiḥ — the wise priests — may Agni be sanitā — the giver of fruit. Viśvacarṣaṇiḥ: one whose carṣaṇis [men] are all; in the bahuvrīhi the end-acute of the first member by P. 6-2-106. Arvadbhiḥ: from ṛ gatau with vanip; before bhis, arvan has tṛ in place of n (P. 6-4-127). Tarutā: from tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ; the tṛn-ending form is given by nipātana in the rule grasitaskabhita… (P. 7-2-34); the u for i by nipātana itself." The bhāṣya ends here; it has no note on viprebhiḥ. Grammar pages 394–395, noted briefly: the words treated are viśvacarṣaṇiḥ [viśve carṣaṇayo yasya — a bahuvrīhi; the first member has the end-acute by P. 6-2-106 bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām because the compound is a name], arvadbhiḥ [ṛ gatau + vanip by P. 3-2-75 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; guṇa of the root: arvan, an n-stem; before the instrumental plural bhis, a case-ending other than su, the n is replaced by tṛ by P. 6-4-127 arvaṇas trasāvanañaḥ; the ṛ of tṛ is it, so arvat, a t-stem, and arvadbhiḥ], tarutā [tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, bhvādi; the tṛn-ending form is given by nipātana in P. 7-2-34 grasitaskabhita…, which records forms with operations not provided elsewhere; so by nipātana the i of the iṭ becomes u; in the nominative singular anaṅ, lengthening and loss of n give tarutā] and viprebhiḥ [vipra + bhis, the ais substitution of P. 7-1-9 ato bhisa ais is optional in the Veda (P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi), so it does not occur; P. 7-3-103 bahuvacane jhaly et gives e to the final a of the stem: viprebhiḥ]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ विश्वचर्षणिः (viśvacarṣaṇiḥ) — he who is honoured by all men | सः (saḥ) — that Agni | अर्वद्भिः (arvadbhiḥ) — with horses | वाजम् (vājam) — the battle | तरुता (tarutā) — one who carries across | अस्तु (astu) — may he be | विप्रेभिः (viprebhiḥ) — with the wise priests | सनिता (sanitā) — giver of the greatest fruit | अस्तु (astu) — may he be.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ May Agni, honoured by all men, bring us through the battle, helped by horses; and may he, worshipped by the wise priests, be the giver of the greatest fruits.

॥ English Translation ॥

May he who is worshipped by all men convey us with horses through the battle; may he, praised by the intelligent priests, be the bestower of riches.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ विश्वचर्षणिः — viśvair manuṣyair upetaḥ: he who is joined by all men; i.e. honoured by all men. Among the twenty-five names of men beginning manuṣyaḥ, nṛ [etc.], the word carṣaṇi is read; so carṣaṇi means 'man'. अर्वद्भिः — among the twenty-six names of horses beginning atyaḥ, hayaḥ, the word arvā is read; so arvadbhiḥ means 'with horses'; there is a śruti sentence arvāsi saptir asi vājy asi ('you are a courser, a steed, a racer'). तरुता — tārayitā: one who carries across; who takes [us] across and brings us through battle without defeat, so that we win. विप्रेभिः — medhāvibhir ṛtvigbhiḥ: by the wise priests (being praised). सनिता — phalasya dātā: the giver of the fruit.

Rik 10 pp. 395–398

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

जरा॑बोध॒ तद्वि॑विड्ढि वि॒शेवि॑शे य॒ज्ञिया॑य । स्तोमं॑ रु॒द्राय॒ दृशी॑कं ॥ १० ॥

járābodha tád viviḍḍhi viśé-viśe yajñíyāya | stómaṃ rudrā́ya dṛ́śīkaṃ || 10 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

जराऽबोध । तत् । विविड्ढि । विशेऽविशे । यज्ञियाय ॥ स्तोमम् । रुद्राय । दृशीकम् ॥ १० ॥

jarā-bodha | tat | viviḍḍhi | viśe-viśe | yajñiyāya || stomam | rudrāya | dṛśīkam || 10 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अप्तोर्यामे होतुरतिरिक्तोक्थे जराबोध तद्विविड्ढीति स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । यस्य पशवो नोपदधेरन्निति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । अतिरिक्तोक्थानि जराबोध तद्विविड्ढि । आ. ९-११ । इति ॥ हे जराबोध जरया स्तुत्या बोधमानाग्ने विशेविशे तत्तद्यजमानरूपप्रजानुग्रहार्थं यज्ञियाय यज्ञसंबन्ध्यनुष्ठानसिद्ध्यर्थं तदेव यजनं विविड्ढि । प्रविश । यजमानोऽपि रुद्राय क्रूरायाग्नये तुभ्यं दृशीकं दर्शनीयं समीचीनं स्तोमं स्तोत्रं करोतीति शेषः । अत्र यास्क एवं व्याख्यातवान् । जरा स्तुतिर्जरतेः स्तुतिकर्मणस्तां बोध तया बोधयितरिति वा तद्विविड्ढि तत्कुरु मनुष्यस्य मनुष्यस्य यजनाय स्तोमं रुद्राय दर्शनीयम् । नि. १०-८ । इति ॥ जराबोध । जॄष् वयोहानौ । अत्र तु स्तुत्यर्थः । षिद्भिदादिभ्योऽङ् । पा. ३-३-१०४ । इत्यङ्प्रत्ययः । ततष्टाप् । जरया स्तुत्या बोधो यस्यासौ जराबोधः । यद्वा । जरया बोध्यत इति जराबोधः । कर्मणि घञ् । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । विविड्ढि । विश प्रवेशने । लोटो हिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । अभ्यासहलादिशेषौ । हुझल्भ्यो हेर्धिरिति हेर्धिरादेशः । षत्वष्टुत्वे । यद्वा । विष्लृ व्याप्तावित्यस्माल्लोण्मध्यमैकवचनेऽभ्यासस्य गुणाभावः । विशेविशे । सावेकाच इति चतुर्थ्या उदात्तत्वम् । अनुदात्तं चेत्याम्रेडितानुदात्तत्वम् । यज्ञियाय । यज्ञर्त्विग्भ्यां घखञौ । पा. ५-१-७१ । इति घः । दृशीकम् । अनिदृशिभ्यां चेति कीकन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥ २३ ॥

aptoryāme hotur atiriktokthe jarābodha tad viviḍḍhīti stotriyas tṛcaḥ | yasya paśavo nopadadheran iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | atiriktokthāni jarābodha tad viviḍḍhi | ā. 9-11 | iti || he jarābodha jarayā stutyā bodhamānāgne viśe-viśe tattadyajamānarūpaprajānugrahārthaṃ yajñiyāya yajñasaṃbandhyanuṣṭhānasiddhyarthaṃ tad eva yajanaṃ viviḍḍhi | praviśa | yajamāno 'pi rudrāya krūrāyāgnaye tubhyaṃ dṛśīkaṃ darśanīyaṃ samīcīnaṃ stomaṃ stotraṃ karotīti śeṣaḥ | atra yāska evaṃ vyākhyātavān | jarā stutir jarateḥ stutikarmaṇas tāṃ bodha tayā bodhayitar iti vā tad viviḍḍhi tat kuru manuṣyasya manuṣyasya yajanāya stomaṃ rudrāya darśanīyam | ni. 10-8 | iti || jarābodha | jṝṣ vayohānau | atra tu stutyarthaḥ | ṣidbhidādibhyo 'ṅ | pā. 3-3-104 | ity aṅpratyayaḥ | tataṣ ṭāp | jarayā stutyā bodho yasyāsau jarābodhaḥ | yadvā | jarayā bodhyata iti jarābodhaḥ | karmaṇi ghañ | āmantritādyudāttatvam | viviḍḍhi | viśa praveśane | loṭo hiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | abhyāsahalādiśeṣau | hujhalbhyo her dhir iti her dhir ādeśaḥ | ṣatvaṣṭutve | yadvā | viṣlṛ vyāptāv ity asmāl loṇmadhyamaikavacane 'bhyāsasya guṇābhāvaḥ | viśe-viśe | sāvekāca iti caturthyā udāttatvam | anudāttaṃ cety āmreḍitānudāttatvam | yajñiyāya | yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau | pā. 5-1-71 | iti ghaḥ | dṛśīkam | anidṛśibhyāṃ ceti kīkanpratyayaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ || 23 ||

Translation: "In the Aptoryāma, in the extra uktha of the Hotṛ, the triplet jarābodha tad viviḍḍhi is a stotriya; so it is laid down in the section yasya paśavo nopadadheran: 'the extra ukthas, jarābodha tad viviḍḍhi' (Āś. 9-11). O jarābodha — Agni, awakened (bodha) by praise (jarā)! For every people (viśe-viśe), that is, for the favour of the people in the form of sacrificers, for the accomplishment of the sacrifice (yajñiyāya), enter (viviḍḍhi) that very worship. And the sacrificer also offers to you, Rudra — the terrible Agni — a dṛśīkam — pleasing, excellent — stomam — hymn: this is to be supplied. Yāska explains thus: 'jarā is praise, from jarati of the sense of praising; awaken to it, or [O] awakener by it; do that; for the worship of every man, a pleasing stoma for Rudra' (Ni. 10-8). Jarābodha: jṝṣ vayohānau [to decay with age]; here the sense of praise; the suffix aṅ by P. 3-3-104 [ṣidbhidādibhyo 'ṅ], then ṭāp; 'he whose awakening (bodha) is by praise', or 'he who is awakened by praise', with ghañ in the passive sense; the vocative's first-syllable acute. Viviḍḍhi: viśa praveśane; hi for the loṭ; ślu for śap by bahulaṃ chandasi; the reduplicate keeps only its first consonant; dhi for hi by hujhalbhyo her dhiḥ; ṣ and ṣṭutva. Or from viṣlṛ vyāptau, in the loṭ 2nd singular, with no guṇa of the reduplicate. Viśe-viśe: the dative ending acute by sāvekācaḥ; the repeated word anudātta by anudāttaṃ ca. Yajñiyāya: gha by P. 5-1-71 [yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau]. Dṛśīkam: kīkan by anidṛśibhyāṃ ca; first-syllable acute since it is nit." Bhāṣya ends ॥ २३ ॥ = Varga 23; the part after jarābodha's sūtra, p. 396, was missing in this file and has been added from the print, w3. Grammar pages 397–398, noted briefly: the words treated are jarābodha [jṝṣ vayohānau, kryādi — roots have more than one sense, so here it means 'praise'; aṅ by P. 3-3-104 ṣidbhidādibhyo 'ṅ after a ṣit root; guṇa by P. 7-4-16 ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ; jara, and ṭāp by P. 4-1-4 ajādyataṣ ṭāp: jarā; budha avagamane + ghañ in the passive sense; guṇa; jarayā bodho yasya — he who is known by praise; or jarayā bodhyate; the vocative with the loss of su; not lowered (the āṣṭamika lowering) because it is at the head of the pāda; first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca], viviḍḍhi [viśa praveśane, tudādi; loṭ 2nd singular sip → hi; śa replaced by śluḥ by bahulaṃ chandasi; doubling; hi → dhi by P. 6-4-101; ś → ṣ by P. 8-2-36 vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ; ṣ + dh with ṣṭutva (ḍh) — or from viṣlṛ vyāptau, juhotyādi: ślu by P. 2-4-75 juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ, doubling; the guṇa due by P. 7-4-75 nijāṃ trayāṇāṃ guṇaḥ ślau is not made, by P. 3-1-85 vyatyayo bahulam], viśe-viśe [viś in the dative singular: the acute on the ending by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ, so end-acute; doubled by P. 8-1-4 nityavīpsayoḥ; the second is anudātta by P. 8-1-3 anudāttaṃ ca], yajñiyāya [yajña + gha in the sense of 'worthy of' by P. 5-1-71 yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau; gha → iya by P. 7-1-2; loss of the a by P. 6-4-148; dative] and dṛśīkam [dṛśir prekṣaṇe, bhvādi + kīkan by anidṛśibhyāṃ ca (Daśa. pā. 3 as printed); k and n are it, leaving īka; first-syllable acute because kīkan is nit, P. 6-1-197]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ जराबोध (jarābodha) — O Agni, awakened by praise | विशेविशे (viśe-viśe) — for every sacrificer | यज्ञियाय (yajñiyāya) — for the accomplishment of the sacrifice | तत् (tat) — that [divine sacrificial place] | विविड्ढि (viviḍḍhi) — enter | रुद्राय (rudrāya) — to you of terrible form | दृशीकम् (dṛśīkam) — pleasant | स्तोमम् (stomam) — hymn | [करोति] ([karoti]) — [the sacrificer] offers.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Agni, awakened by praise! For the success of each man's sacrifice, enter the sacrificial place of the gods. That sacrificer too offers to you, of terrible form, pleasing hymns.

॥ English Translation ॥

(O Agni) you who are awakened by praise enter into the oblation for the completion of the sacrifice that benefits mankind; the worshipper offers beautiful (or agreeable) prayers to the terrible Agni.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Application. In the Soma-sacrifice called Aptoryāma, the priest called Hotṛ is to recite, at the time of reciting the atirikta-uktha śastra mantras, the three riks beginning jarābodha (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-27-10, 11, 12). Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra, in the section yasya paśavo nopadadheran, explains it in the sūtra atiriktokthāni jarābodha tad viviḍḍhi (Āś. 9-11).

जराबोध — jarayā stutyā bodhamāna: one who is awakened by praise. In order that Agni may be awakened at dawn for carrying out the sacrifice in the sacrificial ground, these three riks beginning jarābodha are used at that time. विविड्ढि — praviśa: enter. विशेविशे — for every people; for every sacrificer. यज्ञियाय — for the success of the sacrifice; for the sacrifice to be performed in complete form. रुद्राय — krūrāyogney: to Agni of terrible form; because Agni burns up all things, he has the nature of Rudra. Among the thirteen names of praisers beginning rebhaḥ, jaritā [etc.] the word rudra is read (Ni. 3-19), so rudrāya may mean 'to the praiser'; here one can take it either as 'to Agni, who is pleased by praise' or 'to the Agni who is praised with hymns'. दृशीकम् — darśanīyaṃ saṃdarśanīyam: beautiful, excellent; stomaṃ — hymn; the words yajamānaḥ karoti ['the sacrificer offers'] must be supplied.

Rik 11 pp. 398–401

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

स नो॑ म॒हाँ अनि॑मा॒नो धू॒मके॑तुः पुरुश्च॒न्द्रः । [accent ?] धि॒ये वाजा॑य हिन्वतु ॥ ११ ॥

sá no mahā́m̐ ánimānó dhūmáketuḥ puruścandráḥ | dhiyé vā́jāya hinvatu || 11 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: the stroke over अनि and the bar under मा stand between two akṣaras (read as नि॑ and मा॒); no stroke is printed over मानो; the न्द्र of पुरुश्चन्द्रः is broken type; Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

सः । नः । महान् । अनिऽमानः । धूमऽकेतुः । पुरुऽचन्द्रः ॥ धिये । वाजाय । हिन्वतु ॥ ११ ॥

saḥ | naḥ | mahān | ani-mānaḥ | dhūma-ketuḥ | puru-candraḥ || dhiye | vājāya | hinvatu || 11 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

सोऽग्निर्नोऽस्माकं धिये कर्मणे वाजायान्नाय च हिन्वतु । प्रीणयतु । कीदृशः । महान् गुणाधिकः । अनिमानो निमानवर्जितः । अपरिच्छिन्न इत्यर्थः । धूमकेतुर्धूमेन ज्ञाप्यमानः पुरुश्चन्द्रो बहुदीप्तिः ॥ महाँ अनीत्यत्र संहितायां नकारस्य रुत्वानुनासिकावुक्तौ । अनिमानः । न विद्यते निमानोऽस्येति बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । धूमकेतुः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । पुरुश्चन्द्रः । चदि आह्लादने दीप्तौ च । अस्मात्स्फायितञ्चीत्यादिना कर्तरि रक् । पुरुश्चासौ चन्द्रश्चेति समासान्तोदात्तत्वम् । ह्रस्वाच्चन्द्रोत्तरपदे मन्त्रे । पा. ६-१-१५१ । इति सुट् । तस्य श्चुत्वेन शकारः । धिये । सावेकाच इति चतुर्थ्या उदात्तत्वम् । हिन्वतु । हिवि प्रीणनार्थः । इदितो नुम् धातोरिति नुम् ॥

so 'gnir no 'smākaṃ dhiye karmaṇe vājāyānnāya ca hinvatu | prīṇayatu | kīdṛśaḥ | mahān guṇādhikaḥ animāno nimānavarjitaḥ aparicchinna ity arthaḥ | dhūmaketur dhūmena jñāpyamānaḥ puruścandro bahudīptiḥ || mahām̐ anīty atra saṃhitāyāṃ nakārasya rutvānunāsikāv uktau | animānaḥ | na vidyate nimāno 'syeti bahuvrīhau nañsubhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatvam | dhūmaketuḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | puruścandraḥ | cadi āhlādane dīptau ca | asmāt sphāyitañcīty ādinā kartari rak | puruś cāsau candraś ceti samāsāntodāttatvam | hrasvāc candrottarapade mantre | pā. 6-1-151 | iti suṭ | tasya ścutvena śakāraḥ | dhiye | sāvekāca iti caturthyā udāttatvam | hinvatu | hivi prīṇanārthaḥ | idito num dhātor iti num ||

Translation: "May that Agni gladden (hinvatu) us — for our dhī, our rite, and for vāja, food. What is he like? Mahān — great, surpassing in qualities; animānaḥ — without measure, unlimited; dhūmaketuḥ — known by smoke [as his banner]; puruścandraḥ — of much radiance. Mahām̐ animānaḥ: in the Saṃhitā the n becomes ru and anunāsika. Animānaḥ: a bahuvrīhi 'whose measure does not exist'; the end-acute of the second member by nañsubhyām. Dhūmaketuḥ: the first member's accent in the bahuvrīhi. Puruścandraḥ: cadi āhlādane dīptau ca ['to delight, to shine']; rak by [the rule sphāyitañci…]; the compound of puru and candra; the suṭ augment by P. 6-1-151 [hrasvāc candrottarapade mantre]; its s → ś by ścutva. Dhiye: the dative's acute by sāvekāca. Hinvatu: hivi prīṇane; num by P. 7-1-58." Grammar pages 399–401, noted briefly: the words treated are mahān [mahat + su; in the Saṃhitā before ṭ, t etc. the n → ru by P. 8-3-9 dīrghād aṭi samānapāde; the ā before the ru nasalized by P. 8-3-3 āto 'ṭi nityam], animānaḥ [na vidyate nimānam — a nañ-bahuvrīhi; nañsubhyām P. 6-2-172 gives the end-acute to the second member, overriding the first member's accent], dhūmaketuḥ [dhūmaḥ ketuḥ yasya, a bahuvrīhi; P. 6-2-1 bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam keeps the first member's accent, overriding the compound-final accent; the a after m — the long ū — is acute], puruścandraḥ [cadi āhlādane dīptau ca, bhvādi; rak in the sense of agent by U. sū. 1-170 sphāyitañcivañci…; idito num dhātoḥ P. 7-1-58 adds num; puru + candra — a karmadhāraya; the compound-final acute by P. 6-1-223 samāsasya; the augment suṭ by P. 6-1-151 hrasvāc candrottarapade mantre — puruscandra: s → ś by ścutva (no number printed) — hence puruścandraḥ], dhiye [dhī + ṅe; the ending takes the acute by P. 6-1-168] and hinvatu [hivi prīṇane, bhvādi; loṭ 3rd singular tip → tu by P. 3-4-86 eruḥ; num by P. 7-1-58; śap by P. 3-1-68 kartari śap; since num is mit it stands after the vowel: hinvatu; the verb is lowered since it follows a word that is not a finite verb (no number printed)]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ महान् (mahān) — great in qualities | अनिमानः (animānaḥ) — unlimited | धूमकेतुः (dhūmaketuḥ) — known by smoke | पुरुश्चन्द्रः (puruścandraḥ) — of surpassing radiance | सः (saḥ) — that Agni | नः (naḥ) — our | धिये (dhiye) — for the [sacrificial] rite | वाजाय (vājāya) — for food | हिन्वतु (hinvatu) — may he be pleased [may he please].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ May Agni — great in qualities, unlimited, known by smoke, of great radiance — be pleased with our rite and gladden us with food.

॥ English Translation ॥

May the great, illimitable, smoke-bannered and brilliant Agni be pleased with our rite and grant (inspire) us food.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अनिमानः — na vidyate nimāno 'sya: one with no nimāna [measure]; one without measure; unlimited. धूमकेतुः — one whose ketu (banner) is smoke; it is well known that smoke is Agni's flag. पुरुश्चन्द्रः — cadi āhlādane dīptau ca; puruścandro bahudīptiḥ: one of much radiance. धिये — karmaṇe prajñāyai: of the twenty-six names for 'act' beginning apaḥ, apnaḥ, the word dhī is read (Ni. 3-1), so dhī means 'act'; and of the eleven names for 'intellect' beginning ketaḥ, ketuḥ, the word dhī is read (Ni. 3-13), so dhī means 'intellect'. Here we pray: 'so that the sacrifices that we perform may be completed, and for our prajñā — knowledge — grant us [food]'. हिन्वतु — prīṇayatu: may he be pleased; may he grant us food and the like.

Rik 12 pp. 401–403

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

स रे॒वाँ इ॑व वि॒श्पति॒र्दैव्यः॑ के॒तुः शृ॑णोतु नः । उ॒क्थैर॒ग्निर्बृ॒हद्भा॑नुः ॥ १२ ॥

sá revā́m̐ iva viśpátir daívyaḥ ketúḥ śṛṇotu naḥ | ukthaír agnír bṛhádbhānuḥ || 12 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

सः । रेवान्ऽइव । विश्पतिः । दैव्यः । केतुः । शृणोतु । नः ॥ उक्थैः । अग्निः । बृहत्ऽभानुः ॥ १२ ॥

saḥ | revān-iva | viśpatiḥ | daivyaḥ | ketuḥ | śṛṇotu | naḥ || ukthaiḥ | agniḥ | bṛhat-bhānuḥ || 12 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

सोऽग्निरुक्थैः स्तोत्रैर्युक्तान्नोऽस्मान्शृणोतु । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । रेवानिव । यथा लोके धनवान्राजा वन्दिनां स्तोत्रं शृणोति तद्वत् । कीदृशः । विश्पतिः प्रजापालको दैव्यो देवानां संबन्धी । अग्निर्वै देवानां होता । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-१४ । इति श्रुत्यन्तरात् । केतुर्दूतवज्ज्ञापकः । अग्निर्वै देवानां दूत आसीत् । तै. सं. २-५-८-५ । इति श्रुतेः । बृहद्भानुः प्रौढरश्मिः ॥ स रेवान् । एतत्तदोः । पा. ६-१-१३२ । इति सोर्लोपः । रेवान् । रयेर्मतौ बहुलमिति संप्रसारणं परपूर्वत्वम् । आद्गुणः । छन्दसीर इति मतुपो वत्वम् । आरेशब्दाच्च मतुप उदात्तत्वम् । विश्पतिः । परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । बृहद्भानुः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

so 'gnir ukthaiḥ stotrair yuktān no 'smān śṛṇotu | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | revān iva | yathā loke dhanavān rājā vandināṃ stotraṃ śṛṇoti tadvat | kīdṛśaḥ | viśpatiḥ prajāpālako daivyo devānāṃ saṃbandhī | agnir vai devānāṃ hotā | ai. brā. 3-14 | iti śrutyantarāt | ketur dūtavaj jñāpakaḥ | agnir vai devānāṃ dūta āsīt | tai. saṃ. 2-5-8-5 | iti śruteḥ | bṛhadbhānuḥ prauḍharaśmiḥ || sa revān | etattadoḥ | pā. 6-1-132 | iti sor lopaḥ | revān | rayer matau bahulam iti saṃprasāraṇaṃ parapūrvatvam | ād guṇaḥ | chandasīra iti matupo vatvam | āreśabdāc ca matupa udāttatvam | viśpatiḥ | parādiś chandasi bahulam ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | bṛhadbhānuḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||

Translation: "May that Agni hear us (śṛṇotu naḥ), who are furnished with ukthas — hymns. An illustration: revān iva — as, in the world, a wealthy king listens to the hymn of his bards. What is Agni like? Viśpatiḥ — protector of the people; daivyaḥ — belonging to the gods, for another śruti says 'Agni is indeed the Hotṛ of the gods' (Ai. Brā. 3-14); ketuḥ — the one who makes [them] known like a messenger, as the śruti says 'Agni was the messenger of the gods' (Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-8-5); bṛhadbhānuḥ — of vast rays. Sa revān: loss of su of sas by P. 6-1-132 [etattadoḥ sulopo 'koranañsamāse hali]. Revān: saṃprasāraṇa of rayi before matup, by bahulam; pararūpa; guṇa; v for m of matup; the acute from the ā-ending. Viśpatiḥ: the second member's initial acute by parādiś chandasi bahulam. Bṛhadbhānuḥ: the first member's accent in the bahuvrīhi." Grammar page 403, noted briefly: the words treated are sa revān [sas + revān: the su is lost before a consonant by P. 6-1-132], revān [rayi + matup; in the Veda saṃprasāraṇa by rayer matau bahulam (Vā. 34-73 as printed); the rule P. 6-1-37 na saṃprasāraṇe saṃprasāraṇam prevents a second saṃprasāraṇa, so only the y → i; saṃprasāraṇāc ca P. 6-1-108 gives pūrvarūpa; ād guṇaḥ → e; matup's m → v by P. 8-2-15 chandasīraḥ; nominative singular with num, lengthening, loss of su and t; although matup is pit, it takes the acute after re by āre śabdāc ca matupa udāttatvaṃ vaktavyam (Pā. sū. 6-1-176-1); revān iva — n → ru and anunāsika before iva as before], viśpatiḥ [viśāṃ patiḥ; P. 6-1-223 samāsasya would give the end-acute, but P. 6-2-199 parādiś chandasi bahulam gives the acute to the beginning of the second member] and bṛhadbhānuḥ [bṛhataḥ bhānavaḥ yasya, a bahuvrīhi; P. 6-2-1 gives the first member's accent; the a after h is acute]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ विश्पतिः (viśpatiḥ) — protector of the people | दैव्यः (daivyaḥ) — belonging to the gods | केतुः (ketuḥ) — the messenger of the gods | बृहद्भानुः (bṛhadbhānuḥ) — of vast rays | सः अग्निः (saḥ agniḥ) — that Agni | रेवान् इव (revān iva) — like a rich king, listening to his bards' praises | उक्थैः (ukthaiḥ) — with hymns | नः (naḥ) — us | शृणोतु (śṛṇotu) — may he hear.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ May that Agni — protector of the people, belonging to the gods, the messenger of the gods, of great shining rays — hear our hymns as a wealthy king hears the praises of his bards.

॥ English Translation ॥

May Agni, of vast splendour, the lord of men, the invoker and messenger of gods hear us through our prayers as a wealthy king listens to his followers.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ रेवानिव — dhanavān rājā: a king who is rich; or a rich man. It is natural, in the world, for people to praise a rich man, and for him to be pleased at hearing that praise. विश्पतिः — prajāpālakaḥ: Agni who protects the people. दैव्यः — belonging to the gods: i.e. of the company of the gods; moreover because Agni invokes the gods, he is called dūta — the messenger. On this the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa has the sentence agnir vai devānāṃ hotā (Ai. Brā. 3-14) and the Taittirīya Saṃhitā has agnir vai devānāṃ dūta āsīt (Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-8-5). केतुः — since ketu has the sense prajñā, the commentator gives for the word an alternative meaning, 'the messenger who makes the gods known, as he brings them to the place of sacrifice'; as the word also has the sense of 'act' [karma], ketuḥ may be taken as 'one who completes sacrificial acts'. बृहद्भानुः — prauḍharaśmiḥ: of fierce rays — one with fiery, burning rays.

Rik 13 (closing rik; Viśvedevas; Triṣṭubh) pp. 404–407

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

नमो॑ म॒हद्भ्यो॒ नमो॑ अर्भ॒केभ्यो॒ नमो॒ युव॑भ्यो॒ नम॑ आशि॒नेभ्यः॑ । यजा॑म दे॒वान्यदि॑ श॒क्नवा॑म॒ मा ज्याय॑सः॒ शंस॒मा वृ॑क्षि देवाः ॥ १३ ॥

námo mahádbhyo námo arbhakébhyo námo yúvabhyo náma āśinébhyaḥ | yájāma devā́n yádi śaknávāma mā́ jyā́yasaḥ śáṃsam ā́ vṛkṣi devāḥ || 13 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3), four printed lines; Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

नमः । महत्ऽभ्यः । नमः । अर्भकेभ्यः । नमः । युवऽभ्यः । नमः । आशिनेभ्यः ॥ यजाम । देवान् । यदि । शक्नवाम । मा । ज्यायसः । शंसम् । आ । वृक्षि । देवाः ॥ १३ ॥

namaḥ | mahat-bhyaḥ | namaḥ | arbhakebhyaḥ | namaḥ | yuva-bhyaḥ | namaḥ | āśinebhyaḥ || yajāma | devān | yadi | śaknavāma | mā | jyāyasaḥ | śaṃsam | ā | vṛkṣi | devāḥ || 13 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

दर्शपूर्णमासयोः स्रुगादापनात्पूर्वभाविनि जपे नमो महद्भ्य इत्येषा । ब्रह्मादेने प्राशिष्यमाण इति खण्डे सूर्यो नो दिवस्पातु नमो महद्भ्यो नमो अर्भकेभ्यः । आ. १-४ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥ अग्निना प्रेरितः शुनःशेपो विश्वान्देवाननया तुष्टाव । तथा चाम्नायते — तमग्निरुवाच विश्वान्नु देवान्स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति स विश्वान्देवांस्तुष्टाव नमो महद्भ्यो नमो अर्भकेभ्य इत्येतयर्चा । ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१६ । इति ॥ महान्तो गुणैरधिकाः । अर्भका गुणैर्न्यूनाः । युवानस्तरुणाः । आशिना वयसा व्याप्ता वृद्धाः । यथोक्तचतुर्विधदेहयुक्तेभ्यो देवेभ्यो नमोऽस्तु । यदि शक्नवाम कथंचिद्धनादिसंपत्त्या शक्ताश्चेत्तदानीं देवान्यजाम । हे देवा ज्यायसो ज्येष्ठस्य देवताविशेषस्य आ सर्वतः प्रसृतं शंसं स्तोत्रं मा वृक्षि । अहं विच्छिन्नं मा कार्षम् ॥ आशिनेभ्यः । अशू व्याप्तौ । बहुलमन्यत्रापि । उ. २-४९ । इत्याणादिक [sic] इनच्प्रत्ययः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । यजाम । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः । शक्नवाम । शक्लृ शक्तौ । आडुत्तमस्य पिच्चेति तिङः पित्त्वद्भावादनुदात्तत्वे सति विकरणस्वरः । निपातैर्यद्यदिहन्तेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । ज्यायसः । प्रशस्यशब्दादीयसुनि ज्य च । पा. ५-३-६१ । इति ज्यादेशः । ज्यादादीयसः । पा. ६-४-१६० । इतीयसुन ईकारस्यात्वम् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । शंसम् । हलश्चेति घञ् । वृक्षि । ओ व्रश्चू छेदने । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदोत्तमपुरुषैकवचनमिट् । च्लेः सिच् । स्वरतिसूतीत्यादिना इडभावः । स्कोः संयोगाद्योरित्युपधासकारलोपः । व्रश्चादिना षत्वम् । षढोः कः सीति कत्वम् । आदेशप्रत्यययोरिति षत्वम् । न माङ्योग इत्यडभावः ॥ २४ ॥

darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ srugādāpanāt pūrvabhāvini jape namo mahadbhya ity eṣā | brahmādene prāśiṣyamāṇa iti khaṇḍe sūryo no divaspātu namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhyaḥ | ā. 1-4 | iti sūtritam || agninā preritaḥ śunaḥśepo viśvān devān anayā tuṣṭāva | tathā cāmnāyate — tam agnir uvāca viśvān nu devān stuhy atha tvotsrakṣyāma iti sa viśvān devāṃs tuṣṭāva namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhya ity etayarcā | ai. brā. 7-16 | iti || mahānto guṇair adhikāḥ | arbhakā guṇair nyūnāḥ | yuvānas taruṇāḥ | āśinā vayasā vyāptā vṛddhāḥ | yathoktacaturvidhadehayuktebhyo devebhyo namo 'stu | yadi śaknavāma kathaṃcid dhanādisaṃpattyā śaktāś cet tadānīṃ devān yajāma | he devā jyāyaso jyeṣṭhasya devatāviśeṣasya ā sarvataḥ prasṛtaṃ śaṃsaṃ stotraṃ mā vṛkṣi | ahaṃ vicchinnaṃ mā kārṣam || āśinebhyaḥ | aśū vyāptau | bahulam anyatrāpi | u. 2-49 | ity āṇādika [sic] inacpratyayaḥ | cita ity antodāttatvam | yajāma | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | tiṅaś ca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvaraḥ | śaknavāma | śaklṛ śaktau | āḍuttamasya pic ceti tiṅaḥ pittvadbhāvād anudāttatve sati vikaraṇasvaraḥ | nipātair yad yadihanteti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | jyāyasaḥ | praśasyaśabdād īyasuni jya ca | pā. 5-3-61 | iti jyādeśaḥ | jyād ādīyasaḥ | pā. 6-4-160 | itīyasuna īkārasyātvam | nittvād ādyudāttatvam | śaṃsam | halaś ceti ghañ | vṛkṣi | o vraścū chedane | vyatyayenātmanepadottamapuruṣaikavacanam iṭ | cleḥ sic | svaratisūtīty ādinā iḍabhāvaḥ | skoḥ saṃyogādyor ity upadhāsakāralopaḥ | vraścādinā ṣatvam | ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ sīti katvam | ādeśapratyayayor iti ṣatvam | na māṅyoga ity aḍabhāvaḥ || 24 ||

Translation: "In the japa [muttering] that comes before the srugādāpana [as printed; the taking up of the ladle] at the Darśa-pūrṇamāsa, this rik namo mahadbhyaḥ is used; so it is laid down in the section brahmādene prāśiṣyamāṇe: 'sūryo no divaspātu; namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhyaḥ' (Āś. 1-4). Impelled by Agni, Śunaḥśepa praised all the gods (viśvān devān) with this rik. So it is handed down: 'Agni said to him, "Now praise the Viśvedevas; then we shall release you." He praised the Viśvedevas with this rik, namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhyaḥ' (Ai. Brā. 7-16). Mahantaḥ: those greater in qualities; arbhakāḥ: those lesser in qualities; yuvānaḥ: the young; āśinaḥ: those pervaded by age, the old. Adoration to the gods having these four kinds of body, as named. If (yadi) we are able (śaknavāma) — if in some way we may have power by wealth and the like — then (tarhi) we shall worship the gods now (yajāma). O gods! May I not break off (mā vṛkṣi) the praise (śaṃsam) of the elder (jyāyasaḥ) — the foremost — deity, spread on every side: may I not cause it to be interrupted. Āśinebhyaḥ: from aśū vyāptau; the Uṇādi inac by bahulam anyatrāpi (Uṇ. 2-49); end-acute through cit. Yajāma: śap is anudātta since it is pit; and the [tiṅ] too [is anudātta] by the lasārvadhātuka accent, so the root's accent [stands]. Śaknavāma: śaklṛ śaktau; since the tiṅ is treated as pit by āḍuttamasya pic ca and is anudātta, the vikaraṇa's accent [stands]; the lowering is prevented by nipātair yad yadihanta…. Jyāyasaḥ: jya for praśasya before īyasun by P. 5-3-61; ā for the ī of īyasun by P. 6-4-160 [jyād ādīyasaḥ]; first-syllable acute from nit. Śaṃsam: ghañ by halaś ca. Vṛkṣi: o vraścū chedane ['to cut']; the ātmanepada first person singular iṭ by vyatyaya; sic for cli; no iṭ by svaratisūti…; loss of the s of the penultimate by skoḥ saṃyogādyoḥ; ṣ by vraśca…; k by ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si; ṣ by ādeśapratyayayoḥ; no aṭ since joined with mā." Bhāṣya ends ॥ २४ ॥ = Varga 24. Grammar pages 406–408, noted briefly: the words treated are āśinebhyaḥ [aśū vyāptau, svādi, inac by bahulam anyatrāpi (U. sū. 2-20[7?]; the last digit read as 7); dative plural āśinebhyaḥ; end-acute by P. 6-1-163 citaḥ], yajāma [yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, bhvādi; loṭ 1st plural: yajāma; śap is pit and so anudātta; the la-sārvadhātuka is anudātta by P. 6-1-186 tāsyanudāttet… since it follows an adupadeśa; the root's end-acute remains], śaknavāma [śaklṛ śaktau, svādi; loṭ 1st plural mas; its s lost by P. 3-4-99 nityaṃ ṅitaḥ; āṭ by P. 3-4-92 āḍ uttamasya pic ca; śnu by P. 3-1-73 svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ; śak + nu + āma with guṇa and av: śaknavāma; the tiṅ, treated as pit, is anudātta, and by the vikaraṇa's accent the a after n is acute; because yadi precedes, P. 8-1-30 nipātair yad yadihanta… prevents the lowering of the verb], jyāyasaḥ [atiśayena praśasyaḥ: praśasya + īyasun (no number printed); jya substituted for the whole of praśasya (being of more than one letter) by P. 5-3-61 jya ca; the ī of īyas → ā after jya by P. 6-4-160 jyād ādīyasaḥ: jyāyas; genitive singular; first-syllable acute since īyasun is nit, P. 6-1-197], śaṃsam [śaṃsu stutau + ghañ by P. 3-3-121 halaś ca; accusative singular] and vṛkṣi [o vraścū bhedane, tudādi, parasmaipadī; by P. 3-1-85 vyatyayo bahulam the ātmanepada iṭ in the luṅ 1st singular; cli by P. 3-1-43 cli luṅi, sic for it by P. 3-1-44 cleḥ sic; since the root is ūdit, iṭ before the ārdhadhātuka sic is optional by P. 7-2-44 svarati sūti sūyati…, and here not added; the s (from the ś of the cluster) at the beginning of the conjunct lost by P. 8-2-29 skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca; ṣ by P. 8-2-36 vraścabhrasja…; saṃprasāraṇa by the grahijyā sūtra; vṛṣ + s + i; ṣ → k by P. 8-2-41 ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si; the s of sic → ṣ by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: kṣ — vṛkṣi; no aṭ because of mā, P. 6-4-74 na māṅyoge; the tiṅanta lowering]; numerals checked against the print, w3. Printed p. 408, upper part: "The twenty-seventh sūkta is ended" — ippatteḷaneya sūktavu mugidudu.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ महद्भ्यः (mahadbhyaḥ) — to the great gods [those greater in qualities] | नमः (namaḥ) — salutation | अर्भकेभ्यः (arbhakebhyaḥ) — to the small [those lesser in qualities] gods | नमः (namaḥ) — salutation | युवभ्यः (yuvabhyaḥ) — to the young gods | नमः (namaḥ) — salutation | आशिनेभ्यः (āśinebhyaḥ) — to the aged gods | नमः (namaḥ) — salutation | यदि शक्नवाम (yadi śaknavāma) — to the extent we are able | देवान् (devān) — the gods | यजाम (yajāma) — we worship | देवाः (devāḥ) — O gods | ज्यायसः (jyāyasaḥ) — of the elder gods | आ शंसम् (ā śaṃsam) — the praise [made on all sides] | मा वृक्षि (mā vṛkṣi) — I shall not cease [I shall not stop].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ I bow to the gods who are great, to the small ones, to the young and to the aged. As far as we are able, we shall worship the gods. O gods! I shall not stop praising the elder gods in this manner.

॥ English Translation ॥

Adoration to the great gods; adoration to the small gods; adoration to the young and adoration to the old (gods); we worship all the gods as well as we are able; may I not omit the praise of all these great divinities.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ After praying to Agni, Śunaḥśepa, impelled by Agni, prays to the Viśvedevas — that is, to all the gods collectively. On this matter the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says: tam agnir uvāca viśvān nu devān stuhy atha tvotsrakṣyāma iti sa viśvān devāṃs tuṣṭāva namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhya ity etayarcā (Ai. Brā. 7-16).

महद्भ्यः — mahānto guṇair adhikāḥ tebhyaḥ: those greater in qualities or excellence among the gods. अर्भकेभ्यः — those less in qualities (the little ones). युवभ्यः — to the young. आशिनेभ्यः — āśinā vayasā prāptā vṛddhāḥ: those advanced in age, the old. ज्यायसः — the great, the excellent, the endowed with good qualities, or elder in age. मा वृक्षि — o vraścū bhedane; I shall not cause it to be broken off: that is, I shall not stop reciting the praise; I shall go on doing it.

॥ Close of Sūkta 27 ॥ p. 408, upper part: large print "The twenty-seventh sūkta is ended"; the varga number is not given.

॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೆಂಟನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 28 — "yatra grāvā pṛthubudhna ūrdhvo" ("The Twenty-eighth Sūkta"; fifth sūkta of the Sixth Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 408 lower half–437. The introductory note is on the lower half of p. 408 and p. 409, with the heading block on p. 409; Rik 1 begins on p. 410.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note; printed p. 408) re-read from the print, w3

यत्र ग्रावेति पञ्चमं सूक्तं नवर्चम् । आदितः षडनुष्टुभः । आयजी इत्याद्यास्तिस्रो गायत्र्यः । आदितश्चतसृणामिन्द्रो देवता । ततो द्वे उलूखलदेवत्ये । तदनन्तरभाविन्यावुलूखलमुसलोभयदेवताके । अन्त्याया उच्छिष्टमित्यस्या हरिश्चन्द्राधिषवणचर्मसोमानामन्यतमो देवता । तथा च बृहद्देवतायामुक्तम् । चर्माधिषवणीयं वा सोमं वान्त्या प्रशंसति । बृ. ३-४११ । इति । तदुक्तमनुक्रमण्याम् । यत्र ग्रावा नव षळनुष्टुबादि यच्चिद्ध्यूलूखल्यौ परे मौसल्यौ च प्रजापतेर्हरिश्चन्द्रस्यान्त्या चर्मप्रशंसा वेति ॥ आद्याश्चतस्रोऽञ्जःसवे होमे विनियुक्ताः । पञ्चम्याद्याश्चतस्रोऽभिषवणे । अन्त्या द्रोणकलशे सोमावनयने । तथा च ब्राह्मणम् । अथ हैतं शुनःशेपोऽञ्जःसवं ददर्श तमेताभिश्चतसृभिरभिसुषाव यच्चिद्धि त्वं गृहे गृह इत्यथैनं द्रोणकलशमभ्यवनिनायोच्छिष्टं चम्वोर्भरेत्येतयर्चाथ हास्मिन्नन्वारब्धे पूर्वाभिश्चतसृभिः सस्वाहाकाराभिर्जुहवांचकार । ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१७ । इति ॥

yatra grāveti pañcamaṃ sūktaṃ navarcam | āditaḥ ṣaḍ anuṣṭubhaḥ | āyajī ityādyās tisro gāyatryaḥ | āditaś catasṛṇām indro devatā | tato dve ulūkhaladevatye | tadanantarabhāvinyāv ulūkhalamusalobhayadevatāke | antyāyā ucchiṣṭam ity asyā hariścandrādhiṣavaṇacarmasomānām anyatamo devatā | tathā ca bṛhaddevatāyām uktam | carmādhiṣavaṇīyaṃ vā somaṃ vāntyā praśaṃsati | bṛ. 3-411 | iti | taduktam anukramaṇyām | yatra grāvā nava ṣaḷ anuṣṭubādi yac cid dhy ūlūkhalyau pare mausalyau ca prajāpater hariścandrasyāntyā carmapraśaṃsā veti || ādyāś catasro 'ñjaḥsave home viniyuktāḥ | pañcamyādyāś catasro 'bhiṣavaṇe | antyā droṇakalaśe somāvanayane | tathā ca brāhmaṇam | atha haitaṃ śunaḥśepo 'ñjaḥsavaṃ dadarśa tam etābhiś catasṛbhir abhisuṣāva yac cid dhi tvaṃ gṛhe gṛha ity athainaṃ droṇakalaśam abhyavanināyocchiṣṭaṃ camvor bharety etayarcātha hāsminn anvārabdhe pūrvābhiś catasṛbhiḥ sasvāhākārābhir juhavāṃcakāra | ai. brā. 7-17 | iti ||

Translation: "The sūkta yatra grāvā is the fifth [of this anuvāka] and has nine riks. The first six are in Anuṣṭubh; the three beginning āyajī are in Gāyatrī. Of the first four the deity is Indra; then two have the mortar (ulūkhala) as deity; the two that come next have both mortar and pestle (musala); of the last, ucchiṣṭam, the deity is one of these: Hariścandra, the pressing-skin (adhiṣavaṇa-carma) or Soma. So the Bṛhaddevatā says: 'with the last [rik] he praises either the pressing-skin or the Soma' (Bṛ. 3-411 as printed). So also the Anukramaṇikā: 'yatra grāvā, nine, six Anuṣṭubh at the beginning; yac cid dhi, two to the mortar; the next two to the pestle as well; the last, of Prajāpati Hariścandra, is in praise of the skin.' The first four are applied in the homa at the añjaḥsava; the four from the fifth in the pressing; the last at the Droṇakalaśa, in the pouring-down of the Soma. So the Brāhmaṇa: 'Then Śunaḥśepa saw this añjaḥsava; he pressed it with these four; with yac cid dhi tvaṃ gṛhe gṛhe he then poured it down into the Droṇakalaśa; with the rik ucchiṣṭaṃ camvor bhara; then, when [Hariścandra] had taken hold of him, he offered it with the four former [riks] with the svāhā-call' (Ai. Brā. 7-17)." [Translation of the Anukramaṇikā and Brāhmaṇa editorial and tentative.]

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ Yatra grāvā is the fifth sūkta of the sixth anuvāka and has nine riks. The first six riks are in Anuṣṭubh; the three beginning āyajī are in Gāyatrī. The first four riks have Indra as deity; the next two the mortar; the two after that the mortar and the pestle; the last rik has Hariścandra, the adhiṣavaṇa skin, or Soma as deity. The Bṛhaddevatā, a work by Śaunaka, says: carmādhiṣavaṇīyaṃ vā somaṃ vāntyā praśaṃsati (Bṛ. 3-411 as printed); the Anukramaṇikā too says: yatra grāvā nava ṣaḷanuṣṭubādi yac cid dhy ūlūkhalyau pare mausalyau ca prajāpater hariścandrasyāntyā carmapraśaṃsā veti [as printed]. The application of this sūkta is as follows: the first four riks are used in the homa called añjassava; the four from the fifth in the pressing (abhiṣavaṇa); the last rik is used when the Soma-juice is poured into the Droṇakalaśa, the wooden vessel, for the mantras needed. In this connection:

अथ हैतं शुनःशेपोऽञ्जस्सवं ददर्श तमेताभिश्चतसृभिरभिसुषाव यच्चिद्धि त्वं गृहे गृह इत्यथैनं द्रोणकलशमभ्यवनिनायोच्छिष्टं चम्वोर्भरेत्येतयर्चाथ हास्मिन्नन्वारब्धे पूर्वाभिश्चतसृभिः सस्वाहाकाराभिर्जुहवांचकार । ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१७ । इति ।

atha haitaṃ śunaḥśepo 'ñjassavaṃ dadarśa tam etābhiś catasṛbhir abhisuṣāva yac cid dhi tvaṃ gṛhe gṛha ity athainaṃ droṇakalaśam abhyavanināyocchiṣṭaṃ camvor bharety etayarcātha hāsminn anvārabdhe pūrvābhiś catasṛbhiḥ sasvāhākārābhir juhavāṃcakāra | ai. brā. 7-17 | iti | — "Then Śunaḥśepa saw this añjaḥsava; he pressed it with these four [riks]; with yac cid dhi tvaṃ gṛhe gṛhe he then poured it down into the Droṇakalaśa; with the rik ucchiṣṭaṃ camvor bhara …; then, when he had been taken hold of, he offered it with the four former [riks] with the svāhā-call" (editorial and tentative). The Kannada gloss that follows says: "we have explained its meaning in the Śunaḥśepa legend itself."

॥ Heading block of the sūkta (p. 409) ॥

मण्डल १ — अनुवाक ६ — सूक्त २८ । अष्टक १ — अध्याय २ — वर्ग २५, २६ । ऋक्संख्या ९ । ऋषिः — शुनःशेप आजीगर्तिः । देवता — १–४ इन्द्रः । ५–६ उलूखलम् । ७–८ उलूखलमुसले । ९ हरिश्चन्द्र अधिषवणचर्म वा सोमो वा । छन्दः — १–६ अनुष्टुप् । ७–९ गायत्री ।

Maṇḍala 1 — Anuvāka 6 — Sūkta 28. Aṣṭaka 1 — Adhyāya 2 — Varga 25, 26. Riks: 9. Ṛṣi: Śunaḥśepa Ājīgarti. Devatā: 1–4 Indra; 5–6 the Mortar; 7–8 the Mortar and the Pestle; 9 Hariścandra, or the pressing-skin, or Soma. Metre: 1–6 Anuṣṭubh; 7–9 Gāyatrī. Varga numerals read from the print, w3.

Rik 1 pp. 410–416

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

यत्र॒ ग्रावा॑ पृ॒थुबु॑ध्न ऊ॒र्ध्वो भव॑ति॒ सोत॑वे । उ॒लूख॑लसुताना॒मवेद्वि॑न्द्र जल्गुलः ॥ १ ॥ [accent ?]

yátra grā́vā pṛthúbudhna ūrdhvó bhávati sótave | ulū́khalasutānām ávéd vindra jalgulaḥ || 1 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: line 2 has no bar under वे and the stroke stands over द्वि, not over न्द्र; Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

यत्र । ग्रावा । पृथुऽबुध्नः । ऊर्ध्वः । भवति । सोतवे ॥ उलूखलऽसुतानाम् । अव । इत् । ऊं इति । इन्द्र । जल्गुलः ॥ १ ॥

yatra | grāvā | pṛthu-budhnaḥ | ūrdhvaḥ | bhavati | sotave || ulūkhala-sutānām | ava | it | ūṃ iti | indra | jalgulaḥ || 1 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र यत्र यस्मिन्नञ्जःसवे कर्मणि सोतवेऽभिषवार्थं ग्रावा पाषाणः पृथुबुध्नः स्थूलमूल ऊर्ध्व उन्नतो भवति तस्मिन्कर्मण्युलूखलसुतानामुलूखलेनाभिषुतानां रसमवेत् स्वकीयत्वेनावगत्यैव जल्गुलः । भक्षय ॥ पृथुबुध्नः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । भवति । निपातैर्यद्यदिहन्तेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । सोतवे । षुञ् अभिषवे । तुमर्थे सेसेनिति तवेन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । उलूखलसुतानाम् । उलूखलेन सुतानाम् । तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । जल्गुलः । गल अदने । अस्माद्यङो लुकि लेण्मध्यमैकवचने लेटोऽडाटाविति अडागमः । इतश्च लोप इतीकारलोपः । उपधायाः उत्त्वं च हलादिशेषाभावश्च पृषोदरादित्वात् ॥

he indra yatra yasminn añjaḥsave karmaṇi sotave 'bhiṣavārthaṃ grāvā pāṣāṇaḥ pṛthubudhnaḥ sthūlamūla ūrdhva unnato bhavati tasmin karmaṇy ulūkhalasutānām ulūkhalenābhiṣutānāṃ rasam aved svakīyatvenāvagatyaiva jalgulaḥ | bhakṣaya || pṛthubudhnaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | bhavati | nipātair yad yadihanteti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | sotave | ṣuñ abhiṣave | tumarthe sesen iti tavenpratyayaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttatvam | ulūkhalasutānām | ulūkhalena sutānām | tṛtīyā karmaṇīti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | jalgulaḥ | gala adane | asmād yaṅo luki leṇmadhyamaikavacane leṭo 'ḍāṭāv iti aḍāgamaḥ | itaś ca lopa itīkāralopaḥ | upadhāyāḥ utvaṃ ca halādiśeṣābhāvaś ca pṛṣodarāditvāt ||

Translation: "O Indra! In the rite in which (yatra) the grāvan — the pressing stone — pṛthubudhnaḥ (broad at the base) ūrdhvaḥ bhavati — is raised up — for pressing (sotave): in that rite, ulūkhalasutānām — of the juices pressed in the mortar — know (ava it, 'know indeed') the juice [to be] your own and partake (jalgulaḥ, eat/drink). Pṛthubudhnaḥ: bahuvrīhi, the first member's accent. Bhavati: the lowering of the verb is prevented by nipātair yad yadi… because yatra precedes. Sotave: ṣuñ abhiṣave; tavenn in the infinitive sense; first-syllable acute by nit. Ulūkhalasutānām: 'pressed with the mortar'; the third-case compound with a kṛdanta [sutānām] takes the first member's accent by P. 6-2-48. Jalgulaḥ: gala adane ['to swallow']; yaṅ-luk; leṭ, 2nd singular, with the aṭ augment; loss of the i; the u for the penultimate and the absence of halādiḥ śeṣa are by the pṛṣodarādi rule." Grammar pages 415–416, noted briefly: the words treated are pṛthubudhnaḥ [bahuvrīhi; first member's accent, P. 6-2-1], bhavati [bhū sattāyām, laṭ 3rd singular; since yatra precedes, the lowering is prevented by P. 8-1-30 nipātair yad yadi…], sotave [ṣuñ abhiṣave; taven by P. 3-4-9 tumarthe sesen…; the ṣ of the root becomes s by P. 6-1-64 dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; guṇa by P. 7-3-84; first-syllable acute since taven is nit, P. 6-1-197], ulūkhalasutānām [ulūkhalena sutāḥ; P. 6-1-223 samāsasya would give the end-acute, but since a kta in the passive sense follows, the instrumental first member keeps its accent by P. 6-2-48 tṛtīyā karmaṇi; the u is acute] and jalgulaḥ [gala adane, curādi [as printed]; yaṅ in the sense of intensity, lost by P. 2-4-74 yaṅo 'ci ca; the name dhātu by P. 3-1-32 sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; leṭ 2nd singular sip; its i lost by P. 3-4-97 itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu; aṭ by P. 3-4-94 leṭo 'ḍāṭau; doubling by P. 6-1-9 sanyaṅoḥ; the loss due by P. 7-4-60 halādiḥ śeṣaḥ does not take place, and the penultimate a becomes u, both by P. 6-3-109 pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam; jalgulas, ru-visarga: jalgulaḥ; the verb is lowered]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | यत्र (yatra) — in which sacrificial rite | सोतवे (sotave) — for pressing | पृथुबुध्नः (pṛthubudhnaḥ) — broad at the base | ग्रावा (grāvā) — the stone | ऊर्ध्वः भवति (ūrdhvaḥ bhavati) — stands raised up [in that rite] | उलूखलसुतानाम् (ulūkhalasutānām) — of the [soma] pressed in the mortar | अवेत् उ (aved u) — know [it to be] yours | जल्गुलः (jalgulaḥ) — partake.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Indra! In the sacrificial rite in which the broad-based stone is lifted up in order to crush the soma-creeper, [do you], knowing that the soma-juice pressed in the mortar in that rite is prepared for you alone, partake of it.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

Indra, in the sacrifice in which flat-bottomed stone is raised to press the Soma-juice, partake of that Soma expressed in the mortar.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Chief sense. O Indra! In this sacrifice the soma-creeper is placed in the mortar, and a broad-based stone is raised in the hand for crushing it, and the juice is taken; know that the soma-juice thus crushed and standing here is prepared for you alone; accept it, that is, drink it, and be satisfied.

The preparation of the soma-juice (summary of the author's long note, pp. 411–413). In the Soma-yāga it is customary to crush, press and strain the soma-creeper with a stone, mix with it milk, curds and barley, offer it to the gods, and then for the priests and the sacrificer to drink the rest. This is done on the chief days in the morning, at midday and in the evening — the prātaḥsavana, mādhyandinasavana and tṛtīyasavana — the pressing being called abhiṣavaṇa, savana. The soma-creeper is no longer found nowadays; formerly it grew on river banks and on the mountains and was brought, at great cost, for sacrificial use; even now the rite of somakrayaṇa ('buying the soma') is performed. The creeper is brown (babhru), ruddy (aruṇa), or yellow-brown; it was brought chiefly from the mountains, the mountain called Mūjavat being famous for it. Its shoot is called aṃśa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-168-3; 3-48-2, etc.); the shoot with sprouts vakṣaṇā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-1-17) and vāṇa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-24-9; 9-50-1); the juice andhaḥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-28-7; 3-48-1; 4-16-1); the stalk parvan (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-9-1). These references were omitted in the first version and are restored from the print, w3. The mortar in which it is crushed is the ulūkhala; the stone for pounding is the grāvan (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-83-6; 1-135-7) or adri (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-2; 1-135-5; 1-137-1); the vessel in which it is offered to the gods is camū; the vessels for the priests' drinking are kalaśa and camasa; in some places camū stands for the mortar and the pounding stone, 'mortar and pestle' (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-28-9; 4-18-3; 6-57-2); the skin (tvak) on which it is pounded is of ox-hide (gocarma) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-9; 10-116-4); the vessels for collecting the juice are kośa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-101-4; 8-20-8), sadastha (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-62-15; 9-1-2; 9-17-8), dru (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-1-2; 9-65-6; 9-98-2), vana (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-9; 9-66-9), droṇa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-15-7; 9-33-2); the ladle is sruva (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-24); the cloth or net for straining is pavitra, and sometimes the soma was strained through the gaps of the fingers; the juice used unmixed is called śukra (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-137-1; 3-32-2; 8-2-10) or śuci (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-5-5; 1-30-2; 8-2-9), and, according to colour, babhru (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-33-2; 9-63-4 & 6), harita (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-3-9; 9-7-6; 9-65-8), aruṇa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-40-2; 9-45-3), aruṣa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-61-21), śoṇa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-97-13); it is also fragrant (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-97-9; 9-107-2). To give the juice a taste, milk is mixed (gavāśira), curds (dadhyāśira), barley (yavāśira); the residue after pressing is ṛjīṣa.

ग्रावा — the stone for crushing the soma: here it is described as pṛthubudhna, a stone with a broad base — like the round pounding stone in a stone mill. पृथुबुध्नः — sthūlamūla ūrdhva unnataḥ: broad at the base; a stone that is round like a grindstone. ऊर्ध्वो भवति सोतवे — to lift the stone up in the hand to crush the creeper — when it is necessary to pound the creeper placed in the mortar or on the stone, another stone is held and brought down: this is what is said here. उलूखलसुतानाम् — the ulūkhala is the mortar, a stone in the middle of which there is a hollow, the vessel to receive the creeper pounded and its juice. On the word ulūkhala Yāska says:

उलूखलम् । उलूखलमुरुकरं वोर्ध्वखं वोर्क्करं वोरु मे कुर्वित्यब्रवीत्तदुलूखलमभवत् । उरुकरं वैतत्तदुलूखलमित्याचक्षते परोक्षेणेति ब्राह्मणम् ॥ (नि. ९-२०)

ulūkhalam | ulūkhalam urukaraṃ vordhvakhaṃ vorkkaraṃ voru me kurv ity abravīt tad ulūkhalam abhavat | urukaraṃ vaitat tad ulūkhalam ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇeti brāhmaṇam || (ni. 9-20) — "Ulūkhala: either urukara, 'making much [food]'; or ūrdhvakha, 'a hollow that is upright'; or ūrkkara, 'making sap' [ūrj]; or, 'he said: "Make much for me!" [uru me kuru], and that became the ulūkhala'; 'this is indeed urukara; they call it ulūkhala indirectly' — so the Brāhmaṇa." The Kannada exposition follows: the l is for r, so urukhara/urukara; the grain placed in it and pounded with the pestle gives much food; or the one on which the creeper is crushed gives the juice; and so on.

The Taittirīya Saṃhitā lists ten sacrificial implements:

यो वै दश यज्ञायुधानि वेद मुखतोऽस्य यज्ञः कल्पते । स्फ्यश्च कपालानि चाग्निहोत्रहवणी च शूर्पं च कृष्णाजिनं च शम्या चोलूखलं च मुसलं च दृषच्चोपला चैतानि वै दश यज्ञायुधानि य एवं वेद मुखतोऽस्य यज्ञः कल्पते ॥ (तै. सं. १-६-८)

yo vai daśa yajñāyudhāni veda mukhato 'sya yajñaḥ kalpate | sphyaś ca kapālāni cāgnihotrahavaṇī ca śūrpaṃ ca kṛṣṇājinaṃ ca śamyā colūkhalaṃ ca musalaṃ ca dṛṣac copalā caitāni vai daśa yajñāyudhāni ya evaṃ veda mukhato 'sya yajñaḥ kalpate || — "He who knows the ten sacrificial weapons — for him the sacrifice is arranged from the very start: the sphya (wooden sword), the kapālas (potsherds), the agnihotra-havaṇī (ladle), the śūrpa (winnowing-basket), the black antelope skin, the śamyā (peg), the mortar, the pestle, the dṛṣad (lower stone) and the upalā (upper stone). These are the ten weapons of the sacrifice; for him who knows thus the sacrifice is arranged from the very start." Tai. Saṃ. 1-6-8. The author then explains each: the sphya is a wooden sword for cutting darbha and the like; the kapālas are the potsherds on which the puroḍāśa cake is baked; the agnihotra-havaṇī is a wooden ladle-like vessel for the agnihotra oblation; the śūrpa is the winnowing basket; the kṛṣṇājina is the black antelope-skin on which the pounding is done; the śamyā is the peg used for killing the animal; the ulūkhala, the mortar, is for pounding grain and pressing soma; the musala, pestle, for pounding grain; the dṛṣad is the lower stone on which soma is pounded, or a stone slab; the upalā is the pebble stone used to crush what is placed on the dṛṣad. Of these ten implements, the mortar is one.

अव इत् — avagatyaiva: knowing; i.e. 'knowing that the soma-juice pressed in the mortar is prepared for you'. The commentator gives ava the sense avagamanārtha ('knowing'). Skandasvāmin takes ava and it as prepositions to be joined with the verb, and glosses ava it jalgulaḥ as punar punar avagira pibety arthaḥ — 'swallow again and again; drink'. जल्गुलः — gala adane; bhakṣaya: eat, drink — 'knowing that the juice of the soma-creeper pressed in the mortar is prepared for you alone, drink it'.

Rik 2 pp. 416–419

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

यत्र॒ द्वावि॑व ज॒घना॑धिषव॒ण्या॑ कृ॒ता । उ॒लूख॑लसुताना॒मवेद्वि॑न्द्र जल्गुलः ॥ २ ॥ [accent ?]

yátra dvā́v iva jaghánādhiṣavaṇyā kṛtā́ | ulū́khalasutānām ávéd vindra jalgulaḥ || 2 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: in line 2 the stroke stands over द्वि (a doubled mark there), as in Ṛk 1; Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

यत्र । द्वौऽइव । जघना । अधिऽसवन्या । कृता ॥ उलूखलऽसुतानाम् । अव । इत् । ऊं इति । इन्द्र । जल्गुलः ॥ २ ॥

yatra | dvau-iva | jaghanā | adhi-savanyā | kṛtā || ulūkhala-sutānām | ava | it | ūṃ iti | indra | jalgulaḥ || 2 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

यत्र यस्मिन्कर्मण्यधिषवण्या उभे अधिषवणफलके द्वाविव जघना द्वौ जघनप्रदेशाविव । जघनं जंघन्यतेरिति यास्कः । नि. ९-२० । कृता विस्तीर्णे कृते संपादिते । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ जघना । हन्तेः शरीरावयवे द्वे च । उ. ५-३२ । इति हन्धातोरच् । द्वित्वम् । कर्दमादित्वान्मध्योदात्तः । फि. ३-१० । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । अधिषवण्या । षुञ् अभिषवे । ल्युट् । भवे छन्दसीति यत् । उपसर्गात्सुनोतीति षत्वम् । तित्स्वरित इति स्वरितः । न च यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । तत्र हि निष्ठा च द्व्यजनात् । पा. ६-१-२०५ । इत्यस्यानुवृत्तेर्द्व्यच्कस्यैव तदिति । कृता । पूर्ववदाकारः ॥

yatra yasminkarmaṇyadhiṣavaṇyā ubhe adhiṣavaṇaphalake dvāviva jaghanā dvau jaghanapradeśāviva | jaghanaṃ jaṃghanyateriti yāskaḥ | ni. 9-20 | kṛtā vistīrṇe kṛte saṃpādite | anyatpūrvavat ‖ jaghanā | hanteḥ śarīrāvayave dve ca | u. 5-32 | iti handhātorac | dvitvam | kardamāditvānmadhyodāttaḥ | phi. 3-10 | supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | adhiṣavaṇyā | ṣuñ abhiṣave | lyuṭ | bhave chandasīti yat | upasargātsunotīti ṣatvam | titsvarita iti svaritaḥ | na ca yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvam | tatra hi niṣṭhā ca dvyajanāt | pā. 6-1-205 | ityasyānuvṛtterdvyackasyaiva taditi | kṛtā | pūrvavadākāraḥ ‖

Translation: "In the rite in which the two adhiṣavaṇyā — the two pressing-boards — are made (kṛtā) wide, as if two hips (dvāv iva jaghanā), the two hip-regions — [jaghana is by Yāska 'jaṅghanyate' (Ni. 9-20)] — [do you, Indra,] know and partake of the juice pressed in the mortar. The rest is as before. Jaghanā: from han with ac and doubling in the sense of 'a body-part' (U. 5-32); middle acute as a kardamādi word (Phi. 3-10); ā for the dual ending by supāṃ suluk. Adhiṣavaṇyā: from ṣuñ abhiṣave with lyuṭ; yat by bhave chandasi; ṣatva after the preposition; the svarita by tit svaritam; the initial acute of yato 'nāvaḥ does not apply, since there P. 6-1-205 (niṣṭhā ca dvyaj anāt) continues, so that rule holds only for words of two syllables. Kṛtā: ā as before." Grammar pages 418–419, noted briefly: the words treated are jaghanā [han + ac by U. sū. 5-710 (as printed; haner…); doubling; h → gh by P. 7-3-55; dual au → ā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ suluk; middle acute by Phi. sū. 59 kardamādīnāṃ ca] and adhiṣavaṇyā [ṣuñ abhiṣave + lyuṭ; yu → ana by P. 7-1-1; yat by P. 4-4-110 bhave chandasi; loss of a by P. 6-4-148; ṣatva by P. 8-3-65; ṇatva by P. 8-4-2; svarita by P. 6-1-185 tit svaritam; P. 6-1-213 yato 'nāvaḥ excluded by P. 6-1-205]; numerals as printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | यत्र (yatra) — in which rite | द्वौ जघनौ इव (dvau jaghanau iva) — like two hips | अधिषवण्या (adhiṣavaṇyā) — the two pressing-boards | कृता (kṛtā) — are made [widely spread] | उलूखलसुतानाम् (ulūkhalasutānām) — of the [juice] pressed in the mortar | अवेत् उ (aved u) — know [it to be yours] | जल्गुलः (jalgulaḥ) — partake.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Indra! In the sacrificial rite in which the two pressing-boards are spread out wide like two hips, take the soma-juice pressed in the mortar — knowing it to be prepared for you alone.

॥ English Translation ॥

Where, Indra, the two halves (or platters) of the Soma-press are placed close together like the broad hips of a woman, partake of that Soma expressed in the mortar.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ जघना अधिषवण्या — jaghanā means the two hip-regions of women, the upper parts of the thighs; they are by nature broad and fleshy. Adhiṣavaṇa means the wooden boards [vessels] for filling with soma-juice; they are as big as hips — that is, they hold much juice. Or the hip-regions touch each other when close; so when the juice is taken, the two boards, rubbing against each other, press the soma and take the juice: that is the intention. On this occasion adhiṣavaṇa means the two wooden boards used for pressing out the soma-juice. Between the ends of these boards the soma-creeper is placed, and the juice is pressed out. The seer compares the rubbing of these boards with the hip-regions of a woman. Or, as the commentator explains, the adhiṣavaṇa means the large wooden vessels used for filling with the pressed soma; these, like women's hips, are large and hold much juice — that is the chief intention. [Rik 2, grammar tail — printed p. 419] Grammar, noted briefly: the last word treated is kṛtā [ḍukṛñ karaṇe + kta; the dual ending is replaced by ā by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ suluk…]; numerals as printed.

Rik 3 pp. 419–421

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

यत्र॒ नार्य॑प॒च्यव॑मुप॒च्यवं॑ च॒ शिक्षते । उ॒लूख॑लसुताना॒मवेद्वि॑न्द्र जल्गुलः ॥ ३ ॥ [accent ?]

yátra nā́ry apacyávam upacyávaṃ ca śíkṣate | ulū́khalasutānām ávéd vindra jalgulaḥ || 3 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: in line 1 the stroke stands between ना and र्य (read as over र्य); line 2 printed as in Ṛk 1 (stroke over द्वि); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

यत्र । नारी । अपऽच्यवम् । उपऽच्यवम् । च । शिक्षते ॥ उलूखलऽसुतानाम् । अव । इत् । ऊं इति । इन्द्र । जल्गुलः ॥ ३ ॥

yatra | nārī | apa-cyavam | upa-cyavam | ca | śikṣate || ulūkhala-sutānām | ava | it | ūṃ iti | indra | jalgulaḥ || 3 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

यत्र यस्मिन्कर्मणि नारी पत्न्यपच्यवं शालाया निर्गमनमुपच्यवं च शालाप्राप्तिं च शिक्षते अभ्यासं करोति । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ अपच्यवम् । च्युङ् गतौ । ऊदोरबित्यप् । गुणावादेशौ । थाथादिना । पा. ६-२-१४४ । उत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । एवमुपच्यवम् । शिक्षते । शिक्ष विद्योपादाने । आदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । निपातैर्यद्यदिहन्तेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥

yatra yasmin karmaṇi nārī patny apacyavaṃ śālāyā nirgamanam upacyavaṃ ca śālāprāptiṃ ca śikṣate abhyāsaṃ karoti | anyat pūrvavat || apacyavam | cyuṅ gatau | ūdor ab ity ap | guṇāvādeśau | thāthādinā | pā. 6-2-144 | uttarapadāntodāttatvam | evam upacyavam | śikṣate | śikṣa vidyopādāne | ādupadeśāl lasārvadhātukānudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ | nipātair yad yadihanteti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ ||

Translation: "In the rite in which (yatra) the nārī — the [sacrificer's] wife — practises (śikṣate) the apacyavam — going out of the hall — and the upacyavam — coming back into the hall; the rest as before. Apacyavam: cyuṅ gatau; ap [by the sūtra beginning ūdor ap]; guṇa and av; by the thāthādi rule (P. 6-2-144) the end-acute of the second member. So also upacyavam. Śikṣate: śikṣa vidyopādāne; the root accent. The verb is not lowered since it follows yatra." Grammar pages 420–421, noted briefly: the words treated are apacyavam [cyuṅ gatau, bhvādi, with apa + ap by P. 3-3-57 ūdor ap; guṇa → cyav; the end-acute of the kṛdanta second member by P. 6-2-144 thāthaghañktājabitrakāṇām], upacyavam [as above, with the preposition upa] and śikṣate [śikṣa vidyopādāne, bhvādi; laṭ 3rd singular; śap anudātta as pit; after an ād-upadeśa root the lasārvadhātuka ending is anudātta by P. 6-1-186 tāsyanudāttet…, so the root accent remains; the lowering of the verb is prevented by yatra, P. 8-1-30]; numerals as printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | यत्र (yatra) — in which rite | नारी (nārī) — the wife [of the sacrificer] | अपच्यवम् (apacyavam) — going out of the sacrificial hall | उपच्यवं च (upacyavaṃ ca) — and coming into the hall | शिक्षते (śikṣate) — practises | उलूखलसुतानाम् (ulūkhalasutānām) — of the soma pressed in the mortar | अवेत् उ (aved u) — know [it to be yours] | जल्गुलः (jalgulaḥ) — partake.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Indra! In the sacrificial rite in which the sacrificer's wife keeps going out of the hall and coming back in, partake of the soma pressed in the mortar, knowing it is prepared for you alone.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra, in the sacrifice in which the wife of the sacrificer, every now and then enters and goes out of the sacrificial chamber, partake of that Soma expressed in the mortar.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ In the sacrifice, the women — the sacrificer's wife and the others — come and go frequently; the seer describes the sacrificial hall as adorned with such comings and goings. अपच्यवम् उपच्यवम् — cyuṅ gatau: the sense of these words, formed from the root with the prefixes apa and upa, is respectively 'going out' and 'coming in'. शिक्षते — since the women's comings and goings are repeated, the seer uses the word śikṣate, which here has the sense of repetition (abhyāsa).

Rik 4 pp. 421–423

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

यत्र॒ मन्थां॑ विब॒ध्नते रश्मी॑न्यमि॒तवा इ॑व । उ॒लूख॑लसुताना॒मवेद्वि॑न्द्र जल्गुलः ॥ ४ ॥ [accent ?]

yátra mánthāṃ vibadhnate ráśmīn yamitávā iva | ulū́khalasutānām ávéd vindra jalgulaḥ || 4 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: line 1 shows no bar under वि of विबध्नते or under य of यमितवा and the stroke stands over इ of इव; line 2 printed as in Ṛk 1 (stroke over द्वि); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

यत्र । मन्थाम् । विऽबध्नते । रश्मीन् । यमितवै । इव ॥ उलूखलऽसुतानाम् । अव । इत् । ऊं इति । इन्द्र । जल्गुलः ॥ ४ ॥

yatra | manthām | vi-badhnate | raśmīn | yamitavai | iva || ulūkhala-sutānām | ava | it | ūṃ iti | indra | jalgulaḥ || 4 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

यत्र यस्मिन्कर्मणि मंथामाशिरमथनहेतुं मन्थानं विबध्नन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । रश्मीनश्वबन्धनार्थान्प्रग्रहान्यमितवा इव । नियन्तुमिव । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ मंथाम् । पथिमथ्यृभुक्षामात् । ७-१-८५ । इति द्वितीयायामपि व्यत्ययेनात्वम् । प्रातिपदिकस्वराणामन्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते पथिमथोः सर्वनामस्थाने । पा. ६-१-१९९ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । यद्वा । मथ्यतेऽनेनेति मन्था । मथि विलोडन इत्यस्माद्धलश्चेति करणे घञ् । ततष्टाप् । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । विबध्नते । बन्ध बन्धने । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । अनिदितामिति नलोपे श्नाभ्यस्तयोरात इत्याकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । तिङि चोदात्तवतीति गतेर्निघातः । यमितवै । यम उपरमे । तुमर्थे सेसेनिति तवैप्रत्ययः । इडागमश्छान्दसः । यद्वा । ण्यन्तात्तवैप्रत्ययस्येडागमे सति णिलोपश्छान्दसः । अन्तश्च तवै युगपत् । पा. ६-१-२०० । इत्याद्यन्तयोरुदात्तत्वम् ॥

yatra yasmin karmaṇi manthām āśiramathanahetuṃ manthānaṃ vibadhnanti | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | raśmīn aśvabandhanārthān pragrahān yamitavā iva | niyantum iva | anyat pūrvavat || maṃthām | pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt | 7-1-85 | iti dvitīyāyām api vyatyayenātvam | prātipadikasvarāṇām antodāttatve prāpte pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne | pā. 6-1-199 | ity ādyudāttatvam | yadvā | mathyate 'neneti manthā | mathi viloḍana ity asmād dhalaś ceti karaṇe ghañ | tataṣ ṭāp | ñitvād ādyudāttatvam | vibadhnate | bandha bandhane | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | aniditām iti nalope śnābhyastayor āta ity ākāralopaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | tiṅi codāttavatīti gater nighātaḥ | yamitavai | yama uparame | tumarthe sesen iti tavaipratyayaḥ | iḍāgamaś chāndasaḥ | yadvā | ṇyantāt tavaipratyayasyeḍāgame sati ṇilopaś chāndasaḥ | antaś ca tavai yugapat | pā. 6-1-200 | ity ādyantayor udāttatvam ||

Translation: "In the rite in which (yatra) they tie up (vibadhnate) the manthā — the churning-stick, the means of churning the āśīr [mixed milk] — like [a rider who ties] the reins (raśmīn) yamitavai iva — to restrain [the horse]; the rest as before. Maṃthām: [mathin + accusative with] ā by vyatyaya [7-1-85 pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt]; the end-acute of the stem would be expected, but by P. 6-1-199 the first-syllable acute. Or: manthā is 'that by which one churns', mathi viloḍane with ghañ in the sense of instrument; ṭāp; first-syllable acute by ñit. Vibadhnate: bandha bandhane; śnā of the kryādi class; loss of the nasal and of ā of śnā; the suffix's accent; vi is lowered by P. 8-1-71. Yamitavai: yama uparame; the infinitive tavai; the iṭ augment is Vedic; both the first and the last syllable are acute by P. 6-1-200." Grammar pages 422–423, noted briefly: the words treated are maṃthām [mathin: the accusative singular with ā in the stem by P. 7-1-85 pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt; i → a by P. 7-1-86 ito 't sarvanāmasthāne; th → nth by P. 7-1-87 before the strong endings; ā + am → ām by P. 6-1-107; the first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-199 pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne; alternatively mathi viloḍane + ghañ by P. 3-3-121 halaś ca, with num [idito num dhātoḥ] and ṭāp — manthā; ñit gives the first-syllable acute], vibadhnate [bandha bandhane, kryādi; laṭ 3rd plural jha → ate by P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere (te); śnā by P. 3-1-81 kryādibhyaḥ śnā; śnā, with its ā lost by P. 6-4-112 śnābhyastayor ātaḥ; the nasal of the root lost by P. 6-4-24; śnā is śit and anudātta, but the suffix accent remains; vi is lowered by P. 8-1-71 tiṅi codāttavati] and yamitavai [yamu uparame, bhvādi; the infinitive tavai by P. 3-4-9; iṭ augment by chandasi; alternatively ṇic + tavai with iṭ and the Vedic loss of ṇic; P. 6-1-200 tavai cāntaś ca yugapat gives the acute on the first and last syllables: ya and vai]; numerals as printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | यत्र (yatra) — in which rite | रश्मीन् (raśmīn) — the reins | यमितवै इव (yamitavai iva) — [as one ties] to restrain [a horse] | मन्थाम् (manthām) — the churning staff | विबध्नते (vibadhnate) — they tie with ropes | उलूखलसुतानाम् (ulūkhalasutānām) — of the juice pressed in the mortar | अवेत् उ (aved u) — know [it as yours] | जल्गुलः (jalgulaḥ) — partake.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Indra! In the sacrificial rite in which they tie a rope round the churning-staff, as one ties reins to hold back a horse, know that the soma-juice pressed in the mortar in that rite is prepared for you alone, and partake of it.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra, where they bind the churning staff with ropes like reins to restrain (a horse), partake of that Soma expressed in the mortar.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ In this rik the seer describes the process of churning butter with a churning-stick and rope, in which the rope round the churning-stick is compared to the reins tied to a horse. The reins tied to a horse let it go no further than the driver wishes; so the rope fixed to the churning-staff makes it work under control. The seer thus describes the sacrifice as adorned with works of churning and the like. मन्थाम् — mathi viloḍane; mathnāty anena iti manthā: the churning-staff used for churning. रश्मीन् यमितवा इव — here the word aśva is not stated, but to complete the sense the commentator explains 'as one ties the reins of a horse'. Though raśanā means a rope, how the word raśmi got this sense the commentator does not explain.

Rik 5 pp. 424–426

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

यच्चि॒द्धि त्वं गृ॒हेगृ॑ह॒ उलू॑खलक यु॒ज्यसे । इ॒ह द्यु॒मत्त॑मं वद॒ जय॑तामिव दुन्दु॒भिः ॥ ५ ॥ [accent ?]

yac ciddhí tvaṃ gṛhégṛha úlūkhalaka yujyáse | ihá dyumáttamaṃ vada jáyatām iva dundubhíḥ || 5 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: no bar is seen under उ of उलूखलक (the stroke stands over लू), and the bar in दुन्दुभिः stands under the second दु; Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

यत् । चित् । हि । त्वम् । गृहेऽगृहे । उलूखलक । युज्यसे ॥ इह । द्युमत्ऽतमम् । वद । जयताम्ऽइव । दुन्दुभिः ॥ ५ ॥

yat | cit | hi | tvam | gṛhe-gṛhe | ulūkhalaka | yujyase || iha | dyumat-tamam | vada | jayatām-iva | dundubhiḥ || 5 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे उलूखलक यच्चिद्धि यद्यपि त्वमवघाताथं गृहे गृहे युज्यसे तथापीह वैदिके कर्मणि तीव्रमुसलप्रहारेण द्युमत्तमममतिशयेन दीप्तं प्रभूतध्वनियुक्तं शब्दं वद । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । जयतामिव दुन्दुभिः । यथा युद्धे जयं प्राप्नुवतां राज्ञां दुन्दुभिर्महान्तं ध्वनिं करोति तद्वत् । उलूखलशब्दं यास्क एवं व्याख्यातवान् । उलूखलमुरुकरं वोर्ध्वखं वोर्ककरं वोरु मे कुर्विति वाब्रवीत्तदुलूखलमभवदुरुकरं वै तत्तदुलूखलमित्याचक्षते परोक्षेणेति च ब्राह्मणम् । नि. ९-२० । इति ॥ उलूखलक । आपादादाविति पर्युदासादाष्टमिकनिघाताभावे षाष्ठिकमाद्युदात्तत्वम् । युज्यसे । आदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे यक्स्वरः शिष्यते । न च तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । निपातैर्यद्यदिहन्तेति प्रतिषेधात् । द्युमत्तमम् । दीप्त्यर्थस्य संपदादिलक्षणः क्विप् । दिव उत् । पा. ६-१-१३१ । इत्युत्त्वम् । यणादेशे । ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुबित मतुप उदात्तत्वम् । ननु दिव उदित्यत्र प्रातिपदिकं गृह्यते न धातुरित्युक्तत्वात् । अक्षद्यूरित्यादाविवात्राप्यूठा भवितव्यम् । पा. ६-४-१९ । एवं तर्हि दीप्तिमत्स्वर्गवाचकेन दिव्प्रातिपदिकेन दीप्तिर्लक्ष्यत इत्युत्त्वं भविष्यति ॥

he ulūkhalaka yac cid dhi yady api tvam avaghātārthaṃ gṛhe gṛhe yujyase tathāpīha vaidike karmaṇi tīvramusalaprahāreṇa dyumattamam atiśayena dīptaṃ prabhūtadhvaniyuktaṃ śabdaṃ vada | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | jayatām iva dundubhiḥ | yathā yuddhe jayaṃ prāpnuvatāṃ rājñāṃ dundubhir mahāntaṃ dhvaniṃ karoti tadvat | ulūkhalaśabdaṃ yāska evaṃ vyākhyātavān | ulūkhalam urukaraṃ vordhvakhaṃ vorkakaraṃ voru me kurv iti vābravīt tad ulūkhalam abhavad urukaraṃ vai tat tad ulūkhalam ity ācakṣate parokṣeṇeti ca brāhmaṇam | ni. 9-20 | iti || ulūkhalaka | āpādādāv iti paryudāsād āṣṭamikanighātābhāve ṣāṣṭhikam ādyudāttatvam | yujyase | ādupadeśāl lasārvadhātukānudāttatve yaksvaraḥ śiṣyate | na ca tiṅ atiṅa iti nighātaḥ | nipātair yad yadihanteti pratiṣedhāt | dyumattamam | dīptyarthasya saṃpadādilakṣaṇaḥ kvip | diva ut | pā. 6-1-131 | ity uttvam | yaṇādeśe | hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matub iti matupa udāttatvam | nanu diva ud ity atra prātipadikaṃ gṛhyate na dhātur ity uktatvāt | akṣadyūr ityādāv ivātrāpy ūṭhā bhavitavyam | pā. 6-4-19 | evaṃ tarhi dīptimatsvargavācakena divprātipadikena dīptir lakṣyata ity uttvaṃ bhaviṣyati ||

Translation: "O ulūkhalaka — dear mortar! Although (yac cid dhi) you are employed in every house for pounding [grain], yet here, in this Vedic rite, with the sharp strokes of the pestle, utter (vada) a sound dyumattamam — most brilliant, exceedingly bright, with a great noise. An illustration: jayatām iva dundubhiḥ — as, in war, the drum of kings who have won the victory makes a great sound. Yāska has explained the word ulūkhala thus [the same passage as under Rik 1]. Ulūkhalaka: the first-syllable acute [vocative]; since the sūtra apādādau excludes ... the lowering does not apply. Yujyase: the yak accent remains; no lowering since the yat-type particle precedes. Dyumattamam: kvip of the saṃpadādi class for the sense 'to shine'; ut for div by P. 6-1-131; y by yaṇ ...; matup is acute by [hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup]; But it was said that in diva ut the stem, not the root, is meant; then, as in akṣadyūḥ, ūṭh (P. 6-4-19) would be due here too. Answer: the stem div, meaning the shining heaven, here indicates (by lakṣaṇā) shining, so the ut holds." Grammar pages 426, noted briefly: the words treated are ulūkhalaka [the vocative singular: since the sūtra āpādādau forbids the lowering at the beginning of the pāda... the word ulūkhalaka has the vocative āmantrita status, but being at the head of the line it is not lowered; the suffix ka gives the middle acute; ū is acute], yujyase [yuja samādhau, divādi; laṭ in the passive; yak is ṅit-like; the accent of yak remains because the sūtra tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam… makes se anudātta; the word is middle-acute; tiṅ atiṅaḥ does not lower it because it follows yat — P. 8-1-28 tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ and P. 8-1-30], and dyumattamam [div in the sense of 'shining' (a saṃpadādi word with kvip, Vā. 2233 as printed); div + u → dyu by P. 6-1-131 diva ut; dyumat + tamap in the sense of excess; matup after a short-voweled stem gets the acute by P. 6-1-176; ...the print adds a long argument about diva ut applying to the stem and not the root, with the example akṣadyūḥ and the lakṣaṇā sense dīpti]; se is anudātta by P. 6-1-186; ūṭh P. 6-4-19 cited in the argument; numerals as printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ उलूखलक (ulūkhalaka) — O mortar | यत् चित् हि (yat cit hi) — although | गृहेगृहे (gṛhe-gṛhe) — in every house | युज्यसे (yujyase) — you are employed | इह (iha) — in this Vedic rite especially | जयताम् (jayatām) — of the victorious | दुन्दुभिः इव (dundubhiḥ iva) — like the war-drum | द्युमत्तमम् (dyumattamam) — [a sound] with exceeding brilliance | वद (vada) — utter.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O mortar! Although you are by nature to be found in every house, in this Vedic rite you must make a ringing sound, loud and clear, for everyone to hear, like the war-drums of conquerors. That is, sound forcefully.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Mortar, although you are employed in every house (for household purposes), make a most roaring sound (in the sacrifice) like the drums of victorious warriors.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ गृहे गृहे — in every house; for pounding grain, a mortar is present in every house. उलूखलक — ulūkhala — mortar; although the mortar is an inanimate object, it is here addressed, one must understand, as the deity presiding over it. We have explained the meaning of the word ulūkhala under the first rik of this sūkta. द्युमत्तमम् — atiśayena dīptam, prabhūtadhvaniyuktam: of exceeding brightness, that is, with a very loud sound — the idea is that the sound which is heard when the soma-creeper is placed in the mortar and pounded with the grāvan is made loud. जयतामिव दुन्दुभिः — yathā yuddhe jayaṃ prāpnuvatāṃ rājñāṃ dundubhir mahāntaṃ dhvaniṃ karoti tadvat: as the kings or warriors who have won victory in battle sound their victory-drum loudly. दुन्दुभिः — a bherī, a war-drum.

Rik 6 pp. 427–429

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

उ॒त स्म॑ ते वनस्पते॒ वातो॒ वि वा॒त्यग्र॒मित् । अथो॒ इन्द्रा॑य पा॒त॑वे सु॒नु सोम॑मुलूखल ॥ ६ ॥ [accent ?]

utá smá te vanaspate vā́to ví vātyágram ít | átho índrāya pātave sunú sómam ulūkhala || 6 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: in line 2 the bar stands under पा and the stroke over त of पातवे, and the stroke of इन्द्राय stands over न्द्रा; Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

उत । स्म । ते । वनस्पते । वातः । वि । वाति । अग्रम् । इत् ॥ अथो इति । इन्द्राय । पातवे । सुनु । सोमम् । उलूखल ॥ ६ ॥

uta | sma | te | vanaspate | vātaḥ | vi | vāti | agram | it || atho iti | indrāya | pātave | sunu | somam | ulūkhala || 6 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

उतापि च हे वनस्पते उलूखलरूपवृक्ष ते अग्रमित्तव पुरत एव वातो वि वाति स्म । श्रोरोपेतमुसलप्रहारैर्वायुर्विशेषेण प्रसरति खलु । अथो अनन्तरं हे उलूखल इन्द्रायेन्द्रोपकारार्थं पातवे पातुं सोमं सुनु । सोमाभिषवं कुरु ॥ वनस्पते । पारस्करादित्वात्सुट् । कार्ये कारणशब्दः । पातवे । पा पाने । तुमर्थे सेसेनिति तवेन्प्रत्ययः । ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यमित्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । सुनु । उतश्च प्रत्ययाद्यसंयोगपूर्वादिति हेर्लुक् । विकरणस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । पादादित्वादनिघातः । उलूखल । ऊर्ध्वं खमस्येत्युलूखलः । पृषोदरादिः ॥
