utāpi ca he vanaspate ulūkhalarūpavṛkṣa te agram it tava purata eva vāto vi vāti sma | śrorope tamusalaprahārair vāyur viśeṣeṇa prasarati khalu | atho anantaraṃ he ulūkhala indrāyendropakārārthaṃ pātave pātuṃ somaṃ sunu | somābhiṣavaṃ kuru || vanaspate | pāraskarādityāt suṭ | kārye kāraṇaśabdaḥ | pātave | pā pāne | tumarthe sesen iti tavenpratyayaḥ | ñnityādir nityam ity ādyudāttatvam | sunu | utaś ca pratyayād asaṃyogapūrvād iti her luk | vikaraṇasvareṇāntodāttatvam | pādāditvād anighātaḥ | ulūkhala | ūrdhvaṃ kham asyety ulūkhalaḥ | pṛṣodarādiḥ ||

Translation: "And, O vanaspate — [O mortar, you] tree-formed — in front of you, at the very top (agram it), the wind (vātaḥ) blows (vi vāti sma); [for] by the strokes of the pestle the air spreads specially. Then, O ulūkhala, press the soma (sunu somam) for Indra to drink (pātave) — for Indra's benefit. Vanaspate: the augment suṭ by the pāraskarādi class; the word for the cause is used for the effect. Pātave: pā pāne; tavenn in the infinitive sense; first-syllable acute by ñnityādir nityam. Sunu: the hi is lost after a u-suffix not preceded by a conjunct consonant [P. 6-4-106]; the end-acute from the vikaraṇa; no lowering as it is at the head of the pāda. Ulūkhala: 'whose hollow (kha) is upward' — a pṛṣodarādi form." Grammar pages 428–429, noted briefly: the words treated are vanaspate [vanasya patiḥ; the augment suṭ by P. 6-1-157 pāraskaraprabhṛtīni ca saṃjñāyām; in the vocative ṅi→ the ṛ-guṇa; the print explains that the word vanaspati is applied to the mortar by lakṣaṇā — 'a cause for its effect', as in āyurghṛtam ('ghee is life'): the mortar is made from the vanaspati, i.e. from a tree], pātave [pā pāne + tavenn P. 3-4-9; nit, so first-syllable acute P. 6-1-197], sunu [ṣuñ abhiṣave, svādi; loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi; śnu by P. 3-1-73; ṣa → sa by P. 6-1-64; the hi lost by P. 6-4-106 utaś ca pratyayād asaṃyogapūrvāt; the end-acute; no lowering by P. 8-1-28 tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ at the head of the pāda (āpādādau)] and ulūkhala [ūrdhvaṃ khaṃ yasya saḥ ulūkhalaḥ — a pṛṣodarādi form, with the loss, augment and change of letters according to need, P. 6-3-109 pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam; the vocative is lowered by P. 8-1-19]; numerals as printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (हे) वनस्पते ((he) vanaspate) — O tree-formed mortar [or mortar made of wood] | ते (te) — your | अग्रम् इत् (agram it) — in front, at the top | वातः (vātaḥ) — the wind | वि वाति स्म (vi vāti sma) — blows specially | अथो (atho) — therefore | (हे) उलूखल ((he) ulūkhala) — O mortar | इन्द्राय (indrāya) — for Indra | पातवे (pātave) — to drink | सोमम् (somam) — the soma-juice | सुनु (sunu) — press out.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O mortar in the form of a tree, or made of a tree! The wind blows specially in front of you [by the strokes of the pestle]. Therefore press out the soma-juice for Indra to drink.

॥ English Translation ॥

And, lord of the forest, the wind is blowing gently over your head; therefore, O mortar, press out the Soma for Indra to drink.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ वनस्पते — here the seer addresses the mortar as vanaspati, 'lord of the forest', which is to be understood from the fact that the mortar is made of wood; mortars are made both of stone and of wood; the one used here may be a wooden one; hence the word vanaspati is used. वातो वि वात्यग्रमित् — the wind blows in front, or above; the commentator says that, by the strokes of the pestle, the air stirs and blows. This sense does not fit very well. उलूखल — ūrdhvaṃ khaṃ yasya sa ulūkhalaḥ: one whose hollow (kha, space) is upward.

Rik 7 (Gāyatrī riks begin) pp. 429–432

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

आ॒य॒जी वा॑ज॒सात॑मा॒ ता ह्यु१॑च्चा वि॑जर्भृ॒तः । हरी॑ इवा॒न्धां॑सि॒ बप्स॑ता ॥ ७ ॥ [accent ?]

āyajī́ vājasā́tamā tā́ hy uccā́ vijarbhṛtáḥ | hárī ivāndhāṃsi bápsatā || 7 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: the kampa numeral १ after ह्यु carries the stroke, with a bar under it or under च्चा (not settled); the stroke over वि of विजर्भृतः; Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

आयजी इत्याऽयजी । वाजऽसातमा । ता । हि । उच्चा । विऽजर्भृतः ॥ हरी इवेति हरी ऽइव । अन्धांसि । बप्सता ॥ ७ ॥

āyajī ity ā-yajī | vāja-sātamā | tā | hi | uccā | vi-jarbhṛtaḥ || harī ivā iti harī-iva | andhāṃsi | bapsatā || 7 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

ये उलूखलमुसले आयजी सर्वतो यज्ञसाधने वाजसातमा अतिशयेनान्नप्रदे ता हि ते खलूच्चा प्रौढध्वनिर्यथा भवति तथा विजर्भृतः । विशेषेण पुनःपुनर्विहारं कुरुतः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अन्धांस्यन्नानि चणकादीनि खाद्यानि बप्सता भक्षयन्तौ हरी इव इन्द्रस्याश्वाविव । अत्र यास्क एवं व्याचख्यौ । आयजी आयष्टव्ये अन्नानां संभक्तृतमे ते ह्युच्चैर्विह्रियेते हरी इवान्नानि भुञ्जाने । नि. ९-३६ । इति ॥ आयजी । यजेरौणादिकः करणे इप्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । वाजसातमा । वाजं सनोतीति वाजसाः । षणु दाने । जनसनेत्यादिना विट्प्रत्ययः । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यादित्यात्वम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अतिशायनिकस्तमप् । सुपां सुलुगिति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः । विजर्भृतः । हृञ् हरणे । अस्माद्यङ्लुक्यभ्यासहलादिशेषोरत्जश्त्वेषु कृतेषु रुग्रिकौ च लुकि । पा. ७-४-९१ । इति रुगागमः । ततः प्रत्ययलक्षणेन धातुसंज्ञायां लटि द्विवचनं तस् । अदादिवच्चेति वचनाच्छपो लुक् । गुणे प्राप्ते क्ङिति चेति प्रतिषेधः । हृग्रहोर्भश्छन्दसीति भत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । बप्सता । भस भक्षणदीप्त्योः । लटः शतृ । जुहोत्यादिभ्यः श्लुः । घसिभसोर्हलि च । पा. ६-४-१०० । इत्युपधालोपः । नाभ्यस्ताच्छतुः । पा. ७-१-७८ । इति नुम्प्रतिषेधः । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

ye ulūkhalamusale āyajī sarvato yajñasādhane vājasātamā atiśayenānnaprade tā hi te khalūccā prauḍhadhvaniryathā bhavati tathā vijarbhṛtaḥ | viśeṣeṇa punaḥpunarvihāraṃ kurutaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | andhāṃsyannāni caṇakādīni khādyāni bapsatā bhakṣayantau harī iva indrasyāśvāviva | atra yāska evaṃ vyācakhyau | āyajī āyaṣṭavye annānāṃ saṃbhaktṛtame te hyuccairvihriyete harī ivānnāni bhuñjāne | ni. 9-36 | iti || āyajī | yajerauṇādikaḥ karaṇe ipratyayaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | vājasātamā | vājaṃ sanotīti vājasāḥ | ṣaṇu dāne | janasanetyādinā viṭpratyayaḥ | viḍvanoranunāsikasyādityātvam | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | atiśāyanikastamap | supāṃ sulugiti pūrvasavarṇadīrghaḥ | vijarbhṛtaḥ | hṛñ haraṇe | asmādyaṅlukyabhyāsahalādiśeṣoratjaśtveṣu kṛteṣu rugrikau ca luki | pā. 7-4-91 | iti rugāgamaḥ | tataḥ pratyayalakṣaṇena dhātusaṃjñāyāṃ laṭi dvivacanaṃ tas | adādivacceti vacanācchapo luk | guṇe prāpte kṅiti ceti pratiṣedhaḥ | hṛgrahorbhaśchandasīti bhatvam | pratyayasvaraḥ | hi ceti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | bapsatā | bhasa bhakṣaṇadīptyoḥ | laṭaḥ śatṛ | juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ | ghasibhasorhali ca | pā. 6-4-100 | ityupadhālopaḥ | nābhyastācchatuḥ | pā. 7-1-78 | iti numpratiṣedhaḥ | abhyastānāmādirityādyudāttatvam ||

Translation: "These two, mortar and pestle — āyajī, the instruments of sacrifice on every side; vājasātamā, most bountiful givers of food — tā te khalu — they, indeed, uccā — with a loud sound — vijarbhṛtaḥ: they keep working back and forth, repeatedly. An illustration: like the two horses of Indra (harī iva) that are eating (bapsatā) andhāṃsi — grain such as gram. Here Yāska explains: 'āyajī are things to be offered to; the two collectors of food, they move noisily up and down, like the two [horses] eating their food' (Ni. 9-36). Āyajī: i in the instrumental sense by the Uṇādi rule; the kṛdanta second member's accent. Vājasātamā: 'who gives (sanoti) food (vāja)' — viṭ by P. 3-2-67; ā for the nasal by P. 6-4-41; tamap in the sense of excess; supāṃ suluk. Vijarbhṛtaḥ: hṛñ haraṇe with yaṅ-luk, rugāgama by P. 7-4-91; the dual tas; the śap is lost as in the adādi class; no guṇa by P. 1-1-5; bha for ha by hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi; the suffix's accent; no lowering of the verb. Bapsatā: bhasa bhakṣaṇadīptyoḥ; śluḥ; doubling; śatṛ; loss of the penultimate by P. 6-4-100; no num by P. 7-1-78; first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-189." Grammar pages 431–432, noted briefly: the words treated are āyajī [ā + yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu + i in the instrumental sense (an Uṇādi suffix), the compound with the gati ā takes the kṛdanta-final accent by P. 6-2-139; dual au → ī by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ suluk; the word is end-acute], vājasātamā [vājaṃ sanoti; ṣaṇu dāne, tanādi; viṭ by P. 3-2-67 janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ; the nasal of the root → ā by P. 6-4-41 viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt; vājasā; tamap by P. 5-3-55 atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau + dual with ā by supāṃ suluk; the second member's accent by P. 6-2-139], vijarbhṛtaḥ [hṛñ haraṇe, bhvādi, here with yaṅ-luk — 'repeated going': doubling of the root; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; yaṅ lost before ac by P. 2-4-74 yaṅo 'ci ca; doubling by P. 6-1-9 sanyaṅoḥ; the reduplicate's a by urat; cutva by kuhoś cuḥ; jaśtva — ja for ha; the augment ruk by P. 7-4-91 rugrikau ca luki; so jarhṛ → the root jarbhṛ; tas for laṭ 3rd dual; śap lost; the ṅit-treatment blocks guṇa; the root status by P. 1-1-62 pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam and sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; hṛ → bhṛ by hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi (P. 3-1-84, Vā. 48-23); the suffix accent; the verb is not lowered since hi precedes (P. 8-1-34 hi ca)] and bapsatā [bhasa bhakṣaṇadīptyoḥ, juhotyādi; śatṛ; śluḥ; bhas doubled — babhas-at; the penultimate a lost by P. 6-4-100 ghasibhasor hali ca; bh → p before s by khari ca, so bapsat; the dual au → ā; no num — P. 7-1-78 nābhyastācchatuḥ; first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-189 abhyastānām ādiḥ]; numerals as printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ आयजी (āyajī) — the two implements of the sacrifice | वाजसातमा (vājasātamā) — the two great givers of food | ता (tā) — they, the mortar and the pestle | हि (hi) — [as is known] | उच्चा (uccā) — [making] a loud sound | अन्धांसि (andhāṃsi) — grains such as gram | बप्सता (bapsatā) — [two] that are chewing | हरी इव (harī iva) — like the two horses of Indra | विजर्भृतः (vijarbhṛtaḥ) — they sport [they move to and fro].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ The implements of the sacrifice, which are also the givers of food, the mortar and the pestle, strike together and sound loudly, and sport like the two horses of Indra chewing their gram and the like.

॥ English Translation ॥

For, these two impliments [sic] of sacrifice (mortal [sic] and pounder) bestowers of food are sporting like the horses of Indra chewing their fodder (grains).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ आयजी — sarvato yajñasādhane: the two implements of sacrifice on every side, i.e. the mortar and the pestle; this is a dual form. वाजसातमा — vājaṃ sanotīti vājasāḥ; atiśayena vājasāḥ vājasātamau: vāja means food; by giving it the mortar and the pestle are called vājasātamā; by pounding grain in the mortar with the help of the pestle one prepares food; so they are said to give the food and the like. उच्चा — uccaiḥ, with a loud sound: when grain is pounded with the pestle in the mortar, a loud sound is natural. विजर्भृतः — hṛñ haraṇe: they sport; they seem to sport. हरी इव — like Indra's horses; the two horses of Indra are called harī; Yāska gives the derivation harī indrasya ('the two bay horses of Indra'). अन्धांसि — foods: andhaḥ (Ni. 5-1, as printed) is a name for food. बप्सता — bhasa bhakṣaṇadīptyoḥ: eating, chewing; the sound made as horses chew gram and the like is compared to the sound made by pounding in the mortar with the pestle.

Rik 8 pp. 432–435

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

ता नो॑ अ॒द्य व॑नस्पती ऋ॒ष्वावृ॒ष्वेभिः॑ सो॒तृभिः॑ । इन्द्रा॑य॒ मधु॑मत्सुतम् ॥ ८ ॥ [accent ?]

tā́ no adyá vanaspatī ṛṣvā́v ṛṣvébhiḥ sotṛ́bhiḥ | índrāya mádhumat sutam || 8 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: the stroke of मधुमत् stands between धु and म, and the stroke over व of वनस्पती; Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

ता । नः । अद्य । वनस्पती इति । ऋष्वौ । ऋष्वेभिः । सोतृऽभिः ॥ इन्द्राय । मधुऽमत् । सुतम् ॥ ८ ॥

tā | naḥ | adya | vanaspatī iti | ṛṣvau | ṛṣvebhiḥ | sotṛ-bhiḥ || indrāya | madhu-mat | sutam || 8 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

अद्यास्मिन्कर्मणि हे वनस्पती उलूखलमुसलरूपौ तौ युवामृष्वेभिर्दर्शनीयैः सोतृभिरभिषवहेतुभिः सह ऋष्वौ दर्शनीयौ भूत्वेन्द्रायेन्द्रार्थं मधुमत् माधुर्योपेतं सोमद्रव्यं नोऽस्मदीयं सुतं । अभिषुणुतम् ॥ ता । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । नो अद्य । प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमिति प्रकृतिभावः । वनस्पती । उभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते आमन्त्रितस्येति सर्वानुदात्तत्वम् । प्लुतप्रगृह्या अचि । पा. ६-१-१२५ । इति प्रकृतिभावः । सुतम् । षुञ् अभिषवे । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । निघातः ॥

adyāsmin karmaṇi he vanaspatī ulūkhalamusalarūpau tau yuvām ṛṣvebhir darśanīyaiḥ sotṛbhir abhiṣavahetubhiḥ saha ṛṣvau darśanīyau bhūtvendrāyendrārthaṃ madhumat mādhuryopetaṃ somadravyaṃ no 'smadīyaṃ sutaṃ | abhiṣuṇutam || tā | supāṃ suluk ity ākāraḥ | no adya | prakṛtyāntaḥpādam iti prakṛtibhāvaḥ | vanaspatī | ubhayapadaprakṛtisvare prāpte āmantritasyeti sarvānudāttatvam | plutapragṛhyā aci | pā. 6-1-125 | iti prakṛtibhāvaḥ | sutam | ṣuñ abhiṣave | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | nighātaḥ ||

Translation: "Today (adya), in this rite, O vanaspatī — two [mortar and pestle] — you two, with the ṛṣvebhiḥ — beautiful — sotṛbhiḥ — pressers [the pounders], being yourselves ṛṣvau — beautiful — press (sutam) for Indra (indrāya) the madhumat — sweet — soma-substance, ours. Tā: ā by supāṃ suluk. No adya: the particle o in the pāda stays unchanged by P. 6-1-115. Vanaspatī: the dual vocative is pragṛhya (P. 1-1-11), so no sandhi before a vowel by P. 6-1-125. Sutam: ṣuñ abhiṣave, with the vikaraṇa lost; the lowering of the accent." Grammar pages 434–435, noted briefly: the words treated are tā [tad + dual au; the final ā by P. 7-2-102 tyadādīnām aḥ; pararūpa by P. 6-1-97 ato guṇe; ā for the ending by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ suluk; savarṇadīrgha gives tā], no adya [naḥ + adya: the o of the naḥ → no before a; P. 6-1-115 prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare: prakṛtibhāva, so the a of adya is not elided], vanaspatī [dual: the print explains that though the two members would each retain their accent (P. 6-2-140 ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat), the word, being a vocative with āmantrita status, is wholly anudātta by P. 8-1-19; the dual ending ī is pragṛhya by P. 1-1-11 īdūd dvivacanaṃ pragṛhyam so, though a vowel follows, there is no sandhi; yaṇ by P. 6-1-77 iko yaṇ aci is barred by P. 6-1-125 plutapragṛhyā aci nityam], sutam [ṣuñ abhiṣave, loṭ 2nd dual thas → tam by P. 3-4-101 tasthasthamipāṃ tāntantāmaḥ; śnu by P. 3-1-73 svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ, lost by bahulaṃ chandasi, the root remains with ṣ → s; sārvadhātuka-ṅit so no guṇa; the verb is lowered since indrāya madhumat are acute-bearing words]; numerals as printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ (वनस्पती) ((vanaspatī)) — O mortar and pestle in the form of trees | ऋष्वौ (ṛṣvau) — [being] beautiful | ऋष्वेभिः सोतृभिः (ṛṣvebhiḥ sotṛbhiḥ) — with beautiful pressing-implements | अद्य (adya) — now | नः (naḥ) — our | इन्द्राय (indrāya) — for Indra | मधुमत् (madhumat) — sweet | सुतम् (sutam) — press out [the soma].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O mortar and pestle, you who are in the form of trees! Beautiful as you are, and with the beautiful pressing-implements, press out sweet soma-juice for Indra at this our rite.

॥ English Translation ॥

Lords of the forest, (mortar and pounder) of pleasing appearance, prepare the sweet Soma-juice for Indra to drink.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अद्य — now; i.e. in the sacrificial rite we are performing. वनस्पती — here the mortar and pestle are addressed as in the previous rik by the word vanaspati; since they are made of wood, they are called vanaspatī. ऋष्वौ, ऋष्वेभिः — darśanīyau, darśanīyaiḥ: beautiful to look at, giving delight; ṛṣvau is an epithet of vanaspatī, ṛṣvebhiḥ of sotṛbhiḥ; the sense 'giving pleasure, desirable' may also be taken. सोतृभिः — with the things that press out the soma-juice, that is: the mortar, the pestle, the soma-creeper, the stone, the straining cloth, the kalaśa (jar) which receives the juice, and so on. मधुमत् — mādhuryopetam: of sweet, tasty soma-juice. सुतम् — sunoti, the dual loṭ second person of the root.

Rik 9 (closing rik; the Soma is poured into the cow-hide filter) pp. 435–437

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

उच्छि॒ष्टं च॒म्वो॑र्भर॒ सोमं॑ प॒वित्र॒ आ सृ॑ज । नि धेहि॒ गोरधि॑ त्व॒चि ॥ ९ ॥ [accent ?]

ucchiṣṭáṃ camvor bhara sómaṃ pavítra ā́ sṛja | ni dhehi gór ádhi tvací || 9 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: the bar in उच्छिष्टं stands under च्छि, and the strokes over म्वो and सृ; Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

उत् । शिष्टम् । चम्वोः । भर । सोमम् । पवित्रे । आ । सृज ॥ नि । धेहि । गोः । अधि । त्वचि ॥ ९ ॥

ut | śiṣṭam | camvoḥ | bhara | somam | pavitre | ā | sṛja || ni | dhehi | goḥ | adhi | tvaci || 9 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे ऋत्विग्विशेष हरिश्चन्द्रदेवतापक्षे हे हरिश्चन्द्रेति वा चम्वोः सोमस्य भक्षणसंपादकयोरधिषवणफलकयोः शिष्टमभिषवराहित्येनावशिष्टं सोममुद्धर । शकटस्योपरि हर । सोममभिषुतं सोमं पवित्रे दशापवित्रे आ सृज । आनीय प्रक्षिप । प्रक्षेपे सत्यवशिष्टं सोमं गोस्त्वच्यानडुहे चर्मण्यधि नि धेहि । अध्यारोप्य स्थापय ॥ चम्वोः । चमु अदने । चम्यते भक्ष्यतेऽत्रेति चमूः । कृषिचमितनिधनीत्यादिना । उ. १-८२ । औणादिक उप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । सप्तमीद्विवचनस्योदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरित इति स्वरितत्वम् । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति व्यत्ययेन न भवति । भर । हृग्रहोर्भः । धेहि । घ्वसोरेद्धावभ्यासलोपश्च । पा. ६-४-११९ । इत्येत्वाभ्यासलोपौ । निघातः । त्वचि । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ २६ ॥

he ṛtvigviśeṣa hariścandradevatāpakṣe he hariścandreti vā camvoḥ somasya bhakṣaṇasaṃpādakayoradhiṣavaṇaphalakayoḥ śiṣṭamabhiṣavarāhityenāvaśiṣṭaṃ somamuddhara | śakaṭasyopari hara | somamabhiṣutaṃ somaṃ pavitre daśāpavitre ā sṛja | ānīya prakṣipa | prakṣepe satyavaśiṣṭaṃ somaṃ gostvacyānaḍuhe carmaṇyadhi ni dhehi | adhyāropya sthāpaya || camvoḥ | camu adane | camyate bhakṣyate 'treti camūḥ | kṛṣicamitanidhanītyādinā | u. 1-82 | auṇādika upratyayaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | saptamīdvivacanasyodāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ svarita iti svaritatvam | udāttayaṇo halpūrvāditi vyatyayena na bhavati | bhara | hṛgrahorbhaḥ | dhehi | ghvasoreddhāvabhyāsalopaśca | pā. 6-4-119 | ityetvābhyāsalopau | nighātaḥ | tvaci | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvam || 26 ||

Translation: "O particular priest — or, if the deity is Hariścandra, 'O Hariścandra' — from the camvoḥ — the two pressing-boards that make the soma ready for drinking — take up (ud bhara) the śiṣṭam soma, what is left over because it was not pressed; carry it onto the cart. The pressed soma pour (ā sṛja) into the pavitra — the ten-fringed filter: having brought it, put it in. When it has been put in, place the remaining soma on (adhi ni dhehi) the cow's hide (goḥ tvaci) — the ox-skin: set it on top. Camvoḥ: camu adane; 'that in which one eats (drinks) is camū'; by the rule beginning kṛṣicamitanidhani (U. 1-82) the Uṇādi suffix u; the suffix accent; in the locative dual the yaṇ standing for an udātta becomes svarita by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya; udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt does not apply, by vyatyaya. Bhara: bha by hṛgrahor bhaḥ. Dhehi: e and loss of the reduplicate by P. 6-4-119 ghvasor eddhāv abhyāsalopaś ca; the lowering. Tvaci: the ending is acute by sāvekācaḥ." (Varga 26 ends here.) Grammar pages 436–438, noted briefly: the words treated are camvoḥ [camu adane, bhvādi; the suffix u by U. sū. 1-81 kṛṣicamitanidhani… (the bhāṣya prints U. 1-82); the suffix accent; in the locative dual the yaṇ → svarita by P. 8-2-4; P. 6-1-174 udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt would make the ending acute, but by P. 3-1-85 vyatyayo bahulam it does not apply here, so the svarita stands], bhara [hṛñ haraṇe, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular; ha → bha by hṛgrahor bhaḥ (Vā. 48-23)], dhehi [ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, juhotyādi; loṭ 2nd singular sip → hi by ato heḥ; śluḥ by juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ; doubling; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, hrasva, jaśtva: dadhā + hi; by P. 6-4-119 ghvasor eddhāv abhyāsalopaś ca the reduplicate is lost and the root's ā → e; the verb is lowered after a non-verb] and tvaci [(p. 438) tvac + locative singular; the ending is acute by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ; end-acute]; numerals as printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ शिष्टम् (śiṣṭam) — the remaining [soma, left unpressed] | चम्वोः (camvoḥ) — in the two vessels [boards] | उद्भर (ud bhara) — bring up | सोमम् (somam) — the soma-juice | पवित्रे (pavitre) — in the filter | आ सृज (ā sṛja) — pour it | गोः त्वचि (goḥ tvaci) — on the cow-hide | अधि नि धेहि (adhi ni dhehi) — place it above.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ Take what remains of the soma in the two vessels; pour the juice into the strainer; and place it on the cow-hide.

॥ English Translation ॥

Fill the remaining Soma in the two jars, pour it on the sieve, and put it on the cow-hide.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ In this rik the seer, addressing Hariścandra, the sacrificer, or some priest (the adhvaryu, perhaps), tells him what is to be done with the remaining soma. उच्छिष्टम् — śiṣṭam, the remainder: the soma-creeper is placed in the mortar and crushed, and the juice, standing on top of the stone (grāvan), flows down; the remainder, small in amount, is what stays in the mortar [and on the boards]. चम्वोः — camū is a wooden vessel used in the soma-pressing, used for offering the soma to the gods; here it means the two wooden boards (adhiṣavaṇa-phalaka) between which the soma-creeper is pressed. Skandasvāmin explains camasa as the drinking-vessel of the priests; the dual here, by vyatyaya, stands for 'the two camasa vessels'. पवित्रे — Yāska explains pavitra as 'what purifies' (punāti) (Ni. 5-6), listing its many senses — mantra, ray, water, fire — but here it must be understood as the filter or sieve with which the soma-juice is strained. In some places kuśa grass is placed over the vessel in which the soma is strained, and the juice is poured over it so that the pure juice falls into the vessel; hence pavitra here means the 'filter'. गोः त्वचि — on the cow-hide: besides pouring the soma into droṇakalaśa and other wooden vessels, there are descriptions in the Ṛgveda of the soma being poured on a sieve made of cow-hide, or of the hide being spread under the stalks, so that the juice falls on it and goes down — so a cow-hide was used in the soma-pressing.

॥ Close of Sūkta 28 ॥ The grammar of Rik 9 ends on printed p. 438 (the note on tvaci), followed by the closing line ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೆಂಟನೇ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ಸಮಾಪ್ತವಾಗಿದೆ — "The twenty-eighth sūkta is ended." Corrected in the numeral pass: an earlier note here said that the sūkta ended on p. 437 without a closing line.

॥ ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂಭತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 29 — "yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ" ("The Twenty-ninth Sūkta"; sixth sūkta of the Sixth Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 438 lower half–446. The introductory note is on p. 438, the heading block on p. 439; Rik 1 begins on p. 439.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note; printed p. 438)

यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा इति षष्ठं सूक्तं सप्तर्चं शुनःशेपस्यार्षं पाङ्क्तमैन्द्रम् । अनुक्रमणिका च — यच्चिद्धि सप्त पाङ्क्तमिति ॥ पृष्ठ्यषडहस्य पञ्चमेऽहनि माध्यंदिने सवने होत्रका यच्चिद्धीति सप्तर्चं सूक्तं त्रींस्तृचान्कृत्वा स्वस्वशस्त्र एकैकं तृचमावपेरन् । चतुर्थेऽहनीति खण्डे यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा इत्येकैकमेवमेव । आ. ७-११ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥

yac cid dhi satya somapā iti ṣaṣṭhaṃ sūktaṃ saptarcaṃ śunaḥśepasyārṣaṃ pāṅktam aindram | anukramaṇikā ca — yac cid dhi sapta pāṅktam iti || pṛṣṭhyaṣaḍahasya pañcame 'hani mādhyaṃdine savane hotrakā yac cid dhīti saptarcaṃ sūktaṃ trīṃs tṛcān kṛtvā svasvaśastra ekaikaṃ tṛcam āvaperan | caturthe 'hanīti khaṇḍe yac cid dhi satya somāpā ity ekaikam evam eva | ā. 7-11 | iti sūtritam ||

Translation: "The sixth sūkta, beginning yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ, has seven riks; its seer is Śunaḥśepa; the metre is Pankti; the deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇikā too says: 'yac cid dhi — seven, Pāṅkta.' In the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, on the fifth day, at the midday pressing, the hotrakas [assistants of the Hotṛ] should make the seven-rik sūkta yac cid dhi into three triplets and insert one triplet each into their own śastra; in the section caturthe 'hani: 'yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ — one each, in the same way' (Ā. 7-11) — so it is laid down in the sūtra."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥ Yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ is the sixth sūkta of the sixth anuvāka and has seven riks. Śunaḥśepa is the seer; the metre is Pankti. The Anukramaṇikā says 'yac cid dhi sapta pāṅktam', that is, the sūkta yac cid dhi has seven riks. In the Soma-sacrifice called Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, on the fifth day, at the mādhyandina-savana (midday pressing), three priests who are assistants of the Hotṛ (the hotrakas) are to take the three triplets of this sūkta — tṛca, tṛca, [and the remaining rik] — and use them, each at his own śastra recitation: so it is explained in Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra in the section caturthe 'hani, in the sūtra yac cid dhi satya somapā (Ā. 7-11).

॥ Heading block of the sūkta (p. 439) ॥

मण्डल १ — अनुवाक ६ — सूक्त २९ । अष्टक १ — अध्याय २ — वर्ग २७ । ऋक्संख्या ७ । ऋषिः — शुनःशेप आजीगर्तिः । देवता — इन्द्रः । छन्दः — पङ्क्तिः ।

Maṇḍala 1 — Anuvāka 6 — Sūkta 29. Aṣṭaka 1 — Adhyāya 2 — Varga 27. Riks: 7. Ṛṣi: Śunaḥśepa Ājīgarti. Devatā: Indra. Metre: Pankti. Varga 27 as printed, w3.

Rik 1 pp. 439–442

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

यच्चि॒द्धि स॑त्य सोमपा अनाश॒स्ता इ॑व॒ स्मसि॑ । आ तू न॑ इन्द्र शंसय॒ गोष्वश्वे॑षु शु॒भ्रिषु॑ स॒हस्रे॑षु तुवीमघ ॥ १ ॥

yac cid dhí satya somapā anāśastā́ iva smási | ā tū́ na indra śaṃsaya góṣv áśveṣu śubhríṣu sahásreṣu tuvīmagha || 1 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

यत् । चित् । हि । सत्य । सोमऽपाः । अनाशस्ताःऽइव । स्मसि ॥ आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुविऽमघ ॥ १ ॥

yat | cit | hi | satya | soma-pāḥ | anāśastāḥ-iva | smasi || ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvi-magha || 1 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

विश्वैर्देवैः प्रेरितः शुनःशेप एतदादिकाभिर्द्वाविंशतिसंख्याकाभिर्ऋग्भिरिन्द्रं तुष्टाव । तथा च ब्राह्मणम् । तं विश्वे देवा ऊचुरिन्द्रो वै देवानामोजिष्ठो बलिष्ठः सहिष्ठः सत्तमः पारयिष्णुतमस्तं नु स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति स इन्द्रं तुष्टाव यच्चिद्धि सत्य सोमपा इत्येतेन सूक्तेनोत्तरस्य च पञ्चदशभिः । ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१६ । इति ॥ हे सोमपाः सोमस्य पातः सत्य सत्यवादिन्निन्द्र यच्चिद्धि यद्यपि वयमनाशस्ता इव स्मसि अप्रशस्ता इव भवामः तथापि हे तुवीमघ बहुधनेन्द्र त्वं गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु शोभनेषु सहस्रेषु सहस्रसंख्याकेषु च निमित्तभूतेषु नोऽस्माना शंसय । सर्वतः प्रशस्तान्कुरु । अस्मद्दोषमनपेक्ष्य गवादीन्प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः ॥ सोमपाः । विजन्तः । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । अनाशस्ता इव । शंसु स्तुतौ । निष्ठेति भावे क्तः । यस्य विभाषेतीट्प्रतिषेधः । नञा बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । स्मसि । इदन्तो मसिः । तू नः । ऋचि तुनुघेत्यादिना दीर्घः । गोषु । सावेकाच इति प्राप्तस्य विभक्त्युदात्तत्वस्य न गोश्वन्साववर्णेति प्रतिषेधः । अश्वेषु । अश्नुतेऽध्वानमित्यश्वः । अशिप्रुषीत्यादिना क्वन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । शुभ्रिषु । शुभ दीप्तौ । अदिशदिभूशुभिभ्यः क्रिन् । उ. ४-६५ । इति क्रिन्प्रत्ययः । व्यत्ययेनान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥

viśvairdevaiḥ preritaḥ śunaḥśepa etadādikābhirdvāviṃśatisaṃkhyākābhirṛgbhirindraṃ tuṣṭāva | tathā ca brāhmaṇam | taṃ viśve devā ūcurindro vai devānāmojiṣṭho baliṣṭhaḥ sahiṣṭhaḥ sattamaḥ pārayiṣṇutamastaṃ nu stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti sa indraṃ tuṣṭāva yacciddhi satya somapā ityetena sūktenottarasya ca pañcadaśabhiḥ | ai. brā. 7-16 | iti ‖ he somapāḥ somasya pātaḥ satya satyavādinnindra yacciddhi yadyapi vayamanāśastā iva smasi apraśastā iva bhavāmaḥ tathāpi he tuvīmagha bahudhanendra tvaṃ goṣvaśveṣu śubhriṣu śobhaneṣu sahasreṣu sahasrasaṃkhyākeṣu ca nimittabhūteṣu no 'smānā śaṃsaya | sarvataḥ praśastānkuru | asmaddoṣamanapekṣya gavādīnprayacchetyarthaḥ ‖ somapāḥ | vijantaḥ | āmantritanighātaḥ | anāśastā iva | śaṃsu stutau | niṣṭheti bhāve ktaḥ | yasya vibhāṣetīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | nañā bahuvrīhau nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvam | smasi | idanto masiḥ | tū naḥ | ṛci tunughetyādinā dīrghaḥ | goṣu | sāvekāca iti prāptasya vibhaktyudāttatvasya na gośvansāvavarṇeti pratiṣedhaḥ | aśveṣu | aśnute 'dhvānamityaśvaḥ | aśipruṣītyādinā kvanpratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvam | śubhriṣu | śubha dīptau | adiśadibhūśubhibhyaḥ krin | u. 4-65 | iti krinpratyayaḥ | vyatyayenāntodāttatvam ‖

Translation: "Impelled by the Viśvedevas, Śunaḥśepa praised Indra with the twenty-two riks beginning with this one. So the Brāhmaṇa says: 'The Viśvedevas said to him: "Indra is the most vigorous, the strongest, the mightiest, the best, the most capable of carrying across of the gods; praise him now; then we shall release you." He praised Indra with the sūkta yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ and fifteen [riks] of the next' (Ai. Brā. 7-16). O somapāḥ — drinker of soma! Satya — truth-speaking Indra! Yac cid dhi — although we are anāśastā iva — as if undeserving of praise, as if unworthy — yet, O tuvīmagha — O Indra of much wealth — śaṃsaya: make us praised on all sides goṣu aśveṣu — with cows, with horses — śubhriṣu — good ones — sahasreṣu — in thousands: the sense is: disregarding our fault, give us cows and the like." (Tail: somapāḥ ends in viC, vocative nighāta; anāśastāḥ: kta in the bhāva sense by niṣṭhā, no iṭ by yasya vibhāṣā, a nañ-bahuvrīhi with end-acute by nañsubhyām; smasi: idanto masi; tū naḥ: lengthening by ṛci tunugha…; goṣu: the ending-acute blocked by na gośvan…; aśveṣu: aśnute 'dhvānam iti aśvaḥ, kvan by aśipruṣi…, first-syllable acute, being nit; śubhriṣu: krin by adiśadibhūśubhibhyaḥ krin (U. 4-65), end-acute by vyatyaya.) Grammar pages 441–442, noted briefly (corrected from the print, w3): somapāḥ [somaṃ pibati iti somapāḥ; pā pāne, bhvādi; viC by āto manin-kvanib-vanipaś ca (P. sū. 3-2-74), the root being ā-final; the whole of viC is lost, leaving an ā-final word; as a vocative, nighāta by āmantritasya ca], anāśastā iva [śaṃsu stutau, bhvādi; kta in the bhāva sense by niṣṭhā (P. sū. 3-2-102); no iṭ by yasya vibhāṣā (P. sū. 7-2-15); in śaṃs+ta the penultimate n is lost by aniditāṃ halaḥ, giving śasta; with the upasarga āṅ: na vidyate āśastaṃ yeṣāṃ te anāśastāḥ, a bahuvrīhi; where the first member's natural accent would apply, nañsubhyām (P. sū. 6-2-172) gives the second member's end-acute; with ru, ya and its loss, anāśastā iva], smasi [asa bhuvi, adādi; 1st pl. mas; as+mas: the a of as is lost by śnasor allopaḥ (P. sū. 6-4-111), as mas is treated as ṅit; in s+mas, idanto masi (P. sū. 7-1-46) adds the augment i: smasi], tū na [ṛci tunugha… (P. sū. 6-3-133) lengthens tu in the Saṃhitā], goṣu [go being monosyllabic, sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ (P. sū. 6-1-168) would make the ending acute; it is blocked by na gośvan sāv avarṇa… (P. sū. 6-1-182), so first-syllable acute], aśveṣu [aśnute adhvānam iti aśvaḥ; aśū vyāptau, svādi; kvan by aśipruṣilaṭikaṇi… (U. sū. 1-149); as kvan has n as it, ñnity ādir nityam (P. sū. 6-1-197) gives first-syllable acute], śubhriṣu [śubha dīptau, bhvādi; krin by adiśadibhūśubhibhyaḥ krin (U. sū. 4-505 as printed; the bhāṣya prints U. 4-65); loc. pl. śubhriṣu; being nit the first syllable would be acute, by vyatyaya the end-acute: "śubhriṣu is a middle-acute word" (as printed)]. ॥ १ ॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ सोमपाः (somapāḥ) — O drinker of soma | सत्य (satya) — O truth-speaking | इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | यत् चित् हि (yat cit hi) — if perchance | अनाशस्ताः इव स्मसि (anāśastāḥ iva smasi) — we are as if unworthy | तुवीमघ (tuvīmagha) — O one of abundant wealth | नः (naḥ) — us | सहस्रेषु (sahasreṣu) — in thousands | शुभ्रिषु (śubhriṣu) — auspicious | गोषु (goṣu) — cows | अश्वेषु (aśveṣu) — horses | आ शंसय (ā śaṃsaya) — make [us] fit to receive [the praise-worthy].

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O truth-speaking Indra, drinker of soma! Although we are not worthy of obtaining your wealth, you, who have abundant wealth, make us worthy of thousands of auspicious cows and horses, and fill us with your riches.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

O truth-speaking Indra, drinker of Soma juice, although we do not deserve it, yet you Indra, of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Śunaḥśepa, having prayed to the Viśvedevas with the rik namo mahadbhyaḥ, [was told by them:] "Śunaḥśepa, among the gods Indra is the strongest, the most glorious, the most patient (sahiṣṇu); praise him, so that you may be released from this bond"; and, with their consent, Śunaḥśepa praises Indra with this sūkta yac cid dhi satya somapāḥ and with the next fifteen riks of the following sūkta ā va indraṃ kriviṃ yathā — twenty-two riks in all. (Ai. Brā. 7-16). We have explained this matter in the Śunaḥśepa story itself.

सत्य — satyavādin: one who speaks truth. सोमपाः — somasya pātā: the drinker of soma. अनाशस्ता इव — śaṃsu stutau:

अनाशस्ता इव अप्रशस्ता इव । ईषच्छंसनं स्तुतिराशस्तं अविद्यमानं आशस्तं येषां ते अनाशस्ताः ईषत्स्तुतिवर्जिताः ।

anāśastā iva apraśastā iva | īṣacchaṃsanaṃ stutirāśastaṃ avidyamānaṃ āśastaṃ yeṣāṃ te anāśastāḥ īṣatstutivarjitāḥ |

"Anāśastā iva: as if unpraised. A slight praising is āśasta; those who have no āśasta are anāśastāḥ: devoid of even slight praise." Unworthy of praise: we are, in praising you, not fit [for it]; yet because we praise you, may you be pleased and give us the cows and horses we need. आ तू न इन्द्र शंसय गोष्वश्वेषु शुभ्रिषु सहस्रेषु तुवीमघ — the sense of śaṃsaya — 'make [us] praiseworthy among cows and horses' — appears to be: 'give us thousands of cows and horses, and make us renowned as persons possessing them'. तुवीमघ — tuvi means 'much' (Ni. 3-13), magha means 'wealth' (Ni. 3-9 as printed); hence tuvīmagha is 'having much wealth'.

Rik 2 pp. 443–445

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

शि॑प्रिन्वाजानां पते॒ शची॑व॒स्तव॑ दं॒सना॑ । आ तू न॑ इन्द्र शंसय॒ गोष्वश्वे॑षु शु॒भ्रिषु॑ स॒हस्रे॑षु तुवीमघ ॥ २ ॥

śiprin vājānāṃ pate śácīvas táva daṃsánā | ā tū́ na indra śaṃsaya góṣv áśveṣu śubhríṣu sahásreṣu tuvīmagha || 2 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

शिप्रिन् । वाजानाम् । पते । शचीवः । तव । दंसना ॥ आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुविऽमघ ॥ २ ॥

śiprin | vājānām | pate | śacīvaḥ | tava | daṃsanā || ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvi-magha || 2 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे शचीवः शक्तिमन् शिप्रिन् शोभनहनूयुक्त वाजानां पतेऽन्नानां पालक तव दंसना कर्मविशेषोऽनुग्रहरूपः सर्वदा वर्तते । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ शिप्रिन् । शिप्रे हनू नासिके वा । नि. ९-१७ । इति यास्कः । अत इनिठनाविति मत्वर्थीय इनिः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । वाजानां पते । सुबामन्त्रिते इति पराङ्गवद्भावात् षष्ठ्यामन्त्रितसमुदायनिघातः । न चामन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदिति शिप्रिन्नित्यस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वेन पदादपरत्वात्पादादित्वाच्च न निघातः । नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरणे सामान्यवचनमित्यविद्यमानवत्त्वप्रतिषेधात् । शचीवः । छन्दसीर इति मतुपो वत्वम् । मतुवसो रुरिति रुत्वे खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः । पा. ८-३-१५ । पादादित्वादामन्त्रितनिघाताभावः ॥

he śacīvaḥ śaktiman śiprin śobhanahanūyukta vājānāṃ pate 'nnānāṃ pālaka tava daṃsanā karmaviśeṣo 'nugraharūpaḥ sarvadā vartate | anyatpūrvavat ‖ śiprin | śipre hanū nāsike vā | ni. 9-17 | iti yāskaḥ | ata iniṭhanāviti matvarthīya iniḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvam | vājānāṃ pate | subāmantrite iti parāṅgavadbhāvāt ṣaṣṭhyāmantritasamudāyanighātaḥ | na cāmantritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavaditi śiprinnityasyāvidyamānavattvena padādaparatvātpādāditvācca na nighātaḥ | nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanamityavidyamānavattvapratiṣedhāt | śacīvaḥ | chandasīra iti matupo vatvam | matuvaso ruriti rutve kharavasānayorvisarjanīyaḥ | pā. 8-3-15 | pādāditvādāmantritanighātābhāvaḥ ‖ Bhāṣya re-read from the print, w3: शोभनहनूयुक्त, पालक, नि. ९-१७ as printed (first digit ೯-like; the grammar page prints Niru. 6-17), अत इनिठनाविति मत्वर्थीय इनिः.

Translation: "O śacīvaḥ — powerful! Śiprin — fair-jawed! Vājānāṃ pate — lord of foods, protector of food! Your daṃsanā — your special acts of favour — are always present. The rest is as before. Śiprin: 'śipre are the two jaws or the nose' says Yāska (Ni. 9-17 as printed); ini in the sense of possession by ata iniṭhanau. Vājānāṃ pate: the vocative group is lowered as a whole ... [argument on whether śiprin is treated as non-existent: it is not, by nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam]. Śacīvaḥ: v for m of matup in the Veda; ru by matuvaso ru; visarga by kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ (P. 8-3-15); being pāda-initial, no vocative nighāta." Grammar pages 444–445, noted briefly (corrected from the print, w3): śiprin [śipre hanū nāsike vā (Niru. 6-17) says Yāska: śipra is the jaw or the nose; śipre asya staḥ iti śiprī; ini in the possessive sense by ata iniṭhanau (P. sū. 5-2-115); vocative śiprin; at the head of the pāda, first-syllable acute by āmantritasya (P. sū. 6-1-198)], vājānāṃ pate [by subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare (P. sū. 2-1-2) the preceding genitive becomes part of the following vocative, and the accent falls on the whole group with the genitive; the vocative śiprin stands before it, so by āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat (P. sū. 8-1-72) it would count as non-existent, the group would stand at the head of the pāda, and by āpādādau the eighth-chapter nighāta would not apply; how then does the earlier procedure hold? Because by nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam (P. sū. 8-1-73) the two vocatives, having one referent, are co-referential, so śiprin is not treated as non-existent; so the doubt does not arise], śacīvaḥ [śacī asya asti iti śacīmat; by chandasīraḥ (P. sū. 8-2-15) the m of matup after an i-final or r becomes v in the Veda; by matuvaso ru sambuddhau (P. sū. 8-3-1 ru; in śacīvar before a pause, the visarga by kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ P. sū. 8-3-15); being pāda-initial, no eighth-chapter nighāta; first-syllable acute by āmantritasya (P. sū. 6-1-198)]. ॥ २ ॥ File's 8-1-74, 8-2-66 and 8-1-18 are not printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ शचीवः (śacīvaḥ) — O powerful | शिप्रिन् (śiprin) — O fair-jawed | वाजानां पते (vājānāṃ pate) — O lord of foods | इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | तव (tava) — your | दंसना (daṃsanā) — [favourable] acts | [सर्वदा] ([sarvadā]) — always | नः (naḥ) — to us | सहस्रेषु (sahasreṣu) — in thousands | शुभ्रिषु (śubhriṣu) — of auspicious | गोषु अश्वेषु (goṣu aśveṣu) — cows and horses | तुवीमघ (tuvīmagha) — O one of abundant wealth | आ शंसय (ā śaṃsaya) — [make us] worthy.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Indra — powerful, handsome, the lord and protector of foods! Your favour toward us is constant. Therefore, O Indra of abundant wealth, make us fit to receive thousands of auspicious cows and horses, and fill us with your wealth.

॥ English Translation ॥

Handsome and mighty lord of food, your exploits are ever before us; therefore, Indra of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellant [sic] cows and horses.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ शिप्रिन् — शोभनहनूयुक्त (śiprin — śobhanahanūyukta): one with fair jaws, i.e. a good mouth, good-looking. शचीवः, दंसना — the words śacī and daṃsas are read among the twenty-six names for 'act' beginning apaḥ, apnaḥ (no Nirukta number printed); hence śacīvaḥ means 'one with strength, powerful', and daṃsanā 'a bold act, or favour in the form of an act'.

Rik 3 pp. 445–448

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

नि ष्वा॑पया मिथू॒दृशा॑ स॒स्तामबु॑ध्यमाने । आ तू न॑ इन्द्र शंसय॒ गोष्वश्वे॑षु शु॒भ्रिषु॑ स॒हस्रे॑षु तुवीमघ ॥ ३ ॥

ní ṣvāpayā mithūdṛ́śā sastā́m ábudhyamāne | ā tū́ na indra śaṃsaya góṣv áśveṣu śubhríṣu sahásreṣu tuvīmagha || 3 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

नि । स्वापय । मिथूऽदृशा । सस्ताम् । अबुध्यमाने इति । आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुविऽमघ ॥ ३ ॥

ni | svāpaya | mithū-dṛśā | sastām | abudhyamāne iti | ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvi-magha || 3 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

मिथूदृशा परस्परं संगतत्वेन दृश्यमाने यमदूत्यौ नि ष्वापय । नितरां सुप्ते कुरु । ते चास्मान्मारयितुमबुध्यमाने सत्यौ सस्तां निद्रां प्राप्नुताम् । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ नि ष्वापय । सुषामादित्वात्षत्वम् । पा. ८-३-९८ । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घः । मिथुनतया युगलरूपेण पश्यत इति मिथूदृशा । क्विप्चेति दृशेः कर्तरि क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । पूर्ववत्पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घः । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेराकारः । सस्ताम् । षस स्वप्ने । लोटि तसस्ताम् । अदिप्रभृतिभ्य इति शपो लुक् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । पादादित्वान्निघाताभावः । अबुध्यमाने । नञ्समासेऽव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

mithūdṛśā parasparaṃ saṃgatatvena dṛśyamāne yamadūtyau ni ṣvāpaya | nitarāṃ supte kuru | te cāsmānmārayitumabudhyamāne satyau sastāṃ nidrāṃ prāpnutām | anyatpūrvavat ‖ ni ṣvāpaya | suṣāmāditvātṣatvam | pā. 8-3-98 | anyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti dīrghaḥ | mithunatayā yugalarūpeṇa paśyata iti mithūdṛśā | kvipceti dṛśeḥ kartari kvip | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | pūrvavatpūrvapadasya dīrghaḥ | supāṃ sulugiti vibhakterākāraḥ | sastām | ṣasa svapne | loṭi tasastām | adiprabhṛtibhya iti śapo luk | pratyayasvaraḥ | pādāditvānnighātābhāvaḥ | abudhyamāne | nañsamāse 'vyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ‖ Bhāṣya re-read from the print, w3: संगतत्वेन, पा. ८-३-९८ (was missing), मिथुनतया युगलरूपेण पश्यत, क्विप्चेति, पूर्ववत्पूर्वपदस्य, षस स्वप्ने (was वस), अदिप्रभृतिभ्य इति शपो लुक्.

Translation: "Put to sleep (ni svāpaya) the two yamadūtyau [female messengers of Yama] who appear (dṛśyamāne) together (mithūdṛśā), in a pair; make them fall into deep sleep; and may they, abudhyamāne — not waking — to kill us, sastām — sleep. The rest as before. Ni ṣvāpaya: ṣa since it belongs to the suṣāmādi group (P. 8-3-98); lengthening by anyeṣām api dṛśyate. Mithūdṛśā: 'the two who see as a couple, in pairs'; by kvip ca, kvip of dṛś in the sense of agent; the preceding member is lengthened; the dual ending ā by supāṃ suluk. Sastām: ṣasa svapne ['to sleep'], loṭ 3rd dual tām; śap lost by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ; the suffix accent; no lowering since at the head of the pāda. Abudhyamāne: in the nañ-compound the first member's accent." Grammar pages 447–448, noted briefly (corrected from the print, w3): ni ṣvāpaya [ñiṣvap śaye; with ṇic, loṭ 2nd sg.; being pāda-initial, sāt padādyoḥ would block ṣatva, but suṣāmādiṣu ca (P. sū. 8-3-48 as printed; for 8-3-98) gives ṣ, the word being in that list; the Saṃhitā lengthening by anyeṣām api dṛśyate (P. sū. 6-1-137 as printed; for 6-3-137)], mithūdṛśā [mithunatayā yugalarūpeṇa paśyataḥ: 'those who see as a pair'; by kvip ca the root dṛś with a sup-ending upapada takes kvip in the agent sense, wholly lost: mithunadṛś; a compound with a kṛt-final second member, so by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (P. sū. 6-2-139) the second member keeps its own accent, the ṛ acute; the Saṃhitā lengthening as before; the dual au → ā by supāṃ suluk], sastām [ṣasa svapne, adādi; loṭ 3rd dual, tas → tām (being treated as laṅ-like); the root's ṣ → s; śap lost by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (P. sū. 2-4-72); end-acute by the suffix accent; being pāda-initial, no nighāta by tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ (P. sū. 8-1-28)], abudhyamāne [in the nañ-compound, by tatpuruṣe tulyārtha… (P. sū. 6-2-2) the nañ first member keeps its accent: first-syllable acute]. ॥ ३ ॥ File's 8-3-65, 3-2-61, 6-3-116 and 3-4-101 are not printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ मिथूदृशा (mithūdṛśā) — the two who look at each other [the two messengers of Yama] | निस्वापय (ni svāpaya) — put to sleep | अबुध्यमाने (abudhyamāne) — not awakening | सस्ताम् (sastām) — let [them] sleep | नः (naḥ) — us | इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | सहस्रेषु (sahasreṣu) — in thousands | शुभ्रिषु (śubhriṣu) — of auspicious | गोषु अश्वेषु (goṣu aśveṣu) — cows and horses | तुवीमघ (tuvīmagha) — one of abundant wealth | आ शंसय (ā śaṃsaya) — [make us] worthy.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ Send to sleep the two female messengers of Yama, who have come to kill us and who look at each other, so that they do not wake again. And, O Indra of abundant wealth, make us fit for thousands of auspicious cows and horses.

॥ English Translation ॥

Send to sleep the two females that see each other, let them sleep and not be wakeful; Indra, of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ The sense of this rik is not clear. The commentator says: Śunaḥśepa, who is expecting death, prays to Indra that the two female messengers of Yama who may come to take away his life at the time of his death should not do so, but fall asleep without waking. Both the commentator and Skandasvāmin explain the sense by supplying words here and there. In the rik there is no word yamadūtī ('Yama's messenger') nor any word suggesting the time of death; the rik speaks only of two persons — females — looking at each other: abudhyamāne is feminine dual; hence the commentator says that mithūdṛśā is 'the two Yama-messengers looking at each other' [by supplying the word]. The seer's intention is not clear.

नि स्वापय — nitarāṃ supte kuru: put them into a deep sleep. मिथूदृशा — mithunatayā paśyantī [those who see as a pair]: two persons seeing each other: the word yamadūtyau ('two messengers of Yama') the commentator supplies; this is a dual word. सस्ताम् — ṣasa svapne: 'let them sleep'. अबुध्यमाने — [two] not waking: a dual word.

Rik 4 pp. 448–450

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

स॒सन्तु॒ त्या अरा॑तयो॒ बोध॑न्तु शूर रा॒तयः॑ । आ तू न॑ इन्द्र शंसय॒ गोष्वश्वे॑षु शु॒भ्रिषु॑ स॒हस्रे॑षु तुवीमघ ॥ ४ ॥

sasántu tyā́ árātayo bódhantu śūra rātáyaḥ | ā tū́ na indra śaṃsaya góṣv áśveṣu śubhríṣu sahásreṣu tuvīmagha || 4 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

ससन्तु । त्याः । अरातयः । बोधन्तु । शूर । रातयः ॥ आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुविऽमघ ॥ ४ ॥

sasantu | tyāḥ | arātayaḥ | bodhantu | śūra | rātayaḥ || ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvi-magha || 4 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

त्या अस्माभिरदृश्यमानाः परोक्षास्ता अरातयोऽदानशीलाः शत्रवः ससन्तु । निद्रां कुर्वन्तु । हे शूर शौर्ययुक्तेन्द्र रातयो दानशीला बन्धवो बोधन्तु । अस्मान्बुध्यन्ताम् । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ ससन्तु । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अरातयः । रा दाने । मन्त्रे वृषेत्यादिना भावे क्तिन् । न विद्यते रातिरेष्विति बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । नञ्सुभ्यामिति तु सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्ते इति न भवति । यद्वा । क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायामिति कर्तरि क्तिच् । नञ्समासेऽव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । बोधन्तु । पादादित्वात्तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघाताभावः ॥

tyā asmābhiradṛśyamānāḥ parokṣāstā arātayo 'dānaśīlāḥ śatravaḥ sasantu | nidrāṃ kurvantu | he śūra śauryayuktendra rātayo dānaśīlā bandhavo bodhantu | asmānbudhyantām | anyatpūrvavat ‖ sasantu | pratyayasvaraḥ | arātayaḥ | rā dāne | mantre vṛṣetyādinā bhāve ktin | na vidyate rātireṣviti bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | nañsubhyāmiti tu sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyante iti na bhavati | yadvā | kticktau ca saṃjñāyāmiti kartari ktic | nañsamāse 'vyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | bodhantu | pādāditvāttiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātābhāvaḥ ‖ Bhāṣya re-read from the print, w3: परोक्षास्ता (was परोक्षाः शास्त्राः), ससन्तु (was सत्वन्तु), बोधन्तु । अस्मान्बुध्यन्ताम् (was …पृथ्यंताम् [?]), मन्त्रे वृषेत्यादिना, रातिरेष्विति, नञ्सुभ्यामिति तु, क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायामिति.

Translation: "Tyāḥ — those, unseen by us, out of sight — arātayaḥ, niggardly enemies, may they sasantu — sleep, fall into slumber. O śūra — heroic Indra! May the rātayaḥ — generous kinsmen — bodhantu — wake: may they be aware of us. The rest as before. Arātayaḥ: rā dāne; ktin in the sense of the action by mantre vṛṣa…; a bahuvrīhi 'in whom there is no giving' with the first member's accent; the rules beginning nañsubhyām are optional in the Veda, so [the end-acute] does not apply; or ktic in the agent sense by ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām. Bodhantu: no lowering because it begins the pāda." Grammar pages 449–450, noted briefly (corrected from the print, w3): sasantu [ṣasa svapne; loṭ 3rd plural; by the suffix's initial acute, sasantu is a middle-acute word], arātayaḥ [rā dāne, adādi; ktin in the bhāva sense by mantre vṛṣeṣapaca… (P. sū. 3-3-96): rāti; na vidyate rātir yeṣu te arātayaḥ, a bahuvrīhi, so by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam the first member's accent; strictly, with nañ as first member, nañsubhyām would give the end-acute, but by sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante it does not apply here; or else ktic in the agent sense by ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām (P. sū. 3-3-174), rāti, and na rātayaḥ arātayaḥ is a nañ-tatpuruṣa, where by tatpuruṣe tulyārtha… (P. sū. 6-2-2) the avyaya (nañ) first member keeps its accent: arātayaḥ is first-syllable acute], bodhantu [budha avagamane, bhvādi, loṭ 3rd plural; being pāda-initial, no nighāta by tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ (P. sū. 8-1-28); since śap is anudātta and the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta by tāsyanudāttet… (P. sū. 6-1-186), the root accent makes it first-syllable acute]. ॥ ४ ॥ File's 7-1-3, 3-3-97, 6-2-1, 6-2-172 numbers and 8-1-18 are not printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ शूर (śūra) — O valiant Indra | त्याः (tyāḥ) — those [unseen, remote] | अरातयः (arātayaḥ) — enemies who do not give | सस॑न्तु (sasantu) — let them sleep | रातयः (rātayaḥ) — [our] generous friends | बोधन्तु (bodhantu) — let them awake [be alert, to know us] | तुवीमघ (tuvīmagha) — O one of abundant wealth | नः (naḥ) — us | सहस्रेषु शुभ्रिषु (sahasreṣu śubhriṣu) — in thousands of auspicious | गोषु अश्वेषु (goṣu aśveṣu) — cows and horses | आ शंसय (ā śaṃsaya) — [make us] worthy.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O valiant Indra! May those enemies of ours, who are out of sight, fall asleep there, so that they do not know of us; and may our generous friends be wakeful, so that they know us. And, O Indra of abundant wealth, make us fit for thousands of auspicious cows and horses.

॥ English Translation ॥

O hero, may our enemies sleep and our friends be wakeful; Indra, of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ त्याः — tya is a word of the sense of tad; hence tyāḥ means 'those' (tāḥ). रातयः, अरातयः — rā dāne: adānaśīlāḥ are arātayaḥ. The root rā has the sense of giving; so those who give to us, who help, are rātayaḥ, 'friends'; those who give us nothing and obstruct us are arātayaḥ, 'enemies'. शूर — Indra of great prowess.

Rik 5 pp. 450–452

॥ Saṃhitāpāṭhaḥ ॥

समि॑न्द्र गर्द॒भं मृ॑ण नु॒व॑न्तं पा॒प॑यामु॒या । आ तू न॑ इन्द्र शंसय॒ गोष्वश्वे॑षु शु॒भ्रिषु॑ स॒हस्रे॑षु तुवीमघ ॥ ५ ॥

sám indra gardabháṃ mṛṇa nuvantaṃ pāpayāmuyā́ | ā tū́ na indra śaṃsaya góṣv áśveṣu śubhríṣu sahásreṣu tuvīmagha || 5 || Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

॥ Padapāṭhaḥ ॥

सम् । इन्द्र । गर्दभम् । मृण । नुवन्तम् । पापयाः । अमुया ॥ आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुविऽमघ ॥ ५ ॥

sam | indra | gardabham | mṛṇa | nuvantam | pāpayā | amuyā || ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvi-magha || 5 ||

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥

हे इन्द्र अमुयानयास्माभिः श्रूयमाणया पापया निन्दारूपया वाचा नुवन्तं स्तुवन्तम् । अपकीर्तिं प्रकटयन्तमित्यर्थः । तादृशं गर्दभं गर्दभसमानवैरिणं सं मृण । सम्यक् मारय । यथा गर्दभः श्रोत्रमशक्यं परुषं शब्दं करोति तथा शत्रुरपि । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ गर्दभम् । नर्द गर्द शब्दे । कॄगॄशॄशलिगर्दिभ्योऽभच् । उ. ३-१२२ । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । मृण । मृण हिंसायाम् । तौदादिकः । शस्य ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । नुवन्तम् । णु स्तुतौ । शतर्यदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपो लुक् । शतुर्ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभाव उवङादेशः । प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

he indra amuyānayāsmābhiḥ śrūyamāṇayā pāpayā nindārūpayā vācā nuvantaṃ stuvantam | apakīrtiṃ prakaṭayantamityarthaḥ | tādṛśaṃ gardabhaṃ gardabhasamānavairiṇaṃ saṃ mṛṇa | samyak māraya | yathā gardabhaḥ śrotramaśakyaṃ paruṣaṃ śabdaṃ karoti tathā śatrurapi | anyatpūrvavat ‖ gardabham | narda garda śabde | kṝgṝśṝśaligardibhyo 'bhac | u. 3-122 | cita ityantodāttatvam | mṛṇa | mṛṇa hiṃsāyām | taudādikaḥ | śasya ṅittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | nuvantam | ṇu stutau | śataryadiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapo luk | śaturṅittvādguṇābhāva uvaṅādeśaḥ | pratyayādyudāttatvam ‖ Bhāṣya re-read from the print, w3: अमुयानयास्माभिः, अपकीर्तिं (was आशकीर्तिं), सम्यक् मारय, श्रोत्रमशक्यं (was …असह्यं), अन्यत्पूर्ववत् added; the file's अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यत इति गर्दभः is not printed; the Uṇādi sūtra reads कॄगॄशॄशलि… with the long-ṝ signs as printed, उ. ३-१२२ (was ३-१३३ [?]); शतर्यदिप्रभृतिभ्यः (was अदादिप्रभृतिभ्यः); ङित्त्वात् in both places.

Translation: "O Indra! Gardabham — the ass-like enemy who, with this (amuyā) speech that we hear, pāpayā — a blaming speech — nuvantam — 'praises', that is, proclaims [our] ill-fame: such a gardabha, an enemy like an ass — saṃ mṛṇa — destroy utterly; kill completely. As the ass (gardabha) makes an unbearable harsh noise for the ear, so does the enemy. The rest as before. Gardabham: from narda garda śabde ['to sound']; the suffix abhac (Uṇ. 3-122); end-acute through cit. Mṛṇa: mṛṇa hiṃsāyām, of the tudādi class; śa is ṅit-like so no guṇa. Nuvantam: ṇu stutau ['to praise'], with śatṛ; the śap is lost by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ when śatṛ follows; no guṇa because śatṛ is ṅit; uvaṅ [uv] substituted; the accent of the suffix." Grammar page 452, noted briefly (corrected from the print, w3): gardabham [narda garda śabde; the suffix abhac by kṛ gṛ śṛ śali gardibhyo 'bhac (U. sū. 3-402); accusative singular gardabham; ending in the cit suffix, end-acute by citaḥ (P. sū. 6-1-163)], mṛṇa [mṛṇa hiṃsāyām, tudādi; loṭ 2nd sg., sip → hi; the vikaraṇa śa by tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ (P. sū. 3-1-77); being apit it is ṅit, so no guṇa of the light penultimate; after a, hi is lost by ato heḥ (P. sū. 6-4-105): mṛṇa; the finite verb is lowered (nighāta)], nuvantam [ṇu stutau, adādi; śatṛ in the sense of laṭ; the śap is lost by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (P. sū. 2-4-72); the root's ṇ → n; nu+at: an apit sārvadhātuka is ṅit, so no guṇa; by aci śnudhātubhruvām… (P. sū. 6-4-77 uvaṅ: nuvat; accusative singular with num as an ugit: nuvantam; by the suffix accent (its first syllable acute) nuvantam is a middle-acute word]. ॥ ५ ॥ File's 3-2-75, 3-4-87, 1-2-4, 8-1-28, 6-4-88 and 7-1-70 are not printed.)

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | अमुया (amuyā) — with this | पापया (pāpayā) — with ill [harsh, blaming] | नुवन्तम् (nuvantam) — [speech] who utters [the words] | गर्दभम् (gardabham) — [him who is like] an ass, an enemy | सं मृण (saṃ mṛṇa) — destroy completely | तुवीमघ (tuvīmagha) — O Indra of abundant wealth | नः (naḥ) — us | गोषु अश्वेषु (goṣu aśveṣu) — in cows and horses | शुभ्रिषु (śubhriṣu) — auspicious | सहस्रेषु (sahasreṣu) — in thousands | आ शंसय (ā śaṃsaya) — [make us] worthy.

॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥ O Indra! Destroy utterly this enemy, who is like an ass, who is wearing out our ears with this harsh blaming speech. And, O Indra of abundant wealth, make us fit for thousands of auspicious cows and horses.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, kill this ass (enemy) praising you with such harsh speech; Indra, of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ गर्दभम् — [it means] 'an ass'; here the commentator has said 'our enemy, who is like an ass'. नुवन्तं पापया अमुया — the sense: 'with this harsh speech, which is blaming and cruel to hear, one who reviles you'. [My note: the Kannada says 'reviles you', following the commentator's stuvantam, 'praising', as a euphemism for 'noisy, calling out'; the English the source prints, 'praising you with such harsh speech', follows the Sanskrit.]

Rik 6 pp. 452–454

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

पता॑ति कुण्डृ॒णाच्या॑ दू॒रं वातो॒ वना॒दधि॑ । [accent ?] आ तू न॑ इन्द्र शंसय॒ गोष्वश्वे॑षु शु॒भ्रिषु॑ स॒हस्रे॑षु तुवीमघ ॥ ६ ॥

pátāti kuṇḍṛṇā́cyā dūráṃ vāto vánād ádhi | ā tū́ na indra śaṃsaya góṣv áśveṣu śubhríṣu sahásreṣu tuvīmagha ‖ 6 ‖ Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); [accent ?]: the stroke in कुण्डृणाच्या stands between णा and च्या; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha

पताति । कुण्डृणाच्या । दूरम् । वातः । वनात् । अधि । आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुवीमघ ॥ ६ ॥

patāti | kuṇḍṛṇācyā | dūram | vātaḥ | vanāt | adhi | ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvīmagha ‖ 6 ‖

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

वातोऽस्मत्प्रतिकूलो वायुः कुण्डृणाच्या कुटिलगत्या स त्वस्मान्परित्यज्य वनादध्यरण्यादप्यधिकं दूरं देशं पताति । पततु । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ पताति । लेट्याडागमः । कुण्डृणाच्या । कुडि दाहे । अस्मात् ल्युडन्ते कुण्डनशब्दे डकारात्परस्याकारस्य ऋकारश्छान्दसः । ऋवर्णाच्चेति वक्तव्यमिति णत्वम् । तदञ्चतीति कुण्डृणाची । ऋत्विगित्यादिना क्विन् । अनिदितामिति नलोपेऽञ्चतेश्चेति वक्तव्यम् । पा. ४-१-६-२ । इति ङीप् । अचः । पा. ६-४-१३८ । इत्यकारलोपः । चौ । पा. ६-३-१३८ । इति पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घत्वम् । चौ । पा. ६-१-२२२ । इत्याकारस्योदात्तत्वम् ॥

vāto 'smatpratikūlo vāyuḥ kuṇḍṛṇācyā kuṭilagatyā sa tvasmānparityajya vanādadhyaraṇyādapyadhikaṃ dūraṃ deśaṃ patāti | patatu | anyatpūrvavat ‖ patāti | leṭyāḍāgamaḥ | kuṇḍṛṇācyā | kuḍi dāhe | asmāt lyuḍante kuṇḍanaśabde ḍakārātparasyākārasya ṛkāraśchāndasaḥ | ṛvarṇācceti vaktavyamiti ṇatvam | tadañcatīti kuṇḍṛṇācī | ṛtvigityādinā kvin | aniditāmiti nalope 'ñcateśceti vaktavyam | pā. 4-1-6-2 | iti ṅīp | acaḥ | pā. 6-4-138 | ityakāralopaḥ | cau | pā. 6-3-138 | iti pūrvapadasya dīrghatvam | cau | pā. 6-1-222 | ityākārasyodāttatvam ‖ Bhāṣya completed from the print, w3: वनादध्यरण्यादप्यधिकं (was …[?]), पततु (was पतेत्), and the grammatical tail, missing in the file, added.

Gist (mine): "The wind that is hostile to us, going by a crooked course, leaving us, may fall (blow) far away, beyond the forest. Patāti = patatu. The rest as before." (Tail: patāti with the leṭ augment āṭ; kuṇḍṛṇācyā: kuḍi dāhe + lyuṭ → kuṇḍana, the ṛ after the ḍ Vedic, ṇatva by the vārttika ṛvarṇāc ca; tad añcati → kuṇḍṛṇācī with kvin, nasal lost, ṅīp by añcateś ca (Pā. 4-1-6-2), the a lost by acaḥ (6-4-138), the first member lengthened by cau (6-3-138), the ā acute by cau (6-1-222).)

Grammar (p. 454), noted briefly (corrected from the print, w3): patāti (patḷ gatau; leṭ 3rd sg. tip, śap; the augment āṭ by leṭo 'ḍāṭau (P. sū. 3-4-94); first-syllable acute by the root accent); kuṇḍṛṇācyā (kuḍi dāhe, bhvādi; lyuṭ, ana by yuvor anākau (P. sū. 7-1-1); num as an idit root: kuṇḍana; the a after the ḍ becomes ṛ in the Veda; ṇatva by ṛvarṇāc ceti vaktavyam (Vā. 4969); kuṇḍṛṇam añcati: kvin by ṛtvig dadhṛk… (P. sū. 3-2-59); the nasal lost by aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ… (P. sū. 6-4-24): kuṇḍṛṇāc; in the feminine ṅīp by añcateś ceti vaktavyam (P. sū. 4-1-6-2); in the instrumental the a of añc lost by acaḥ (P. sū. 6-4-138), the first member lengthened by cau (P. sū. 6-3-138), and its final ā made acute by cau (P. sū. 6-1-222): the ā after the ṇ is acute). ॥ ६ ॥

English Translation as printed, p. 454

Let the (adverse) wind with crooked course blow away to far off places beyond the forest; Indra of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — वातः कुण्डृणाच्या — kuḍi dāhe; kuṭilagatyā: by a bad, crooked path: the wind that blows against us. दूरं वनादधि पताति — may it go to a region far beyond the forest; may it not be near us.

Rik 7 (last rik of the sūkta) pp. 455–457

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

सर्वं॑ परिक्रो॒शं ज॑हि ज॒म्भ॑या कृकदा॒श्वं॑ । आ तू न॑ इन्द्र शंसय॒ गोष्वश्वे॑षु शु॒भ्रिषु॑ स॒हस्रे॑षु तुवीमघ ॥ ७ ॥

sárvaṃ parikrośáṃ jahi jambhayā kṛkadāśvaṃ | ā tū́ na indra śaṃsaya góṣv áśveṣu śubhríṣu sahásreṣu tuvīmagha ‖ 7 ‖ Saṃhitā accents as printed (w3); Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha

सर्वम् । परिऽक्रोशम् । जहि । जम्भय । कृकदाश्वम् । आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । शंसय । गोषु । अश्वेषु । शुभ्रिषु । सहस्रेषु । तुवीमघ ॥ ७ ॥

sarvam | pari 'krośam | jahi | jambhaya | kṛkadāśvam | ā | tu | naḥ | indra | śaṃsaya | goṣu | aśveṣu | śubhriṣu | sahasreṣu | tuvīmagha ‖ 7 ‖

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

परिक्रोशमस्मद्विषये सर्वत आक्रोशकर्तारं सर्वं पुरुषं जहि । मारय । कृकदाश्वमस्मद्विषये हिंसाप्रदं शत्रुं जम्भय । मारय । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥ परिक्रोशम् । क्रुश आह्वाने । परितः क्रोशयतीति परिक्रोशः । पचाद्यच् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । जहि । हन हिंसागत्योः । हन्तेर्जः । पा. ६-४-३६ । इति जादेशः । तस्यासिद्धवदत्राभादित्यसिद्धत्वादतो हेरिति हेर्लुग्न भवति । जम्भय । जभि नाशने । चुरादित्वात्स्वार्थिको णिच् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे णिच एव स्वरः शिष्यते । कृकदाश्वम् । कृञ् हिंसायाम् । कृदाधारार्चिकलिभ्यः कन् । उ. ३-४० । इति भावे कन्प्रत्ययः । किदित्यनुवृत्तेर्गुणाभावः । तथा च कृको हिंसा । तां दाशति प्रयच्छतीति कृकदाशुः । बहुलग्रहणाद्दाशतेरपि कृक उपपदे कृके वचः कश्च । उ. १-६ । इत्युण् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । द्वितीयायाममि पूर्वत्वे प्राप्ते वा छन्दसीति तस्य बाधितत्वाद्यणादेशः । उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यण इति विभक्तेः स्वरितत्वम् ॥ २७ ॥

parikrośamasmadviṣaye sarvata ākrośakartāraṃ sarvaṃ puruṣaṃ jahi | māraya | kṛkadāśvamasmadviṣaye hiṃsāpradaṃ śatruṃ jambhaya | māraya | anyatpūrvavat ‖ parikrośam | kruśa āhvāne | paritaḥ krośayatīti parikrośaḥ | pacādyac | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | jahi | hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ | hanterjaḥ | pā. 6-4-36 | iti jādeśaḥ | tasyāsiddhavadatrābhādityasiddhatvādato heriti herlugna bhavati | jambhaya | jabhi nāśane | curāditvātsvārthiko ṇic | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatve ṇica eva svaraḥ śiṣyate | kṛkadāśvam | kṛñ hiṃsāyām | kṛdādhārārcikalibhyaḥ kan | u. 3-40 | iti bhāve kanpratyayaḥ | kidityanuvṛtterguṇābhāvaḥ | tathā ca kṛko hiṃsā | tāṃ dāśati prayacchatīti kṛkadāśuḥ | bahulagrahaṇāddāśaterapi kṛka upapade kṛke vacaḥ kaśca | u. 1-6 | ityuṇ | pratyayasvareṇodāttaḥ | dvitīyāyāmami pūrvatve prāpte vā chandasīti tasya bādhitatvādyaṇādeśaḥ | udāttasvaritayoryaṇa iti vibhakteḥ svaritatvam ‖ 27 ‖ Bhāṣya re-read from the print, w3: the compressed and doubtful parts of the tail filled (तस्यासिद्धवत्…, जभि नाशने, कृञ् हिंसायाम् (was कृकं हिंसायाम् [?]), कृदाधारार्चिकलिभ्यः कन्, उ. ३-४० and उ. १-६ confirmed, किदित्यनुवृत्तेर्गुणाभावः, तथा च कृको हिंसा…कृकदाशुः, बहुलग्रहणाद्दाशतेरपि कृक उपपदे, प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः); पा. ६-४-३६ confirmed; the closing ॥ २७ ॥ is the varga number (Varga 27 ends here).

Gist (mine): "Kill (jahi) every man who abuses (parikrośam) us from all sides; destroy (jambhaya) the enemy who deals harm (kṛkadāśvam). The rest as before." The grammatical tail (p. 455) treats parikrośam (pacādi ac), jahi (hanter jaḥ, with the principle asiddhavad atrābhāt), jambhaya (curādi ṇic) and kṛkadāśvam (kṛka from kṛñ hiṃsāyām with kan (U. 3-40) in the bhāva sense, dāś dāne with uṇ by kṛke vacaḥ kaś ca (U. 1-6), end-acute; in the accusative ami pūrvaḥ is set aside by vā chandasi, yaṇ, and the ending made svarita by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ).

Pratipadārtha p. 456, rendered — परिक्रोशम् [him] who reviles and blames us; सर्वम् every one; जहि destroy; कृकदाश्वम् the enemy who does us harm; जम्भय kill; तुवीमघ [Indra] of plentiful wealth; इन्द्र O Indra; नः us; सहस्रेषु in thousands; शुभ्रिषु excellent; गोषु in cows; अश्वेषु in horses; आ शंसय make [us] worthy (give us thousands of cows and horses).

Bhāvārtha — O Indra, destroy every enemy who reviles us and speaks ill of us; kill all who do us harm. O Indra of abundant wealth, give us thousands of excellent cows and horses and make us rich.

English Translation as printed, p. 456

Strike down everyone who reviles us; destroy everyone that does us injury; O Indra of plentiful wealth, enrich us with thousands of excellent cows and horses.

Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — परिक्रोशम् — kruśa āhvāne; paritaḥ krośayatīti parikrośaḥ: one who, out of hostility, rages at us or speaks ill. जहि — hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ: restrain, injure, destroy. जम्भय — jabhi nāśane: destroy. कृकदाश्वम् — kṛñ hiṃsāyām; kṛko hiṃsā | tāṃ dāśati prayacchatīti kṛkadāśuḥ: a man who deals injury, who brings us harm.

Grammar pages (pp. 456–457), noted briefly (corrected from the print, w3): the Kannada grammar treats parikrośam (kruśa āhvāne, bhvādi; paritaḥ krośayati iti parikrośaḥ; ac by nandigrahapacādibhyo… (P. sū. 3-1-134), being in the pacādi list; guṇa of the light penultimate; accusative; a compound with a kṛt-final second member, so gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (P. sū. 6-2-139)), jahi (hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi, loṭ 2nd sg. sip → hi; ja for the root by hanter jaḥ (P. sū. 6-4-36); since by asiddhavad atrābhāt (P. sū. 6-4-22) the ja-substitute counts as not effected, the loss of hi by ato heḥ (P. sū. 6-4-105) does not occur), jambhaya (jabhi nāśane, curādi; ṇic in its own sense by satyāpapāśa… (P. sū. 3-1-25); num as an idit; the ṇic-final jambhi is a root by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ (P. sū. 3-1-32); loṭ, śap, hi lost after a; guṇa and ay of ṇic; śap being pit is anudātta, so the udātta of ṇic remains: the a after the bh is acute) and kṛkadāśvam (kṛñ hiṃsāyām, kryādi; kan in the bhāva sense by kṛdādhārārcikalibhyaḥ kan (U. sū. 3-320), kit carried over, so no guṇa: kṛkaḥ; kṛkaṃ hiṃsāṃ dāśati prayacchati iti kṛkadāśuḥ: dāś dāne; by the word bahulam in uṇādayo bahulam (P. sū. 3-3-1), with kṛka as upapada, uṇ by kṛke vacaḥ kaś ca (U. sū. 1-6); end-acute by the suffix's initial acute; in the accusative kṛkadāśu+am: ami pūrvaḥ (P. sū. 6-1-107) would give the single prior form, but by vā chandasi it does not apply; yaṇ: kṛkadāśvam; the ending becomes svarita by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya (P. sū. 8-2-4): a svarita-final word). ॥ ७ ॥ File's Uṇ. 3-40 [?] (grammar prints U. sū. 3-320), Uṇ. 1-6 [?] (confirmed) and P. 6-1-106 (not printed) corrected.

Close of Sūkta 29 — ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೊಂಭತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ಸಮಾಪ್ತವಾಗಿದೆ (ippattombhattaneya sūktavu samāptavāgide) — "The twenty-ninth sūkta is ended." At the foot of p. 457: sheet-mark "58" and "VOLUME 3".

॥ ಮೂವತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 30 — "ā va indram" ("The Thirtieth Sūkta"; seventh sūkta of the Sixth Anuvāka)

Heading : "The thirtieth sūkta." Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 6; Sūkta 30. Aṣṭaka 1; Adhyāya 2; Varga 28, 29, 30, 31. Number of Riks in the sūkta: 22. Ṛṣi: Śunaḥśepa Ājīgarti. Devatā: Riks 1–16 Indra; 17–19 the Aśvins; 20–22 Uṣas. Chandas: Riks 1–10, 12–15, 17–22 Gāyatrī; Rik 11 Gāyatrī pādanicṛt; Rik 16 Triṣṭubh. p. 458 is read from the old scan, scans/Rig_Vol3.pdf PDF 473: the better scan's PDF 472 is a wrong page, headed 358. Heading numerals and Anu. 4-4 re-checked from that page in the pass, w3.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, introductory note

आ व इन्द्रमिति द्वाविंशत्यृचं सप्तमं सूक्तं शुनःशेपस्यार्षं गायत्रम् । अस्माकमित्येषा पादनिचृद्गायत्री । त्रयः सप्तकाः पादनिचृत् । अनु. ४-४ । इत्युक्तत्वात् । शश्वदिन्द्र इत्येषा त्रिष्टुप् । आदितः षोडशर्च ऐन्द्र्यः । अश्विनावश्वावत्येत्याद्यास्तिस्र आश्विन्यः । कस्त उष इत्याद्यास्तिस्र उषोदेवताकाः । तथा चानुक्रमणिका । आ वो द्व्यधिकास्माकं पादनिचृच्छश्वत्त्रिष्टुप्स्परौ तृचावाश्विनोषस्याविति ॥

ā va indramiti dvāviṃśatyṛcaṃ saptamaṃ sūktaṃ śunaḥśepasyārṣaṃ gāyatram | asmākamityeṣā pādanicṛdgāyatrī | trayaḥ saptakāḥ pādanicṛt | anu. 4-4 | ityuktatvāt | śaśvadindra ityeṣā triṣṭup | āditaḥ ṣoḍaśarca aindryaḥ | aśvināvaśvāvatyetyādyāstisra āśvinyaḥ | kasta uṣa ityādyāstisra uṣodevatākāḥ | tathā cānukramaṇikā | ā vo dvyadhikāsmākaṃ pādanicṛcchaśvattriṣṭupsparau tṛcāvāśvinoṣasyāviti ‖

Translation: "Ā va indram is the seventh sūkta [of the anuvāka]; it has twenty-two Riks; its seer is Śunaḥśepa; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Rik asmākam is pādanicṛd Gāyatrī; [the Anukramaṇikā rule] 'three [pādas] of seven [syllables] are pādanicṛt' (Anu. 4-4) having been stated. The Rik śaśvad indra is Triṣṭubh. From the beginning, sixteen Riks are Indra's (aindryaḥ); the three beginning aśvināv aśvāvatyā are the Aśvins'; the three beginning kas ta uṣaḥ have Uṣas as deity. The Anukramaṇikā says so: 'ā vo [has] two more [than twenty]; asmākam is pādanicṛt; śaśvat is Triṣṭubh; the last two triplets are the Aśvins' and Uṣas's.'"

Anuvāda p. 458, rendered — Ā va indram is the seventh sūkta in the sixth anuvāka and has twenty-two Riks. Śunaḥśepa is the seer; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Rik asmākam it is pādanicṛt Gāyatrī; śaśvad indraḥ is Triṣṭubh. The first sixteen Riks have Indra as deity; the three from aśvināv aśvāvatyā have the Aśvins; the three from kas ta uṣaḥ have Uṣas. The Anukramaṇikā says: ā vo dvyadhikāsmākaṃ pādanicṛc chaśvat triṣṭup sparau tṛcāv āśvinoṣasyāv iti.

Rik 1 pp. 459–461

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

आ व॒ इन्द्रं॒ क्रिविं॑ यथा वाज॒यन्तः॑ श॒तक्र॑तुं । मंहि॑ष्ठं सिञ्च॒ इन्दु॑भिः ॥ १ ॥

ā va índraṃ kríviṃ yathā vājayántaḥ śatákratuṃ | máṃhiṣṭhaṃ siñca índubhiḥ || 1 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha

आ । वः । इन्द्रं । क्रिविं । यथा । वाजऽयन्तः । शतऽक्रतुं । मंहिष्ठं । सिञ्चे । इन्दुऽभिः ॥ १ ॥

ā | vaḥ | indraṃ | kriviṃ | yathā | vāja 'yantaḥ | śata 'kratuṃ | maṃhiṣṭhaṃ | siñce | indu 'bhiḥ ‖ 1 ‖

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

As printed: क्रिविशब्दो वप्रिः (so printed; the sense of वप्रिः here is unclear); उ. ४-५६ (the grammar page, p. 461, prints ४-४६); फि. ४-१७ (the last digit is the flat-footed glyph also used for 7 in पा. ७-४-३७ on p. 461; the grammar page prints फि. सू. ८५).

वाजयन्तोऽन्नमिच्छन्तो वयं शुनःशेपा हे ऋत्विग्यजमाना वो युष्माकं संबन्धिनमिममिन्द्रमिन्दुभिः सोमैरासिञ्चे । सर्वतः सिञ्चामहे । तर्पयामः । कीदृशम् । शतक्रतुं शतसंख्याककर्मोपेतं मंहिष्ठमतिशयेन प्रवृद्धम् । सेचने दृष्टान्तः । यथा येन प्रकारेण क्रिविमवटं जलेन पूरयन्ति तद्वत् । क्रिविशब्दो वप्रिः । काटुरित्यादिषु चतुर्दशसु कूपनामसु क्रिविः कूपः सूद इति पठितम् ॥ क्रिविम् । कृती छेदने । कृन्तत इति क्रिविः । क्रिविघृष्विच्छविस्थवीत्यादौ । उ. ४-५६ । क्विन्प्रत्ययान्तो निपातितः । अत एव तशब्दलोपः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । यथा । यथेति पादान्ते । फि. ४-१७ । इति सर्वानुदात्तत्वम् । वाजयन्तः । वाजमात्मन इच्छन्तः । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । न छन्दस्यपुत्रस्येतीत्वदीर्घत्वयोर्निषेधः । अश्वाघस्यादिति पुनर्दीर्घविधानाज्ज्ञापकात् । मंहिष्ठम् । महि वृद्धौ । अतिशयेन मंहिता मंहिष्ठः । तुश्छन्दसि । पा. ५-३-५९ । इति तृजन्तादिष्ठन्प्रत्ययः । तुरिष्ठेमेयःसु । पा. ६-४-१५४ । इति तृलोपः । इष्ठनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सिञ्चे । षिचिर् क्षरणे । व्यत्ययेनैकवचनम् । शे मुचादीनामिति नुमागमः ॥

vājayanto 'nnamicchanto vayaṃ śunaḥśepā he ṛtvigyajamānā vo yuṣmākaṃ saṃbandhinamimamindramindubhiḥ somairāsiñce | sarvataḥ siñcāmahe | tarpayāmaḥ | kīdṛśam | śatakratuṃ śatasaṃkhyākakarmopetaṃ maṃhiṣṭhamatiśayena pravṛddham | secane dṛṣṭāntaḥ | yathā yena prakāreṇa krivimavaṭaṃ jalena pūrayanti tadvat | kriviśabdo vapriḥ | kāṭurityādiṣu caturdaśasu kūpanāmasu kriviḥ kūpaḥ sūda iti paṭhitam ‖ krivim | kṛtī chedane | kṛntata iti kriviḥ | krivighṛṣvicchavisthavītyādau | u. 4-56 | kvinpratyayānto nipātitaḥ | ata eva taśabdalopaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvam | yathā | yatheti pādānte | phi. 4-17 | iti sarvānudāttatvam | vājayantaḥ | vājamātmana icchantaḥ | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | na chandasyaputrasyetītvadīrghatvayorniṣedhaḥ | aśvāghasyāditi punardīrghavidhānājjñāpakāt | maṃhiṣṭham | mahi vṛddhau | atiśayena maṃhitā maṃhiṣṭhaḥ | tuśchandasi | pā. 5-3-59 | iti tṛjantādiṣṭhanpratyayaḥ | turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu | pā. 6-4-154 | iti tṛlopaḥ | iṣṭhano nittvādādyudāttatvam | siñce | ṣicir kṣaraṇe | vyatyayenaikavacanam | śe mucādīnāmiti numāgamaḥ ‖

Translation: "We, the Śunaḥśepas, desiring food (vājayantaḥ), O priests and sacrificers, pour (ā siñce: 'we sprinkle on all sides, we satisfy') this Indra of yours with Soma-juices (indubhiḥ) — Indra who has a hundred rites (śatakratum) and is exceedingly grown (maṃhiṣṭham). The illustration for the sprinkling: as one fills a well (krivim) with water, so. The word krivi is vapriḥ [as printed]: among the fourteen names of a well beginning with kāṭuḥ, 'kriviḥ, kūpaḥ, sūdaḥ' is read." The grammatical tail treats krivim (kṛtī chedane; kvin, by nipātana under Uṇ. 4-56, hence loss of the t; initial udātta as nit), yathā (all-grave at the end of a pāda, Phi. 4-17), vājayantaḥ (kyac; the ī and lengthening prohibited by na chandasy aputrasya, as the separate rule aśvāghasyāt shows), maṃhiṣṭham (iṣṭhan after tṛc by Pā. 5-3-59, loss of tṛ by Pā. 6-4-154) and siñce (singular by vyatyaya; num by śe mucādīnām).

Pratipadārtha pp. 459–460, rendered — वाजयन्तः we who desire food; वः [you], the priests and sacrificers — your; शतक्रतुम् him who is endowed with a hundred deeds; मंहिष्ठम् the exceedingly grown

Rik 1 (continued) pp. 460

Pratipadārtha continued इन्द्रम् Indra; इन्दुभिः with Soma-juices; यथा क्रिविम् as a well [is filled with water]; आ सिञ्चे we fill all round and satisfy.

Bhāvārtha — We who desire food satisfy, on every side, with Soma-juices this your Indra, who has a hundred deeds and is exceedingly great, as a well is filled with water.

English Translation as printed, p. 460

We, desirous of wealth satisfy this your Indra who is the mightiest (among gods) and (is the performer or is praised) in a hundred sacrifices with drops of Soma-juice as a well (is filled with water).

Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — क्रिविम् — kūpaḥ kātuḥ and so on: since the word krivi is read among the fourteen names of a well, krivi means a well. Krivim yathā: as a well is filled with water, so Indra's belly is filled with Soma-juice: much Soma is prepared for Indra's drinking. शतक्रतुम् — kratu is 'act' (Ni. 3-1) and 'wisdom' (Ni. 3-13); hence śatakratu is 'one who has done a hundred mighty deeds' or 'very wise'. The Purāṇas say 'one who did a hundred sacrifices' (Indra obtained Indra's rank so); but that sense does not fit here; the sense intended is 'one who has done a hundred [mighty] deeds'. मंहिष्ठम् — mahi vṛddhau; atiśayena maṃhitā maṃhiṣṭhaḥ: most grown, most excellent. वः इन्द्रम् — 'your Indra', the Indra whom you praise: by the word vaḥ the speech is understood as addressed to the priests. सिञ्चे — ṣicir kṣaraṇe: we make [him] wet, fill; with indubhiḥ: we satisfy Indra with Soma-juices.

Rik 1: grammar pp. 461

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 461, noted briefly — krivim: kṛtī chedane, rudhādi; kvin by nipātana under 'krivi ghṛṣvi chavi sthavi' (U. sū. 4-46, as printed; the bhāṣya, p. 459, prints उ. ४-५६); loss of the t; initial udātta by 'ñnity ādir nityam' (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); accusative singular. yathā: thāl by 'prakāravacane thāl' (Pā. sū. 5-3-23); a for the final by 'tyadādīnām aḥ' (Pā. sū. 7-2-102); all-grave by 'yatheti pādānte' (Phi. sū. 85, as printed; the bhāṣya prints फि. ४-१७). vājayantaḥ: kyac by 'supa ātmanaḥ kyac' (Pā. sū. 3-1-8); ī etc. due by 'kyaci ca' (Pā. sū. 7-4-33) but barred by 'na chandasy aputrasya' (Pā. sū. 7-4-35); 'aśvāghasyāt' (Pā. sū. 7-4-37) as jñāpaka; śatṛ, num (ugit). maṃhiṣṭha: mahi vṛddhau, bhvādi; iṣṭhan by 'tuś chandasi' (Pā. sū. 5-3-59); loss of tṛ by 'turiṣṭhemeyaḥsu' (Pā. sū. 6-4-154); initial udātta. siñce: ṣicir kṣaraṇe, tudādi, laṭ first person plural; singular by 'vyatyayo bahulam' (Pā. sū. 3-1-85); s for ṣ; e by 'ṭita ātmanepa-' (Pā. sū. 3-4-79); num by 'śe mucādīnām' (Pā. sū. 7-1-59); unaccented (tiṅ after a non-tiṅ).

Rik 2 pp. 462–464

Saṃhitā-pāṭha As printed, the anudātta bar stands under वा after शतं and under स of सहस्रं, and the svarita stroke over मा of समाशिरां.

श॒तं वा॒ यः शुची॑नां स॒हस्रं॑ वा॒ समा॑शिरां । एदु॑ नि॒म्नं न री॑यते ॥ २ ॥

śatáṃ vā yáḥ śúcīnāṃ sahásraṃ vā sámāśirāṃ | édu nimnáṃ ná rīyate || 2 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha

शतं । वा । यः । शुचीनां । सहस्रं । वा । संऽआशिरां । आ । इत् । ऊं इति । निम्नं । न । रीयते ॥ २ ॥

śataṃ | vā | yaḥ | śucīnāṃ | sahasraṃ | vā | saṃ 'āśirāṃ | ā | it | ūṃ iti | nimnaṃ | na | rīyate ‖ 2 ‖

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

य इन्द्रः शुचीनां शुद्धानां सोमानां शतं वा शतसंख्याकं समूहं वा । समाशिरां समीचीनेनाशिराख्येन श्रपणद्रव्येणोपेतानां सोमानां सहस्रं वा सहस्रसंख्याकं समूहं वा एदुरीयते । आगच्छत्येव । सोऽस्माननुगृह्णात्विति शेषः । सोमप्राप्तौ दृष्टान्तः । निम्नं न । यथा निम्नप्रदेशमाप आप्नुवन्ति तद्वत् ॥ समाशिराम् । श्रीञ् पाक इत्यस्य समाङ्पूर्वस्य क्विप्यपस्पृधेथामित्यादावाशीरादेशो निपातितः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । रीयते । रीङ् श्रवणे । दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् ॥

ya indraḥ śucīnāṃ śuddhānāṃ somānāṃ śataṃ vā śatasaṃkhyākaṃ samūhaṃ vā | samāśirāṃ samīcīnenāśirākhyena śrapaṇadravyeṇopetānāṃ somānāṃ sahasraṃ vā sahasrasaṃkhyākaṃ samūhaṃ vā edurīyate | āgacchatyeva | so 'smānanugṛhṇātviti śeṣaḥ | somaprāptau dṛṣṭāntaḥ | nimnaṃ na | yathā nimnapradeśamāpa āpnuvanti tadvat ‖ samāśirām | śrīñ pāka ityasya samāṅpūrvasya kvipyapaspṛdhethāmityādāvāśīrādeśo nipātitaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | rīyate | rīṅ śravaṇe | divādibhyaḥ śyan ‖

Translation: "The Indra who [receives] a hundred — a group of a hundred — of pure Soma-offerings, or a thousand — a group of a thousand — of Soma-offerings joined with the āśir, the right cooking (mixing) substance: he comes (ed u rīyate) — comes indeed; [the supplied rest:] 'may he favour us'. Illustration of reaching the Soma: nimnaṃ na — as waters reach a low place, so." The grammatical tail treats samāśirām (śrīñ pāke with sam and āṅ; kvip; the substitute āśīr fixed by nipātana in the rule beginning apaspṛdhethām; a bahuvrīhi with the first member's own accent) and rīyate (rīṅ śravaṇe; śyan of the divādi class). No sūtra numbers are printed in the bhāṣya.

Pratipadārtha p. 462, rendered — यः which Indra; शुचीनाम् of pure; शतं वा a hundred [Soma-juices] or; समाशिराम् of Soma-juices mixed with purified sweet substances; सहस्रं वा a thousand [to receive them]; निम्नं न as water [flows] to a low place; एदु रीयते comes (naturally) [may that Indra favour us].

Bhāvārtha — May that Indra, who accepts a hundred pure Soma-juices and a thousand mixed with sweet substances, come to us, easy and natural, like a stream of water flowing to a low place, and favour us.

Rik 2 (continued) pp. 463

English Translation as printed, p. 463

May he who (drinks) of a hundred pure and thousand mixed libations of Soma come to this sacrifice as water runs to a low place.

Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — शतं, सहस्रम् — though śata and sahasra mean only a hundred and a thousand, the sense is a hundred or a thousand vessels (or sacrificial offerings) of Soma-juice. समाशिराम् — Soma-juices joined with āśir substances: milk, curds, barley-meal; with milk it is gavāśir, with curds dadhyāśir, with barley yavāśir; the rik names none, so it is Soma mixed with some one of them. आ इत् उ रीयते — āgacchaty eva, dhāvaty eva: he does come, comes quickly. निम्नं न — nimna is a low place, a hollow; as water runs naturally to a lower place, so Indra comes to our sacrifice to drink Soma.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 463–464, noted briefly — samāśirām: śrīñ pāke, kryādi, with sam and āṅ; kvip by 'kvip ca' (Pā. sū. 3-2-76); āśīr by nipātana under 'apaspṛdhethām ānṛcuḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-1-36); genitive plural; first-member accent by 'bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam' (Pā. sū. 6-2-1), initial udātta. rīyate: rīṅ śravaṇe, divādi, the sense changed by the preverb; ātmanepada (ṅit); e by 'ṭita ātmanepadānām' (Pā. sū. 3-4-79); śyan by 'divādibhyaḥ śyan' (Pā. sū. 3-1-69); unaccented by 'tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ' (Pā. sū. 8-1-28).

Rik 3 pp. 464–466

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

सं यन्मदा॑य शु॒ष्मिण॑ ए॒ना ह्य॑स्यो॒दरे॑ । स॒मु॒द्रो न व्यचो॑ द॒धे ॥ ३ ॥

saṃ yanmádāya śuṣmíṇa enā́ hyasyodáre | samudró na vyáco dadhé || 3 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha

सं । यत् । मदाय । शुष्मिणे । एना । हि । अस्य । उदरे । समुद्रः । न । व्यचः । दधे ॥ ३ ॥

saṃ | yat | madāya | śuṣmiṇe | enā | hi | asya | udare | samudraḥ | na | vyacaḥ | dadhe ‖ 3 ‖

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya The bhāṣya runs over the page break after संप्र- (p. 464) / सारणं (p. 465).

यत्पूर्वोक्तं शतं सहस्रं वा शुष्मिणे बलवत इन्द्रस्य मदाय मदार्थं संगतं भवति । एना ह्यनेनैव शतेन सहस्रेण चास्येन्द्रस्योदरे व्यचो व्याप्तिर्दधे । धृता भवति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । समुद्रो न समुद्र इव । यथा समुद्रमध्ये जलं व्याप्तं तद्वत् ॥ एना । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयाया आडादेशः । व्यचः । व्यचेः कुटादित्वमनसि । का. १-२-१-१ । इति ङिद्वद्भावस्य प्रतिषिद्धत्वाद्ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना संप्रसारणं न भवति असुनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । दधे । दधातेः कर्मण्यभ्यासह्रस्वजश्त्वेषु कृतेष्वातो लोप इटि चेत्याकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । हि चेति प्रतिषेधान्निघाताभावः ॥

yatpūrvoktaṃ śataṃ sahasraṃ vā śuṣmiṇe balavata indrasya madāya madārthaṃ saṃgataṃ bhavati | enā hyanenaiva śatena sahasreṇa cāsyendrasyodare vyaco vyāptirdadhe | dhṛtā bhavati | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | samudro na samudra iva | yathā samudramadhye jalaṃ vyāptaṃ tadvat ‖ enā | supāṃ sulugiti tṛtīyāyā āḍādeśaḥ | vyacaḥ | vyaceḥ kuṭāditvamanasi | kā. 1-2-1-1 | iti ṅidvadbhāvasya pratiṣiddhatvādgrahijyetyādinā saṃprasāraṇaṃ na bhavati asuno nittvādādyudāttatvam | dadhe | dadhāteḥ karmaṇyabhyāsahrasvajaśtveṣu kṛteṣvāto lopa iṭi cetyākāralopaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttatvam | hi ceti pratiṣedhānnighātābhāvaḥ ‖

Translation: "The aforesaid hundred or thousand [of Soma] is brought together for the exhilaration (madāya) of mighty (śuṣmiṇe: strong) Indra. By this very hundred and thousand (enā hi), in this Indra's belly, the pervasion (vyacaḥ) is held (dadhe): is held. Illustration: samudro na — like the sea: as water pervades the middle of the sea, so." The grammatical tail treats enā (ā for the instrumental by supāṃ suluk), vyacaḥ (the kuṭādi status of vyac is denied before asi (Kā. 1-2-1-1), so the ṅit-like treatment lapses and grahijyā… gives no saṃprasāraṇa; initial udātta as asun is nit) and dadhe (passive liṭ; after the reduplicated syllable's shortening and jaś, loss of ā by āto lopa iṭi ca; final udātta by the suffix accent; not made grave because of hi ca).

Rik 3 (continued) pp. 465

Pratipadārtha p. 465, rendered — यत् those (described before) hundreds and thousands of Soma-juices; शुष्मिणे for the strong Indra; मदाय for satisfaction (exhilaration); एना हि these [Soma-juices]; समुद्रः न as the sea [is filled with water]; अस्य this Indra's; उदरे in the belly; व्यचः दधे [they] fill.
