Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 505, noted briefly — samānayojanaḥ: 'samānaṃ yojanaṃ yasya', bahuvrīhi; first-member accent by 'bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam' (Pā. sū. 6-2-1): the ā after n of samāna is udātta. vām: genitive dual of yuṣmad; vām for the stem with its ending by 'yuṣmadasmadoḥ ṣaṣṭhīcaturthī-' (Pā. sū. 8-1-20); grave. amartyaḥ: 'na martyaḥ', nañ tatpuruṣa; the indeclinable first member keeps its accent by 'tatpuruṣe tulyārtha-' (Pā. sū. 6-2-2): initial udātta. īyate: īṅ gatau, divādi, laṭ third person singular ta; e by 'ṭita ātmanepadānām' (Pā. sū. 3-4-79); śyan by 'divādibhyaḥ śyan' (Pā. sū. 3-1-69); the lasārvadhātuka grave by 'tāsyanudātteṭ-' (Pā. sū. 6-1-186); initial udātta, śyan being nit, by 'ñnity ādir nityam' (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); though after a non-tiṅ, not grave, because of hi, by 'hi ca' (Pā. sū. 8-1-34). aśvinā: vocative dual; pūrvasavarṇadīrgha by 'supāṃ suluk' (Pā. sū. 7-1-39).

Rik 19 (to the Aśvins) pp. 506–508

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Line 1 flagged [accent ?]: besides the bar under न्य and the stroke over स्य, a second stroke stands over घ्न्य; it is not entered.

न्य॒घ्न्य॑स्य मू॒र्धनि॑ च॒क्रं रथ॑स्य येमथुः । [accent ?] प॒रि द्याम॒न्यदी॑यते ॥ १९ ॥

nyaghnyasya mūrdháni cakráṃ ráthasya yemathuḥ | [accent ?] parí dyāmanyádīyate || 19 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha

नि । अघ्न्यस्य । मूर्धनि । चक्रं । रथस्य । येमथुः । परि । द्यां । अन्यत् । ईयते ॥ १९ ॥

ni | aghnyasya | mūrdhani | cakraṃ | rathasya | yemathuḥ | pari | dyāṃ | anyat | īyate ‖ 19 ‖

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे अश्विनौ युवामघ्न्यस्य हन्तुं विनाशयितुमशक्यस्य दृढस्य पर्वतस्य मूर्धन्युपरि चक्रं भवदीयरथसंबन्ध्येकं चक्रं नि येमथुः । नियमितवन्तौ । अन्यच्चक्रं परि द्यां द्युलोकस्य परित ईयते । गच्छति ॥ अघ्न्यस्य । अहननमघ्नः । घञर्थे कविधानं स्थास्नापाव्यधिहनियुध्यर्थम् । पा. ३-३-५८-४ । इति हन्तेः कप्रत्ययः । अघ्नमर्हत्यघ्न्यः । छन्दसि च । पा. ५-१-६७ । इति यप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । येमथुः । यम उपरमे । कित लिट्यत एकहल्मध्ये । पा. ६-४-१२० । इत्येत्वाभ्यासलोपौ ॥

he aśvinau yuvāmaghnyasya hantuṃ vināśayitumaśakyasya dṛḍhasya parvatasya mūrdhanyupari cakraṃ bhavadīyarathasaṃbandhyekaṃ cakraṃ ni yemathuḥ | niyamitavantau | anyaccakraṃ pari dyāṃ dyulokasya parita īyate | gacchati ‖ aghnyasya | ahananamaghnaḥ | ghañarthe kavidhānaṃ sthāsnāpāvyadhihaniyudhyartham | pā. 3-3-58-4 | iti hanteḥ kapratyayaḥ | aghnamarhatyaghnyaḥ | chandasi ca | pā. 5-1-67 | iti yapratyayaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttatvam | yemathuḥ | yama uparame | kita liṭyata ekahalmadhye | pā. 6-4-120 | ityetvābhyāsalopau ‖

Translation: "O Aśvins, you have fixed (ni yemathuḥ: fixed) one wheel belonging to your chariot on the summit (mūrdhani, above) of the aghnya — the firm mountain that cannot be struck, that is, destroyed; the other wheel goes (īyate) round heaven (pari dyām)." The grammatical tail treats aghnyasya ('not striking' = aghna; ka after han in the sense of ghañ by the vārttika on Pā. 3-3-58; 'what deserves the aghna' = aghnya, with ya by 'chandasi ca', Pā. 5-1-67; end-acute by the suffix) and yemathuḥ (yama uparame; e and loss of the reduplicate by Pā. 6-4-120).

Pratipadārtha p. 506, rendered — दस्रौ [O Aśvin gods]; अघ्न्यस्य of what cannot be destroyed by anyone — a firm mountain; मूर्धनि on the upper peak; रथस्य चक्रम् one wheel of [your] chariot; नि येमथुः you have fixed; अन्यत् the other wheel; परि द्याम् round heaven; ईयते goes.

Bhāvārtha — O Aśvins! You have fixed one wheel of your chariot on the summit of a mountain that no one can destroy; and the other wheel goes about heaven.

Rik 19 (continued) pp. 507

English Translation as printed, p. 507

You have placed one wheel on the summit of the solid mountain, the other goes round the heaven.

Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — अघ्न्यस्य — hantuṃ vināśayitum aśakyasya dṛḍhasya parvatasya: impossible to destroy, that is, of a firm or steady mountain: so the commentator explains; Skandasvāmin explains this word as 'of Prajāpati' or 'of the Sun', because of the rik

सप्त युञ्जन्ति रथमेकचक्रमेको अश्वो वहति सप्तनामा ।

sapta yuñjanti rathamekacakrameko aśvo vahati saptanāmā |

Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-164-2, as the source gives it; editorial and tentative: "Seven yoke the one-wheeled chariot; one horse of seven names draws it" — so that though the Aśvins' chariot has three wheels, one of them is near the Sun. नि येमथुः — yama uparame: you have fixed. परि द्याम् अन्यत् ईयते — another wheel goes round heaven or the atmosphere. Since in many places the Aśvins' chariot is said to have three wheels (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-34-9 etc.), the third wheel is not located in this Rik.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 507–508, noted briefly — aghnyasya: 'ahananam aghnaḥ'; ka after han in the sense of ghañ by 'ghañarthe kavidhānaṃ sthāsnāpāvyadhihaniyudhyartham' (Pā. sū. 3-3-58-4); as ka is kit, loss of the penult by 'gamahana-' (Pā. sū. 6-4-98); gh for h before n by 'ho hanter ñṇinneṣu' (Pā. sū. 7-3-54); nañ compound with ghna; in the sense 'aghnam arhati' yat by 'chandasi ca' (Pā. sū. 5-1-67); loss of a before y by 'yasyeti ca' (Pā. sū. 6-4-148); genitive singular; as the suffix is initial-acute, aghnya is end-acute. mūrdhani: the a of an in the bha stem optionally dropped by 'vibhāṣā ṅiśyoḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-4-136). yemathuḥ: yama uparame, bhvādi, liṭ second person dual thas; athus for it by 'parasmaipadānām' (Pā. sū. 3-4-82); kit by 'asaṃyogāl liṭ kit' (Pā. sū. 1-2-5); then by 'ata ekahalmadhye' (Pā. sū. 6-4-120), after the doubling, e and loss of the reduplicate; grave after a non-tiṅ. īyate: explained in the preceding mantra.

Rik 20 (first of the Uṣas Riks) pp. 508–513

Saṃhitā-pāṭha As printed, line 1 reads कस्ते उषः. Line 1 flagged [accent ?]: the only bar stands under जे of भुजे (not under भु); the strokes stand over स्ते and र्तो. In line 2 the stroke is over न of नक्षसे.

कस्ते॑ उषः कधप्रिये भु॒जे॒ मर्तो॑ अमर्त्ये । [accent ?] कं न॑क्षसे विभावरि ॥ २० ॥

káste uṣaḥ kadhapriye bhuje márto amartye | [accent ?] káṃ nakṣase vibhāvari || 20 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha

कः । ते । उषः । कधऽप्रिये । भुजे । मर्तः । अमर्त्ये । कं । नक्षसे । विभाऽवरि ॥ २० ॥

kaḥ | te | uṣaḥ | kadha 'priye | bhuje | martaḥ | amartye | kaṃ | nakṣase | vibhā 'vari ‖ 20 ‖

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

प्रातरनुवाक आश्विनशस्त्र उषस्ये क्रतौ गायत्रे छन्दसि कस्त उष इति तृचः । अथोषस्य इति खण्डे कस्त उष इति तिस्रः । आ. ४-१४ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥ अश्विभ्यां प्रेरितः शुनःशेप उषसं तुष्टाव । तथा च ब्राह्मणम् । तमश्विना ऊचतुरुषसं नु स्तुह्यथ त्वोत्स्रक्ष्याम इति स उषसं तुष्टावात उत्तरेण तृचेन तस्य ह स्मर्च्यृच्युक्तायां वि पाशो मुमुचे कनीय ऐक्ष्वाकस्योदरं भवत्युत्तमस्यामेवर्च्युक्तायां वि पाशो मुमुचेऽगद ऐक्ष्वाक आस । ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१६ । इति ॥ हे कधप्रिये स्तुतिप्रिये अमर्त्ये मरणरहिते उष एतच्छब्दाभिधेय उषःकालाभिमानिनि देवते भुजे तव भोगाय मर्तो मनुष्यः को विद्यते । हे विभावरि विशेषप्रभावयुक्त उषो देवि कं पुरुषं नक्षसे । प्राप्नोषि । तवोचितं भोगं दातुं न कोऽपि मनुष्यः समर्थः । अत एव त्वं कमपि पुरुषं भोगापेक्षया न प्राप्नोषि । ईदृशस्तव महिमेत्यर्थः ॥ ते । तेमयावेकवचनस्य । पा. ८-१-२२ । इति युष्मच्छब्दस्य ते आदेशः सर्वानुदात्तः । कधप्रिये । कथ वाक्यप्रबन्धे । चुरादिरदन्तः । णावतो लोपस्य स्थानिवद्भावादुपधावृद्ध्यभावः । चिन्तिपूजिकथिकुम्बिचर्चश्च । पा. ३-३-१०५ । इत्यङ्प्रत्ययः । णेरनिटीति णिलोपः । ततष्टाप् । षष्ठीसमासे ङ्यापोः संज्ञाछन्दसोर्बहुलम् । पा. ६-३-६३ । इति ह्रस्वत्वम् । थकारस्य धकारश्छान्दसः । आमन्त्रितानुदात्तत्वम् । भुजे । भुज पालनाभ्यवहारयोः । संपदादिलक्षणः क्विप् । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । मर्तः । असिहसीत्यादिना तन्प्रत्ययान्त आद्युदात्तः । नक्षसे । तृक्ष ष्टृक्ष णक्ष गतौ । विभावरि । भा दीप्तौ । विपूर्वादस्मादातो मनिन्क्वनिब्वनिपश्चेति वनिप् । वनो र च । पा. ४-१-७ । इति ङीप् । तत्संनियोगेन नकारस्य रेफादेशः । अम्बार्थनद्योर्ह्रस्वः । पा. ७-३-१०७ । इति ह्रस्वत्वम् ॥

prātaranuvāka āśvinaśastra uṣasye kratau gāyatre chandasi kasta uṣa iti tṛcaḥ | athoṣasya iti khaṇḍe kasta uṣa iti tisraḥ | ā. 4-14 | iti sūtritam ‖ aśvibhyāṃ preritaḥ śunaḥśepa uṣasaṃ tuṣṭāva | tathā ca brāhmaṇam | tamaśvinā ūcaturuṣasaṃ nu stuhyatha tvotsrakṣyāma iti sa uṣasaṃ tuṣṭāvāta uttareṇa tṛcena tasya ha smarcyṛcyuktāyāṃ vi pāśo mumuce kanīya aikṣvākasyodaraṃ bhavatyuttamasyāmevarcyuktāyāṃ vi pāśo mumuce 'gada aikṣvāka āsa | ai. brā. 7-16 | iti ‖ he kadhapriye stutipriye amartye maraṇarahite uṣa etacchabdābhidheya uṣaḥkālābhimānini devate bhuje tava bhogāya marto manuṣyaḥ ko vidyate | he vibhāvari viśeṣaprabhāvayukta uṣo devi kaṃ puruṣaṃ nakṣase | prāpnoṣi | tavocitaṃ bhogaṃ dātuṃ na ko 'pi manuṣyaḥ samarthaḥ | ata eva tvaṃ kamapi puruṣaṃ bhogāpekṣayā na prāpnoṣi | īdṛśastava mahimetyarthaḥ ‖ te | temayāvekavacanasya | pā. 8-1-22 | iti yuṣmacchabdasya te ādeśaḥ sarvānudāttaḥ | kadhapriye | katha vākyaprabandhe | curādiradantaḥ | ṇāvato lopasya sthānivadbhāvādupadhāvṛddhyabhāvaḥ | cintipūjikathikumbicarcaśca | pā. 3-3-105 | ityaṅpratyayaḥ | ṇeraniṭīti ṇilopaḥ | tataṣṭāp | ṣaṣṭhīsamāse ṅyāpoḥ saṃjñāchandasorbahulam | pā. 6-3-63 | iti hrasvatvam | thakārasya dhakāraśchāndasaḥ | āmantritānudāttatvam | bhuje | bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ | saṃpadādilakṣaṇaḥ kvip | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvam | martaḥ | asihasītyādinā tanpratyayānta ādyudāttaḥ | nakṣase | tṛkṣa ṣṭṛkṣa ṇakṣa gatau | vibhāvari | bhā dīptau | vipūrvādasmādāto maninkvanibvanipaśceti vanip | vano ra ca | pā. 4-1-7 | iti ṅīp | tatsaṃniyogena nakārasya rephādeśaḥ | ambārthanadyorhrasvaḥ | pā. 7-3-107 | iti hrasvatvam ‖

Translation: "In the morning litany, in the Āśvina-śastra, at the Uṣas rite, in the Gāyatrī metre, the triplet kas ta uṣaḥ; laid down in the section athoṣasyaḥ: 'the three beginning kas ta uṣaḥ' (Āś. 4-14). Impelled by the Aśvins, Śunaḥśepa praised Uṣas; so the Brāhmaṇa: 'The Aśvins said to him: "Praise Uṣas now; then we shall let you go." He praised Uṣas with the following triplet. As each Rik was spoken the fetter loosened and the belly of the Aikṣvāka grew smaller; when the last Rik was spoken the fetter was loosened and the Aikṣvāka was free of disease' (Ai. Br. 7-16). O kadhapriye (fond of praise), amartye (deathless) Uṣas — the deity presiding over the dawn-time, the one named by this word! What mortal (martaḥ: man) is there for your enjoyment (bhuje)? O vibhāvari (endowed with special splendour), goddess Uṣas, which man do you reach (nakṣase)? No man is able to give the enjoyment fitting you; therefore you go to no man in expectation of enjoyment: such is your greatness." The grammatical tail treats te (Pā. 8-1-22, all grave), kadhapriye (katha, an a-final curādi root; no vṛddhi of the penult because the lost a counts before ṇi; aṅ by Pā. 3-3-105; loss of ṇi; ṭāp; shortening in the genitive compound by Pā. 6-3-63; dh for th, Vedic; grave as a vocative), bhuje (kvip of the saṃpad group; the ending udātta by sāv ekācaḥ), martaḥ (initial udātta, ending in tan by asihasi…), nakṣase (tṛkṣa stṛkṣa ṇakṣa gatau) and vibhāvari (vanip; ṅīp and r for n by Pā. 4-1-7; shortening by Pā. 7-3-107).

Rik 20 (continued) pp. 509

Pratipadārtha p. 509, rendered — कधप्रिये fond of praises; अमर्त्ये free from death; उषः O goddess Uṣas; भुजे for your enjoyment; मर्तः a mortal; कः which one [is there]; विभावरि O Uṣas, possessed of special lustre; कम् which man; नक्षसे you reach (do you reach).

Bhāvārtha — O goddess Uṣas, fond of praise and deathless! Which mortal is there to enjoy you? O Uṣas of special lustre! Which man do you come to of your own will?

English Translation as printed, p. 509

O immortal Ushas, fond of praises, what mortal is fit for your enjoyment ? O fair one, to whom do you go ?

Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — After praising the Aśvins, Śunaḥśepa, impelled by them, praises Uṣas with this and the two following Riks; on this the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa has tam aśvinā ūcatur uṣasaṃ nu stuhy atha tvotsrakṣyāma iti… (Ai. Br. 7-16); its meaning was given in the Śunaḥśepa narrative. On Uṣas: the deity of this Rik and the two that follow is the dawn, or the deity who presides over it; in the Ṛgveda there are about twenty sūktas to Uṣas, mostly of the best class, in both the description of colour and the arrangement of words and sense. Uṣas is the light before sunrise, when night is gone; since dawn is the time of great joy for sages and all people, they describe it beautifully. Poets imagine the dawn as a young woman and describe her qualities with ornaments; because light comes from the sky she is divo duhitā, 'daughter of heaven'; she is ever young, shortens men's lives as days pass, gladdens all creatures as soon as she rises, drives away demons and night-wanderers, wakes the cows with morning light so that they go out lowing, and, since the sun's rays at sunrise are slightly red, she is said to travel swiftly on a chariot drawn by red horses or red oxen. Derivation of uṣas — Yāska: As printed, p. 510: the definition stands as one line, then a Kannada link "how did the word uṣā arise? —", then the rest; the second पुनरियमुषाः is followed by a printed "?".

उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः ॥ उच्छतीति सत्याः । उच्छी विवासे । विवासयति हीयं तमांसि तस्मादुच्छतीत्येनमस्या उषा इत्येतदभिधानं भवति । पुनरियमुषा? रात्रेरपरः कालः ॥ (नि. २-१९)

uṣāḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ ‖ ucchatīti satyāḥ | ucchī vivāse | vivāsayati hīyaṃ tamāṃsi tasmāducchatītyenamasyā uṣā ityetadabhidhānaṃ bhavati | punariyamuṣā? rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ ‖ (ni. 2-19)

editorial and tentative: "Why is it uṣas? Because it shines forth (ucchati): truly, the time after night. Ucchī is 'to dispel': for she dispels the darkness; hence the name uṣā." In another place Yāska gives a different derivation:

Rik 20 (continued) pp. 511

उषाः वष्टेः कान्तिकर्मण उच्छतेरितरा माध्यमिका । (नि. १२-७)

uṣāḥ vaṣṭeḥ kāntikarmaṇa ucchateritarā mādhyamikā | (ni. 12-7)

Mine, tentative: "Uṣas is from vaṣṭi (to shine); the other, from ucchati, is optional [mādhyamikā]." That is, uṣas may be derived from vaś kāntau ('to shine'); the derivation from ucchī is optional. The sages describe the goddess with many epithets — beloved of the Sun, daughter of night, sister of Āditya, Bhaga and Varuṇa, daughter of heaven, friend of the Aśvins. दुहितर्दिवः — since the sun's light comes to us from heaven (the atmosphere), and dawn precedes sunrise, she is called divo duhitā ("daughter of heaven", English as printed). कधप्रिये — stotrapriye: fond of hearing praises. भुजे — bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ; bhogāya: "for enjoyment" (English as printed). नक्षसे — nakṣ gatau: you reach, you seek. विभावरि — bhā dīptau: shining with light or beauty (Ni. 2-19). Skandasvāmin explains bhuje as pālanāya 'for protection', and kaṃ nakṣase bhuje as 'to protect which man do you go?'.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 511–513, noted briefly — te: genitive singular of yuṣmad; te by 'temayāv ekavacanasya' (Pā. sū. 8-1-22); all grave by 'anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau' (Pā. sū. 8-1-18). kadhapriye: katha vākyaprabandhe, curādi, a-final; ṇic by 'satyāpapāśa-' (Pā. sū. 3-1-25); loss of a by 'ato lopaḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-4-48); root by 'sanādyantā dhātavaḥ' (Pā. sū. 3-1-32); by 'acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau' (Pā. sū. 1-1-57) no vṛddhi by 'ata upadhāyāḥ' (Pā. sū. 7-2-116); aṅ by 'cintipūjikathikumbicarcaś ca' (Pā. sū. 3-3-105); loss of ṇi by 'ṇer aniṭi' (Pā. sū. 6-4-51); ṭāp by 'ajādyataṣ ṭāp' (Pā. sū. 4-1-4): kathā; 'kathāyāḥ priyā', genitive compound; shortening by 'ṅyāpoḥ saṃjñāchandasor bahulam' (Pā. sū. 6-3-63); dh for th, Vedic; all grave by 'āmantritasya ca', not being at the head of a pāda. bhuje: bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ, rudhādi; kvip by 'saṃpadādibhyaḥ kvip' (Vā. 2233), the whole suffix dropped; dative singular; the ending, grave by 'anudāttau suppitau', made udātta by 'sāv ekācas tṛtīyādiḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-1-168). martaḥ: mṛṅ prāṇatyāge; tan by the sūtra 'asihasi-'; guṇa; initial udātta, tan being nit, by 'ñnity ādir nityam' (Pā. sū. 6-1-197). nakṣase: tṛkṣa stṛkṣa ṇakṣa gatau; n for ṇ by 'ṇo naḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-1-65); se for thās by 'thāsaḥ se' (Pā. sū. 3-4-80); śap by 'kartari śap' (Pā. sū. 3-1-68). vibhāvari: bhā dīptau, adādi; vanip after vi by 'āto manin kvanip vanipaś ca' (Pā. sū. 3-4-[2 or 7]4, so printed; the bhāṣya does not number it; the second digit is the ಳ-shaped 4); ṅīp by 'vano ra ca' (Pā. sū. 4-1-7), with r for n; in the vocative the nadī shortened by 'ambārthanadyor hrasvaḥ' (Pā. sū. 7-3-107); all grave by 'āmantritasya ca'.

Rik 21 (to Uṣas) pp. 513–514

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Line 2 flagged [accent ?]: the bar stands under श्वे, not under अ.

व॒यं हि ते॒ अम॑न्म॒ह्यान्ता॒दा प॑रा॒कात् । अश्वे॒ न चि॑त्रे अरुषि ॥ २१ ॥ [accent ?]

vayáṃ hi te ámanmahyā́ntādā́ parākā́t | aśve ná citre aruṣi || 21 || [accent ?] Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha

वयं । हि । ते । अमन्महि । आ । अन्तात् । आ । पराकात् । अश्वे । न । चित्रे । अरुषि ॥ २१ ॥

vayaṃ | hi | te | amanmahi | ā | antāt | ā | parākāt | aśve | na | citre | aruṣi ‖ 21 ‖

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

अश्वे व्यापनशीले चित्रे चायनीये अरुषि आरोचमान उषःकालाभिमानिनि देवते तव स्वरूपमान्तात्समीपपर्यन्तमा पराकाद्दूरपर्यन्तं वयं मनुष्या नामन्महि । न बोद्धुं समर्थाः । हिशब्दः प्रसिद्धौ । देवतामहिम्नः पारावारयोरज्ञानमस्मासु प्रसिद्धमित्यर्थः ॥ अमन्महि । मन ज्ञाने । बहुलं छन्दसीति बहुलवचनात् श्यनो लुक् । लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । अश्वे । अशू व्याप्तौ । अशिप्रुषीत्यादिना क्वन्प्रत्ययः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

aśve vyāpanaśīle citre cāyanīye aruṣi ārocamāna uṣaḥkālābhimānini devate tava svarūpamāntātsamīpaparyantamā parākāddūraparyantaṃ vayaṃ manuṣyā nāmanmahi | na boddhuṃ samarthāḥ | hiśabdaḥ prasiddhau | devatāmahimnaḥ pārāvārayorajñānamasmāsu prasiddhamityarthaḥ ‖ amanmahi | mana jñāne | bahulaṃ chandasīti bahulavacanāt śyano luk | luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣvaḍudāttaḥ | hi ceti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | aśve | aśū vyāptau | aśipruṣītyādinā kvanpratyayaḥ | āmantritādyudāttatvam ‖

Translation: "O pervading (aśve), lovely (citre: to be looked at), shining (aruṣi) goddess presiding over the dawn-time! Your nature, from near (āntāt: up to what is close) to far (ā parākāt: up to what is distant), we men do not know (na amanmahi): we are unable to understand it. The word hi is in the sense 'well known': that we do not know the near and far shores of the goddess's greatness is well known among us." The grammatical tail treats amanmahi (mana jñāne; luk of śyan by the word bahula in bahulaṃ chandasi; the augment aṭ udātta; not grave by hi ca) and aśve (aśū vyāptau; kvan by aśipruṣi…; initial udātta of the vocative).

Pratipadārtha p. 513, rendered — अश्वे [O Uṣas,] widely pervading; चित्रे of many-coloured splendour; अरुषि shining; आ अन्तात् from your form that is near; आ पराकात् from your form that is far; वयम् we [mortals]; न अमन्महि cannot know.

Rik 21 (continued) pp. 514

Bhāvārtha — O goddess Uṣas, widely pervading, of manifold hue and shining! Your greatness is immeasurable. We mortals are unable rightly to know your greatness, whether in your form near us or in your form far away.

English Translation as printed, p. 514

O Ushas, spreading in all places, with tinted and brilliant rays we do not know your limit whether we are near or far off.

Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — अश्वे — aśū vyāptau: she who pervades everything, all regions, with her rays. चित्रे — endowed with manifold splendour. अरुषे [as printed, for अरुषि] — shining. अश्वे चित्रे अरुषि — Skandasvāmin explains: vicitra, that is, endowed with horses of various colours; and citre as 'worshipful'.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā p. 514, noted briefly — te: explained in the thirtieth mantra [as printed; the explanation is in Ṛk 20]. amanmahi: mana jñāne, divādi, laṅ first person plural mahiṅ; śyan due by 'divādibhyaḥ śyan' is dropped by 'bahulaṃ chandasi'; aṭ to the stem (Pā. sū. 6-4-71, so printed), and as aṭ is 'udāttaḥ' the word is initial-acute; the tiṅ-lowering barred by 'hi ca' (Pā. sū. 8-1-34). aśve: printed as a vocative dual form; aśū vyāptau, rudhādi; kvan by 'aśipruṣilaṭikaṇi-' (U. sū. 1-149); at the head of the pāda the all-grave accent does not come (apādādau); initial udātta by 'āmantritasya' (Pā. sū. 6-1-198). citre, aruṣi: all grave by 'āmantritasya ca' (Pā. sū. 8-1-19).

Rik 22 (last Rik; to Uṣas) pp. 515–517

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Line 1 flagged [accent ?]: the first svarita stroke stands over रा (of त्येभिरा), not over ग; the bars are under भि and हि, the second stroke over जे.

त्वं त्येभि॒रा॑ गहि॒ वाजे॑भिर्दुहितर्दिवः । [accent ?] अ॒स्मे र॒यिं नि धा॑रय ॥ २२ ॥

tvaṃ tyebhirā gahi vā́jebhirduhitardivaḥ | [accent ?] asmé rayíṃ ní dhāraya || 22 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha

त्वं । त्येभिः । आ । गहि । वाजेभिः । दुहितः । दिवः । अस्मे इति । रयिं । नि । धारय ॥ २२ ॥

tvaṃ | tyebhiḥ | ā | gahi | vājebhiḥ | duhitaḥ | divaḥ | asme iti | rayiṃ | ni | dhāraya ‖ 22 ‖

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya The bhāṣya ends with ॥ ३१ ॥ ॥ ६ ॥: the varga number 31 (as in the page header, Varga 31) and the end of the sixth anuvāka.

हे दिवो दुहितर्द्युदेवतायाः पुत्रि उषो देवि त्येभिर्वाजेभिस्तैरन्नैः सह त्वमा गहि । अत्रागच्छ । अस्मे अस्मासु रयिं धनं नि धारय । नितरां स्थापय ॥ त्येभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति त्यद्शब्दाद्भिस ऐसादेशाभावः । गहि । असकृदुक्तम् । दुहितर्दिवः । परस्यापि दिव इत्यस्य दिवो दुहितरित्यन्वये सति पूर्ववत्त्वात्सुबामन्त्रित इति पराङ्गवद्भावेन षष्ठ्यामन्त्रितसमुदायस्य सर्वानुदात्तत्वम् । यद्वा । कार्यकालं हि संज्ञापरिभाषम् । परि. ३ । इति न्यायेन सुबामन्त्रित इत्यस्यामन्त्रितस्य चेत्याष्टमिकेन योगेनैकवाक्यत्वे सति परत्वात्पराङ्गवद्भावे सति सर्वानुदात्तत्वम् । कृतस्वरयोः षष्ठ्यामन्त्रितयोः पश्चाद्व्यत्ययो बहुलमिति व्यत्यस्तप्रयोगः । अस्मे । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्याः शे आदेशः ॥ ॥ ३१ ॥ ॥ ६ ॥

he divo duhitardyudevatāyāḥ putri uṣo devi tyebhirvājebhistairannaiḥ saha tvamā gahi | atrāgaccha | asme asmāsu rayiṃ dhanaṃ ni dhāraya | nitarāṃ sthāpaya ‖ tyebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti tyadśabdādbhisa aisādeśābhāvaḥ | gahi | asakṛduktam | duhitardivaḥ | parasyāpi diva ityasya divo duhitarityanvaye sati pūrvavattvātsubāmantrita iti parāṅgavadbhāvena ṣaṣṭhyāmantritasamudāyasya sarvānudāttatvam | yadvā | kāryakālaṃ hi saṃjñāparibhāṣam | pari. 3 | iti nyāyena subāmantrita ityasyāmantritasya cetyāṣṭamikena yogenaikavākyatve sati paratvātparāṅgavadbhāve sati sarvānudāttatvam | kṛtasvarayoḥ ṣaṣṭhyāmantritayoḥ paścādvyatyayo bahulamiti vyatyastaprayogaḥ | asme | supāṃ sulugiti saptamyāḥ śe ādeśaḥ ‖ ‖ 31 ‖ ‖ 6 ‖

Translation: "O daughter of heaven (divo duhitaḥ: daughter of the heaven-deity), goddess Uṣas, come (ā gahi: come here) with those (tyebhiḥ) foods (vājebhiḥ); establish (ni dhāraya: set firmly) wealth (rayim) in us (asme)." The grammatical tail treats tyebhiḥ (no ais for bhis after tyad, by bahulaṃ chandasi), gahi ('said more than once'), duhitar divaḥ (though divaḥ follows, it is construed first, so by subāmantrite the genitive and the vocative together are all grave; or, by the maxim 'kāryakālaṃ hi saṃjñāparibhāṣam' (Pari. 3), subāmantrite is read together with the āṣṭamika 'āmantritasya ca', and parāṅgavadbhāva, being later, applies, giving the all-grave accent; after the accents are fixed the order of genitive and vocative is reversed by vyatyayo bahulam) and asme (śe for the locative ending by supāṃ suluk).

Pratipadārtha p. 515, rendered — दिवः of the sky-deity; दुहितः O Uṣas, the daughter; त्येभिः वाजेभिः with those foods; त्वम् you; आ गहि come here; अस्मे in us; रयिम् wealth; नि धारय establish permanently.

Bhāvārtha — O goddess Uṣas, daughter of the sky-deity! Come here with those foods, and make wealth abide in us.

Rik 22 (continued) pp. 516

English Translation as printed, p. 516

Daughter of heaven, come to us with plenty of food and place wealth among us.

Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu — त्येभिः — tya has the sense of tad; tyebhiḥ = taiḥ, 'by those'. अस्मे रयिं निधारय — 'place wealth in us specially': give us wealth in particular.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 516–517, noted briefly — tyebhiḥ: tyad, instrumental plural bhis; a for the final by 'tyadādīnām aḥ' (Pā. sū. 7-2-102); pararūpa by 'ato guṇe' (Pā. sū. 6-1-97); ais for bhis after a withheld by 'bahulaṃ chandasi' (Pā. sū. 7-1-10); rutva and visarga. gahi: gamḷ gatau, loṭ second person singular, hi for sip, ṅit as apit; loss of m by 'anudāttopadeśa-' (Pā. sū. 6-4-37); as that loss is treated as not done by 'asiddhavad atrābhāt' (Pā. sū. 6-4-22), hi is not dropped by 'ato heḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-4-105). vājebhiḥ: no ais for bhis by 'bahulaṃ chandasi'. duhitar divaḥ: though divaḥ follows, it is construed before duhitaḥ, so by 'subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare' (Pā. sū. 2-1-2) the genitive joins the vocative, and the all-grave accent of 'āmantritasya ca' covers the genitive group; or by 'kāryakālaṃ saṃjñāparibhāṣam' (Pari. 3) the paribhāṣā subāmantrite is read at the place of the āṣṭamika rule 'āmantritasya ca' and makes one sentence with it, so parāṅgavadbhāva comes first and then the all-grave accent; once the accents are fixed, the reversed order divaḥ duhitaḥ is to be explained by 'vyatyayo bahulam', and no doubt remains. asme: asmad, locative plural sup; śe by 'supāṃ suluk' (Pā. sū. 7-1-39), for the whole ending, as it is śit; loss of the d-portion by 'śeṣe lopaḥ' (Pā. sū. 7-2-90).

Close of Sūkta 30 — mūvattane sūktavu samāptavāgide (as printed) — "The thirtieth sūkta is ended."

॥ ಮೂವತ್ತೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 31 — "tvam agne prathamo aṅgirāḥ" ("The Thirty-first Sūkta"; first sūkta of the Seventh Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 517 lower half–. The introductory note and Kannada Anuvāda are on pp. 517–518, the heading block on p. 518; Rik 1 begins on p. 518 foot and continues on p. 519.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note; printed p. 517) As printed: अष्टमीषोळश्यौ with ळ; the quoted pratīka ऋषिर्नो चित्सहोजा अमृतो नि तुन्दते is given as printed (the first word's र्नो is not fully clear [?]); त्र्यर्यमेति as printed.

सप्तमेऽनुवाके पञ्च सूक्तानि । तत्र त्वमग्ने प्रथम इति प्रथमं सूक्तमष्टादशर्चम् । आङ्गिरसो हिरण्यस्तूप ऋषिः । अष्टमीषोडश्यष्टादश्यस्त्रिष्टुभः । शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुबन्तपरिभाषया जगत्यः । अग्निर्देवता । तथा चानुक्रमणिका । त्वमग्ने द्व्यूना हिरण्यस्तूप आग्नेयं त्रिष्टुबन्त्याष्टमीषोळश्यौ चेति ॥ प्रातरनुवाक आग्नेये क्रतावाश्विनशस्त्रे च त्वमग्ने प्रथम इति सूक्तम् । अथैतस्या रात्रेरिति खण्डे त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरा ऋषिर्नो चित्सहोजा अमृतो नि तुन्दते । आ. ४-१३ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥ अभिप्लवषडहस्य तृतीयेऽहन्याग्निमारुते शस्त्र इदं सूक्तं जातवेदस्यनिविद्धानीयम् । तथा च तृतीयस्य त्र्यर्यमेति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरा इत्याग्निमारुतम् । आ. ७-७ । इति ॥ वाजपेय आग्निमारुत एतत्सूक्तं जातवेदस्यं निविद्धानीयं तृतीयेनाभिप्लविकेनोक्तं तृतीयसवनम् । आ. ९-९ । इत्यतिदिष्टत्वात् ॥

saptame 'nuvāke pañca sūktāni | tatra tvamagne prathama iti prathamaṃ sūktamaṣṭādaśarcam | āṅgiraso hiraṇyastūpa ṛṣiḥ | aṣṭamīṣoḍaśyaṣṭādaśyastriṣṭubhaḥ | śiṣṭāstriṣṭubantaparibhāṣayā jagatyaḥ | agnirdevatā | tathā cānukramaṇikā | tvamagne dvyūnā hiraṇyastūpa āgneyaṃ triṣṭubantyāṣṭamīṣoḷaśyau ceti ‖ prātaranuvāka āgneye kratāvāśvinaśastre ca tvamagne prathama iti sūktam | athaitasyā rātreriti khaṇḍe tvamagne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣirno citsahojā amṛto ni tundate | ā. 4-13 | iti sūtritam ‖ abhiplavaṣaḍahasya tṛtīye 'hanyāgnimārute śastra idaṃ sūktaṃ jātavedasyanividdhānīyam | tathā ca tṛtīyasya tryaryameti khaṇḍe sūtritam | tvamagne prathamo aṅgirā ityāgnimārutam | ā. 7-7 | iti ‖ vājapeya āgnimāruta etatsūktaṃ jātavedasyaṃ nividdhānīyaṃ tṛtīyenābhiplavikenoktaṃ tṛtīyasavanam | ā. 9-9 | ityatidiṣṭatvāt ‖

Translation: "In the seventh anuvāka there are five sūktas. Of these, the first, tvam agne prathamaḥ, has eighteen riks; the seer is Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa; the eighth, sixteenth and eighteenth riks are Triṣṭubh; the rest are Jagatī by the convention 'what remains after the Triṣṭubh'. Deity: Agni. So the Anukramaṇikā: 'tvam agne — two less than twenty [i.e. eighteen]; Hiraṇyastūpa; Āgneya; Triṣṭubh: the last, the eighth, and the sixteenth.' In the prātar-anuvāka, in the Agni-rite [āgneya kratu] and in the Aśvina-śastra, the sūkta tvam agne prathamaḥ [is used]; in the section athaitasyā rātreḥ [of the Āśvalāyana sūtra] it is laid down: 'tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣir no cit sahojā amṛto ni tundate' (Āś. 4-13). On the third day of the abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, in the Agni-Māruta śastra, this sūkta serves as the jātavedasya [and] nividdhānīya; so it is laid down in the section tṛtīyasya tryaryama [as printed]: 'tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā — the Āgnimāruta [śastra]' (Āś. 7-7). In the Vājapeya, in the Agnimāruta [śastra], this sūkta is the jātavedasya [and] nividdhānīya, because the third pressing is extended [to it] by the rule 'the third pressing as stated for the third abhiplavika [day]' (Āś. 9-9)."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada) ॥ From this sūkta the seventh anuvāka begins. In this anuvāka there are five sūktas (Sūktas 31–35). Of them the first, beginning tvam agne prathama, has eighteen riks. The seer of this sūkta is Hiraṇyastūpa, son of Aṅgiras. Of its eighteen riks the eighth, sixteenth and eighteenth are in Triṣṭubh metre; the rest are in Jagatī. The deity is Agni. The Anukramaṇikā says: tvam agne dvyūnā hiraṇyastūpa āgneyaṃ triṣṭubantyāṣṭamīṣoḍaśyau ca. In the section rātriḥ of Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra it is said that this sūkta has its use [viniyoga] in reciting the morning-litany mantras connected with the Agni-sacrifice, and for reciting the mantras of the Aśvina-śastra (Āś. 4-13). In the sacrifice called Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, on the third day, the Agni-Māruta-śastra mantras are to be recited with this sūkta: this is explained in the section tṛtīyasya tryahaḥ by the sūtra tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ity āgnimārutam (Āś. 7-7). In the sacrifice Vājapeya, too, this sūkta is used in reciting the Agni-Māruta-śastra mantras: so, in Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra [it is said] jātavedasyaṃ nividdhānīyaṃ tṛtīyenābhiplavikenoktaṃ tṛtīyasavanam (Āś. 9-9).

Page 518 — Sūkta 31: heading

The Anuvāda's end, from eight, sixteen and eighteenth riks are Triṣṭubh, is on p. 518.

Heading block (p. 518): Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 7; Sūkta 31. Aṣṭaka 1; Adhyāya 2; Varga 32, 33, 34, 35. Number of riks: 18. Ṛṣi: Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa. Devatā: Agni. Chandas: 1–7, 9–15, 17 Jagatī; 8, 16, 18 Triṣṭubh.

Saṃhitā-pāṭha As printed in four lines, line 1 breaking after देवानाम-, line 3 after मरुतो. Line 3 flagged [accent ?]: the bar under प of विद्मनापसो has no stroke before it on ना; the stroke over यो and over जा are clear. Lines 3–4 are on p. 519.

त्वम॑ग्ने प्रथ॒मो अङ्गि॑रा॒ ऋषि॑र्दे॒वो दे॒वाना॑म- भवः शि॒वः सखा॑ । तव॑ व्र॒ते क॒वयो॑ वि॒द्मनाप॒सोऽजा॑यन्त म॒रुतो॒ [accent ?] भ्राज॑दृष्टयः ॥ १ ॥

tvámagne prathamó áṅgirā ṛ́ṣirdevó devā́nāma- bhavaḥ śiváḥ sákhā | táva vraté kaváyo vidmánāpasó 'jāyanta marúto [accent ?] bhrā́jadṛṣṭayaḥ || 1 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha

त्वं । अग्ने । प्रथमः । अङ्गिराः । ऋषिः । देवः । देवानां । अभवः । शिवः । सखा । तव । व्रते । कवयः । विद्मनाऽअपसः । अजायन्त । मरुतः । भ्राजत्ऽऋष्टयः ॥ १ ॥

tvaṃ | agne | prathamaḥ | aṅgirāḥ | ṛṣiḥ | devaḥ | devānāṃ | abhavaḥ | śivaḥ | sakhā | tava | vrate | kavayaḥ | vidmanā 'apasaḥ | ajāyanta | marutaḥ | bhrājat 'ṛṣṭayaḥ ‖ 1 ‖

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे अग्ने त्वं प्रथम आद्य आङ्गिरसानामृषीणां सर्वेषां जनकत्वात् । तादृशोऽङ्गिरोनामक ऋषिरभवः । तथा च ब्राह्मणम् । येऽङ्गारा आसंस्तेऽङ्गिरसोऽभवन् । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-३४ । इति । तथा स्वयं देवो भूत्वा देवानामन्येषां शिवः शोभनः सखाभवः । तव व्रते त्वदीये कर्मणि कवयो मेधाविनो विद्मनापसो ज्ञानेन व्याप्नुवाना ज्ञातकर्माणो वा भ्राजदृष्टयो दीप्यमानायुधा मरुतो मरुत्संज्ञका देवा अजायन्त ॥ विद्मनापसः । विद ज्ञाने । विद्मो वेदनम् । बहुलग्रहणादौणादिको मक्प्रत्ययः । तदस्यास्तीति पामादिलक्षणो नः । पा. ५-२-१०० । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । विद्मनान्यपांसि येषां ते विद्मनापसः । पूर्वपदस्यान्येषामपि दृश्यत इति दृशिग्रहणादवग्रहसमयेऽपि दीर्घत्वम् । अजायन्त । जनी प्रादुर्भावे । तस्य श्यनि ज्ञाजनोर्जा । पा. ७-३-७९ । इति जादेशः । भ्राजदृष्टयः । भ्राजृ दीप्तौ । व्यत्ययेन शतृ । तस्य लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । ऋषी गतावित्यस्मात् क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायामिति क्तिजन्त ऋष्टिशब्दः । ततो बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥

he agne tvaṃ prathama ādya āṅgirasānāmṛṣīṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ janakatvāt | tādṛśo 'ṅgironāmaka ṛṣirabhavaḥ | tathā ca brāhmaṇam | ye 'ṅgārā āsaṃste 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan | ai. brā. 3-34 | iti | tathā svayaṃ devo bhūtvā devānāmanyeṣāṃ śivaḥ śobhanaḥ sakhābhavaḥ | tava vrate tvadīye karmaṇi kavayo medhāvino vidmanāpaso jñānena vyāpnuvānā jñātakarmāṇo vā bhrājadṛṣṭayo dīpyamānāyudhā maruto marutsaṃjñakā devā ajāyanta ‖ vidmanāpasaḥ | vida jñāne | vidmo vedanam | bahulagrahaṇādauṇādiko makpratyayaḥ | tadasyāstīti pāmādilakṣaṇo naḥ | pā. 5-2-100 | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttatvam | vidmanānyapāṃsi yeṣāṃ te vidmanāpasaḥ | pūrvapadasyānyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti dṛśigrahaṇādavagrahasamaye 'pi dīrghatvam | ajāyanta | janī prādurbhāve | tasya śyani jñājanorjā | pā. 7-3-79 | iti jādeśaḥ | bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ | bhrājṛ dīptau | vyatyayena śatṛ | tasya lasārvadhātukānudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ | ṛṣī gatāvityasmāt kticktau ca saṃjñāyāmiti ktijanta ṛṣṭiśabdaḥ | tato bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ‖

Translation: "O Agni, you are the first (prathamaḥ), the earliest, being the begetter of all the Āṅgirasa seers; such a one, you became the seer named Aṅgiras. So the Brāhmaṇa: 'The embers that were became the Aṅgirases' (Ai. Br. 3-34). Likewise, being yourself a god, you became the auspicious (śivaḥ: excellent) friend of the other gods. In your rite (tava vrate: in your work) the wise (kavayaḥ), vidmanāpasaḥ (pervading by knowledge, or knowing the works), with shining weapons (bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ), the Maruts, the gods so named, were born (ajāyanta)." The grammatical tail treats vidmanāpasaḥ (vida jñāne; vidma = knowing, with the Uṇādi mak by the word bahula; na in the possessive sense as in the pāmādi group, Pā. 5-2-100; end-acute by the suffix; 'they whose works are vidmana'; lengthening of the first member even in the avagraha, because of the word dṛśi in 'anyeṣām api dṛśyate'), ajāyanta (jā for jan before śyan by Pā. 7-3-79) and bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ (bhrājṛ dīptau, śatṛ by vyatyaya, grave as lasārvadhātuka, the root accent remains; ṛṣṭi from ṛṣī gatau with ktic by 'kticktau ca saṃjñāyām'; first-member accent in the bahuvrīhi).

Rik 1 (continued) pp. 520

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | प्रथमः (prathamaḥ) — the first | अङ्गिराः (aṅgirāḥ) — [the seer] named Aṅgiras (the first among all the seers called Aṅgirases) | ऋषिः (ṛṣiḥ) — seer | अभवः (abhavaḥ) — were | देवः (devaḥ) — (yourself) a deity | देवानाम् (devānām) — of all the gods | शिवः (śivaḥ) — the auspicious | सखा (sakhā) — (were) the friend | तव व्रते (tava vrate) — in the rites performed for you | कवयः (kavayaḥ) — the intelligent | विद्मनापसः (vidmanāpasaḥ) — [those] who know everything by knowledge, or all works | भ्राजदृष्टयः (bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ) — [those] who hold shining weapons | मरुतः (marutaḥ) — the Marut gods | अजायन्त (ajāyanta) — were created.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You are the first among all the seers named Aṅgirases. By your own nature you are a god, a friend who does good to all other gods. In the rites performed for you, the Marut gods — wise, knowing all things by knowledge, with shining weapons — were created.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

O Agni, you are the first Angiras Raishi; a good friend of the gods; in your rite, the wise, the skilful and the bright-weaponed Maruts were born.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ On the Aṅgirases. In this rik it is said that Agni is the first among the Aṅgiras seers; that is, Agni became the root-man [mūla-puruṣa] of the Aṅgirasa seers. In many other riks of the Ṛgveda too the word aṅgiraḥ is used to address Agni; discussion of this matter is necessary. [The Brāhmaṇa passage:] ये ऽङ्गारा आसंस्तेऽङ्गिरसोऽभवन् (ye 'ṅgārā āsaṃs te 'ṅgiraso 'bhavan; Ai. Br. 3-34) — "the embers [aṅgāras] that were, those became the Aṅgirases": thus, in the Prajāpati-duhitṛ-dhyāna [Prajāpati's-daughter-meditation] narrative of the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa it is said that the embers [of the sacrifice that sprang from the seed of Rudra's arrow] were named Aṅgirases. [The Kannada gives the story:] In the beginning Prajāpati (Brahmā), with a wicked thought — with desire — meditated in his mind on his own daughter (Uṣas, or in the form of Dyaus); the gods, knowing it, resolved to prevent this wicked act. But they had no strength to force Prajāpati to refrain from the deed; so all the gods, bringing together their own several forms, produced a deity called Rudra, and said [to him], "punish this Prajāpati." Hearing this, Prajāpati, terrified, assumed the form of a stag and fled to the sky. As the constellation Mṛgaśiras [Orion's head / the Deer], Prajāpati may be seen even now.

Rik 1 (continued) pp. 521

Then Rudra, appearing in the form of the star Ārdrā, discharged an arrow at Prajāpati. Prajāpati's seed fell, and the Maruts scattered it in many directions and burned it to ashes. From that seed first Āditya and then Bhṛgu Vāruṇi were born; from the remaining embers the Aṅgirases were born: so it is said.

In the Purāṇas and other works the sage Aṅgiras is said to be one of Brahmā's mind-born sons. In the Vedas, the Aṅgiras is said to be a seer of great fame, the root-man of many famous seers. In the Mahābhārata, Vana-parvan, in the dialogue of Mārkaṇḍeya and Yudhiṣṭhira, there is this story: For some reason Agni left his duty and went off to the forest in disguise. Then the sage named Aṅgiras, in Agni's place, carried the shares of the oblation to the gods in the sacrifice and did Agni's work; and he prayed Agni to come back and do his own duty. Because he did Agni's duties, this sage Aṅgiras came to be called Agni's son; hence the descendants of this sage became famous as 'Aṅgirases'. There are still other such narratives in the Purāṇas. Besides, in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā itself:

ते अङ्गिरसः सूनवस्ते अग्नेः परिजज्ञिरे । (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-62-5) te aṅgirasaḥ sūnavas te agneḥ parijajñire | Mine, tentative: "They, the Aṅgirases, are the sons; they were born around Agni."

— that is, it is said clearly that the seers called Aṅgirases are Agni's sons. The commentator, however, does not cite this rik as an instance; why, one cannot tell.

That the sage Aṅgiras was of very ancient time, and that many seers in the Ṛgveda call this one the root-man of their own lineage, appears from several riks of the Ṛgveda:

मनुष्वदग्ने अङ्गिरस्वदङ्गिरो ययातिवत्सदने पूर्ववच्छुचे ॥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-17) manuṣvad agne aṅgirasvad aṅgiro yayātivat sadane pūrvavac chuce || — Mine, tentative: "As with Manu, O Agni, as with Aṅgiras, O Aṅgiras, as with Yayāti, in the seat, as of old, O bright one." अङ्गिरस्वन्महिव्रत प्रस्कण्वस्य श्रुधी हवम् ॥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-45-3) — aṅgirasvan mahivrata praskaṇvasya śrudhī havam || — Mine, tentative: "As [you heard] Aṅgiras, O you of great ordinances, hear the call of Praskaṇva." दध्यङ् ह मे जनुषं पूर्वो अङ्गिराः प्रियमेधः कण्वो अत्रिर्मनुर्विदुस्ते मे पूर्वे मनुर्विदुः ॥ (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-139-9; the line runs over to p. 522) — dadhyaṅ ha me januṣaṃ pūrvo aṅgirāḥ priyamedhaḥ kaṇvo atrir manur vidus te me pūrve manur vidus || — Mine, tentative: "Dadhyañc, the ancient Aṅgiras, Priyamedha, Kaṇva, Atri, Manu knew my birth: they, my forefathers, Manu knew it."

Rik 1 (continued) pp. 522

These riks show that Aṅgiras is known as the forefather of many seers. In the lineage of the Aṅgirasa seers was one named Atharvan, a leading man; he had three sons, Bṛhaspati, Gotama and Vṛṣaṇa. The one named Vṛṣaṇa was a son born to this Atharvan of his wife Pathyā; his history is hinted at in many places in the Veda. The son of Vṛṣaṇa, called Sudhanvan Āṅgirasa, had three sons, Ṛbhu, Vibhvan and Vāja. These three, who are called the Ṛbhus in the Veda, are said to be pupils of Tvaṣṭṛ-Prajāpati. In this lineage of Aṅgiras there were three seers named Bṛhaspati. The Ṛbhus mentioned above and Bṛhaspati are imagined as gods, and many riks that are their praise are in the Ṛgveda. Of those three Bṛhaspatis, the first, so the tradition goes, killed the Dasyu king called Paṇi and brought back the cows he had carried off; and, with his ten thousand followers, fought and defeated another Dasyu chief named Dāsa, who ruled on the bank of the river Aṃśumatī. Another Bṛhaspati's son named Bharadvāja was the priest of Divodāsa, who killed the daitya Śambara. Thus the lineage of Aṅgiras was very large, and many famous men belonged to it. In the Ṛgveda, in many places — wherever the word agni would have to be used — the word aṅgira is used plentifully.

Since Hiraṇyastūpa, the seer of this sūkta, was born in the Aṅgirasa line, he praises Agni, the root-man of his line, with riks full of excellent meanings. Most of the riks of this sūkta begin with the words tvam agne or tvaṃ no agne. This seer Hiraṇyastūpa is the seer of the 31st–35th sūktas of the first maṇḍala in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā (71 riks), of the 4th sūkta of the ninth maṇḍala (10 riks) and of the [?]th sūkta of the tenth maṇḍala (10 riks; the number is printed like ೬೯ but not clear [?]) — in all 91 riks. All the sūktas of this seer are in the prauḍha style [i.e. of mature, weighty composition].

देवो देवानामभवः शिवः सखा (devo devānām abhavaḥ śivaḥ sakhā) — to the gods you became a friend of excellent mind. तव व्रते (tava vrate) — tvadīye karmaṇi: in the work that belongs to you; that is, in sacrifices and the like performed with your help. कवयः (kavayaḥ) — medhāvinaḥ: the intelligent.

Rik 1 (continued) pp. 523

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 523–524, noted briefly — abhavaḥ: bhū sattāyām, laṅ second person singular; grave by 'tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ' (Pā. sū. 8-1-28). vidmanāpasaḥ: vida jñāne, adādi; vidma ('knowing'); mak of the Uṇādi list by the word bahula in 'uṇādayo bahulam' (Pā. sū. 3-3-1); no guṇa of the light penult as mak is kit; 'vidma asyāsti': na in the possessive sense by 'lomādipāmādipicchādibhyaḥ śanelacaḥ' (Pā. sū. 5-2-100), the word being in the pāmādi group; end-acute by the suffix's initial udātta; 'vidmanāni apāṃsi yeṣāṃ te': first-member accent by 'bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam' (Pā. sū. 6-2-1); as 'anyeṣām api dṛśyate' (Pā. sū. 6-3-137) names the root dṛś, the first member is lengthened even at the time of avagraha. ajāyanta: janī prādurbhāve, divādi, laṅ third person plural, anta for jha; śyan by 'divādibhyaḥ śyan' (Pā. sū. 3-1-69); before śyan jā for the root by 'jñājanor jā' (Pā. sū. 7-3-79); aṭ; ajāya + anta: pararūpa by 'ato guṇe' (Pā. sū. 6-1-97); as the augment is udātta, initial udātta. bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ: bhrājṛ dīptau, bhvādi, ātmanepadī; by 'vyatyayo bahulam' (Pā. sū. 3-1-85) śatṛ in the sense of laṭ; śap; bhrājat; śap grave as pit; after śap the lasārvadhātuka śatṛ is grave by the sūtra 'tāsyanudātteṭ', so the root's end-acute remains. ṛṣī gatau: ktic by 'kticktau ca saṃjñāyām' (Pā. sū. 3-3-174); ṛṣ + ti: ṣṭutva by 'ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ' (Pā. sū. 8-4-41); no guṇa of the light penult as the suffix is kit: ṛṣṭi; 'bhrājantaḥ (jantya) ṛṣṭayaḥ yeṣāṃ te' [so printed], bahuvrīhi; first-member accent by 'bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā' (Pā. sū. 6-2-1).

Rik 2 pp. 524–528

त्वम॑ग्ने प्रथ॒मो अङ्गि॑रस्तमः क॒विर्दे॒वानां॒ परि॑ भूषसि व्र॒तं । वि॒भुर्विश्व॑स्मै॒ भुव॑नाय॒ मेधि॑रो द्वि॒मा॒ता श॒युः [accent ?] क॑ति॒धा चि॑दा॒यवे॑ ॥ २ ॥ [accent ?]

tvámagne prathamó áṅgirastamaḥ kavírdevā́nāṃ pári bhūṣasi vratáṃ | vibhúrvíśvasmai bhúvanāya médhiro dvimātā́ śayúḥ [accent ?] katidhā́ cidāyáve || 2 || [accent ?] Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha

त्वं । अग्ने । प्रथमः । अङ्गिरःऽतमः । कविः । देवानां । परि । भूषसि । व्रतं । विऽभुः । विश्वस्मै । भुवनाय । मेधिरः । द्विऽमाता । शयुः । कतिऽधा । चित् । आयवे ॥ २ ॥

tvaṃ | agne | prathamaḥ | aṅgiraḥ 'tamaḥ | kaviḥ | devānāṃ | pari | bhūṣasi | vrataṃ | vi 'bhuḥ | viśvasmai | bhuvanāya | medhiraḥ | dvi 'mātā | śayuḥ | kati 'dhā | cit | āyave ‖ 2 ‖

Rik 2 (continued) pp. 525

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे अग्ने त्वं प्रथम आद्य अङ्गिरस्तमोऽतिशयेनाङ्गिरा भूत्वा कविर्मेधावी सन् देवानामन्येषां व्रतं कर्म परि भूषसि । परितोऽलंकरोषि । कीदृशस्त्वम् । विश्वस्मै भुवनाय समस्तलोकानुग्रहार्थं विभुर्बहुविधः । आहवनीयाद्यनेकरूपधारीत्यर्थः । मेधिरो मेधावान् द्विमाता द्वयोररण्योरुत्पन्नः । यद्वा । द्वयोर्लोकयोर्निर्माता । आयवे मनुष्यार्थं कतिधा चित् कतिभिः प्रकारैः सर्वत्र शयुः शयानः । तत्तन्मनुष्यगृहेऽवस्थितस्य तव प्रकारा इयन्त इति न केनापि ज्ञायत इत्यर्थः ॥ भूषसि । भूष अलंकारे । भौवादिकः । विभुः । विप्रसंभ्यो ड्वसंज्ञायाम् । पा. ३-२-१८० । इति विपूर्वाद्भवतेर्डुप्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । भुवनाय । भूसूधूभ्रस्जिभ्यश्छन्दसि । उ. २-८० । इति क्युन् । योरनादेशे नित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वम् । मेधिरः । मेधृ संगमे च । अस्माद्बाहुलक इरन्प्रत्ययः । नित्स्वरः । द्विमाता । द्वे मातरौ यस्यासौ द्विमाता । नद्यृतश्च । पा. ५-४-१५३ । इति कप्प्रत्ययो न भवति । मातृमातृकयोर्भेदेनोपादानान्नद्यृतश्चेति कबपि विभाष्यत इति तस्य मातृशब्दविषये पाक्षिकत्वोक्तिः । त्रिचक्रादित्वादुत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । यद्वा । द्वयोर्माता । द्विमाता । समासस्येत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । शयुः । शीङ् स्वप्ने । भृमृशीत्यादिना । उ. १-७ । उप्रत्ययः । कतिधा । डत्यन्तस्य किंशब्दस्य बहुगणवतुडति संख्या । पा. १-१-२३ । इति संख्यासंज्ञायां संख्याया विधार्थे धा । पा. ५-३-४२ । इति धाप्रत्ययः । आयवे । छन्दसीणः । उ. १-२ । इत्येतेरुण्प्रत्ययः ॥

he agne tvaṃ prathama ādya aṅgirastamo 'tiśayenāṅgirā bhūtvā kavirmedhāvī san devānāmanyeṣāṃ vrataṃ karma pari bhūṣasi | parito 'laṃkaroṣi | kīdṛśastvam | viśvasmai bhuvanāya samastalokānugrahārthaṃ vibhurbahuvidhaḥ | āhavanīyādyanekarūpadhārītyarthaḥ | medhiro medhāvān dvimātā dvayoraraṇyorutpannaḥ | yadvā | dvayorlokayornirmātā | āyave manuṣyārthaṃ katidhā cit katibhiḥ prakāraiḥ sarvatra śayuḥ śayānaḥ | tattanmanuṣyagṛhe 'vasthitasya tava prakārā iyanta iti na kenāpi jñāyata ityarthaḥ ‖ bhūṣasi | bhūṣa alaṃkāre | bhauvādikaḥ | vibhuḥ | viprasaṃbhyo ḍvasaṃjñāyām | pā. 3-2-180 | iti vipūrvādbhavaterḍupratyayaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | bhuvanāya | bhūsūdhūbhrasjibhyaśchandasi | u. 2-80 | iti kyun | yoranādeśe nitsvareṇādyudāttatvam | medhiraḥ | medhṛ saṃgame ca | asmādbāhulaka iranpratyayaḥ | nitsvaraḥ | dvimātā | dve mātarau yasyāsau dvimātā | nadyṛtaśca | pā. 5-4-153 | iti kappratyayo na bhavati | mātṛmātṛkayorbhedenopādānānnadyṛtaśceti kabapi vibhāṣyata iti tasya mātṛśabdaviṣaye pākṣikatvoktiḥ | tricakrāditvāduttarapadāntodāttatvam | yadvā | dvayormātā | dvimātā | samāsasyetyantodāttatvam | śayuḥ | śīṅ svapne | bhṛmṛśītyādinā | u. 1-7 | upratyayaḥ | katidhā | ḍatyantasya kiṃśabdasya bahugaṇavatuḍati saṃkhyā | pā. 1-1-23 | iti saṃkhyāsaṃjñāyāṃ saṃkhyāyā vidhārthe dhā | pā. 5-3-42 | iti dhāpratyayaḥ | āyave | chandasīṇaḥ | u. 1-2 | ityeteruṇpratyayaḥ ‖

Gist: Agni, first and most Aṅgiras-like, wise, adorns the work of the other gods; he takes many forms (the Āhavanīya and the rest) for the good of all the world; wise; born of the two fire-sticks, or maker of the two worlds; for man's sake he lies in each man's house in ways no one can count. The grammatical tail treats bhūṣasi, vibhuḥ (ḍu, Pā. 3-2-180), bhuvanāya (kyun, U. 2-80), medhiraḥ (iran), dvimātā (no kap by Pā. 5-4-153, which the bhāṣya calls optional for mātṛ; or a tatpuruṣa), śayuḥ (u, U. 1-7), katidhā (Pā. 1-1-23, 5-3-42) and āyave (uṇ, U. 1-2).

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | प्रथमः अङ्गिरस्तमः (prathamaḥ aṅgirastamaḥ) — the first among the Aṅgirases and exceedingly great | कविः (kaviḥ) — [the] wise | विश्वस्मै भुवनाय (viśvasmai bhuvanāya) — for the favour of all the worlds | विभुः (vibhuḥ) — [one] of many forms such as the Āhavanīya | मेधिरः (medhiraḥ) — [the] wise | द्विमाता (dvimātā) — [the] one born of two mothers [the araṇis] or the maker of two worlds | आयवे (āyave) — for [the sake of] man | कतिधा चित् (katidhā cit) — in many ways | शयुः (śayuḥ) — [the] sleeper, lying everywhere | देवानाम् (devānām) — [of other] gods | व्रतम् (vratam) — [the] work | परि भूषसि (pari bhūṣasi) — you adorn all round.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You are the first among the seers named Aṅgirases, and exceedingly great; wise, endowed with many forms such as the Āhavanīya for the favour of all the worlds; intelligent; born of the two araṇi [sticks] as of two mothers; lying in many ways for the sake of man; you adorn all round the works of the other gods.

Rik 2 (continued) pp. 526

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed, p. 526

O Agni, you are the very first and foremost among Angiras ; you conduct the work (sacrifice or worship) of the gods ; you are wise, son of two mothers ; manifold for the benefit of all the world you reside in every house for the use of man.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ देवानां परिभूषसि व्रतम् (devānāṃ paribhūṣasi vratam) — 'you adorn the works of the gods': in the rites performed with the gods in view [sacrifices and the like], you take the chief part and complete the sacrifice; without Agni there is no sacrifice; so Agni is the adornment of the sacrificial rites. विभुः (vibhuḥ) — vipūrvād bhavater ḍuprayayaḥ: viśeṣeṇa bahuprakāreṇa bhavatīti vibhuḥ: because [he exists] in many forms as in the Āhavanīya [fire] and others, and in many houses, he is 'one existing in many forms'. विश्वस्मै भुवनाय (viśvasmai bhuvanāya) — for all the world [the source adds "For all the world"]. मेधिरः (medhiraḥ) — medhṛ saṅgame ca: medhāvān: the intelligent, the wise. द्विमाता (dvimātā) — dvayor mātā | dvayor araṇyor utpannaḥ | yadvā dvayor lokayor nirmātā: 'Agni is born, in the sacrifice, when two pieces of wood called araṇi are rubbed together; so, with the two araṇis as 'two mothers', Agni is called dvimātā — "one with two mothers". Or: when the Śruti tells the order of creation, by its words agner āpaḥ | adbhyaḥ pṛthivī ('from Agni the waters; from the waters the earth') the atmosphere (āpaḥ means the atmosphere, Ni. 2-10) and the earth come from Agni; so they say Agni is dvayor lokayor nirmātā, the maker of the two worlds, the earth and the atmosphere. आयवे (āyave) — āyuḥ ayanāt eti hy asau viśvam: 'for the sake of pervading the whole world'. [The Kannada: "to pervade the whole creation".]

Rik 2 (continued) pp. 527

शयुः — śīṅ svapne: one who lies down, that is, one who exists in a gentle (saumya) state.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 527–528, noted briefly — bhūṣasi: bhūṣa alaṃkāre, bhvādi, second person singular; grave as a tiṅ form (no number printed). vibhuḥ: bhū sattāyām with vi; ḍu by 'viprasaṃbhyo ḍvasaṃjñāyām' (Pā. sū. 3-2-180); loss of the ṭi as ḍit; a kṛdanta second member after a gati, so its accent by 'gatikārakopapadāt kṛt' (Pā. sū. 6-2-139): end-acute. bhuvanāya: kyun by 'bhūsūdhūbhrasjibhyaś chandasi' (U. sū. 2-238, as printed; the bhāṣya prints उ. २-८०); ana for yu by 'yuvor anākau' (Pā. sū. 7-1-1); guṇa and av; dative singular; initial udātta, the suffix being nit, by 'ñnity ādir nityam' (Pā. sū. 6-1-197). medhiraḥ: medhṛ saṃgame ca, bhvādi; iran by the word bahula in 'uṇādayo bahulam' (Pā. sū. 3-3-1); initial udātta as nit. dvimātā: 'dve mātarau yasya asau', a bahuvrīhi with a numeral first member; as it ends in ṛ, the samāsānta kap is due by 'nadyṛtaś ca' (Pā. sū. 5-4-153); but since mātṛ and mātṛka differ in sense in common use, the rule is said to be optional for mātṛ; mātṛ has many senses ('mother', 'one who measures' and others); so no kap; being in the tricakrādi group, the second member is end-acute; or 'dvayoḥ mātā', a tatpuruṣa, no question of kap, end-acute by 'samāsasya'. śayuḥ: śīṅ svapne, adādi; u by 'bhṛmṛśī-' (U. sū. 1-7); guṇa, ay; end-acute by the suffix. katidhā: ḍati after kim by 'kimaḥ saṃkhyāparimāṇe ḍati ca' (Pā. sū. 5-2-41); loss of the ṭi; kati is called saṃkhyā by 'bahugaṇavatuḍati saṃkhyā' (Pā. sū. 1-1-23); dhā by 'saṃkhyāyā vidhārthe dhā' (Pā. sū. 5-3-42), 'in many ways'; end-acute by the suffix. āyave: iṇ gatau, adādi; uṇ by 'chandasīṇaḥ' (U. sū. 1-2); vṛddhi as ṇit by 'aco ñṇiti' (Pā. sū. 7-2-115); āy by 'eco 'yavāyāvaḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-1-78); dative singular; middle udātta by the suffix.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya As printed: नि. ३-२१; उ. १-१५८; पा. ७-४-२५ (the 7 is the flat-footed glyph, read ×3); पा. ३-३-१०२; पा. ३-१-१०९; पा. ८-१-१८-५. The bhāṣya ends at the top of p. 530 with वचनात् । महः ….

हे अग्ने त्वं मातरिश्वने प्रथमो मुख्यो भूत्वा वर्तसे । अग्निर्वायुरादित्य इति वाय्वपेक्षया सर्वत्र मुख्यत्वावगमात् । तादृशस्त्वं सुक्रतूया शोभनकर्मेच्छया विवस्वते परिचरते यजमानायाविर्भव । प्रकटो भव । तव सामर्थ्यं दृष्ट्वा रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावरेजेताम् । अकम्पेताम् । भ्यसते रेजत इति भयवेपनयोः । नि. ३-२१ । इति यास्कः । होतृवूर्ये होतृवरणयुक्ते कर्मणि भारं भरणमसघ्नोः । ऊढवानसि । हे वसो निवासहेतो वह्ने महः पूज्यान्देवानयजः । इष्टवानसि ॥ मातरिश्वने । निर्माणहेतुत्वान्माता अन्तरिक्षम् । तत्र श्वसिति प्राणितीति मातरिश्वा वायुः । श्वन्नुक्षन्नित्यादौ । उ. १-१५८ । मातरिश्वन्शब्दः कनिन्प्रत्ययान्तो निपातितः । सुक्रतूया । सुक्रतुमात्मन इच्छति । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोरिति दीर्घः । पा. ७-४-२५ । क्यजन्तस्य धातुसंज्ञायाम् अ प्रत्ययात् । पा. ३-३-१०२ । इति भावेऽकारप्रत्ययः । ततष्टाप् । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयैकवचनस्य डादेशः । टिलोपे उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण तस्योदात्तत्वम् । संहितायामन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घः । विवस्वते । विवासतिः परिचरणकर्मा । अस्मात्संपदादिलक्षणः क्विप् । व्यत्ययेनोपधाह्रस्वत्वम् । तदस्यास्तीति मतुप् । मादुपधाया इति मतोर्वत्वम् । तसौ मत्वर्थ इति भत्वेन पदत्वाभावाद्रुत्वाभावः । मतुपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । रोदसी । वा छन्दसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वम् ॥ होतृवूर्ये । होता व्रियत इति होतृवूर्यो यज्ञः । वृञ् वरणे । बहुलग्रहणादौणादिकः क्यप् । उदोष्ठ्यपूर्वस्येत्युत्वम् । हलि चेति दीर्घः । यद्वा । वृञ् वरण इत्यस्मादेतिस्तुशास्वित्यादिना । पा. ३-१-१०९ । क्यप् । अनित्यमागमशासनमिति तुगभावः । अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोरिति दीर्घत्वे पूर्ववदुत्वदीर्घौ । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन स एव शिष्यते । असघ्नोः । षघ हिंसायाम् । अत्र तु वहनार्थः । स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः । पादादित्वादनिघातः । अयजः । भारमित्यस्य पूर्वपदस्य वाक्यान्तरगतत्वात्तदपेक्षयास्य निघातो न भवति । समानवाक्ये निघातयुष्मदस्मदादेशा वक्तव्याः । पा. ८-१-१८-५ । इति वचनात् । महः । मह पूजायाम् । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । सुपां सुपो भवन्तीति शसो जसादेशः । सावेकाच इति तस्योदात्तत्वम् । यद्वा । शसि महच्छब्दस्याच्छब्दलोपश्छान्दसः । बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानमिति शस उदात्तत्वम् ॥

svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ | pādāditvādanighātaḥ | ayajaḥ | bhāramityasya pūrvapadasya vākyāntaragatatvāttadapekṣayāsya nighāto na bhavati | samānavākye nighātayuṣmadasmadādeśā vaktavyāḥ | pā. 8-1-18-5 | iti vacanāt | mahaḥ | maha pūjāyām | kvipceti kvip | supāṃ supo bhavantīti śaso jasādeśaḥ | sāvekāca iti tasyodāttatvam | yadvā | śasi mahacchabdasyācchabdalopaśchāndasaḥ | bṛhanmahatorupasaṃkhyānamiti śasa udāttatvam ‖

Translation: "O Agni, you are first (prathamaḥ), chief, for Mātariśvan (the wind) — for in 'agnir vāyur ādityaḥ' the chief place is everywhere understood relative to Vāyu. Such as you are, with the desire for good works (sukratūyā), become manifest (āvir bhava: be visible) to the sacrificer who serves you (vivasvate). Seeing your power, heaven and earth (rodasī) trembled (arejetām: shook) — 'bhyasate rejate' are [verbs] of fear and trembling (Ni. 3-21), says Yāska. In the rite with the choosing of the hotṛ (hotṛvūrye) you bore (asaghnoḥ: carried) the burden (bhāram). O Vasu (cause of dwelling), O Fire, you worshipped (ayajaḥ) the worshipful gods (mahaḥ)." The grammatical tail treats mātariśvane (mātṛ = the atmosphere, 'which measures'; 'he breathes there'; kanin by nipātana under U. 1-158), sukratūyā (kyac; lengthening by Pā. 7-4-25; the abstract a by Pā. 3-3-102; ṭāp; ḍā for the instrumental; udātta by the loss of the udātta; lengthening of the first member in the Saṃhitā), vivasvate (kvip of the saṃpad group, shortening by vyatyaya, matup with v, no ru since the stem is bha; the root accent remains), rodasī (lengthening by vā chandasi), hotṛvūrye (kyap; u after a labial; lengthening; or kyap by Pā. 3-1-109 without the augment tuk; the root accent remains), asaghnoḥ (ṣagha hiṃsāyām, here 'carrying'; śnu; not grave at the head of the pāda), ayajaḥ (not grave, as bhāram belongs to another clause; the rule of Pā. 8-1-18-5 [vārttika]) and mahaḥ (kvip; jas for śas; udātta by sāv ekācaḥ; or the loss of at of mahat, Vedic, with the udātta of śas by the dictum on bṛhat and mahat).

Rik 3 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada and first half of the bhāṣya are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 529–534

The Saṃhitā, Pada and the whole bhāṣya, with its grammatical tail, are now given in full in the preceding section, read from the print.

Rik 3 (continued) pp. 530

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | मातरिश्वने (mātariśvane) — for the wind | प्रथमः (prathamaḥ) — [being] the chief | सुक्रतूया (sukratūyā) — desiring [and so approving] the excellent works | विवस्वते (vivasvate) — [to you] the sacrificer who is fit to worship | आविर्भव (āvirbhava) — be visible | रोदसी (rodasī) — heaven and earth, both | अरेजेताम् (arejetām) — tremble [seeing your greatness] | होतृवूर्ये (hotṛvūrye) — in the sacrificial work in which the hotṛ is chosen | भारम् (bhāram) — the burden [of the work] of execution | असघ्नोः (asaghnoḥ) — [you] bore | वसो (vaso) — O Agni, in the form of the Vasus | महः (mahaḥ) — the worshipful gods | अयजः (ayajaḥ) — you worshipped.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You, being the chief over the wind, desiring and so approving the excellent sacrificial works, appear before the sacrificer who is fit to worship you. Seeing your greatness, heaven and earth both tremble. In the sacrificial work in which the hotṛ has been appointed, you bear the burden of carrying the work out. O Agni, in the form of the Vasus! You have worshipped the worshipful gods.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed, p. 530

O Agni, you are the first or emminent [sic] over the wind ; become manifes [sic] to the worshipper in appreciation of his services ; heaven and earth tremble at your power ; you have taken over the responsibility in the rite in which the priest (Hotri) was appointed ; O Vasu, you have worshipped the great gods.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ प्रथमो मातरिश्वने (prathamo mātariśvane) — tvaṃ mātariśvane prathamo mukhyo bhūtvā vartase | agnir vāyur ādityaḥ iti vāyum apekṣayā mukhyatvād agamāt — "You are the chief to Mātariśvan [Vāyu]; because it is said 'agnir vāyur ādityaḥ' ['Agni, Vāyu, Āditya'], Agni is, in comparison with Vāyu, the chief";

Rik 3 (continued) pp. 531

Vāyu requires Agni as the chief; since in the Śruti sentence agnir vāyur ādityaḥ Agni is mentioned first among the deities Agni, Vāyu, Āditya etc., Agni is the first, the chief; that is, Agni and Vāyu are closely related; and of the two, Agni is the chief — that is the sense. Skandasvāmin's view. Skandasvāmin explains the sentence tvam agne prathamo mātariśvana āvir bhava in a different way: "O Agni! At the beginning of creation [or: at the first beginning], you were first seen directly by Vāyu, before everyone else." To support this he tells an old story (itihāsa): "In the beginning the whole world was enveloped in darkness. Then Mātariśvan (Vāyu) saw Agni in the sky in a subtle form. Then the sages Atharvan, Parāśara, Bharadvāja and others, by churning, brought Agni forth in the araṇi." This is described in the riks: > मथीद्यदीं विष्वो मातरिश्वा होतारं विश्वाप्सुं विश्वदेव्यम् ॥ Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-148-1 — mathīd yad īṃ viṣṇo mātariśvā hotāraṃ viśvāpsuṃ viśvadevyam || — Mine, tentative: "When Mātariśvan churned him, the all-formed, all-divine hotṛ." > त्वामग्ने पुष्करादध्यथर्वा निरमन्थत ॥ Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-13 — tvām agne puṣkarād adhy atharvā niramanthata || — Mine, tentative: "From the lotus, O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth." Then Agni, shining with a great flame, became visible to them. [The idea that] Agni was seen first by Mātariśvan is described in this rik; so [Skandasvāmin] says. सुक्रतूया (sukratūyā) — sukratum ātmana icchatīti; śobhanakarmecchayā: out of desire for excellent works, i.e. [out of] anticipation of the best works. विवस्वते (vivasvate) — [Sanskrit: vivasati] or vivāsati: because the word means paricaraṇakarma (Ni. 3-13), vivasvate [the dative of vivasvān] means 'to the sacrificer who performs paricaryā, that is, service'. Vivasvān is also a name of Manu; see the special remark made in a later rik on the word manave. रोदसी (rodasī) — since the word rodasī is read among the twenty-four names of 'heaven and earth' beginning svadhe, purandhī, rodasī means the two [worlds] heaven and earth (Ni. 3-22, as printed). होतृवूर्ये (hotṛvūrye) — hotrā vriyate iti hotṛvūryo yajñaḥ | hotṛvaraṇayukte — 'the sacrifice in which the hotṛ is chosen'; in a sacrifice in which the priest called hotṛ is appointed. भारम् (bhāram) — bharaṇam: the load, the duty, the responsibility, the weight; Skandasvāmin explains a purāṇa-narrative about carrying the burden:

Rik 3 (continued) pp. 532

असघ्नोर्भारम् । अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । देवाः किल स्वयमेव स्वानि स्वानि हवींष्यूढ्वाभक्षयन् । तेषां केचिन्नोढुं नाशक्नुवन् । एकैकाहुतिस्त्रैलोक्यभारादतिरिच्यते । कांश्चित्तु शक्नुवतोऽप्यसुरा अभ्यद्रवन् । ते सर्वेऽग्निमब्रुवन् हव्यं नो वहेति । स तल्लीलायमानोऽवहत् । तदिहोच्यते असघ्नोर्भारमिति ॥

asaghnorbhāram | atretihāsamācakṣate | devāḥ kila svayameva svāni svāni havīṃṣyūḍhvābhakṣayan | teṣāṃ kecinnoḍhuṃ nāśaknuvan | ekaikāhutistrailokyabhārādatiricyate | kāṃścittu śaknuvato 'pyasurā abhyadravan | te sarve 'gnimabruvan havyaṃ no vaheti | sa tallīlāyamāno 'vahat | tadihocyate asaghnorbhāramiti ‖

That is: in olden times the gods themselves used to come, take the oblations offered to them, and eat them. Since it was well known that each single oblation offered in a sacrifice weighs more than the three worlds, some gods had no strength to carry off their oblations. Then the asuras snatched those oblations and ran off [the Sanskrit adds: even from some who could]. Seeing this, the gods came to Agni and prayed: "O Agni, carry for us the oblations offered in the sacrifice and bring them to us"; and Agni agreed and carried those heavy oblations as mere play. This story, [Skandasvāmin] says, is what the words asaghnor bhāram describe.

महः (mahaḥ) — maha pūjāyām ['to worship']: pūjyān devān — the worshipful gods. वसो (vaso) — nivāsahetoḥ | the one who is the cause of dwelling-places, or the protector, Agni.

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 532–534, noted briefly — mātariśvane: 'nirmāṇahetutvāt mātā antarikṣam' (the atmosphere, ākāśa); 'tatra śvasiti prāṇiti iti mātariśvā vāyuḥ': the wind that lives in the sky; by the sūtra 'śvannukṣan-' (U. sū. 1-152, as printed; the bhāṣya prints उ. १-१५८) mātariśvan is fixed by nipātana as ending in kan ('nipāta' is a statement that includes further operations). sukratūyā: 'sukratuṃ ātmana icchati'; kyac by 'supa ātmanaḥ kyac' (Pā. sū. 3-1-8); lengthening of the u by 'akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ' (Pā. sū. 7-4-25); root by 'sanādyantā dhātavaḥ' (Pā. sū. 3-1-32); a in the abstract sense by 'a pratyayāt' (Pā. sū. 3-3-102); loss of the a of kyac by 'ato lopaḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-4-48); ṭāp by 'ajādyataṣ ṭāp' (Pā. sū. 4-1-4); in the instrumental singular ḍā by 'supāṃ suluk' (Pā. sū. 7-1-39), loss of the ṭi; though the ending is grave, by 'anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-1-161) it becomes udātta because the udātta a before it was dropped; end-acute; in the Saṃhitā the first member lengthened by 'anyeṣām api dṛśyate'. vivasvate: vivāsati 'to serve'; kvip by 'saṃpadādibhyaḥ kvip' (Vā. 2233); shortening of the penult by 'vyatyayo bahulam': vivas; 'vivas asya asti': matup by 'tad asya-'; v for m by 'mādupadhāyāḥ' (Pā. sū. 8-2-9); by 'tasau matvarthe' (Pā. sū. 1-4-19) the stem is bha, so no ru for the s; dative singular of vivasvat; matup grave as pit, the root accent remains. rodasī: accusative dual; lengthening by 'vā chandasi' (Pā. sū. 6-1-106). hotṛvūrye: 'hotrā vriyate iti hotṛvūryo yajñaḥ', chosen by the hotṛ; vṛñ varaṇe, svādi; kyap by 'etistuśās-' (Pā. sū. 3-1-109); tuk due by 'hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk' not applied, as 'āgamaśāstram anityam'; lengthening of the ṛ by 'akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ'; u for ṝ by 'ud oṣṭhyapūrvasya' (Pā. sū. 7-1-102); lengthening of the penult by 'hali ca'; locative singular; kyap grave as pit, the root accent remains on the ū; as a kṛdanta second member, its accent by 'gatikārakopapadāt kṛt'. asaghnoḥ: ṣagha hiṃsāyām, svādi, used here in the sense of 'carrying' (roots have many senses); laṅ second person singular sip, loss of its i by 'itaś ca'; śnu by 'svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ'; s for the initial ṣ; guṇa of the u of the vikaraṇa; the augment aṭ; ru and visarga; at the head of the pāda not grave; initial udātta as the augment is udātta. ayajaḥ: yaja devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadāneṣu, laṅ second person singular; though bhāram precedes, the vārttika 'samānavākye nighātayuṣmadasmadādeśā vaktavyāḥ' (Pā. sū. 8-1-18-5) restricts the lowering to one sentence, and bhāram belongs to the other clause, so no lowering; initial udātta by the augment. mahaḥ: maha pūjāyām; kvip by 'kvip ca', wholly dropped; śas; jas for śas by 'supāṃ supo bhavanti'; mah + as, ru and visarga; udātta ending after a monosyllable by 'sāv ekācaḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-1-168); or with śas the at of mahat dropped, Vedic; udātta of śas after mahat by 'bṛhanmahator upasaṃkhyānam'.

त्वम॑ग्ने मन॑वे॒ द्याम॑वाशयः पुरू॒रव॑से सु॒कृते॑ सु॒कृ॑त्तरः । [accent ?] श्वा॒त्रेण॒ यत्पि॒त्रोर्मुच्य॑से॒ पर्या त्वा॒ पूर्व॑मनय॒न्नाप॑रं॒ पुनः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

tvámagne mánave dyā́mavāśayaḥ purūrávase sukṛ́te sukṛttaraḥ | [accent ?] śvātréṇa yátpitrórmúcyase páryā tvā pū́rvamanayannā́paraṃ púnaḥ || 4 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The Pada-pāṭha and the bhāṣya of Rik 4 begin on p. 535, PDF 550 — to be written in the next batch.

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । अग्ने । मनवे । द्याम् । अवाशयः । पुरूरवसे । सुऽकृते । सुकृत्ऽतरः । श्वात्रेण । यत् । पित्रोः । मुच्यसे । परि । आ । त्वा । पूर्वम् । अनयन् । आ । अपरम् । पुनरिति ॥ ४ ॥ tvam | agne | manave | dyām | avāśayaḥ | pururavase | su-kṛte | sukṛt-taraḥ | śvātreṇa | yat | pitroḥ | mucyase | pari | ā | tvā | pūrvam | anayan | ā | aparam | punar iti || 4 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अग्ने त्वं मनवे मनोरनुग्रहार्थं द्यां द्युलोकमवाशयः । शब्दितवानसि । पुण्यकर्मभिः साध्यो द्युलोक इति प्रकटितवानसि । सुकृते तव परिचरणं कुर्वते पुरूरवस एतन्नामकस्य राज्ञोऽनुग्रहार्थं सुकृत्तरोऽतिशयेन शोभनफलकार्यभूः । यद्यदा पित्रोररण्योः श्वात्रेण क्षिप्रमथनेन परि मुच्यसे परितो मुक्तो भवसि । उत्पद्यस इत्यर्थः । तदानीं त्वा अरण्योरुत्पन्नं त्वां पूर्वं वेदेः पूर्वदेशमानयन् । आहवनीयत्वेन स्थापितवन्तः । पुनः पश्चादपरं पश्चिमदेशमानयन् । गार्हपत्यरूपेण प्रापितवन्तः । आहवनीयकर्मानुष्ठानादूर्ध्वं गार्हपत्यरूपेण धारितवन्त इत्यर्थः ॥ अवाशयः । वाशृ शब्दे । पुरूरवसे । पुरु रौतीति पुरूरवाः । रु शब्दे । अस्मादौणादिकेऽसुनि पुरसि च पुरूरवाः । उ. ४-१३१ । इति पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घो निपात्यते । सुकृते । सुकर्मपापमन्त्रपुण्येषु कृञः । पा. ३-२-८९ । इति क्विप् । ततस्तुक् । पित्रोः । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । मुच्यसे । अदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वम् । यद्यपि सतिशिष्टस्वरबलीयस्त्वमन्यत्र विकरणेभ्य इति वचनाद्विकरणस्वरः सति शिष्टोऽपि लसार्वधातुकस्वरस्य बाधको न भवति तथापि धातुस्वरं बाधत एव धातुस्वरं श्नास्वर इत्युक्तत्वात् । अतो यक एव स्वरे प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ he agne tvaṃ manave manor anugrahārthaṃ dyāṃ dyulokam avāśayaḥ | śabditavān asi | puṇyakarmabhiḥ sādhyo dyuloka iti prakaṭitavān asi | sukṛte tava paricaraṇaṃ kurvate pururavasa etannāmakasya rājño 'nugrahārthaṃ sukṛttaro 'tiśayena śobhanaphalakāryabhūḥ | yad yadā pitror araṇyoḥ śvātreṇa kṣipramathanena pari mucyase parito mukto bhavasi | utpadyasa ity arthaḥ | tadānīṃ tvā araṇyor utpannaṃ tvāṃ pūrvaṃ vedeḥ pūrvadeśam ānayan | āhavanīyatvena sthāpitavantaḥ | punaḥ paścād aparaṃ paścimadeśam ānayan | gārhapatyarūpeṇa prāpitavantaḥ | āhavanīyakarmānuṣṭhānād ūrdhvaṃ gārhapatyarūpeṇa dhāritavanta ity arthaḥ || avāśayaḥ | vāśṛ śabde | purūravase | puru rautīti purūravāḥ | ru śabde | asmādauṇādike 'suni purasi ca purūravāḥ | u. 4-131 | iti pūrvapadasya dīrgho nipātyate | sukṛte | sukarmapāpamantrapuṇyeṣu kṛñaḥ | pā. 3-2-89 | iti kvip | tatastuk | pitroḥ | udāttayaṇo halpūrvāditi vibhakterudāttatvam | mucyase | adupadeśāllasārvadhātukānudāttatvam | yadyapi satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvamanyatra vikaraṇebhya iti vacanādvikaraṇasvaraḥ sati śiṣṭo 'pi lasārvadhātukasvarasya bādhako na bhavati tathāpi dhātusvaraṃ bādhata eva dhātusvaraṃ śnāsvara ityuktatvāt | ato yaka eva svare prāpte vyatyayenādyudāttatvam ‖ "O Agni! You declared [avāśayaḥ, 'made known'] heaven (dyām) for Manu, for Manu's favour: you announced that the heavenly world is to be won by pious deeds. For King Pururavas, who served you [sukṛte, 'the doer of good'], for his favour you are the exceedingly good [sukṛttaraḥ], the source of well-flavoured fruit. When, by the quick churning (śvātreṇa) of the two parents (the two fire-sticks) you are released [mucyase] — that is, you are born — then they, having brought you who were born from the two araṇis, led you first to the east part of the altar [vedi], and set you [there] as the Āhavanīya [fire]; then again, later, they led you to the western part [aparam], and placed you there in the form of the Gārhapatya fire. The sense is: after the performance of the Āhavanīya rite, they kept you in the Gārhapatya form." (The grammatical tail: vāśṛ śabde; pururavāḥ from ru with the Uṇādi asun, the first member lengthened by purasi ca pururavāḥ (Uṇ. 4-131 in the bhāṣya); sukṛt by P. 3-2-89 with kvip and tuk; pitroḥ: the ending acute by udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt; mucyase: the lasārvadhātuka unaccented; though the vikaraṇa accent does not override the lasārvadhātuka accent, it does override the root accent (dhātusvaraṃ śnāsvaraḥ); so yak's accent would apply, and the initial acute is by vyatyaya.)

Grammar pages 538–539, noted briefly: avāśayaḥ — vāśṛ śabde, divādi, śyan; the causal ṇic, then laṅ 2nd singular; the tiṅanta is unaccented (tiṅantanighāta; no sūtra number printed); pururavase — puru rauti iti pururavāḥ; ru śabde, adādi; the affix asun by sarvadhātubhyo 'sun; ravas is a sānta word; the first member's lengthening is a nipātana by purasi ca pururavāḥ (U. sū. 4-671; the bhāṣya prints उ. ४-१३१); dative singular pururavase; sukṛte — ḍukṛñ karaṇe; kvip by sukarmapāpamantrapuṇyeṣu kṛñaḥ (सुकर्मपापमन्त्रपुण्येषु कृञः, Pā. sū. 3-2-89) when su etc. are upapada; pit, so tuk after the short ṛ by the hrasvasya sūtra; sukṛt; dative singular; pitroḥ — pitṛ + os, yaṇ; the ending acute by udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt (उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वात्, Pā. sū. 6-1-174); mucyase — mucḷ mokṣaṇe, tudādi; passive laṭ 2nd singular, yak by sārvadhātuke yak (Pā. sū. 3-1-67); the lasārvadhātuka unaccented by tāsyanudāttet; the order is root accent, then suffix accent, then vikaraṇa accent; satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvam anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ — so the vikaraṇa accent does not override the lasārvadhātuka accent, but dhātusvaraṃ śnāsvaraḥ (said elsewhere): the vikaraṇa accent overrides the root accent; so yak's initial acute would apply, but by vyatyayo bahulam the root accent remains, giving an initial acute; anayan — ṇīñ prāpaṇe, bhvādi, laṅ 3rd plural; since the atiṅanta pūrvam precedes, the tiṅanta is unaccented (no sūtra number printed). ॥ ४ ॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | मनवे (manave) — for Manu | द्याम् (dyām) — the heavenly world | अवाशयः (avāśayaḥ) — made known | सुकृते (sukṛte) — to the one who does good deeds, honouring you | पुरूरवसे (pururavase) — to Pururavas | सुकृत्तरः (sukṛttaraḥ) — [one who gives] exceedingly good fruits | यत् (yat) — when | पित्रोः (pitroḥ) — of the two parents, the araṇis | श्वात्रेण (śvātreṇa) — by quick churning | परिमुच्यसे (parimucyase) — you are released, born | त्वा (tvā) — you | पूर्वम् (pūrvam) — [of the altar] in the front part | आ अनयन् (ā anayan) — they placed [as the Āhavanīya form] | पुनः (punaḥ) — afterwards | अपरम् (aparam) — in the western part | आ अनयन् (ā anayan) — they placed [in the Gārhapatya form].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You made the heavenly world known to Manu; to Pururavas, who does good deeds in your honour, you gave exceedingly excellent fruits. When you were born, released from the swift churning of the two araṇis, they placed you first in the front part of the altar in the form of the Āhavanīya, and then in the western part in the form of the Gārhapatya fire-pit.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, you announced heaven to Manu ; you were the benefactor to the king Pururavas who worshipped you ; when you, after being kindled were released from your parents, they brought you first to the east, then to the west (of the altar).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ मनवे द्यामवाशयः (manave dyām avāśayaḥ) — Manu Prajāpati has been made known [to have received] the fruit of heaven. In the Ṛgveda the name Manu occurs in many riks (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-80-16; 2-33-13; 8-63-1; 10-100-5); in the Yajurveda, Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1-5-1-3; 7-5-15-3; 2-5-9-1; 2-6-7-1; 3-3-2-1; 5-4-10-5; 6-6-6-1; Atharvaveda 14-2-41; Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā 8-15; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1-1-4-14; Jaiminīya Upaniṣad-Brāhmaṇa 3-15-2 — and in many other mantras Manu is spoken of. In the Ṛgveda this Manu is said to be the root-man of mankind, and the first and the chief among those who perform sacrifice and in other matters. In Taittirīya Saṃhitā 3-1-9-4 and in the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa 5-14-1-2 [as printed], Nābhānediṣṭha, a son of this Manu, is described as striving to get his share of his father's estate. To Manu in the Ṛgveda the name Vivasvān (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-50-1), or Vaivasvata, son of Vivasvān (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-10-24 [as printed]; Śata. Brā. 13-4-3-3; Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra 10-7; Nirukta 12-10), is given; and since he is said to be of the line of Savarṇā or Saraṇyū, he is also called Sāvarṇi (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-10-24 [as printed] etc.); and as Saṃvaraṇa's line, Sāṃvaraṇi (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-51-1). In the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, in the eighth maṇḍala, of sūktas 27–31 (59 riks), Manu Vaivasvata is the seer; and in the ninth maṇḍala, in sūkta 101, of riks 10–12 (3 riks), Manu Sāṃvaraṇa is the seer. So Vaivasvata and Sāṃvaraṇi must be taken as different persons. अवाशयः (avāśayaḥ) — vāśṛ śabde: śabditavān asi, prakaṭitavān asi: you uttered, made known. पुरूरवसे (pururavase) — puru rautīti pururavāḥ; ru śabde: 'one who makes much noise (sound) in front'; that is the etymological sense of pururavas. Yāska says pururavā bahudhā roruyate ['Pururavas is much shouted at'] (Ni. 10-46). In this rik the word pururavase denotes a king of that name. In the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, in the 95th sūkta of the tenth maṇḍala, as in the line pururavo mā mṛthā ... [the print quotes:]

पुरूरवोऽनु ते केतमायं राजा मी [?] वीर तन्वस्तदासीः । purūravo 'nu te ketamāyaṃ rājā mī [?] vīra tanvastadāsīḥ |

Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-5; मी as read, the vowel sign is not certain. Gloss (editorial and tentative): "Pururavas, I followed your will; the king [?], O hero, was [master] of my body." This rik supports the account of a king Pururavas. In the 95th sūkta of the tenth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā there is a conversation between this king and the apsaras Urvaśī, who deserted him; this conversation is explained in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (11-5-1) as a story, nicely. The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa [11-5-1-1] says this king is the son of the goddess Iḍā; in the Ṛgveda he is called Aila ['son of Iḍā'] Pururavas [by the name] ailaḥ pururavāḥ; and this king is the seer of 9 riks in all (1, 3, 6, 8–10, 12, 14, 17) of the 95th sūkta [of the tenth maṇḍala]. In the Purāṇas and other works the history of this king Pururavas is described in different ways. सुकृते (sukṛte) — tava paricaraṇaṃ kurvate: 'one who does service to you, [i.e.] who does work in the form of attendance on you'. सुकृत्तरः (sukṛttaraḥ) — atiśayena śobhanaphalakāryabhūḥ: 'one who gives in abundance excellent fruits'. श्वात्रेण (śvātreṇa) — kṣipramathanena: 'by the swift [kṣipra] churning, [the one] who is born'; śvātram iti kṣipranāma āśu ātanaṃ bhavati (Ni. 5-3): 'the word śvātra is a name of "swift": it is a quick spreading'. पित्रोर्मुच्यसे (pitror mucyase) — here pitroḥ means the two araṇis, which are the two parents; [the sense is] 'you are released from them'; that is, 'you are born from them'. Skandasvāmin explains pitroḥ as dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ — 'of heaven and earth'. आ त्वा पूर्वमनयन् आ अपरं पुनः (ā tvā pūrvam anayan ā aparaṃ punaḥ) — after Agni is produced in the araṇi, [priests] first place him in the fire-pit called Āhavanīya in the eastern part of the sacrificial altar; and then, from there, in the fire-pit called Gārhapatya in the western part — that is the sense. This order is still followed in sacrifices; it is described in the Śrauta-sūtras.

The sacrificer who knows the oblation joined with vaṣaṭ, that is, who offers it … [the Sanskrit continues on p. 540]."
