Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, remainder p. 540, top: एकायुर्मुख्यान्नस्त्वमग्रे प्रथमं तं यजमानं विशस्तदनुकूलाः प्रजा आविवाससि । सर्वतः प्रकाशयसि ॥ पुष्टिवर्धनः । वृधु वृद्धौ । अस्माण्णिजन्तान्नन्द्यादित्वात् ल्युः । लित्स्वरेणोत्तरपदस्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन स एव शिष्यते । उद्यतस्रुचे । यमु उपरमे । अस्मादुत्पूर्वान्निष्ठेति क्तप्रत्यये अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिकलोपः । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । उद्यता स्रुग्येनेति बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । वेद । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घत्वम् ॥ ३२ ॥ ekāyurmukhyānnastvamagre prathamaṃ taṃ yajamānaṃ viśastadanukūlāḥ prajā āvivāsasi | sarvataḥ prakāśayasi ‖ puṣṭivardhanaḥ | vṛdhu vṛddhau | asmāṇṇijantānnandyāditvāt lyuḥ | litsvareṇottarapadasyādyudāttatvam | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvena sa eva śiṣyate | udyatasruce | yamu uparame | asmādutpūrvānniṣṭheti ktapratyaye anudāttopadeśetyādinānunāsikalopaḥ | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | udyatā srugyeneti bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | veda | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvam ‖ 32 ‖ "[Ekāyuḥ:] you, the chief food[-giver], first (agre) make that sacrificer, and then the subjects (viśaḥ) favourable to him, shine: you make [them] shine on all sides." (The grammatical tail: puṣṭivardhanaḥ, vṛdhu vṛddhau, causative, lyu as of the nandyādi class; initial acute of the second member by the lit accent, kept by the kṛt-second-member rule; udyatasruce: yamu uparame with ut, kta by niṣṭhā, the nasal lost by anudāttopadeśa…; gatir anantaraḥ; udyatā srug yena, a bahuvrīhi with the first member's accent; veda: lengthened in the Saṃhitā by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ. The close ॥ ३२ ॥ marks the end of Varga 32.)

Grammar pages 541–542, noted briefly: puṣṭivardhanaḥ — vṛdhu vṛddhau, bhvādi; ṇic by P. 3-1-26 hetumati ca (हेतुमति च); lyu by P. 7-1-134 [as printed; for 3-1-134] nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ, the root being in the nandyādi class; the l of lyu is it; yu → ana by P. 6-1-1 [as printed; for 7-1-1] yuvor anākau; guṇa of the penultimate; vardhana; being lit-final, initial acute by liti (P. 6-1-193); puṣṭiṃ vardhayatīti, a kṛt-final compound, the accent by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; udyatasruce — yamu uparame; with ut, the affix kta by P. 3-2-102 niṣṭhā (निष्ठा); the m lost by P. 6-4-37 anudāttopadeśa…; udyata; the accent by P. 6-2-49 gatir anantaraḥ (गतिरनन्तरः); a bahuvrīhi with first-member accent by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (no number printed); dative singular; veda — vida jñāne, adādi; ṇal in place of laṭ by P. 3-4-83 vido laṭo vā (विदो लटो वा); guṇa; yaḥ being correlated, the tiṅanta is not unaccented; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-135 dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | वृषभः (vṛṣabhaḥ) — [one who] showers (the wishes) | पुष्टिवर्धनः (puṣṭivardhanaḥ) — [one who] increases the wealth of the sacrificer | उद्यतस्रुचे (udyatasruce) — for the sacrificer who lifts the ladle | श्रवाय्यः (śravāyyaḥ) — [one who is] called by mantras | भवसि (bhavasi) — you are | यः (yaḥ) — which sacrificer | वषट्कृतिम् (vaṣaṭkṛtim) — with vaṣaṭ | आहुतिम् (āhutim) — the oblation | परि वेद (pari veda) — knows well (and offers) | एकायुः (ekāyuḥ) — [you, the] cause of his principal life | अग्रे (agre) — first [that sacrificer] | विशः (viśaḥ) — [afterwards] subjects favourable to him | आविवाससि (āvivāsasi) — you make shine.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You shower the wishes and increase the sacrificer's prosperity. Hear the call of the sacrificer who lifts the ladle for the oblation. You, the cause of his principal life [or: the foremost giver of food], first make that sacrificer shine, who knows well the oblation with vaṣaṭ [and the recitation] and offers it; and afterwards make the subjects favourable to him shine too. [That is, you please him by giving his wishes.]

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, you are the showerer of desires, the increaser of prosperity of your worshipper ; you will hear the hymns of the worshipper as soon as the ladle is lifted (to pour the oblation on the fire). Upon him who fully understands the invocation and makes the oblation with the word Vashatkriti at the moment of pouring the clarified butter on the fire, you, the provider of food, first bestow light, and then upon all men.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ वृषभः (vṛṣabhaḥ) — kāmānāṃ varṣitā: the one who rains down wishes; 'the bestower of desires' [English as printed]. पुष्टिवर्धनः (puṣṭivardhanaḥ) — vṛdhu vṛddhau, puṣṭeḥ vardhitā: one who gives the sacrificer wealth, food and the like; one who nourishes and increases growth. उद्यतस्रुचे (udyatasruce) — sruk is the wooden ladle with which the homa is made; one who, with that ladle filled with ghee (tuppa), lifts it up to pour it in the fire — the sacrificer. श्रवाय्यः (śravāyyaḥ) — śravaṇīyo bhavasi: you hear the sacrificer's call. य आहुतिं परि वेदा वषट्कृतिम् (ya āhutiṃ pari vedā vaṣaṭkṛtim) — when performing a homa in the fire, after reciting the yājyā mantra addressed to the deity, they add at the end of the invocation the word vaṣaṭ and perform the homa; this is called vaṣaṭkṛti. Knowing this rule, the sacrificer who performs the homa with the vaṣaṭkāra is one who knows the rules of rites. एकायुः (ekāyuḥ) — mukhyānnastvam: [you are] the chief among givers of food. On the sense of this word Skandasvāmin tells a story: formerly, Āyu, a gandharva, son of the apsaras Urvaśī, brought Agni from the world of the Gandharvas and performed a sacrifice; so Agni first favoured that Āyu and afterwards favoured the people of the other gods; that story is hinted at here, he says, by the words ekāyur agre. विशः (viśaḥ) — prajāḥ: subjects, and other people. आविवाससि (āvivāsasi) — sarvataḥ prakāśayati: you cause to shine; that is, you gratify; you make glad.

saṃbhajanamatreti bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | supāṃ sulugiti saptamyā ḍādeśaḥ | paritakmye | taka hasane | asmādauṇādiko bhāve mak | tadarhatīti chandasi ca | pā. 5-1-67 | iti yaḥ | prādayo gatādyarthe prathamayeti samāse 'vyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | dabhrebhiḥ | dambhu dambhe | sphāyitañcītyādinā rak | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisādeśābhāvaḥ | samṛtā | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | pūrvavadākāraḥ | haṃsi | hanteḥ sipi naścāpadāntasya jhali | pā. 8-3-24 | ityanusvāraḥ | yadvṛttayogādanighātaḥ | bhūyasaḥ | bahorlopo bhū ca bahoḥ | pā. 6-4-158 | iti bahuśabdāduttarasyeyasuna īkāralopo bahorbhūbhāvaśca | nittvādādyudāttatvam ‖ "O Agni, who are vicarṣaṇi [of excellent knowledge]! You protect or fill [piparṣi] the man who walks the crooked path (vṛjina-vartani), who is without right conduct, [bringing him] into the rite (vidathe) fit for [his] coming together [sakman]: that is, you make him fit for the performance of good deeds. And you who, when in the contest for wealth (dhane) — [wealth] that is to be gone after on all sides and is most dear to the brave, as wealth [is to others] — in the battle (śūrasātā) where the brave seek to share, with the few (dabhrebhiḥ cit), even the little [alpa] and heroism-less men [yourself being the means], destroy [haṃsi] the many (bhūyasaḥ), mighty enemies, when it has come to a proper fighting [samṛtā], for his favour. 'Such is your greatness.' [Yāska: dabhram arbhakam among the names of 'small' (Nirukta 3-20).]"

Grammar pages 545–547, noted briefly: vṛjinavartanim — vṛjinā vartaniḥ yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (no number printed): the first member's accent overrides the compound accent; sakman — ṣaca samavāye; s for the initial ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; manin by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. sū. 3-2-75); no iṭ by neḍ vaśi kṛti (नेड्वशि कृति, Pā. sū. 7-2-8); being in the nyaṅkvādi class, kutva of the c by nyaṅkvādīnāṃ ca (Pā. sū. 7-3-53); locative singular, luk by supāṃ suluk; nit, so initial acute by ñnityādir nityam (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); piparṣi — pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ, juhotyādi; laṭ 2nd singular sip; ślu by juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ; doubling by ślau; the reduplicate ṛ shortened by hrasvaḥ, made a by urat and ar by uraṇ raparaḥ; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; the reduplicate a → i by artipipartyoś ca (अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च, Pā. sū. 7-4-77); guṇa before the sārvadhātuka sip; ṣatva by ādeśapratyayayoḥ (आदेशप्रत्यययोः); after an atiṅanta the tiṅanta is unaccented (no sūtra numbers printed for these); śūrasātā — śu gatau, sautra; kran by śuṣicimīnāṃ dīrghaś ca (U. sū. 2-183; the bhāṣya prints उ. २-२५) with lengthening; kit, no guṇa; nit, initial acute; vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau, bhvādi; ktin by striyāṃ ktin; ā by janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-42); śūrāṇāṃ sātiḥ saṃbhajanam atra, a bahuvrīhi with the first member's accent; locative ḍā by supāṃ suluk (Pā. sū. 7-1-39); ḍit, so the final i drops; paritakmye — taka hasane, bhvādi; the Uṇādi mak in the sense of the action; takma; ya by chandasi ca (Pā. sū. 5-1-67) in the sense takmam arhati; compounded with pari by prādayo gatādyarthe prathamayā (Pā. Ma. 2-2-18-4); the avyaya-first compound keeps the first member's accent by tatpuruṣe tulyārtha… (Pā. sū. 6-2-2); dabhrebhiḥ — dambhu dambhe, svādi; rak by sphāyitañcivañciśaki… (U. sū. 2-170); kit, so the penultimate n drops by aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-24); ais for bhis by ato bhisa ais (Pā. sū. 7-1-9) is optional by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. sū. 3-1-10 [as printed; for 7-1-10]) and does not come; ru and visarga; samṛtā — locative ḍā by supāṃ suluk (Pā. sū. 7-1-39); sam keeps its accent by gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. sū. 6-2-49) before the kta-final; initial acute; haṃsi — hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi; laṭ 2nd singular sip; anusvāra by naś cāpadāntasya jhali (Pā. sū. 8-3-24); with yaḥ the tiṅanta is not unaccented, by yadvṛttayogān nityam (no number printed); sip is pit and unaccented, so the root accent: initial acute; bhūyasaḥ — bahu + īyasun in the comparative sense; bahor lopo bhū ca bahoḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-158): the ī of īyasun drops and bahu becomes bhū; accusative plural bhūyasaḥ; īyasun is nit, so initial acute by ñnityādir nityam (Pā. sū. 6-1-197). ॥ ६ ॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ विचर्षणे (vicarṣaṇe) — [O one] endowed with excellent knowledge | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | वृजिनवर्तनिम् (vṛjinavartanim) — [a man] walking on a bad path | नरम् (naram) — the man | सक्मन् (sakman) — [in a rite] fit to join | विदथे (vidathe) — in the rite | पिपर्षि (piparṣi) — you join [and protect] | यः (yaḥ) — [you] who | परितक्म्ये (paritakmye) — [in the] wealth that is to be sought on all sides | धने (dhane) — [that] is to be won only by the brave | शूरसाता (śūrasātā) — [in] the battle sought by the brave | दभ्रेभिः चित् (dabhrebhiḥ cit) — even with the few, heroism-less [men] | संमृता (saṃmṛtā) — at the time of battle | भूयसः (bhūyasaḥ) — [the] many, mighty | हंसि (haṃsi) — you kill.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni, of excellent knowledge! You join in a good rite, and protect, the man who walks on a bad path; and when a battle is on [sought by the brave], to win wealth which is to be sought on all sides and can be won only by the brave, you, by your favour, kill the mighty enemy hosts with the few and heroism-less [men].

॥ English Translation ॥

All-knowing Agni, you direct the man who follows improper paths to acts that are fitted to make him good ; in a battle where the great warriors strive for wealth you kill the many by means of the few.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ वृजिनवर्तनिम् (vṛjinavartanim) — kuṭilavartanim, sadācārarahitam: one who goes on crooked paths; one who has no good conduct; [that is] one who leads bad ways, and does not perform actions of good conduct. विदथे (vidathe) — vedane svakarmādhikārayukte: [fit for] knowing, [that is] having a right to his own rites — so that he becomes attached to the works fitting to him; or vidatha means the sacrifice (Ni. 3-19): so that he engages in the sacrificial rites. सक्मन् (sakman) — sacanīye samavetuṃ yogye: fit to be joined; [i.e.] suitable. विश्वचर्षणे / विचर्षणे (vicarṣaṇe) — viśiṣṭajñānayukta: endowed with special knowledge; the one who knows everything. शूरसाता (śūrasātā) — śūrāṇāṃ sātiḥ saṃbhajanam atra; śūraiḥ saṃbhajanīye yuddhe: 'in the battle that is full of heroes who are in it'. परितक्म्ये (paritakmye) — parito gantavye dhane: [wealth] that is to be gone after on all sides; 'dhana is dear to the brave [as the wealth of the battle]; as to ordinary men wealth is dear, to the brave a battle is dear': that is the idea. दभ्रेभिः (dabhrebhiḥ) — since the word dabhra is read among the names of 'small', such as arbhaka (Ni. 3-20), dabhrebhiḥ means 'by the small [forces], the weak and non-heroic'. समृता (samṛtā) — ṛ gatau: samyag yoddhuṃ prāpte sati: when [men] are set out to fight, [in that battle]. भूयसः (bhūyasaḥ) — prauḍhān pratipakṣiṇaḥ: [slaying] the very mighty soldiers of the enemy hosts, the enemy hosts of the heroes, the mightier ones.

Rik 7 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 547–552

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Line 1 flagged [accent ?]: the bar under त्त of उत्तमे lies close to the subscript त. In line 2 the bar under स्ता is taken as the subscript त, not an accent.

त्वं तम॑ग्ने अमृत॒त्व उ॑त्त॒मे मर्तं॑ दधासि॒ श्रव॑से दि॒वेदि॑वे । [accent ?] यस्ता॑तृषा॒ण उ॒भया॑य॒ जन्म॑ने॒ मयः॑ कृ॒णोषि॒ प्रय॒ आ च॑ सू॒रये॑ ॥ ७ ॥

tvaṃ támagne amṛtatvá uttamé mártaṃ dadhāsi śrávase divédive | [accent ?] yástātṛṣāṇá ubháyāya jánmane máyaḥ kṛṇóṣi práya ā́ ca sūráye || 7 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Rik 7 — continued (the Saṃhitā and Pada are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 548–550

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अग्ने त्वं तं मर्तं तथाविधं त्वत्सेविनं मनुष्यं दिवेदिवे प्रतिदिनं श्रवसेऽन्नार्थमुत्तमेऽमृतत्वे उत्कृष्टे मरणरहिते पदे दधासि । धारयसि । यो यजमान उभयाय जन्मने द्विविधजन्मार्थम् । द्विपदां चतुष्पदां लाभायेत्यर्थः । ततृषाणोऽतिशयेन तृष्णायुक्तो भवति तस्मै सूरयेऽभिज्ञाय यजमानाय मयः सुखम् । यद्वै सुखं तन्मय इति श्रुत्यन्तरात् । प्रयश्चान्नमस्मा कृणोषि । सर्वतः करोषि ॥ ततृषाणः । ञितृषा पिपासायाम् । लिटः कानच् । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वम् । संहितायां दीर्घश्छान्दसः । कृणोषि । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च । धिन्विकृण्व्योरच्चेत्युप्रत्ययः । चादिलोपे विभाषेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥ he agne tvaṃ taṃ martaṃ tathāvidhaṃ tvatsevinaṃ manuṣyaṃ divedive pratidinaṃ śravase 'nnārthamuttame 'mṛtatve utkṛṣṭe maraṇarahite pade dadhāsi | dhārayasi | yo yajamāna ubhayāya janmane dvividhajanmārtham | dvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ lābhāyetyarthaḥ | tatṛṣāṇo 'tiśayena tṛṣṇāyukto bhavati tasmai sūraye 'bhijñāya yajamānāya mayaḥ sukham | yadvai sukhaṃ tanmaya iti śrutyantarāt | prayaścānnamasmā kṛṇoṣi | sarvataḥ karoṣi ‖ tatṛṣāṇaḥ | ñitṛṣā pipāsāyām | liṭaḥ kānac | cittvādantodāttatvam | saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaśchāndasaḥ | kṛṇoṣi | kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayośca | dhinvikṛṇvyoraccetyupratyayaḥ | cādilope vibhāṣeti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ ‖ "O Agni! You set such a mortal [martam], who serves you,, day by day [dive-dive], for food [śravase], in the highest [uttame] immortality — in the best, deathless place. The sacrificer who, for the sake of both kinds of birth (ubhayāya janmane) — that is, to gain two-footed and four-footed beings — is exceedingly eager: for that wise sacrificer you provide mayas [happiness] and prayas [food], from all sides. [Tatṛṣāṇaḥ: from ñitṛṣā pipāsāyām ('to thirst'), liṭ replaced by kānac, end-acute as cit, the lengthening in the Saṃhitā Vedic; kṛṇoṣi: from kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca, the u by dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca; the verb is not unaccented by cādilope vibhāṣā. (Yad vai sukhaṃ tan mayaḥ is cited from another Śruti for mayas = happiness.)]"

Grammar pages 549–550, noted briefly: dadhāsi — ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, juhotyādi, laṭ 2nd singular; after an atiṅanta the verb is unaccented by tiṅ atiṅaḥ (Pā. sū. 8-1-28); martaḥ — explained at 1-2-30 [as printed], in the 20th mantra; śravase — śru śravaṇe, bhvādi; the Uṇādi asun; śravas; dative singular; nit, initial acute; tatṛṣāṇaḥ — ñitṛṣā pipāsāyām; kānac by liṭaḥ kānaj vā (लिटः कानज्वा, Pā. sū. 3-2-106); doubling as in place of liṭ; halādiśeṣa leaves tṛ in the reduplicate; its ṛ becomes a by urat, ar by the paribhāṣā uraṇ raparaḥ; ṇ by aṭkupvāṅ…; kānac is cit, so end-acute by citaḥ (Pā. sū. 6-1-163); if the word were taken as tujādi, the length would appear in the Pada too, so the Saṃhitā lengthening is to be taken as Vedic; kṛṇoṣi — kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca, bhvādi, laṭ 2nd singular sip; idit, so num; its n → ṇ by ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam; the affix u as vikaraṇa, with a for the root-final, by dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca (धिन्विकृण्व्योर च, Pā. sū. 3-1-80); the a drops before u by ato lopaḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-48); guṇa of the u before sip; ṣatva by ādeśapratyayayoḥ; by acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau the dropped a counts as present (sthānivadbhāva), so the penult does not take guṇa because of u; by cādilope vibhāṣā (चादिलोपे विभाषा, Pā. sū. 8-1-63), ca being dropped, the verb is not made unaccented. ॥ ७ ॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | तं मर्तम् (taṃ martam) — that man [who worships you] | दिवेदिवे (dive-dive) — every day | श्रवसे (śravase) — for food | उत्तमे (uttame) — in the best | अमृतत्वे (amṛtatve) — in the deathless place | दधासि (dadhāsi) — you place | यः (yaḥ) — which sacrificer | उभयाय जन्मने (ubhayāya janmane) — for beings of the two kinds of birth, or for two-footed [and others] and four-footed beings, [for the gain of them] | ततृषाणः (tatṛṣāṇaḥ) — [is] exceedingly eager | सूरये (sūraye) — [to him,] the wise sacrificer | मयः (mayaḥ) — happiness | प्रयः च (prayaḥ ca) — and food | आ कृणोषि (ā kṛṇoṣi) — you give completely.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You place the man who worships you, day after day, for food, in the best and deathless place. And to the sacrificer who is exceedingly eager to gain beings of the two kinds of birth, two-footed (men and others) and four-footed (cows, horses and others), that wise sacrificer you give happiness and food completely.

॥ English Translation ॥

O Agni, you always keep that mortal in the highest immortality by daily food ; you bestow on the prudent man who desires wealth consisting creatures of both kinds of birth, happiness and food.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अमृतत्वे (amṛtatve) — maraṇarahite pade: 'in a place free of death', that is, in the highest [places] such as heaven. श्रवसे (śravase) — annārtham: for the sake of food (to bring about the use of food). दिवेदिवे (dive-dive) — pratidinam: every day. ततृषाणः (tatṛṣāṇaḥ) — atiśayena tṛṣṇāyuktaḥ: one who is full of desire; one who has much desire. उभयाय जन्मने (ubhayāya janmane) — 'for beings of the two kinds of birth': two-footed beings — that is, his own household, such as sons, grandsons, servants; four-footed beings — cows, horses and other useful animals. The sense: the sacrificer who longs for riches of these two kinds. मयः (mayaḥ) — sukham: 'mayas' is 'happiness', as a Śruti sentence has it. Since mayas is read among the twenty names of happiness beginning śiṃbātā, śatarā, mayaḥ means happiness (Ni. 3-13). प्रयः (prayaḥ) — since the word prayas is read among the twenty-eight names of food beginning andhas, vāja, prayaḥ means food (Ni. 3-9). सूरये (sūraye) — abhijñāya yajamānāya: to the sacrificer who is knowing, or discerning.

Rik 8 (Triṣṭubh) (begun; see the next batch) pp. 550–556

Saṃhitā-pāṭha Line 2 flagged [accent ?]: a bar is printed under म of ऋध्याम, next to the subscript of ध्या.

त्वं नो॑ अग्ने स॒नये॒ धना॑नां य॒शसं॑ का॒रुं कृ॑णुहि॒ स्तवा॑नः । ऋ॒ध्याम॒ कर्मा॒पसा॒ नवे॑न दे॒वैर्द्या॑वापृथिवी॒ प्राव॑तं नः ॥ ८ ॥ [accent ?]

tváṃ no agne sanáye dhánānāṃ yaśásaṃ kārúṃ kṛṇuhi stávānaḥ | ṛdhyā́ma kármāpásā návena deváirdyāvāpṛthivī prā́vataṃ naḥ || 8 || [accent ?] Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The Pada-pāṭha and the bhāṣya of Rik 8 begin on p. 551, PDF 566 — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 8 — continued (the Saṃhitā is given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 551–553

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । नः । अग्ने । सनये । धनानाम् । यशसम् । कारुम् । कृणुहि । स्तवानः । ऋध्याम । कर्म । अपसा । नवेन । देवैः । द्यावापृथिवी इति । प्र । अवतम् । नः ॥ ८ ॥ tvam | naḥ | agne | sanaye | dhanānām | yaśasam | kārum | kṛṇuhi | stavānaḥ | ṛdhyāma | karma | apasā | navena | devaiḥ | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | pra | avatam | naḥ || 8 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अग्ने स्तवानः स्तूयमानस्त्वं नोऽस्माकं धनानां सनये दानार्थं यशसं यशोयुक्तं कारुं कर्मणां कर्तारं पुत्रं कृणुहि । कुरु । नवेन नूतनेनापसा प्राप्तेन त्वद्दत्तेन पुत्रेण कर्म योगदानादिरूपमृध्याम । वर्धयाम । हे द्यावापृथिवी उभे देवते देवैरन्यैः सह नोऽस्मान्प्रावतम् । प्रकर्षेण रक्षतम् ॥ यशसम् । अर्शआदित्वादच्प्रत्ययः । व्यत्ययेन प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । यद्वा । सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्यः क्विब्वक्तव्यः । म. ३-१-११-३ । इति यशस्शब्दात् क्विप् । तस्य प्रत्ययान्तस्य सनाद्यन्तत्वाद्धातुसंज्ञायां क्विप्चेति क्विप्प्रत्ययान्तधातोः सति शिष्टत्वाद्धातोरित्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । कृणुहि । उतश्च प्रत्ययाच्छन्दोवावचनम् । पा. ६-४-१०६-१ । इति हेर्लुगभावः । स्तवानः । सम्यानच् स्तुवः । उ. २-८६ । इति बहुलवचनात्केवलस्यापि स्तौतेरानच्प्रत्ययः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । ऋध्याम । ऋधु वृद्धौ । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । यासुट उदात्तत्वम् । द्यावापृथिवी । दिवो द्यावा । पा. ६-३-२९ । इति द्यावादेशः । आमन्त्रितानुदात्तत्वम् ॥ he agne stavānaḥ stūyamānas tvaṃ no 'smākaṃ dhanānāṃ sanaye dānārthaṃ yaśasaṃ yaśoyuktaṃ kāruṃ karmaṇāṃ kartāraṃ putraṃ kṛṇuhi | kuru | navena nūtanenāpasā prāptena tvaddattena putreṇa karma yogadānādirūpam ṛdhyāma | vardhayāma | he dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe devate devair anyaiḥ saha no 'smān prāvatam | prakarṣeṇa rakṣatam ‖ yaśasam | arśaāditvādacpratyayaḥ | vyatyayena pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvam | yadvā | sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kvibvaktavyaḥ | ma. 3-1-11-3 | iti yaśasśabdāt kvip | tasya pratyayāntasya sanādyantatvāddhātusaṃjñāyāṃ kvipceti kvippratyayāntadhātoḥ sati śiṣṭatvāddhātorityantodāttatvam | kṛṇuhi | utaśca pratyayācchandovāvacanam | pā. 6-4-106-1 | iti herlugabhāvaḥ | stavānaḥ | samyānac stuvaḥ | u. 2-86 | iti bahulavacanātkevalasyāpi stauterānacpratyayaḥ | vṛṣāditvādādyudāttatvam | ṛdhyāma | ṛdhu vṛddhau | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | yāsuṭa udāttatvam | dyāvāpṛthivī | divo dyāvā | pā. 6-3-29 | iti dyāvādeśaḥ | āmantritānudāttatvam ‖ "O Agni, being praised: for the gift [sanaye, 'for the giving'] of wealth to us, make [kṛṇuhi] a son — a renowned (yaśasam) doer (kārum) of works. By a new (navena) work [apasā] — a son given by you — may we prosper (ṛdhyāma, 'increase') in the work, [that is,] in yoga [rites], gift-giving and so on. O Heaven and Earth, both goddesses, protect us well, together with the other gods."

Grammar pages 552–553, noted briefly: yaśasam — yaśaḥ asya asti: the affix ac in the possessive sense by arśa ādibhyo 'c (अर्श आदिभ्योऽच्, Pā. sū. 5-2-127); the suffix's initial acute would apply, but by vyatyayo bahulam the syllable before the suffix is acute, so the word is middle-acute; or, by sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kvip vaktavyaḥ (Pā. Ma. 3-1-11-3), kvip after yaśas in a verbal sense; it is then a root by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; again kvip by kvip ca (Pā. sū. 3-2-76); a prātipadika by kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca; accusative singular; by dhātoḥ, the root accent being satiśiṣṭa, end-acute (no numbers printed for these); kṛṇuhi — kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca, loṭ 2nd singular, hi for sip; the stem kṛṇu by dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca as before (1-2-31-7 [as printed]); hi would be dropped by utaś ca pratyayād asaṃyogapūrvāt (Pā. sū. 6-4-106), but by utaś ca pratyayāc chandovāvacanam (Pā. sū. 6-4-106-1) it is optional in the Veda and is not dropped; the tiṅanta is unaccented (no number printed); stavānaḥ — ṣṭuñ stutau, adādi; s for the initial ṣ; ānac by sam yānac stuvaḥ (U. sū. 2-246; the bhāṣya prints उ. २-८६), which names stu with sam, but by the bahula of the Uṇādi also after the bare root; guṇa before ānac, av for o; end-acute by citaḥ (Pā. sū. 6-1-163) would apply, but as a vṛṣādi word it is initial-acute by vṛṣādīnāṃ ca (Pā. sū. 6-1-203); ṛdhyāma — ṛdhu vṛddhau, divādi; vidhiliṅ 1st plural mas; its s dropped by nityaṃ ṅitaḥ (Pā. sū. 3-4-99); yāsuṭ by yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅic ca (Pā. sū. 3-4-103); the śyan due by divādibhyaḥ śyan dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; yāsuṭ is ṅit, so no guṇa of the penult; yāsuṭ is acute, so the ā of ṛdhyāma is acute; at the head of the pāda the āṣṭamika lowering does not apply; dyāvāpṛthivī — dyauś ca pṛthivī ca, an itaretara dvandva; dyāvā for div in the compound by divo dyāvā (Pā. sū. 6-3-29); vocative dual by supāṃ suluk (Pā. sū. 7-1-39), the pūrvasavarṇa lengthening as ekādeśa; all-low by āmantritasya ca (no number printed); avatam — ava rakṣaṇe, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd dual; the tiṅanta is unaccented. ॥ ८ ॥ The right half of the last lines of p. 553 is cut off in the better scan; they were read from the old scan, PDF 568.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | स्तवानः (stavānaḥ) — praised | त्वम् (tvam) — you | नः (naḥ) — to us | धनानाम् (dhanānām) — of wealth | सनये (sanaye) — for the gift | यशसम् (yaśasam) — endowed with fame | कारुम् (kārum) — [a son] who does [good] works | कृणुहि (kṛṇuhi) — grant | नवेन (navena) — [by] the new | अपसा (apasā) — [by your] favour [by the son] obtained | कर्म (karma) — [we] sacrifices and other rites | ऋध्याम (ṛdhyāma) — may we make flourish | द्यावापृथिवी (dyāvāpṛthivī) — O deities of Heaven and Earth | देवैः (devaiḥ) — together with other gods | नः (naḥ) — us | प्रावतम् (prāvatam) — protect.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! Praised by us, grant us a son — a renowned doer of works — for the gift of wealth. We shall make the sacrifices and other rites flourish by that new son, obtained by your favour. O deities of Heaven and Earth, protect us together with the other gods.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, who are praised by us for the sake of wealth, give us an illustrious son the performer of the sacrifice ; we may increase (or improve) the act by a new offspring (given by you) ; Heaven and Earth, protect us with the other gods.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ कारुम् (kārum) — karmaṇāṃ kartāram: one who does works [the Kannada: 'one who performs the tasks']. Here the commentator supplies the word putram ('son'). स्तवानः (stavānaḥ) — stūyamānaḥ: [one who is] praised. ऋध्याम (ṛdhyāma) — ṛdhu vṛddhau: vardhayāma — may we make [it] prosper. यशसम् (yaśasam) — yaśoyuktam: endowed with fame; or the word yaśas means 'food' (Ni. 3-9).

nittvādādyudāttatvam | bodhi | budha avagamane | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | vā chandasīti herapittvasya vikalpitatvena pittvādaṅittve satyaṅitaśca | pā. 6-4-103 | iti herdhirādeśaḥ | laghūpadhaguṇaḥ | dhātorantyalopaśchāndasaḥ | pramatiḥ | mana jñāne | ktinyanudāttopadeśetyādinānunāsikalopaḥ | prakṛṣṭā matiryasyeti bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | ūpiṣe | ḍuvap Being the wakeful (jāgṛvi) among all the gods, dwelling in the lap (upasthe) — the proximity — of your parents, Heaven and Earth, in the form of mother and father, become for us the maker of our bodies [tanūkṛt: taking the form of a son], and wake up [bodhi, 'be aware'] — that is, favour us (anugṛhāṇa). Likewise be for the sacrificer, the worker, endowed with pramati ['favourable intent']: this [bhava] is supplied. O auspicious one (kalyāṇa)! You pour out (opiṣe) all wealth for the sacrificer. " (The grammatical tail: upasthe with ka by P. 3-2-4 and the first member end-acute by the marudvṛdhādi Vārttika (P. 6-2-106-2); jāgṛviḥ with kvin by Uṇ. 4-54, initial acute; bodhi: śap dropped, hi made pit optionally, then dhi by P. 6-4-103, guṇa, the root-final dropped as a Vedic form; pramatiḥ, a bahuvrīhi; ūpiṣe: Vedic liṭ, se for thās, saṃprasāraṇa, reduplication, iṭ by the krādi restriction.)

Grammar pages 556–557, noted briefly: upasthe — ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; with a subanta as upapada, the affix ka by supi sthaḥ (सुपि स्थः, Pā. sū. 3-2-4); kit and vowel-initial, so the root's ā drops by āto lopa iṭi ca (आतो लोप इटि च, Pā. sū. 6-4-64); stha; compounded with the gati upa; locative singular; the first member end-acute by marudvṛdhādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam (Pā. sū. 6-2-106-2); jāgṛviḥ — jāgṛ nidrākṣaye, adādi; kvin by jṝśṝstṝjāgṛbhyaḥ kvin (U. sū. 4-54); vi remains; kit, so no guṇa of the root; nit, so initial acute by ñnityādir nityam (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); bodhi — budha avagamane, bhvādi; loṭ 2nd singular, hi; the śap due by kartari śap (Pā. sū. 3-1-68) is dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; hi, though apit, is optionally pit in the Veda by vā chandasi (Pā. sū. 3-4-84 [as printed; for 3-4-88]), so the light penult takes guṇa; not being ṅit, hi becomes dhi by aṅitaś ca (Pā. sū. 6-4-103); the root-final is dropped as a Vedic form; bodhi; the tiṅanta is unaccented; pramatiḥ — mana jñāne; ktin by striyāṃ ktin (Pā. sū. 3-3-94); the nasal drops before the kit suffix by anudāttopadeśa… (Pā. sū. 6-4-37); mati; prakṛṣṭā matir yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi, the first member's accent by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. sū. 6-2-1); ūpiṣe — ḍuvap bījatantusantāne, bhvādi; ḍu dropped by ādir ñiṭuḍavaḥ (Pā. sū. 1-3-5); liṭ in the present sense by chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. sū. 3-4-6); se for thās by thāsaḥ se (Pā. sū. 3-4-80); saṃprasāraṇa of v by vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti (Pā. sū. 6-1-15) and pūrvarūpa by saṃprasāraṇāc ca; asaṃyogāl liṭ kit: liṭ is not pit here, so its substitute is kit; doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, savarṇadīrgha; the iṭ prohibition of kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusru… (Pā. sū. 7-2-13) is restricted to kryādi roots (krādiniyama), so although vap is aniṭ, the val-initial se takes iṭ; ṣatva; ūpiṣe. ॥ ९ ॥

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अनवद्य (anavadya) — [O Agni] free of faults | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | देवेषु (deveṣu) — among all the gods | जागृविः (jāgṛviḥ) — [being] ever-wakeful | त्वम् (tvam) — you | पित्रोः (pitroḥ) — of Heaven and Earth in the form of mother and father | उपस्थे (upasthe) — in the neighbourhood [being] | नः (naḥ) — to us | तनूकृत् (tanūkṛt) — [in] the form of a son, the preserver of our bodies | बोधि (bodhi) — wake [us] | कारवे (kārave) — [to] the sacrificer who does works | प्रमतिः च (pramatiḥ ca) — [be] endowed with favourable intent | कल्याण (kalyāṇa) — O Agni in the form of auspiciousness | त्वम् (tvam) — you | विश्वं वसु (viśvaṃ vasu) — all wealth | ओपिषे (opiṣe) — you sow [you give, favouring the sacrificer].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O faultless Agni! You, ever wakeful among all the gods, dwell near Heaven and Earth, your mother and father; awake us, as a son who keeps our bodies; and be favourably disposed to the sacrificer who does the rites. O Agni in the form of auspiciousness! You pour out all wealth, favouring the sacrificer.

॥ English Translation ॥

O stainless Agni, you are a watchful god among gods living in the proximity of your parents (Heaven and Earth) and bestowing upon us progeny, awake us ; be well disposed to the offerer of the oblation ; you grant us all that is good and auspicious.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अनवद्य (anavadya) — doṣarahita: faultless; being worthy of praise, [the source adds] "irreproachable". पित्रोः (pitroḥ) — [the sense:] 'of the father and mother', that is, 'in the neighbourhood of Heaven and Earth'. जागृविः (jāgṛviḥ) — jāgarūka: wakeful, 'vigilant, watchful' [English as printed]. तनूकृत् (tanūkṛt) — putrādisaṃtatīnām — one who makes [produces] the progeny, children and so on; that is, one who gives. ऊपिषे (ūpiṣe) — ḍuvap bījatantusantāne: you sow; that is, you favour.

त्वम॑ग्ने प्रम॑ति॒स्त्वं पि॒तासि॑ न॒स्त्वं व॑य॒स्कृत्तव॑ जा॒म॑यो व॒यम् । [accent ?] सं त्वा॒ रायः॑ श॒तिनः॒ सं स॑ह॒स्रिणः॑ सु॒वीरं॑ यन्ति व्रत॒पाम॑दाभ्य ॥ १० ॥

tvám agne prámatis tváṃ pitā́si nas tváṃ vayaskṛ́t táva jāmayo vayám | [accent ?] saṃ tvā rā́yaḥ śatínaḥ sáṃ sahasríṇaḥ suvī́raṃ yanti vratapā́m adābhya || 10 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । अग्ने । प्रऽमतिः । त्वम् । पिता । असि । नः । त्वम् । वयःऽकृत् । तव । जामयः । वयम् । सम् । त्वा । रायः । शतिनः । सम् । सहस्रिणः । सुऽवीरम् । यन्ति । व्रतऽपाम् । अदाभ्य ॥ १० ॥ tvam | agne | pra-matiḥ | tvam | pitā | asi | naḥ | tvam | vayaḥ-kṛt | tava | jāmayaḥ | vayam | sam | tvā | rāyaḥ | śatinaḥ | sam | sahasriṇaḥ | su-vīram | yanti | vrata-pām | adābhya || 10 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अग्ने त्वं प्रमतिरस्मदनुग्रहरूपप्रकृष्टमतियुक्तोऽसि । तथा त्वं नोऽस्माकं पिता पालकोऽसि । तथा त्वं वयस्कृत् । आयुष्यप्रदोऽसि । वयमनुष्ठातारस्तव जामयो बन्धवः । हे अदाभ्य केनाप्यहिंसनीयाग्ने सुवीरं शोभनपुरुषयुक्तं व्रतपां कर्मणः पालकं त्वां शतिनः शतसंख्यायुक्ता रायो धनानि सं यन्ति । सम्यक् प्राप्नुवन्ति । तथा सहस्रिणः सहस्रसंख्याका रायः सं यन्ति ॥ सुवीरम् । बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते वीरवीर्यौ च । पा. ६-२-१२० इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । अदाभ्य । दभेः प्रकृत्यन्तरमस्तीति केचिदाहुः । दभेश्चेति वक्तव्यम् । पा. ३-१-१२४-३ । इति ण्यत् ॥ ३३ ॥ he agne tvaṃ pramatir asmadanugraharūpaprakṛṣṭamatiyukto 'si | tathā tvaṃ no 'smākaṃ pitā pālako 'si | tathā tvaṃ vayaskṛt | āyuṣyaprado 'si | vayam anuṣṭhātāras tava jāmayo bandhavaḥ | he adābhya kenāpy ahiṃsanīyāgne suvīraṃ śobhanapuruṣayuktaṃ vratapāṃ karmaṇaḥ pālakaṃ tvāṃ śatinaḥ śatasaṃkhyāyuktā rāyo dhanāni saṃ yanti | samyak prāpnuvanti | tathā sahasriṇaḥ sahasrasaṃkhyākā rāyaḥ saṃ yanti || suvīram | bahuvrīhau nañsubhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatve prāpte vīravīryau ca | pā. 6-2-120 ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | adābhya | dabheḥ prakṛtyantaram astīti kecid āhuḥ | dabheś ceti vaktavyam | pā. 3-1-124-3 | iti ṇyat || 33 || "O Agni! You are pramati — endowed with favourable intent [for us]; you are our father, our protector; you are vayaskṛt — the giver of life. We, the performers [of the rites], are your kinsmen [jāmayaḥ]. O unharmable (adābhya) Agni, who protect the rite and are accompanied by good men [suvīram]: hundred-fold riches [śatinaḥ] come together to you, and thousand-fold riches (sahasriṇaḥ) come together [to you]. [Suvīram: in a bahuvrīhi with su the second member would be end-acute, but by the rule vīravīryau ca it is initial-acute on the second member (P. 6-2-120); adābhya: some say dabh has another stem; ṇyat [P. 3-1-124-3].]"

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | प्रमतिः (pramatiḥ) — [one who is] favourably disposed (in regard to us) | त्वम् (tvam) — you | नः (naḥ) — to us | पिता (pitā) — [as] protector | असि (asi) — you are | त्वम् (tvam) — you | वयस्कृत् (vayaskṛt) — the giver of life | वयम् (vayam) — we (who perform sacrifices) | तव (tava) — your | जामयः (jāmayaḥ) — kinsmen | अदाभ्य (adābhya) — O Agni who cannot be injured by anyone | सुवीरम् (suvīram) — [one] endowed with excellent men | व्रतपाम् (vratapām) — the protector of the rites | त्वा (tvā) — you | शतिनः (śatinaḥ) — [riches] numbering a hundred | रायः (rāyaḥ) — riches | सं यन्ति (saṃ yanti) — reach completely | सहस्रिणः (sahasriṇaḥ) — [riches] numbering a thousand | सं (saṃ) — completely [reach].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You are favourably disposed to us; you are our protector and the giver of life. We who perform sacrifices are your kinsmen. O Agni, who cannot be injured by anyone, accompanied by excellent men and protector of the rites! Riches in hundreds and thousands reach you completely: you have abundant wealth.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, you are well disposed to us, you are our protector, the giver of life to us ; we are your kinsmen ; uninjurable Agni, hundred and thousand of riches belong to you ; you are the supporter of pious acts and you are surrounded by good men. The Special Topics and grammar of Rik 10 continue on p. 559 and after, PDF 574 — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 10 — continued (everything up to the English Translation is given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 559–561

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ प्रमतिः (pramatiḥ) — asmadanugraharūpaprakṛṣṭamatiyuktaḥ: one who has good intention for our favour — endowed with a good mind [in order] to favour us. पिता (pitā) — pālakaḥ: protector. वयस्कृत् (vayaskṛt) — āyuṣyapradaḥ: giver of life; 'giver of long life' [English as printed]. जामयः (jāmayaḥ) — bandhavaḥ: kinsmen. व्रतपाम् (vratapām) — karmaṇaḥ pālakam: protector of rites such as sacrifices. अदाभ्य (adābhya) — kenāpy ahiṃsanīyāgne: one that cannot be harmed by anyone.

Grammar page 559, noted briefly: vayaskṛt — vayaḥ karotīti vayaskṛt; kvip ca after kṛñ; as the suffix is pit, tuk by P. 6-1-71 hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk; the s of vayas becomes ru and visarga; the visarga before k becomes s by ataḥ kṛkamikaṃsakumbhapātrakuśākarṇiṣv anavyayasya (अतः कृकमिकंसकुम्भपात्रकुशाकर्णीष्वनव्ययस्य, P. 8-3-46); gatikāra [kāraka]-first compound kṛt-final accent; suvīram — śobhanāḥ vīrāḥ yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; the first-member accent would apply, but by nañsubhyām (नञ्सुभ्याम्, P. 6-2-172) the end-acute of the second member prevails since it is su-first; this is set aside by vīravīryau ca (वीरवीर्यौ च, P. 6-2-120), by which, since vīra is the second member, the second member is initial-acute; adābhya — in the vocative, luk by eṅhrasvāt sambuddheḥ (एङ्ह्रस्वात्सम्बुद्धेः); some say that dabhi has a different stem; if one takes the root dambh, vṛddhi and the loss of the penult cannot arise — that is their view; by the saying dabheś ceti vaktavyam (P. 3-1-124-3) the affix ṇyat arises; ya remains; being ṇit, vṛddhi of the root's penult by ata upadhāyāḥ: dābhya; with na [a] negation, adābhya; vocative singular; all-low by āmantritasya ca (P. 8-1-19). Numerals as printed.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya transcribed in full from the print; म. २-३-३२-१ as printed, the grammar on p. 562 prints 2-3-62-1: हे अग्ने त्वां प्रथमं पुरा देवा आयव आयोर्मनुष्यरूपस्य नहुषस्यैतन्नामकराजविशेषस्यायुं मनुष्यरूपं विश्पतिं सेनापतिमकृण्वन् । कृतवन्तः । तथा मनुष्यस्य मनोरिळामेतन्नामधेयां पुत्रीं शासनीं धर्मोपदेशकर्त्रीमकृण्वन् । कृतवन्तः । तथा च तैत्तिरीयैराम्नायते । इडा वै मानवी यज्ञानुकाशिन्यासीत् । ममकादेशः । संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्य इति वृद्ध्यभावः । व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ he agne tvāṃ prathamaṃ purā devā āyava āyormanuṣyarūpasya nahuṣasyaitannāmakarājaviśeṣasyāyuṃ manuṣyarūpaṃ viśpatiṃ senāpatimakṛṇvan | kṛtavantaḥ | tathā manuṣyasya manoriḷāmetannāmadheyāṃ putrīṃ śāsanīṃ dharmopadeśakartrīmakṛṇvan | kṛtavantaḥ | tathā ca taittirīyairāmnāyate | iḍā vai mānavī yajñānukāśinyāsīt | tai. brā. 1-1-4-4 | iti | vājasaneyino 'pyevamāmananti | prayājānuyājānāṃ madhye māmavakalpaya mayā sarvānavāpsyasi kāmāniti sā manumanvaśāditi yat śāditi | yadvā yadā mamakasya madīyasya hiraṇyastūpasaṃbandhino yaḥ pitāṅgirāstasya pituḥ putro jāyate | tadānīṃ he agne tvameva putrarūpa āsīriti śeṣaḥ ‖ āyave | ṣaṣṭhyarthe caturthī vaktavyā | ma. 2-3-32-1 | iti caturthī | nahuṣasya | ṇaha bandhane | nahikalihanyatirlasibhya uṣac | u. 4-75 | vṛṣāditvādādyudāttatvam | viśpatim | parādiśchandasi bahulamityuttarapadādyudāttatvam | manuṣasya | manornidityuṣac | nittvādādyudāttatvam | śāsanīṃ śiṣyate 'nayeti śāsanī | karaṇādhikaraṇayośceti lyuṭ | ṭiḍḍhāṇañityādinā | pā. 4-1-15 | ṅīp | litsvareṇādyudāttatvam | mamakasya | mamedamityarthe tasyedam | pā. 4-3-120 | ityaṇi tavakamamakāvekavacane | pā. 4-3-3 | ityasmacchabdasya mamakādeśaḥ | saṃjñāpūrvako vidhiranitya iti vṛddhyabhāvaḥ | vyatyayenādyudāttatvam ‖ "O Agni! You first, in former times, the gods made āyu (a mortal-form, 'a living one') for Āyu — [that is,] for the king named Nahuṣa, a particular king of human kind — the viśpati (lord of the clans; 'general of the army'). And they made [Manu's] daughter Iḷā, so named, the śāsanī — the instructress in dharma. So in the Taittirīya [Brāhmaṇa]: 'Iḍā, daughter of Manu, was the teacher who followed on the sacrifice' (Tai. Br. 1-1-4-4); the Vājasaneyins too declare: 'Between the fore-offerings and after-offerings place me; by me you will obtain all desires' — so she instructed Manu: that is why [she is the instructress] (yat śādit). Or [alternatively]: when to my [seer's] father, that is, the Aṅgiras who is the father connected with Hiraṇyastūpa, a son is born — then, O Agni, you yourself were [in] the form of a son: this is supplied."

Grammar pages 562–563, noted briefly: āyave — by the Vārttika ṣaṣṭhyarthe caturthī vaktavyā (षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी वक्तव्या, Pā. sū. 2-3-62-1) the dative stands for a genitive; āyu in the dative; nahuṣasya — ṇaha bandhane, with the Uṇādi uṣac by nahikalihanyatirlasibhya uṣac (नहिकलिहन्यतिर्लसिभ्य उषच्, U. sū. 4-515); ṇ → n by ṇo naḥ; genitive singular; the cit suffix would give end-acute, but the word being in the vṛṣādi group, initial acute by P. 6-1-203 vṛṣādīnāṃ ca (वृषादीनां च); viśpatim — viśāṃ patiḥ; the accent: by P. 6-2-199 parādiś chandasi bahulam (परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलम्), the initial syllable of the second member is acute; manuṣasya — mana jñāne; by [Uṇ.] maner nit the affix uṣac, which is nit; manuṣa ends with a; initial acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam; śāsanīm — śāsu anuśiṣṭau; 'that by which one is instructed' is śāsanī; lyuṭ in the sense of instrument and locus by P. 3-3-117 karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca (करणाधिकरणयोश्च); yu → ana by P. 7-1-1; the feminine by P. 4-1-15 ṭiḍḍhāṇañ… (टिड्ढाणञ्…) in ṅīp; as the suffix is lit-accented, initial acute by liti; ṅīp is pit, so unaccented; mamakasya — mama idam ('this is mine') in the sense of tasyedam P. 4-3-120 with aṇ; the substitute mamaka for asmad in the singular by P. 4-3-3 tavakamamakāv ekavacane (तवकममकावेकवचने); since a rule beginning with a technical term is not constant (saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ), no vṛddhi; a lost by yasyeti ca; the initial acute is by vyatyaya; jāyate — janī prādurbhāve, divādi; jā for jan by P. 7-3-79 jñājanor jā; śyan by P. 3-1-69; e for ṭ of laṭ ātmanepada by P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; yat being correlated, the lowering of the verb is barred by yadvṛttānnityam; śyan is nit, so initial acute. Numerals as printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वाम् (tvām) — you | प्रथमम् (prathamam) — first | देवाः (devāḥ) — the gods | आयवे (āyave) — for the man [Āyu] | नहुषस्य (nahuṣasya) — of the king named Nahuṣa | आयुम् (āyum) — in human form | विश्पतिम् (viśpatim) — as the general of the army | अकृण्वन् (akṛṇvan) — made | मनुषस्य (manuṣasya) — of Manu | इळाम् (iḷām) — [the daughter] called Iḷā | शासनीम् (śāsanīm) — as the instructress of dharma | अकृण्वन् (akṛṇvan) — made | यत् (yat) — when | मम (mama) — my | पितुः (pituḥ) — [to the] father [in the form of the Aṅgiras seer] | पुत्रः (putraḥ) — as a son | जायते (jāyate) — [you] are born (then you were in the form of a son).

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! The gods first made you, in the form of a man, the general of the army of the king named Nahuṣa, and made Iḷā, Manu's daughter, the instructress of dharma. And you are born as a son to my father, who is in the form of the Aṅgiras seer.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, the gods formerly made you the living general of the King Nahusha ; they made Ila, the daughter of Manu, the instructress in performing the sacrifices, when you were born as the son of my father.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ नहुषस्य (nahuṣasya) — Nahuṣa was a king. This king's name occurs in the Ṛgveda in: > अरट्ने अक्षे नहुषे सुकृत्वनि सुकृत्तराय सुक्रतुः । Ṛg-Saṃhitā 8-46-27 [?] [as the source gives it; last digit 7 or 6] — aratne akṣe nahuṣe sukṛtvani sukṛttarāya sukratuḥ | > अग्निं विश ईळते मानुषीर्या अग्निं मनुषो नुहुषो [sic] वि जाताः । Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-80-6 [as the source gives it] — agniṃ viśa īḷate mānuṣīr yā agniṃ manuṣo nuhuṣo [sic] vi jātāḥ | > यया दासान्यार्याणि वृत्रा करो वज्रिन्सुतुका नाहुषाणि । Ṛg-Saṃhitā 6-22-10 [as the source gives it] — yayā dāsāny āryāṇi vṛtrā karo vajrin sutukā nāhuṣāṇi | > यदिन्द्र नाहुषीष्वाँ ओजो नृम्णं च कृष्टिषु । Ṛg-Saṃhitā 6-46-7 [as the source gives it] — yad indra nāhuṣīṣvām̐ ojo nṛmṇaṃ ca kṛṣṭiṣu | My tentative glosses: aratne akṣe nahuṣe sukṛtvani sukṛttarāya sukratuḥ — "to the generous, the nahuṣa of good works, for the very good; the skilful"; agniṃ viśa īḷate mānuṣīr yāḥ — "the human clans who praise Agni"; yad indra nāhuṣīṣv ā ojo nṛmṇaṃ ca kṛṣṭiṣu — "O Indra, the strength and manhood that [you place] among the peoples of Nahuṣa" — all tentative. In these [riks] we get no direct details of the king; he may perhaps be guessed, from the examples [the nāhuṣa and nāhuṣī] as king of a people called Nāhuṣa. From some riks one may also guess that this king was a king of the region on the banks of the river Sindhu or Sarasvatī. इळामकृण्वन्मनुषस्य शासनीम् (iḷām akṛṇvan manuṣasya śāsanīm) — [on Iḷā as instructress]: in explaining that the daughter of Manu, the goddess Iḷā, was made the instructress, the commentator quotes two Śruti sentences: > इडा वै मानवी यज्ञानुकाशिन्यासीत् ॥ Taittirīya-Brāhmaṇa 1-1-4-4 [as the source gives it] — iḍā vai mānavī yajñānukāśinyāsīt — "Iḍā, indeed, Manu's daughter, was the one who followed the sacrifice [as its teacher]." Mine, tentative. > प्रयाजानूयाजानां मध्ये मामवकल्पय मया सर्वानवाप्स्यसि कामानिति सा मनुमन्वशादिति यत् शादिति ॥ — prayājānūyājānāṃ madhye mām avakalpaya mayā sarvān avāpsyasi kāmān iti sā manum anvaśād iti yat śād iti — "Between the fore-offerings and after-offerings place me: by me you will obtain all desires": thus she instructed Manu — [this is the sense of] śāsanī. पितुः यत् पुत्रः ममकस्य जायते (pituḥ yat putraḥ mamakasya jāyate) — the seer says: "You, Agni, are born as a son to my father, who belongs to the line of the Aṅgiras seer." The relationship between Agni and the Aṅgiras seer we have already taken up in the first rik of this sūkta.

Rik 12 pp. 564–566

त्वं नो॑ अग्ने तव॑ देव पा॒युभि॑र्म॒घोनो॑ रक्ष त॒न्व॑श्च वन्द्य । [accent ?] त्रा॒ता तो॒कस्य॒ तन॑ये॒ गवा॑म॒स्यनि॑मेषं॒ रक्ष॑माण॒स्तव॑ व्र॒ते ॥ १२ ॥

tváṃ no agne táva deva pāyúbhir maghóno rakṣa tanvaśca vandya | [accent ?] trātā́ tokásya tánaye gávām asyánimeṣaṃ rákṣamāṇas táva vraté || 12 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha: त्वम् । नः । अग्ने । तव । देव । पायुऽभिः । मघोनः । रक्ष । तन्वः । च । वन्द्य । त्राता । तोकस्य । तनये । गवाम् । असि । अनिऽमेषम् । रक्षमाणः । तव । व्रते ॥ १२ ॥ tvam | naḥ | agne | tava | deva | pāyu-bhiḥ | maghonaḥ | rakṣa | tanvaḥ | ca | vandya | trātā | tokasya | tanaye | gavām | asi | ani-meṣam | rakṣamāṇaḥ | tava | vrate || 12 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya transcribed in full from the print; its last line is cut off in the better scan and read from the old scan, PDF 579: हे वन्द्य वन्दनीयाग्ने देव त्वं तव पायुभिस्त्वदीयैः पालनैर्मघोनो धनयुक्तान्नोऽस्मान् रक्ष । तथा तन्वश्च । तनूः पुत्रदेहानपि रक्ष । तोकस्यास्मदीयस्य पुत्रस्य यस्तनयोऽस्मत्पौत्रादिस्तव व्रते त्वदीये कर्मण्यनिमेषं निरन्तरं रक्षमाणः सावधानो वर्तते तस्मिन्या गावः सन्ति तासां गवां त्राता रक्षकोऽसि । ईदृशस्य तवास्मद्रक्षणे किमु वक्तव्यमित्यर्थः ॥ मघोनः । शसि श्वयुवमघोनामतद्धिते । पा. ६-४-१३३ । इति संप्रसारणम् । तन्वः । सुपां सुपो भवन्तीति शसो जसादेशः । पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घस्य दीर्घाज्जसि चेति प्रतिषेधः । उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यण इति स्वरितत्वम् । शसि ह्युदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्त्युदात्तत्वं स्यात् ॥ he vandya vandanīyāgne deva tvaṃ tava pāyubhistvadīyaiḥ pālanairmaghono dhanayuktānno 'smān rakṣa | tathā tanvaśca | tanūḥ putradehānapi rakṣa | tokasyāsmadīyasya putrasya yastanayo 'smatpautrādistava vrate tvadīye karmaṇyanimeṣaṃ nirantaraṃ rakṣamāṇaḥ sāvadhāno vartate tasminyā gāvaḥ santi tāsāṃ gavāṃ trātā rakṣako 'si | īdṛśasya tavāsmadrakṣaṇe kimu vaktavyamityarthaḥ ‖ maghonaḥ | śasi śvayuvamaghonāmataddhite | pā. 6-4-133 | iti saṃprasāraṇam | tanvaḥ | supāṃ supo bhavantīti śaso jasādeśaḥ | pūrvasavarṇadīrghasya dīrghājjasi ceti pratiṣedhaḥ | udāttasvaritayoryaṇa iti svaritatvam | śasi hyudāttayaṇo halpūrvāditi vibhaktyudāttatvaṃ syāt ‖ "O adorable (vandya) Agni, O god! With your protections [pāyubhiḥ] protect us who are wealthy (maghonaḥ), and also our bodies [tanvaḥ] — [that is,] our sons' bodies. You are the protector of the cows of him who, for the work connected with you, remains attentive without a wink [animeṣam] — who is the son (tanaya) of our son [tokasya] — our grandson and so on — the cows that are with him, of those cows you are the protector: such as you are, what need is there to speak of your protecting us? — this is the sense."

Grammar pages 565–566, noted briefly: maghonaḥ — the stem maghavan; with śas (printed "tṛtīyā bahuvacana") following, saṃprasāraṇa by śvayuvamaghonām ataddhite (श्वयुवमघोनामतद्धिते, Pā. sū. 6-4-133): by ig yaṇaḥ saṃprasāraṇam the v becomes u; magha + u + an + as; by saṃprasāraṇāc ca the following vowel takes the prior form; guṇa by ād guṇaḥ; s → ru and visarga: maghonaḥ; tanvaḥ — tanū + śas: by the saying supāṃ supo bhavanti (सुपां सुपो भवन्ति) jas replaces śas; the lengthening by prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ (प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः) is barred by dīrghāj jasi ca (दीर्घाज्जसि च, Pā. sū. 6-1-105); yaṇ by iko yaṇ aci: tanvaḥ; since yaṇ comes in the place of the udātta, svarita by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ; with śas the form would be the same but the accent different: by udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt (Pā. sū. 6-1-174) the case-ending would be acute, so the change of case is by vyatyaya; rakṣa — rakṣa pālane, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular; hi for sip is dropped (luk) by ato heḥ; after a non-verb, the finite-verb lowering; vandya — vandayituṃ yogyaḥ: vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ, ṇyat by ṛhalor ṇyat (ऋहलोर्ण्यत्); the root being idit, num: vandya; as a vocative, the lowering by āmantritasya ca. Numerals as printed; grammar ends ॥ १२ ॥.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वन्द्य (vandya) — [O Agni] worshipful | देव (deva) — O god, the soul of the deities | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | तव (tava) — your | पायुभिः (pāyubhiḥ) — with protections | मघोनः (maghonaḥ) — [who are] endowed with wealth | नः (naḥ) — us | रक्ष (rakṣa) — protect | तन्वः (tanvaḥ) — the bodies [of our sons] | (रक्ष) — protect | तव व्रते (tava vrate) — in the rite connected with you | अनिमेषम् (animeṣam) — without a wink, continuously | रक्षमाणः (rakṣamāṇaḥ) — [being] attentive | तोकस्य तनये (tokasya tanaye) — [of him who] is in the grandson of [our] son | गवाम् (gavām) — of the cows | त्राता (trātā) — protector | असि (asi) — you are.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni — worshipful, soul of the gods! Protect us, who are endowed with wealth, with your protections; and also protect the bodies of our sons and grandsons. You are the protector of our cows and of our attentive [sacrificers] who without wink perform the rites in your honour.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni who deserves to be praised, preserve us and also our sons and grandsons ; you are the protector of our cattle and you keep your worshippers in the performance of your rite.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ तोकस्य तनये (tokasya tanaye) — tokasya means 'of the son'; tokasya tanaye means 'of the son's son, the grandson, or great-grandson' (in the sense of 'of the son's descendants'). अनिमेषम् (animeṣam) — nirantaram: always. तव व्रते (tava vrate) — 'in the performance of rites that are yours [sambandhavāda]'; that is, in the sacrificial rites that are done with your help.

For the sacrificer who is to sacrifice [yajyave] you are the protector [pāyuḥ]. Being near (antaraḥ), you are kindled (idhyase) — four-eyed (caturakṣaḥ) — endowed with flames that serve as eyes in all four directions — for the sacrifice that is without hindrance [aniṣaṅgāya: not [to be] attached to by the Rākṣasas]. The sacrificer who has offered oblations to you — the harmless one and the nourisher (dhāyase) — you take, with your mind, [the sense of] his praise-mantra, as it is that of a praiser [kīreḥ cit] alone: [vanoṣi — yācasi, you ask for (it)]."

Grammar pages 569–570, noted briefly: yajyave — yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, bhvādi; by yajimaniśundhi- (U. sū. 3-300) the affix yu: yajyu; in the dative singular, the stem being ghi, guṇa by gher ṅiti and av: yajyave; pāyuḥ — pā rakṣaṇe, adādi; uṇ by kṛvāpājimisvadi- (U. sū. 1-1); pā + u: the root ending in ā, the augment yuk by āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ (Pā. sū. 7-3-33): pāyuḥ; end-acute by the suffix accent; aniṣaṅgāya — ṣañja saṅge; with ni, ghañ: niṣaṅga; na vidyate niṣaṅgaḥ asya: aniṣaṅgaḥ, a bahuvrīhi; dative singular; end-acute of the second member by nañsubhyām (Pā. sū. 6-2-172); caturakṣaḥ — catvāri akṣīṇi jvālārūpāṇi yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; by bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac (Pā. sū. 5-4-113) the samāsānta ṣac after akṣi; ṣac being cit, end-acute by citaḥ; idhyase — ñi indhī dīptau, passive laṭ; yak by sārvadhātuke yak; before yak, the loss of n by aniditāṃ hala…; se for thās: idhyase; the finite-verb lowering; dhāyase — ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; asun by vahihādhāñbhyaś chandasi (U. sū. 4-660); by vaser ṇit the ṇit carries over, so, the root ending in ā, yuk by āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ: dhāyas; dative singular dhāyase; initial acute, the suffix being nit; kīreḥ — kṛta saṃśabdane; in the causative sense ṇic by hetumati ca; by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ the ṇic-form is a root; ending in a vowel, the affix i by aca iḥ (U. sū. 4-578; middle digit 7, possibly 2); ṇi dropped by ṇer aniṭi; the root-final t dropped as Vedic; ṛ → i by ṝta id dhātoḥ, with r by uraṇ raparaḥ: ir, the penult lengthened: kīri; genitive singular kīreḥ; end-acute by the suffix accent; mantram — matri guptaparibhāṣaṇe; being idit, num; in the pacādi group, ac by the nandigraha[-pacādi] sūtra: mantra; end-acute by citaḥ would arise, but being in the vṛṣādi group, initial acute by vṛṣādīnāṃ ca (Pā. sū. 6-1-203); vanoṣi — vanu yācane, tanādi, laṭ 2nd singular sip; the vikaraṇa u by tanādikṛñbhya uḥ (Pā. sū. 3-1-79); guṇa of u before sip; ṣatva of the s of sip by ādeśapratyayayoḥ; by the suffix's initial acute vanoṣi is middle-acute. Numerals as printed; grammar ends ॥ १३ ॥.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | यज्यवे (yajyave) — [of] the sacrificer | पायुः (pāyuḥ) — the protector | अन्तरः (antaraḥ) — very near | अनिषङ्गाय (aniṣaṅgāya) — [by your protection] for the rite going on without hindrance | चतुरक्षः (caturakṣaḥ) — [in all four directions] with flames [shining] in the form of four eyes | इध्यसे (idhyase) — you shine | अवृकाय (avṛkāya) — [for you,] harmless | धायसे (dhāyase) — [for you,] the benefactor | रातहव्यः (rātahavyaḥ) — [who] has offered oblations | यः (yaḥ) — which sacrificer | कीरेश्चित् (kīreś cit) — [as of your] praiser | मन्त्रम् (mantram) — the praise in the form of a mantra | मनसा (manasā) — in your mind | वनोषि (vanoṣi) — you cherish.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You are the protector of the sacrificer, and being close to him you shine, by your protection, in all four directions with flames in the form of four eyes, for the sacrifice that goes on without hindrance. You, the harmless and the benefactor, receive in your mind with regard the praise-mantra of the sacrificer who offers oblations to you.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, you are four-eyed and shine with brightness (or blaze) as the protector of the worshipper ; you are at hand to support the praiser in the uninterrupted rite ; you cherish in your mind the prayer of your adorer who offers oblations to you, the harmless and the benevolent.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अनिषङ्गाय (aniṣaṅgāya) — ṣañja saṅge: na vidyate niṣaṅgo 'syeti: that which is free of hindrance — a rite that goes on without any obstruction. चतुरक्षः (caturakṣaḥ) — catvāry akṣīṇi jvālārūpāṇi yasyāsau caturakṣaḥ: 'one who has four eyes'; 'eyes' here means the directions: the sacrificial altar shines, facing the four directions; that is the idea. रातहव्यः (rātahavyaḥ) — dattahavyaḥ: one who has offered oblations. अवृकाय (avṛkāya) — ahiṃsakāya: harmless, free of violence. कीरेश्चित् (kīreś cit) — kṛ̥ta saṃśabdane; stotur eva: of the praiser.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे अग्ने त्वमुरुशंसाय बहुभिः स्तोतव्याय वाघते ऋत्विजे तदुपकारार्थं स्पार्हं स्पृहणीयं परममुत्तमं यद्रेक्णो धनमस्ति तद्धनं वनोषि । अनुष्ठाता लभतामिति कामयसे । तथा त्वमाध्रस्य चित् सर्वतो धारणीयस्य पोषणीयस्य दुर्बलस्य यजमानस्यापि प्रमतिः प्रकृष्टबुद्धियुक्तः पिता पालक इत्यभिज्ञैरुच्यसे । तथा विदुष्टरोऽतिशयेनाभिज्ञस्त्वं पाकं शिशुम् । पोतः पाकोऽर्भको डिम्भः । अम. २-५-३८ । इत्यभिधानात् । यास्कोऽप्येवमाह । पाकः पक्तव्यो भवति । नि. ३-१२ । तथाविधं यजमानं प्र शास्सि । प्रकर्षेणानुशिष्टं करोषि । तथा दिशः प्राच्यादिकाः प्र शास्सि । त्वदीयशासनाभावेऽनुष्ठातॄणां विभ्रमः स्यात् । तथा च श्रूयते । देवा वै देवयजनमध्यवसाय दिशो न प्राजानन् । तै. सं. ६-१-५-१ । इति । स भ्रमो दक्षिणादिग्गतोऽग्निना निवर्तते । तदपि तत्रैवाम्नातम् । पथ्यां स्वस्तिमयजन् प्राचीमेव तया दिशं प्राजानन्नग्निना दक्षिणेति । ऐतरेयिणापि तथैवाम्नातम् । अथो एतं वरमवृणीत मय्येव प्राचीं दिशं प्रजानाथाग्निना दक्षिणाम् । ऐ. ब्रा. १-७ । इति ॥ उरुशंसाय । शंसु स्तुतौ । शस्यत इति शंसः । कर्मणि घञ् । ञित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन स एव शिष्यते । स्पार्हम् । स्पृहासंबन्धि । तस्येदमित्यण् । रेक्णः । रिचिर् विरेचने । रिचेर्धने । उ. ४-१९८ । इत्यसुन् । चकारान्नुडागमः । चजोः कु घिण्ण्यतोः । पा. ७-३-५२ । इति कुत्वम् । आध्रस्य । ध्रै तृप्तौ । आदेच उपदेशेऽशितीत्यात्त्वम् । आतश्चोपसर्गे । पा. ३-१-१३६ । इति कप्रत्ययः । शास्सि । शासु अनुशिष्टौ । अदादित्वाच्छपो लुक् । सिपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः । पाकं च प्रशास्सि दिशश्च प्रशास्सीत्यत्र चार्थो गम्यते । अतश्चादिलोपे विभाषेति प्रथमा तिङ्विभक्तिर्न निहन्यते । विदुष्टरः । विद्वच्छब्दात्तरप्ययस्मयादीनि छन्दसि । पा. cakārānnuḍāgamaḥ | cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ | pā. 7-3-52 | iti kutvam | ādhrasya | dhrai tṛptau | ādeca upadeśe 'śitītyāttvam | ātaścopasarge | pā. 3-1-136 | iti kapratyayaḥ | śāssi | śāsu anuśiṣṭau | adāditvācchapo luk | sipaḥ pittvādanudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ | pākaṃ ca praśāssi diśaśca praśāssītyatra cārtho gamyate | ataścādilope vibhāṣeti prathamā tiṅvibhaktirna nihanyate | viduṣṭaraḥ | vidvacchabdāttarapyayasmayādīni chandasi | pā. 1-4-20 | iti bhasaṃjñāyāṃ vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇamiti saṃprasāraṇaṃ parapūrvatvam | śāsivasīti ṣatvam | tarapaḥ pittvādanudāttatve vasoḥ svareṇokāra udāttaḥ ‖ "O Agni! For the Ṛtvij (vāghate) who is to be praised by many (uruśaṃsāya), for his benefit, you cherish [vanoṣi, 'desire'] the wealth that is desirable (spārham) and the best — [wanting that] the performer may get it. And you are spoken of by the knowledgeable as the 'father' (pitā), the protector — pramati, one of excellent understanding — even of the sacrificer who is [weak and] to be sustained from all sides (ādhrasya cit). Likewise you, the most knowing (viduṣṭaraḥ), instruct (pra śāssi) the child [pākam] — [the sacrificer] who is 'to be cooked' [paktavyaḥ] — and also instruct the directions, east and the rest. Without your guidance the performers would be bewildered. So it is heard [in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, 6-1-5-1]: 'The gods, setting out to the sacrificial ground, did not know the directions' — that bewilderment is removed from the south and other directions by Agni. That, too, is told there: 'They performed the pathyā svasti; they knew the eastern direction; then by Agni the southern.' The Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa too says so: 'Then he chose this boon: "In me alone shall they know the east, then by Agni the south"' (Ai. Br. 1-7)."

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | उरुशंसाय (uruśaṃsāya) — [for him] praised by many | वाघते (vāghate) — for the priest | स्पार्हम् (spārham) — desirable | परमम् (paramam) — excellent | यत् रेक्णः (yat rekṇaḥ) — whatever wealth | तत् (tat) — that wealth | वनोषि (vanoṣi) — you wish [that the performer of the sacrifice may obtain] | आध्रस्य चित् (ādhrasya cit) — even for the weak sacrificer [fit to be protected] | प्रमतिः (pramatiḥ) — [one] of favourable intent | पिता (pitā) — [and] protector [you are] | उच्यसे (ucyase) — [by the wise] you are called | विदुष्टरः (viduṣṭaraḥ) — [you,] very wise | पाकम् (pākam) — the sacrificer who knows nothing, like a child | प्र शास्सि (pra śāssi) — you make wise by instruction | दिशः (diśaḥ) — the directions east and so on | प्र (śāssi) — you point out [explain].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You wish the desirable and excellent wealth for the priest who is praised by many, that the performer of the sacrifice may obtain it. Even for a weak sacrificer who is fit for protection, the wise say that you are of favourable intent and his protector. You, most wise, make the sacrificer who knows nothing, like a child, wise by your instruction; and you point out to him the directions east and the rest in a way that suits him.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, you desire that excellent wealth which is required for the priest ; you are called protector of the worshipper who ever needs protection ; you are all-wise, instructs [sic] the disciple and teaches the ignorant, the four points of the horizon.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ स्पार्हम् (spārham) — spṛhaṇīyam: that which is desired by all; that which everyone wants. रेक्णः (rekṇaḥ) — dhanam: since the word rekṇas is read among the twenty-eight names of wealth such as maghaṃ rekṇaḥ, rekṇaḥ means wealth (Ni. 3-9). आध्रस्य (ādhrasya) — dhrai tṛptau: [for] the weak sacrificer who is without protection. पिता (pitā) — pālakaḥ: protector. पाकम् (pākam) — śiśum: one who knows nothing, like a child. विदुष्टरः (viduṣṭaraḥ) — atiśayena vidvān; atiśayenābhijñaḥ: very wise. दिशः (diśaḥ) — the directions, east and the others. When [they] perform a sacrifice, the gods did not know the eastern and other directions: so, in many places in the Veda it is said that [they] learned the southern direction through Agni. The commentator has cited these Śruti sentences here [in the bhāṣya].

Grammar pages 573–574, noted briefly: uruśaṃsāya — śaṃsu stutau; śasyata iti śaṃsaḥ, ghañ in the sense of the object: śaṃsa; ghañ being ñit, initial acute by ñnityādir nityam (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); compounded with uru, which has the gati designation, the kṛt-final second member keeps its own accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; dative singular; spārham — spṛhāyā idam: aṇ by tasyedam; the ā dropped by yasyeti ca; initial vṛddhi by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ: spārham; rekṇaḥ — ricir virecane, irit; asun by ricer dhane ghicca (U. sū. 4-638); hence ghit-treatment, and by the ca the augment nuṭ; before asun guṇa of the light penult; in recnas the c → k by cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ (Pā. sū. 7-3-52); with k intervening, n → ṇ by the aṭkupv-… sūtra: rekṇaḥ; ādhrasya — dhrai tṛptau with the prefix āṅ; by ād eca upadeśe 'śiti (Pā. sū. 6-1-45) a root ending in a diphthong in the upadeśa takes ā when no śit follows; then, ending in ā, ka by ātaś copasarge (Pā. sū. 3-1-136); ādhrā + a: ā dropped by āto lopa iṭi ca: ādhra; genitive singular; śāssi — śāsu anuśiṣṭau, adādi; laṭ 2nd singular; luk of śap by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ: śāssi; [the ending] being unaccented, the root accent obtained by dhātoḥ remains; since the construction pākaṃ ca praśāssi, diśaś ca praśāssi shows the sense of ca, the lowering is barred by cādilope vibhāṣā (Pā. sū. 8-1-63); viduṣṭaraḥ — vidvas; tarap in the sense of excess by dvivacanavibhaja-…; by ayasmayādīni chandasi (Pā. sū. 1-4-20) the bha-designation; so by vasoḥ samprasāraṇam (Pā. sū. 6-4-131) saṃprasāraṇa of the v of vidvas; pūrvarūpa by saṃprasāraṇāc ca; in viduṣ + tara, though the [s] belongs to the stem, ṣatva by śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca (Pā. sū. 8-3-60): viduṣṭaraḥ; tarap being pit is unaccented, and the accent of vasu being satiśiṣṭa, the u is acute. Numerals as printed; grammar ends ॥ १४ ॥.
