Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya transcribed in full from the print; ॥ ३४ ॥ closes Varga 34: हे अग्ने त्वं प्रयतदक्षिणं येन यजमानेन ऋत्विग्भ्यो दक्षिणा दत्ता तादृशं नरं पुरुषं यजमानं विश्वतः सर्वतः परि पासि । सम्यक् पालयसि । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । स्यूतं निश्छिद्रत्वेन सूचीभिः सम्यक् निष्पादितं वर्मेव । यथा कवचं युद्धे पालयति तद्वत् । स्वादुक्षद्मा स्वाद्वन्नो वसतौ निवासभूते स्वगृहे स्योनकृत् अतिथीनां सुखकारी यो यजमानो जीवयाजं जीवयजनसहितं यज्ञं यद्वा जीवनिष्पाद्यं यजते अनुतिष्ठति स यजमानो दिवः स्वर्गस्योपमा दृष्टान्तो भवति । यथा स्वर्गोऽनुष्ठातॄन्सुखयति तथा त्वमप्यृत्विगादीनित्यर्थः ॥ स्यूतम् । षिवु तन्तुसंताने । निष्ठेति क्तः । यस्य विभाषेतीट्प्रतिषेधः । छ्वोः शूडनुनासिके च । पा. ६-४-१९ । इति वकारस्योडादेशः । स्वादून्क्षदतीति स्वादुक्षद्मा । क्षदतिरत्तिकर्मा । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति मनिन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । बहुव्रीहौ तु व्यत्ययेन । जीवयाजम् । जीवा ऋत्विज इज्यन्ते दक्षिणाभिः पूज्यन्तेऽत्रेत्यधिकरणे घञ् । कुत्वाभावश्छान्दसः । यद्वा । जीवैः पशुभिर्याजनं जीवयाजः । याजयतेर्घञ् । णेरनिटीति णिलोपस्याचः परस्मिन्निति स्थानिवद्भावाच्चजोः कु घिण्ण्यतोरिति कुत्वाभावः । थाथादिस्वरेणोत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । सोपमा । सोऽचि लोपे चेत्पादपूरणमिति संहितायां सोर्लोपः । दिवः । ऊडिदमिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ ३४ ॥ he agne tvaṃ prayatadakṣiṇaṃ yena yajamānena ṛtvigbhyo dakṣiṇā dattā tādṛśaṃ naraṃ puruṣaṃ yajamānaṃ viśvataḥ sarvataḥ pari pāsi | samyak pālayasi | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | syūtaṃ niśchidratvena sūcībhiḥ samyak niṣpāditaṃ varmeva | yathā kavacaṃ yuddhe pālayati tadvat | svādukṣadmā svādvanno vasatau nivāsabhūte svagṛhe syonakṛt atithīnāṃ sukhakārī yo yajamāno jīvayājaṃ jīvayajanasahitaṃ yajñaṃ yadvā jīvaniṣpādyaṃ yajate anutiṣṭhati sa yajamāno divaḥ svargasyopamā dṛṣṭānto bhavati | yathā svargo 'nuṣṭhātṝnsukhayati tathā tvamapyṛtvigādīnityarthaḥ ‖ syūtam | ṣivu tantusaṃtāne | niṣṭheti ktaḥ | yasya vibhāṣetīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | chvoḥ śūḍanunāsike ca | pā. 6-4-19 | iti vakārasyoḍādeśaḥ | svādūnkṣadatīti svādukṣadmā | kṣadatirattikarmā | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti manin | nittvādādyudāttatve kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | bahuvrīhau tu vyatyayena | jīvayājam | jīvā ṛtvija ijyante dakṣiṇābhiḥ pūjyante 'tretyadhikaraṇe ghañ | kutvābhāvaśchāndasaḥ | yadvā | jīvaiḥ paśubhiryājanaṃ jīvayājaḥ | yājayaterghañ | ṇeraniṭīti ṇilopasyācaḥ parasminniti sthānivadbhāvāccajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoriti kutvābhāvaḥ | thāthādisvareṇottarapadāntodāttatvam | sopamā | so 'ci lope cetpādapūraṇamiti saṃhitāyāṃ sorlopaḥ | divaḥ | ūḍidamiti vibhakterudāttatvam ‖ 34 ‖ "O Agni! You protect on every side the man — the sacrificer — who has given sacrificial fees [dakṣiṇā] to the priests (prayatadakṣiṇam) — as [you protect] armour well sewn [syūtam] with needles, without a hole: as armour protects in battle, so. The sacrificer who, having sweet food (svādukṣadmā) in his dwelling (vasatau) and making guests comfortable (syonakṛt), performs the jīvayāja — a sacrifice with a living [animal], or one to be performed with living [offerings] — he becomes the likeness of heaven (divaḥ upamā): as heaven gives comfort to those who perform [the rites], so do you too [to] the priests and the others."

Grammar pages 576–577, noted briefly: syūtam — ṣivu tantusaṃtāne; kta in the sense of the object by niṣṭhā (Pā. sū. 3-2-102); iṭ barred by yasya vibhāṣā (Pā. sū. 7-2-15); ūṭ for the v by chvoḥ śūḍ anunāsike ca (च्छ्वोः शूडनुनासिके च); s for the root-initial ṣ; si + ū + ta: yaṇ: syūta; pāsi — pā rakṣaṇe, adādi, laṭ 2nd singular; the finite-verb lowering; svādukṣadmā — svādūn kṣadati iti; kṣada bhakṣaṇe; manin by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. sū. 3-2-75): svādukṣadman; before su, the penult lengthened by sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau; su dropped by halṅyābbhyaḥ; n dropped by nalopaḥ…: svādukṣadmā; manin being nit, kṣadman initial-acute by ñnityādir nityam; as a kāraka-first compound, the kṛt-final keeps its accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; if taken as a bahuvrīhi, the second member's initial acute must be explained by vyatyayo bahulam; jīvayājam — jīvāḥ ṛtvijaḥ ijyante dakṣiṇābhiḥ pūjyante atra; ghañ in the sense of locus after yaj; being ñit, vṛddhi of the root's a by ata upadhāyāḥ; the kutva due by cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ does not come, by vyatyayo bahulam: jīvayāja; or jīvaiḥ paśubhiḥ yājanam: ṇic after yaj, then ghañ, ṇi dropped by ṇer aniṭi; since by acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau that loss is sthānivat, cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ does not apply to the j; as a ghañ-final, by thāthaghañktāja-… (Pā. sū. 6-2-114 [as printed; for 6-2-144]) the compound is end-acute in the second member; sopamā — saḥ upamā; as it fills out the pāda, su is dropped by so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam (Pā. sū. 6-1-134); after the loss, guṇa: sopamā; divaḥ — by ūḍidampadādi- (Pā. sū. 6-1-171) the case-ending is acute. Numerals as printed; grammar ends ॥ १५ ॥.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | त्वम् (tvam) — you | प्रयतदक्षिणम् (prayatadakṣiṇam) — [the one who gives to the priests] abundantly fees | नरम् (naram) — the sacrificer | स्यूतम् (syūtam) — [well-sewn] without a hole | वर्मेव (varmeva) — as armour (in battle) | परि पासि (pari pāsi) — you protect well | स्वादुक्षद्मा (svādukṣadmā) — [who has] sweet food | वसतौ (vasatau) — [in his] house | स्योनकृत् (syonakṛt) — [by the honour of guests] comforting | यः (yaḥ) — which sacrificer | जीवयाजम् (jīvayājam) — a living-sacrifice [or a sacrifice that is accomplished with living beings] | यजते (yajate) — offers | सः (saḥ) — that sacrificer | दिवः (divaḥ) — to heaven | उपमा (upamā) — becomes equal (that is, goes to heaven).

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! You protect well the sacrificer who gives abundant fees to the priests, like armour well sewn without a hole protects the warrior in battle. The sacrificer who, having sweet food in his house, makes his guests comfortable by honouring them and so performs the jīvayāja — he becomes equal to heaven in conferring comfort.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, you protect the man who gives presents to the priest on every side like well-stiched [sic] armour ; the man who keeps good food in his dwellings and with them entertains his guest, and performs the animal sacrifice, approaches the heaven.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥

The first item, printed without a headword, concerns the mantra imām agne (Ṛk 16 of this sūkta). If an anāhitāgni — one who has not set up the sacred fires and does not perform sacrifices — himself takes part in a sacrifice performed by another, that is, performs the duty of an ṛtvij, he must offer an oblation in the fire with the Ṛk beginning imām agne: this is stated in the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra, in the section ṛtvijo vṛṇīta, in the sūtra (Āś. Gṛ. 1-23-23):

एवमनाहिताग्निर्गृह्य इमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो नः । evam anāhitāgnir gṛhya imām agne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo naḥ |

"So the anāhitāgni, [in] the domestic [fire], [with] imām agne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo naḥ ('Agni, forgive this fault of ours')."

प्रयतदक्षिणम् (prayatadakṣiṇam) — one who has given fees (dakṣiṇā) to the priests who took part in the sacrifice. वर्मेव स्यूतम् (varmeva syūtam) — as well-woven armour protects the body in battle; as when [one] is fighting in armour the enemy's arrows do not reach the body: so Agni protects the sacrificer's body like armour. स्वादुक्षद्मा (svādukṣadmā) — svādu means sweet, delicious; kṣadma means food (Ni. 3-9): sweet food, or provisions. स्योनकृत् (syonakṛt) — syona means comfort (Ni. 3-13): one who brings about comfort. जीवयाजम् (jīvayājam) — jīvayajanasahitaṃ yajñam: a sacrifice in which living creatures are offered: that is, a sacrifice in which animals are bound at the stake, offered to the gods, and an oblation made; hence the sense 'animal sacrifice'.

Rik 16 pp. 578–581

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

इ॒माम॑ग्ने श॒रणिं॑ मीमृषो न इ॒ममध्वा॑नं॒ यमगा॑म दू॒रात् । आ॒पिः पि॒ता प्रम॑तिः सो॒म्यानां॒ भृमि॑रस्यृषि॒कृन्मर्त्या॑नाम् ॥ १६ ॥

imā́m agne śaráṇiṃ mīmṛṣo na imám ádhvānaṃ yám ágāma dūrā́t | āpíḥ pitā́ prámatiḥ somyā́nāṃ bhṛ́mir asy ṛṣikṛ́n mártyānām || 16 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The strokes of इममध्वानं and यमगाम stand over ध्वा and गा in the print.

Pada-pāṭha: इमाम् । अग्ने । शरणिम् । मीमृषः । नः । इमम् । अध्वानम् । यम् । अगाम । दूरात् । आपिः । पिता । प्रऽमतिः । सोम्यानाम् । भृमिः । असि । ऋषिऽकृत् । मर्त्यानाम् ॥ १६ ॥ imām | agne | śaraṇim | mīmṛṣaḥ | naḥ | imam | adhvānam | yam | agāma | dūrāt | āpiḥ | pitā | pra-matiḥ | somyānām | bhṛmiḥ | asi | ṛṣi-kṛt | martyānām || 16 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : इमामग्न इत्यनयानाहिताग्निरार्त्विज्यं कृत्वा स्वाग्न्यावाहुतिं जुहुयात् । ऋत्विजो वृणीत इति खण्ड एवमनाहिताग्निर्गृह्य इमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो नः । आ. गृ. १-२३-२३ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥ हे अग्ने त्वं नोऽस्मत्संबन्धिनीमिमामिदानीं संपादितां शरणिं हिंसां व्रतलोपरूपां मीमृषः । क्षमस्व । तथा त्वदीयसेवामग्निहोत्रादिरूपां परित्यज्य दूराद्दूरदेशं यमिममध्वानमगाम वयं गतवन्तः । तमपि क्षमस्वेति शेषः । सोम्यानां सोमार्हाणामनुष्ठातॄणां मर्त्यानां त्वमाप्यादिगुणयुक्तोऽसि । आपिः प्रापणीयः पिता पालकः प्रमतिः प्रकृष्टमननयुक्तो भृमिर्भ्रामकः । कर्मनिर्वाहक इत्यर्थः । ऋषिकृत् दर्शनकारी । अनुजिघृक्षया प्रत्यक्षो भवसीत्यर्थः ॥ शरणिम् । शॄ हिंसायामित्यस्मादौणादिकोऽनिप्रत्ययः । मीमृषः । मृष तितिक्षायाम् । अस्माण्णौ चङि गुणे प्राप्ते नित्यं छन्दसि । पा. ७-४-८ । इत्युपधर्कारस्य ऋकारादेशः । णिलोपद्विर्भावहलादिशेषोरदत्त्वसन्वद्भावेत्त्वदीर्घत्वानि । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । अगाम । इण् गतौ । इणो गा लुङि । पा २-४-४५ । इति गादेशः । गातिस्थेति सिचो लुक् । अडागम उदात्तः । भृमिः । भ्रमु अनवस्थाने । भ्रमेः संप्रसारणं च । उ. ४-१२० । इतीन्प्रत्ययः । संप्रसारणे परपूर्वत्वम् । इगुपधात्किदित्यनुवृत्तेः कित्त्वाद्गुणप्रतिषेधः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ imām agna ity anayānāhitāgnir ārtvijyaṃ kṛtvā svāgnyāv āhutiṃ juhuyāt | ṛtvijo vṛṇīta iti khaṇḍa evam anāhitāgnir gṛhya imām agne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo naḥ | ā. gṛ. 1-23-23 | iti sūtritam || he agne tvaṃ no 'smatsaṃbandhinīm imām idānīṃ saṃpāditāṃ śaraṇiṃ hiṃsāṃ vratalopa-rūpāṃ mīmṛṣaḥ | kṣamasva | tathā tvadīyasevām agnihotrādirūpāṃ parityajya dūrād dūradeśaṃ yam imam adhvānam agāma vayaṃ gatavantaḥ | tam api kṣamasveti śeṣaḥ | somyānāṃ somārhāṇām anuṣṭhātṝṇāṃ martyānāṃ tvam āpyādiguṇayukto 'si | āpiḥ prāpaṇīyaḥ pitā pālakaḥ pramatiḥ prakṛṣṭamananayukto bhṛmir bhrāmakaḥ | karmanirvāhaka ity arthaḥ | ṛṣikṛt darśanakārī | anujighṛkṣayā pratyakṣo bhavasīty arthaḥ || śaraṇim | śṝ hiṃsāyām ity asmād auṇādiko 'nipratyayaḥ | mīmṛṣaḥ | mṛṣa titikṣāyām | asmāṇ ṇau caṅi guṇe prāpte nityaṃ chandasi | pā. 7-4-8 | ity upadharkārasya ṛkārādeśaḥ | ṇilopa-dvirbhāva-halādiśeṣa-uradattva-sanvadbhāva-ittva-dīrghatvāni | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | agāma | iṇ gatau | iṇo gā luṅi | pā 2-4-45 | iti gādeśaḥ | gātistheti sico luk | aḍāgama udāttaḥ | bhṛmiḥ | bhramu anavasthāne | bhrameḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca | u. 4-120 | itīnpratyayaḥ | saṃprasāraṇe parapūrvatvam | igupadhāt kid ity anuvṛtteḥ kittvād guṇapratiṣedhaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttatvam || "With this ṛk the anāhitāgni (one who has not set up the fires), having performed the priestly office, should offer an oblation in his own fire. In the section ṛtvijo vṛṇīta, it is laid down in the sūtra: 'thus the anāhitāgni, taking [the fire], [recites] imām agne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo naḥ' (Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra 1-23-23). O Agni! Forgive (mīmṛṣaḥ) this fault (śaraṇi) of ours that has now occurred — an injury, in the form of a lapse in our vows. Likewise forgive also this path (adhvānam) that we have gone, far (dūrāt) to a distant place, giving up your service in the form of the agnihotra and the like — so the sense is to be completed. To the mortals who are somya — fit for Soma, the performers [of the rites] — you are endowed with the qualities of āpi and the rest: āpi, the one to be attained; pitā, the protector; pramati, endowed with excellent thought; bhṛmi, the mover (bhrāmaka), that is, the one who carries out the rite; ṛṣikṛt, the one who makes [himself] seen — that is, out of the wish to favour [them] you become visible." Grammatical tail: śaraṇi with the Uṇādi affix ani from śṝ hiṃsāyām; mīmṛṣaḥ — mṛṣ titikṣāyām with ṇic and caṅ, the penultimate ṛ kept by nityaṃ chandasi (P. 7-4-8), with ṇi-elision, reduplication etc., and lowering by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ; agāma — iṇ gatau, gā by P. 2-4-45, sic dropped by gātisthā…, the augment aṭ acute; bhṛmiḥ — bhramu anavasthāne, in with saṃprasāraṇa (U. 4-120), no guṇa as kit, initial acute as nit.

Grammar pages 580–581, noted briefly from the print: śaraṇim — śṝ hiṃsāyām, kryādi; the Uṇādi affix ani; guṇa by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ; ṇ by aṭkupvāṅ-; initial acute of the affix; mīmṛṣaḥ — mṛṣa titikṣāyām; ṇic; sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; luṅ 2nd singular sip, itaś ca; ṇiśridrusrubhyaḥ kartari caṅ; guṇa by puganta-laghūpadhasya ca is barred by nityaṃ chandasi (Pā. sū. 7-4-8), the penult takes ṛ; ṇer aniṭi, caṅi (reduplication), halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, ur at, sanval laghuni caṅpare 'naglope (Pā. sū. 7-4-93), sanyataḥ (Pā. sū. 7-4-79), dīrgho laghoḥ; ru and visarga; tiṅṅatiṅaḥ; agāma — iṇ gatau, adādi; iṇo gā luṅi (Pā. sū. 2-4-45); mas, nityaṃ ṅitaḥ; cli luṅi, cleḥ sic; gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ (Pā. sū. 2-4-77) drops sic; the augment aṭ, initial acute; bhṛmiḥ — bhramu anavasthāne; bhrameḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca (U. sū. 4-560) gives in; saṃprasāraṇāc ca (pūrvarūpa); by the continuation of igupadhāt kit no guṇa of the light penult; ñnity ādir nityam, initial acute. Ends ॥ १६ ॥.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | नः (naḥ) — our (arisen from us) | इमां शरणिम् (imāṃ śaraṇim) — this fault [which is of the nature of a lapse in vows] | मीमृषः (mīmṛṣaḥ) — forgive | दूरात् (dūrāt) — [leaving the agnihotra and the like] far | यम् इमम् अध्वानम् (yam imam adhvānam) — which this path [on which we have strayed] | अगाम (agāma) — we have come [forgive that too] | सोम्यानाम् (somyānām) — [of those who] perform the sacrifices by pressing Soma | मर्त्यानाम् (martyānām) — [for] men, the sacrificers | आपिः (āpiḥ) — [you are] a relation | पिता (pitā) — protector | प्रमतिः (pramatiḥ) — [the one of] favourable intent | भृमिः (bhṛmiḥ) — [the one who] carries out the rite | ऋषिकृत् (ṛṣikṛt) — [the one who] gives vision | असि (asi) — you are.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! Forgive this fault of ours, arising from the lapse of our vows; and likewise forgive the path on which we have strayed, far away from the agnihotra and other rites. You are to the sacrificers who perform sacrifices with Soma a relation, a protector, a friend of favourable intent, the carrier-out of the rites, and the one who gives vision.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, forgive us our negligence, this path in which we have gone astray ; you will be sought as the protector and encourager of those who offer suitable libations ; you are the conductor of the sacrifice and make yourself visible to all men.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ शरणिम् (śaraṇim) — śṝ hiṃsāyām: injury [that is, the faults and omissions that we could have made in the sacrifice] — the defects, or the shortcomings [nyūnatā]. मीमृषः (mīmṛṣaḥ) — mṛṣa titikṣāyām: forgive. इमं अध्वानं यं अगाम दूरात् (imam adhvānam yam agāma dūrāt) — 'in carrying out this sacrifice, if we have transgressed the prescribed procedures, rules [the path], forgive that': that is the sense. आपिः पिता (āpiḥ pitā) — prāpaṇīyaḥ pālakaḥ: we have approached you, thinking you the protector; that is, 'we have come to you as the one who protects'. सोम्यानाम् (somyānām) — somārhāṇām anuṣṭhātṝṇām: the priests and others who drink Soma in the sacrifice. भृमिः (bhṛmiḥ) — bhramu anavasthāne; bhrāmakaḥ: [literally 'the wanderer'] — the one who carries out the sacrifice. ऋषिकृत् (ṛṣikṛt) — darśanakṛt samyag jñānakaraḥ: 'the maker of vision' — he who gives vision, that is, makes [things] visible; or gives knowledge.

Rik 17 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 581–588

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

म॒नु॒ष्व॑दग्ने अङ्गिर॒स्व॑दङ्गिरो ययाति॒वत्सद॑ने पूर्व॒वच्छु॑चे । अच्छ॑ या॒ह्या व॑हा॒ दैव्यं॒ जन॒मा सा॑दय ब॒र्हिषि॒ यक्षि॑ च प्रि॒यम् ॥ १७ ॥

manuṣvad agne aṅgirasvad aṅgiro yayātivát sádane pūrvavác chuce | áccha yāhy ā́ vahā dáivyaṃ jánam ā́ sādaya barhíṣi yákṣi ca priyám || 17 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. In वहा the print has the stroke over व and the bar under हा.

Pada-pāṭha: मनुष्वत् । अग्ने । अङ्गिरस्वत् । अङ्गिरः । ययातिऽवत् । सदने । पूर्वऽवत् । शुचे । अच्छ । याहि । आ । वह । दैव्यम् । जनम् । आ । सादय । बर्हिषि । यक्षि । च । प्रियम् ॥ १७ ॥ manuṣvat | agne | aṅgirasvat | aṅgiraḥ | yayāti-vat | sadane | pūrva-vat | śuce | accha | yāhi | ā | vaha | daivyam | janam | ā | sādaya | barhiṣi | yakṣi | ca | priyam || 17 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे शुचे शुद्धियुक्ताङ्गिरोऽङ्गनशील हविरादानाय तत्र तत्र गमनशीलाग्ने अच्छाभिमुख्येन सदने देवयजनदेशे याहि । गच्छ । तत्र चत्वारो दृष्टान्ताः । मनुष्वत् यथा मनुरनुष्ठानदेशे गच्छति । अङ्गिरस्वत् यथा चाङ्गिरा गच्छति । ययातिवत् यथा ययातिर्नाम राजा गच्छति । पूर्ववत् अन्ये च पूर्वपुरुषा यथा गच्छन्ति । यथा मन्वादयो यज्ञे गच्छन्ति तद्वत् । अथवा मन्वादीनां यज्ञे यथा त्वं गच्छसि तद्वत् । गत्वा च दैव्यं देवतासमूहरूपं जनमा वह । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यानय । आनीय च बर्हिष्यास्तीर्णे दर्भ आ सादय । तान्देवानुपवेशय । उपवेश्य च प्रियमभीष्टं हविर्यक्षि च । देहि ॥ मनुष्वत् । तेन तुल्यमिति प्रथमार्थे वा तत्र तस्येवेति षष्ठ्यर्थे वा वतिः । पा. ५-१-११५-११६ । अयस्मयादित्वेन भत्वाद्रुत्वाद्यभावः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । एवमङ्गिरस्वदित्यादिषु । वह । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घः । यक्षि । लोटि बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । सेर्ह्यपिच्चेति हेरभावश्छान्दसः । षत्वकत्वे ॥ he śuce śuddhiyuktāṅgiro 'ṅganaśīla havirādānāya tatra tatra gamanaśīlāgne acchābhimukhyena sadane devayajanadeśe yāhi | gaccha | tatra catvāro dṛṣṭāntāḥ | manuṣvat yathā manur anuṣṭhānadeśe gacchati | aṅgirasvat yathā cāṅgirā gacchati | yayātivat yathā yayātir nāma rājā gacchati | pūrvavat anye ca pūrvapuruṣā yathā gacchanti | yathā manvādayo yajñe gacchanti tadvat | athavā manvādīnāṃ yajñe yathā tvaṃ gacchasi tadvat | gatvā ca daivyaṃ devatāsamūharūpaṃ janam ā vaha | asmin karmaṇy ānaya | ānīya ca barhiṣy āstīrṇe darbha ā sādaya | tān devān upaveśaya | upaveśya ca priyam abhīṣṭaṃ havir yakṣi ca | dehi || manuṣvat | tena tulyam iti prathamārthe vā tatra tasyeveti ṣaṣṭhyarthe vā vatiḥ | pā. 5-1-115-116 | ayasmayāditvena bhatvād rutvādyabhāvaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | evam aṅgirasvad ityādiṣu | vaha | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaḥ | yakṣi | loṭi bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | serhy apic ceti her abhāvaś chāndasaḥ | ṣatvakatve || "O pure (śuce) Aṅgiras — one who goes about [aṅganaśīla] — O Agni who go here and there to take the oblations! Go (yāhi) to the sacrificial place (sadane), facing it (accha). There are four examples here: as Manu goes to the place of performance; as Aṅgiras goes; as the king named Yayāti goes; as other forefathers go (pūrvavat) — as Manu and the others go to the sacrifice, so; or, as you go to the sacrifices of Manu and the others, so. Having gone, bring (ā vaha) the host of the gods — daivyam janam — to this rite; having brought them, seat them (ā sādaya) on the spread grass (barhiṣi) — seat those gods; and, having seated them, give (yakṣi) the dear, desired oblation." Grammatical tail: manuṣvat — vati in the nominative sense 'equal to that' or the genitive sense 'as of that' (P. 5-1-115–116), no ru etc. as bha by the ayasmayādi list, affix accent, likewise aṅgirasvat etc.; vaha — lengthening in the Saṃhitā by dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ; yakṣi — śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi, hi not substituted (chāndasa), ṣ and k.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ शुचे (śuce) — [O Agni,] pure | अङ्गिरः (aṅgiraḥ) — [for taking the oblations] one who goes about in many places | अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | अच्छ (accha) — [to the sacrifice] facing | सदने (sadane) — to the place of the divine sacrifice | मनुष्वत् (manuṣvat) — like Manu | अङ्गिरस्वत् (aṅgirasvat) — like Aṅgiras | ययातिवत् (yayātivat) — like Yayāti | पूर्ववत् (pūrvavat) — like other forefathers, or [as you went] to the sacrifices of Manu and the others | याहि (yāhi) — go | दैव्यम् (daivyam) — the host of the gods | जनम् (janam) — people | आ वह (ā vaha) — bring (to this rite) | बर्हिषि (barhiṣi) — upon the spread darbha [grass] | आ सादय (ā sādaya) — seat [them] | प्रियम् (priyam) — [for them] the desired oblation | यक्षि च (yakṣi ca) — and offer.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O pure Agni, who go about in many places to take the oblations! Come, facing this rite, to the place of the divine sacrifice, as you went to the sacrifices of Manu, Aṅgiras, Yayāti and the other forefathers. Bring the host of the gods to this rite; seat them on the excellent darbha seats; and offer them the oblations that they desire. The English Translation, Special Topics and grammar of Rik 17 are on pp. 583–, PDF 598 — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 17 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya, Prati-padārtha and Bhāvārtha are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 583–584

Bhāvārtha, alternative (pp. 582–583; the print gives it after "Or"): O pure Agni, who go about to take the oblations! Come facing this sacrifice of ours, as [you went] to the sacrifices of Manu, Aṅgiras, Yayāti and the other forefathers. Having come, [bring] the hosts of the gods, seat them on the spread darbha seat called barhis-straṇa, and offer them the oblations that they like.

॥ English Translation ॥

Pure Agni, in the same way as you went to the sacrifices of Manu, Angiras, Yayati and other ancestors to receive the oblations, you bring hither the divine personages, seat them on the sacred grass and offer them sacrificial oblation.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ ययातिवत् (yayātivat) — Yayāti was a king. His name occurs in the Ṛgveda in this rik, and in > ययातेर्यो नहुषस्य बर्हिषि देवा आसते ते अधि ब्रुवन्तु नः ॥ Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-63-1 [as the source gives it] — yayater yo nahuṣasya barhiṣi devā āsate te adhi bruvantu naḥ || — Mine, tentative: "[They] who sit on the sacrificial grass of Yayāti, [son] of Nahuṣa — let those gods speak for us." and nowhere else [by the author's count]. From this example, Yayāti is said to be related to Nahuṣa or the Nahuṣa clan; this king can therefore be said to have been a king of the Nahuṣa people, or he may have been of the lineage of Nahuṣa. The kings named Nahuṣa and Yayāti spoken of in the Purāṇas and other works have no connection with the kings of those names spoken of in the Ṛgveda. दैव्यं जनम् (daivyaṃ janam) — devatāsaṃbandhiyād janaran: 'people connected with deities', that is, the gods.

Grammar pages 583–584, noted briefly: manuṣvat — the affix vati by P. 5-1-115 tena tulyaṃ kriyā ced vatiḥ (तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः), 'resembling in action', after the nominative [in the sense of 'equal action']; or, by P. 5-1-116 tatra tasyeva (तत्र तस्येव), the affix vati in the sense of the genitive; as the word is in the ayasmayādi list, by P. 1-4-20 ayasmayādīni chandasi it has the designation bha, hence pada-designation is lacking, so the s does not take ru and visarga; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: manuṣvat; by the suffix's initial acute, the a after the v is acute; aṅgirasvat, yayātivat and pūrvavat are the same — in the nominative or in the genitive sense, the affix vati applies, the process as before; vaha — vaha prāpaṇe, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi; śap by P. 3-1-68 kartari śap; hi dropped by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ; vaha; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-135 dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ; yakṣi — yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular sip; hi substitution is not applied by vyatyayo bahulam; śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; yaj + si: j → ṣ by P. 8-2-36 vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ (व्रश्चभ्रस्ज…षः); ṣ + s → k by P. 8-2-41 ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si (षढोः कः सि); the s after k → ṣ by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: yakṣi. Numerals as read.

Rik 18 (Triṣṭubh; last rik of the sūkta) pp. 584–587

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

ए॒तेना॑ग्ने॒ ब्रह्म॑णा वावृधस्व॒ शक्ती॑ वा॒ यत्ते॑ चकृ॒मा वि॒दा वा॑ । उ॒त प्र णे॑ष्य॒भि वस्यो॑ अ॒स्मान्त्सं नः॑ सृज सुम॒त्या वाज॑वत्या ॥ १८ ॥

eténāgne bráhmaṇā vāvṛdhasva śáktī vā yát te cakṛmā́ vidā́ vā | utá prá ṇeṣy abhí vásyo asmā́nt sáṃ naḥ sṛja sumatyā́ vā́javatyā || 18 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The print reads अस्मान्त्सं (was अस्मान्सं).

Pada-pāṭha: एतेन । अग्ने । ब्रह्मणा । ववृधस्व । शक्ती । वा । यत् । ते । चकृम । विदा । वा । उत । प्र । नेषि । अभि । वस्यः । अस्मान् । सम् । नः । सृज । सुऽमत्या । वाजऽवत्या ॥ १८ ॥ etena | agne | brahmaṇā | vavṛdhasva | śaktī | vā | yat | te | cakṛma | vidā | vā | uta | pra | neṣi | abhi | vasyaḥ | asmān | sam | naḥ | sṛja | su-matyā | vāja-vatyā || 18 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : साग्निचयने क्रतावुखासंभरणीयायामिष्टावग्नेर्ब्रह्मण्वतः पुरोनुवाक्यैतेनाग्न इत्येषा । दर्शपूर्णमासाभ्यामिष्ट्वेति खण्ड एतेनाग्ने ब्रह्मणा वावृधस्व ब्रह्म च ते जातवेदो नमश्च । आ. ४-१ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥ हे अग्ने एतेनास्मत्प्रयुक्तेन ब्रह्मणा मन्त्रेण ववृधस्व । अभिवृद्धो भव । शक्ती वा विदा वा अस्मदीयशक्त्या चास्मदीयज्ञानेन च ते तव यत्स्तोत्रं चकृम वयं कृतवन्तः । एतेन ब्रह्मणेति पूर्वत्रान्वयः । उतापि चास्माननुष्ठातॄन् वस्यो वसुमत्तरं रत्नलक्षणं श्रेयः प्र णेषि । प्रकर्षेण प्रापय । नोऽस्मान्वाजवत्या प्रभूतान्नयुक्तया सुमत्यानुष्ठानविषयया शोभनबुद्ध्या सं सृज । संयोजय ॥ ववृधस्व । वृधु वृद्धौ । लेट्यडागमः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । द्विर्भावहलादिशेषोरदत्वानि । अभ्यासस्य संहितायां दीर्घश्छान्दसः । शक्ती । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयायाः पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वम् । क्तिनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । विदा । सावेकाच इति तृतीयाया उदात्तत्वम् । नेषि । णीञ् प्रापणे । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । उपसर्गादसमास इति णत्वम् । सुमत्या । मन्क्तिन्नित्यादिनोत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं प्रथमाध्याये प्रपञ्चितम् । ऋग्वे. १-७-७ । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ ३५ ॥ sāgnicayane kratāv ukhāsaṃbharaṇīyāyām iṣṭāv agner brahmaṇvataḥ puronuvākyaitenāgna ity eṣā | darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭveti khaṇḍa etenāgne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva brahma ca te jātavedo namaś ca | ā. 4-1 | iti sūtritam || he agne etenāsmatprayuktena brahmaṇā mantreṇa vavṛdhasva | abhivṛddho bhava | śaktī vā vidā vā asmadīyaśaktyā cāsmadīyajñānena ca te tava yat stotraṃ cakṛma vayaṃ kṛtavantaḥ | etena brahmaṇeti pūrvatrānvayaḥ | utāpi cāsmān anuṣṭhātṝn vasyo vasumattaraṃ ratnalakṣaṇaṃ śreyaḥ pra ṇeṣi | prakarṣeṇa prāpaya | no 'smān vājavatyā prabhūtānnayuktayā sumatyānuṣṭhānaviṣayayā śobhanabuddhyā saṃ sṛja | saṃyojaya || vavṛdhasva | vṛdhu vṛddhau | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ śluḥ | dvirbhāva-halādiśeṣa-uradatvāni | abhyāsasya saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaś chāndasaḥ | śaktī | supāṃ suluk iti tṛtīyāyāḥ pūrvasavarṇadīrghatvam | ktino nittvād ādyudāttatvam | vidā | sāvekāca iti tṛtīyāyā udāttatvam | neṣi | ṇīñ prāpaṇe | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | upasargād asamāsa iti ṇatvam | sumatyā | mankitn nityādinottarapadāntodāttatvaṃ prathamādhyāye prapañcitam | ṛgve. 1-7-7 | udāttayaṇo halpūrvād iti vibhakter udāttatvam || 35 || "In the sāgnicayana sacrifice [the fire-altar-building rite], in the iṣṭi belonging to the bringing together of the ukhā [the fire-pot], this [ṛk] etenāgne is the puronuvākyā ('invitatory') for Agni brahmaṇvat; it is laid down in the sūtra, in the section darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭvā: 'etenāgne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva, brahma ca te jātavedo namaś ca' (Āś. 4-1). O Agni! Be strengthened (vavṛdhasva) by this brahman — the mantra we have used; become increased [in power]. The praise (stotra) of yours that we have made (cakṛma) according to our ability (śaktī) and our knowledge (vidā) — [it] is connected with the preceding 'by this brahman'. And lead (pra ṇeṣi) us, the performers, to the better good (vasyaḥ) — the 'more wealthy' welfare in the form of riches (ratna). Unite us (saṃ sṛja) with good intelligence (sumatyā) concerned with the rite, [and] rich in plentiful food (vājavatyā)." Grammatical tail: vavṛdhasva — vṛdhu vṛddhau, leṭ with aṭ, ślu for śap by bahulaṃ chandasi, reduplication etc., the reduplicate lengthened in the Saṃhitā (Vedic); śaktī — instrumental lengthened by supāṃ suluk…, initial acute as ktin is nit; vidā — the instrumental acute by sāvekācaḥ; neṣi — ṇīñ prāpaṇe, śap dropped, ṇ by upasargād asamāse…; sumatyā — end-acute of the second member by mankitn…, explained in the first adhyāya (Ṛgve. 1-7-7, as printed), the ending acute by udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt. Varga 35 ends.

Grammar pages 586–587, noted briefly from the print: vavṛdhasva — vṛdhu vṛddhau, bhvādi; leṭ 2nd singular thās; leṭo 'ḍāṭau gives aṭ; bahulaṃ chandasi: ślu in place of śap; ślau: reduplication; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; ur at: a for ṛ, with ra following, then dropped by halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; savābhyāṃ vāmau (Pā. sū. 3-4-91): se → sva; the reduplicate lengthened in the Saṃhitā (Vedic); being after a non-verb, the verb is unaccented; śaktī — instrumental singular, supāṃ suluk- (Pā. sū. 7-1-39) gives the lengthening; śakḷ śaktau with ktin; nit, so initial acute; vidā — vid with kvip; instrumental singular; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. sū. 6-1-168): the ending acute; neṣi — ṇīñ prāpaṇe, bhvādi, laṭ, sip; śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; n for the initial ṇ; guṇa (sārvadhātuka); ṣatva by ādeśapratyayayoḥ; pra + neṣi: upasargād asamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya (Pā. sū. 8-4-14) gives praṇeṣi; sumatyā — śobhanā cāsau matiś ca sumatiḥ; the end-acute of the second member, from man-ktin-, explained at length in the first adhyāya (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-7, as printed); yaṇ in the instrumental; udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt: the ending acute. Ends ॥ १८ ॥.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अग्ने (agne) — O Agni | शक्ती वा (śaktī vā) — according to [our] ability | विदा वा (vidā vā) — according to [our] knowledge | ते (te) — your | यत् (yat) — which [praise] | चकृम (cakṛma) — we have made | एतेन ब्रह्मणा (etena brahmaṇā) — by this mantra [which we used] | वावृधस्व (vāvṛdhasva) — be increased [in strength] | उत (uta) — and | अस्मान् (asmān) — us [who perform the rites] | वस्यः (vasyaḥ) — with good fortune | प्रणेषि (praṇeṣi) — unite | नः (naḥ) — us | वाजवत्या (vājavatyā) — with abundant food | सुमत्या (sumatyā) — with good intelligence [concerned with the performance of the rite] | संसृज (saṃsṛja) — unite well.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Agni! Be increased in strength by this mantra, which we have used, and by the praise of you that we have made according to our ability and our knowledge. Favour us, who perform the rites, with good fortune; give us plentiful food, and unite us well with the good understanding that is fit for the performance of the rite.

॥ English Translation ॥

Agni, allow yourself to be pleased with this hymn, which we have composed according to our ability, according to our knowledge ; therefore lead us towards the highest good and endow as [sic] with right understanding together with abundant food.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ In the fire-piling rite called agnicayana, in the iṣṭi called ukhāsaṃbharaṇa, when oblations are offered to Agni 'of the Brahmaṇvat name', this rik is to be used as the purono-vākyā [invitatory verse]: this is laid down in the section darśapūrṇamāsābhyām iṣṭvā of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra etenāgne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 1-31-18) brahma ca te jātavedo namaś ca (Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-4-7, as printed). ब्रह्मणा (brahmaṇā) — stotreṇa: by praise. वावृधस्व (vāvṛdhasva) — vṛdhu vṛddhau: abhivṛddho bhava: be pleased; be satisfied. शक्ती विदा (śaktī vidā) — as far as our strength goes, as far as our knowledge goes. सं नः सृज सुमत्या वाजवत्या (saṃ naḥ sṛja sumatyā vājavatyā) — 'unite us with good understanding and with food and other requisites': that is, 'give us these and favour us'.

Close of Sūkta 31 : the Kannada colophon reads mūvattoṃdane sūktavu samāptavāgide — "The thirty-first sūkta is ended." The bhāṣya of Rik 18 ends with ॥ ३५ ॥, the end of Varga 35; the grammar ends ॥ १८ ॥.

॥ ಮೂವತ್ತೆರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 32 — "indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam" ("The Thirty-second Sūkta"; second sūkta of the Seventh Anuvāka)

(Printed pp. 587 lower half–. The introductory note is on p. 587, the Kannada Anuvāda and heading block on p. 588; Rik 1 begins on p. 588 foot and continues on p. 589.)

॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note; printed p. 587) re-read from the print

इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीति पञ्चदशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तम् । आङ्गिरसो हिरण्यस्तूप ऋषिः । त्रिष्टुप् छन्दः । इन्द्रो देवता । इन्द्रस्य पञ्चोनेत्यनुक्रमणिका । अग्निष्टोमे माध्यंदिने सवने निष्केवल्यशस्त्र इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीति निविद्धानीयं सूक्तम् । निष्केवल्यस्येति खण्ड इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीत्येतस्मिन्नैन्द्रीं निविदं दध्यात् । आ. ५-१५ । इति ॥ विषुवत्यपि तस्मिन् शस्त्र एतद्विनियुक्तम् । विषुवान्दिवा कीर्त्य इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । इन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणीत्येतस्मिन्नैन्द्रीं निविदं शस्त्वा । आ. ८-६ । इति ॥ महाव्रते निष्केवल्येऽप्येतदेव विनियुक्तम् । राथन्तरो दक्षिणः पक्ष इति खण्डे चतस्रः सतीः षड् बृहतीः करोतीन्द्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्र वोचम् । ऐ. ब्रा. ५-२-१ ।

indrasya nu vīryāṇīti pañcadaśarcaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūktam | āṅgiraso hiraṇyastūpa ṛṣiḥ | triṣṭup chandaḥ | indro devatā | indrasya pañconetyanukramaṇikā | agniṣṭome mādhyaṃdine savane niṣkevalyaśastra indrasya nu vīryāṇīti nividdhānīyaṃ sūktam | niṣkevalyasyeti khaṇḍa indrasya nu vīryāṇītyetasminnaindrīṃ nividaṃ dadhyāt | ā. 5-15 | iti ‖ viṣuvatyapi tasmin śastra etadviniyuktam | viṣuvāndivā kīrtya iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | indrasya nu vīryāṇītyetasminnaindrīṃ nividaṃ śastvā | ā. 8-6 | iti ‖ mahāvrate niṣkevalye 'pyetadeva viniyuktam | rāthantaro dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣa iti khaṇḍe catasraḥ satīḥ ṣaḍ bṛhatīḥ karotīndrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam | ai. brā. 5-2-1 |

Translation: "Indrasya nu vīryāṇi is the second sūkta [of this anuvāka]; it has fifteen riks; the seer is Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa; the metre is Triṣṭubh; the deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇikā: 'indrasya — five less [than twenty]'. In the Agniṣṭoma, at the midday pressing, in the Niṣkevalya-śastra, the sūkta indrasya nu vīryāṇi is the nividdhānīya. In the section niṣkevalyasya it is laid down: 'in this [sūkta] indrasya nu vīryāṇi one should place the Indra-nivid' (Āśvalāyana 5-15). In the Viṣuvat too, in that [Niṣkevalya] śastra, it is used: in the section viṣuvān divā kīrtyaḥ it is laid down: 'having recited the Indra-nivid in this [sūkta] indrasya nu vīryāṇi' (Āś. 8-6). In the Mahāvrata also, in the Niṣkevalya, this same [sūkta] is used: in the section rāthantaro dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ ['the Rāthantara is the right wing']: 'he makes four satī and six bṛhatī [verses] — indrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam' (ऐ. ब्रा. ५-२-१ (ai. brā. 5-2-1) as printed; the Kannada gives Ai. Ā. 5-2-1)."

॥ Anuvāda (Kannada) ॥ Indrasya nu vīryāṇi is the second sūkta in the seventh anuvāka. It has fifteen riks. Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa is the seer of this sūkta; the metre is Triṣṭubh; Indra is the deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said indrasya pañconā [fifteen]. In the Agniṣṭoma and other sacrifices, at the midday pressing, in reciting the mantras of the Niṣkevalya-śastra, the sūkta indrasya nu vīryāṇi is to be recited as a nividdhānīya sūkta: this is explained in the section niṣkevalyasya of Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra indrasya nu vīryāṇīty etasminn aindrīṃ nividaṃ dadhyāt (Āś. 5-15). In the Viṣuvat too, this sūkta is used for reciting the mantras of that śastra; that matter is shown in the section viṣuvān vā kīrtyaḥ of Āśvalāyana's Śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra indrasya nu vīryāṇīty etasminn aindrīṃ nividaṃ śaṃstvā (Āś. 8-6). In the Mahāvrata also the sūkta is used for reciting the Niṣkevalya-śastra mantras. This matter is described in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka, in the section rāthantaro dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ, in the sentence catasraḥ satīḥ ṣaḍbṛhatīḥ karotīndrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocam (Ai. Ā. 5-2-1).

Heading block (p. 588): Maṇḍala 1; Anuvāka 7; Sūkta 32. Aṣṭaka 1; Adhyāya 2; Varga 36, 37, 38. Number of riks: 15. Ṛṣi: Hiraṇyastūpa Āṅgirasa. Devatā: Indra. Chandas: Triṣṭubh.

Rik 1 pp. 588–592

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

इन्द्र॑स्य॒ नु वी॒र्या॑णि॒ प्र वो॑चं॒ यानि॑ च॒कार॑ प्रथ॒मानि॑ व॒ज्री । अह॒न्नहि॒मन्व॒पस्त॑तर्द॒ प्र व॒क्षणा॑ अभिन॒त्पर्व॑तानाम् ॥ १ ॥

índrasya nú vīryāṇi prá vocaṃ yā́ni cakā́ra prathamā́ni vajrī́ | ahann áhim ánv apás tatarda prá vakṣáṇā abhinat párvatānām || 1 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 1: one bar only, under थ, as printed.

Pada-pāṭha: इन्द्रस्य । नु । वीर्याणि । प्र । वोचम् । यानि । चकार । प्रथमानि । वज्री । अहन् । अहिम् । अनु । अपः । ततर्द । प्र । वक्षणाः । अभिनत् । पर्वतानाम् ॥ १ ॥ indrasya | nu | vīryāṇi | pra | vocam | yāni | cakāra | prathamāni | vajrī | ahan | ahim | anu | apaḥ | tatarda | pra | vakṣaṇāḥ | abhinat | parvatānām || 1 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : वज्री वज्रयुक्त इन्द्रः प्रथमानि पूर्वसिद्धानि मुख्यानि वा यानि वीर्याणि पराक्रमयुक्तानि कर्माणि चकार तस्येन्द्रस्य तानि वीर्याणि नु क्षिप्रं प्रब्रवीमि । कानि वीर्याणीति तदुच्यते । अहिं मेघमहन् हतवान् । तदेतदेकं वीर्यम् । अनु पश्चादपो जलानि ततर्द हिंसितवान् । भूमौ पातितवानित्यर्थः । इदं द्वितीयं वीर्यम् । पर्वतानां संबन्धिनीर्वक्षणाः प्रवहणशीला नदीः प्राभिनत् । भिन्नवान् । कूलद्वयकर्षणेन प्रवाहितवानित्यर्थः । इदं तृतीयं वीर्यम् । एवमुत्तरत्रापि द्रष्टव्यम् ॥ वीर्याणि । शूर वीर विक्रान्तौ । ण्यन्तादचो यदिति यत् । णेरनिटीति णिलोपः । तित्स्वरितमिति स्वरितत्वम् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं न भवति । आद्युदात्तत्वे हि सुशब्देन बहुव्रीहावाद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसीत्यनेनैवोत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वस्य सिद्धत्वाद्वीरवीर्यौ चेति पुनस्तद्विधानमनर्थकं स्यात् । अतोऽवगम्यते यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं वीरशब्दे न प्रवर्तत इति । अतः परिशेषात्तित्स्वरितमिति प्रत्ययस्य स्वरितत्वमेव । वोचम् । अस्यतिवक्तिख्यातिभ्योऽङिति च्लेरङादेशः । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः । चकार । णलि लित्स्वरेण प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । अहन् । लङीतश्चेतीकारलोपे हल्ङ्याब्भ्य इति तकारलोपः । अहिम् । आङ्पूर्वाद्धन्तेराङि श्रिहनिभ्यां ह्रस्वश्च । उ. ४-१३७ । इतीप्रत्ययः । आङो ह्रस्वत्वं च । चशब्देन वेञो डित् समाने ख्यश्चोदात्त इति डित्त्वं पूर्वपदोदात्तत्वं चानुकृष्यते । ततष्टिलोपे पूर्वपदस्योदात्तत्वम् । ततर्द । उतृदिर् हिंसानादरयोः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । वक्षणाः । वक्ष रोषे । क्रुधमण्डार्थेभ्यश्च । पा. ३-२-१५१ । इति युच् । चित्स्वरं बाधित्वा व्यत्ययेन प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥ grammatical tail transcribed from the print, p. 589; not explained vajrī vajrayukta indraḥ prathamāni pūrvasiddhāni mukhyāni vā yāni vīryāṇi parākramayuktāni karmāṇi cakāra tasyendrasya tāni vīryāṇi nu kṣipraṃ prabravīmi | kāni vīryāṇīti tad ucyate | ahiṃ megham ahan hatavān | tad etad ekaṃ vīryam | anu paścād apo jalāni tatarda hiṃsitavān | bhūmau pātitavān ity arthaḥ | idaṃ dvitīyaṃ vīryam | parvatānāṃ saṃbandhinīr vakṣaṇāḥ pravahaṇaśīlā nadīḥ prābhinat | bhinnavān | kūladvayakarṣaṇena pravāhitavān ity arthaḥ | idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vīryam | evam uttaratrāpi draṣṭavyam || vīryāṇi | śūra vīra vikrāntau | ṇyantādaco yaditi yat | ṇeraniṭīti ṇilopaḥ | titsvaritamiti svaritatvam | yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvaṃ na bhavati | ādyudāttatve hi suśabdena bahuvrīhāvādyudāttaṃ dvyacchandasītyanenaivottarapadādyudāttatvasya siddhatvādvīravīryau ceti punastadvidhānamanarthakaṃ syāt | ato 'vagamyate yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvaṃ vīraśabde na pravartata iti | ataḥ pariśeṣāttitsvaritamiti pratyayasya svaritatvameva | vocam | asyativaktikhyātibhyo 'ṅiti cleraṅādeśaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasyamāṅyoge 'pītyaḍabhāvaḥ | cakāra | ṇali litsvareṇa pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvam | yadvṛttayogādanighātaḥ | ahan | laṅītaścetīkāralope halṅyābbhya iti takāralopaḥ | ahim | āṅpūrvāddhanterāṅi śrihanibhyāṃ hrasvaśca | u. 4-137 | itīpratyayaḥ | āṅo hrasvatvaṃ ca | caśabdena veño ḍit samāne khyaścodātta iti ḍittvaṃ pūrvapadodāttatvaṃ cānukṛṣyate | tataṣṭilope pūrvapadasyodāttatvam | tatarda | utṛdir hiṃsānādarayoḥ | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | vakṣaṇāḥ | vakṣa roṣe | krudhamaṇḍārthebhyaśca | pā. 3-2-151 | iti yuc | citsvaraṃ bādhitvā vyatyayena pratyayasvaraḥ ‖ "I proclaim at once the heroic deeds (vīryāṇi) of Indra — the thunderbolt-bearer (vajrī) — which he did first (prathamāni, 'foremost', or 'previously accomplished'). Which exploits? It is said: ahim ahan — he struck the ahi, the cloud: this is one exploit. Then (anu) he cleft [tatarda] the waters (apaḥ) — made them fall upon the earth: this is the second. He split open the vakṣaṇāḥ — the streams related to the mountains, flowing rivers — so that, by drawing [cutting] the two banks, he made them flow: this is the third exploit. So it is to be understood in what follows also."

Grammar pages 591–592, noted briefly: the Kannada restates the bhāṣya's tail, giving sūtras by name: vīryāṇi — śūra vīra vikrāntau, ṇic, yat by 'aco yat', ṇic dropped by 'ṇer aniṭi', svarita by 'tit svaritam'; 'yato 'nāvaḥ' does not apply, since otherwise 'vīravīryau ca' would be superfluous after 'ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi' (bahuvrīhi śobhanaṃ vīryaṃ yasya saḥ); vocam — vaca paribhāṣaṇe or brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci, luṅ, vac-substitution, mip, am by 'tas-thas-tha-', cli → aṅ, um augment, guṇa, no aṭ by 'bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi'; cakāra — ḍukṛñ karaṇe, liṭ, ṇal by 'parasmaipadānām', vṛddhi, accent by 'liti', no nighāta (yad-clause); ahan — hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi, laṅ, 'itaś ca', luk of śap by 'adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ', t dropped by 'halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt-', aṭ, pāda-initial so no nighāta, initial acute; ahim — 'āṅi śrihanibhyāṃ hrasvaś ca' (U. sū. 4-577), the ca bringing 'veño ḍit' and 'samāne khyaś codāttaḥ', ṭi-lopa, the prior member acute; tatarda — utṛdir hiṃsānādarayoḥ, liṭ, nighāta by 'tiṅṅatiṅaḥ'; vakṣaṇāḥ — vakṣa roṣe, yuc by 'krudhamaṇḍārthebhyaś ca' (Pā. sū. 3-2-151), 'yuvor anākau', ṇatva, the cit accent set aside by 'vyatyayo bahulam': middle-acute. No other numbers are printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वज्री (vajrī) — Indra, who holds the thunderbolt | प्रथमानि (prathamāni) — [those] done in the past | यानि वीर्याणि (yāni vīryāṇi) — whatever deeds of prowess | चकार (cakāra) — he did | इन्द्रस्य (indrasya) — of Indra | वीर्याणि (vīryāṇi) — those deeds of valour | नु (nu) — at once | प्र वोचम् (pra vocam) — I shall tell [(of) them one by one] | अहिम् (ahim) — the cloud | अहन् (ahan) — he struck | अनु (anu) — afterwards | अपः (apaḥ) — the waters | ततर्द (tatarda) — he split open (made to fall on the earth) | पर्वतानाम् (parvatānām) — [flowing] from the mountains | वक्षणाः (vakṣaṇāḥ) — the flowing rivers | प्र अभिनत् (pra abhinat) — he made them flow by splitting [the banks].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ I proclaim, one by one and at once, the deeds of valour which Indra, the thunderbolt-bearer, did in the past. For example: Indra struck the cloud; afterwards he made the waters fall upon the earth; and he made a path, by cutting the two banks, for the rivers that flow from the mountains.

॥ English Translation ॥ as printed in the source

I will now ennumerate [sic] the valorous deeds of Indra, the weilder [sic] of the thunderbolt has achieved ; he clove the cloud, he sent down the waters, he broke open a way for the torrents of the mountain.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ The seer of this sūkta, Hiraṇyastūpa, begins, with this sūkta and the next, to praise Indra by relating, one by one, Indra's mighty deeds. Of these, the commentator says that Indra's first heroic deed is the striking, with his vajra, of Vṛtra, who has the form of a cloud; the second is the work of making the rain from that cloud fall on the earth; the third, [the] water fallen on the earth flows as a river and breaks through the mountains. वीर्याणि (vīryāṇi) — deeds of prowess; mighty deeds done with prowess. प्र वोचम् (pra vocam) — I shall say; I shall describe them one by one. यानि प्रथमानि (yāni prathamāni) — the first deeds of valour; or one may say that the word prathamāni means 'chief' — the principal deeds of valour. वज्री (vajrī) — one who holds the vajra in hand. अहिम् (ahim) — 'the cloud': since the word ahi is read among the thirty names of cloud beginning adri, grāvā, ahim means 'the cloud' (Ni. 2-21); ahi also means 'water' (Ni. 2-24); in modern Sanskrit ahi means 'a serpent' [the print: ādhunikasaṃskṛta]. वक्षणाः (vakṣaṇāḥ) — since the word vakṣaṇāḥ is read among the thirty-seven names of rivers beginning avanayaḥ, yakṣyaḥ, vakṣaṇāḥ means 'rivers': the rain from the cloud falls on the mountains and flows from there as rivers: that is what is described here. प्र अभिनत् पर्वतानाम् (pra abhinat parvatānām) — the rivers that flow out of the mountains split the mountains and the earth and flow, [and he] makes a way for them; that is the sense. See the Ṛgveda-Saṃhitā, part 3, pp. 123–124 [the print gives the page numbers of its own earlier volume], for the account of the demon Vṛtra.

Rik 2 pp. 593–595

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

अह॒न्नहिं॒ पर्व॑ते शिश्रिया॒णं त्वष्टा॑स्मै॒ वज्रं॑ स्व॒र्यं॑ ततक्ष । वा॒श्रा इ॑व धे॒नवः॒ स्यन्द॑माना॒ अञ्जः॑ स॒मुद्रमव॑ जग्मु॒रापः॑ ॥ २ ॥

ahann áhiṃ párvate śiśriyāṇáṃ tváṣṭāsmai vájraṃ svaryaṃ tatakṣa | vāśrā́ iva dhenávaḥ syándamānā áñjaḥ samúdram áva jagmur ā́paḥ || 2 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha: अहन् । अहिम् । पर्वते । शिश्रियाणम् । त्वष्टा । अस्मै । वज्रम् । स्वर्यम् । ततक्ष । वाश्राःऽइव । धेनवः । स्यन्दमानाः । अञ्जः । समुद्रम् । अव । जग्मुः । आपः ॥ २ ॥ ahan | ahim | parvate | śiśriyāṇam | tvaṣṭā | asmai | vajram | svaryam | tatakṣa | vāśrāḥ-iva | dhenavaḥ | syandamānāḥ | añjaḥ | samudram | ava | jagmuḥ | āpaḥ || 2 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : पर्वते शिश्रियाणमाश्रितमहिं मेघमहन् । हतवान् । अस्मा इन्द्राय स्वर्यं सुष्ठु प्रेरणीयं यद्वा शब्दनीयं स्तुत्यं त्वष्टा विश्वकर्मा वज्रं ततक्ष । तनूकृतवान् । तेन वज्रेण मेघे भिन्ने सति स्यन्दमानाः प्रस्रवणयुक्ता आपः समुद्रमञ्जः सम्यगजग्मुः । प्राप्ताः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वाश्रा वत्सान्प्रति हम्भारवोपेता धेनव इव । यथा धेनवः सहसा वत्सगृहं गच्छन्ति तद्वत् ॥ शिश्रियाणम् । श्रिञ् सेवायाम् । लिटः कानच् । द्विर्भावहलादिशेषेयङादेशाः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । स्वर्यम् । षु गतौ । अस्मात्सुपूर्वादृहलोर्ण्यदिति ण्यत् । संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्य इति वृद्ध्यभावः । यद्वा । स्वृ शब्दोपतापयोरित्यस्मात् ण्यति पूर्ववद्वृद्ध्यभावः । तित्स्वरितमिति स्वरितत्वम् । वाश्राः । वाश्यन्त इति वाश्राः । वाशृ शब्दे । स्फायितञ्चीत्यादिना the last line of p. 593 is cut off in both scans; the file's earlier reading of it, not verified: रक् । जग्मुः । उसि गमहनेत्युपधालोपः ॥ parvate śiśriyāṇam āśritam ahiṃ megham ahan | hatavān | asmā indrāya svaryaṃ suṣṭhu preraṇīyaṃ yadvā śabdanīyaṃ stutyaṃ tvaṣṭā viśvakarmā vajraṃ tatakṣa | tanūkṛtavān | tena vajreṇa meghe bhinne sati syandamānāḥ prasravaṇayuktā āpaḥ samudram añjaḥ samyag ajagmuḥ | prāptāḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vāśrā vatsān prati hambhāravopetā dhenava iva | yathā dhenavaḥ sahasā vatsagṛhaṃ gacchanti tadvat || śiśriyāṇam | śriñ sevāyām | liṭaḥ kānac | dvirbhāvahalādiśeṣeyaṅādeśāḥ | cita ity antodāttatvam | svaryam | ṣu gatau | asmāt supūrvād ṛhalor ṇyad iti ṇyat | saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anitya iti vṛddhyabhāvaḥ | yadvā | svṛ śabdopatāpayor ity asmāt ṇyati pūrvavad vṛddhyabhāvaḥ | tit svaritam iti svaritatvam | vāśrāḥ | vāśyanta iti vāśrāḥ | vāśṛ śabde | sphāyitañcīty ādinā [last line cut off in the scans:] rak | jagmuḥ | usi gamahanety upadhālopaḥ || "He struck (ahan) the cloud [ahim] that had taken refuge (śiśriyāṇam) on the mountain. For him — Indra — Tvaṣṭṛ, the universal craftsman, shaped a vajra well [svaryam: to be sent forth well, or to be praised]. When the cloud was split by that vajra, the flowing waters, streaming forth, quickly reached the sea [samudram], just as lowing cows run to their calves — as cows hasten straightway to the calf's stall." Grammar page 595, noted briefly: śiśriyāṇam — śriñ sevāyām, bhvādi; kānac by 'liṭaḥ kānaj vā', doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, iyaṅ by 'aci śnudhātubhruvām-', ṇatva by 'aṭ kupvāṅ-', end-acute by 'citaḥ'; svaryam — ṣu gatau with su, ṇyat by 'ṛhalor ṇyat' (Pā. sū. 3-1-124), vṛddhi by 'aco ñṇiti' set aside by 'saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ', guṇa, 'uraṇ raparaḥ', yaṇ: svarya; svarita by 'tit svaritam' (Pā. sū. 6-1-185); vāśrāḥ — vāśṛ śabde, rak by 'sphāyitañcivañciśaki-' (U. sū. 2-120), end-acute by the affix accent; syandamānāḥ — syandū prasravaṇe, śānac, śap, muk by 'āne muk', śānac unaccented by 'tāsyanudātten-', so the root accent: initial-acute; jagmuḥ — gamḷ gatau, liṭ, us by 'parasmaipadānām-', kit by 'asaṃyogāl liṭ kit', penult dropped by 'gamahanajanakhana-' (Pā. sū. 6-4-98), doubling etc.; tiṅanta nighāta. Only these four numbers are printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ पर्वते (parvate) — on the mountain | शिश्रियाणम् (śiśriyāṇam) — [one that] had taken shelter | अहिम् (ahim) — the cloud | अहन् (ahan) — he cleft | अस्मै (asmai) — for this Indra | स्वर्यम् (svaryam) — [of] quick motion, or [that makes] noise | वज्रम् (vajram) — the thunderbolt | त्वष्टा (tvaṣṭā) — Tvaṣṭṛ [the craftsman] | ततक्ष (tatakṣa) — fashioned [for him; after the cloud was cleft by that weapon] | स्यन्दमानाः (syandamānāḥ) — flowing | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters [of the rivers] | वाश्रा इव (vāśrā iva) — as, lowing, | धेनवः (dhenavaḥ) — cows, [carefully] going to their calves | समुद्रम् (samudram) — the sea | अञ्जः (añjaḥ) — eagerly | अव जग्मुः (ava jagmuḥ) — went and reached.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Tvaṣṭṛ made for Indra a vajra of quick motion, or sounding loudly. By that vajra Indra cleft the cloud that had taken shelter on the mountain. Afterwards the waters, streaming down as rivers, hastened eagerly and reached the sea, as cows, lowing, go with eagerness to their calves.

॥ English Translation ॥

He clove the cloud which had taken shelter on the mountain ; on that occasion Twasta fashioned for him the rumbling thunderbolt ; the flowing waters quickly hastened to the ocean like lowing cows hastening to their calves.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ What was said in the previous rik is described more fully in this rik. पर्वते शिश्रियाणम् (parvate śiśriyāṇam) — since clouds ordinarily rest [on the peaks] of mountains, the seer has described the clouds as having taken shelter on a mountain. त्वष्ट्रास्मै वज्रं स्वर्यं ततक्ष (tvaṣṭrāsmai vajraṃ svaryaṃ tatakṣa) — Tvaṣṭṛ, the divine craftsman, made the vajra weapon for Indra. In many places in the Ṛgveda it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ made, of iron, the shining vajra weapon for the killing of Vṛtra: > मह्यं त्वष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासोऽवृजन्नपि क्रतुम् ॥ Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-48-3 [as the source gives it] — mahyaṃ tvaṣṭā vajram atakṣad āyasaṃ mayi devāso 'vṛjann api kratum || — Mine, tentative: "For me Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the iron vajra; in me the gods set [their] will." In this rik Indra himself says that Tvaṣṭṛ made the iron vajra for him. वाश्रा इव धेनवः (vāśrā iva dhenavaḥ) — as cows go to their calves, lowing, so the rivers, roaring loudly from the mountain regions, go to the sea: this is the simile.

Rik 3 pp. 596–599

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

वृ॒षा॒यमा॑णोऽवृणीत॒ सोमं॒ त्रिक॑द्रुकेष्वपिबत्सु॒तस्य॑ । आ साय॑कं म॒घवा॑दत्त॒ वज्र॒मह॑न्नेनं प्रथम॒जामही॑नाम् ॥ ३ ॥

vṛṣāyámāṇo 'vṛṇīta sómaṃ tríkadrukeṣv apibat sutásya | ā sā́yakaṃ maghávādatta vájram áhann enaṃ prathamajā́m áhīnām || 3 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.

Pada-pāṭha: वृषऽयमानः । अवृणीत । सोमम् । त्रिऽकद्रुकेषु । अपिबत् । सुतस्य । आ । सायकम् । मघऽवा । अदत्त । वज्रम् । अहन् । एनम् । प्रथमऽजाम् । अहीनाम् ॥ ३ ॥ vṛṣa-yamānaḥ | avṛṇīta | somam | tri-kadrukeṣu | apibat | sutasya | ā | sāyakam | magha-vā | adatta | vajram | ahan | enam | prathama-jām | ahīnām || 3 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : वृषायमाणो वृष इवाचरन्निन्द्रः सोममवृणीत । वृतवान् । त्रिकद्रुकेषु ज्योतिर्गौरायुरित्येतन्नामकास्त्रयो यागास्त्रिकद्रुका उच्यन्ते । तेषु सुतस्याभिषुतस्य सोमस्यांशमपिबत् । पीतवान् । मघवा धनवानिन्द्रः सायकं बन्धकं वज्रमादत्त । स्वीकृतवान् । तेन च वज्रेणाहीनां मेघानां मध्ये प्रथमजां प्रथमोत्पन्नमेनं मेघमहन् । हतवान् ॥ वृषायमाणः । वृष इवाचरन् । कर्तुः क्यङ् सलोपश्च । पा. ३-१-११ । इति क्यङ् । अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोरिति दीर्घः । अदुपदेशाद्धातोरन्तोदात्तत्वे क्यङन्ताद्धातोरन्तोदात्तत्वम् । सायकम् । षिञ् बन्धने । सिनोतीति सायकः । ण्वुल् । लित्स्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वम् । प्रथमजाम् । प्रथमं जायत इति प्रथमजाः । जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् । विड्वनोरित्यात्वम् ॥ vṛṣāyamāṇo vṛṣa ivācarann indraḥ somam avṛṇīta | vṛtavān | trikadrukeṣu jyotir gaur āyur ity etannāmakās trayo yāgās trikadrukā ucyante | teṣu sutasyābhiṣutasya somasyāṃśam apibat | pītavān | maghavā dhanavān indraḥ sāyakaṃ bandhakaṃ vajram ādatta | svīkṛtavān | tena ca vajreṇāhīnāṃ meghānāṃ madhye prathamajāṃ prathamotpannam enaṃ megham ahan | hatavān || vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ | vṛṣa ivācaran | kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaś ca | pā. 3-1-11 | iti kyaṅ | akṛtsārvadhātukayor iti dīrghaḥ | adupadeśād dhātor antodāttatve kyaṅantād dhātor antodāttatvam | sāyakam | ṣiñ bandhane | sinotīti sāyakaḥ | ṇvul | litsvareṇādyudāttatvam | prathamajām | prathamaṃ jāyata iti prathamajāḥ | janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ | viḍvanor ity ātvam || "Behaving like a bull (vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ), Indra chose [avṛṇīta] the Soma; he drank the portion of the pressed [sutasya] Soma in the trikadrukas — [the three rites named] jyotiḥ, gauḥ and āyuḥ are called trikadrukas. Indra, the wealthy (maghavā), took (ā adatta) the vajra (sāyakam, 'the binder'), and with that vajra struck this first-born (prathamajām) cloud among the clouds (ahīnām)."

Grammar pages 598–599, noted briefly: vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ — kyaṅ by 'kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaś ca' (Pā. sū. 3-1-11) after a word denoting the agent of comparison, lengthening by 'akṛtsārvadhātukayor dīrghaḥ', root by 'sanādyantā dhātavaḥ', śānac, muk by 'āne muk', ṇatva; śap unaccented, śānac unaccented by 'tāsyanudātten-', so the kyaṅ-root's end-acute stays: the ya is acute; avṛṇīta — vṛñ varaṇe, kryādi, laṅ, ta, śnā, ī by 'ī halyaghoḥ', ṇatva, aṭ; śnā ṅit-like, no guṇa; tiṅanta nighāta; apibat — pā pāne, laṅ, tip, śap, piba by 'pāghrādhmā-', 'itaś ca', no laghūpadha-guṇa (a-final), aṭ; nighāta by 'tiṅṅatiṅaḥ'; sāyakam — ṣiñ bandhane, ṇvul, aka by 'yuvor anākau', vṛddhi by 'aco ñṇiti', āy by 'eco 'yavāyāvaḥ', initial acute by 'liti'; adatta — ḍudāñ dāne, juhotyādi, laṅ, ta, ślu, doubling by 'ślau', short reduplicate, ā dropped by 'śnābhyastayor ātaḥ', cartva by 'khari ca', aṭ; nighāta; prathamajām — janī prādurbhāve, viṭ by 'janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ' (Pā. sū. 3-2-67), n → ā by 'viḍvanor anunāsikasyāt' (Pā. sū. 6-4-41), the kṛt-final accent by 'gatikārakopapadāt kṛt'. Only these three numbers are printed.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वृषायमाणः (vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ) — [Indra,] like a bull, in his own time [with the passion of a bull] | सोमम् (somam) — Soma-juice | अवृणीत (avṛṇīta) — he chose | त्रिकद्रुकेषु (trikadrukeṣu) — in the three kinds of sacrifices, jyotiḥ, gauḥ and āyuḥ | सुतस्य (sutasya) — [of the Soma-juice, a portion] pressed | अपिबत् (apibat) — drank | मघवा (maghavā) — Indra, the possessor of wealth | सायकम् (sāyakam) — the thunderbolt | आ अदत्त (ā adatta) — lifted (with it) | अहीनाम् (ahīnām) — [among] the clouds | प्रथमजाम् (prathamajām) — born first | एनम् (enam) — this cloud | अहन् (ahan) — he struck.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Indra, like a bull, chose the Soma-juice with eagerness. He drank the pressed Soma-juice in the three kinds of sacrifice called jyotiḥ, gauḥ and āyuḥ. Indra, the wealthy, lifted up the vajra in his hand and struck with it the cloud that was first born among the clouds.

॥ English Translation ॥

Impetuous (or mighty) as a bull, Indra desired Soma ; he drank of the extracted Soma-juice in the three-fold sacrifice ; Indra, lord of riches took his deadly thunderbolt and with it struck the first-born of the clouds.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ वृषायमाणः (vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ) — vṛṣa ivācaran: 'behaving like a bull'; having the strength of a bull, or the strength of the bull-like; that is, 'one who shows [his] strength like a bull': exceedingly powerful. त्रिकद्रुकेषु (trikadrukeṣu) — for this word the commentator says: 'the three kinds of sacrifice (yāga) called jyotiḥ, gauḥ and āyuḥ'. This word has the sense of 'wooden vessels in which Soma-juice is placed'. A few riks in which this sense is found we give as examples: > उग्रेष्विन्नु शूर मन्दसानस्त्रिकद्रुकेषु पाहि सोममिन्द्र ॥ Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-11-17 — ugreṣv in nu śūra mandasānas trikadrukeṣu pāhi somam indra || — Mine, tentative: "Exhilarated among the mighty, O hero, drink Soma in the trikadrukas, O Indra." > त्रिकद्रुकेष्वपिबत्सुतस्यास्य मदे अहिमिन्द्रो जघान ॥ Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-15-1 — trikadrukeṣv apibat sutasyāsya made ahim indro jaghāna || — Mine, tentative: "In the trikadrukas he drank of the pressed [Soma]; in its exhilaration Indra slew the ahi." > त्रिकद्रुकेषु महिषो यवाशिरं तुविशुष्मस्तृपत्सोममपिबद्विष्णुना सुतं यथावशत् ॥ Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-22-1; the reference line is cut off in the better scan, read from the old scan — trikadrukeṣu mahiṣo yavāśiraṃ tuviśuṣmas tṛpat somam apibad viṣṇunā sutaṃ yathāvaśat || — Mine, tentative: "In the trikadrukas the mighty one, of great vigour, satisfied, drank the Soma mixed with barley, pressed with Viṣṇu, as he desired." > त्रिकद्रुकेषु चेतनं देवासो यज्ञमत्नत ॥ Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-13-18 — trikadrukeṣu cetanaṃ devāso yajñam atnata || — Mine, tentative: "In the trikadrukas the gods spread the thoughtful sacrifice." > त्रिकद्रुकेष [sic] चेतनं देवासो यज्ञमत्नत ॥ Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-92-21; the same pāda printed again, with केष — trikadrukeṣa [sic] cetanaṃ devāso yajñam atnata || — Mine, tentative: as the preceding. > त्रिकद्रुकेभिः पतति षळुर्वीरेकमिद्बृहत् ॥ Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-14-16 — trikadrukebhiḥ patati ṣaḷ urvīr ekam id bṛhat || — Mine, tentative: "With the trikadrukas [one] flies over the six wide [regions], the one great." This word is always used in the plural, and its use is always in contexts of drinking Soma. प्रथमजामहीनाम् (prathamajām ahīnām) — meghānāṃ madhye prathamotpannaṃ megham: among the clouds, the cloud that was first produced. When clouds, in the form of masses, gather, the first of them to arise is called prathamajā. Since, in the beginning of a rain-cloud, small drops [of the cloud] have already been gathered into small, scattered pieces, it is [said] here that [Indra] struck the cloud that was produced first.

Saṃhitā-pāṭha the last line from the old scan

यदि॒न्द्राह॑न्प्रथम॒जामही॑ना॒मान्मा॒यिना॒ममि॑नाः॒ प्रोत मा॒याः । आत्सूर्यं॑ ज॒नय॒न्द्यामु॒षासं॑ ता॒दीत्ना॒ शत्रुं॒ न किला॑ विवित्से ॥ ४ ॥

yad indrā́han prathamajā́m áhīnām ā́n māyínām ámināḥ próta māyā́ḥ | āt sū́ryaṃ janáyan dyā́m uṣā́saṃ tādī́tnā śátruṃ ná kílā vivitse || 4 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The last Saṃhitā line (न किला विवित्से) is cut off in the better scan (PDF 613) and read from the old scan (PDF 614).

Pada-pāṭha: यत् । इन्द्र । अहन् । प्रथमऽजाम् । अहीनाम् । आत् । मायिनाम् । अमिनाः । प्र । उत । मायाः । आत् । सूर्यम् । जनयन् । द्याम् । उषासम् । तादीत्ना । शत्रुम् । न । किल । विवित्से ॥ ४ ॥ yat | indra | ahan | prathama-jām | ahīnām | āt | māyinām | aminaḥ | pra | uta | māyāḥ | āt | sūryam | janayan | dyām | uṣāsam | tādītnā | śatrum | na | kila | vivitse || 4 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : उतापि च हे इन्द्र यद्यदाहीनां मेघानां मध्ये प्रथमजां प्रथमोत्पन्नं मेघमहन् हतवानसि आत्तदनन्तरं मायिनां मायोपेतानामसुराणां संबन्धिनीर्मायाः प्रामिनाः । प्रकर्षेण नाशितवानसि । अनन्तरं सूर्यमुषसमुषःकालं द्यामाकाशं च जनयन् उत्पादयन्नावरकमेघनिवारणेन प्रकाशयन् वर्तसे । तादीत्ना तदानीमावरकान्धकाराभावाच्छत्रुं घातकं वैरिणं न विवित्से किल । त्वं न लब्धवान्खलु ॥ अहन् । हन्तेर्लङि हल्ङ्याब्भ्य इति सिलोपः । आडागम उदात्तः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । मायिनाम् । मायाशब्दस्य व्रीह्यादिषु पाठाद्व्रीह्यादिभ्यश्च । पा. ५-२-११६ । इति मत्वर्थीय इनिः । अमिनाः । मीञ् हिंसायाम् । क्र्यादिकः । मीनातेर्निगमे । पा. ७-३-८१ । इति ह्रस्वत्वम् । तादीत्ना । तदानीमित्यस्य पृषोदरादित्वाद्वर्णविपर्ययः । किल । निपातस्येति दीर्घत्वम् । विवित्से । विद्लृ लाभे । क्रादिनियमात्प्राप्त इट् व्यत्ययेन न भवति ॥ utāpi ca he indra yad yadāhīnāṃ meghānāṃ madhye prathamajāṃ prathamotpannaṃ megham ahan hatavān asi āt tadanantaraṃ māyināṃ māyopetānām asurāṇāṃ saṃbandhinīr māyāḥ prāminaḥ | prakarṣeṇa nāśitavān asi | anantaraṃ sūryam uṣasam uṣaḥkālaṃ dyām ākāśaṃ ca janayan utpādayann āvarakameghanivāraṇena prakāśayan vartase | tādītnā tadānīm āvarakāndhakārābhāvāc chatruṃ ghātakaṃ vairiṇaṃ na vivitse kila | tvaṃ na labdhavān khalu || ahan | hanter laṅi halṅyābbhya iti silopaḥ | āḍāgama udāttaḥ | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ | māyinām | māyāśabdasya vrīhyādiṣu pāṭhād vrīhyādibhyaś ca | pā. 5-2-116 | iti matvarthīya iniḥ | aminaḥ | mīñ hiṃsāyām | kryādikaḥ | mīnāter nigame | pā. 7-3-81 | iti hrasvatvam | tādītnā | tadānīm ity asya pṛṣodarāditvād varṇaviparyayaḥ | kila | nipātasyeti dīrghatvam | vivitse | vidḷ lābhe | krādiniyamāt prāpta iṭ vyatyayena na bhavati || "And also, O Indra, when you struck the cloud first born among the clouds, then (āt) you destroyed the wiles (māyāḥ) of the demons who possess wiles (māyinām). Afterwards, creating the sun, the dawn and the sky — by removing the covering cloud — you shine; then, since there is no covering [cloud], you [indeed] did not find (vivitse) a foe, an enemy who could strike you." The Prati-padārtha, Bhāvārtha, English, Special Topics and the grammar of Rik 4 are on pp. 600–602 (PDF 615–617) — to be written in the next batch, with the next Rik's pages.

Rik 4 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada and bhāṣya are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 600–602

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ उत (uta) — moreover | इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | यत् (yat) — when | अहीनाम् (ahīnām) — among the clouds | प्रथमजाम् (prathamajām) — the first-born cloud | अहन् (ahan) — you struck | आत् (āt) — after that | मायिनाम् (māyinām) — [of] the deceitful demons | मायाः (māyāḥ) — the wiles | प्र अमिनाः (pra aminaḥ) — you destroyed completely | सूर्यम् (sūryam) — the sun | उषसम् (uṣasam) — the time of dawn | द्याम् (dyām) — the sky | जनयन् (janayan) — [making, that is] creating, making [them] clearly visible | तादीत्ना (tādītnā) — then | शत्रुम् (śatrum) — a foe that injures | न विवित्से किल (na vivitse kila) — you have not found [that is, there is no enemy who would oppose you].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Indra! Having killed the cloud that was first born among the clouds, those deeds described before — you who destroyed the wiles of the deceitful demons, and who made the sun, the dawn-time and the sky clearly visible and shining: at that time there was no enemy to oppose you and to cause harm to the world.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra, after you have destroyed the first-born of the clouds, you have destroyed machinations of the deluders and then making the sun, the dawn and the firmament bright and clear, you have not left an enemy to oppose you.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ मायिनाम्, मायाः (māyinām, māyāḥ) — māyopetānām asurāṇāṃ saṃbandhinīr māyāḥ: 'the wiles of the demons who are endowed with wiles'. Māyā means 'deceit, wile, strategy &c.' [the English as printed]: here māyināṃ māyāḥ means the deceitful tricks of the demons who have [such] wiles. For the detailed sense of these words see the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 3 [the print: bhāga 3], pp. 476–477. प्र अमिनाः (pra aminaḥ) — mīñ hiṃsāyām: you destroyed. आत् सूर्यं जनयन् द्यां उषसम् (āt sūryaṃ janayan dyām uṣasam) — removing completely the network of clouds that covered the sun, [you] make the sun, the atmosphere, and the dawn-time shine clearly and brightly: that is the sense. तादीत्ना (tādītnā) — tadānīm: 'then'; at the time after the removal of the clouds.

Grammar pages 601–602, noted briefly: ahan — hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi, laṅ, tip, 'itaś ca', luk of śap by 'adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ', t dropped by 'hal ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt', aṭ (acute): initial-acute; no nighāta by 'yadvṛttān nityam'; māyinām — māyā asya asti; ini by 'vrīhyādibhyaś ca' (Pā. sū. 5-2-116), ā dropped by 'yasyeti ca', genitive plural, the i acute by the affix accent; aminaḥ — mīñ hiṃsāyām, kryādi, laṅ 2nd singular sip, 'itaś ca', śnā by 'kryādibhyaḥ śnā', aṭ, rutva and visarga; the root shortened in the Veda by 'mīnāter nigame' (Pā. sū. 7-3-81); no nighāta by 'yadvṛttān nityam', so the aṭ-accent stands; tādītnā — for tadānīm, by 'pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam': varṇaviparyaya and augments; kila — nipāta by 'cādayo 'sattve', lengthened in the Saṃhitā by 'nipātasya ca' (Pā. sū. 6-3-136): kilā; vivitse — vidḷ lābhe, tudādi, liṭ 2nd singular thās, se by 'thāsaḥ se', doubling by 'liṭi dhātoḥ', halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cartva by 'khari ca'; 'kṛsṛbhṛ-' restricts the iṭ-prohibition in liṭ to kṛ etc., so iṭ would come to se, but by 'vyatyayo bahulam' it does not; after an atiṅanta, nighāta by 'tiṅṅatiṅaḥ'. Only these three numbers are printed.

Rik 5 (begun; see the next batch) pp. 603–608

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

अह॑न्वृ॒त्रं वृ॑त्र॒तरं॒ व्यं॑स॒मिन्द्रो॒ वज्रे॑ण मह॒ता व॒धेन॑ । स्कन्धां॑सीव॒ कुलि॑शेना॒ विवृ॒क्णाहिः॑ शयत उप॒पृक्पृ॑थि॒व्याः ॥ ५ ॥

áhan vṛtráṃ vṛtratáraṃ vyaṃsam índro vájreṇa mahatā́ vadhéna | skándhāṃsīva kúliśenā vívṛkṇā́hiḥ śayata upapṛ́k pṛthivyā́ḥ || 5 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The stroke of हिः stands over the junction of क्णा and हि.

Pada-pāṭha: अहन् । वृत्रम् । वृत्रऽतरम् । विऽअंसम् । इन्द्रः । वज्रेण । महता । वधेन । स्कन्धांसिऽइव । कुलिशेन । विऽवृक्णा । अहिः । शयते । उपऽपृक् । पृथिव्याः ॥ ५ ॥ ahan | vṛtram | vṛtra-taram | vi-aṃsam | indraḥ | vajreṇa | mahatā | vadhena | skandhāṃsi-iva | kuliśena | vi-vṛkṇā | ahiḥ | śayate | upa-pṛk | pṛthivyāḥ || 5 ||

For the cutting of the shoulders there is a simile: as trunks (skandhāṃsi) of trees cut by an axe (kuliśena) fall, so, the serpent, Vṛtra, lies [śayate] close to the earth, touching [upapṛk] the earth: he lies like a cut log of wood on the ground."

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, remainder p. 604, top; re-read from the print: …पदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः इति स्वरितत्वम् । वधेन । हनश्च वध इति भावेऽप् । तत्संनियोगेन धातोर्वधादेशः । स चान्तोदात्तः । अन्त्यस्याकारस्यातो लोप इति लोपे उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण प्रत्ययस्योदात्तत्वम् । विवृक्णा । ओव्रश्चू छेदने । कर्मणि निष्ठा । यस्य विभाषेतीट्प्रतिषेधः । ओदितश्च । पा. ८-२-४५ । इति परत्वान्निष्ठानत्वम् । ततो व्रश्चभ्रस्जेति षत्वे प्राप्ते निष्ठादेशः षत्वस्वरप्रत्ययेड्विधिषु सिद्धो वक्तव्यः । पा. ८-२-६-७ । इति नत्वस्य सिद्धत्वेन झल्परत्वाभावात् षत्वं न भवति । कुत्वे तु कर्तव्ये तदसिद्धमेव । पा. ८-२-१ । इति चोः कुरिति कुत्वम् । शेश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । शयते । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुगभावः । पृथिव्याः । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥ ३६ ॥ grammatical tail, not explained; Varga 36 ends here … padaprakṛtisvaratvam | udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ iti svaritatvam | vadhena | hanaśca vadha iti bhāve 'p | tatsaṃniyogena dhātorvadhādeśaḥ | sa cāntodāttaḥ | antyasyākārasyāto lopa iti lope udāttanivṛttisvareṇa pratyayasyodāttatvam | vivṛkṇā | ovraścū chedane | karmaṇi niṣṭhā | yasya vibhāṣetīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | oditaśca | pā. 8-2-45 | iti paratvānniṣṭhānatvam | tato vraścabhrasjeti ṣatve prāpte niṣṭhādeśaḥ ṣatvasvarapratyayeḍvidhiṣu siddho vaktavyaḥ | pā. 8-2-6-7 | iti natvasya siddhatvena jhalparatvābhāvāt ṣatvaṃ na bhavati | kutve tu kartavye tadasiddhameva | pā. 8-2-1 | iti coḥ kuriti kutvam | śeśchandasi bahulamiti śerlopaḥ | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | śayate | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo lugabhāvaḥ | pṛthivyāḥ | udāttayaṇo halpūrvāditi vibhakterudāttatvam ‖ 36 ‖

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | वज्रेण (vajreṇa) — with the thunderbolt | वृत्रतरम् (vṛtratarama) — [him who] covered [the world] in the form of intense darkness, or [who] covered [it] more than all enemies | वृत्रम् (vṛtram) — the demon Vṛtra | कुलिशेन (kuliśena) — with an axe | विवृक्णा (vivṛkṇā) — [as] cut off completely | स्कन्धांसीव (skandhāṃsīva) — like trunks | व्यंसम् (vyaṃsam) — [with] shoulders cut off | अहन् (ahan) — [he] killed | अहिः (ahiḥ) — Vṛtra | पृथिव्याः (pṛthivyāḥ) — [on] the earth | उपपृक् (upapṛk) — closely clasping | शयते (śayate) — lies [lifeless, like a cut-off trunk].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Indra, with his great vajra, cut off the shoulders of the demon Vṛtra, who had covered the world in the form of deep darkness, and killed him — as trunks of trees cut by an axe fall down. Then Vṛtra lies lifeless, like a severed trunk, closely embracing the earth.

॥ English Translation ॥

Indra struck the enemy (Vritra) more hostile than other enemies, with his destroying thunderbolt ; as the trunks of trees are felled by the axe, so Vritra deprived of his arms lies prostrate on the earth.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ वृत्रतरम् (vṛtrataram) — an enemy more [hostile] than the [other] enemies; or one who covers all the worlds with darkness (with a cloud). व्यंसम् (vyaṃsam) — vigatāṃsam: 'with the shoulders gone', that is, one without arms: the sense is that with the vajra [Indra] cut off Vṛtra's arms. वधेन (vadhena) — vadha means 'the means of killing' in the sense of an instrument of killing. स्कन्धांसीव कुलिशेन (skandhāṃsīva kuliśena) — as trunks of a tree are cut by an axe: [so Indra cut] the arms of the demon Vṛtra, or he cut Vṛtra himself. अहिः शयते उपपृक् पृथिव्याः (ahiḥ śayate upapṛk pṛthivyāḥ) — after Indra struck Vṛtra with the vajra, that Vṛtra fell on the ground like a tree cut down by an axe; the principal sense is: Vṛtra, who was in the clouds, [was] cut off by Indra's vajra; his arms [or his body] fell upon the earth like the trunk of a tree, and the water that was in the cloud fell onto the earth.

Grammar pages 605–606, noted briefly: vṛtrataram — vṛtu vartane, bhvādi, rak in the sense of bhāva by 'sphāyitañcivañciśaki-' (U. sū. 2-1[7?]0 here: the middle digit has a flat foot; p. 595 prints 2-120 for the same sūtra), kit, so no laghūpadha-guṇa; vṛtreṇa … tarati iti vṛtrataraḥ, tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, ac as pacādi by 'nandigrahipacādibhyaḥ', guṇa; the end-acute from 'gatikārake' set aside by 'parādiś chandasi bahulam' (Pā. sū. 6-2-199): the second member initial-acute; if tara is taken as tarap, the accent is by vyatyaya; vyaṃsam — vigatau aṃsau yasmāt, bahuvrīhi, 'bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam': vi acute; yaṇ for it, so svarita by 'udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ' (Pā. sū. 8-2-4); vadhena — 'hanaś ca vadhaḥ' (Pā. sū. 3-3-76): ap in bhāva, vadha (end-acute) substituted, its a dropped by 'ato lopaḥ', ap unaccented (pit), the suffix acute by 'anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ'; vivṛkṇā — ovraścū chedane, kta (niṣṭhā) in the passive, s dropped by 'skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca', iṭ barred by 'yasya vibhāṣā', ta → na by 'oditaś ca' (Pā. sū. 8-2-45), the ṣatva of 'vraścabhrasja-' blocked since the niṣṭhā-substitute is siddha (Pā. sū. 8-2-6-7, vārttika), but asiddha for kutva by 'pūrvatrāsiddham' (Pā. sū. 8-2-1): k by 'coḥ kuḥ', ṇatva; vi keeps its accent by 'gatir anantaraḥ'; neuter plural jas → śi by 'jaśśasoḥ śiḥ', num, upadhā-lengthening, śi dropped by 'śeś chandasi bahulam' (Pā. sū. 6-1-70), na-lopa: vivṛkṇā; śayate — śīṅ svapne, adādi, laṭ, ta → te by 'ṭita ātmanepadānām-', luk of śap by 'adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ' withheld by 'bahulaṃ chandasi', ay by 'eco 'yavāyāvaḥ'; nighāta after an atiṅanta; pṛthivyāḥ — genitive singular; after yaṇ in the acute's place, the ending is acute by 'udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt' (Pā. sū. 6-1-174). Only these numbers are printed.

kūlānīti rujānā nadyaḥ | rujānā nadyo bhavanti rujanti kūlāni | ni. 6-4 | iti yāskaḥ | vyatyayena śānac | tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ | numabhāvaśchāndasaḥ | adupadeśāllasārvadhātukānudāttatve vikaraṇasvaraḥ | what Indra? the great hero (mahāvīram), being great in qualities, endowed with valour, the oppressor of many (tuvibādham), the scatterer of enemies [ṛjīṣam]. But he could not escape (nātārīt) the meeting (saṃṛtim) of the slayings [vadhānām] of the enemies that belong to this Indra. Vṛtra, whose enemy is Indra [indraśatruḥ], struck by Indra and fallen on the rivers, crushed (saṃ pipiṣe) the banks (rujānāḥ) of the rivers: by the fall of Vṛtra's body, which covered all the worlds, the banks of the rivers and the stones etc. there were reduced to powder." The Kannada grammar on this Ṛk is on pp. 610–611; see the section below. The note formerly given here described the bhāṣya's grammatical tail on p. 608, now transcribed above.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ दुर्मदः (durmadaḥ) — [Vṛtra,] the arrogant | अयोद्धेव (ayoddheva) — [thinking] 'there is no fighter equal to me' | महावीरम् (mahāvīram) — [Indra,] great, endowed with valour | तुविबाधम् (tuvibādham) — [the one who] harms many enemies | ऋजीषम् (ṛjīṣam) — [one] who makes the enemies run far | आ जुह्वे हि (ā juhve hi) — he called, for [battle] | अस्य (asya) — this Indra's | वधानाम् (vadhānām) — [of] those killings | संमृतिम् (saṃmṛtim) — the encounter | न अतारीत् (na atārīt) — [he] could not escape | इन्द्रशत्रुः (indraśatruḥ) — the enemy of Indra [Vṛtra] | रुजानाः (rujānāḥ) — the rivers [or the banks of the rivers] | सं पिपिषे (saṃ pipiṣe) — crushed well.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ The arrogant Vṛtra, thinking that there was no warrior equal to him, called to battle the great hero Indra, who is rich in valour, who harms many enemies and makes his foes run far. But Vṛtra could not escape the killing blows of Indra. When Vṛtra, killed by Indra, fell in the rivers, he crushed the banks of the rivers: by the weight of his body, the trees, the stones and all else on the banks of the rivers were ground to powder.

॥ English Translation ॥

The arrogant Vritra, as if unequalled, challenged Indra, the mighty hero, the destroyer of many and the scatterer of foes ; but he did not escape the fate of Indra's enemies ; the enemy of Indra was dashed against the banks of the rivers.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अयोद्धेव (ayoddheva) — yoddṛrahite iva, niśśatrur iva sagarvaḥ: as if there were no fighter, as if he had no enemy, in arrogance: [he is] intoxicated by the pride that 'there is no warrior who is able to fight with me, who is my equal'. दुर्मदः (durmadaḥ) — Vṛtra, who has [the pride of] evil arrogance. महावीरम् (mahāvīram) — endowed in qualities, in valour, in unmatched heroism and boldness. तुविबाधम् (tuvibādham) — tuvi means 'many'; one who in battle harms many enemies. ऋजीषम् (ṛjīṣam) — one who is capable of conquering; one who has strength. न अतारीत् (na atārīt) — he was not able to endure. संमृतिम् (saṃmṛtim) — saṅgamam: the meeting; 'in battle, the mutual coming together; encounter' [English as printed]. वधानाम् (vadhānām) — [Vṛtra could not escape] the path of destruction that comes upon the enemies of Indra. रुजानाः (rujānāḥ) — nadīḥ: the rivers; or the banks of the river. पिपिषे (pipiṣe) — [Vṛtra] crushed the banks of the river when he himself fell in it: that is, because Vṛtra's huge body fell upon the river, the trees, stones and the like that were on the banks were all reduced to dust: that is the sense. इन्द्रशत्रुः (indraśatruḥ) — Vṛtra, who is Indra's enemy. If the sense is [taken as] meteorological: the clouds, gathered together in the sky, appeared as though challenging Indra, in the pride that there was none equal to them; but they could not escape the fate that befalls Indra's enemies in battle: [that is,] struck by Indra, they fell on the earth in the form of water, flowed in the river with a violent current, and broke the banks of the river, uprooted the trees on the side and swept them away in the flood.

Rik 6 — grammar (pp. 610–611)

Re-read from the print: the grammar on Rik 6 is on pp. 610–611; the last line of p. 610 is cut off in the better scan and read from the old scan, PDF 625.

Grammar pages 610–611, noted briefly: ayoddhā — na vidyate yoddhā asya, bahuvrīhi; the first-member accent set aside by 'nañsubhyām': end-acute; the samāsānta is optional by 'samāsāntavidhir anityaḥ' (Paribhā. 84), so no kap by 'nadyṛtaś ca' (Pā. sū. 5-4-153); juhve — hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca, liṭ, ta → e by 'liṭas tajhayor eśirec', saṃprasāraṇa by 'abhyastasya ca' (Pā. sū. 6-1-33), pūrvarūpa by 'saṃprasāraṇāc ca': hu, doubling, cutva; uvaṅ by 'huśnuvoḥ sā-' not applied in the Veda; or, sārvadhātuka by 'chandasy ubhayathā', yaṇ by 'huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke' (Pā. sū. 6-4-87); the paribhāṣā 'lakṣaṇapratipadoktayoḥ pratipadoktasyaiva grahaṇam' (Paribhā. 105) is not applied (else ājuhvānaḥ would fail); sātaye huve vām (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-10-13 as printed here; the bhāṣya prints 6-60-13) has no yaṇ since 'er anekācaḥ' requires a polysyllabic stem; end-acute by the affix accent; mahāvīram — mahāṃś cāsau vīraś ca, ā by 'ān mahataḥ samā-' (Pā. sū. 6-3-46), end-acute by 'samāsasya'; tuvibādham — bādhṛ viloḍane, ac by 'nandigrahipacādibhyaḥ' (Pā. sū. 3-1-134), the kṛt-final accent by 'gatikārakopapadāt kṛt'; samṛtim — ktin by 'striyāṃ ktin', sam a gati by 'gatiś ca', which keeps its accent by 'tādau ca niti kṛty atau' (Pā. sū. 6-2-50); rujānāḥ — rujo bhaṅge, rujanti kūlāni iti; śānac by 'vyatyayo bahulam' though parasmaipadin, śa by 'tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ', no num (Vedic); Yāska: 'rujānā nadyo bhavanti rujanti kūlāni' (Niru. 6-4); śānac unaccented, so the vikaraṇa accent; pipiṣe — piṣḷ saṃcūrṇane, liṭ by 'chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ', eś, doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; nighāta after an atiṅanta; indraśatruḥ — bahuvrīhi, first-member accent by 'bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā'. Only these numbers are printed.
