pādaśabdasyāntyalopaśchāndasaḥ | ahastaḥ | bahuvrīhau nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvam | apṛtanyat | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | kavyadhvarapṛtanasyetyantyalopaḥ | bubhūṣan | sani grahaguhośca | pā. 7-2-12 | itīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | purutrā | devamanuṣyapuruṣapurumartyebhyo dvitīyāsaptamyorbahulam | pā. 5-4-56 | iti saptamyarthe trāpratyayaḥ | aśayat | vyatyayena parasmaipadam | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo lugabhāvaḥ | vyastaḥ | asu kṣepaṇe ityasmātkarmaṇi ktaḥ | yasya vibhāṣetīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | saṃhitāyāmudāttasvaritayoryaṇa iti parasyānudāttasya svaritatvam | "Vṛtra, footless (apāt) and handless (ahastaḥ) because [his limbs] had been cut off by the vajra, still sought to fight (apṛtanyat) with Indra: out of excess of hatred, though pierced in many ways, he did not give up the battle. On this handless, footless Vṛtra's shoulder (sānau) — [like] a mountain-peak, a mighty shoulder — Indra, facing him, dashed (jaghāna) the vajra. For the wish to fight in one who is unable [the illustration is]: as a vadhri — a man who has been castrated — wishing to equal (pratimānam bubhūṣan) another man who is capable of impregnating, cannot do so, so [Vṛtra could not]. That Vṛtra, thrown about and struck (vyastaḥ) in many limbs (purutrā), lay down (aśayat) — fell on the earth."

Grammar page 614, noted briefly: apāt — na vidyete pādau yasya, bahuvrīhi, the final of pāda dropped (Vedic); ahastaḥ — nañ-bahuvrīhi, end-acute by 'nañsubhyām' (Pā. sū. 6-2-172); apṛtanyat — pṛtanām ātmana icchati, kyac by 'supa ātmanaḥ kyac' (Pā. sū. 3-1-8), the final of pṛtanā dropped in the Veda by 'kavyadhvarapṛtanasya-' (Pā. sū. 7-4-39), root by 'sanādyantā dhātavaḥ', laṅ; bubhūṣan — bhavitum icchan, san, doubling by 'sanyaṅoḥ', 'hrasvaḥ', jaś by 'abhyāse carca', iṭ barred by 'sani grahaguhoś ca' (Pā. sū. 7-2-12), root by 'sanādyantā dhātavaḥ', śatṛ; purutrā — trā in the sense of the locative by 'devamanuṣyapuruṣapurumartyebhyo dvitīyāsaptamyor bahulam' (Pā. sū. 5-4-56), end-acute by the affix accent; aśayat — śīṅ svapne, adādi, tip by 'vyatyayo bahulam', 'itaś ca', no luk of śap by 'bahulaṃ chandasi', guṇa, ay, aṭ; nighāta after an atiṅanta; vyastaḥ — asu kṣepaṇe, kta in the passive, iṭ barred by 'yasya vibhāṣā', yaṇ; vi keeps its accent by 'gatir anantaraḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-2-49); in the Saṃhitā the following anudātta becomes svarita by 'udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ' (Pā. sū. 8-2-4). Page 613 holds the end of the Pratipadārtha, the Bhāvārtha, the printed English and the Special Topics.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अपात् (apāt) — [Vṛtra, who was] footless [his feet being cut off by the vajra] | अहस्तः (ahastaḥ) — [and] handless | इन्द्रम् (indram) — Indra | अपृतन्यत् (apṛtanyat) — he [Vṛtra] challenged to battle | अस्य (asya) — this [footless and handless] Vṛtra's | सानौ अधि (sānau adhi) — on the peak of the mountain-like shoulder | वज्रम् (vajram) — the thunderbolt | आ जघान (ā jaghāna) — [Indra] dashed | वृष्णः (vṛṣṇaḥ) — [of a man] capable of impregnating (that is, of a virile man) | प्रतिमानम् (pratimānam) — the equal | बुभूषन् (bubhūṣan) — [as one] wishing to become | वध्रिः (vadhriḥ) — a castrated man (a man without virility) [does so in vain] | वृत्रः (vṛtraḥ) — Vṛtra | पुरुत्रा (purutrā) — [in] many parts of the body | व्यस्तः (vyastaḥ) — cut asunder | अशयत् (aśayat) — fell on the earth, and lay [still].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Even after Indra had cut off his hands and feet with the vajra, Vṛtra still challenged Indra, and fought him. Then Indra dashed his vajra on the mountain-like shoulder of Vṛtra. As a man who has no virility, wishing to be the equal of a virile man, cannot, so Vṛtra, longing to match Indra, could not; with many of his limbs cut asunder he fell on the earth and lay motionless.

॥ English Translation ॥

Footless and armless he (Vritra) still defied Indra who struck him with the thunderbolt upon his mountain-like shoulder ; desirous of encountering Indra like one emasculated who pretends to virility, Vritra mutilated of many organs, fell down and remained motionless.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अपात् अहस्तः अपृतन्यदिन्द्रम् (apāt ahastaḥ apṛtanyad indram) — although in the battle his hands and feet had been cut off, Vṛtra, without regard for that, rushed at Indra: this is the idea. सानौ (sānau) — on the arm of that Vṛtra, whose body was spread wide and large like the ridge of a mountain. वृष्णो वध्रिः प्रतिमानं बुभूषन् (vṛṣṇo vadhriḥ pratimānaṃ bubhūṣan) — a weak man, wishing to fight with a hero, wishing to defeat him: so [Vṛtra]. Vṛṣṇaḥ means 'one capable of the power of semen' — that is, a warrior having valour; vadhriḥ means a man without strength, a neuter, a eunuch [the print adds: 'a hermaphrodite']. पुरुत्रा (purutrā) — bahvavayaveṣu: in many parts of the body. व्यस्तः (vyastaḥ) — tāḍitaḥ: struck, [with] limbs split into many pieces. अशयत् (aśayat) — he lay: that is, he fell on the earth.

न॒दं न भि॒न्नम॑मु॒या शया॑नं॒ मनो॒ रुहा॑णा॒ अति॑ य॒न्त्यापः॑ । [accent ?] याश्चि॑द्वृ॒त्रो म॑हि॒ना प॒र्यति॑ष्ठ॒त्तासा॒महिः॑ पत्सुतः॒शीर्बभूव॑ ॥ ८ ॥

nadáṃ na bhinnám amuyā́ śáyānaṃ máno rúhāṇā áti yanty ā́paḥ | [accent ?] yā́ś cid vṛtró mahinā́ paryátiṣṭhat tā́sām áhiḥ patsutaḥśī́r babhū́va || 8 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Pada-pāṭha: नदम् । न । भिन्नम् । अमुया । शयानम् । मनः । रुहाणाः । अति । यन्ति । आपः । याः । चित् । वृत्रः । महिना । परिऽअतिष्ठत् । तासाम् । अहिः । पत्सुतःऽशीः । बभूव ॥ ८ ॥ nadam | na | bhinnam | amuyā | śayānam | manaḥ | ruhāṇāḥ | ati | yanti | āpaḥ | yāḥ | cit | vṛtraḥ | mahinā | pari-atiṣṭhat | tāsām | ahiḥ | patsutaḥ-śīḥ | babhūva || 8 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : अमुयामुष्यां पृथिव्यां शयानं पतितं मृतं वृत्रमापो जलान्यतियन्ति । अतिक्रम्य गच्छन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । भिन्नं बहुधाभिन्नकूलं नदं न सिन्धुमिव । यथा वृष्टिकाले प्रभूता आपो नद्याः कूलं भित्वातिक्रम्य गच्छन्ति तद्वत् । कीदृश आपः । मनो रुहाणाः । नॄणां चित्तमारोहन्त्यः । पुरा वृत्रे जीवति सति तेन निरुद्धा मेघस्थिता आपो भूमौ वृष्ट्वा न भवन्ति । तदानीं नॄणां मनः खिद्यते । मृते तु वृत्रे निरोधरहिता आपो वृत्रशरीरमुल्लङ्घ्य प्रवहन्ति । तदा वृष्टिलाभेन तु मनुष्यास्तुष्यन्तीत्यर्थः । तदेतदुत्तरार्धेन स्पष्टीक्रियते । वृत्रो जीवनदशायां महिना स्वकीयेन महिम्ना याश्चिद्या एव मेघगता अपः पर्यतिष्ठत् परिवृत्य स्थितवान् अहिर्वृत्रो मेघस्तासामपां पत्सुतःशीः पादस्याधःशयानो … amuyāmuṣyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ śayānaṃ patitaṃ mṛtaṃ vṛtramāpo jalānyatiyanti | atikramya gacchanti | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | bhinnaṃ bahudhābhinnakūlaṃ nadaṃ na sindhumiva | yathā vṛṣṭikāle prabhūtā āpo nadyāḥ kūlaṃ bhitvātikramya gacchanti tadvat | kīdṛśa āpaḥ | mano ruhāṇāḥ | nṝṇāṃ cittamārohantyaḥ | purā vṛtre jīvati sati tena niruddhā meghasthitā āpo bhūmau vṛṣṭvā na bhavanti | tadānīṃ nṝṇāṃ manaḥ khidyate | mṛte tu vṛtre nirodharahitā āpo vṛtraśarīramullaṅghya pravahanti | tadā vṛṣṭilābhena tu manuṣyāstuṣyantītyarthaḥ | tadetaduttarārdhena spaṣṭīkriyate | vṛtro jīvanadaśāyāṃ mahinā svakīyena mahimnā yāścidyā eva meghagatā apaḥ paryatiṣṭhat parivṛtya sthitavān ahirvṛtro meghastāsāmapāṃ patsutaḥśīḥ pādasyādhaḥśayāno … "The waters flow over (ati yanti) Vṛtra, who lies (śayānam) dead on this earth (amuyā), as [the waters] go over a river-bank that has been broken (bhinnam nadam na) in many places: as in the rainy season abundant waters break through and go over a river's banks, so. How are the waters? Mano ruhāṇāḥ — rising into [pleasing] the minds of men: formerly, while Vṛtra lived, the waters held back by him in the cloud did not rain down on the earth; then men's minds were pained; but when Vṛtra was dead, the waters, free of obstruction, leapt over Vṛtra's body and flowed on; then, at the gain of rain, men are glad: this is the meaning. This is made clear by the second half [of the Ṛk]: Vṛtra in his lifetime, by his own greatness (mahinā), had stood around (pari atiṣṭhat) those very waters that were in the cloud; Ahi, Vṛtra, the cloud, lying beneath the feet (patsutaḥśīḥ) of those waters …"

(Grammatical tail: bhinnam — na by radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ (P. 8-2-42); amuyā — yā for the locative ending by supāṃ suluk; śayānam — guṇa by śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ (P. 7-4-21), the root accent; ruhāṇāḥ — śānac and the śa-vikaraṇa by vyatyaya, no muk since augment-rules are not constant, the root accent by vyatyaya; mahinā — in by in sarvadhātubhyaḥ (Uṇ. 4-117), acute ending by vyatyaya; or = mahimnā, imanic by pṛthvādibhya imanij vā (P. 5-1-122), ṭi-loss, end-acute as cit, the ending acute after the loss of a, the m dropped in Vedic usage; patsutaḥśīḥ — 'one who lies below the foot', kvip, pad for pāda by paddan… (the word prabhṛti in śasprabhṛtiṣu means 'kind', Kā. 6-1-63), the inserted su Vedic; or tasil in the locative sense by itarābhyo 'pi dṛśyante (P. 5-3-14) after the locative plural, the ending not dropped in the Veda.)"

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ अमुया (amuyā) — on this earth | शयानम् (śayānam) — lying dead, Vṛtra | मनोरुहाणाः (manoruhāṇāḥ) — [the waters] that attract the mind | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters | भिन्नम् (bhinnam) — [with] its bank broken in many places | नदम् न (nadam na) — like a river | अति यन्ति (ati yanti) — flow over [and go] | वृत्रम् (vṛtram) — Vṛtra [while he lived] | महिना (mahinā) — by his [own] power | याः चित् (yāḥ cit) — [of] whatever [waters of the clouds] | पर्यतिष्ठत् (paryatiṣṭhat) — stood around [stopping them] | अहिः (ahiḥ) — that cloud-form Vṛtra | तासाम् आपाम् (tāsām āpām) — of those very waters | पत्सुतःशीः (patsutaḥśīḥ) — [one] lying under the feet | बभूव (babhūva) — became.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Vṛtra lies dead upon the earth. The waters, attractive to the minds of men, flow wherever they like and in full abundance over him, like a river that has burst its banks and flows over them in many places. In his lifetime, by his strength, he held back the waters of the clouds so that they did not fall on the earth below; now he lies dead beneath those same waters.

॥ English Translation ॥

The waters that delight the minds of men flow over him as a river bursts forth its broken banks ; Ahi (Vritra) has been prostrated beneath the feet of the waters which he had obstructed by his strength.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अमुया शयानं अति यन्ति (amuyā śayānam ati yanti) — [the waters] going past, over Vṛtra, who lies dead on this earth. मनोरुहाणाः (manoruhāṇāḥ) — making delight to the mind: since Vṛtra had kept back the clouds, people were wretched in mind for lack of rain; after the killing of Vṛtra the water runs on [freely], flows without minding the banks, breaking them and flowing, and gives men's minds joy: so the commentator explains the words mano ruhāṇāḥ. महिना पर्यतिष्ठत् (mahinā paryatiṣṭhat) — [the waters] which Vṛtra, by his very great power, had obstructed. पत्सुतःशीः (patsutaḥśīḥ) — pādasyādhaḥ śete: [one] who lies at the foot; or who is thrown down. When it is said here that the waters have feet, the meaning is that, as the waters flow over him, he must be said to lie beneath the water; this idea is put as 'in the region of the feet of the water', that is, 'in the lower part'.

Grammar pages 617–618, noted briefly, from the print: bhinnam — bhidir vidāraṇe, kta; n for t by radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ pūrvasya ca daḥ (Pā. sū. 8-2-42); amuyā — adas, locative singular, yā-substitute by supāṃ suluk…, tyadādīnām aḥ, ato guṇe (pararūpa), adaso 'ser dād u do maḥ; śayānam — śīṅ svapne, śānac, ṅit by apit, guṇa restored by śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ (Pā. sū. 7-4-21), eco 'yavāyāvaḥ, unaccented affix by tāsy anudāttet…, the root's end-acute; ruhāṇāḥ — śānac by vyatyaya (the root being parasmaipadin), the śa-vikaraṇa for kartari śap, no guṇa, āne muk not applied (āgamaśāsanam anityam), ṇatva by aṭ-kupvāṅ…, the root accent by vyatyaya; mahinā — in sarvadhātubhyaḥ, acute ending by vyatyaya; or mahimnā, tasya bhāvaḥ, imanic by pṛthvādibhya imanij vā (Pā. sū. 5-1-122), ṭeḥ, citaḥ, allopo 'naḥ, anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ; patsutaḥśīḥ — kvip ca, sarvalopa, pad for pāda by paddan-no-mās…, prabhṛti = 'kind' as the commentators explain (Kā. 6-1-63), the augment su Vedic; or tasil by itarābhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. sū. 5-3-14), no luk in the Veda. The print gives only these five numbers; ends ॥ ८ ॥.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : वृत्रपुत्रा वृत्रः पुत्रो यस्या मातुः सेयं माता वृत्रपुत्रा नीचावया न्यग्भावं प्राप्ता हताभवत् । पुत्रं प्रहाराद्रक्षितुं पुत्रदेहस्योपरि तिरश्ची पतितवतीत्यर्थः । तदानीमयमिन्द्रोऽस्या मातुरवाधोभागे वृत्रस्योपरि वधो हननसाधनमायुधं जभार । प्रहृतवान् । तदानीं सूर्मातोत्तरोपरिस्थितासीत् । पुत्रस्त्वधोभागस्थित आसीत् । सा च दानुर्दानवी वृत्रमाता शये । मृता शयनं कृतवती । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । धेनुर्लोकप्रसिद्धा गौः सहवत्सा न । यथा वत्ससहिता शयनं करोति तद्वत् ॥ नीचावयाः । वेति खादतीति वयो बाहुः । औणादिकोऽसिप्रत्ययः । न्यञ्चौ वयसौ यस्याः सा नीचावयाः । न्यच्शब्दादुत्तरस्या विभक्तेः सुपां सुपो भवन्तीति तृतीयैकवचनादेशः । अच इत्यकारलोपे चाविति दीर्घत्वम् । अञ्चेश्छन्दस्यसर्वनामस्थानम् । पा ६-१-१७० । इति तस्योदात्तत्वम् । समासे लुगभावश्छान्दसः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । यद्वा । नीचौ निकृष्टौ वयसौ यस्याः सा । पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घश्छान्दसः । वधः । हन्यतेऽनेनेति वधः । असुनि हन्तेर्वधादेशः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । जभार । हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वम् । सूः । षूङ् प्राणिगर्भविमोचने । सूते vṛtraḥ putro yasyā mātuḥ seyaṃ mātā vṛtraputrā nīcāvayā nyagbhāvaṃ prāptā hatābhavat | putraṃ prahārādrakṣituṃ putradehasyopari tiraścī patitavatītyarthaḥ | tadānīmayamindro 'syā māturavādhobhāge dṛṣṭāntaḥ | dhenurlokaprasiddhā gauḥ sahavatsā na | yathā vatsasahitā śayanaṃ karoti tadvat ‖ nīcāvayāḥ | veti khādatīti vayo bāhuḥ | auṇādiko 'sipratyayaḥ | nyañcau vayasau yasyāḥ sā nīcāvayāḥ | nyacśabdāduttarasyā vibhakteḥ supāṃ supo bhavantīti tṛtīyaikavacanādeśaḥ | aca ityakāralope cāviti dīrghatvam | añceśchandasyasarvanāmasthānam | pā 6-1-170 | iti tasyodāttatvam | samāse lugabhāvaśchāndasaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | yadvā | nīcau nikṛṣṭau vayasau yasyāḥ sā | pūrvapadasya dīrghaśchāndasaḥ | vadhaḥ | hanyate 'neneti vadhaḥ | asuni hantervadhādeśaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvam | jabhāra | hṛgrahorbha iti bhatvam | sūḥ | ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane | sūte garbhaṃ vimuñcatīti sūrmātā | kvipceti kvip | dānuḥ | do avakhaṇḍane | dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ | u. 3-32 | śaye | laṭi lopasta ātmanepadeṣu | pā. 7-1-41 | iti talopaḥ | śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke iti guṇe 'yādeśaḥ ‖ "Vṛtra's mother — she whose son was Vṛtra — became nīcāvayāḥ ('with bowed-down arms'): reduced to a lowly posture, she was struck down. To protect her son from the blow, she fell across his body, bending over him. Then Indra dashed (jabhāra) the vadha — the instrument of killing, the weapon — on the lower part of this mother, on top of Vṛtra. At that time the mother (sūḥ) was above, [and] the son was below; and she, the dānu, the Dānavī, Vṛtra's mother,, lay (śaye) dead, as a cow, well known in the world, lies down with its calf (sahavatsā). (Grammatical tail: nīcāvayāḥ — vayas = 'arm' (veti khādatīti), the Uṇādi asi; nyañcau vayasau yasyāḥ; the instrumental-singular substitute by supāṃ supo bhavanti, loss of a and lengthening, the ending acute by añceś chandasy asarvanāmasthānam (P. 6-1-170); no luk in the compound, a Vedic usage; bahuvrīhi first-member accent; or nīcau nikṛṣṭau vayasau yasyāḥ, the lengthening Vedic; vadhaḥ — hanyate 'neneti, asun with vadha for han, initial acute as nit; jabhāra — bh by hṛgrahor bhaḥ; sūḥ — ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane, 'she who brings forth', the mother, kvip; dānuḥ — do avakhaṇḍane, nu by dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ (Uṇ. 3-32); śaye — loss of t by lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu (P. 7-1-41), guṇa and ay.)"

Grammar pages 621–622, noted briefly, from the print: nīcāvayāḥ — the instrumental-singular substitute by supāṃ supo bhavanti, acaḥ (loss of a), cau (lengthening), the ending acute by añceś chandasy asarvanāmasthānam (Pā. sū. 6-1-170); luk prevented by vyatyayo bahulam; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam; or nīcau nikṛṣṭau vayasau yasyāḥ, the first member lengthened in the Veda, the nipāta's end-acute kept; vadhaḥ — sarvadhātubhyo 'sun, vadha for han, ato lopaḥ, initial acute by ñnity ādir nityam; jabhāra — hṛñ haraṇe, liṭ, ṇal, doubling, urat, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cutva, vṛddhi, uraṇ raparaḥ, bh by hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi, nighāta after a non-verb; sūḥ — ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane, kvip by kvip ca (Pā. sū. 3-2-76), kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca, end-acute by the root accent; dānuḥ — do avakhaṇḍane, ād eca upadeśe 'śiti, nu by dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ (U. sū. 3-312; the bhāṣya prints उ. ३-३२ (u. 3-32)); śaye — śīṅ svapne, laṭ, ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere, t dropped by lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu (Pā. sū. 7-1-41), guṇa by śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ (Pā. sū. 7-4-21), eco 'yavāyāvaḥ, nighāta by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ; sahavatsā — bahuvrīhau…, first-member accent. The print gives only these numbers; ends ॥ ९ ॥.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वृत्रपुत्रा (vṛtraputrā) — the mother who had Vṛtra for her son | नीचावयाः (nīcāvayāḥ) — with strength gone [with arms drooping] | अभवत् (abhavat) — became [struck down] | इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra | अस्याः (asyāḥ) — of this [mother] | अव (ava) — in the lower part | वधः (vadhaḥ) — the weapon | जभार (jabhāra) — struck | सूः (sūḥ) — the mother | उत्तरा (uttarā) — became the upper one | पुत्रः (putraḥ) — the son, Vṛtra | अधरः (adharaḥ) — [the lower one] | आसीत् (āsīt) — was | दानुः (dānuḥ) — the demoness [Vṛtra's mother] | शये (śaye) — lay [dead] | सहवत्सा न धेनुः (sahavatsā na dhenuḥ) — like a cow with her calf.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ When Indra was killing Vṛtra, Vṛtra's mother came to protect her son, for fear of the vajra's blow. Indra then struck her strength, hitting her on the lower part of her body, and she fell over her son. After the vajra had hit her, the mother was above and the son below; he lay beneath her, and the demoness lay dead together with her son Vṛtra, as a cow lies with her calf.

॥ English Translation ॥

The mother of Vritra was bending over her son when Indra struck her lower part with his thunderbolt ; so the mother was above and the son underneath and the demoness (Vritra's mother) with her son slept (or lay dead) like a cow with its calf.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ नीचावयाः (nīcāvayāḥ) — veti khādatīti vayo bāhuḥ: 'arm'; one whose arms hang down [pralambabāhuḥ], nyañcau vayasau yasyāḥ sā: 'one with drooping arms'. She, to protect her son against the blow, spread over her son's body across it, her arms outspread: that is the sense. वृत्रपुत्रा (vṛtraputrā) — the woman who has Vṛtra for her son; that is, Vṛtra's mother. वधर्जभार (vadhar jabhāra) — hananasādhanam āyudhaṃ prahṛtavān: he used a weapon for the killing. उत्तरा सूः (uttarā sūḥ) — ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane: sūḥ is the mother who gives birth to Vṛtra. She lay across her body above Vṛtra. अधरः पुत्र आसीत् (adharaḥ putra āsīt) — her son Vṛtra was beneath: that is, he lay dead beneath. दानुः (dānuḥ) — a daughter of Danu. Those of the race of rākṣasas who were born of Kaśyapa's wife called Danu are named dānava. Vṛtra's mother, belonging to that dānava tribe, is here called dānu. शये (śaye) — 'lay down': that is, she lay dead. सहवत्सा न धेनुः (sahavatsā na dhenuḥ) — the simile: as a cow lies near her calf, so Vṛtra's mother lay near her son, the demon Vṛtra.

Rik 10 pp. 623–626

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

अति॑ष्ठन्तीनामनिवेश॒नानां॒ काष्ठा॑नां॒ मध्ये॒ निहि॑तं॒ शरी॑रं । [accent ?] वृ॒त्रस्य॑ नि॒ण्यं वि च॑र॒न्त्यापो॑ दी॒र्घं तम॒ आश॑य॒दिन्द्र॑शत्रुः ॥ १० ॥

átiṣṭhantīnām aniveśanā́nāṃ kā́ṣṭhānāṃ mádhye níhitaṃ śárīraṃ | [accent ?] vṛtrásya niṇyáṃ ví caranty ā́po dīrgháṃ tama ā́śayad índraśatruḥ || 10 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 1: the stroke of शरीरं (śarīraṃ) stands at the junction of श and री; set on री.

Pada-pāṭha: अतिष्ठन्तीनाम् । अनिऽवेशनानाम् । काष्ठानाम् । मध्ये । निऽहितम् । शरीरम् । वृत्रस्य । निण्यम् । वि । चरन्ति । आपः । दीर्घम् । तमः । आ । अशयत् । इन्द्रऽशत्रुः ॥ १० ॥ atiṣṭhantīnām | ani-veśanānām | kāṣṭhānām | madhye | ni-hitam | śarīram | vṛtrasya | niṇyam | vi | caranti | āpaḥ | dīrgham | tamaḥ | ā | aśayat | indra-śatruḥ || 10 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : वृत्रस्य शरीरमापो वि चरन्ति । विशेषेणोपर्युत्क्रम्य प्रवहन्ति । कीदृशं शरीरम् । निण्यं निर्णामधेयम् । अप्सु मग्नत्वेन गूढत्वात्तदीयं नाम न केनापि ज्ञायते । एतदेव स्पष्टीक्रियते । काष्ठानामपां मध्ये निहितं निक्षिप्तम् । कीदृशानां काष्ठानाम् । अतिष्ठन्तीनां स्थितिरहितानाम् । अनिवेशनानामुपवेशनरहितानाम् । प्रवहणस्वभावत्वादेतासां मनुष्यवन्न क्वापि स्थितिः सम्भवति । इन्द्रशत्रुर्वृत्रो जलमध्ये शरीरे प्रक्षिप्ते सति दीर्घं तमो दीर्घं निद्रात्मकं मरणं यथा भवति तथा आशयत् । सर्वतः पतितवान् ॥ आतिष्ठन्तीनाम् [= अतिष्ठन्तीनाम्] । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अनिवेशनानाम् । निविशन्तेऽस्मिन्निति निवेशनं स्थानम् । करणाधिकरणयोश्चेति [ल्युट्] । तद्रहितानाम् । बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । क्रान्त्वा स्थिताः काष्ठाः । पृषोदरादि । निहितम् । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥ अत्र यास्कः । the closing grammatical and Nirukta lines are on p. 624, below vṛtrasya śarīram āpo vi caranti | viśeṣeṇopary utkramya pravahanti | kīdṛśaṃ śarīram | niṇyaṃ nirnāmadheyam | apsu magnatvena gūḍhatvāt tadīyaṃ nāma na kenāpi jñāyate | etad eva spaṣṭīkriyate | kāṣṭhānām apāṃ madhye nihitaṃ nikṣiptam | kīdṛśānāṃ kāṣṭhānām | atiṣṭhantīnāṃ sthitirahitānām | aniveśanānām upaveśanarahitānām | pravahaṇasvabhāvatvād etāsāṃ manuṣyavan na kvāpi sthitiḥ sambhavati | indraśatrur vṛtro jalamadhye śarīre prakṣipte sati dīrghaṃ tamo dīrghaṃ nidrātmakaṃ maraṇaṃ yathā bhavati tathā āśayat | sarvataḥ patitavān || "The waters flow over (vi caranti) Vṛtra's body — rising above it in particular. What body? Niṇyam — 'nameless': since it is hidden by being submerged in the waters, its name is known to no one. This is made clear: [the body] lies in the midst of the kāṣṭhās — the waters. What waters? Atiṣṭhantīnām — never standing still; aniveśanānām — without a resting-place: since it is the nature of these to flow, they have no rest anywhere as human beings do. Vṛtra, the enemy of Indra, with his body cast in the midst of the water, lay (āśayat) in a long darkness (dīrgham tamaḥ) — in a long sleep-like death; he fell on all sides."

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, closing lines p. 624, top: अतिष्ठन्तीनामनिविशमानानामित्यस्थावराणां काष्ठानां मध्ये निहितं शरीरं मेघः । शरीरं शृणातेः शम्नातेर्वा । वृत्रस्य निण्यं निर्णामं विचरन्ति विजानन्त्याप इति दीर्घं द्राघतेस्तमस्तनोतेराशयदाशेतेरिन्द्रशत्रुरिन्द्रोऽस्य शमयिता वा शातयिता वा तस्मादिन्द्रशत्रुः । तत्को वृत्रो मेघ इति नैरुक्तास्त्वाष्ट्रोऽसुर इत्यैतिहासिकाः ॥ नि. २. १६ । इति ॥ ॥ ३७ ॥ atiṣṭhantīnāmaniviśamānānāmityasthāvarāṇāṃ kāṣṭhānāṃ madhye nihitaṃ śarīraṃ meghaḥ | śarīraṃ śṛṇāteḥ śamnātervā | vṛtrasya niṇyaṃ nirṇāmaṃ vicaranti vijānantyāpa iti dīrghaṃ drāghatestamastanoterāśayadāśeterindraśatrurindro 'sya śamayitā vā śātayitā vā tasmādindraśatruḥ | tatko vṛtro megha iti nairuktāstvāṣṭro 'sura ityaitihāsikāḥ ‖ ni. 2. 16 | iti ‖ ‖ 37 ‖ "[Yāska:] 'Atiṣṭhantīnām aniviśamānānām, that is, of the non-stationary — in the midst of the waters (kāṣṭhānām) is placed the body, the cloud. Śarīra from śṝ or from śam. Vṛtrasya niṇyam: the nameless [body] of Vṛtra the waters move over (vicaranti), i.e. know (vijānanti). Dīrgham from drāgh, tamas from tan, āśayat from ā-śī. Indraśatruḥ: Indra is its pacifier or its destroyer, hence indraśatruḥ. Who then is Vṛtra? The cloud, say the etymologists; the asura, son of Tvaṣṭṛ, say the historians' (Ni. 2. 16). [End of Varga 37.]" Mine, tentative.

(Grammar page 626, noted briefly: atiṣṭhantīnām — na tiṣṭhanti, a negative compound; the first member (nañ) is an avyaya, so the avyaya-first accent by Pā. sū. 6-2-2 tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ; the a* is acute;* aniveśanānām — niviśante 'smin iti niveśanam sthānam; viś praveśane; lyuṭ* by Pā. sū. 3-3-117 karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca; yu → ana; guṇa of the light penult by the root's ārdhadhātuka ending; na vidyate niveśanaṃ yeṣāṃ tāni aniveśanāni, a bahuvrīhi; the end-acute of the second member by Pā. sū. 6-2-172 nañsubhyām;* kāṣṭhānām — the genitive plural; krāntvā sthitāḥ kāṣṭhāḥ* — by Pā. sū. 6-3-109 pṛṣodarādīni yathopadiṣṭam the word is established; other processes are made by nipātana;* nihitam — ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; kta* in the passive; by dadhāter hiḥ (Pā. sū. 7-4-42) hi for the root before the t-initial suffix: hita; the end-acute through the suffix; compounded with the gati ni by gatir anantaraḥ so the prefix keeps its accent. Yāska (as above) gives a different explanation: the two qualifiers atiṣṭhantīnām and aniveśanānām indicate that the things in question are not stationary; they are the kāṣṭhā [waters] among which the body — i.e. the cloud — lies; śarīra from śṝ hiṃsāyām with an Uṇādi affix: 'what is destroyed or perishes'; vṛtrasya niṇyam = nirṇāmam; vicaranti = vijānanti, since verbs of motion also have the sense of knowing; dīrgha from drāgh sāmarthye; tamas from tan vistāre; āśayat from śīṅ svapne; indraśatruḥ — 'Indra is its (Vṛtra's) pacifier or destroyer' [the root śam / śad with ṇic], or 'of whom Indra is the enemy'; tatko vṛtro megha iti: Yāska says successively that the cloud is Vṛtra [nairuktāḥ]; the historians say the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, a demon, is Vṛtra (Niru. 2-16).) The print gives only Pā. sū. 6-2-2, 3-3-117, 6-2-172, 6-3-109, 7-4-42 and Niru. 2-16; ends ॥ १० ॥.*

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वृत्रस्य (vṛtrasya) — of the demon Vṛtra | निण्यम् (niṇyam) — [which because it is sunk in the water, no one knows] the name of him | शरीरम् (śarīram) — the body | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters | वि चरन्ति (vi caranti) — flow over | अतिष्ठन्तीनाम् (atiṣṭhantīnām) — [which are] not stopping a little | अनिवेशनानाम् (aniveśanānām) — [and] without rest [that flow always] | काष्ठानाम् (kāṣṭhānām) — of the waters | मध्ये (madhye) — in the midst | निहितम् (nihitam) — [Vṛtra's body is] cast | इन्द्रशत्रुः (indraśatruḥ) — Indra's enemy Vṛtra | दीर्घं तमः (dīrghaṃ tamaḥ) — a long death-like sleep | आ अशयत् (ā aśayat) — attained.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ Because Vṛtra has sunk in the water, no one even knows his name, and the waters flow over his body. In the midst of the currents — which never stand still a little and never rest, ever flowing on — his body lies cast down; and Indra's enemy Vṛtra has attained a long sleep, death-like and in the form of darkness.

॥ English Translation ॥

The waters flow over the nameless body of Vritra placed in the midst of the never stopping, never-resting currents ; the enemy of Indra has slept (lay dead) an endless darkness.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अतिष्ठन्तीनाम् (atiṣṭhantīnām) — not standing in one place, that is, flowing. अनिवेशनानाम् (aniveśanānām) — satataṃ gacchantīnām: always going forward. The two words atiṣṭhantīnām and aniveśanānām indicate meanings which are the same, with a slight addition or deficiency. काष्ठानां मध्ये (kāṣṭhānāṃ madhye) — the word kāṣṭhā is read among the waters: āpo 'pi kāṣṭhā ucyante — 'the waters too are called kāṣṭhā' (Ni. 2-16); kāṣṭhā means water, running water; kāṣṭhānāṃ madhye means 'in the midst of the current of the water'. निण्यम् (niṇyam) — nirṇāmam (Ni. 2-16); niṇyaṃ suśuṣkaḥ — among the six words beginning nirṇītāntarhita, the word niṇya is read (Ni. 3-19); niṇya means 'hidden' or 'concealed', not visible, hidden inside. Because Vṛtra's body is under the water, it is hidden and no one sees it. वि चरन्त्यापः (vi caranty āpaḥ) — the water runs over in streams. दीर्घं तम आ अशयत् इन्द्रशत्रुः (dīrghaṃ tama ā aśayat indraśatruḥ) — Vṛtra, Indra's enemy, lay in a long, that is, an endless darkness — that is, he attained death in the form of darkness, he lay dead. Yāska's etymology of this rik is as given above in the bhāṣya's closing lines; of it the Kannada says: āsthāvarāṇām ['of the not-standing'] — those that move constantly; kāṣṭhānāṃ madhye nihitaṃ śarīram — the body of Vṛtra in the midst of the waters, that is, the cloud: the cloud, because it is moved by the wind in the sky, always moves, and so the two qualifiers atiṣṭhantīnām aniveśanānām are used; śarīram — so called because it is destroyed (the cloud is destroyed or scattered by the wind) — the print continues with niṇyam = nirṇāmam: 'they go on, knowing [by vijānanti, a root of motion with the sense of knowing]; dīrgham — from drāgh vṛddhyarthaḥ: growing; tamaḥ — from tan: spreading, since darkness spreads over everything; āśayat — from ā + śīṅ: he lay down, that is, died, or fell below; indraśatruḥ — [so called] because Indra subdues or destroys him.

Rik 11 pp. 627–633

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

दा॒सप॑त्नी॒रहि॑गोपा अतिष्ठ॒न्निरु॑द्धा॒ आपः॑ प॒णिने॑व॒ गावः॑ । अ॒पां बिल॒मपि॑हितं॒ यदासी॑द्वृ॒त्रं ज॑घ॒न्वाँ अप॒ तद्व॑वार ॥ ११ ॥ [accent ?]

dāsápatnīr áhigopā atiṣṭhan níruddhā ā́paḥ paṇíneva gā́vaḥ | apā́ṃ bilam ápihitaṃ yád ā́sīd vṛtráṃ jaghanvā́m̐ apa tád vavāra || 11 || [accent ?] Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 2: the stroke of जघन्वाँ (jaghanvām̐) stands at the junction of ज and घ, with a bar under घ; set as printed.

Pada-pāṭha: दासऽपत्नीः । अहिऽगोपाः । अतिष्ठन् । निऽरुद्धाः । आपः । पणिनाऽइव । गावः । अपाम् । बिलम् । अपिऽहितम् । यत् । आसीत् । वृत्रम् । जघन्वान् । अप । तत् । ववार ॥ ११ ॥ dāsa-patnīḥ | ahi-gopāḥ | atiṣṭhan | ni-ruddhāḥ | āpaḥ | paṇinā-iva | gāvaḥ | apām | bilam | api-hitam | yat | āsīt | vṛtram | jaghanvān | apa | tat | vavāra || 11 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : दासपत्नीः । दासो विश्वोपक्षपणहेतुर्वृत्रः पतिः स्वामी यासामपां ता दासपत्नीः । अत एवाहिगोपाः । अहिर्वृत्रो गोपा रक्षको यासां ताः । गोपनं नाम स्वच्छन्देन यथा न प्रवहन्ति तथा निरोधनम् । एतदेव स्पष्टीक्रियते । आपो निरुद्धा अतिष्ठन्निति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । पणिनेव गावः । पणिनामकोऽसुरो गा अपहृत्य बिले स्थापयित्वा बिलद्वारमाच्छाद्य यथा निरुद्धवांस्तथेत्यर्थः । अपां यद्बिलं प्रवहणद्वारमपिहितं वृत्रेण निरुद्धमासीत् तद्बिलं प्रवहणद्वारं वृत्रं जघन्वान्हतवानिन्द्रोऽप ववार । अपवृतमकरोत् । वृत्रकृतमपां निरोधं परिहृतवान् । अत्र यास्कः । दासपत्नीर्दासाधिपत्न्यो दासो दस्यतेरुपदासयति कर्माण्यहिगोपा अतिष्ठन्नहिना गुप्ताः । अहिरयनादेत्यन्तरिक्षेऽयमपीतरोऽहिरेतस्मादेव निर्ह्रसितोपसर्ग आहन्तीति । निरुद्धा आपः पणिनेव गावः । पणिर्वणिग्भवति पणिः पणनाद्वणिक् पण्यं नेनेक्ति । अपां बिलमपिहितं यदासीत् । बिलं भरं भवति बिभर्तेर्वृत्रं जघ्निवानपववार तद्वृत्रो वृणोतेर्वा वर्ततेर्वा वर्धतेर्वा यदवृणोत्तद्वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वमिति विज्ञायते । यदवर्तत तद्वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वमिति विज्ञायते । यदवर्धत तद्वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वमिति विज्ञायते । नि २. १७ । इति ॥ दासपत्नीः । दसु उपक्षये । दासयतीति दासो वृत्रः । पचाद्यच् । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । दासः पतिर्यासां विभाषा सपूर्वस्य । पा. ४. १. ३४ । इति ङीप् । तत्संनियोगेनेकारस्य नकारः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । यद्वा । दासस्य पालयित्र्यः । पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । अहिगोपाः । गुपू रक्षणे । गोपायतीति गोपाः । आयादय आर्धधातुके वा । पा. ३. १. ३१ । इत्यायप्रत्ययः । ततः क्विप् । अतो लोपः । वेरपृक्तलोपाद्वलि लोपो बलीयानिति पूर्वं यकारलोपः । पा. ६. १. ६६-६७ । न चाचः परस्मिन्नित्यतो लोपस्य स्थानिवत्त्वम् । न पदान्तद्विर्वचनेति प्रतिषेधात् । अहिर्गोपा यासाम् । पूर्ववत्स्वरः । निरुद्धाः । रुधिर् आवरणे । झषस्तथोर्धोऽधः । पा. ८. २. ४० । इति निष्ठातकारस्य धकारः । गतिरनन्तर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । जघन्वान् । हन्तेर्लिटः क्वसुः । अभ्यासाच्च । पा. ७. ३. ५५ । इत्यभ्यासादुत्तरस्य हकारस्य कुत्वम् । क्रादिनियमप्राप्तस्येटो विभाषा गमहनेत्यादिना । पा. ७. २. ६८ । विकल्पविधानादभावः । संहितायां नकारस्य | niruddhāḥ | rudhir āvaraṇe | jhaṣastathordho 'dhaḥ | pā. 8. 2. 40 | iti niṣṭhātakārasya dhakāraḥ | gatiranantara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvam | jaghanvān | hanterliṭaḥ kvasuḥ | abhyāsācca | pā. 7. 3. 55 | ityabhyāsāduttarasya hakārasya kutvam | krādiniyamaprāptasyeṭo vibhāṣā gamahanetyādinā | pā. 7. 2. 68 | vikalpavidhānādabhāvaḥ | saṃhitāyāṃ nakārasya rutvānunāsikāvuktau ‖ "The waters, whose lord (pati) was the dāsa — Vṛtra, the cause of the destruction of all (viśvopakṣapaṇahetuḥ) — are dāsapatnīḥ ['the wives of the dāsa']; therefore ahigopāḥ — their guardian [gopā] was Vṛtra, the serpent (ahi). 'Guarding' here means holding them back so that they cannot flow freely. This is made plain: the waters stood confined (niruddhāḥ), as cows confined by a Paṇi — as the asura named Paṇi stole the cows, placed them in a cave, shut the mouth of the cave and kept them in. The cave (bilam) of the waters — the passage of their flowing — which had been closed (apihitam), shut by Vṛtra: that opening Indra, having killed Vṛtra, uncovered (apa vavāra); he removed the confinement of the waters that Vṛtra had made. [Yāska explains the words dāsapatnīḥ, ahigopāḥ, niruddhā āpaḥ paṇineva gāvaḥ, bilam and vṛtra as in the passage above (Ni. 2. 17; ahi from ayana, 'going', in the sky, or from ā-han with the prefix shortened; the Paṇi a trader, paṇa from paṇana; bila from bhṛ); vṛtra from vṛ ('to cover'), vṛt ('to be') or vṛdh ('to grow'), because he covered, was, or grew: three etymologies of vṛtra-tva.] (Grammatical tail: dāsapatnīḥ — dasu upakṣaye, dāsa 'who destroys' = Vṛtra, ac of the pacādi group, end-acute as cit; ṅīp by vibhāṣā sapūrvasya (P. 4. 1. 34) with n for the final; bahuvrīhi first-member accent, or ('protectresses of the dāsa') the same by patyāv aiśvarye; ahigopāḥ — gupū rakṣaṇe, āya by āyādaya ārdhadhātuke vā (P. 3. 1. 31), kvip, ato lopaḥ, the y dropped first (P. 6. 1. 66–67), its sthānivattva barred by na padāntadvirvacana…; niruddhāḥ — dh for the niṣṭhā t by jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ (P. 8. 2. 40), the gati accent; jaghanvān — kvasu for liṭ, kutva of the h by abhyāsāc ca (P. 7. 3. 55), no iṭ by vibhāṣā gamahana… (P. 7. 2. 68); in the Saṃhitā rutva and nasalisation.)"

Grammar pages 631–633, noted briefly, from the print: dāsapatnīḥ — dasu upakṣaye, dāsayatīti dāsaḥ = Vṛtra, ac in the pacādi group by nandigrahapacādibhyaḥ…, end-acute by citaḥ; dāsaḥ patir yāsāṃ tāḥ: ṅīp by vibhāṣā sapūrvasya (Pā. sū. 4-1-34) with n for the i; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam; or dāsasya pālayitryaḥ, a genitive tatpuruṣa, first-member accent by patyāv aiśvarye (Pā. sū. 6-2-18); ahigopāḥ — gupū rakṣaṇe, āya by āyādaya ārdhadhātuke vā (Pā. sū. 3-1-31), sanādyantā dhātavaḥ, kvip ca, ato lopaḥ, ver apṛktasya, lopo vyor vali, the y dropped first by ver apṛktalopād valilopo balīyān, the objection from acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau answered by na padāntadvirvacana… yalopa… (Pā. sū. 1-1-58); bahuvrīhau…; niruddhāḥ — rudhir āvaraṇe, kta, dh by jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ (Pā. sū. 8-2-40), gatir anantaraḥ; jaghanvān — han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, kvasu by kvasuś ca (Pā. sū. 3-2-107), doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cutva, kutva by abhyāsāc ca (Pā. sū. 7-3-55), iṭ optional by vibhāṣā gamahana… (Pā. sū. 7-2-68) and not taken; ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ (num), atvasantasya (lengthening), halṅyābbhyaḥ (s-loss), saṃyogāntasya (final s), na lopaḥ… blocked; in the Saṃhitā rutva by dīrghād aṭi samānapāde and nasalisation by āto 'ṭi nityam. The print gives only these numbers; ends ॥ ११ ॥.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ दासपत्नीः (dāsapatnīḥ) — [the waters of which] the destroyer Vṛtra was the lord | अहिगोपाः (ahigopāḥ) — [and] of which Vṛtra [as the obstructor] was the guardian | आपः (āpaḥ) — the waters | पणिना (paṇinā) — by the asura called Paṇi | गावः इव (gāvaḥ iva) — like cows [stolen] | निरुद्धाः (niruddhāḥ) — [being] confined | अतिष्ठन् (atiṣṭhan) — stood | अपाम् (apām) — of the waters | यत् बिलम् (yat bilam) — which opening [a passage for the flow] | अपिहितम् आसीत् (apihitam āsīt) — was closed [by Vṛtra] | तत् (tat) — that [opening] | वृत्रम् जघन्वान् (vṛtram jaghanvān) — Indra, having killed Vṛtra | अप ववार (apa vavāra) — opened [so that the flow might not be obstructed].

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ The waters, in the guard of Vṛtra, who had taken the form of the wives of the destroyer, stood confined as cows are bound by the asura Paṇi. When Vṛtra closed the opening — the passage by which the waters flow — Indra killed him and opened that passage so that the waters could flow free.

॥ English Translation ॥

The waters, the wives of the destroyer (Vritra) guarded by Ahi had stood confined like cows confined by Panin (robber) ; by slaying Vritra, Indra threw open the gate of the water that had stood closed.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ Yāska gives an etymology of this rik (quoted above in the bhāṣya; the Kannada, here, reads it as the Anuvāda): dāsa means one who makes work done by workers; such a worker-master (adhipati) is called adhipatnī [feminine: dāsapatnī]; since the waters, by the water they provide for the work, give the workers rest and comfort, they are said to be those who give [the master] protection. In dāsapatnīḥ the word dāsa means 'one who makes others do labour' — here Vṛtra. Ahigopāḥ — ahinā guptāḥ: 'guarded by ahi (Vṛtra)', that is, hidden and shut up in places. Ahi means ayanāt, 'going in the atmosphere'; or āhanti [from han]: because it kills people, ahi, the ā-prefix being shortened: a serpent. Paṇir vaṇig bhavati — paṇi is a trader. Paṇiḥ paṇanāt — he is so called because he does buying and selling. Vaṇik paṇyaṃ nenekti — a trader washes and cleans the goods he has made ready for sale, as befits their price; such goods are called paṇya. Bilaṃ bharaṃ bhavati — it is a bila because it is filled with water; i.e. an opening. Vṛtro vṛṇoter vā vartater vā vardhater vā: since he covers (vṛṇoti), is (vartate) or grows (vardhate) — and these are said to be the reasons for the name vṛtra: this is Yāska's explanation [as given above]. दासपत्नीः (dāsapatnīḥ) — the waters of which Vṛtra was the husband or lord; since Vṛtra is in the form of the cloud, he is called the lord of the waters in the cloud — that is, 'the waters in his power'. अहिगोपाः (ahigopāḥ) — guarded by the demon Vṛtra, that is, hidden away on the earth and placed, as in a cowshed, in the safe-keeping of one who watches. पणिनेव गावः (paṇineva gāvaḥ) — as cows were [confined] by the Paṇi. In the Ṛgveda the word paṇi in some places denotes 'a miser who deals in trade'; but, since there are places where it is said that he did not perform sacrifices and did not give dakṣiṇā gifts, the seers regard him as a man not worthy of respect and as 'a man of low mind'; in some places [the word] is a singular, and since the use of the plural is particularly frequent, one should understand paṇi as a name pointing to a class of people. On the Paṇis. The commentator quotes a story (upākhyāna): the rākṣasas called Paṇis stole the cows that were in the world of the gods and confined them in a cave in a mountain. To find them, Indra sent Saramā, a divine bitch (a female dog of the gods), who went to the Paṇis and, by friendly words, made friends with them and helped to bring away the cows. With the help of the Maruts, Indra destroyed the mountain-cave and brought back the cows that were in it, so the story says. In the Ṛg-Saṃhitā, sūkta 108 of the tenth maṇḍala treats this matter, with a long dialogue between Saramā and the Paṇis. These Paṇis: that they were [the earlier] inhabitants of this country, engaged in trade and the like, is the opinion of some; they, without performing sacrifices or any pious works and without attachment to them, regarded only the earning of wealth, by right or wrong means, as the chief thing, and since they behaved so, the Āryas call them dasyus and look down on them as people of low conduct; so the prevailing opinion has been put in the mantras. In the Ṛgveda the Paṇis are looked down on in this way, and there are many riks concerning them: the word and its forms occur in these riks (references as printed, p. 631): पणयः (paṇayaḥ) — Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-134-10; 1-151-9; 4-51-3; 6-20-4; 10-108-7; 10-108-8; 10-108-2 (last digit curled 2 as printed, out of order); 10-108-4; 10-108-6; 10-108-10; 10-108-11; पणिः (paṇiḥ) — 1-33-3; 1-1[8?]0-7 (an ink blot covers the middle digit); 5-61-8; पणिना (paṇinā) — 4-25-7; पणिना इव (paṇinā iva) — 1-32-11; पणिभिः (paṇibhiḥ) — 4-58-4; पणिभ्यः (paṇibhyaḥ) — 9-22-7; पणिम् (paṇim) — 1-93-4; 6-44-22; 6-51-14; 6-61-1; 8-45-14; 8-75-7; 10-67-6; 10-156-3; पणीन् (paṇīn) — 1-184-2; 6-33-2; 6-39-2; 7-6-3; 7-19-9; 8-26-10; 8-64-2; 8-66-10; 10-60-6; पणीनाम् (paṇīnām) — 2-24-6; 6-45-31; 6-53-5; 6-53-7; 7-9-2; 9-3-2; पणेः (paṇeḥ) — 1-83-4; 1-182-3; 3-58-2; 5-34-7; 6-13-3; 6-53-3; 6-53-6; 10-92-3; पणौ (paṇau) — 8-97-2. It is customary to say that these Paṇis were the followers of the asura named Vala; and the matter of their having stolen the cows and hidden them in caves is treated in many riks: for this, see what we wrote earlier, in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 2, pages 228, 465–466. बिलम् (bilam) — a door; an opening.

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

अश्व्यो॒ वारो॑ अभवस्त॒दि॑न्द्र सृ॒के यत्त्वा॑ प्र॒त्यह॑न्देव एकः॑ । अज॑यो॒ गा अज॑यः शूर॒ सोम॒मवा॑सृजः॒ सर्त॑वे स॒प्त सिन्धू॑न् ॥ १२ ॥ [accent ?]

aśvyo vā́ro abhavas tad indra sṛké yát tvā pratyáhan deva ékaḥ | ájayo gā́ ájayaḥ śūra sómam ávāsṛjaḥ sártave saptá síndhūn || 12 || [accent ?] Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 2: the bar of the first अजयो (ajayo) stands under the ज/यो junction; set on यो. The mark over सिन्धून् (sindhūn) beside the stroke in the better scan is a pen mark (the old scan, PDF 648, shows only the stroke over धू and the bar under स of सप्त).

Pada-pāṭha: अश्व्यः । वारः । अभवः । तत् । इन्द्र । सृके । यत् । त्वा । प्रतिऽअहन् । देवः । एकः । अजयः । गाः । अजयः । शूर । सोमम् । अव । असृजः । सर्तवे । सप्त । सिन्धून् ॥ १२ ॥ aśvyaḥ | vāraḥ | abhavaḥ | tat | indra | sṛke | yat | tvā | prati-ahan | devaḥ | ekaḥ | ajayaḥ | gāḥ | ajayaḥ | śūra | somam | ava | asṛjaḥ | sartave | sapta | sindhūn || 12 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : सृके वज्रे । सृको वृक इति वज्रनामसु पठितत्वात् । देवो दीप्यमानः सर्वायुधकुशल एकोऽद्वितीयो वृत्रो यद्यदा त्वा त्वां प्रत्यहन् प्रतिकूलत्वेन प्रहृतवान् तत्तदानीं त्वमश्व्यो वारोऽश्वसंबन्धी वालोऽभवः । यथाश्वस्य वालोऽनायासेन मक्षिकादीन्निवारयति तद्वद्वृत्रमगणयित्वा निराकृतवानित्यर्थः । किंच गाः पणिनापहृतास्त्वमजयः । जितवान् । हे शूर शौर्ययुक्तेन्द्र सोममजयः । जितवान् । तथा च तैत्तिरीयास्त्वष्टा हतपुत्र इत्यस्मिन्नुपाख्याने समामनन्ति । स यज्ञवेशसं कृत्वा प्रासहा सोममपिबत् । तै. सं. २-४-१२-१ । इति । सप्त सिन्धून् इमं मे गङ्गे । ऋग्वे. १०-७५-५ । इत्यस्यामृच्याम्नाता गङ्गाद्याः सप्तसंख्याका नदीः सर्तवे सर्तुं प्रवाहरूपेण गन्तुमवासृजः । त्यक्तवान् । वृत्रकृतं प्रवाहनिरोधं निराकृतवानित्यर्थः ॥ अश्व्यः । अश्वे भवः । भवे छन्दसीति यत् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । वारयति दंशमशकानिति वारः । पचाद्यच् । कपिलकादित्वाल्लत्वविकल्पः । म. ८-२-१८ । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । प्रत्यहन् । यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति निघातप्रतिषेधः । तिङि चोदात्तवतीति गतेरनुदात्तत्वम् । अजयः । गा इत्यस्य वाक्यान्तरगतत्वात्तदपेक्षयास्य तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातो न भवति । समानवाक्ये निघातयुष्मदस्मदादेशा वक्तव्याः । पा. १-१-१८-५ । इति वचनात् । सर्तवे । तुमर्थे सेसेनिति तवेन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥ sṛke vajre | sṛko vṛka iti vajranāmasu paṭhitatvāt | devo dīpyamānaḥ sarvāyudhakuśala eko 'dvitīyo vṛtro yadyadā tvā tvāṃ pratyahan pratikūlatvena prahṛtavān tattadānīṃ tvamaśvyo vāro 'śvasaṃbandhī vālo 'bhavaḥ | yathāśvasya vālo 'nāyāsena makṣikādīnnivārayati tadvadvṛtramagaṇayitvā nirākṛtavānityarthaḥ | kiṃca gāḥ paṇināpahṛtāstvamajayaḥ | jitavān | he śūra śauryayuktendra somamajayaḥ | jitavān | tathā ca taittirīyāstvaṣṭā hataputra ityasminnupākhyāne samāmananti | sa yajñaveśasaṃ kṛtvā prāsahā somamapibat | tai. saṃ. 2-4-12-1 | iti | sapta sindhūn imaṃ me gaṅge | ṛgve. 10-75-5 | ityasyāmṛcyāmnātā gaṅgādyāḥ saptasaṃkhyākā nadīḥ sartave sartuṃ pravāharūpeṇa gantumavāsṛjaḥ | tyaktavān | vṛtrakṛtaṃ pravāhanirodhaṃ nirākṛtavānityarthaḥ ‖ aśvyaḥ | aśve bhavaḥ | bhave chandasīti yat | yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvam | vārayati daṃśamaśakāniti vāraḥ | pacādyac | kapilakāditvāllatvavikalpaḥ | ma. 8-2-18 | vṛṣāditvādādyudāttatvam | pratyahan | yadvṛttānnityamiti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | tiṅi codāttavatīti gateranudāttatvam | ajayaḥ | gā ityasya vākyāntaragatatvāttadapekṣayāsya tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighāto na bhavati | samānavākye nighātayuṣmadasmadādeśā vaktavyāḥ | pā. 1-1-18-5 | iti vacanāt | sartave | tumarthe seseniti tavenpratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvam ‖ "Sṛke means 'on the vajra' (sṛka is read among the names of the thunderbolt). When the shining Vṛtra, skilled in all weapons, the one without a second, struck against you — O Indra — then you became a horse's hair (aśvyo vāraḥ): as a horse's tail drives off flies and the like without effort, so you, not reckoning Vṛtra at all, cast him off. Further, you won (ajayaḥ) the cows stolen by the Paṇi; O valiant Indra, you won the Soma. So the Taittirīyas record, in the story of Tvaṣṭṛ whose son was killed: 'having made a disruption of the sacrifice, he drank the Soma by force' (Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12-1). You released the seven rivers (sapta sindhūn) — [the seven] such as the Gaṅgā, named in the Ṛk 'imaṃ me gaṅge' (Ṛg. 10-75-5) — so that they might flow in streams: that is, you cast aside the obstruction of the flow made by Vṛtra. (Grammatical tail: aśvyaḥ — yat by bhave chandasi, initial acute by yato 'nāvaḥ; vāraḥ — 'that wards off gadflies and mosquitoes', ac of the pacādi group, l optional as a kapilakādi word (Ma. 8-2-18), initial acute as a vṛṣādi word; pratyahan — no nighāta by yadvṛttān nityam, the prefix low by tiṅi codāttavati; ajayaḥ — the second ajayaḥ is not lowered after gāḥ, which belongs to another sentence, by the dictum samānavākye nighātayuṣmadasmadādeśā vaktavyāḥ (P. 1-1-18-5 as printed); sartave — taven by tumarthe sesen…, initial acute as nit.)"

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वज्रिणे [= सृके] (sṛke) — O Indra, who hold the thunderbolt | देवः (devaḥ) — [Vṛtra,] shining | एकः (ekaḥ) — the incomparable | यत् (yat) — when | त्वा (tvā) — you | प्रत्यहन् (pratyahan) — he struck against | तत् (tat) — then [you] | अश्व्यः वारः (aśvyaḥ vāraḥ) — [like] the tail-hair of a horse (that without trouble drives off a fly) | अभवः (abhavaḥ) — became [that is, you easily destroyed Vṛtra] | गाः (gāḥ) — the cows [stolen by the Paṇi] | अजयः (ajayaḥ) — you won | शूर इन्द्र (śūra indra) — O valiant Indra | सोमम् (somam) — the Soma-juice | अजयः (ajayaḥ) — you won | सप्त सिन्धून् (sapta sindhūn) — the seven rivers | सर्तवे (sartave) — [for them] to flow as streams | अवासृजः (avāsṛjaḥ) — you freely let go.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Indra, who hold the vajra! When the shining, matchless Vṛtra struck against you, you destroyed him easily, as the hair of a horse's tail drives away a fly. O valiant Indra, you won the cows that were stolen by the Paṇi, and you won the Soma-juice; and you let the seven rivers go free, to flow in streams. The English Translation, Special Topics and the grammar of Rik 12 begin on p. 635 (PDF 650) — to be written in the next batch.

Rik 12 — continued (the Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya, Prati-padārtha and the start of the Bhāvārtha are given at the end of the previous batch) pp. 635–636

Bhāvārtha, end : … you won the stolen cows; you won the Soma-juice; and the seven rivers, such as the Gaṅgā, you let go free to flow in streams.

॥ English Translation ॥

When the mighty Vritra, though single, struck you in return, O weilder [sic] of the thunderbolt, you became furious like a horse's tail (which easily sweeps flies) ; you have rescued the stolen cows ; O hero, you have won the Soma-juice ; you have let loose the seven rivers to flow without obstruction.

[Note on the print's English:* "You became furious like a horse's tail" is as printed; the Kannada says Indra became like *a horse's tail towards the enemies, i.e. swept them off with ease.]

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ अश्व्यो वारो अभवत् (aśvyo vāro abhavat) — here Indra is compared to the tail-hair of a horse. As a horse's tail, with which it swishes away the flies and the like that settle on its body, drives them off without effort: so you, Indra, are, in destroying enemies, like a horse's tail: the seer gives this simile. सृके (sṛke) — vajre, vajrāyudhadharaṇe: among the eighteen names of vajra beginning didyut, nemiḥ, the word sṛkaḥ is read; sṛka means the weapon vajra; sṛko 'syāstīti sṛkī: [he who has the sṛka]; tasya sambuddhiḥ sṛke: 'O Sṛkin' [the Kannada: sṛke is the vocative singular of the word sṛkin]. प्रत्यहन् (pratyahan) — struck back, eight against eight [the print: eṭige prati eṭu, 'blow for blow']. सर्तवे (sartave) — to flow; to flow as streams. सप्त सिन्धून् (sapta sindhūn) — the seven rivers; that is, the seven rivers named in the rik beginning imaṃ me gaṅge [Ṛg-Saṃhitā 10-75-5]: Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī, Paruṣṇī, Asiknī, Marudvṛdhā.

Grammar pages 635–636, noted briefly: aśvyaḥ — aśve bhavaḥ aśvyaḥ; the affix yat by Pā. sū. 4-4-110 bhave chandasi; the initial acute by Pā. sū. 6-1-213 yato 'nāvaḥ; vāraḥ — vārayati daṃśamaśakān iti vāraḥ; ṇic in the causative sense; it is in the pacādi group (nandigrahapacādibhyaḥ…), so ac; ṇic gives vṛddhi of the root; ac causes the loss of ṇi by ṇer aniṭi; since vāra belongs to the kapilakādi group, the l-substitution (vāla) is optional (Pā. sū. Ma. 8-2-18); the end-acute through the suffix, but, the word being in the vṛṣādi group, the initial acute by Pā. sū. 6-1-203 vṛṣādīnāṃ ca; pratyahan — prati as a prefix; han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi; śap dropped by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; the final i of tip and the t dropped by halṅyābbhyo…; lowering would arise but, because of the correlation with yat (Pā. sū. 8-1-66 yadvṛttān nityam), is prevented; the root's end-acute gives the initial acute; the gati prati is low-accented by tiṅi codāttavati (Pā. sū. 8-1-71); ajayaḥ — ji jaye; laṅ 2nd singular, ajayaḥ; the first ajayaḥ is at the pāda's head, so no lowering; although the second ajayaḥ stands after gāḥ, a non-verb, and might be lowered by tiṅ atiṅaḥ, the dictum samānavākye nighātayuṣmadasmadādeśā vaktavyāḥ (Pā. sū. 8-1-18-5; the bhāṣya prints पा. १-१-१८-५ (pā. 1-1-18-5)) applies: since gāḥ is connected to the earlier verb, they are different sentence-parts, and so the second ajayaḥ is the head of a pāda-part and is not lowered; sartave — sṛ gatau; the affix taveṅ by tumarthe sesen… (Pā. sū. 3-4-9); guṇa of ṛ because the suffix is ārdhadhātuka; taveṅ is nit, so initial acute by ñnity ādir nityam. The print gives only Pā. sū. 4-4-110, 6-1-213, Ma. 8-2-18, 6-1-203, 8-1-66, 8-1-71, 8-1-18-5, 3-4-9; ends ॥ १२ ॥.

Rik 13 pp. 636–639

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

नास्मै॑ वि॒द्युन्न त॑न्य॒तुः सि॑षेध॒ न यां मिह॒मकि॑रद्ध्रादु॒निं॑ च । [accent ?] इन्द्र॑श्च॒ यद्यु॑यु॒धाते॒ अहि॑श्चो॒ताप॒रीभ्यो॑ म॒घवा॒ वि जि॑ग्ये ॥ १३ ॥

nā́smai vidyún ná tanyatúḥ siṣedha ná yāṃ miham ákirad dhrāduniṃ ca | [accent ?] índraś ca yád yuyudhā́te áhiś cotā́parī́bhyo maghávā ví jigye || 13 || Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 1: the bar after ह्रा (hrā) stands under the start of दु (du), beside the subscripts; set on दु.

Pada-pāṭha: न । अस्मै । विऽद्युत् । न । तन्यतुः । सिषेध । न । याम् । मिहम् । अकिरत् । ह्रादुनिम् । च । इन्द्रः । च । यत् । युयुधाते इति । अहिः । च । उत । अपरीभ्यः । मघऽवा । वि । जिग्ये ॥ १३ ॥ na | asmai | vi-dyut | na | tanyatuḥ | siṣedha | na | yām | miham | akirat | hrādunim | ca | indraḥ | ca | yat | yuyudhāte iti | ahiḥ | ca | uta | aparībhyaḥ | magha-vā | vi | jigye || 13 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : इन्द्रं निषेद्धुं वृत्रो यान्विद्युदादीन्मायया निर्मितवान् ते सर्वेऽप्येनं निषेद्धुमशक्ताः । सोऽयमर्थोऽनेन मन्त्रेणोच्यते । अस्मै इन्द्रार्थं निर्मिता विद्युन्न सिषेध । इन्द्रं न प्राप्नोत् । तथा तन्यतुर्गर्जनं यां मिहं सेचनं यां वृष्टिमकिरत् वृत्रो विक्षिप्तवान् सापि वृष्टिर्न सिषेध । ह्रादुनिं चाशनिमपि यां वृत्रः प्रयुक्तवान् सापि न सिषेध । इन्द्रश्चाहिश्चेन्द्रवृत्रावुभावपि यद्यदा युयुधाते युद्धं कृतवन्तौ । तदानीं विद्युदादयो न प्राप्ता इति पूर्वत्रान्वयः । उतापि च मघवा धनवानिन्द्रोऽपरीभ्योऽपराभ्योऽन्यासामपि वृत्रनिर्मितानां मायानां सकाशाद्वि जिग्ये । विशेषेण जितवान् ॥ सिषेध । षिधु गत्याम् । मिहम् । मिह सेचने । मेहति सिञ्चतीति मिट् वृष्टिः । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । अकिरत् । कॄ विक्षेपे । तुदादिभ्यः शः । ऋत इद्धातोरितीत्त्वम् । अडागम उदात्तः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । युयुधाते । युधि संप्रहारे । लिटि प्रत्ययस्वरः । जिग्ये । सन्लिटोर्जेः । पा. ७-३-५७ । इत्यभ्यासादुत्तरस्य जकारस्य कुत्वम् ॥ indraṃ niṣeddhuṃ vṛtro yānvidyudādīnmāyayā nirmitavān te sarve 'pyenaṃ niṣeddhumaśaktāḥ | so 'yamartho 'nena mantreṇocyate | asmai indrārthaṃ nirmitā vidyunna siṣedha | indraṃ na prāpnot | tathā tanyaturgarjanaṃ yāṃ mihaṃ secanaṃ yāṃ vṛṣṭimakirat vṛtro vikṣiptavān sāpi vṛṣṭirna siṣedha | hrāduniṃ cāśanimapi yāṃ vṛtraḥ prayuktavān sāpi na siṣedha | indraścāhiścendravṛtrāvubhāvapi yadyadā yuyudhāte yuddhaṃ kṛtavantau | tadānīṃ vidyudādayo na prāptā iti pūrvatrānvayaḥ | utāpi ca maghavā dhanavānindro 'parībhyo 'parābhyo 'nyāsāmapi vṛtranirmitānāṃ māyānāṃ sakāśādvi jigye | viśeṣeṇa jitavān ‖ siṣedha | ṣidhu gatyām | miham | miha secane | mehati siñcatīti miṭ vṛṣṭiḥ | kvipceti kvip | akirat | kṝ vikṣepe | tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ | ṛta iddhātoritīttvam | aḍāgama udāttaḥ | yadvṛttayogādanighātaḥ | yuyudhāte | yudhi saṃprahāre | liṭi pratyayasvaraḥ | jigye | sanliṭorjeḥ | pā. 7-3-57 | ityabhyāsāduttarasya jakārasya kutvam ‖ "All the [weapons] such as lightning that Vṛtra had formed by his māyā to ward Indra off were unable to hold him back. This is told by this mantra: the lightning formed for [attacking] him (asmai) did not obstruct [na siṣedha] Indra — did not reach Indra. Likewise the thunder (tanyatuḥ), and the rain (miham) that Vṛtra scattered (akirat), and the hailstone (hrāduniṃ) that he used — none of them reached him. When Indra and Ahi (Vṛtra) fought (yuyudhāte) — then, the lightning and the others did not reach: this is the connection with the earlier [part]. And the wealthy (maghavā) Indra conquered (vi jigye) in addition the other (aparībhyaḥ) wiles made by Vṛtra, of all kinds. (Grammatical tail: siṣedha — ṣidhu gatyām; miham — mih secane, 'what sprinkles', rain, with kvip; akirat — kṝ vikṣepe, śa by tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ, it for the ṝ by ṛta id dhātoḥ, the aṭ acute, no lowering because of the correlation with yad; yuyudhāte — yudh saṃprahāre, the affix accent in liṭ; jigye — kutva of the j after the reduplicate by sanliṭor jeḥ (P. 7-3-57).)"

Grammar pages 638–639, noted briefly: siṣedha — ṣidhu gatyām, bhvādi; s for ṣ by P. 6-1-64 dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; liṭ 3rd singular, tip → ṇal by P. 3-4-82 parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus…; doubling because of ṇit; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; the root's light penult takes guṇa; ṣatva of the reduplicate's s after i by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: siṣedha; being atiṅanta... the lowering of the verb by P. 8-1-28; miham — miha secane; 'what sprinkles' is miṭ = rain, with kvip by P. 3-2-76; accusative singular; akirat — kṛ vikṣepe, tudādi; laṅ 3rd singular; the i of tip dropped by P. 3-4-100 itaś ca; śa by P. 3-1-77 tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ; apit, hence ṅit by P. 1-2-4 and no guṇa; the ṛ → ir by P. 7-1-100 ṛta id dhātoḥ; → ra by uraṇ raparaḥ; the aṭ augment; the correlation with yām prevents lowering (P. 8-1-66); the aṭ being acute, initial acute; yuyudhāte — yudha saṃprahāre, divādi; liṭ 3rd dual, the ending ātām → ā + te: e by P. 3-4-81 liṭas tajhayor eśirec; the e by P. 3-4-79; doubling; since liṭ is kit [by P. 1-2-5 asaṃyogāl liṭ kit], no guṇa; yuyudhāte; no lowering since yat is correlated; the accent: the ṭhakāra [dhakāra]-following u… is anudātta by the suffix's initial acute; jigye — ji jaye; liṭ 3rd singular, e by P. 3-4-81; doubling of ji; jigye: by P. 7-3-57 sanliṭor jeḥ (सन्लिटोर्जेः) the j of the root after the reduplicate becomes g (kutva); [the print: 'by antaratamya g arises']; lowered by P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ [the print: P. 8-1-28 as tiṅ tiṅaḥ]. Numerals as read.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्रश्च (indraś ca) — and Indra | अहिश्च (ahiś ca) — and Vṛtra | यत् (yat) — when | युयुधाते (yuyudhāte) — fought | अस्मै (asmai) — to kill this Indra | विद्युत् (vidyut) — the lightning [produced by Vṛtra] | न सिषेध (na siṣedha) — did not reach [Indra, nor] | तन्यतुः (tanyatuḥ) — the thunder [did not reach] | याम् मिहम् (yām miham) — [nor] the rain which | अकिरत् (akirat) — [Vṛtra] scattered | न (na) — [that also] did not reach | ह्रादुनिं च (hrāduniṃ ca) — and the hailstorm that he created [that also did not reach] | उत (uta) — and further | मघवा (maghavā) — Indra | अपरीभ्यः (aparībhyaḥ) — [Vṛtra's] other weapons | वि जिग्ये (vi jigye) — [fighting] conquered completely.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ When Indra and Vṛtra fought, Vṛtra produced lightning in order to kill Indra, he scattered the rain, made the thunder resound in the clouds, and made hail. But none of these reached Indra; none did him any harm. Not only that: Indra, fighting, conquered completely Vṛtra's other weapons too.

॥ English Translation ॥

When Ahi (Vritra) and Indra both fought together, neither the lightning nor the thunder (discharged by Vritra) nor the rain which he showered, nor the thunderbolt harmed Indra and afterwards Indra alone was victorious.

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ तन्यतुः (tanyatuḥ) — roaring, the rumble of thunder, the crash, and so on. मिहम् (miham) — miha secane: sprinkling; rain. ह्रादुनिम् (hrāduniṃ) — [a weapon like] the vajra. अपरीभ्यः (aparībhyaḥ) — anyāsām api vṛtranirmitānāṃ māyānāṃ sakāśāt: that Indra defeated the other devices created by the demon Vṛtra by means of his own māyā is the sense.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : हे इन्द्र जघ्नुषो वृत्रं हतवतस्तव हृदि चित्ते यद्यदि भीरगच्छत् न हतवानस्मीति बुद्ध्या भयं प्राप्नुयात् तर्ह्यहेर्वृत्रस्य यातारं हन्तारं कमपश्यः । त्वत्तोऽन्यं कं पुरुषं दृष्टवानसि । तादृशस्य पुरुषान्तरस्याभावान्मा भूत्तव भयमित्यर्थः । यद्यस्मात्कारणात्त्वं नव च नवतिं च स्रवन्तीरेकोनशतसंख्याकाः प्रवहन्तीर्नदीः प्राप्य रजांसि तत्रत्यान्युदकान्यतिरः । तीर्णवानसि । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । श्येनो न । श्येननामको बलवान्पक्षीव दूरगमनात्तव भयमासीदिति गम्यते । तद्भयं मा भूदित्यभिप्रायः । तच्च दूरगमनं ब्राह्मणे समाम्नातम् । इन्द्रो वै वृत्रं हत्वा नास्तृषीति मन्यमानः पराः परावतोऽगच्छत् । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-१५ । इति । तैत्तिरीयाश्चामनन्ति । इन्द्रो वृत्रं हत्वा परां परावतमगच्छदपराधमिति मन्यमानः । तै. ब्रा. १-६-७-४ । इति ॥ हृदि । पद्दन्नित्यादिना हृदयशब्दस्य हृदादेशः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । जघ्नुषः । हन्तेर्लिटः क्वसुः । षष्ठ्येकवचने वसोः संप्रसारणमिति संप्रसारणपरपूर्वत्वे । शासिवसिघसीनां चेति षत्वम् । न च षत्वतुकोरसिद्धः । पा. ६-१-८६ । इत्येकादेशस्यासिद्धत्वात् षत्वं न प्राप्नुयादिति वाच्यं संप्रसारणङीट्सु प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः । का. ६-१-८६-१ । इत्यसिद्धवद्भावस्य प्रतिषिद्धत्वात् । गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । न चासिद्धवदत्राभादिति संप्रसारणस्यासिद्धवद्भावः । भिन्नाश्रयत्वात् । संप्रसारणं हि षष्ठ्येकवचने उपधालोपस्तु वसाविति भिन्नाश्रयत्वम् । स्रवन्तीः । स्रु गतौ । शप्श्यनोर्नित्यम् । पा. ७-१-८१ । इति नुमागमः । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेणाद्युदात्तत्वम् । … the last line of p. 640 is cut off in both scans (better PDF 654, old PDF 655); the earlier text had अतरः । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः ॥ (ataraḥ | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ ||) here, unverified he indra jaghnuṣo vṛtraṃ hatavatastava hṛdi citte yadyadi bhīragacchat na hatavānasmīti buddhyā bhayaṃ prāpnuyāt tarhyahervṛtrasya yātāraṃ hantāraṃ kamapaśyaḥ | tvatto 'nyaṃ kaṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭavānasi | tādṛśasya puruṣāntarasyābhāvānmā bhūttava bhayamityarthaḥ | yadyasmātkāraṇāttvaṃ nava ca navatiṃ ca sravantīrekonaśatasaṃkhyākāḥ pravahantīrnadīḥ prāpya rajāṃsi tatratyānyudakānyatiraḥ | tīrṇavānasi | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | śyeno na | śyenanāmako balavānpakṣīva dūragamanāttava bhayamāsīditi gamyate | tadbhayaṃ mā bhūdityabhiprāyaḥ | tacca dūragamanaṃ brāhmaṇe samāmnātam | indro vai vṛtraṃ hatvā nāstṛṣīti manyamānaḥ parāḥ parāvato 'gacchat | ai. brā. 3-15 | iti | taittirīyāścāmananti | indro vṛtraṃ hatvā parāṃ parāvatamagacchadaparādhamiti manyamānaḥ | tai. brā. 1-6-7-4 | iti ‖ hṛdi | paddannityādinā hṛdayaśabdasya hṛdādeśaḥ | ūḍidamityādinā vibhakterudāttatvam | jaghnuṣaḥ | hanterliṭaḥ kvasuḥ | ṣaṣṭhyekavacane vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇamiti saṃprasāraṇaparapūrvatve | śāsivasighasīnāṃ ceti ṣatvam | na ca ṣatvatukorasiddhaḥ | pā. 6-1-86 | ityekādeśasyāsiddhatvāt ṣatvaṃ na prāpnuyāditi vācyaṃ saṃprasāraṇaṅīṭsu pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ | kā. 6-1-86-1 | ityasiddhavadbhāvasya pratiṣiddhatvāt | gamahanetyādinopadhālopaḥ | na cāsiddhavadatrābhāditi saṃprasāraṇasyāsiddhavadbhāvaḥ | bhinnāśrayatvāt | saṃprasāraṇaṃ hi ṣaṣṭhyekavacane upadhālopastu vasāviti bhinnāśrayatvam | sravantīḥ | sru gatau | śapśyanornityam | pā. 7-1-81 | iti numāgamaḥ | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | śatuśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇādyudāttatvam | … "O Indra! If fear (bhīḥ) had entered your heart when you, [the slayer] of Vṛtra, had killed him — [if] you had thought 'I have slain' — whom [else] did you see as the slayer (yātāram) of Ahi? Whom did you see other than yourself? There was no such other person; hence no fear from anywhere. Or: since you, like a frightened hawk (śyeno na bhītaḥ), reaching the ninety-nine (nava ca navatiṃ ca) flowing rivers (sravantīḥ), crossed their waters (rajāṃsi) — like the hawk (śyena), a strong bird; it is understood that you went far from fear; the intention is: 'let there be no fear'. And that far flight is recorded in the Brāhmaṇa: 'Indra, having killed Vṛtra, thinking "I have not prevailed" [nāstṛṣi; editorial and tentative], went to the farthest distances' (Ai. Br. 3-15); the Taittirīyas also record: 'Indra, having killed Vṛtra, went far away, thinking "[I have committed] an offence"' (Tai. Br. 1-6-7-4). ॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ इन्द्र (indra) — O Indra | जघ्नुषः (jaghnuṣaḥ) — [of you] who killed Vṛtra | हृदि (hṛdi) — in the heart, in the mind | यत् (yat) — when | भीः (bhīḥ) — fear | अगच्छत् (agacchat) — came | अहेः (aheḥ) — of Vṛtra | यातारम् (yātāram) — the slayer | कम् (kam) — [other than you] whom | अपश्यः (apaśyaḥ) — did you see (think of) | यत् (yat) — for which reason | भीतः (bhītaḥ) — being afraid | नव च नवतिं च (nava ca navatiṃ ca) — ninety-nine | स्रवन्तीः (sravantīḥ) — flowing rivers | रजांसि (rajāṃsi) — those waters | श्येनः न (śyenaḥ na) — like a hawk, swiftly | अतरः (ataraḥ) — you crossed.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ O Indra! When fear arose in your heart as you set out to kill Vṛtra, whom, other than yourself, did you think of as the slayer of Vṛtra? For what reason did you, [frightened], cross the ninety-nine flowing rivers swiftly, like a hawk?

॥ English Translation ॥

O Indra, when you killed Vritra, what fear did enter your heart ? what persuer [sic] did you see on behalf of Vritra ? what was that which, frightened as you were, made you flee and traverse ninety-nine streams like a swift hawk ?

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ There is some difficulty in the sense of this rik. The commentator has explained the meaning thus: when Indra was about to kill the demon Vṛtra, he feared in his mind that he, [being] so powerful, might have a slayer; so, frightened, he fled swiftly like a hawk and crossed the rivers flowing in torrents. If we alter this explanation a little the sense fits better: after killing the demon Vṛtra, Indra, from the fear that Vṛtra's followers might come behind him, ran swiftly, like a hawk, and, crossing the ninety-nine rivers that lay on the way, came to a safe place. Support for this idea is found in the Purāṇas and elsewhere; but there, the fear that overcame Indra was that, having killed Vṛtra, who was a Brāhmaṇa, he had committed a great sin and incurred the guilt of Brahmin-slaying; fearing so, he fled far away and hid in a lake, where, it is said, he stayed for a long time. Vṛtra was the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, the craftsman of the gods; being a Brāhmaṇa, Indra, thinking that by his slaying he had done a great wrong, departed to a distant place. This is established by two Śruti sentences cited by the commentator: > (१) इन्द्रो वै वृत्रं हत्वा नास्तृषीति मन्यमानः पराः परावतोऽगच्छत् ॥ Ai. Brā. 3-15 — indro vai vṛtraṃ hatvā nāstṛṣīti manyamānaḥ parāḥ parāvato 'gacchat — "Indra, having killed Vṛtra, thinking 'I have not prevailed', went to the farthest distances." > (२) इन्द्रो वृत्रग्ं हत्वा । परां परावतमगच्छत् । अपाराधमिति मन्यमानः ॥ Tai. Brā. 1-6-7-4; अपाराधम् (apārādham) as printed, the bhāṣya has अपराधम् (aparādham) — indro vṛtragṃ hatvā | parāṃ parāvatam agacchat | apārādham iti manyamānaḥ — "Indra, having killed Vṛtra, went to the farthest distance, thinking [it] an offence." On the basis of such passages one may say that this matter was widely told in the Purāṇas and elsewhere. अहेर्यातारम् (aher yātāram) — the person who comes from the side of Vṛtra to kill [me]. नव च नवतिं च (nava ca navatiṃ ca) — 'ninety-nine': many rivers; the sense is that while going far he crossed many rivers that lay on the way. स्रवन्तीः (sravantīḥ) — sru gatau: rivers flowing in streams. श्येनो न (śyeno na) — the bird called śyena, the hawk; it is well known that it can fly very swiftly and to a great distance; the seer gives it as a simile. रजांसि (rajāṃsi) — waters, that is, currents of flowing water: Yāska has the statement udakaṃ raja ucyate (Ni. 4-19).

Grammar pages 642–643, noted briefly, from the print: hṛdi — hṛd for hṛdaya in the locative by paddan-no-mās-hṛd… (Pā. sū. 6-1-63), the ending acute by ūḍidampadādi… (Pā. sū. 6-1-171); jaghnuṣaḥ — han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, kvasu by kvasuś ca, doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cutva, gh by abhyāsāc ca; genitive singular: saṃprasāraṇa of v by vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam (Pā. sū. 6-4-131), pūrvarūpa by saṃprasāraṇāc ca, the penult a dropped by gamahanajana… (Pā. sū. 6-4-98), ṣatva by śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca; the single substitute would be asiddha for ṣatva by ṣatvatukor asiddhaḥ (Pā. sū. 6-1-86), but the vārttika saṃprasāraṇaṅīṭsu pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ (Kā. 6-1-86-1) bars it; asiddhavad atrābhāt (Pā. sū. 6-4-22) does not apply because the conditions (nimitta) differ, so jaghnuṣaḥ stands; sravantīḥ — sru gatau, bhvādi, śatṛ by laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau, śap by kartari śap, guṇa and av, sravat; ṅīp by ugitaś ca; num by śapśyanor nityam (Pā. sū. 7-1-81); śap unaccented as pit; tāsy anudāttet… and the root's initial acute; ataraḥ — tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, laṅ 2nd singular; no lowering by yadvṛttān nityam because of yan navatim; the aṭ acute, initial acute. The print gives only these numbers; ends ॥ १४ ॥.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya : वज्रबाहुरिन्द्रः शत्रौ हते सति निःसपत्नो भूत्वा यातो गच्छतो जङ्गमस्यावसितस्यैकत्रैव स्थितस्य स्थावरस्य शमस्य शान्तस्य शृङ्गराहित्येन प्रहरणादावप्रवृत्तस्याश्वगर्दभादेः शृङ्गिणः शृङ्गोपेतस्योग्रस्य महिषबलीवर्दादेश्च राजाभूत् । सेदु स एवेन्द्रश्चर्षणीनां मनुष्याणां राजा भूत्वा क्षयति । निवसति । ता तानि पूर्वोक्तानि जङ्गमादीनि सर्वाणि परि बभूव । व्याप्तवान् । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । अरान्न नेमिः । यथा रथचक्रस्य परितो वर्तमाना नेमिररान्नाभौ कीलितान्काष्ठविशेषान्व्याप्नोति तद्वत् ॥ यातः । या प्रापणे । यातीति गच्छतीति यात् । लटः शतृ । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । सः । सोऽचि लोपे चेदिति संहितायां सोर्लोपः । ता । शेश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः । बभूव । भवतेर्लिटो णलि भवतेरः । पा. ७-४-७३ । इत्यभ्यासस्यात्वम् । कृताकृतप्रसङ्गितया वुगागमस्य नित्यत्वाद्वृद्धेः पूर्वं वुगागमः । यद्वा । इन्धिभवतिभ्यां च । पा. १-२-६ । इति लिटः कित्त्वाद्वृद्ध्यभावः । न चासिद्धवदत्राभादिति तस्यासिद्धत्वादुवङादेशः शङ्कनीयः । वुग्युटावुवङ्यणोः सिद्धौ भवतः । पा. ६-४-२२-१४ । इति तस्य सिद्धत्वात् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥ ३८ ॥ vajrabāhurindraḥ śatrau hate sati niḥsapatno bhūtvā yāto gacchato jaṅgamasyāvasitasyaikatraiva sthitasya sthāvarasya śamasya śāntasya śṛṅgarāhityena praharaṇādāvapravṛttasyāśvagardabhādeḥ śṛṅgiṇaḥ śṛṅgopetasyograsya mahiṣabalīvardādeśca rājābhūt | sedu sa evendraścarṣaṇīnāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ rājā bhūtvā kṣayati | nivasati | tā tāni pūrvoktāni jaṅgamādīni sarvāṇi pari babhūva | vyāptavān | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | arānna nemiḥ | yathā rathacakrasya parito vartamānā nemirarānnābhau kīlitānkāṣṭhaviśeṣānvyāpnoti tadvat ‖ yātaḥ | yā prāpaṇe | yātīti gacchatīti yāt | laṭaḥ śatṛ | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvam | saḥ | so 'ci lope cediti saṃhitāyāṃ sorlopaḥ | tā | śeśchandasi bahulamiti śerlopaḥ | babhūva | bhavaterliṭo ṇali bhavateraḥ | pā. 7-4-73 | ityabhyāsasyātvam | kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgitayā vugāgamasya nityatvādvṛddheḥ pūrvaṃ vugāgamaḥ | yadvā | indhibhavatibhyāṃ ca | pā. 1-2-6 | iti liṭaḥ kittvādvṛddhyabhāvaḥ | na cāsiddhavadatrābhāditi tasyāsiddhatvāduvaṅādeśaḥ śaṅkanīyaḥ | vugyuṭāvuvaṅyaṇoḥ siddhau bhavataḥ | pā. 6-4-22-14 | iti tasya siddhatvāt | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ ‖ 38 ‖ "Indra, the vajra-armed, when the foe was slain, being without a rival, became king of what goes [moving things] (yātaḥ, jaṅgama) and of what is settled in one place (avasitasya: the immovable), of the gentle (śamasya: hornless creatures with a single hoof [horse] and the like), and of the horned (śṛṅgiṇaḥ) — fierce, buffalo, bulls and the like. He, that very Indra, being the king of men (carṣaṇīnām), dwells (kṣayati). He encompassed (pari babhūva) all those aforesaid moving and other beings — as the felly (nemiḥ) of a chariot-wheel, going around, encloses the spokes (arān), the special pieces of wood set in the nave. (Grammatical tail: yātaḥ — yā prāpaṇe, śatṛ, the ending acute by sāv ekācaḥ…; saḥ — the su dropped in the Saṃhitā by so 'ci lope cet…; tā — śi dropped by śeś chandasi bahulam; babhūva — ṇal, a for the reduplicate's vowel by bhavater aḥ (P. 7-4-73); the vuk augment, being nitya (kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgī), comes before vṛddhi; or no vṛddhi because liṭ is kit by indhibhavatibhyāṃ ca (P. 1-2-6); uvaṅ is not to be feared from asiddhavad atrābhāt, since vugyuṭāv uvaṅyaṇoḥ siddhau bhavataḥ (P. 6-4-22-14); lowered by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ. End of Varga 38.)"

Grammar pages 646–647, noted briefly, from the print (p. 646 read from the old scan, PDF 661): yātaḥ — yā prāpaṇe, adādi, yātīti yāt, śatṛ by laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau, genitive singular, the ending acute by sāv ekācaḥ… (Pā. sū. 6-1-168); saḥ — the s dropped in the Saṃhitā by so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam (Pā. sū. 6-1-134), sa + it: guṇa; tā — tad, accusative plural, śi by jaśśasoḥ śiḥ, sarvanāmasthāna by śi sarvanāmasthānam, num by napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ, lengthening by sarvanāmasthāne…, the i of śi dropped by śeś chandasi bahulam, n dropped by nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya; babhūva — bhū sattāyām, ṇal, vuk by bhuvo vuk luṅliṭoḥ, doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, a by bhavater aḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-73 [as printed; for 7-4-73]; the bhāṣya prints पा. ७-४-७३ (pā. 7-4-73)), b by abhyāse carca; vuk is nitya (kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgī) and so precedes vṛddhi (aco ñṇiti); or by indhibhavatibhyāṃ ca (Pā. sū. 1-2-6) liṭ is kit and vṛddhi is barred; asiddhavad atrābhāt would make vuk asiddha and bring uvaṅ by aci śnudhātubhruvām…, but by the vārttika vugyuṭāv uvaṅyaṇoḥ siddhau bhavataḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-22-14) vuk is siddha, so no uvaṅ; nighāta by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ after a non-verb. The print gives only these numbers; ends ॥ १५ ॥.

॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥ वज्रबाहुः (vajrabāhuḥ) — [Indra,] armed with the vajra | इन्द्रः (indraḥ) — Indra, [after the enemy was destroyed] | यातः (yātaḥ) — of the moving [beings] | अवसितस्य (avasitasya) — and of the unmoving | शमस्य (śamasya) — of the gentle [horses, etc., having no horns] | शृङ्गिणः च (śṛṅgiṇaḥ ca) — and of the horned [beings] | राजा (rājā) — [became] the king (of all the world) | सेदु (sed u) — that same Indra | चर्षणीनाम् (carṣaṇīnām) — of men | राजा (rājā) — as the king | क्षयति (kṣayati) — dwells | नेमिः (nemiḥ) — the felly of a wheel | अरान् न (arān na) — [surrounding] the spokes, as it were | ता (tā) — all these worlds | परि बभूव (pari babhūva) — he encompassed.

॥ Bhāvārtha ॥ After destroying his enemy, Indra of the vajra-arm became the sovereign of all the world: of the moving and the unmoving, of the gentle — hornless — and of the horned. The same Indra dwells as the king of men. As the felly of a wheel goes round and encloses all the spokes, so Indra stands encompassing all this world.

॥ English Translation ॥

Then Indra, the weilder [sic] of thunderbolt became the sovereign ruler of all that is movable and immovable, of hornless and horned cattle ; and as he resides as the monarch of men he surrounds all these with his protection as does the felly surround the spokes (of a wheel).

॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥ यातः (yātaḥ) — gacchataḥ: of things that move — living creatures able to move about; the jaṅgama world: 'movables' [English as printed]. अवसितस्य (avasitasya) — ekatraiva sthitasya: of what stays in one place, that is, the stationary world that cannot move: mountains and the like, trees and so on; 'immovables' [English as printed]. शमस्य (śamasya) — śāntasya: of the gentle, that is, of beings that are good [harmless]: creatures without horns, such as the horse [and others], that do not do violence to others. शृङ्गिणः (śṛṅgiṇaḥ) — of cows, buffaloes and other creatures that have horns. सेदु राजा क्षयति (sed u rājā kṣayati) — 'that very Indra, as the king of the moving and the unmoving, of the good and the bad, and of men, dwells' — that is, rules as the sole king. अरान्न नेमिः परि ता बभूव (arān na nemiḥ pari tā babhūva) — as the felly of a wheel, going round, encloses the spokes and holds them within it all round, so Indra encloses [and rules] the aforesaid movable and immovable worlds and men, and, protecting them all, shines, having brought them under his sway: this is the sense.

Close of Sūkta 32 : after the grammar of Rik 15 the print gives the colophon of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya on the Second Adhyāya, as below

Colophon of the Second Adhyāya

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्चतुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तकश्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणामात्येन विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये प्रथमाष्टके द्वितीयोऽध्यायः समाप्तः । ॥ ॐ तत्सत् ॥

vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃś caturo deyād vidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ || iti śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvaravaidikamārgapravartakaśrīvīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇāmātyena viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye prathamāṣṭake dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ | || oṃ tat sat ||

Translation: "May Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara, dispelling the darkness of the heart by the illumination of the meaning of the Veda, grant the four human aims. — Thus ends the Second Adhyāya in the First Aṣṭaka, in the Ṛk-Saṃhitā-bhāṣya, [called] the Vedārthaprakāśa of Mādhava, composed by the minister Sāyaṇa, who bears the burden of the empire of the illustrious king Vīra Bukka, the establisher of the Vedic path, king of kings, supreme lord. Oṃ tat sat."

Kannada colophon : illige śrīsāyaṇabhāṣyasahitavū karṇāṭakabhāṣānuvādayuktavū āda ṛgvedasaṃhiteyu prathamāṣṭakadalli eraḍaneya adhyāyavu samāptavādudu — "Here the Second Adhyāya in the First Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, with Śrī Sāyaṇa's commentary and the Kannada translation, is ended."

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ yad akṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yad bhavet | tat sarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stu te || "Whatever has slipped in syllable or word, or is deficient in measure — may all that be forgiven, O god, Lord of Speech: homage to you." ॥ शुभं भूयात् ॥ ॥ मङ्गलम् ॥ — śubhaṃ bhūyāt | maṅgalam — "May it be auspicious. Blessing."

Sūkta 32 and the colophon: the sūkta has 15 Riks. (The Sūkta-32 closing line — "the thirty-second sūkta is ended" — is not separately printed; the adhyāya's colophon above stands in its place.) Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 2 therefore closes with Sūkta 32.

¶ Grammar page 373, noted briefly: the words treated are viśvebhiḥ [viśva + bhis: ais would be substituted by P. 7-1-9 ato bhisa ais, but not in the Veda (P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi); e for a by P. 7-3-103 bahuvacane jhaly et; ru-visarga], canaḥ [cāyṛ pūjāniśāmanayoḥ, bhvādi; in the sense of 'food' asun by cāyer anne hrasvaś ca (U. sū. 4-639 as printed, middle digit read as 3; bhāṣya: 4-199); the shortening of cā → ca, the augment nuṭ; cayas… with y lost by P. 6-1-66 lopo vyor vali, hence canas; the accusative singular of the neuter am lost by P. 7-1-23 svamor napuṃsakāt, and ru-visarga; first-syllable acute by nit P. 6-1-197], dhāḥ [ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; the Vedic luṅ in the sense of the imperative by P. 3-4-6; 2nd singular sip → s; cli → sic, which is lost by P. 2-4-77 gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu because dhā has the name ghu; aṭ absent by P. 6-4-75 bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi; the s of sip → ru-visarga; the verb is lowered since it follows a word that is not a finite verb (no sūtra number printed)] and sahaso yaho [sahas 'strength' → sahasaḥ genitive; yaho is a vocative, so it has the name āmantrita; P. 2-1-2 subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare makes the preceding sahasaḥ a part of it; P. 8-1-19 āmantritasya ca lowers the whole group; the group sahaso yaho is wholly anudātta]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

¶ Grammar pages 376–377, noted briefly: the words treated are vāravantam [vārayati daṃśakān — 'what keeps off insects' = a tail; vṛ + ac by P. 3-1-134 nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ, or ghañ, giving vāra — vāla by the ra/la interchange (kapilakādi); vāra + matup by P. 5-2-94; m → v by P. 8-2-9 mādupadhāyāś ca matorvo 'yavādibhyaḥ; accusative singular — the print explains that Śunaḥśepa's word is read as vālavantam in the Kannada gloss], vandadhyai [vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ; idito num dhātoḥ P. 7-1-58; adhyai for the infinitive by P. 3-4-9 tumarthe se-sen-ase-asen-kase-kasen-adhyai-adhyain-kadhyai-kadhyain-śadhyai-śadhyain-tavai-tavenkenkenyatvanaḥ; the suffix's accent: adhyai has the middle acute], samrājantam [sam + rājṛ dīptau, ubhayapadī, bhvādi; śatṛ in the sense of laṭ; śap, and a + a by P. 6-1-97 ato guṇe; num in the accusative singular (no sūtra number printed); the accent: śap is pit so anudātta; śatṛ is lowered by P. 6-1-186; the root's accent remains; the compound with sam as gati keeps the kṛt-accent, P. 6-2-139] and adhvarāṇām [na vidyate dhvaro hiṃsā yasmin so 'dhvaraḥ; nañ-bahuvrīhi; the end-acute by P. 6-2-172; the genitive plural lengthens its vowel; n → ṇ: adhvarāṇām]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

¶ Grammar pages 379–380, noted briefly: the words treated are ghā naḥ [gha is an Upadeśa-particle; its vowel is lengthened in the Saṃhitā in a rik by P. 6-3-133 ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām], śavasā [śavas 'strength', an s-stem; for the genitive singular ending, ṭā by the dictum supāṃ supo bhavanti, established by vyatyayo bahulam P. 3-1-85], pṛthupragāmā [gam + ghañ with pra: halaś ca P. 3-3-121; upadhāvṛddhi P. 7-2-116 ata upadhāyāḥ; pṛthuḥ pragāmo yasya: a bahuvrīhi; nominative singular su → ā by supāṃ suluk; the accent of the first member, P. 6-2-1], suśevaḥ [śīṅ svapne + van by U. sū. 1-150 iṇśībhyāṃ van (bhāṣya: 1-152); guṇa; śeva; the su-compound: nañsubhyām P. 6-2-172 would give the end-acute, but P. 6-2-119 ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi gives the acute to the first syllable of a disyllabic second member, e.g. śeva], mīḍhvān [miha secane; kvasu by nipātana P. 6-1-12 dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca; ha → ḍha by P. 8-2-31; the dhva with ṣṭutva; the nominative singular: num, lengthening, su lost, and t/s lost; in the Saṃhitā mīḍhvām̐ by P. 8-3-1 ato 'ṭi nityam], and babhūyāt [bhū sattāyām,* bhvādi; liṭ in the sense of loṭ by P. 3-4-6 chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ; liṅ substituted for it by tiṅāṃ tiṅo bhavanti (Pā. Ma. 7-1-39); i lost by P. 3-4-100 itaś ca; yāsuṭ by P. 3-4-103; being sthānivat it is ārdhadhātuka, so no śap; doubling; a for the reduplicate by bhavater aḥ P. 7-4-73; jaśtva: babhūyāt; the verb is lowered by P. 8-1-28 tiṅṅatiṅaḥ because it follows asmākam*, a word that is not a finite verb]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

¶ Grammar pages 381–382, noted briefly: the words treated are aghāyoḥ [agham ātmana icchati — 'wishes evil to oneself' [as printed]; kyac by P. 3-1-8 supa ātmanaḥ kyac; u after kyac in the Veda by P. 3-2-170 kyācchandasi; the a of kyac is lost by P. 6-4-48; aśvāghasyāt P. 7-4-37 makes agha end in ā before kyac in the Veda, so aghāyu; ablative singular aghāyoḥ], pāhi [pā rakṣaṇe, adādi; loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi; hi is not lost since it does not follow a short a; the verb is not lowered since it is at the head of the pāda (the restriction apādādau; no number printed)] and viśvāyuḥ [iṇ gatau, adādi + usi in the sense of the action by U. sū. 2-275 eter ṇic ca (bhāṣya: 2-119); it is ṇit, so vṛddhi of the i by P. 7-2-115 aco ñṇiti; āy by P. 6-1-78 eco 'yavāyāvaḥ: āyus; viśvam āyur (ayanaṃ) gamanaṃ yasya, a bahuvrīhi; the accent of the first member's end by P. 6-2-106 bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām where the name is concerned; 'the acute that would be on the first syllable of the first member is displaced by an end-acute'; viśvāyuḥ has the middle acute]; numerals checked against the print, w3.
