¶ Grammar pages 383–384, noted briefly: the words treated are ū ṣu [ū with its vowel lengthened by P. 6-3-136 nipātasya ca; su → ṣu by P. 8-3-107 suñaḥ], navyāṃsam [nava + īyasun in the sense of excess (no sūtra number printed); the ī of īyas lost as a Vedic form; the a of nava lost by P. 6-4-148 yasyeti ca: navyas; being ugit, num before the accusative singular (a sarvanāmasthāna); lengthening by P. 6-4-14 atvasantasya cādhātoḥ: navyāṃsam; īyasun has n as it, so the first syllable is acute: the a after n] and vocaḥ [vaca paribhāṣaṇe, adādi (or brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci); the Vedic luṅ in the sense of the imperative by P. 3-4-6; sip; the i lost by itaś ca (no number printed); cli by P. 3-1-43 cli luṅi, and aṅ for it by P. 3-1-52 asyativaktikhyātibhyo 'ṅ; vac + a + s with the augment um by P. 7-4-20 vaca um; guṇa of the last vowel since um is mit; ru-visarga: vocaḥ; the aṭ augment is absent by P. 6-4-75 bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi; the verb has the tiṅanta lowering (no number printed)]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

¶ Grammar pages 389–390, noted briefly: the words treated are pṛtsu [pṛtanā + sup: in the locative plural sup, pṛt is substituted by padādiṣu māṃspṛtsnūnām upasaṃkhyānam (Pā. sū. 6-1-63-2 as printed; bhāṣya 6-1-63-1); the case-ending is anudātta, but by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ it takes the acute], avāḥ [ava rakṣaṇe, bhvādi; laṅ 2nd singular sip with śap; with the augment, āvaḥ; in the Veda the a and ā are transposed — or it is taken as a leṭ, with āṭ by P. 3-4-94 leṭo 'ḍāṭau; the i of sip lost by P. 3-4-97 itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu; śap is pit, so anudātta; by the root's accent the first syllable is acute], junāḥ [jū gatau, a sautra root, kryādi; laṅ 2nd singular sip; śnā by P. 3-1-81 kryādibhyaḥ śnā; junās, ru-visarga; no aṭ by P. 6-4-75 bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi; the verb is not lowered since yam is joined to it, P. 8-1-66 yadvṛttān nityam; by the vikaraṇa's accent it is end-acute], yantā [yamu uparame; tṛn in the sense of agent (no number printed); nominative singular yantā; tṛn is nit so first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-197], and śaśvatīḥ [śaśvat + ṅīp by P. 4-1-6 ugitaś ca; the accusative plural śaśvatīḥ]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

¶ Grammar pages 394–395, noted briefly: the words treated are viśvacarṣaṇiḥ [viśve carṣaṇayo yasya — a bahuvrīhi; the first member has the end-acute by P. 6-2-106 bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām because the compound is a name], arvadbhiḥ [ṛ gatau + vanip by P. 3-2-75 anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante; guṇa of the root: arvan, an n-stem; before the instrumental plural bhis, a case-ending other than su, the n is replaced by tṛ by P. 6-4-127 arvaṇas trasāvanañaḥ; the ṛ of tṛ is it, so arvat, a t-stem, and arvadbhiḥ], tarutā [tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, bhvādi; the tṛn-ending form is given by nipātana in P. 7-2-34 grasitaskabhita…, which records forms with operations not provided elsewhere; so by nipātana the i of the iṭ becomes u; in the nominative singular anaṅ, lengthening and loss of n give tarutā] and viprebhiḥ [vipra + bhis, the ais substitution of P. 7-1-9 ato bhisa ais is optional in the Veda (P. 7-1-10 bahulaṃ chandasi), so it does not occur; P. 7-3-103 bahuvacane jhaly et gives e to the final a of the stem: viprebhiḥ]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

¶ Grammar pages 397–398, noted briefly: the words treated are jarābodha [jṝṣ vayohānau, kryādi — roots have more than one sense, so here it means 'praise'; aṅ by P. 3-3-104 ṣidbhidādibhyo 'ṅ after a ṣit root; guṇa by P. 7-4-16 ṛdṛśo 'ṅi guṇaḥ; jara, and ṭāp by P. 4-1-4 ajādyataṣ ṭāp: jarā; budha avagamane + ghañ in the passive sense; guṇa; jarayā bodho yasya — he who is known by praise; or jarayā bodhyate; the vocative with the loss of su; not lowered (the āṣṭamika lowering) because it is at the head of the pāda; first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-198 āmantritasya ca], viviḍḍhi [viśa praveśane, tudādi; loṭ 2nd singular sip → hi; śa replaced by śluḥ by bahulaṃ chandasi; doubling; hi → dhi by P. 6-4-101; ś → ṣ by P. 8-2-36 vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ; ṣ + dh with ṣṭutva (ḍh) — or from viṣlṛ vyāptau, juhotyādi: ślu by P. 2-4-75 juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ, doubling; the guṇa due by P. 7-4-75 nijāṃ trayāṇāṃ guṇaḥ ślau is not made, by P. 3-1-85 vyatyayo bahulam], viśe-viśe [viś in the dative singular: the acute on the ending by P. 6-1-168 sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ, so end-acute; doubled by P. 8-1-4 nityavīpsayoḥ; the second is anudātta by P. 8-1-3 anudāttaṃ ca], yajñiyāya [yajña + gha in the sense of 'worthy of' by P. 5-1-71 yajñartvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau; gha → iya by P. 7-1-2; loss of the a by P. 6-4-148; dative] and dṛśīkam [dṛśir prekṣaṇe, bhvādi + kīkan by anidṛśibhyāṃ ca (Daśa. pā. 3 as printed); k and n are it, leaving īka; first-syllable acute because kīkan is nit, P. 6-1-197]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

¶ Grammar pages 399–401, noted briefly: the words treated are mahān [mahat + su; in the Saṃhitā before ṭ, t etc. the n → ru by P. 8-3-9 dīrghād aṭi samānapāde; the ā before the ru nasalized by P. 8-3-3 āto 'ṭi nityam], animānaḥ [na vidyate nimānam — a nañ-bahuvrīhi; nañsubhyām P. 6-2-172 gives the end-acute to the second member, overriding the first member's accent], dhūmaketuḥ [dhūmaḥ ketuḥ yasya, a bahuvrīhi; P. 6-2-1 bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam keeps the first member's accent, overriding the compound-final accent; the a after m — the long ū — is acute], puruścandraḥ [cadi āhlādane dīptau ca, bhvādi; rak in the sense of agent by U. sū. 1-170 sphāyitañcivañci…; idito num dhātoḥ P. 7-1-58 adds num; puru + candra — a karmadhāraya; the compound-final acute by P. 6-1-223 samāsasya; the augment suṭ by P. 6-1-151 hrasvāc candrottarapade mantre — puruscandra: s → ś by ścutva (no number printed) — hence puruścandraḥ], dhiye [dhī + ṅe; the ending takes the acute by P. 6-1-168] and hinvatu [hivi prīṇane, bhvādi; loṭ 3rd singular tip → tu by P. 3-4-86 eruḥ; num by P. 7-1-58; śap by P. 3-1-68 kartari śap; since num is mit it stands after the vowel: hinvatu; the verb is lowered since it follows a word that is not a finite verb (no number printed)]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

¶ Grammar page 403, noted briefly: the words treated are sa revān [sas + revān: the su is lost before a consonant by P. 6-1-132], revān [rayi + matup; in the Veda saṃprasāraṇa by rayer matau bahulam (Vā. 34-73 as printed); the rule P. 6-1-37 na saṃprasāraṇe saṃprasāraṇam prevents a second saṃprasāraṇa, so only the y → i; saṃprasāraṇāc ca P. 6-1-108 gives pūrvarūpa; ād guṇaḥ → e; matup's m → v by P. 8-2-15 chandasīraḥ; nominative singular with num, lengthening, loss of su and t; although matup is pit, it takes the acute after re by āre śabdāc ca matupa udāttatvaṃ vaktavyam (Pā. sū. 6-1-176-1); revān iva — n → ru and anunāsika before iva as before], viśpatiḥ [viśāṃ patiḥ; P. 6-1-223 samāsasya would give the end-acute, but P. 6-2-199 parādiś chandasi bahulam gives the acute to the beginning of the second member] and bṛhadbhānuḥ [bṛhataḥ bhānavaḥ yasya, a bahuvrīhi; P. 6-2-1 gives the first member's accent; the a after h is acute]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

¶ Grammar pages 406–408, noted briefly: the words treated are āśinebhyaḥ [aśū vyāptau, svādi, inac by bahulam anyatrāpi (U. sū. 2-20[7?]; the last digit read as 7); dative plural āśinebhyaḥ; end-acute by P. 6-1-163 citaḥ], yajāma [yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, bhvādi; loṭ 1st plural: yajāma; śap is pit and so anudātta; the la-sārvadhātuka is anudātta by P. 6-1-186 tāsyanudāttet… since it follows an adupadeśa; the root's end-acute remains], śaknavāma [śaklṛ śaktau, svādi; loṭ 1st plural mas; its s lost by P. 3-4-99 nityaṃ ṅitaḥ; āṭ by P. 3-4-92 āḍ uttamasya pic ca; śnu by P. 3-1-73 svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ; śak + nu + āma with guṇa and av: śaknavāma; the tiṅ, treated as pit, is anudātta, and by the vikaraṇa's accent the a after n is acute; because yadi precedes, P. 8-1-30 nipātair yad yadihanta… prevents the lowering of the verb], jyāyasaḥ [atiśayena praśasyaḥ: praśasya + īyasun (no number printed); jya substituted for the whole of praśasya (being of more than one letter) by P. 5-3-61 jya ca; the ī of īyas → ā after jya by P. 6-4-160 jyād ādīyasaḥ: jyāyas; genitive singular; first-syllable acute since īyasun is nit, P. 6-1-197], śaṃsam [śaṃsu stutau + ghañ by P. 3-3-121 halaś ca; accusative singular] and vṛkṣi [o vraścū bhedane, tudādi, parasmaipadī; by P. 3-1-85 vyatyayo bahulam the ātmanepada iṭ in the luṅ 1st singular; cli by P. 3-1-43 cli luṅi, sic for it by P. 3-1-44 cleḥ sic; since the root is ūdit, iṭ before the ārdhadhātuka sic is optional by P. 7-2-44 svarati sūti sūyati…, and here not added; the s (from the ś of the cluster) at the beginning of the conjunct lost by P. 8-2-29 skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca; ṣ by P. 8-2-36 vraścabhrasja…; saṃprasāraṇa by the grahijyā sūtra; vṛṣ + s + i; ṣ → k by P. 8-2-41 ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si; the s of sic → ṣ by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: kṣ — vṛkṣi; no aṭ because of mā, P. 6-4-74 na māṅyoge; the tiṅanta lowering]; numerals checked against the print, w3.

¶ Grammar pages 422–423, noted briefly: the words treated are maṃthām [mathin: the accusative singular with ā in the stem by P. 7-1-85 pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt; i → a by P. 7-1-86 ito 't sarvanāmasthāne; th → nth by P. 7-1-87 before the strong endings; ā + am → ām by P. 6-1-107; the first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-199 pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne; alternatively mathi viloḍane + ghañ by P. 3-3-121 halaś ca, with num [idito num dhātoḥ] and ṭāp — manthā; ñit gives the first-syllable acute], vibadhnate [bandha bandhane, kryādi; laṭ 3rd plural jha → ate by P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere (te); śnā by P. 3-1-81 kryādibhyaḥ śnā; śnā, with its ā lost by P. 6-4-112 śnābhyastayor ātaḥ; the nasal of the root lost by P. 6-4-24; śnā is śit and anudātta, but the suffix accent remains; vi is lowered by P. 8-1-71 tiṅi codāttavati] and yamitavai [yamu uparame, bhvādi; the infinitive tavai by P. 3-4-9; iṭ augment by chandasi; alternatively ṇic + tavai with iṭ and the Vedic loss of ṇic; P. 6-1-200 tavai cāntaś ca yugapat gives the acute on the first and last syllables: ya and vai]; numerals as printed.

¶ Grammar pages 426, noted briefly: the words treated are ulūkhalaka [the vocative singular: since the sūtra āpādādau forbids the lowering at the beginning of the pāda... the word ulūkhalaka has the vocative āmantrita status, but being at the head of the line it is not lowered; the suffix ka gives the middle acute; ū is acute], yujyase [yuja samādhau, divādi; laṭ in the passive; yak is ṅit-like; the accent of yak remains because the sūtra tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam… makes se anudātta; the word is middle-acute; tiṅ atiṅaḥ does not lower it because it follows yat — P. 8-1-28 tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ and P. 8-1-30], and dyumattamam [div in the sense of 'shining' (a saṃpadādi word with kvip, Vā. 2233 as printed); div + u → dyu by P. 6-1-131 diva ut; dyumat + tamap in the sense of excess; matup after a short-voweled stem gets the acute by P. 6-1-176; ...the print adds a long argument about diva ut applying to the stem and not the root, with the example akṣadyūḥ and the lakṣaṇā sense dīpti]; se is anudātta by P. 6-1-186; ūṭh P. 6-4-19 cited in the argument; numerals as printed.

¶ Grammar pages 431–432, noted briefly: the words treated are āyajī [ā + yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu + i in the instrumental sense (an Uṇādi suffix), the compound with the gati ā takes the kṛdanta-final accent by P. 6-2-139; dual au → ī by P. 7-1-39 supāṃ suluk; the word is end-acute], vājasātamā [vājaṃ sanoti; ṣaṇu dāne, tanādi; viṭ by P. 3-2-67 janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ; the nasal of the root → ā by P. 6-4-41 viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt; vājasā; tamap by P. 5-3-55 atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau + dual with ā by supāṃ suluk; the second member's accent by P. 6-2-139], vijarbhṛtaḥ [hṛñ haraṇe, bhvādi, here with yaṅ-luk — 'repeated going': doubling of the root; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; yaṅ lost before ac by P. 2-4-74 yaṅo 'ci ca; doubling by P. 6-1-9 sanyaṅoḥ; the reduplicate's a by urat; cutva by kuhoś cuḥ; jaśtva — ja for ha; the augment ruk by P. 7-4-91 rugrikau ca luki; so jarhṛ → the root jarbhṛ; tas for laṭ 3rd dual; śap lost; the ṅit-treatment blocks guṇa; the root status by P. 1-1-62 pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam and sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; hṛ → bhṛ by hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi (P. 3-1-84, Vā. 48-23); the suffix accent; the verb is not lowered since hi precedes (P. 8-1-34 hi ca)] and bapsatā [bhasa bhakṣaṇadīptyoḥ, juhotyādi; śatṛ; śluḥ; bhas doubled — babhas-at; the penultimate a lost by P. 6-4-100 ghasibhasor hali ca; bh → p before s by khari ca, so bapsat; the dual au → ā; no num — P. 7-1-78 nābhyastācchatuḥ; first-syllable acute by P. 6-1-189 abhyastānām ādiḥ]; numerals as printed.

¶ Grammar pages 441–442, noted briefly (corrected from the print, w3): somapāḥ [somaṃ pibati iti somapāḥ; pā pāne, bhvādi; viC by āto manin-kvanib-vanipaś ca (P. sū. 3-2-74), the root being ā-final; the whole of viC is lost, leaving an ā-final word; as a vocative, nighāta by āmantritasya ca], anāśastā iva [śaṃsu stutau, bhvādi; kta in the bhāva sense by niṣṭhā (P. sū. 3-2-102); no iṭ by yasya vibhāṣā (P. sū. 7-2-15); in śaṃs+ta the penultimate n is lost by aniditāṃ halaḥ, giving śasta; with the upasarga āṅ: na vidyate āśastaṃ yeṣāṃ te anāśastāḥ, a bahuvrīhi; where the first member's natural accent would apply, nañsubhyām (P. sū. 6-2-172) gives the second member's end-acute; with ru, ya and its loss, anāśastā iva], smasi [asa bhuvi, adādi; 1st pl. mas; as+mas: the a of as is lost by śnasor allopaḥ (P. sū. 6-4-111), as mas is treated as ṅit; in s+mas, idanto masi (P. sū. 7-1-46) adds the augment i: smasi], tū na [ṛci tunugha… (P. sū. 6-3-133) lengthens tu in the Saṃhitā], goṣu [go being monosyllabic, sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ (P. sū. 6-1-168) would make the ending acute; it is blocked by na gośvan sāv avarṇa… (P. sū. 6-1-182), so first-syllable acute], aśveṣu [aśnute adhvānam iti aśvaḥ; aśū vyāptau, svādi; kvan by aśipruṣilaṭikaṇi… (U. sū. 1-149); as kvan has n as it, ñnity ādir nityam (P. sū. 6-1-197) gives first-syllable acute], śubhriṣu [śubha dīptau, bhvādi; krin by adiśadibhūśubhibhyaḥ krin (U. sū. 4-505 as printed; the bhāṣya prints U. 4-65); loc. pl. śubhriṣu; being nit the first syllable would be acute, by vyatyaya the end-acute: "śubhriṣu is a middle-acute word" (as printed)]. ॥ १ ॥

¶ Grammar pages 444–445, noted briefly (corrected from the print, w3): śiprin [śipre hanū nāsike vā (Niru. 6-17) says Yāska: śipra is the jaw or the nose; śipre asya staḥ iti śiprī; ini in the possessive sense by ata iniṭhanau (P. sū. 5-2-115); vocative śiprin; at the head of the pāda, first-syllable acute by āmantritasya (P. sū. 6-1-198)], vājānāṃ pate [by subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare (P. sū. 2-1-2) the preceding genitive becomes part of the following vocative, and the accent falls on the whole group with the genitive; the vocative śiprin stands before it, so by āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat (P. sū. 8-1-72) it would count as non-existent, the group would stand at the head of the pāda, and by āpādādau the eighth-chapter nighāta would not apply; how then does the earlier procedure hold? Because by nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam (P. sū. 8-1-73) the two vocatives, having one referent, are co-referential, so śiprin is not treated as non-existent; so the doubt does not arise], śacīvaḥ [śacī asya asti iti śacīmat; by chandasīraḥ (P. sū. 8-2-15) the m of matup after an i-final or r becomes v in the Veda; by matuvaso ru sambuddhau (P. sū. 8-3-1

6. P. sū. 8-3-15); being pāda-initial, no eighth-chapter nighāta; first-syllable acute by āmantritasya (P. sū. 6-1-198)]. ॥ २ ॥ File's 8-1-74, 8-2-66 and 8-1-18 are not printed.

¶ Grammar pages 447–448, noted briefly (corrected from the print, w3): ni ṣvāpaya [ñiṣvap śaye; with ṇic, loṭ 2nd sg.; being pāda-initial, sāt padādyoḥ would block ṣatva, but suṣāmādiṣu ca (P. sū. 8-3-48 as printed; for 8-3-98) gives ṣ, the word being in that list; the Saṃhitā lengthening by anyeṣām api dṛśyate (P. sū. 6-1-137 as printed; for 6-3-137)], mithūdṛśā [mithunatayā yugalarūpeṇa paśyataḥ: 'those who see as a pair'; by kvip ca the root dṛś with a sup-ending upapada takes kvip in the agent sense, wholly lost: mithunadṛś; a compound with a kṛt-final second member, so by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt (P. sū. 6-2-139) the second member keeps its own accent, the ṛ acute; the Saṃhitā lengthening as before; the dual au → ā by supāṃ suluk], sastām [ṣasa svapne, adādi; loṭ 3rd dual, tas → tām (being treated as laṅ-like); the root's ṣ → s; śap lost by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ (P. sū. 2-4-72); end-acute by the suffix accent; being pāda-initial, no nighāta by tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ (P. sū. 8-1-28)], abudhyamāne [in the nañ-compound, by tatpuruṣe tulyārtha… (P. sū. 6-2-2) the nañ first member keeps its accent: first-syllable acute]. ॥ ३ ॥ File's 8-3-65, 3-2-61, 6-3-116 and 3-4-101 are not printed.

¶ Grammar pages 449–450, noted briefly (corrected from the print, w3): sasantu [ṣasa svapne; loṭ 3rd plural; by the suffix's initial acute, sasantu is a middle-acute word], arātayaḥ [rā dāne, adādi; ktin in the bhāva sense by mantre vṛṣeṣapaca… (P. sū. 3-3-96): rāti; na vidyate rātir yeṣu te arātayaḥ, a bahuvrīhi, so by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam the first member's accent; strictly, with nañ as first member, nañsubhyām would give the end-acute, but by sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante it does not apply here; or else ktic in the agent sense by ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām (P. sū. 3-3-174), rāti, and na rātayaḥ arātayaḥ is a nañ-tatpuruṣa, where by tatpuruṣe tulyārtha… (P. sū. 6-2-2) the avyaya (nañ) first member keeps its accent: arātayaḥ is first-syllable acute], bodhantu [budha avagamane, bhvādi, loṭ 3rd plural; being pāda-initial, no nighāta by tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ (P. sū. 8-1-28); since śap is anudātta and the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta by tāsyanudāttet… (P. sū. 6-1-186), the root accent makes it first-syllable acute]. ॥ ४ ॥ File's 7-1-3, 3-3-97, 6-2-1, 6-2-172 numbers and 8-1-18 are not printed.

¶ Grammar pages 538–539, noted briefly: avāśayaḥ — vāśṛ śabde, divādi, śyan; the causal ṇic, then laṅ 2nd singular; the tiṅanta is unaccented (tiṅantanighāta; no sūtra number printed); pururavase — puru rauti iti pururavāḥ; ru śabde, adādi; the affix asun by sarvadhātubhyo 'sun; ravas is a sānta word; the first member's lengthening is a nipātana by purasi ca pururavāḥ (U. sū. 4-671; the bhāṣya prints उ. ४-१३१); dative singular pururavase; sukṛte — ḍukṛñ karaṇe; kvip by sukarmapāpamantrapuṇyeṣu kṛñaḥ (सुकर्मपापमन्त्रपुण्येषु कृञः, Pā. sū. 3-2-89) when su etc. are upapada; pit, so tuk after the short ṛ by the hrasvasya sūtra; sukṛt; dative singular; pitroḥ — pitṛ + os, yaṇ; the ending acute by udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt (उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वात्, Pā. sū. 6-1-174); mucyase — mucḷ mokṣaṇe, tudādi; passive laṭ 2nd singular, yak by sārvadhātuke yak (Pā. sū. 3-1-67); the lasārvadhātuka unaccented by tāsyanudāttet; the order is root accent, then suffix accent, then vikaraṇa accent; satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvam anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ — so the vikaraṇa accent does not override the lasārvadhātuka accent, but dhātusvaraṃ śnāsvaraḥ (said elsewhere): the vikaraṇa accent overrides the root accent; so yak's initial acute would apply, but by vyatyayo bahulam the root accent remains, giving an initial acute; anayan — ṇīñ prāpaṇe, bhvādi, laṅ 3rd plural; since the atiṅanta pūrvam precedes, the tiṅanta is unaccented (no sūtra number printed). ॥ ४ ॥

¶ Grammar pages 541–542, noted briefly: puṣṭivardhanaḥ — vṛdhu vṛddhau, bhvādi; ṇic by P. 3-1-26 hetumati ca (हेतुमति च); lyu by P. 7-1-134 [as printed; for 3-1-134] nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ, the root being in the nandyādi class; the l of lyu is it; yu → ana by P. 6-1-1 [as printed; for 7-1-1] yuvor anākau; guṇa of the penultimate; vardhana; being lit-final, initial acute by liti (P. 6-1-193); puṣṭiṃ vardhayatīti, a kṛt-final compound, the accent by P. 6-2-139 gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; udyatasruce — yamu uparame; with ut, the affix kta by P. 3-2-102 niṣṭhā (निष्ठा); the m lost by P. 6-4-37 anudāttopadeśa…; udyata; the accent by P. 6-2-49 gatir anantaraḥ (गतिरनन्तरः); a bahuvrīhi with first-member accent by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (no number printed); dative singular; veda — vida jñāne, adādi; ṇal in place of laṭ by P. 3-4-83 vido laṭo vā (विदो लटो वा); guṇa; yaḥ being correlated, the tiṅanta is not unaccented; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-135 dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ.

¶ Grammar pages 545–547, noted briefly: vṛjinavartanim — vṛjinā vartaniḥ yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (no number printed): the first member's accent overrides the compound accent; sakman — ṣaca samavāye; s for the initial ṣ by dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; manin by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. sū. 3-2-75); no iṭ by neḍ vaśi kṛti (नेड्वशि कृति, Pā. sū. 7-2-8); being in the nyaṅkvādi class, kutva of the c by nyaṅkvādīnāṃ ca (Pā. sū. 7-3-53); locative singular, luk by supāṃ suluk; nit, so initial acute by ñnityādir nityam (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); piparṣi — pṝ pālanapūraṇayoḥ, juhotyādi; laṭ 2nd singular sip; ślu by juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ; doubling by ślau; the reduplicate ṛ shortened by hrasvaḥ, made a by urat and ar by uraṇ raparaḥ; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; the reduplicate a → i by artipipartyoś ca (अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च, Pā. sū. 7-4-77); guṇa before the sārvadhātuka sip; ṣatva by ādeśapratyayayoḥ (आदेशप्रत्यययोः); after an atiṅanta the tiṅanta is unaccented (no sūtra numbers printed for these); śūrasātā — śu gatau, sautra; kran by śuṣicimīnāṃ dīrghaś ca (U. sū. 2-183; the bhāṣya prints उ. २-२५) with lengthening; kit, no guṇa; nit, initial acute; vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau, bhvādi; ktin by striyāṃ ktin; ā by janasanakhanāṃ sañjhaloḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-42); śūrāṇāṃ sātiḥ saṃbhajanam atra, a bahuvrīhi with the first member's accent; locative ḍā by supāṃ suluk (Pā. sū. 7-1-39); ḍit, so the final i drops; paritakmye — taka hasane, bhvādi; the Uṇādi mak in the sense of the action; takma; ya by chandasi ca (Pā. sū. 5-1-67) in the sense takmam arhati; compounded with pari by prādayo gatādyarthe prathamayā (Pā. Ma. 2-2-18-4); the avyaya-first compound keeps the first member's accent by tatpuruṣe tulyārtha… (Pā. sū. 6-2-2); dabhrebhiḥ — dambhu dambhe, svādi; rak by sphāyitañcivañciśaki… (U. sū. 2-170); kit, so the penultimate n drops by aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-24); ais for bhis by ato bhisa ais (Pā. sū. 7-1-9) is optional by bahulaṃ chandasi (Pā. sū. 3-1-10 [as printed; for 7-1-10]) and does not come; ru and visarga; samṛtā — locative ḍā by supāṃ suluk (Pā. sū. 7-1-39); sam keeps its accent by gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. sū. 6-2-49) before the kta-final; initial acute; haṃsi — hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi; laṭ 2nd singular sip; anusvāra by naś cāpadāntasya jhali (Pā. sū. 8-3-24); with yaḥ the tiṅanta is not unaccented, by yadvṛttayogān nityam (no number printed); sip is pit and unaccented, so the root accent: initial acute; bhūyasaḥ — bahu + īyasun in the comparative sense; bahor lopo bhū ca bahoḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-158): the ī of īyasun drops and bahu becomes bhū; accusative plural bhūyasaḥ; īyasun is nit, so initial acute by ñnityādir nityam (Pā. sū. 6-1-197). ॥ ६ ॥

Sūkta 31, Rik 7

¶ Grammar pages 549–550, noted briefly: dadhāsi — ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ, juhotyādi, laṭ 2nd singular; after an atiṅanta the verb is unaccented by tiṅ atiṅaḥ (Pā. sū. 8-1-28); martaḥ — explained at 1-2-30 [as printed], in the 20th mantra; śravase — śru śravaṇe, bhvādi; the Uṇādi asun; śravas; dative singular; nit, initial acute; tatṛṣāṇaḥ — ñitṛṣā pipāsāyām; kānac by liṭaḥ kānaj vā (लिटः कानज्वा, Pā. sū. 3-2-106); doubling as in place of liṭ; halādiśeṣa leaves tṛ in the reduplicate; its ṛ becomes a by urat, ar by the paribhāṣā uraṇ raparaḥ; ṇ by aṭkupvāṅ…; kānac is cit, so end-acute by citaḥ (Pā. sū. 6-1-163); if the word were taken as tujādi, the length would appear in the Pada too, so the Saṃhitā lengthening is to be taken as Vedic; kṛṇoṣi — kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca, bhvādi, laṭ 2nd singular sip; idit, so num; its n → ṇ by ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam; the affix u as vikaraṇa, with a for the root-final, by dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca (धिन्विकृण्व्योर च, Pā. sū. 3-1-80); the a drops before u by ato lopaḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-48); guṇa of the u before sip; ṣatva by ādeśapratyayayoḥ; by acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau the dropped a counts as present (sthānivadbhāva), so the penult does not take guṇa because of u; by cādilope vibhāṣā (चादिलोपे विभाषा, Pā. sū. 8-1-63), ca being dropped, the verb is not made unaccented. ॥ ७ ॥

¶ Grammar pages 552–553, noted briefly: yaśasam — yaśaḥ asya asti: the affix ac in the possessive sense by arśa ādibhyo 'c (अर्श आदिभ्योऽच्, Pā. sū. 5-2-127); the suffix's initial acute would apply, but by vyatyayo bahulam the syllable before the suffix is acute, so the word is middle-acute; or, by sarvaprātipadikebhyaḥ kvip vaktavyaḥ (Pā. Ma. 3-1-11-3), kvip after yaśas in a verbal sense; it is then a root by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; again kvip by kvip ca (Pā. sū. 3-2-76); a prātipadika by kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca; accusative singular; by dhātoḥ, the root accent being satiśiṣṭa, end-acute (no numbers printed for these); kṛṇuhi — kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca, loṭ 2nd singular, hi for sip; the stem kṛṇu by dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca as before (1-2-31-7 [as printed]); hi would be dropped by utaś ca pratyayād asaṃyogapūrvāt (Pā. sū. 6-4-106), but by utaś ca pratyayāc chandovāvacanam (Pā. sū. 6-4-106-1) it is optional in the Veda and is not dropped; the tiṅanta is unaccented (no number printed); stavānaḥ — ṣṭuñ stutau, adādi; s for the initial ṣ; ānac by sam yānac stuvaḥ (U. sū. 2-246; the bhāṣya prints उ. २-८६), which names stu with sam, but by the bahula of the Uṇādi also after the bare root; guṇa before ānac, av for o; end-acute by citaḥ (Pā. sū. 6-1-163) would apply, but as a vṛṣādi word it is initial-acute by vṛṣādīnāṃ ca (Pā. sū. 6-1-203); ṛdhyāma — ṛdhu vṛddhau, divādi; vidhiliṅ 1st plural mas; its s dropped by nityaṃ ṅitaḥ (Pā. sū. 3-4-99); yāsuṭ by yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅic ca (Pā. sū. 3-4-103); the śyan due by divādibhyaḥ śyan dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; yāsuṭ is ṅit, so no guṇa of the penult; yāsuṭ is acute, so the ā of ṛdhyāma is acute; at the head of the pāda the āṣṭamika lowering does not apply; dyāvāpṛthivī — dyauś ca pṛthivī ca, an itaretara dvandva; dyāvā for div in the compound by divo dyāvā (Pā. sū. 6-3-29); vocative dual by supāṃ suluk (Pā. sū. 7-1-39), the pūrvasavarṇa lengthening as ekādeśa; all-low by āmantritasya ca (no number printed); avatam — ava rakṣaṇe, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd dual; the tiṅanta is unaccented. ॥ ८ ॥ The right half of the last lines of p. 553 is cut off in the better scan; they were read from the old scan, PDF 568.

¶ Grammar pages 556–557, noted briefly: upasthe — ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau; with a subanta as upapada, the affix ka by supi sthaḥ (सुपि स्थः, Pā. sū. 3-2-4); kit and vowel-initial, so the root's ā drops by āto lopa iṭi ca (आतो लोप इटि च, Pā. sū. 6-4-64); stha; compounded with the gati upa; locative singular; the first member end-acute by marudvṛdhādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam (Pā. sū. 6-2-106-2); jāgṛviḥ — jāgṛ nidrākṣaye, adādi; kvin by jṝśṝstṝjāgṛbhyaḥ kvin (U. sū. 4-54); vi remains; kit, so no guṇa of the root; nit, so initial acute by ñnityādir nityam (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); bodhi — budha avagamane, bhvādi; loṭ 2nd singular, hi; the śap due by kartari śap (Pā. sū. 3-1-68) is dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; hi, though apit, is optionally pit in the Veda by vā chandasi (Pā. sū. 3-4-84 [as printed; for 3-4-88]), so the light penult takes guṇa; not being ṅit, hi becomes dhi by aṅitaś ca (Pā. sū. 6-4-103); the root-final is dropped as a Vedic form; bodhi; the tiṅanta is unaccented; pramatiḥ — mana jñāne; ktin by striyāṃ ktin (Pā. sū. 3-3-94); the nasal drops before the kit suffix by anudāttopadeśa… (Pā. sū. 6-4-37); mati; prakṛṣṭā matir yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi, the first member's accent by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. sū. 6-2-1); ūpiṣe — ḍuvap bījatantusantāne, bhvādi; ḍu dropped by ādir ñiṭuḍavaḥ (Pā. sū. 1-3-5); liṭ in the present sense by chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ (Pā. sū. 3-4-6); se for thās by thāsaḥ se (Pā. sū. 3-4-80); saṃprasāraṇa of v by vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti (Pā. sū. 6-1-15) and pūrvarūpa by saṃprasāraṇāc ca; asaṃyogāl liṭ kit: liṭ is not pit here, so its substitute is kit; doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, savarṇadīrgha; the iṭ prohibition of kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusru… (Pā. sū. 7-2-13) is restricted to kryādi roots (krādiniyama), so although vap is aniṭ, the val-initial se takes iṭ; ṣatva; ūpiṣe. ॥ ९ ॥

¶ Grammar page 559, noted briefly: vayaskṛt — vayaḥ karotīti vayaskṛt; kvip ca after kṛñ; as the suffix is pit, tuk by P. 6-1-71 hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk; the s of vayas becomes ru and visarga; the visarga before k becomes s by ataḥ kṛkamikaṃsakumbhapātrakuśākarṇiṣv anavyayasya (अतः कृकमिकंसकुम्भपात्रकुशाकर्णीष्वनव्ययस्य, P. 8-3-46); gatikāra [kāraka]-first compound kṛt-final accent; suvīram — śobhanāḥ vīrāḥ yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; the first-member accent would apply, but by nañsubhyām (नञ्सुभ्याम्, P. 6-2-172) the end-acute of the second member prevails since it is su-first; this is set aside by vīravīryau ca (वीरवीर्यौ च, P. 6-2-120), by which, since vīra is the second member, the second member is initial-acute; adābhya — in the vocative, luk by eṅhrasvāt sambuddheḥ (एङ्ह्रस्वात्सम्बुद्धेः); some say that dabhi has a different stem; if one takes the root dambh, vṛddhi and the loss of the penult cannot arise — that is their view; by the saying dabheś ceti vaktavyam (P. 3-1-124-3) the affix ṇyat arises; ya remains; being ṇit, vṛddhi of the root's penult by ata upadhāyāḥ: dābhya; with na [a] negation, adābhya; vocative singular; all-low by āmantritasya ca (P. 8-1-19). Numerals as printed.

¶ Grammar pages 562–563, noted briefly: āyave — by the Vārttika ṣaṣṭhyarthe caturthī vaktavyā (षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी वक्तव्या, Pā. sū. 2-3-62-1) the dative stands for a genitive; āyu in the dative; nahuṣasya — ṇaha bandhane, with the Uṇādi uṣac by nahikalihanyatirlasibhya uṣac (नहिकलिहन्यतिर्लसिभ्य उषच्, U. sū. 4-515); ṇ → n by ṇo naḥ; genitive singular; the cit suffix would give end-acute, but the word being in the vṛṣādi group, initial acute by P. 6-1-203 vṛṣādīnāṃ ca (वृषादीनां च); viśpatim — viśāṃ patiḥ; the accent: by P. 6-2-199 parādiś chandasi bahulam (परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलम्), the initial syllable of the second member is acute; manuṣasya — mana jñāne; by [Uṇ.] maner nit the affix uṣac, which is nit; manuṣa ends with a; initial acute by P. 6-1-197 ñnityādir nityam; śāsanīm — śāsu anuśiṣṭau; 'that by which one is instructed' is śāsanī; lyuṭ in the sense of instrument and locus by P. 3-3-117 karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca (करणाधिकरणयोश्च); yu → ana by P. 7-1-1; the feminine by P. 4-1-15 ṭiḍḍhāṇañ… (टिड्ढाणञ्…) in ṅīp; as the suffix is lit-accented, initial acute by liti; ṅīp is pit, so unaccented; mamakasya — mama idam ('this is mine') in the sense of tasyedam P. 4-3-120 with aṇ; the substitute mamaka for asmad in the singular by P. 4-3-3 tavakamamakāv ekavacane (तवकममकावेकवचने); since a rule beginning with a technical term is not constant (saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ), no vṛddhi; a lost by yasyeti ca; the initial acute is by vyatyaya; jāyate — janī prādurbhāve, divādi; jā for jan by P. 7-3-79 jñājanor jā; śyan by P. 3-1-69; e for ṭ of laṭ ātmanepada by P. 3-4-79 ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; yat being correlated, the lowering of the verb is barred by yadvṛttānnityam; śyan is nit, so initial acute. Numerals as printed.

¶ Grammar pages 565–566, noted briefly: maghonaḥ — the stem maghavan; with śas (printed "tṛtīyā bahuvacana") following, saṃprasāraṇa by śvayuvamaghonām ataddhite (श्वयुवमघोनामतद्धिते, Pā. sū. 6-4-133): by ig yaṇaḥ saṃprasāraṇam the v becomes u; magha + u + an + as; by saṃprasāraṇāc ca the following vowel takes the prior form; guṇa by ād guṇaḥ; s → ru and visarga: maghonaḥ; tanvaḥ — tanū + śas: by the saying supāṃ supo bhavanti (सुपां सुपो भवन्ति) jas replaces śas; the lengthening by prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ (प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः) is barred by dīrghāj jasi ca (दीर्घाज्जसि च, Pā. sū. 6-1-105); yaṇ by iko yaṇ aci: tanvaḥ; since yaṇ comes in the place of the udātta, svarita by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ; with śas the form would be the same but the accent different: by udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt (Pā. sū. 6-1-174) the case-ending would be acute, so the change of case is by vyatyaya; rakṣa — rakṣa pālane, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular; hi for sip is dropped (luk) by ato heḥ; after a non-verb, the finite-verb lowering; vandya — vandayituṃ yogyaḥ: vadi abhivādanastutyoḥ, ṇyat by ṛhalor ṇyat (ऋहलोर्ण्यत्); the root being idit, num: vandya; as a vocative, the lowering by āmantritasya ca. Numerals as printed; grammar ends ॥ १२ ॥.

¶ Grammar pages 569–570, noted briefly: yajyave — yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, bhvādi; by yajimaniśundhi- (U. sū. 3-300) the affix yu: yajyu; in the dative singular, the stem being ghi, guṇa by gher ṅiti and av: yajyave; pāyuḥ — pā rakṣaṇe, adādi; uṇ by kṛvāpājimisvadi- (U. sū. 1-1); pā + u: the root ending in ā, the augment yuk by āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ (Pā. sū. 7-3-33): pāyuḥ; end-acute by the suffix accent; aniṣaṅgāya — ṣañja saṅge; with ni, ghañ: niṣaṅga; na vidyate niṣaṅgaḥ asya: aniṣaṅgaḥ, a bahuvrīhi; dative singular; end-acute of the second member by nañsubhyām (Pā. sū. 6-2-172); caturakṣaḥ — catvāri akṣīṇi jvālārūpāṇi yasya saḥ, a bahuvrīhi; by bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac (Pā. sū. 5-4-113) the samāsānta ṣac after akṣi; ṣac being cit, end-acute by citaḥ; idhyase — ñi indhī dīptau, passive laṭ; yak by sārvadhātuke yak; before yak, the loss of n by aniditāṃ hala…; se for thās: idhyase; the finite-verb lowering; dhāyase — ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; asun by vahihādhāñbhyaś chandasi (U. sū. 4-660); by vaser ṇit the ṇit carries over, so, the root ending in ā, yuk by āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ: dhāyas; dative singular dhāyase; initial acute, the suffix being nit; kīreḥ — kṛta saṃśabdane; in the causative sense ṇic by hetumati ca; by sanādyantā dhātavaḥ the ṇic-form is a root; ending in a vowel, the affix i by aca iḥ (U. sū. 4-578; middle digit 7, possibly 2); ṇi dropped by ṇer aniṭi; the root-final t dropped as Vedic; ṛ → i by ṝta id dhātoḥ, with r by uraṇ raparaḥ: ir, the penult lengthened: kīri; genitive singular kīreḥ; end-acute by the suffix accent; mantram — matri guptaparibhāṣaṇe; being idit, num; in the pacādi group, ac by the nandigraha[-pacādi] sūtra: mantra; end-acute by citaḥ would arise, but being in the vṛṣādi group, initial acute by vṛṣādīnāṃ ca (Pā. sū. 6-1-203); vanoṣi — vanu yācane, tanādi, laṭ 2nd singular sip; the vikaraṇa u by tanādikṛñbhya uḥ (Pā. sū. 3-1-79); guṇa of u before sip; ṣatva of the s of sip by ādeśapratyayayoḥ; by the suffix's initial acute vanoṣi is middle-acute. Numerals as printed; grammar ends ॥ १३ ॥.

¶ Grammar pages 573–574, noted briefly: uruśaṃsāya — śaṃsu stutau; śasyata iti śaṃsaḥ, ghañ in the sense of the object: śaṃsa; ghañ being ñit, initial acute by ñnityādir nityam (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); compounded with uru, which has the gati designation, the kṛt-final second member keeps its own accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; dative singular; spārham — spṛhāyā idam: aṇ by tasyedam; the ā dropped by yasyeti ca; initial vṛddhi by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ: spārham; rekṇaḥ — ricir virecane, irit; asun by ricer dhane ghicca (U. sū. 4-638); hence ghit-treatment, and by the ca the augment nuṭ; before asun guṇa of the light penult; in recnas the c → k by cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ (Pā. sū. 7-3-52); with k intervening, n → ṇ by the aṭkupv-… sūtra: rekṇaḥ; ādhrasya — dhrai tṛptau with the prefix āṅ; by ād eca upadeśe 'śiti (Pā. sū. 6-1-45) a root ending in a diphthong in the upadeśa takes ā when no śit follows; then, ending in ā, ka by ātaś copasarge (Pā. sū. 3-1-136); ādhrā + a: ā dropped by āto lopa iṭi ca: ādhra; genitive singular; śāssi — śāsu anuśiṣṭau, adādi; laṭ 2nd singular; luk of śap by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ: śāssi; [the ending] being unaccented, the root accent obtained by dhātoḥ remains; since the construction pākaṃ ca praśāssi, diśaś ca praśāssi shows the sense of ca, the lowering is barred by cādilope vibhāṣā (Pā. sū. 8-1-63); viduṣṭaraḥ — vidvas; tarap in the sense of excess by dvivacanavibhaja-…; by ayasmayādīni chandasi (Pā. sū. 1-4-20) the bha-designation; so by vasoḥ samprasāraṇam (Pā. sū. 6-4-131) saṃprasāraṇa of the v of vidvas; pūrvarūpa by saṃprasāraṇāc ca; in viduṣ + tara, though the [s] belongs to the stem, ṣatva by śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca (Pā. sū. 8-3-60): viduṣṭaraḥ; tarap being pit is unaccented, and the accent of vasu being satiśiṣṭa, the u is acute. Numerals as printed; grammar ends ॥ १४ ॥.

¶ Grammar pages 576–577, noted briefly: syūtam — ṣivu tantusaṃtāne; kta in the sense of the object by niṣṭhā (Pā. sū. 3-2-102); iṭ barred by yasya vibhāṣā (Pā. sū. 7-2-15); ūṭ for the v by chvoḥ śūḍ anunāsike ca (च्छ्वोः शूडनुनासिके च); s for the root-initial ṣ; si + ū + ta: yaṇ: syūta; pāsi — pā rakṣaṇe, adādi, laṭ 2nd singular; the finite-verb lowering; svādukṣadmā — svādūn kṣadati iti; kṣada bhakṣaṇe; manin by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. sū. 3-2-75): svādukṣadman; before su, the penult lengthened by sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau; su dropped by halṅyābbhyaḥ; n dropped by nalopaḥ…: svādukṣadmā; manin being nit, kṣadman initial-acute by ñnityādir nityam; as a kāraka-first compound, the kṛt-final keeps its accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt; if taken as a bahuvrīhi, the second member's initial acute must be explained by vyatyayo bahulam; jīvayājam — jīvāḥ ṛtvijaḥ ijyante dakṣiṇābhiḥ pūjyante atra; ghañ in the sense of locus after yaj; being ñit, vṛddhi of the root's a by ata upadhāyāḥ; the kutva due by cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ does not come, by vyatyayo bahulam: jīvayāja; or jīvaiḥ paśubhiḥ yājanam: ṇic after yaj, then ghañ, ṇi dropped by ṇer aniṭi; since by acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau that loss is sthānivat, cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ does not apply to the j; as a ghañ-final, by thāthaghañktāja-… (Pā. sū. 6-2-114 [as printed; for 6-2-144]) the compound is end-acute in the second member; sopamā — saḥ upamā; as it fills out the pāda, su is dropped by so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam (Pā. sū. 6-1-134); after the loss, guṇa: sopamā; divaḥ — by ūḍidampadādi- (Pā. sū. 6-1-171) the case-ending is acute. Numerals as printed; grammar ends ॥ १५ ॥.

¶ Grammar pages 580–581, noted briefly from the print: śaraṇim — śṝ hiṃsāyām, kryādi; the Uṇādi affix ani; guṇa by sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ; ṇ by aṭkupvāṅ-; initial acute of the affix; mīmṛṣaḥ — mṛṣa titikṣāyām; ṇic; sanādyantā dhātavaḥ; luṅ 2nd singular sip, itaś ca; ṇiśridrusrubhyaḥ kartari caṅ; guṇa by puganta-laghūpadhasya ca is barred by nityaṃ chandasi (Pā. sū. 7-4-8), the penult takes ṛ; ṇer aniṭi, caṅi (reduplication), halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, ur at, sanval laghuni caṅpare 'naglope (Pā. sū. 7-4-93), sanyataḥ (Pā. sū. 7-4-79), dīrgho laghoḥ; ru and visarga; tiṅṅatiṅaḥ; agāma — iṇ gatau, adādi; iṇo gā luṅi (Pā. sū. 2-4-45); mas, nityaṃ ṅitaḥ; cli luṅi, cleḥ sic; gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ (Pā. sū. 2-4-77) drops sic; the augment aṭ, initial acute; bhṛmiḥ — bhramu anavasthāne; bhrameḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca (U. sū. 4-560) gives in; saṃprasāraṇāc ca (pūrvarūpa); by the continuation of igupadhāt kit no guṇa of the light penult; ñnity ādir nityam, initial acute. Ends ॥ १६ ॥.

¶ Grammar pages 583–584, noted briefly: manuṣvat — the affix vati by P. 5-1-115 tena tulyaṃ kriyā ced vatiḥ (तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः), 'resembling in action', after the nominative [in the sense of 'equal action']; or, by P. 5-1-116 tatra tasyeva (तत्र तस्येव), the affix vati in the sense of the genitive; as the word is in the ayasmayādi list, by P. 1-4-20 ayasmayādīni chandasi it has the designation bha, hence pada-designation is lacking, so the s does not take ru and visarga; ṣatva by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: manuṣvat; by the suffix's initial acute, the a after the v is acute; aṅgirasvat, yayātivat and pūrvavat are the same — in the nominative or in the genitive sense, the affix vati applies, the process as before; vaha — vaha prāpaṇe, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular, sip → hi; śap by P. 3-1-68 kartari śap; hi dropped by P. 6-4-105 ato heḥ; vaha; the lengthening in the Saṃhitā by P. 6-3-135 dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ; yakṣi — yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu, bhvādi, loṭ 2nd singular sip; hi substitution is not applied by vyatyayo bahulam; śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; yaj + si: j → ṣ by P. 8-2-36 vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ (व्रश्चभ्रस्ज…षः); ṣ + s → k by P. 8-2-41 ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si (षढोः कः सि); the s after k → ṣ by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: yakṣi. ¶ Grammar pages 586–587, noted briefly from the print: vavṛdhasva — vṛdhu vṛddhau, bhvādi; leṭ 2nd singular thās; leṭo 'ḍāṭau gives aṭ; bahulaṃ chandasi: ślu in place of śap; ślau: reduplication; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; ur at: a for ṛ, with ra following, then dropped by halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; savābhyāṃ vāmau (Pā. sū. 3-4-91): se → sva; the reduplicate lengthened in the Saṃhitā (Vedic); being after a non-verb, the verb is unaccented; śaktī — instrumental singular, supāṃ suluk- (Pā. sū. 7-1-39) gives the lengthening; śakḷ śaktau with ktin; nit, so initial acute; vidā — vid with kvip; instrumental singular; sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ (Pā. sū. 6-1-168): the ending acute; neṣi — ṇīñ prāpaṇe, bhvādi, laṭ, sip; śap dropped by bahulaṃ chandasi; n for the initial ṇ; guṇa (sārvadhātuka); ṣatva by ādeśapratyayayoḥ; pra + neṣi: upasargād asamāse 'pi ṇopadeśasya (Pā. sū. 8-4-14) gives praṇeṣi; sumatyā — śobhanā cāsau matiś ca sumatiḥ; the end-acute of the second member, from man-ktin-, explained at length in the first adhyāya (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-7, as printed); yaṇ in the instrumental; udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt: the ending acute. Ends ॥ १८ ॥.

¶ Grammar pages 605–606, noted briefly: vṛtrataram — vṛtu vartane, bhvādi, rak in the sense of bhāva by 'sphāyitañcivañciśaki-' (U. sū. 2-1[7?]0 here: the middle digit has a flat foot; p. 595 prints 2-120 for the same sūtra), kit, so no laghūpadha-guṇa; vṛtreṇa … tarati iti vṛtrataraḥ, tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, ac as pacādi by 'nandigrahipacādibhyaḥ', guṇa; the end-acute from 'gatikārake' set aside by 'parādiś chandasi bahulam' (Pā. sū. 6-2-199): the second member initial-acute; if tara is taken as tarap, the accent is by vyatyaya; vyaṃsam — vigatau aṃsau yasmāt, bahuvrīhi, 'bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam': vi acute; yaṇ for it, so svarita by 'udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ' (Pā. sū. 8-2-4); vadhena — 'hanaś ca vadhaḥ' (Pā. sū. 3-3-76): ap in bhāva, vadha (end-acute) substituted, its a dropped by 'ato lopaḥ', ap unaccented (pit), the suffix acute by 'anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ'; vivṛkṇā — ovraścū chedane, kta (niṣṭhā) in the passive, s dropped by 'skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca', iṭ barred by 'yasya vibhāṣā', ta → na by 'oditaś ca' (Pā. sū. 8-2-45), the ṣatva of 'vraścabhrasja-' blocked since the niṣṭhā-substitute is siddha (Pā. sū. 8-2-6-7, vārttika), but asiddha for kutva by 'pūrvatrāsiddham' (Pā. sū. 8-2-1): k by 'coḥ kuḥ', ṇatva; vi keeps its accent by 'gatir anantaraḥ'; neuter plural jas → śi by 'jaśśasoḥ śiḥ', num, upadhā-lengthening, śi dropped by 'śeś chandasi bahulam' (Pā. sū. 6-1-70), na-lopa: vivṛkṇā; śayate — śīṅ svapne, adādi, laṭ, ta → te by 'ṭita ātmanepadānām-', luk of śap by 'adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ' withheld by 'bahulaṃ chandasi', ay by 'eco 'yavāyāvaḥ'; nighāta after an atiṅanta; pṛthivyāḥ — genitive singular; after yaṇ in the acute's place, the ending is acute by 'udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt' (Pā. sū. 6-1-174). Only these numbers are printed.

¶ Grammar pages 610–611, noted briefly: ayoddhā — na vidyate yoddhā asya, bahuvrīhi; the first-member accent set aside by 'nañsubhyām': end-acute; the samāsānta is optional by 'samāsāntavidhir anityaḥ' (Paribhā. 84), so no kap by 'nadyṛtaś ca' (Pā. sū. 5-4-153); juhve — hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca, liṭ, ta → e by 'liṭas tajhayor eśirec', saṃprasāraṇa by 'abhyastasya ca' (Pā. sū. 6-1-33), pūrvarūpa by 'saṃprasāraṇāc ca': hu, doubling, cutva; uvaṅ by 'huśnuvoḥ sā-' not applied in the Veda; or, sārvadhātuka by 'chandasy ubhayathā', yaṇ by 'huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke' (Pā. sū. 6-4-87); the paribhāṣā 'lakṣaṇapratipadoktayoḥ pratipadoktasyaiva grahaṇam' (Paribhā. 105) is not applied (else ājuhvānaḥ would fail); sātaye huve vām (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-10-13 as printed here; the bhāṣya prints 6-60-13) has no yaṇ since 'er anekācaḥ' requires a polysyllabic stem; end-acute by the affix accent; mahāvīram — mahāṃś cāsau vīraś ca, ā by 'ān mahataḥ samā-' (Pā. sū. 6-3-46), end-acute by 'samāsasya'; tuvibādham — bādhṛ viloḍane, ac by 'nandigrahipacādibhyaḥ' (Pā. sū. 3-1-134), the kṛt-final accent by 'gatikārakopapadāt kṛt'; samṛtim — ktin by 'striyāṃ ktin', sam a gati by 'gatiś ca', which keeps its accent by 'tādau ca niti kṛty atau' (Pā. sū. 6-2-50); rujānāḥ — rujo bhaṅge, rujanti kūlāni iti; śānac by 'vyatyayo bahulam' though parasmaipadin, śa by 'tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ', no num (Vedic); Yāska: 'rujānā nadyo bhavanti rujanti kūlāni' (Niru. 6-4); śānac unaccented, so the vikaraṇa accent; pipiṣe — piṣḷ saṃcūrṇane, liṭ by 'chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ', eś, doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; nighāta after an atiṅanta; indraśatruḥ — bahuvrīhi, first-member accent by 'bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā'. Only these numbers are printed.

¶ Grammar page 614, noted briefly: apāt — na vidyete pādau yasya, bahuvrīhi, the final of pāda dropped (Vedic); ahastaḥ — nañ-bahuvrīhi, end-acute by 'nañsubhyām' (Pā. sū. 6-2-172); apṛtanyat — pṛtanām ātmana icchati, kyac by 'supa ātmanaḥ kyac' (Pā. sū. 3-1-8), the final of pṛtanā dropped in the Veda by 'kavyadhvarapṛtanasya-' (Pā. sū. 7-4-39), root by 'sanādyantā dhātavaḥ', laṅ; bubhūṣan — bhavitum icchan, san, doubling by 'sanyaṅoḥ', 'hrasvaḥ', jaś by 'abhyāse carca', iṭ barred by 'sani grahaguhoś ca' (Pā. sū. 7-2-12), root by 'sanādyantā dhātavaḥ', śatṛ; purutrā — trā in the sense of the locative by 'devamanuṣyapuruṣapurumartyebhyo dvitīyāsaptamyor bahulam' (Pā. sū. 5-4-56), end-acute by the affix accent; aśayat — śīṅ svapne, adādi, tip by 'vyatyayo bahulam', 'itaś ca', no luk of śap by 'bahulaṃ chandasi', guṇa, ay, aṭ; nighāta after an atiṅanta; vyastaḥ — asu kṣepaṇe, kta in the passive, iṭ barred by 'yasya vibhāṣā', yaṇ; vi keeps its accent by 'gatir anantaraḥ' (Pā. sū. 6-2-49); in the Saṃhitā the following anudātta becomes svarita by 'udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ' (Pā. sū. 8-2-4). Page 613 holds the end of the Pratipadārtha, the Bhāvārtha, the printed English and the Special Topics.

¶ Grammar pages 617–618, noted briefly, from the print: bhinnam — bhidir vidāraṇe, kta; n for t by radābhyāṃ niṣṭhāto naḥ pūrvasya ca daḥ (Pā. sū. 8-2-42); amuyā — adas, locative singular, yā-substitute by supāṃ suluk…, tyadādīnām aḥ, ato guṇe (pararūpa), adaso 'ser dād u do maḥ; śayānam — śīṅ svapne, śānac, ṅit by apit, guṇa restored by śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ (Pā. sū. 7-4-21), eco 'yavāyāvaḥ, unaccented affix by tāsy anudāttet…, the root's end-acute; ruhāṇāḥ — śānac by vyatyaya (the root being parasmaipadin), the śa-vikaraṇa for kartari śap, no guṇa, āne muk not applied (āgamaśāsanam anityam), ṇatva by aṭ-kupvāṅ…, the root accent by vyatyaya; mahinā — in sarvadhātubhyaḥ, acute ending by vyatyaya; or mahimnā, tasya bhāvaḥ, imanic by pṛthvādibhya imanij vā (Pā. sū. 5-1-122), ṭeḥ, citaḥ, allopo 'naḥ, anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ; patsutaḥśīḥ — kvip ca, sarvalopa, pad for pāda by paddan-no-mās…, prabhṛti = 'kind' as the commentators explain (Kā. 6-1-63), the augment su Vedic; or tasil by itarābhyo 'pi dṛśyante (Pā. sū. 5-3-14), no luk in the Veda. The print gives only these five numbers; ends ॥ ८ ॥.

¶ Grammar pages 621–622, noted briefly, from the print: nīcāvayāḥ — the instrumental-singular substitute by supāṃ supo bhavanti, acaḥ (loss of a), cau (lengthening), the ending acute by añceś chandasy asarvanāmasthānam (Pā. sū. 6-1-170); luk prevented by vyatyayo bahulam; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam; or nīcau nikṛṣṭau vayasau yasyāḥ, the first member lengthened in the Veda, the nipāta's end-acute kept; vadhaḥ — sarvadhātubhyo 'sun, vadha for han, ato lopaḥ, initial acute by ñnity ādir nityam; jabhāra — hṛñ haraṇe, liṭ, ṇal, doubling, urat, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cutva, vṛddhi, uraṇ raparaḥ, bh by hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi, nighāta after a non-verb; sūḥ — ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane, kvip by kvip ca (Pā. sū. 3-2-76), kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca, end-acute by the root accent; dānuḥ — do avakhaṇḍane, ād eca upadeśe 'śiti, nu by dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ (U. sū. 3-312; the bhāṣya prints उ. ३-३२ (u. 3-32)); śaye — śīṅ svapne, laṭ, ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere, t dropped by lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu (Pā. sū. 7-1-41), guṇa by śīṅaḥ sārvadhātuke guṇaḥ (Pā. sū. 7-4-21), eco 'yavāyāvaḥ, nighāta by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ; sahavatsā — bahuvrīhau…, first-member accent. The print gives only these numbers; ends ॥ ९ ॥.

¶ Grammar pages 631–633, noted briefly, from the print: dāsapatnīḥ — dasu upakṣaye, dāsayatīti dāsaḥ = Vṛtra, ac in the pacādi group by nandigrahapacādibhyaḥ…, end-acute by citaḥ; dāsaḥ patir yāsāṃ tāḥ: ṅīp by vibhāṣā sapūrvasya (Pā. sū. 4-1-34) with n for the i; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam; or dāsasya pālayitryaḥ, a genitive tatpuruṣa, first-member accent by patyāv aiśvarye (Pā. sū. 6-2-18); ahigopāḥ — gupū rakṣaṇe, āya by āyādaya ārdhadhātuke vā (Pā. sū. 3-1-31), sanādyantā dhātavaḥ, kvip ca, ato lopaḥ, ver apṛktasya, lopo vyor vali, the y dropped first by ver apṛktalopād valilopo balīyān, the objection from acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau answered by na padāntadvirvacana… yalopa… (Pā. sū. 1-1-58); bahuvrīhau…; niruddhāḥ — rudhir āvaraṇe, kta, dh by jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ (Pā. sū. 8-2-40), gatir anantaraḥ; jaghanvān — han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, kvasu by kvasuś ca (Pā. sū. 3-2-107), doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cutva, kutva by abhyāsāc ca (Pā. sū. 7-3-55), iṭ optional by vibhāṣā gamahana… (Pā. sū. 7-2-68) and not taken; ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ (num), atvasantasya (lengthening), halṅyābbhyaḥ (s-loss), saṃyogāntasya (final s), na lopaḥ… blocked; in the Saṃhitā rutva by dīrghād aṭi samānapāde and nasalisation by āto 'ṭi nityam. The print gives only these numbers; ends ॥ ११ ॥.

37. The English Translation, Special Topics and the grammar of Rik 12 begin on p. 635 (PDF 650) — to be written in the next batch.

¶ Grammar pages 635–636, noted briefly: aśvyaḥ — aśve bhavaḥ aśvyaḥ; the affix yat by Pā. sū. 4-4-110 bhave chandasi; the initial acute by Pā. sū. 6-1-213 yato 'nāvaḥ; vāraḥ — vārayati daṃśamaśakān iti vāraḥ; ṇic in the causative sense; it is in the pacādi group (nandigrahapacādibhyaḥ…), so ac; ṇic gives vṛddhi of the root; ac causes the loss of ṇi by ṇer aniṭi; since vāra belongs to the kapilakādi group, the l-substitution (vāla) is optional (Pā. sū. Ma. 8-2-18); the end-acute through the suffix, but, the word being in the vṛṣādi group, the initial acute by Pā. sū. 6-1-203 vṛṣādīnāṃ ca; pratyahan — prati as a prefix; han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, adādi; śap dropped by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; the final i of tip and the t dropped by halṅyābbhyo…; lowering would arise but, because of the correlation with yat (Pā. sū. 8-1-66 yadvṛttān nityam), is prevented; the root's end-acute gives the initial acute; the gati prati is low-accented by tiṅi codāttavati (Pā. sū. 8-1-71); ajayaḥ — ji jaye; laṅ 2nd singular, ajayaḥ; the first ajayaḥ is at the pāda's head, so no lowering; although the second ajayaḥ stands after gāḥ, a non-verb, and might be lowered by tiṅ atiṅaḥ, the dictum samānavākye nighātayuṣmadasmadādeśā vaktavyāḥ (Pā. sū. 8-1-18-5; the bhāṣya prints पा. १-१-१८-५ (pā. 1-1-18-5)) applies: since gāḥ is connected to the earlier verb, they are different sentence-parts, and so the second ajayaḥ is the head of a pāda-part and is not lowered; sartave — sṛ gatau; the affix taveṅ by tumarthe sesen… (Pā. sū. 3-4-9); guṇa of ṛ because the suffix is ārdhadhātuka; taveṅ is nit, so initial acute by ñnity ādir nityam. The print gives only Pā. sū. 4-4-110, 6-1-213, Ma. 8-2-18, 6-1-203, 8-1-66, 8-1-71, 8-1-18-5, 3-4-9; ends ॥ १२ ॥.

Sūkta 32, Rik 13

38. Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 1: the bar after ह्रा (hrā) stands under the start of दु (du), beside the subscripts; set on दु.

¶ Grammar pages 638–639, noted briefly: siṣedha — ṣidhu gatyām, bhvādi; s for ṣ by P. 6-1-64 dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ; liṭ 3rd singular, tip → ṇal by P. 3-4-82 parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus…; doubling because of ṇit; halādiḥ śeṣaḥ; the root's light penult takes guṇa; ṣatva of the reduplicate's s after i by P. 8-3-59 ādeśapratyayayoḥ: siṣedha; being atiṅanta... the lowering of the verb by P. 8-1-28; miham — miha secane; 'what sprinkles' is miṭ = rain, with kvip by P. 3-2-76; accusative singular; akirat — kṛ vikṣepe, tudādi; laṅ 3rd singular; the i of tip dropped by P. 3-4-100 itaś ca; śa by P. 3-1-77 tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ; apit, hence ṅit by P. 1-2-4 and no guṇa; the ṛ → ir by P. 7-1-100 ṛta id dhātoḥ; → ra by uraṇ raparaḥ; the aṭ augment; the correlation with yām prevents lowering (P. 8-1-66); the aṭ being acute, initial acute; yuyudhāte — yudha saṃprahāre, divādi; liṭ 3rd dual, the ending ātām → ā + te: e by P. 3-4-81 liṭas tajhayor eśirec; the e by P. 3-4-79; doubling; since liṭ is kit [by P. 1-2-5 asaṃyogāl liṭ kit], no guṇa; yuyudhāte; no lowering since yat is correlated; the accent: the ṭhakāra [dhakāra]-following u… is anudātta by the suffix's initial acute; jigye — ji jaye; liṭ 3rd singular, e by P. 3-4-81; doubling of ji; jigye: by P. 7-3-57 sanliṭor jeḥ (सन्लिटोर्जेः) the j of the root after the reduplicate becomes g (kutva); [the print: 'by antaratamya g arises']; lowered by P. 8-1-28 tiṅ atiṅaḥ [the print: P. 8-1-28 as tiṅ tiṅaḥ]. Numerals as read.

¶ Grammar pages 642–643, noted briefly, from the print: hṛdi — hṛd for hṛdaya in the locative by paddan-no-mās-hṛd… (Pā. sū. 6-1-63), the ending acute by ūḍidampadādi… (Pā. sū. 6-1-171); jaghnuṣaḥ — han hiṃsāgatyoḥ, kvasu by kvasuś ca, doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, cutva, gh by abhyāsāc ca; genitive singular: saṃprasāraṇa of v by vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam (Pā. sū. 6-4-131), pūrvarūpa by saṃprasāraṇāc ca, the penult a dropped by gamahanajana… (Pā. sū. 6-4-98), ṣatva by śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca; the single substitute would be asiddha for ṣatva by ṣatvatukor asiddhaḥ (Pā. sū. 6-1-86), but the vārttika saṃprasāraṇaṅīṭsu pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ (Kā. 6-1-86-1) bars it; asiddhavad atrābhāt (Pā. sū. 6-4-22) does not apply because the conditions (nimitta) differ, so jaghnuṣaḥ stands; sravantīḥ — sru gatau, bhvādi, śatṛ by laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau, śap by kartari śap, guṇa and av, sravat; ṅīp by ugitaś ca; num by śapśyanor nityam (Pā. sū. 7-1-81); śap unaccented as pit; tāsy anudāttet… and the root's initial acute; ataraḥ — tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ, laṅ 2nd singular; no lowering by yadvṛttān nityam because of yan navatim; the aṭ acute, initial acute. ¶ Grammar pages 646–647, noted briefly, from the print (p. 646 read from the old scan, PDF 661): yātaḥ — yā prāpaṇe, adādi, yātīti yāt, śatṛ by laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau, genitive singular, the ending acute by sāv ekācaḥ… (Pā. sū. 6-1-168); saḥ — the s dropped in the Saṃhitā by so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam (Pā. sū. 6-1-134), sa + it: guṇa; tā — tad, accusative plural, śi by jaśśasoḥ śiḥ, sarvanāmasthāna by śi sarvanāmasthānam, num by napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ, lengthening by sarvanāmasthāne…, the i of śi dropped by śeś chandasi bahulam, n dropped by nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya; babhūva — bhū sattāyām, ṇal, vuk by bhuvo vuk luṅliṭoḥ, doubling, halādiḥ śeṣaḥ, a by bhavater aḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-73 [as printed; for 7-4-73]; the bhāṣya prints पा. ७-४-७३ (pā. 7-4-73)), b by abhyāse carca; vuk is nitya (kṛtākṛtaprasaṅgī) and so precedes vṛddhi (aco ñṇiti); or by indhibhavatibhyāṃ ca (Pā. sū. 1-2-6) liṭ is kit and vṛddhi is barred; asiddhavad atrābhāt would make vuk asiddha and bring uvaṅ by aci śnudhātubhruvām…, but by the vārttika vugyuṭāv uvaṅyaṇoḥ siddhau bhavataḥ (Pā. sū. 6-4-22-14) vuk is siddha, so no uvaṅ; nighāta by tiṅṅatiṅaḥ after a non-verb.
